title: feat(cli): refuse batch runs whose --out folder is the --in folder
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

`photocraft-cli batch` writes each result to `<--out>/<stem>.<ext>`. When `--out` names the same folder as `--in`, results replace source images without any warning: without `--format` each result replaces its own source and the run reports success, and with `--format` a result can replace a different input that shares its stem. Make `batch` refuse that configuration before it writes anything, unless the user explicitly asks for in-place processing.

## Problem to solve

The CLI usage (`--in <dir> --out <dir>`) and the README example (`--in ./raw --out ./graded`) present `batch` as reading from one folder and writing to another. Nothing stops `--out` from being the input folder, and nothing reports that the originals were replaced. With the v0.2.0 release CLI (`photocraft-cli 0.2.0 (ad8632173, 2026-10-05)`) and a source build of `main` at 93bd44899baf17f28f48ca47a652fb2dd5db2821, on macOS 27.0 arm64:

```text
$ shasum in/a.png        # 85e7894aed59…
$ photocraft-cli batch --actions act.json --in in --out in
ok    in/a.png -> in/a.png
ok    in/b.jpg -> in/b.jpg
warning: lossy compression
2 succeeded, 0 failed
$ echo $?
0
$ shasum in/a.png        # 074f0b085151…
```

Here `act.json` is `[{"command":"image.adjustments.invert"}]` and `in/` holds `a.png` and `b.jpg`, made with `ffmpeg -v error -f lavfi -i testsrc=size=64x48 -frames:v 1 in/a.png` and the same command writing `in/b.jpg`. Both originals now hold the inverted result; for the JPEG the original pixels are also re-encoded lossily. A slip such as `--out .` run inside the input folder, or a script that reuses one variable for both flags, loses the source images with no prompt and no non-zero exit.

The same-output check added for #420 does not cover this case: it reports two inputs that map to one output name, while here each input maps to its own path, which is the input file itself. It was re-run on the `main` build above with the same result.

With `--format`, the in-place run can also replace a di…

title: feat(algo): keep Median and Dust & Scratches run time from growing with the square of the radius
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

Filter › Noise › Median and Dust & Scratches accept a radius from 1 to 500, but their run time grows with the square of the radius. On a 1920×1280 RGB image, Median at radius 64 took 23 s, and on a 192×128 image radius 252 took 33 s. Large radii, which the registry advertises, are therefore impractical on real photos. This request is for these two filters to scale no worse than linearly with the radius while producing the same pixels.

## Problem to solve

`AGENTS.md` sets the project goal of Photoshop parity "with better performance". The registry advertises `filter.noise.median {"radius":1..500=1}` and `filter.noise.dustAndScratches {"radius":1..500=1,"threshold":0..255=0}` (`crates/engine/src/filters.rs:297-298`). `median` in `crates/algo/src/noise.rs` (lines 52-81 on `main` at 93bd44899baf17f28f48ca47a652fb2dd5db2821) gathers every sample in a disc of the given radius, about πr² values, for each pixel and channel, and selects their median, so each doubling of the radius multiplies the work by about four.

Measured through `photocraft-cli serve` (`doc.open`, then one `engine.execute`, timing the reply) on an 18-core arm64 Mac running other jobs (load average 8-18 during the runs). Images were made with `ffmpeg -f lavfi -i testsrc2=size=WxH -frames:v 1`:

| Build | Image | Command | Radius | Time |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| `main` | 192×128 | Median | 32 / 63 / 126 / 252 | 0.53 / 2.01 / 7.95 / 32.96 s |
| `main` | 192×128 | Dust & Scratches, threshold 64 | 32 / 63 / 126 / 252 | 0.53 / 1.97 / 8.18 / 37.62 s |
| `main` | 1920×1280 | Dust & Scratches, threshold 0 | 8 / 16 / 32 | 0.35 / 1.26 / 5.29 s |
| `main` | 1920×1280 | Median | 64 | 23.04 s |
| v0.2.0 (`photocraft-cli 0.2.0 (ad8632173, 2026-10-05)`) | 192×128 | Median / Dust & Scratches, threshold 64 | 126 | 8.26 / 8.13 s |

Each doubling of the radius multiplied the time by 3.6 to 4.6. Extrapolating that ratio, which was not measured, radius 500 on the 1920×1280 image would take roughly 20 to 25 min…

In headless automation (`photocraft-cli mcp` and `photocraft-cli serve`), a background job started with `"wait": false` is applied to its document only when a later request runs a command or calls `jobs_list` / `jobs.list`. Until then, `doc_save`, `doc_export`, `doc_inspect`, `doc_render_preview` and `session_list` (and their `serve` equivalents) report and write the document as it was before the job, even after the job has finished, with no warning. A client that starts a filter as a job and saves once it expects the job to be done gets a file without the filter; only a client that polls `jobs_list` first sees the result.

title: fix(automation): MCP `command_batch` loses every step result when its reply budget stops the batch
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

On current `main`, an MCP `command_batch` whose aggregate reply budget stops the batch can still produce a tool result larger than the 8 MiB MCP ceiling, because the batch result is then embedded as an escaped JSON string in the MCP text content. The whole result is replaced by "response encoding failed: response exceeds 8388607 bytes; operation may have completed", so the client learns neither how many steps completed nor which step stopped the batch. The same request over `photocraft-cli serve` returns the partial result as documented.

## Runtime or environment

- PhotoCraft `main` at 93bd44899baf17f28f48ca47a652fb2dd5db2821, `photocraft-cli` built from source (`photocraft-cli --version` prints `photocraft-cli 0.2.0 (dev build)`). The only later `main` commit at the time of writing changes TGA export and does not touch `crates/automation`.
- Headless MCP mode (`photocraft-cli mcp --automation-read-root W --automation-write-root W`, protocol version `2025-06-18`), driven by a minimal JSON-RPC client over stdio; `photocraft-cli serve` on stdio for comparison.
- macOS 27.0 arm64.
- Not applicable to the v0.2.0 release, which has no reply budget or reply ceiling.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start `photocraft-cli mcp --automation-read-root W --automation-write-root W` (absolute path for an empty directory `W`) and initialize the MCP session.
2. Call `command_batch` with `steps` set to 255 copies of `{"id":"command.list"}` followed by `{"id":"file.new"}`, and `"stop_on_error": false`.

title: feat(automation): keep the `photocraft-cli serve` stdio session after rejecting an over-long request line
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

On current `main`, `photocraft-cli serve` over stdio answers a request line longer than 1 MiB with an error and then exits with status 0, so every document open in the headless session, including unsaved edits, is lost, and later requests on the same pipe get no reply. Over stdio the pipe is the whole session, so the TCP behavior it mirrors (closing the offending connection while the shared session survives) costs much more here. This asks for the stdio server to reject the over-long line safely and keep serving.

## Problem to solve

The 1 MiB request ceiling was applied to stdio in #93, matching the TCP listener. Over TCP, an oversized line closes that one connection and the shared headless session keeps its documents. Over stdio, `serve_lines` returns after the error and the process ends. Observed on the current `main` source build at 93bd44899baf17f28f48ca47a652fb2dd5db2821 (`photocraft-cli 0.2.0 (dev build)`), on macOS 27.0 arm64, with `photocraft-cli serve --automation-read-root W --automation-write-root W` driven one line at a time:

```text
{"id":1,"method":"doc.new","params":{"width":8,"height":8}}   -> {"id":1,"ok":true,"result":{"document":0}}
{"id":2,"method":"methods","params":{"pad":"xxx…"}} (1,100,054 bytes) -> {"error":"request exceeds 1048576 bytes","id":null,"ok":false}
{"id":3,"method":"session.list"}                               -> no reply; the process exited with status 0 and empty stderr
```

The 8×8 document from request 1 is gone. Other bad input on the same transport does not end the session: a line that is not JSON gets `{"error":"bad JSON: key must be a string at line 1 column 2","id":null,"ok":false}`, and a reply over 8 MiB is replaced by `{"error":"response exceeds 8388608 bytes; operation may have completed",…}`, after which the server keeps answering (both observed on the same build). A line of 1,000,074 bytes, under the limit, is processed normally. The v0.2.0 release CLI (`photocraft-cli 0.2.0 (ad8632173, 2026-10-05)`)…

title: feat(automation): reject command `params` that are not a JSON object instead of running with defaults
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

Every entry point that runs an engine command accepts a `params` value of any JSON type: an array, string or number is treated like `{}`, and the command runs with all its defaults and reports success. `photocraft-cli run --new` does the same for the new-document spec. A caller who passes `"radius=3"` or `[3]` gets a different edit from the one requested and no error. This asks for such calls to fail with an error that names the command and says that params must be an object.

## Problem to solve

The registry describes each command's params as an object (`command_list` / `engine.commands` hints such as `{"radius":0.1..1000=1}`), MCP `command_run` documents `params` as "Command parameters as a JSON object", and the CLI usage says `--params <json>` applies to the preceding `--cmd`. Observed on the current `main` source build at 93bd44899baf17f28f48ca47a652fb2dd5db2821 and on the v0.2.0 release CLI (`photocraft-cli 0.2.0 (ad8632173, 2026-10-05)`), macOS 27.0 arm64, with a 640×480 `bars.png`:

```text

Drawing a selection with the Elliptical Marquee tool adds a history step named "Rectangular Marquee". The selection itself is elliptical; only the step name is wrong. title: feat(automation): let MCP `ui_pointer` send `button`, so bridge clients can right-click
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

The control method `ui.pointer` accepts `button: "right"` (or `"secondary"`): with a painting tool it opens the Brush Preset picker, and on `main` with the Move tool (or `command: true`) it opens the canvas layer menu. The MCP bridge tool `ui_pointer` forwards only `events` and `modifiers`, so a bridge client cannot send a right-button gesture through it. A `button` field sent anyway is dropped without an error, and the gesture runs as a left-button one: with the Brush tool it paints a dot instead of opening the picker or the menu. Give `ui_pointer` a `button` field that reaches `ui.pointer`, and reject arguments it does not forward.

## Problem to solve

An agent connected through `photocraft-cli mcp --bridge` drives the live app with the `ui_*` tools. To open the layer menu or the Brush Preset picker it has to know that `ui_pointer` cannot do it and fall back to the raw `control_call` tool. An agent that adds `button: "right"` to `ui_pointer`, as `docs/control-protocol.md:45` documents for `ui.pointer`, gets a success result and an unwanted paint stroke in the document's history.

title: fix(format): .pcraft documents with 40 or more nested group levels save but cannot be reopened
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

Saving a document whose layer groups are nested 40 or more levels deep as `.pcraft` succeeds with exit 0 and no warning, but opening the saved file fails with `manifest JSON: recursion limit exceeded`. The native format therefore writes files that PhotoCraft cannot read back. A 39-level document reopens, and the same 40-level document saved as `.psd` reopens.

## Runtime or environment

- Release: v0.2.0 release CLI, reporting `photocraft-cli 0.2.0 (ad8632173, 2026-10-05)`, on macOS 27 arm64.
- Source: `main` at 93bd44899baf17f28f48ca47a652fb2dd5db2821, reporting `photocraft-cli 0.2.0 (dev build)`, same host. The one later commit on `main` at the time of writing only adds TGA to the desktop Save As and export dialogs and does not touch `crates/format`.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Build a document with 40 nested groups and save it as `.pcraft` (bash or zsh):

```sh
args=(); for i in $(seq 40); do args+=(--cmd layer.groupLayers); done
photocraft-cli run --new '{"width":8,"height":8}' "${args[@]}" --out g40.pcraft; echo "exit $?"
photocraft-cli info --compact g40.pcraft
```

2. Repeat step 1 with `seq 39` and `--out g39.pcraft` as a control.
3. Repeat step 1 with `--out g40.psd`, run `photocraft-cli info --compact g40.psd`, then `photocraft-cli convert g40.psd g40b.pcraft` and `photocraft-cli info --compact g40b.pcraft`.

## Expected behavior

`book/src/formats/pcraft.md` describes `.pcraft` as "the native lossless document" format. A document that PhotoCraft saves as `.pcraft` without an error should open again with its layer tree. The loader's own layer-tree conversion accepts groups nested up to 256 levels (`layer()` in `crates/format/src/convert.rs` returns `layer groups nested deeper than 256` only beyond that), so 40 levels is inside the depth the format intends to accept. title: fix(codecs): a truncated JPEG opens and converts with no error or warning, its missing rows filled grey
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

A JPEG cut off partway through its image data opens and converts with exit 0 and an empty `warnings` list. The rows the file no longer contains come back as uniform mid-grey (128, 128, 128). Users and agents get no signal that the file is damaged, so a conversion or batch run writes the grey-filled result as if it were complete.

title: fix(docs): README, architecture and the book overstate format support and give outdated decode limits
author: coygeek
body:

title: fix(io): JPEG exports from the CLI, MCP and Layers to Files drop alpha and show hidden colours, while Export As and Quick Export composite over white

body:
## Summary

Exporting a document with transparent pixels to JPEG gives different pixels depending on the route. File › Export › Export As and Quick Export composite the image over white. `photocraft-cli convert`, `run` and `batch`, MCP `doc_export`, File › Export › Layers to Files and Layer › Export As instead discard the alpha channel: fully transparent pixels come out in whatever colour they store (black in the test file), and half-transparent pixels become fully opaque in their stored colour. body:
## Summary

When PhotoCraft opens an animated GIF or APNG (observed), or an animated WebP or multi-page TIFF (documented in the codecs README, not run here), it keeps only the first frame or page and reports no warning. Add an import warning so users and agents know the rest of the file was not imported.

## Problem to solve

A 3-frame GIF and a 3-frame APNG each open as a single layer with `warnings: []`, on both the v0.2.0 release CLI (`photocraft-cli 0.2.0 (ad8632173, 2026-10-05)`) and a source build of `main` at 93bd44899baf17f28f48ca47a652fb2dd5db2821, on macOS 27 arm64. The import path already reports other discarded data as warnings, for example `N text metadata entries are not kept in the document`, and `FormatCaps::animation` already marks containers that can hold more frames. When an import decodes only the first of several frames or pages, the import result carries a warning that says only the first frame (or page) was imported and, when known, how many there were. title: fix(docs): the 1 MiB request-line claim omits the MCP stdio exception
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

The automation security book says "Encoded request lines are limited to 1 MiB" without naming the transports. MCP normally uses stdio, but its input transport accepts larger request lines. The authoritative control protocol scopes the request ceiling to TCP and headless JSON-lines stdio, so this report concerns the book's wording rather than claiming that MCP violates its protocol contract. A reader of the book cannot tell that the ceiling does not cover MCP stdio input.

title: Windows: Shift+Delete cuts the selection instead of opening Edit › Fill
author: sommerper
body:
On Linux and macOS, Shift+Delete on the canvas opens Edit › Fill…: `shortcut_dispatch::SECONDARY` binds Fill to Shift+Backspace, and `shortcuts::key_matches` treats Delete and Backspace as the same key.

On Windows, egui-winit 0.36 turns Shift+Delete into `Event::Cut` before the app sees the key (`is_cut_command` in egui-winit's `lib.rs`). Outside text fields, `shortcuts::clipboard_keys` turns that into ⌘X. So on Windows, Shift+Delete on the canvas should run Edit › Cut, while Shift+Backspace opens Fill.

Found by reading the code. Not reproduced: no Windows machine to test on.

**To check on Windows**
1. Select an area of a pixel layer and press Shift+Delete. Linux/macOS open the Fill dialog. Suspected on Windows: the selection is cut.
2. In a text field, Shift+Delete should still cut text (the Windows convention).

**Possible fix:** in `clipboard_keys` on Windows, outside text fields, turn an `Event::Cut` that arrives with Shift held and Ctrl not held back into a Shift+Delete key press. (Ctrl+X still arrives with Ctrl held.)

author: niclotterie

**Observed on:** a large (~1 GB) real-world Photoshop-authored PSD (details withheld; structure only below).

Opening it warns:

```
smart filter masks (FEid) could not be read: invalid data: filter effects: 128002566 unexpected bytes after the data
```

The document opens fine; the casualty is the smart-filter mask/cache data — filters render unmasked, and since export preserves `FEid` items only when they parsed, a save-back would not round-trip the block.

title: Menu bar: dropdowns open over their menu titles (Linux/Wayland)
author: theDavidCoen
body:
## Summary

On Linux (Wayland), top-menu dropdowns (and their submenus) open **on top of** the menu title instead of below it. The first row of the popup sits where **File** / **View** / etc. should remain visible.

Same class of bug as in LightCraft (shared egui 0.36 in-window menubar behaviour).

## Screenshots

File menu covering the File title:

![PhotoCraft File menu overlap](https://files.catbox.moe/j9f2cv.png)

View → Proof Setup submenu with the same upward overlap:

![PhotoCraft View menu overlap](https://files.catbox.moe/5r1gen.png)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run PhotoCraft 0.2.0 linux-x86_64 AppImage on Linux/Wayland.
2. Open **File**, **View**, or other top-level menus.
3. Optionally open a submenu (e.g. View → Proof Setup).

## Expected

Dropdowns open **below** the menu title; submenus open beside the parent item without covering the top bar.

## Actual

Popup top aligns with the top of the window/menu bar and covers the title. Submenus share the same vertical misplacement.

## Environment

- PhotoCraft 0.2.0 (linux-x86_64 AppImage)
- Linux CachyOS, **Wayland**
- egui / eframe **0.36** (`menus::menu_bar` → `egui::MenuBar` + `ui.menu_button`)

## Notes / likely cause

- Code already assumes the bar is not under its own dropdowns (`switch_on_hover` comment: “the bar is never under its own dropdowns”), but with this bug the popup covers the titles and that hit-testing assumption fails.
- egui `Popup` default is `RectAlign::BOTTOM_START`, with `get_best_align()` falling back to symmetries / `MENU_ALIGNS` (including `TOP_START`). An “open above” choice clamped to the window top would produce exactly this overlap.
- Sibling report filed on LightCraft (same egui generation / in-window menus).

## Suggested direction

- Prefer below-the-button alignment for top-level menu popups on Linux.
- Re-check anchor rect / available screen rect under Wayland with eframe 0.36.

title: [Feature] Choose installed monitor profiles or ICC files with per-display overrides
author: ha1des
body:
Origin: Codex · Role: Status · Mode: change · Baseline: 2026-10-07

**Feature proposal: choose an installed monitor profile at any time, with an explicit assignment per display**

PhotoCraft should offer a regular manual monitor-profile selection alongside automatic detection. Users must be able to choose an installed operating-system profile or an ICC file even when auto detection succeeds. The choice affects how images are displayed; it must not change the document's embedded profile or exported pixels.

This feature is separated from [#569, the macOS automatic display-profile bug](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/issues/569), at the reporter's request. That issue owns correct automatic resolution for the image window and following display/profile changes. This issue owns the profile catalog, selection UI and persistent manual assignment. It is a proposal for implementation, not a claim that the feature has been implemented.

**Existing capability and gap**

At reviewed commit `7eb3b2e072aa3110da2a329bb49109744292a87b`, the engine's [`edit.colorSettings` command](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/7eb3b2e072aa3110da2a329bb49109744292a87b/crates/engine/src/color_cmds.rs#L954) already accepts a monitor-profile ICC path and persists the choice. The generated dialog presents static built-in profile choices, without an OS profile catalog or an ICC-file picker. A generic sRGB/Adobe RGB/ProPhoto choice cannot stand in for a particular calibrated display profile.

The present selection is session-wide. A global manual profile can become incorrect when the image window moves to another monitor. Recheck current preference code when implementing; this proposal describes the reviewed behavior, not a guarantee that `main` is unchanged.

**Requested behavior**

- Keep **Automatic — use this display's OS-assigned profile** as the default and an always-available option.
- Provide **Manual — choose a profile for this display**, available regardless of auto-detecti…

title: PSD placed layers: perspective (nonAffineTransform) is dropped, so Edit Contents flattens mockup covers
author: arturneumann
body:
**Version:** 0.2.0 release (ad86321), macOS arm64. Same code path on main @ 2628b0d.

### What happens

Book and packaging mockups place the cover as a Smart Object with a perspective transform. PhotoCraft opens such a PSD correctly, because it shows Photoshop's cached pixels. As soon as the Smart Object is re-rendered (Edit Contents and save, Replace Contents, a smart filter), the cover is drawn as an axis-aligned rectangle stretched over its bounding box instead of in perspective. In a book mockup it also covers the spine.

### Steps

1. Open a Photoshop-authored mockup PSD whose cover Smart Object has a perspective (non-affine) transform.
2. Layer › Smart Objects › Edit Contents, change anything, save.
3. The cover in the mockup is now flat and stretched over the bounding box of the book.

### Why

`blocks::parse_smart` (and `smart_map::parse_transform`) builds the affine from corners 0, 1 and 3 of `Trnf`. In Photoshop files with a perspective transform, `Trnf` holds the axis-aligned bounding box and the real corners are in `nonAffineTransform`. Example from the file I tested (source 1166 × 1654 px, `warpNone`):

```
Trnf               = [126,288, 1868.25,288, 1868.25,1595.25, 126,1595.25]
nonAffineTransform = [126,668, 981.5,288, 1868.25,1102, 947,1595.25]
```

### Suggestion

#215 already lists "Smart Object corner skew and perspective (store a quad or homography instead of an affine)". Until that lands, an import-time fallback works well with what is already there: map the unit square to the `nonAffineTransform` quad (a homography) and store it as a custom `warp` mesh on the Smart Object (`SmartObject::warp`, applied before `transform`).

I tried this with `layer.smartObjects.warp` and a fitted `mesh` (the 4 × 4 interpolation scheme of `BezierMesh::fit`):

- one bicubic patch matches the homography to within 0.05 px for this mockup, a 2 × 2 grid to within 0.004 px
- after that, Edit Contents re-renders the cover in the right place; the flattened result differs…

title: [Architecture decision] macOS: let the OS colour-match the canvas per display (tagged CAMetalLayer colour space)
author: ha1des
body:
Origin: Claude Code · Role: Proposal · Mode: decision needed · Baseline: 2628b0dd3d667e481e1c0c5e3bf487708b4b1bf5 (2026-10-07)

> **This needs an explicit architecture decision by the owner before any implementation.** It would add a second isolated exception to the workspace-wide `unsafe_code = "forbid"` rule (today only `photocraft-tablet` has one, see `AGENTS.md` › Never crash) and would change where the canvas's display conversion happens on macOS. Nobody should start on it without that decision recorded here.

**Proposal: on macOS, let the OS colour-match the canvas to each display (tagged `CAMetalLayer` colour space)**

[#569](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/issues/569) is being fixed within the current rules (option A there): PhotoCraft finds the display its window is on, reads that display's profile through the existing `osascript` helper and converts to it itself, per window. This issue records the alternative that native Cocoa applications use, so it can be decided on its own merits.

**How it would work**

PhotoCraft draws through wgpu into a `CAMetalLayer` whose [`colorspace`](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/quartzcore/cametallayer/colorspace) is left unset. macOS then sends the pixel values to each display unchanged, so PhotoCraft has to convert to the monitor profile itself, and has to know which display that is. If the layer is tagged with a colour space instead, macOS colour-matches its content to whichever display shows it, including:

- moving a window to another display, without PhotoCraft noticing or re-rendering;
- a profile reassigned in System Settings (e.g. after calibration) on an unchanged display;
- a window spanning two displays, each half matched to its own display (option A can only pick one display per window);
- several windows on different displays, each matched to its own display, without per-window output state in PhotoCraft.

The canvas transform would then be document profile → the layer's colour space, the same…

title: Windows MSIs: Start Menu shortcuts point at the installer-cache icon, and the executables have no embedded icon (PhotoCraft, VectorCraft, EffectCraft 0.4.0)
author: cayorivera
body:
﻿### Summary

The Windows MSI installers create a **broken Start Menu shortcut** and the executables ship **without an embedded icon**. Verified with three apps from the family, including the newest release:

| App | Version tested | Shortcut target created by the MSI |
|---|---|---|
| PhotoCraft | 0.2.0 | `C:\Windows\Installer\{9DC6461B-A3ED-4B40-9CEE-754295B7AB99}\PhotocraftIcon` |
| VectorCraft | 0.3.1 | `C:\Windows\Installer\{CDC56573-BBE4-4DEC-8BF7-2F5FE9FE9453}\VectorcraftIcon.ico` |
| EffectCraft | **0.4.0** | `C:\Windows\Installer\{AD98B147-97B2-401F-95F1-C450C5C79883}\EffectcraftIcon.ico` |

### 1. Start Menu shortcut points at the installer-cache icon, not the executable

For every app above, `C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\<App>.lnk` has its `TargetPath` set to the icon blob inside the MSI installer cache instead of the real `.exe` — so the shortcut does not launch the application.

Attempting to repair the icon with `WScript.Shell` (reading the shortcut, setting only `IconLocation`, then saving) silently writes the icon path into the shortcut's **target**, leaving it pointing at a non-executable file. The only reliable repair is to delete the shortcut and create a fresh plain shortcut pointing at the executable with the icon from `assets/app-icon/<app>.ico`.

This reproduces on **EffectCraft 0.4.0**, i.e. it is not fixed in the current release.

### 2. The executables appear to have no embedded icon

`photocraft.exe`, `vectorcraft.exe` and `effectcraft.exe` all show the **generic Windows document icon** in Explorer, the taskbar and Alt-Tab, even though each repository ships a proper multi-size `.ico` (e.g. `assets/app-icon/photocraft.ico`, 9 sizes 16–256 px). Setting the icon on a shortcut works around it, but the application window itself keeps the generic icon.

`photocraft-cli.exe` additionally exposes no version metadata at all (no CompanyName / ProductName / FileVersion).

### Environment

- Windows 11 Pro, build 26300, x64
- N…

title: ⌘-scroll or Ctrl-scroll to pan the canvas sideways
author: rosematcha
body:
Howdy! A feature I'm fond of in the reference app is the easy ability to scroll sideways. This is done on macOS by holding ⌘ and scrolling, and the behavior also exists on Windows by holding Ctrl and scrolling. I've bound this to muscle memory, and it's a feature that's very important to me.

PhotoCraft's current behavior on Mac is a zoom on ⌘-scroll, which is asymmetrical with the reference app. Ctrl-scroll also zooms on Mac. I tried a fix for both ⌘-scroll and Ctrl-scroll in #362, but it was pointed out this would also break touchpad pinch on Windows.

From what I've found, that's because Windows has two ways of delivering a touchpad pinch. Apps that don't opt in to touchpad gestures get a legacy fallback, where Windows turns the pinch into mouse-wheel messages with the Ctrl flag set. Those can't be told apart from a real Ctrl+wheel. Apps that use the [DirectManipulation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/directmanipulation/direct-manipulation-portal) API get the pinch as its own gesture instead, which leaves Ctrl+wheel free. Chromium and Blender do this, and Zed (also Rust) shipped it in [zed#51354](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/51354). winit doesn't support it yet ([winit#4602](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/issues/4602)), so we'd need to call the Windows API directly, which means `unsafe` code. macOS doesn't have this problem: winit delivers a trackpad pinch there as a separate `PinchGesture` event, never as ⌘-scroll.

I'd like to make this issue a discussion thread on implementing this behavior cleanly. Open questions:

1. Do we want to establish the precedent of a "behavior break" from macOS to Windows? I think feature parity across platforms is important, and wouldn't want just macOS to get a feature and Windows to not.
2. How do we hypothetically want to implement this on Linux? Should we follow Windows' Ctrl-scroll, or make it Super-scroll? I lean the former, but I don't use Linux. For what it's worth, winit currently de…

title: Finding: how layers, brush strokes, and the smooth rendering pipeline are implemented — architecture walkthrough with code paths
author: IAFahim
body:
## Finding: architecture walkthrough — how layers, brush strokes, and the smooth rendering pipeline are implemented

**Type:** finding / documentation write-up (no bug, no repro needed — this is a static-analysis walkthrough of the current code, with code paths for each claim)

**Verified against:** commit `b07a2e5b43939497032a0c27489df55a1a1a7295` (2026-10-07). All paths are relative to the repo root; `file:line` references point at the definitions as of that commit.

**TL;DR:** The engine's responsiveness is architectural, not hardware-dependent: every stage of the pipeline (stroke rasterization → layer compositing → texture upload → on-screen draw) is proportional to *what changed*, never to document size. And it is **100% local compute** — there is no cloud/remote offload anywhere in the workspace. This issue documents the full chain with the code paths that implement it.

---

### 1. Layer model — non-destructive by construction (`crates/doc`)

- `pub struct Document` at `crates/doc/src/lib.rs:625`, `pub struct Layer` at `:436`, `pub enum LayerContent` at `:411`.
- A layer's content is an enum — `Raster | Group | Adjustment | Fill | Text | Shape | Smart` (`crates/doc/src/lib.rs:411`) — plus per-layer blend mode, opacity vs. fill opacity, clipping, raster mask, vector mask, layer `Effects` (`:154`) and blend-if.
- The compositor evaluates this **graph** every frame; nothing is flattened or baked. That's what keeps adjustment layers, smart filters and layer styles live and reversible.

### 2. Pixel storage — sparse copy-on-write tiles (`crates/raster`)

- `pub struct Surface` at `crates/raster/src/lib.rs:45`: a sparse `BTreeMap<TileCoord, Arc<Tile>>` of 256×256 tiles (`:48`); missing tiles read as the surface's default pixel (transparent for layers, white for "reveal all" masks).
- All mutation funnels through `Surface::tile_mut` (`crates/raster/src/lib.rs:90`) → `Arc::make_mut`: copy-on-write. Consequences that everything else builds on:
  - Cloning a whole docu…

### What happens

File › Export › Export As… (desktop: `export_dialog.rs` → `photocraft_io::export` with
`ExportOptions::default()`), `photocraft-cli convert` and Layers/Artboards to Files write the document's
full XMP packet into every flat image, because `EncodeOptions::embed_metadata` defaults to `true` and the
dialog has no metadata choice.

PSDs from the source application carry a lot of document-only XMP: `photoshop:DocumentAncestors` (one
UUID per placed/pasted document, often thousands) and `photoshop:TextLayers` (the name **and full text**

- **content leaking**: `photoshop:TextLayers` puts the text of every type layer, including hidden ones
  and other artboards, into an image that only shows one part of the design.

Save for Web and Quick Export already default to "copyright" metadata and Generate › Image Assets
writes none, so only the Export As path (and the CLI/batch exporters that share `photocraft_io::export`)
behave this way. The source application's Export As defaults to no metadata and offers
"None / Copyright and Contact Info".

```sh

title: WebP export is lossless-only and its encoder is weak: photos come out ~30× larger than a lossy WebP, flat UI art ~10× larger than libwebp's lossless
author: EthanSuquet
body:
**Version:** main @ b07a2e5 (built from source, release) · macOS 26.6, Apple M2 Max

### What happens

Export As offers "WebP (lossless)" only, with no quality setting (`crates/codecs/src/codecs/webp.rs`:
`image-webp`'s encoder, lossless only). Two separate size problems follow:

1. **No lossy WebP.** Web developers export WebP to get photo-sized files; lossless WebP of a
   photographic image is as big as a PNG. This is very likely the "WebP is ~21× too large" report.
2. **The lossless encoder is far from libwebp.** `image-webp`'s encoder doesn't use the predictor,
   cross-colour or colour-cache transforms, so even lossless output is several times larger than
   `cwebp -lossless`, and on photos it is larger than our own PNG.

### Repro (synthetic images)

```python
# photo.png: 1200×800 smooth gradient + gaussian grain (σ=6); ui.png: 1200×800 white,
# 40 flat coloured rectangles and 30 lines of black text (PIL default font)
```
```sh
photocraft-cli convert photo.png photo.webp
cwebp -lossless photo.png -o photo.cl.webp; cwebp -q 80 photo.png -o photo.q80.webp
```

| image | PNG | PhotoCraft WebP | `cwebp -lossless` | `cwebp -q 80` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| photo.png | 1,883,875 | 1,971,992 | 1,823,254 | 63,132 (31× smaller) |
| ui.png | 63,310 | 55,040 | 5,758 (9.6× smaller) | 47,694 |

On real designer PSDs (2026-10-07, 14 files) PhotoCraft's WebP was 1.2–3.6× `cwebp -lossless` and on
two large files bigger than our PNG; `cwebp -q 85` was 3–8× smaller than ours.

**Expected:** Export As › WebP has a Quality slider (lossy) and a lossless option, like the source
application; lossless output is in the range of libwebp's.
**Actual:** lossless only, with large files.

### Notes

A pure-Rust lossy VP8 encoder doesn't exist in the dependency tree today (`EncodeOptions::webp_lossless
= false` returns `Unsupported`), so lossy needs either a new encoder or an optional libwebp backend
(native only; wasm could keep lossless). Improving lossless could start with the subtract-…

title: Plugin system v2: extension points and a capability model (design)
author: Mawfyy
body:
Design proposal (this repo's RFC-by-issue convention). Complements #219; if adopted, the plug-in ABI line of that issue is tracked here. Design doc to follow at `docs/plugins-rfc.md` once the open questions below settle.

## Today — ABI v1 exists

PhotoCraft already ships sandboxed WebAssembly **filters**: [`docs/plugins.md`](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/main/docs/plugins.md), `crates/plugins` (wasmi, no imports, fuel/memory/stack/wall limits, fresh instance per band), `plugin.install/list/run/remove/reload` commands, **Filter › Plug-ins** menu with generated dialogs, smart-filter integration, one `.wasm` on native + web, measured perf (24 MP invert 1.1–1.6 s through the plugin vs 3.6–5.1 s built-in).

**Not in v1:** panel/UI plug-ins, reading other layers, progress/cancel host calls, plug-in file formats, *Last Filter* repeats plug-ins (scorecard `AUTO-219-6`, #219).

## Proposal: a plug-in *system*, not just a filter API

### Extension points (manifest `kind`)

- [ ] `filter` — shipped; v1 modules keep working behind the `pc_abi_version` gate.
- [ ] `command` — manifest declares id / label / menu path / shortcut / params schema; the host registers a real `CommandSpec`, so the palette, shortcuts, CLI, MCP and Actions drive it like any built-in command.
- [ ] `format` — open/save: declares extensions + MIME, exports `pc_read`/`pc_write`; wired into `io`/`codecs` dispatch, unknown bytes kept verbatim like unknown PSD blocks.
- [ ] `panel` — **declarative** manifest UI rendered by egui (architecture principle 3: data describes the UI), clicks route back as plug-in commands. This is #219's "panel kind" ask; plug-in *code* never touches the toolkit.
- [ ] `tool` — deferred: overlay primitives + pointer events need host callbacks first.

### Capability model (the core change)

v1 bans all imports — that is what makes the sandbox airtight, and it stays (no WASI, no FS/network/clock/randomness). v2 adds **opt-in host functions** declared in the manifest and…

title: fix(security): automation reaches the host filesystem through engine commands and preferences that still use ambient paths
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

The automation filesystem policy in `crates/automation/src/workspace.rs` fails closed for the capability-scoped document methods (`doc.open`, `doc.save`, `doc.render`, `app.open`, `app.save`) and for a hardcoded deny list of ambient-path commands, but several engine commands and preference keys that resolve host paths are not covered, so an authenticated automation client can read files, enumerate folders, load WebAssembly plug-in modules and point the app's history log at files anywhere the app's user can reach. I reproduced the read and module-load cases against a session configured with no read root and no write root, where `doc.open` and `doc.save` correctly refuse; the same session's `plugin.install {path: …}` read and installed a plug-in module from outside any grant. title: fix(psd): malformed pattern rectangle overflows i32 and panics the parser
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

`photocraft-psd` promises that parsing never panics on malformed input, but the pattern reader computes its size with unchecked `i32` subtraction. A `Patt`/`Pat2`/`Pat3` tagged block, a `.pat` file, or an `.abr` file's `patt` section whose pattern rectangle stores extreme coordinate values makes the process abort with a Rust arithmetic-overflow panic instead of returning `Err`. Opening such a file through `photocraft-cli info` exits with status 101 and prints no result.

## Steps to reproduce

The trigger is a pattern whose VMA-list rectangle holds `left = i32::MIN` and `right = i32::MAX`; both are ordinary 4-byte values any file field can carry. The same `read_pattern` runs for all three public readers: the PSD `Patt`/`Pat2`/`Pat3` global block (parsed on import by `pattern_map::from_global_blocks`), the `.pat` importer behind the `pattern.import` command (`parse_pat_file`), and the `.abr` importer behind `brush.presets.importAbr` (`abr::parse` calls `parse_pattern_block` for its `patt` section).

The smallest self-contained reproduction is a temporary integration test in `crates/psd/tests/` (run with `cargo test -p photocraft-psd --test zz_hunt_a01_patterns -- --nocapture`):

```rust
use photocraft_psd::patterns::{parse_pat_file, parse_pattern_block};

fn hostile_pattern_block() -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut p = Vec::new();
    p.extend_from_slice(&1u32.to_be_bytes()); // pattern version
    p.extend_from_slice(&3u32.to_be_bytes()); // mode: RGB
    p.extend_from_slice(&0u16.to_be_bytes()); // height (i16, unused)
    p.extend_from_slice(&0u16.to_be_bytes()); // width (i16, unused)
    p.extend_from_slice(&0u32.to_be_bytes()); // name length
    p.push(0); // id length
    p.extend_from_slice(&3u32.to_be_bytes()); // virtual memory array list version
    let mut body = Vec::new();
    body.extend_from_slice(&0i32.to_be_bytes()); // top
    body.extend_from_slice(&i32::MIN.to_be_bytes()); // left
    body.extend_from_slice(&1i32.to_be_bytes()); // bottom
   …

title: fix(psd): pattern channel placement allocates from the declared rect, not the input
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

When a pattern channel's own rectangle is smaller than the pattern's rectangle, `read_pattern` places it into a full-size plane allocated as `w * h * bpp` bytes, where `w` and `h` come from the pattern rectangle declared in the file. Nothing caps that allocation against the input, so a tiny pattern block can force allocations up to 3.6 GB per channel (the parser's `MAX_EDGE` is 30000 and a 32-bit channel uses 4 bytes per pixel), and the slot loop runs up to `count + 2` times. An 85-byte block declaring a 10000x10000 grayscale pattern with a single 1x1 channel produces a 100,000,000-byte plane; at `MAX_EDGE` with 32-bit channels and 66 slots the same shape demands roughly 221 GiB, which exceeds available memory and would abort the process (Rust aborts on allocation failure, and this is not gated by overflow checks). The three public readers affected are the PSD `Patt`/`Pat2`/`Pat3` global block import, the `.pat` importer (`pattern.import`) and the `.abr` importer (`brush.presets.importAbr`).

## Steps to reproduce

The trigger is a pattern whose declared rectangle is large, whose colour channel carries a small rectangle (1x1), and whose channel data is present but tiny. The block below is 85 bytes; run it as a temporary integration test in `crates/psd/tests/` with `cargo test -p photocraft-psd --test zz_hunt_a01_alloc -- --nocapture`:

```rust

fn hostile(edge: i32) -> Vec<u8> {

    p.extend_from_slice(&1u32.to_be_bytes()); // pattern version 1

title: Publish matching debug symbols with releases to enable community performance profiling
author: ColumbusUtrigas
body:
Could matching debug symbols be published alongside PhotoCraft releases so community members can profile the distributed binaries and share readable flame graphs?

This would help users investigate performance on different CPUs, GPUs, memory configurations, and operating systems, and identify bottlenecks that may be difficult to reproduce on a maintainer's hardware. It would also make performance reports more actionable: instead of only describing a slowdown, contributors could show which PhotoCraft functions account for the CPU time.

For example, my Windows 0.2.0 installation has no accompanying application PDB. I started looking for symbols while investigating the Gaussian Blur preview slowdown in #464, but the benefit would extend to other filters, large documents, compositing, and general UI responsiveness.

Suggested release assets:

- A separate, optional symbols archive for each supported release platform and architecture, starting with Windows PDB files for the desktop app and CLI.
- Symbols produced from the **same optimized build as the distributed executables**, so they match the binaries users are actually running. Rebuilding the same source commit locally does not provide a matching PDB for the published Windows executable.
- A short note explaining how to load the symbols in a profiler, such as Windows Performance Analyzer or Superluminal Performance, and which release/architecture the archive belongs to.

Keeping symbols in a separate download would let regular users keep the existing installation size while giving community contributors a practical way to find and report more performance bottlenecks without first setting up a development build.

title: fix(cms): LUT file sizes overflow when parsing .cube and .look input
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

`photocraft_cms::lutfile::parse` computes sizes from the file's own declarations with unchecked arithmetic in two places, so a LUT whose declared size is large panics instead of returning `LutError`. `parse_cube` multiplies a file-declared 1D size by 3 (`crates/cms/src/lutfile.rs:131`) and `parse_look` raises a file-declared size to the third power (`crates/cms/src/lutfile.rs:191`). ## Steps to reproduce

Prerequisite state: none; the baseline build is stated under Runtime or environment.

1. Parse the LUT text directly:
```rust

let _ = lutfile::parse("a.cube", b"LUT_1D_SIZE 18446744073709551615\n"); // panics
let _ = lutfile::parse("a.look", b"<look><size>4294967296</size><data>00</data></look>"); // panics

title: fix(ui): colour picker hex field panics on multi-byte input
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary
`color_picker_ui::parse_hex` accepts only a 6-character hex colour but validates the *byte* length (`h.len() != 6`) and then slices at fixed byte offsets (`&h[0..2]`, `&h[2..4]`, `&h[4..6]`). A 6-byte string whose slice boundary falls inside a multi-byte character (for example `"€€"`, three bytes each) passes the length check and panics on the slice. The colour picker dialog's body calls `parse_hex` on the dialog's `color` field every frame, so one bad `ui.dialog.set` value, or entering such text in the hex field, crashes the running app and can lose unsaved work.

## Steps to reproduce
With the app running and the control channel authenticated, open the colour picker and set its `color` field to a 6-byte multi-byte string:
```json
{"id":1,"method":"ui.dialog.open","params":{"kind":"colorPicker","target":"foreground"}}
```
The reply carries the dialog id (`{"result":{"dialog":N}}`). Then:
```json
{"id":2,"method":"ui.dialog.set","params":{"dialog":N,"field":"color","value":"€€"}}
```
On the next rendered frame `crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs.rs:115` dispatches to `color_picker_ui::body`, which calls `current(fields)` (`crates/ui-egui/src/color_picker_ui.rs:182`), which calls `parse_hex` (`crates/ui-egui/src/color_picker_ui.rs:144`) and panics. `ui.dialog.set` writes any JSON value verbatim (`crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs:304-313`), so no GUI interaction is required.

The same failure is reachable without the control channel: the dialog's hex text field parses what it contains on change (`crates/ui-egui/src/color_picker_ui.rs:313-316`), and `__orig` is parsed the same way (`crates/ui-egui/src/color_picker_ui.rs:227`). Minimal public-API regression test (fails today):
```rust
#[test]
fn parse_hex_rejects_six_byte_multibyte_input() {
    assert_eq!(photocraft_ui_egui::color_picker_ui::parse_hex("€€"), None);
}
```

## Expected behavior
A malformed colour is not a colour: `parse_hex` returns `None` and the caller falls back or ignores the value; it never panics. …

title: fix(photocraft): an unparseable --control port is silently ignored, so no control server starts
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

The desktop app reads `--control` and `PHOTOCRAFT_CONTROL_PORT` with `.parse().ok()`, so any value that is not a `u16` port (a typo such as `--control 78787`, a missing value, or a value out of range) becomes `None` and the app runs without a control server and without any diagnostic: no message, no non-zero exit, just an editor window. The documented way to start the control channel is therefore silently inert for those inputs, and a launcher or agent that believed it granted control discovers the failure only later, as a connection error that does not point at the cause. The same arm consumes the next argument unconditionally, so `photocraft --control --safe-gpu` silently discards `--safe-gpu` as the (invalid) port value and drops both settings.

## Runtime or environment

Baseline: commit 2628b0dd3d667e481e1c0c5e3bf487708b4b1bf5 on `main`. This is a static proof; no runtime reproduction was run.

## Steps to reproduce

These steps were traced in the source, not executed (the desktop binary was not built or launched in the reporting environment; the app needs a window and a GPU adapter).

1. Launch the app with an unparseable port: `photocraft --control 78787` (or `PHOTOCRAFT_CONTROL_PORT=78787 photocraft`).
2. Try the documented control call from `docs/development.md`, for example `printf '%s\n' '{"id":"auth","method":"auth","params":{"token":"…"}}' | nc 127.0.0.1 78787`.
3. Launch with a missing value: `photocraft --control --safe-gpu`, and observe that neither a control server nor the CPU-renderer launch is reported.

## Expected behavior

`docs/control-protocol.md` promises that the desktop app listens on `127.0.0.1:<port>` when started with `--control <port>` (and `docs/development.md` gives `PHOTOCRAFT_CONTROL_PORT` as the same setting). title: fix(engine): document.pixel panics on an out-of-canvas coordinate
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

The `document.pixel` query panics when either coordinate is `i32::MAX`: it renders a 1x1 region and then indexes the result with `[0]` without checking that the region produced a pixel.

`Session::execute` catches the panic and returns a generic internal error, so the caller never gets the composite pixel it asked for, and the same unchecked `[0]` is a direct violation of the "Never panic on input" rule and of the instruction to use `get()` rather than `[i]` for indices derived from params.

## Steps to reproduce

Use the baseline build under Runtime or environment and run the following commands through any supported entry point (the CLI `photocraft-cli run`, the MCP server, the TCP control channel, or `Session::execute` directly); no other state is required.

```text
file.new {"width": 24, "height": 16}
document.pixel {"x": 2147483647, "y": 2147483647}
```

The reproduction is minimized: no layers, selection or extra state are needed, and changing only the two coordinates to a value inside the canvas removes the failure.

## Expected behavior

`document.pixel` is declared with `params: {"x":i32,"y":i32}` and the label "Read Composite Pixel" (`crates/engine/src/commands.rs:820`), so it must return the composite pixel at a coordinate. Per AGENTS.md rule 9, its `run` closure and everything it calls must return `Err`, never panic, for any params or document state, and input-derived indices must use `get()`. A coordinate outside the canvas should yield a graceful result (a transparent composite pixel or an error), never a panic.

## Actual behavior

The command panics at `crates/engine/src/commands.rs:830` with `index out of bounds: the len is 0 but the index is 0`.

`int(p, "x").unwrap_or(0) as i32` turns `2147483647` into `i32::MAX`; `Rect::from_xywh(x, y, 1, 1)` saturates `x1` to `x0` (`crates/geom/src/lib.rs:48`), making the rect empty; `photocraft_compose::render` returns `Buffer::transparent` for an empty rect (`crates/compose/src/lib.rs:101-103`), who…

body:

`edit.findAndReplaceText` panics on the `action:"find"`, `"change"` and `"changeFind"` paths when `allLayers:false` selects a layer set that ends up empty: the command filters the type-layer list down to nothing and then indexes `layers[0]` in its search loop.

title: fix(engine): view.newGuideLayout hangs on large columns or rows
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

`view.newGuideLayout` runs one loop iteration per requested column/row with no upper bound and rebuilds its guide list with a linear duplicate scan per insertion.

A single command with a large `columns` or `rows` value, well inside the accepted `u32` range, performs on the order of the square of that count and never returns, blocking the desktop app, the CLI, the MCP server and the TCP control channel. The command should reject or clamp an absurd count before doing the work, as the "Never panic on input" and performance rules require.

## Steps to reproduce

Use the baseline build under Runtime or environment and run the following through any supported entry point (CLI `photocraft-cli run`, MCP server, TCP control channel, or `Session::execute`).

title: fix(engine): file.new eagerly allocates the whole canvas with no memory limit
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

`file.new` clamps `width` and `height` only to `1..=300000` and then creates a document whose background layer is filled across the whole canvas immediately.

A request near that cap, for example 300000x300000, makes a single command attempt to allocate and fill roughly 360 GB of tile memory, so the command does not return and the process can abort. The workspace rule requires rejecting absurd sizes before allocating and capping allocations sized by input; this command does neither.

## Steps to reproduce

Use the baseline build under Runtime or environment and run the following through any supported entry point (CLI `photocraft-cli run`, MCP server, TCP control channel, or `Session::execute`).

```text
file.new {"width": 300000, "height": 300000}
```

No extra state is needed; the failure is in document creation.

## Expected behavior

AGENTS.md requires that input-derived sizes be treated as hostile: "reject absurd sizes before allocating" and "cap allocations sized by input". A creation command must either return `Err` for a size whose backing allocation cannot fit, or create the document without materializing a full-canvas buffer, rather than attempting the allocation. Photoshop also refuses sizes it cannot honor.

## Actual behavior

`file.new` accepts `width`/`height` after clamping each to `1..=300000` (`crates/engine/src/commands.rs:219-229`); `Document::with_background` then fills the background layer across `d.bounds()` at creation (`crates/doc/src/lib.rs:703-711`), and `Surface::fill_rect` materializes every 256x256 tile in that rect (`crates/raster/src/lib.rs:436-450`).

Measured on the baseline build, the cost grows linearly with the pixel count: 1000x1000 about 6 ms, 2000x2000 about 19 ms, 4000x4000 about 75 ms, 8000x8000 about 309 ms (each step is about 4x the work and about 4x the time). title: Crash on opening PSD (Windows, DX12): picks up foreign `dxcompiler.dll` from PATH
author: schliz
body:
(This issue is written by Claude, I didn't read it myself)

## Description

PhotoCraft 0.3.0.0 crashes (APPCRASH) when opening a PSD on Windows with the default DX12 backend. The faulting module is `dxcompiler.dll`, but it was loaded from another application's folder (a Chrome download) rather than from PhotoCraft's install directory or System32.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Install PhotoCraft 0.3.0.0 to `C:\Program Files\PhotoCraft\`.
2. Have a folder containing a different `dxcompiler.dll` reachable (in my case a Chrome folder from Playwright).
3. Open a PSD
4. The app crashes.
## Expected behavior
The PSD opens. The app should not load an unrelated `dxcompiler.dll` from `PATH`, or should fail gracefully.

## Actual behavior
Crash with exception `0xc000041d` in `dxcompiler.dll`.

```
Faulting application: photocraft.exe, version 0.3.0.0, timestamp 0x6ac61def
Faulting module:      dxcompiler.dll, version 1.8.2505.0, timestamp 0x68b1f816
Exception code:       0xc000041d
Fault offset:         0x000000000142ba80
Faulting module path: C:\Users\(redacted)\chrome\win64-140.0.7339.82\chrome-win64\dxcompiler.dll
Faulting app path:    C:\Program Files\PhotoCraft\photocraft.exe
```

## Workaround
Setting `WGPU_BACKEND=vulkan` avoids the crash and the PSD opens normally.

## Suspected cause
PhotoCraft does not appear to ship its own `dxcompiler.dll`/`dxil.dll`, so Windows resolves the DLL via `PATH`/search order and finds an incompatible build. Possible fixes: bundle a known-good DXC next to the exe, load it by explicit path, or fall back to Vulkan/FXC if DXC fails to initialize. (This is my hypothesis, not confirmed.)

title: fix(engine): type.edit with a reversed runs range panics on an integer underflow
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

`type.edit` documents `runs` as `[{"start":char,"end":char,…character keys}]?` (`crates/engine/src/type_cmds.rs:524`). When a run has `end < start`, the command calls `style_range` with `a > b` and `style_range` computes `cb - ca` with `cb < ca`, which underflows. The debug build panics, and the dispatch-level `catch_unwind` turns that into a generic internal error instead of the actionable error the run rule requires; with overflow checks off, the same subtraction wraps into a huge run length that is stored in the text layer.

## Steps to reproduce

Use the baseline build under Runtime or environment and run the following through any supported entry point (CLI `photocraft-cli run`, MCP, TCP control channel, or `Session::execute`). No other state is required.

```text
file.new {"width": 80, "height": 80}
type.create {"x": 0, "y": 40, "text": "Hello world", "size": 20}
type.edit {"layer": <the id returned by type.create>, "runs": [{"start": 5, "end": 2, "fauxBold": true}]}
```

Only the reversed `start`/`end` pair is unusual; the same call with `{"start":2,"end":5}` succeeds. The reproduction is minimized: one text layer, one run, no selection.

## Expected behavior

`runs` is a documented character-range parameter. AGENTS.md rule 9 says a command's `run` closure and everything it calls must return `Err`, never panic, for any params or document state, and every other range parameter in the same file normalises order before use: `range_param` swaps `a.min(b)`/`a.max(b)` (`crates/engine/src/type_cmds.rs:73-83`) and `replace` uses `b.max(a)` (`crates/engine/src/type_cmds.rs:584`). A reversed `runs` range should therefore error or be treated as an empty range, leaving the document unchanged.

The command panics at `crates/engine/src/type_cmds.rs:302` in `push_merge(&mut out, cb - ca, st)`; the caller at `crates/engine/src/type_cmds.rs:586-593` reads `start`/`end` without ordering them, so `ca`/`cb` come from `a.clamp(rs, re)`/`b.clamp(rs, …

title: fix(engine): slice.new and slice.set panic on a large rect coordinate
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

`slice.new` and `slice.set` document `"rect":[x,y,w,h]` with no bound (`crates/engine/src/slice_cmds.rs:455` for `slice.new`; the `slice.set` params string below it). `rect_param` rounds each component to `i32` and then computes `x + w` / `y + h` in `i32` without a checked add (`crates/engine/src/slice_cmds.rs:123-133`). A finite coordinate near `i32::MAX` overflows; the debug build panics and the dispatch guard reports a generic internal error instead of a parameter error.

## Steps to reproduce

Use the baseline build under Runtime or environment and run the following through any supported entry point. No other state is required beyond an open document.

```text
file.new {"width": 24, "height": 16}
slice.new {"rect": [2147483647, 0, 1, 1]}
```

Replacing `2147483647` with any ordinary coordinate (for example `1`) succeeds and creates the slice, so only the magnitude of the coordinate triggers the failure.

## Expected behavior

`rect_param` accepts any finite number and only requires `w`/`h` positive; a value that cannot be represented as a rectangle corner should be refused with `BadParams` (as the sibling `select.*` geometry does), not overflow. AGENTS.md says input-derived lengths, offsets and counts must use `checked_*`/`saturating_*`. The neighbouring code in the same command family already does this in `f64` and only converts at the end (`crates/engine/src/smartselect_cmds.rs:105-113`).

The command panics at `crates/engine/src/slice_cmds.rs:128` with `attempt to add with overflow` (the `v[0] + v[2]` sum). Dispatch catches it, so the observed public result is `Err(Other("`slice.new` failed with an internal error (logged); the document is unchanged"))` rather than a parameter error.

With overflow checks off the add wraps: `x + w` becomes negative, `Rect::new` produces an empty rect, and the command returns the graceful "the slice is outside the canvas" error. I did not execute a release build; only the debug panic is observed.…

title: fix(engine): Migrate Presets edits the library without bumping the preferences revision, so the migration is not saved
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

`edit.presets.migratePresets` appends groups to the preset library, which the crate documents as persisted with the preferences document (`crates/engine/src/presets/mod.rs:17-18`: "User edits persist with the preferences document … saved under `"presets"` by `Session::prefs_to_json`"). Every other preset-mutating path signals persistence with `Session::presets_changed`, which bumps both the preset revision and the preferences revision (`crates/engine/src/presets/mod.rs:165-168`), but `migrate` only increments the preset revision (`crates/engine/src/migrate_cmds.rs:55-58`). The shell's persist loop is gated solely on `session.prefs.rev()` (`crates/ui-egui/src/prefs_ui.rs:255-257`), so a migration is not written to the preferences file until some unrelated preference change happens; quitting before that loses it.

## Steps to reproduce

Use the baseline build under Runtime or environment. Write a presets file that contains at least one group the library does not already have, then run:

```text
edit.presets.migratePresets {"path": "$TMPDIR/merged-presets.json"}
```

The file's contents (a new gradient group) are the only prerequisite:

```json
{"presets": {"gradients": [{"name": "My Imported Set", "items": []}]}}
```

The command reports `{"migrated":1,…}` and the group is added in memory, yet the preferences revision is unchanged, unlike the same change made through a normal preset command.

## Expected behavior

title: fix(engine): edit.keyboardShortcuts clears both commands when one bulk set puts two of them on the same key
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

`edit.keyboardShortcuts` documents `"set":{"<command id>":"<shortcut>"}` with `"removeConflicts":bool=true`, and its own comment states the intent: "Like Photoshop, a shortcut moved to a new command is taken away from the old one" (`crates/engine/src/prefs.rs:1411-1413`). The conflict pass iterates over the whole `set` map against the already-updated preferences for every entry, so when a single call assigns the same key to two commands, each entry blank out the other. The result is that both commands lose their binding and the reported `conflicts` list is empty.

## Steps to reproduce

Use the baseline build under Runtime or environment and run one command through any supported entry point:

```text

```

`edit.undo`'s default is already `Cmd+Z`, so only `edit.fill` is new; the observable outcome is that neither command keeps the key. Assigning the same key in two separate calls (second call clears the first, as documented) behaves differently, which isolates the bulk-set path.

## Expected behavior

The documented behaviour is that a shortcut moved to a new command is taken away from the old one, leaving one owner for the key; alternatively the clash is reported in `conflicts` so the user can resolve it. Either way a bulk `set` that names the same key twice must not silently leave both commands unbound, and `conflicts` must not be empty for a clash inside the call.

After the call, `prefs().shortcuts["edit.undo"]` and `prefs().shortcuts["edit.fill"]` are both the empty string (which `Preferences::shortcut` maps to "no binding", `crates/engine/src/prefs.rs:1067-1073`), and the command's returned `conflicts` array is empty. title: fix(io): PSD export drops lspf bit 3 and writes the artboard lock as bit 4
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

PhotoCraft maps a layer's PSD protection block `lspf` in `crates/io/src/blocks.rs`, and that mapping reads the artboard lock from bit 4 (`0x10`) while ignoring bit 3 (`0x08`), and it writes the artboard lock back to bit 4. Photoshop stores the artboard lock in bit 3, so a layer whose stored `lspf` sets bit 3 loses that bit when the document is saved again, and a lock the user sets in PhotoCraft is written as a bit Photoshop does not use. A document that opens with that lock no longer carries it after a save-and-reopen round trip.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open a PSD whose layer protection is `0x0000000D` (bits 0, 2 and 3, the value Photoshop writes for a Background layer) and save it to PSD again with no edits.
2. Read the layer's `lspf` block from the output and compare it with the input.
3. A layer locked with Lock All changes the same way: `0x80000000` is written back as `0x80000001`, and any value with bit 3 set loses only that bit.

Runtime reproduction was not executed in this investigation; the failure is a static proof from the two masked expressions below and their only two call sites.

## Expected behavior

The protection mapping must keep the bit Photoshop uses. `crates/doc/src/lib.rs:81` gives `Locks` a dedicated `artboard` field, so the `lspf` bit that carries that lock must be read into `Locks::artboard` and written back from it. The Adobe PSD specification ("Layer records", layer protection flags) defines bit 3 as the artboard lock, so an untouched document must round-trip its `lspf` bytes unchanged.

## Actual behavior

`crates/io/src/blocks.rs:52` decodes `artboard: v & 0x10 != 0` and `crates/io/src/blocks.rs:57` encodes `u32::from(l.artboard) << 4`, so bit 3 is never read and never written.

- An input `lspf` of `0x0000000D` decodes to transparency and position only, and the export path `crates/io/src/psd_export.rs:342` writes `0x00000005`: bit 3 is dropped.
- An input `lspf` of `0x80000000` whose record also sets the transparency-prot…

title: fix(io): artboard guide indices are numbered horizontal-first while the guide resource is written vertical-first
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

`crates/io/src/comps_map.rs` computes an artboard's `guideIndeces` through `guides_in`, which numbers a document's guides horizontal-first and then vertical, while `crates/io/src/psd_export.rs` writes image resource 1032 vertical-first and then horizontal. For a document with guides of both orientations the indices the artboard stores name different guides than the ones `guides_in` selected, so the exported artboard is associated with the wrong guides when Photoshop opens the file.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Build a document with one vertical guide and one horizontal guide, and give it an artboard whose rectangle contains the horizontal guide but not the vertical one.
2. Export it to PSD and read the artboard's `artb` block together with image resource 1032.

## Expected behavior

The artboard's `guideIndeces` must name the guides inside its rectangle in resource 1032's own order, so for that case it must be the horizontal guide's index, which is 1 because the resource stores the vertical guide at index 0 and the horizontal guide at index 1. `crates/io/src/comps_map.rs:105-111` documents `guides_in` as the indices of the document guides that lie inside the rectangle, and `crates/io/src/comps_map.rs:98` stores them as the board's `guideIndeces`, so both must use one order.

## Actual behavior

`crates/io/src/comps_map.rs:110` builds `h.chain(v).enumerate()`, which numbers the horizontal guides first and the vertical guides after them, while `crates/io/src/psd_export.rs:869` writes the resource with `[(&doc.guides.vertical, 0u8), (&doc.guides.horizontal, 1u8)]`, which puts the vertical guides first. With one vertical and one horizontal guide, `guides_in` returns 0 for the horizontal guide, so the exported `guideIndeces` is `[0]`, the index of the vertical guide in the resource.

Runtime reproduction was not run. The proof is static: the two orders above disagree whenever both guide lists are non-empty, and the one-vertical/one-horizontal case fixes the wro…

title: fix(io): PSD import allocates a layer surface from the file's rectangle before reading pixels
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

`crates/io/src/psd_import.rs` builds a layer's interleaved pixel buffer with `crates/io/src/pixels.rs` `interleave`, sized by the layer record's rectangle, and the only bound on that rectangle is the PSD parser's 300000-pixel-per-side limit. A layer record declaring a 300000 by 300000 rectangle needs 300000 * 300000 * 4 bytes (about 360 GB at 8 bits per channel with alpha) from a file whose channel data may be empty, so a few-hundred-byte malformed PSD aborts the process on allocation failure instead of reporting an error. The export path already bounds its own buffers with a checked reservation, so this is limited to the import side.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Craft a PSD with a valid small header and one raster layer whose rectangle is top 0, left 0, bottom 300000, right 300000, with three channels whose declared data lengths are zero or absent.
2. Open it through any supported entry point, for example `photocraft-cli info` or a file open.

## Expected behavior

The import must refuse a layer whose declared rectangle it cannot justify from the input, or size the buffer by the bytes actually present, and return an error. `AGENTS.md` requires input-derived sizes to be capped before allocating, and the crate already applies that rule where it can: `crates/io/src/flat.rs:218` `try_buffer` turns an allocation failure into `IoError::Unsupported` on the export side, and `crates/psd/src/compression.rs:15` caps one decode at 2 GiB on the parser side.

## Actual behavior

`record_surface` (`crates/io/src/psd_import.rs:118`) accepts any layer rectangle that passes `Rect::size()` (at most 300000 per side, `crates/psd/src/layer.rs:58`) and calls `interleave` with `n = w * h`. `crates/io/src/pixels.rs:44` then allocates `vec![0u8; n * ch * bps]` before any channel data is read, where `ch` is the channel count and `bps` the bytes per sample. For the crafted file that is 300000 * 300000 * 4 bytes, about 360 GB, and the allocation failure aborts the process; Rust abort…

title: fix(ui-egui): GPU canvas tests report a setup-command failure as "no GPU adapter" and skip green
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

`crates/ui-egui/tests/canvas_16f.rs` and `crates/ui-egui/tests/color_managed_canvas.rs` build the app inside `std::panic::catch_unwind` and run their setup commands with `.expect(...)` in that same closure. The harness runs the builder closure synchronously inside the `catch_unwind`, so any panic from a setup command (or from app construction) is caught and labelled `"skipping: no GPU adapter"`, and the test returns success. Those tests therefore cannot fail for a regression in the commands they exist to verify; they skip green instead.

## Steps to reproduce

This is a static proof of the control flow; runtime reproduction was not run. The mechanism is:

1. `crates/ui-egui/tests/canvas_16f.rs:189` opens `std::panic::catch_unwind(...)` around the harness builder; line `190` calls `.wgpu().build_eframe(move |cc| { ... })`; lines `198-200` run the setup commands with `app.run(&id, p).expect("setup command")`. Lines `204-207` do `let Ok(mut harness) = built else { eprintln!("skipping: no GPU adapter"); return None; };`.
2. `crates/ui-egui/tests/color_managed_canvas.rs:20` does the same; lines `30-32` run `file.new`, `edit.assignProfile` and `edit.fill` with `.expect("new")` / `.expect("assign")` / `.expect("fill")`; lines `40-43` catch and print `"skipping: no GPU adapter"`.
3. `egui_kittest`'s `build_eframe` calls the user closure synchronously before returning: `let app = build(&mut cc);` (`egui_kittest-0.36.2/src/builder.rs`, in `HarnessBuilder::build_eframe`), which is inside the caller's `catch_unwind`.
4. `PhotocraftApp::run` returns `Result<Value, String>` (`crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs:501`), so `.expect(...)` on a command that returns `Err` panics and unwinds into the `catch_unwind`.

A regression that makes any of those commands return `Err` (for example `view.thirtyTwoBitPreviewOptions`, `edit.assignProfile`, or `edit.fill`) is therefore caught, printed as a missing GPU, and the test passes.

title: Locking a group doesn't lock its children (no "Lock All Layers in Group
author: Joather
body:
### What happens
When I lock a layer group (any lock: all, position, pixels…), the lock is only applied to the
group itself. The layers inside it stay unlocked, so I can still move or paint on them.
To protect a whole group I have to lock every child layer one by one.

Also, the lock buttons in the Layers panel (`Lock:` bar) only apply to the **active** layer,
even when several layers are selected. `Layer › Lock Layers…` does apply to the whole
selection, so that's the current workaround (expand the group, Shift-click first → last child,
then Layer › Lock Layers…).

### Expected (Photoshop behaviour)
- Locking a group locks its contents: children show an inherited (hollow) lock and can't be
  moved/painted while the group is locked.
- With a group selected, `Layer › Lock Layers…` becomes **Lock All Layers in Group…**.
- Layers added to a locked group later are covered by the group's lock too.
- The panel lock buttons apply to every selected layer.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Create a group with 2+ layers.
2. Select the group and click "Lock all" in the Layers panel.
3. Select a layer inside the group and drag it with the Move tool → it moves.

### Notes from the code
Locks seem to be checked only on the layer itself, never on its parent groups:
- `crates/engine/src/layer_multi_cmds.rs` → `lock_layers()` sets locks on the selected IDs only;
  `move_layers()` checks `l.locks.position || l.locks.all` on the layer alone.
- `crates/engine/src/commands.rs` → `paint_surface()` checks `l.locks.pixels || l.locks.all`
  on the layer alone.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/panels.rs` → the lock buttons emit `layer.setProps` for `l.id` (active layer).

An "effective locks" helper that ORs a layer's locks with all its ancestors' would probably
cover move, paint and transform in one place.

### Environment
- PhotoCraft: v0.3.0 (AppImage)
- OS: Arch Linux, KDE Plasma

Standard dialog buttons like Yes/No and Ok/Cancel are being shown with Mac button order even though I'm using Windows, which makes it feel somewhat alien. I think the program should respect the button order of the OS it is being used it.

For instance the "Unsaved changes" dialog has buttons "Don't save", "Cancel", "Save". In Windows you would have the default action (Save) first in left-to-right reading order. Here are some other examples:

Windows: [ Ok ] [ Cancel ]
KDE: [ Ok ] [ Cancel ]
Mac: [ Cancel ] [ Ok ]

title: fix(automation): `image.applyDataSet` is denied unconditionally, so text and visibility data sets cannot be applied over automation
author: Wynnde
body:
﻿## Summary

`image.applyDataSet` is a hardcoded arm of the ambient-path deny list in `authorize_engine_command` (`crates/automation/src/workspace.rs:181`), so it is refused for every call regardless of its parameters or of what the active data sets contain. A data set whose values are only `text` and `visibility` resolves no host path at all, yet it is refused with `automation command 'image.applyDataSet' uses ambient filesystem paths and is disabled; use capability-scoped document methods`.

The advice in that message cannot be followed, because there is no capability-scoped method for variables. The headless server's `methods` reply is `engine.execute`, `jobs.list`, `jobs.cancel`, `engine.commands`, `session.list`, `doc.open`, `doc.new`, `doc.save`, `doc.inspect`, `doc.render`, `doc.select`, `doc.close`, `batch`, `methods`. The net effect is that Image > Variables is reachable over automation right up to the point of use: `image.variables.define` and `image.variables.dataSets` both succeed and `variables.list` confirms the state, but nothing can ever be applied.

This is deliberately a narrow report. `file.import.variableDataSets` and `file.export.dataSetsAsFiles` are *not* in the hardcoded list; they are caught by `params_contain_ambient_path` because they really do take `path` and `dir` arguments, and refusing them is correct. Only the unconditional arm for `image.applyDataSet` looks wrong.

I am also aware this pushes against #676, which argues the same gate is too permissive elsewhere. The two are compatible: #676 wants commands that resolve host paths to be covered, and this asks that a command be judged on whether it actually resolves one. The suggested fix below keeps the pixel-replacement case denied.

## Steps to reproduce

Against a session with both roots granted to one directory:

```
photocraft-cli serve --automation-read-root <dir> --automation-write-root <dir>
```

// -> {"ok…

title: macOS menu is nested in window instead
author: brennanMKE
body:
# Use the native macOS menu bar instead of the in-window menus

## Summary

On macOS, PhotoCraft draws its menus inside the window, under the title bar. The menu bar at the
top of the screen only has winit's default menu. Mac users look for menus at the top of the
screen, and macOS features that rely on the real menu bar don't work with the in-window one:

- VoiceOver can't read the menus.
- The Help menu's search field can't find commands.
- App Shortcuts in System Settings › Keyboard can't rebind them.
- There's no app menu (About, Settings, Services, Hide, Quit) and no Window menu.

The in-window bar has also been the source of several bugs. In #92 (and its duplicate #319), a tall
submenu slid up over the menu titles, and moving the pointer inside it opened a different menu.
#402 reports menus running past the window on macOS Tahoe, with a request to make them scroll. A
native menu leaves layout, scrolling and hover to AppKit.

## Proposal

On macOS, build a native menu bar (with [muda](https://github.com/tauri-apps/muda)) from the same
data the in-window bar uses (`menu_items`). Keep the in-window bar on Linux and Windows, and as an
option on macOS.

The native menu should follow the macOS layout:

- **App menu "PhotoCraft"**: About PhotoCraft (moved from Help), Settings… ⌘, (moved from
