title: Save for Web silently overwrites slices with the same file name
body:
Two slices with the same name export to the same path, so the second replaces the first. Names that sanitize to the same string (`a/b` and `a?b`) collide too.

Suggested reproduction: create a 100 × 100 document with two non-overlapping user slices named `tile`; run `file.export.saveForWebLegacy` with `{"dir":"<temporary export folder>","format":"png","slices":"user","html":true}`. Both entries use `images/tile.png`, and both HTML cells use the second image.

Please make output names unique or reject collisions before writing. HTML export should also reserve `spacer.gif`.

Source review at `1ea96cb2883811256ba4dc19d15bcb5cca1551a8`; I have not run the app. [Naming and writes](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/1ea96cb2883811256ba4dc19d15bcb5cca1551a8/crates/engine/src/web_cmds.rs#L765).

title: Save for Web HTML drops a later slice when slices overlap
body:
The HTML table discards a whole slice if any of its grid cells overlap an earlier slice. This loses the later slice's link, text and image even where it extends outside the earlier one.

Suggested reproduction: create a 100 × 100 document with slices `[0,0,60,60]` and `[40,40,60,60]`; give the second a distinct link and export all slices with HTML. The second image is written, but its table cell is skipped.

Please resolve overlaps before building the table. The resolver describes later slices covering earlier ones, while the table gives earlier slices precedence.

Source review at `1ea96cb2883811256ba4dc19d15bcb5cca1551a8`; not run in the app. [Resolver](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/1ea96cb2883811256ba4dc19d15bcb5cca1551a8/crates/doc/src/slices.rs#L171) · [HTML overlap check](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/1ea96cb2883811256ba4dc19d15bcb5cca1551a8/crates/engine/src/web_cmds.rs#L659).

title: Rejected Slice Options can still change the document
body:
`slice.set` can return an error after committing an edit.

Suggested reproduction on a new 120 × 90 document: run `slice.set {"number":1,"kind":"bogus"}`, then inspect slices and history. The auto slice is promoted before the invalid kind is checked. A user slice set to rect `[500,500,10,10]` is likewise committed before the command returns “slice is off the canvas”.

An unsuccessful command should leave the document and history unchanged. Please validate the complete options and resolved result before promoting or committing.

Source review at `1ea96cb2883811256ba4dc19d15bcb5cca1551a8`; these examples were not executed. [Target promotion](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/1ea96cb2883811256ba4dc19d15bcb5cca1551a8/crates/engine/src/slice_cmds.rs#L199) · [Later validation](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/1ea96cb2883811256ba4dc19d15bcb5cca1551a8/crates/engine/src/slice_cmds.rs#L295).

title: Dividing an auto slice takes two undos
body:
`slice.divide` promotes an auto slice and divides it in separate history steps. One undo restores a user slice rather than the original auto slice.

Suggested reproduction: create a 120 × 90 document without user slices; run `slice.divide {"number":1,"vertical":2}`, then undo once. The division is undone, but “Promote to User Slice” remains.

The command should be one history step, so one undo restores the original state. Promotion also remains if division is rejected because there are too many pieces.

Source review at `1ea96cb2883811256ba4dc19d15bcb5cca1551a8`; not run locally. [Target](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/1ea96cb2883811256ba4dc19d15bcb5cca1551a8/crates/engine/src/slice_cmds.rs#L199) records promotion; [divide](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/1ea96cb2883811256ba4dc19d15bcb5cca1551a8/crates/engine/src/slice_cmds.rs#L364) records division separately.

title: Slice Options merges into an earlier explicit Promote action
body:
`slice.set` merges into a promotion by checking only the last undo label and whether `number` is present. It does not check whether the current command actually promoted a slice.

Suggested reproduction: create a document; run `slice.promote {"number":1}`, then `slice.set {"number":1,"name":"renamed"}`, then undo once. The rename and earlier explicit promotion disappear together.

These separate actions should be independently undoable. Please coalesce only a promotion performed inside the current Slice Options command.

Source review at `1ea96cb2883811256ba4dc19d15bcb5cca1551a8`; no runtime reproduction. [Condition and document replacement](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/1ea96cb2883811256ba4dc19d15bcb5cca1551a8/crates/engine/src/slice_cmds.rs#L301).

title: Request: a private channel for security reports
author: coygeek
body:
We have a set of security-relevant findings for PhotoCraft, checked against `main` at `52ccb8a`, that we would rather not describe in public. `SECURITY.md` asks reporters to request a private transfer method first, and GitHub private vulnerability reporting is currently disabled for this repository.

Could you either enable private vulnerability reporting (Settings → Code security → Private vulnerability reporting) or name a private address we can use? Once a channel exists, we will send each finding separately, with source locations and suggested fixes.

The findings are in file import and document loading, the automation control surface, and the release signing workflows. Several items that came up during the same review have already been fixed on `main`, and those are not included. Nothing further is described here.

title: Out-of-range slice and layer-comp IDs can target an existing item
body:
Numeric IDs are narrowed to `u32` without checking the range. An ID such as `4294967297` becomes `1`, so an invalid request can delete or rename a real item.

Suggested reproduction: create a user slice with ID 1, then run `slice.delete {"slice":4294967297}`. The lookup targets slice 1. The `slices` array has the same problem. Layer comps also accept the wrapped value in `comp_param` and the export `comps` array.

Please reject numeric IDs above `u32::MAX` rather than wrapping them. Verify that the error leaves the original items unchanged.

Source review of main at `1ea96cb2883811256ba4dc19d15bcb5cca1551a8`; not executed locally. Evidence: [single slice ID](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/1ea96cb2883811256ba4dc19d15bcb5cca1551a8/crates/engine/src/slice_cmds.rs#L199), [slice ID array](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/1ea96cb2883811256ba4dc19d15bcb5cca1551a8/crates/engine/src/slice_cmds.rs#L342), [comp ID](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/1ea96cb2883811256ba4dc19d15bcb5cca1551a8/crates/engine/src/comps_cmds.rs#L41). Existing #685 concerns allocating IDs, rather than accepting an out-of-range command target; “comp id” searches found no matching report.

title: fix(algo): Vanishing Point clone footprint overflows i32 for a far clone point
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

`filter.vanishingPoint` with a `clone` stroke whose later point lies far outside the plane overflows `i32` in `clone_stroke` (`crates/algo/src/vanishing.rs:263`). The command parses clone `source` and `points` as `f64` pairs with no coordinate bound (`crates/engine/src/vp_cmds.rs:152-153`), and `clone_stroke` checks plane membership only for the source and the first destination point (`crates/algo/src/vanishing.rs:265`). For each later point it builds an image-space footprint with `Rect::new(bb[0].floor() as i32, bb[1].floor() as i32, bb[2].ceil() as i32 + 1, bb[3].ceil() as i32 + 1)` at `crates/algo/src/vanishing.rs:292`, before the empty/4096-size guard on line 293. For a far x coordinate, `bb[2].ceil() as i32` saturates to `i32::MAX` and the `+ 1` overflows. With overflow checks on (the default debug/test profile), this panics; the dispatch guard catches the panic and the command fails with a generic internal error, leaving the document unchanged. With overflow checks off (the default native release profile), the source indicates that the addition wraps and the far dab is skipped.

## Steps to reproduce

Run these three commands through the engine's command dispatch on the baseline stated under Runtime or environment, with overflow checks on (an engine integration test under `cargo test -p photocraft-engine`):

```text
file.new {"width":24,"height":24}
layer.new.layer {}
filter.vanishingPoint {"planes":[{"corners":[[0,0],[400,0],[400,300],[0,300]]}],"clone":[{"source":[200,150],"points":[[200,150],[3000000000,150]],"size":12}]}
```

The source and the first destination point, both `[200,150]`, lie inside the plane, so the plane membership, frame and inverse checks pass. The second point `[3000000000,150]` reaches the footprint construction with no membership or coordinate check.

title: fix(ui): the brush stroke-preview cache ignores spacing_enabled, so toggling Spacing leaves a stale preview
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

`brush_preview::preview_sig` hashes the brush fields that change the S-curve stroke strip, but omits `spacing_enabled`, which does change the rendered dabs. With it checked, the engine spaces dabs by the configured `spacing` fraction (10% by default) of the pressure-dependent diameter, subject to minimum step lengths; with it unchecked, the pointer's speed sets the spacing, and the preview's untimed points produce one dab per moving input segment. Once the Brush Settings strip has been rendered, toggling the "Spacing" checkbox (or setting `spacingEnabled` through `tools.setBrush`) reuses the cached texture, so the strip keeps showing the previous spacing until another hashed input changes. The module's own documentation states that a preview re-renders when something that changes it changes. The brush setting itself updates; only the informational preview is stale.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Use the baseline stated under Runtime or environment. In a headless integration test in `crates/ui-egui/tests/`, create a session with `Session::new` and execute `tools.setBrush` with `{"reset":true,"brush":{"size":6.0,"spacingEnabled":true}}`. 2. Render that brush through `brush_preview::stroke_texture` for one slot, theme color and size, so the slot is cached. Do this at 488×76, the live Brush Settings strip size, and separately at 220×60.

4. Call `stroke_texture` again with the same slot, dimensions and color. Record the texture ID and `brush_preview::render_count`, and compare `preview_sig` and fresh `preview_pixels` for the two brushes.

title: fix(engine): filter.filterGallery allocates a read window sized by the summed effect reach
author: coygeek
body:
## Runtime or environment

Baseline: storytold/photocraft at commit `d7df9d8aa6de4763ab587af7c01ee64b1f368409`. The failure source is still present on `main` at `52ccb8a`; the line locators below refer to that `main` revision. The missing bound is established from source; reduced read-window sizes were measured on the baseline, and the large case was calculated, not executed.

## Summary

`filter.filterGallery` accepts an `effects` list with no bound on its length or on its total reach, and the filter's halo is the sum of every effect's reach. The command clips its output to the union of the canvas and the layer's content bounds, which is the canvas for the populated 64x64 layer used here, but it still reads each output tile's source window inflated by the full summed halo and materialises that window as one dense float buffer with no byte budget. A parameter of about 5 KB with 100 maximum-`cellSize` `stainedGlass` effects therefore asks for a single source window of 26,980,033,536 bytes on a 64x64 layer, instead of the command returning `Err` for a size it cannot serve. Whether such a request then fails to allocate or runs for an unacceptable time depends on the machine's resources; neither outcome was observed.

title: fix(engine): filter.liquify runs an impractically long loop on a stroke segment whose points are far apart
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary
`filter.liquify` validates each stroke's brush size and point values but not the distance between points. `LiquifyStroke::validate` (`crates/algo/src/liquify.rs:142-153`) accepts any finite coordinates, and `stroke_segment` turns the segment length into a dab count with `let steps = (len / spacing).ceil().max(1.0) as usize;` and `for k in 1..=steps` (`crates/algo/src/liquify.rs:322-323`). A segment between two far-apart points therefore produces about 3.3 × 10¹⁴ dabs in a finite loop with no deadline or cancellation check, so the command would not return in any practical time and would block its caller. This is established from source; the extreme input was not run. It conflicts with the project's requirement that a command return `Err`, never panic or hang, for any params.

## Steps to reproduce
Prerequisite: a document with a pixel layer (the command's `enabled` check, `has_filterable_layer`, admits a raster layer). No build flags are needed. The baseline is stated under Runtime or environment.

1. Request a single forward-warp stroke whose two points are far apart (not executed; see Actual behavior):

```json
{"strokes": [{"tool": "forwardWarp", "size": 30, "points": [[0, 0], [1e15, 0]]}]}
```

2. Sending this as `filter.liquify` passes every guard: `Session::execute` dispatches synchronously after checking the params shape, enabled state and job conflicts (`crates/engine/src/jobs.rs:590-615`); `liquify_params` deserializes and validates the strokes and uses `auto_cell` when `meshSize` is absent (`crates/engine/src/distort_cmds.rs:41-60`); `validate` accepts `size` 30 (within 1..15000) and the finite two-element points.

title: fix(format): a .pcraft tile at an extreme coordinate overflows on layer bounds
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

The `.pcraft` loader accepts a manifest whose surface tiles sit at any `i32` coordinate and never checks that the coordinate can be turned back into a rectangle. `TileCoord::rect()` computes `tx * TILE_SIZE` and `ty * TILE_SIZE` with unchecked `i32` multiplication (`crates/geom/src/lib.rs`), which is representable only for tile indices from -8,388,608 through 8,388,607 inclusive. This range describes representable origins; at the upper endpoint the full half-open tile rectangle's far edge exceeds `i32::MAX`, and `Rect::from_xywh` currently saturates that edge. A tile index outside that range overflows: with Cargo's default dev/test profile the multiplication panics with `attempt to multiply with overflow`, and with the default release profile it wraps, so the bounds query returns a rectangle that does not describe where the tile is stored. `photocraft_io::import` returns `Ok` for the malformed bundle, so the failure surfaces later, on ordinary paths that ask for a layer's bounds: the status bar's document-size calculation, the Properties controls, `edit.transform`'s default source frame, and the compositor's content-bounds helper. This is reachable from any `.pcraft` file the app is asked to open, including a damaged one, and the loader's `LoadOptions` limits do not cover tile coordinates.

author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

`photocraft-io` reads a PSD `Anno` block's note icon rectangle as four signed `i32`s and copies the icon's left and top into `Note::position` without a range check (`crates/io/src/annotations_map.rs:146-161`). In the default release profile the addition wraps, and when the `Anno` block is regenerated the saved note gets a wrapped icon coordinate. `export_blocks` builds the regenerated comparison block on every PSD save, so importing and re-saving the file is enough to reach the overflow; no edit to the note is needed.

In an overflow-checked build (the default dev and test profiles) the command's `run` closure panics instead of returning `Err`; the native dispatch guard catches the panic and reports an internal error. With overflow checks off (the default release profile) the addition wraps and the command reports success without changing the gradient. title: fix(engine): image.crop accepts an unbounded document size, so a following image.trim aborts the process on allocation
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

`image.crop` sets the document size from the requested explicit rectangle with no upper bound on its dimensions or area. A crop far larger than the canvas returns success and leaves a document with an enormous `size`. A following command that flattens the whole canvas, such as `image.trim` or `image.duplicate` with `mergedOnly`, then makes an infallible allocation of 16 bytes per canvas pixel; when that allocation cannot be satisfied, Rust's default allocation-error handling aborts the process, which the dispatch guard's `catch_unwind` cannot turn into an error. This is established from source; the oversized allocation was not run in verification.

## Steps to reproduce

Baseline as stated under Runtime or environment, on a 64-bit target. Through the headless CLI:

```sh
photocraft-cli run --new '{"width":8,"height":8}' \
  --cmd image.crop --params '{"x":0,"y":0,"width":100000000,"height":100000000}' \
  --cmd image.trim --params '{"basedOn":"transparent"}'
```

`--cmd image.duplicate --params '{"mergedOnly":true}'` as the second command reaches the same full-canvas flatten (confirmed from source).

## Expected behavior

`AGENTS.md` section 3 (Never crash) covers bad command and automation parameters: it requires an actionable error, caps on allocations sized by input, and checked arithmetic; rule 9 requires a command's `run` closure and its callees to reject absurd sizes before allocating. `image.crop` should therefore reject a rectangle with absurd dimensions with an error before changing the document, so that no later command is asked to allocate the resulting canvas. Extending a crop beyond the existing canvas is supported (the comment in the crop branch and the test `crop_to_explicit_rect_can_extend_canvas`) and must keep working at reasonable dimensions. The sibling size commands clamp each side to 300,000 pixels (`file.new` at `crates/engine/src/commands.rs:224`, `image.imageSize` at `crates/engine/src/image_cmds.rs:117`, `image.canvasSize` at `c…

title: fix(cms): absolute-colorimetric transforms divide by a zero media white from a malformed ICC profile
author: coygeek
body:
## Runtime or environment

PhotoCraft at baseline commit `d7df9d8aa6de4763ab587af7c01ee64b1f368409`, tested with `cargo test -p photocraft-cms`. The failure source is still present on `main` at `52ccb8a800942991abe55c0ab9c677a278a4e39a`, unchanged at `crates/cms/src/transform.rs:587` (division) and `crates/cms/src/profile.rs:474-488` (`wtpt` parsing).

## Summary

`connection()` scales the PCS by `src.media_white() / dst.media_white()` for the absolute colorimetric intent and never checks that the divisor is nonzero or that the result is finite. An otherwise valid v4 ICC profile whose `wtpt` tag holds a malformed zero media white parses successfully and returns that white verbatim, so both a direct absolute transform and a soft-proof transform built from it produce `[NaN, NaN, NaN]`. The supported `view.proofSetup` command accepts such a profile file with the absolute intent, and enabling Proof Colors then builds the proof transform from it. v2 display profiles are not affected, because `media_white` substitutes D50 for them.

## Steps to reproduce

Parsed-file fixture, as run at the baseline: start from the bytes of `Builtin::Srgb.profile().to_bytes()` (a v4 display profile); read the big-endian tag count at byte 128; walk the 12-byte tag records starting at byte 132 to the `wtpt` record; read its big-endian data offset from record bytes 4-7; confirm the data starts with `XYZ `; set data bytes offset + 8 through offset + 19 (the three XYZ values) to zero; and call `Profile::parse` on the result. Then build `Transform::new(&srgb, &parsed, Intent::AbsoluteColorimetric, false)` and `Transform::proof(&srgb, &parsed, &srgb, Intent::AbsoluteColorimetric, true, false)`, and evaluate `[0.2, 0.4, 0.6]` with each.

The connection arithmetic can also be pinned without a file, by setting the destination model's white directly:

#[test]

title: fix(paint): retouch tools emit an unbounded number of dabs for a far-apart stroke segment
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary
The retouching commands parse their stroke `points` without the coordinate bound the painting commands enforce, and `photocraft-paint`'s path walker then emits one dab per spacing step with no count, deadline or allocation cap. A Dodge stroke whose segment joins two far-apart finite points therefore starts excessive, uncapped work and keeps growing allocations instead of returning a bad-params error; for an extreme coordinate this can end in resource failure. The complete supported witness is `paint.dodge` on an unlocked raster layer. The other retouch commands (Burn, Sponge, Blur, Sharpen, Smudge, Clone Stamp, Healing Brush, Spot Healing, History Brush) share the same `points` parser, but some take a different coverage path and the clone and history tools have extra source or state preconditions, so the identical minimal request has not been verified for each of them.

## Steps to reproduce
Prerequisite: an open document whose active layer is an unlocked raster layer, with the composite channel targeted and no conflicting background job. The baseline is stated under Runtime or environment. The extreme request below was not executed; the failure is established from source.

1. Send `paint.dodge` with two points far apart:

```json
{"points": [[0, 0], [1e300, 0]]}
```

2. `parse_brush` (`crates/engine/src/retouch_cmds.rs:68-101`) reads `points[i][0]` and `points[i][1]` straight into `StrokePoint::new` at line 76, with no finiteness or magnitude check. Contrast `parse_points` for the painting tools, which rejects any coordinate outside ±1,000,000 (`crates/engine/src/brush_cmds.rs:50-79`) because "an absurd coordinate would mean billions of dabs".
3. `dodge_burn_cmd` (`crates/engine/src/retouch_cmds.rs:501-513`) enters `run_stroke` and calls `apply_dab_stroke`, which builds the dabs with `dabs(stroke)` (`crates/paint/src/retouch.rs:225-239`) before computing bounds or reading pixels.

title: fix(text): EngineData writes a bare "." for a tiny non-zero real, producing unparseable PSD text
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary
`format_real` formats a real with five decimals, strips trailing zeros and then strips the leading `0.`, which for a tiny non-zero value such as `4e-6` leaves the single character `.` (and `-.` for the negative side). Type-layer style values such as baseline shift are written through this function into the PSD `TySh` EngineData, so a type layer carrying such a value produces an EngineData block that PhotoCraft's own parser rejects as a whole. On readback PhotoCraft falls back to the descriptor's plain text with default styling: the text string and the layer survive, but character and paragraph styling carried only in EngineData is lost.

## Steps to reproduce
Prerequisite: an open document at 72 DPI with an existing text layer. The baseline is stated under Runtime or environment. Steps 1-2 are traced from source and were not executed end to end; the serialization and readback were executed (see Runtime or environment).

1. Set a tiny non-zero baseline shift on the whole layer with `type.setStyle {"baselineShift": 0.000004}`, or on a run with `type.edit {"runs":[{"start":0,"end":2,"baselineShift":0.000004}]}` on a two-character layer. `type.setStyle` advertises `baselineShift` (`CHAR_PARAMS`, `crates/engine/src/type_cmds.rs:481`) and applies it through `apply_char_props` (lines 663-671); the setter stores it unclamped (lines 159-163). Both commands regenerate the layer's stored TySh through `with_text_layer` and `refresh` (lines 381-400).
2. Export the document as PSD. The text writer emits `("BaselineShift".into(), real(s.baseline_shift_pt / k))` (`crates/text/src/psd.rs:584`; at 72 DPI `k` is 1), `build_tysh` writes the generated EngineData (line 848), and PSD export uses that TySh (`crates/io/src/psd_export.rs:442-449`) with no parseability check.
3. `ed::write` formats the value with `format_real` (`crates/text/src/engine_data.rs:293`), so the EngineData contains the token `/BaselineShift .`.

title: fix(ui): ui.click count is unclamped and grows the pending synthetic-input queue without bound
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary
`ui.click {count}` uses `count` directly as a loop bound and synchronously pushes a press and a release `egui::Event` into the pending synthetic-input queue per iteration, after one initial pointer move, with no upper bound or allocation budget (`crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs:466-485`). One small request therefore materializes `1 + 2 * count` events on the UI thread before the handler returns. At 72 bytes per event on the tested native build, `count: 1000000000` would need 144,000,000,072 bytes (over 134 GiB) of event payload before vector spare capacity, which can freeze or terminate the application instead of producing an actionable error; the extreme outcome was not executed. The method is reachable from an authenticated desktop control connection and from MCP `control_call` in bridge mode, which forwards raw params.

## Steps to reproduce
Prerequisite: the app running with `--control`, and either a TCP control connection that has completed the required `auth` request first, or an MCP server in bridge mode configured with the control token. The baseline is stated under Runtime or environment. The extreme request was not executed; its outcome is established from source.

1. After authenticating, send one `ui.click` request with a large `count`, directly or through MCP `control_call`:

```json
{"method": "ui.click", "params": {"x": 100, "y": 100, "count": 1000000000}}
```

2. The request is a few dozen bytes, so the transport's request-size ceilings do not bound it, and the queue growth happens synchronously inside `control::handle` before the reply waiter is recorded.

A bounded check was executed instead (see Actual behavior).

## Expected behavior
AGENTS.md section 3, "Never crash", covers bad command and MCP params and requires allocations sized by input to be capped, and Rule 9 requires rejecting absurd sizes before allocating; the general rule applies to this UI control handler even though it is outside an engine command's `run`. `ui.click {x, y, b…

title: fix(prefs): prefs.set and prefs.reset change colorSettings without applying the text gamma to the compositor
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary
The `colorSettings.blendTextGamma` preference drives an application-wide compositor gamma (`photocraft_compose::psblend::set_text_gamma`) used to blend type-layer edges. The dedicated `edit.colorSettings` command and preference loading apply it, but `prefs.set` and `prefs.reset` with a `colorSettings` path or a full reset only store the value. The compositor keeps the previous gamma, so type layers are blended with a gamma that disagrees with what `prefs.get` reports and what the preferences serialize, until an actual color-settings change or a preference reload applies it. Direct engine callers and the trusted-local CLI are affected.

## Steps to reproduce
Prerequisite: a fresh engine `Session` (direct `Session::execute`, or the CLI, which runs commands in trusted-local mode). The baseline is stated under Runtime or environment. These steps were not executed; the resulting states are deduced from source.

1. `edit.colorSettings {"blendTextGamma": 1.8}`: stored gamma 1.8, compositor gamma 1.8.
2. `prefs.set {"path": "colorSettings.blendTextGamma", "value": 1.0}`: stored gamma 1.0, compositor gamma still 1.8.
3. `prefs.reset {"path": "colorSettings.blendTextGamma"}`: stored gamma returns to the default 1.45, compositor gamma still 1.8.

The same applies to `prefs.reset {"path": "colorSettings"}` and to `prefs.reset` with no path. Compare `s.color.settings.blend_text_gamma` with `photocraft_compose::psblend::text_gamma()` after each step.

Rooted automation is not a route for this sequence: it rejects `edit.colorSettings` and rejects `prefs.set` with an explicit `colorSettings` path or batch key (`crates/automation/src/workspace.rs:221-243`).

`docs/control-protocol.md:94-107` documents dotted preference keys, including `colorSettings`, and supports setting and resetting a section or a key. `crates/engine/src/color_cmds.rs:123-125` says type layers mix anti-aliased edges in `blend_text_gamma` (default `TEXT_GAMMA`, line 146), and `crate…

title: fix(prefs): prefs.reset rejects a recognized single shortcuts.<id> or menus.colors.<id> key
author: coygeek
body:
## Runtime or environment

Baseline: storytold/photocraft at commit `d7df9d8aa6de4763ab587af7c01ee64b1f368409`, verified with a focused `photocraft-engine` integration test that dispatches commands through `Session::execute`. The failure source is unchanged on `main` at `52ccb8a`: `Preferences::reset` still looks the key up in `Preferences::default()` at `crates/engine/src/prefs.rs:1073`, and `prefs_reset` still routes these paths there at `crates/engine/src/prefs.rs:1389-1392`.

## Summary

`prefs.get` and `prefs.set` accept the map-key paths `shortcuts.<command id>` and `menus.colors.<id>` (they use the `keyed` helper and `free_map` handling in `crates/engine/src/prefs.rs`), and `prefs.reset` is documented to accept a section or key. But `prefs.reset` looks the default up in `Preferences::default()`, whose `shortcuts` and `menus.colors` maps are empty, so resetting one of those keys fails with "unknown preference" even though the key is set and readable. The failure leaves the preferences unchanged.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open a document (`file.new`, for example 8 by 8).
2. `prefs.set {"path": "shortcuts.edit.undo", "value": "Ctrl+Z"}` succeeds.
3. `prefs.get {"path": "shortcuts.edit.undo"}` returns `"Ctrl+Z"`.
4. `prefs.reset {"path": "shortcuts.edit.undo"}` fails with `BadParams { cmd: "prefs.reset", msg: "unknown preference \`shortcuts.edit.undo\`" }`.
5. `prefs.set {"path": "menus.colors.edit.fill", "value": "red"}` succeeds and `prefs.get` on the same path returns `"red"`.
6. `prefs.reset {"path": "menus.colors.edit.fill"}` fails with `BadParams { cmd: "prefs.reset", msg: "unknown preference \`menus.colors.edit.fill\`" }`.

title: fix(variables): importing a data-set CSV turns every non-ASCII character into mojibake
author: coygeek
body:
## Runtime or environment

Baseline: storytold/photocraft at commit `d7df9d8aa6de4763ab587af7c01ee64b1f368409`. The failure source is still present on `main` at `52ccb8a`: `split_csv` in `crates/engine/src/variables_cmds.rs` (lines 306–334) still walks `line.as_bytes()` and appends `cur.push(c as char)` at lines 323 and 330.

## Summary

`file.import.variableDataSets` reads a CSV as UTF-8, but its field splitter walks raw bytes and converts each byte to a `char`, so every non-ASCII character in a header, data-set name, or cell becomes Latin-1 mojibake during parsing. Altered data-set names and matched text or pixel-path values are stored; visibility values are parsed as booleans. For a text-replacement variable, the altered string is copied into the text layer by `image.applyDataSet` and into each cloned document that `file.export.dataSetsAsFiles` exports. A non-ASCII header no longer matches its variable, so that whole column is dropped without an error.

## Steps to reproduce

These steps follow the static source trace below; they were not executed for this report.

1. Open a document, add a text layer, and bind a text variable to it: `image.variables.define {"defs":[{"name":"headline","layer":<id>,"type":"textReplacement"}]}`.
2. Write a UTF-8 CSV with a non-ASCII cell, for example the two-line file `DataSet,headline` / `row1,Café`, saved as `sets.csv`.
3. `file.import.variableDataSets {"path": "sets.csv"}`.
4. `image.applyDataSet {"name": "row1"}`.
5. Read the text layer's `text`. The source trace gives `CafÃ©`, not `Café`.

The same conversion applies to header cells and data-set names. A header `café` becomes `cafÃ©`, fails the exact-name lookup against a variable defined as `café`, and its column is skipped. A non-ASCII data-set name is also altered, so applying that row by its original name fails lookup. Quoting the cell does not avoid the conversion, because the quoted branch performs the same per-byte push.

title: fix(variables): applying a text data set leaves the text layer unrendered, so its text disappears
author: coygeek
body:
## Runtime or environment

Baseline: storytold/photocraft at commit `d7df9d8aa6de4763ab587af7c01ee64b1f368409`. The failure source is still present on `main` at `52ccb8a`: the text branch of `apply_to_doc` in `crates/engine/src/variables_cmds.rs` still sets `t.cache = None` at line 171 without rebuilding it, `apply_data_set` commits that edit at line 245, and `export_as_files` applies the same helper at line 358 and exports the clone at line 363.

Applying a data set that carries a text value for a text-replacement variable replaces the type layer's `text` and clears its render cache, but nothing rebuilds the cache, so that text layer stops contributing pixels to the composite. `file.export.dataSetsAsFiles` uses the same helper on a cloned document and exports the clone directly, so each exported PNG for a row with a matching text replacement omits that layer's rendered text.

title: fix(vector): rasterizing a feathered vector mask drops its feather and hardens the layer edge
author: coygeek
body:
## Runtime or environment

Baseline: storytold/photocraft at commit `d7df9d8aa6de4763ab587af7c01ee64b1f368409`. The failure source is still present on `main` at `52ccb8a`: `vector_mask_rasterize` in `crates/engine/src/vector_cmds.rs` (line 1140) still calls `vector::vector_mask_values` at line 1146 and multiplies those raw values into the pixel mask at lines 1155–1157, and `vector_mask_values` in `crates/vector/src/lib.rs` (line 120) still renders coverage without feather.

## Summary

A vector mask's `feather` is part of its rendered appearance: the compositor blurs an enabled vector mask by `feather_sigma(feather)` when it builds the layer's effective mask. `layer.rasterize.vectorMask` is documented as multiplying the vector mask into the layer mask, but it multiplies in the unfeathered path coverage and does not carry the feather over. For a layer without a pre-existing pixel mask, the new pixel mask has feather 0, so a soft vector-mask edge becomes a hard pixel-mask edge.

## Steps to reproduce

These steps follow the static source trace below; they were not executed for this report.

1. Create a document with a filled pixel layer and no pixel mask, for example `file.new {"width":64,"height":64,"background":"white"}`, `layer.new.layer`, `select.rect {"x":4,"y":4,"width":56,"height":56}`, `edit.fill {"color":"#000000"}`, `select.deselect`.
2. Add a rectangular vector mask: `layer.vectorMask.add {"layer":<id>,"path":{"subpaths":[{"closed":true,"knots":[[16,16],[48,16],[48,48],[16,48]]}]}}`.
3. Feather it: `layer.vectorMask.edit {"layer":<id>,"feather":8.0}`.
4. Read the layer's effective mask with `photocraft_compose::masks::combined_mask` at `(12,32)`, a few pixels outside the path edge on the rectangle's central row. Per the source trace the value is positive: the raw coverage there is 0, and the feather blur (sigma 8, box radius 7) spreads coverage to that point.

title: fix(selection): select.modify silently clamps a negative radius instead of refusing it
author: coygeek
body:
## Runtime or environment

Baseline: storytold/photocraft at commit `d7df9d8aa6de4763ab587af7c01ee64b1f368409`. The failure source is still present on `main` at `52ccb8a`: `modify` in `crates/engine/src/selection_cmds.rs` still rejects only non-finite and over-maximum radii at lines 234–236 and clamps with `let r = r.max(0.0);` at line 237, and the `select.modify.*` specifications at lines 353–357 still document the positive minima.

The Select › Modify commands document a minimum radius (1 px, or 0.1 px for Feather), and the implementation's own comment says out-of-range values are "refused, never clamped silently", but the guard only rejects non-finite values and values above the maximum. A negative radius is accepted and clamped to 0, and the command reports success. title: fix(transform): transformSelection with a far-off-canvas warp mesh allocates the union of the old and warped bounds
author: coygeek
body:
## Runtime or environment

Baseline: storytold/photocraft at commit `d7df9d8aa6de4763ab587af7c01ee64b1f368409`; the extreme case is established by static proof, and smaller translations were run through the engine. The failure source is still present on `main` at `52ccb8a`: `warp_mesh_gray` in `crates/algo/src/warp.rs:301-315` still unions the source and warped bounds at line 314 and writes one dense buffer over that union at line 315, and `transform_selection` in `crates/engine/src/select_extra_cmds.rs` still reaches it from the warp branch at line 173.

## Summary

`select.transformSelection` with a warp mesh resamples the selection through `warp_mesh_gray`, which clears the source and warped regions as one dense buffer spanning their union. The homography path in the same command was fixed to write the two regions separately because a far transform allocated a huge buffer and hung the app, but the mesh path still builds the union. For a valid custom warp mesh whose control points are far off-canvas, the requested buffer and the tiles written grow with the square of the distance even though the resulting selection stays the same size; at a 100000-pixel translation of a 48 by 48 selection the dense float buffer alone is about 37.29 GiB.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open a 64 by 64 document with a selection (`file.new {"width":64,"height":64}`, `select.rect {"x":8,"y":8,"width":48,"height":48}`).
2. Build a valid custom warp mesh and translate every control point by `d` in both axes: take `photocraft_geom::warp::BezierMesh::identity([8,8,56,56], 1, 1)`, add `d` to the x and y of every point, and pass it as the `mesh` parameter.
3. `select.transformSelection {"mesh": <that mesh>}`.
4. Compare the union of the original and resulting selection bounds with the final selection.

title: fix(docs): the README's "34 tools" heading disagrees with its own list and the app's tool inventory
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

`README.md` heads the first cell of the "Everything in the box" table "🧰 34 tools", but the list directly beneath it names a different number of tools, and the app's selectable tool inventory (`Tool::ALL` in `crates/ui-egui/src/state.rs`, which the toolbar and command palette both use) is larger still. The heading is the only numeric tool count on the front page. Impact is confined to the front-page description: no tool behaves differently.

## Runtime or environment

- Baseline: commit `d7df9d8aa6de4763ab587af7c01ee64b1f368409`; this is a text-versus-source comparison, and no application run was needed.
- On `main` at `52ccb8a` the mismatch is still present with updated numbers: `README.md:180` still reads "🧰 34 tools"; the list at line 181 now has 33 entries (Magnetic Lasso was added) that expand to 38 names; and `Tool::ALL` at `crates/ui-egui/src/state.rs:116` is declared `[Tool; 48]` after Magnetic Lasso, Vertical Type and Content-Aware Move were added.

title: fix(automation): the MCP bridge resends a request whose reply was lost, applying non-idempotent edits twice
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

`BridgeClient::call` retries any transport failure once on a fresh connection. The retry comment says it covers an app restart, but the same arm also catches a reply read error or a connection close that happens after the request line has been written and flushed, when the app may already have run the command. If the app ran a non-idempotent edit such as `layer.new.layer` and the reply was then lost while the same app session stays available, the bridge reconnects, sends the same method and params again under a new request id, and the edit is applied a second time; the caller sees only the second, successful reply. The bridge already refuses to retry a possibly completed edit when a reply is oversized; the transport-failure arm does not follow the same rule.

## Steps to reproduce

These steps were not executed for this report; the failure is established from source (see Actual behavior), using the baseline under Runtime or environment.

1. Start the desktop app with control enabled, open a document, and make sure no job is running that would block the command (otherwise `layer.new.layer` returns an error).
2. Connect `photocraft-cli mcp --bridge 127.0.0.1:<port> --control-token-file <path>`.
3. Call `command_run {"id":"layer.new.layer","params":{"name":"Once"}}`.
4. After the app has executed the command and before the bridge's timeout, the connection fails without the reply reaching the bridge (the socket closes or a read error occurs) while the same app session remains running.
5. The bridge reconnects, authenticates and sends `engine.execute` with the same command and params again; the app inserts a second layer, and the tool call reports one success.

author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

Layer-comp positions decoded from a PSD are computed with unchecked `i32` arithmetic on values taken from the file. `comps_from_psd` stores a comp layer's absolute position as `x + dx` / `y + dy` (`crates/io/src/comps_map.rs:211`), adding the layer origin to the `Ofst` offset read from the layer's `shmd` → `cmls` descriptor, and `write_cmls` converts a stored position back to an offset as `x - hx` / `y - hy` (`crates/io/src/comps_map.rs:258`) when it regenerates comp data on export. Neither expression is checked. A comp offset of `Hrzn = i32::MAX` on a layer whose origin is `(4, 4)` makes PSD import panic in a build with overflow checks on (the default `dev`/`test` profile), and a stored comp position of `i32::MIN` makes export panic there; this was reproduced through the public `photocraft_io::import` and `photocraft_io::export` entry points. In the desktop app the panic guard around file I/O turns the import panic into a generic internal-error message, so that file cannot be opened in such a build. With overflow checks off (the default `release` profile), the same addition wraps instead, and the document holds an absolute comp position that no file described.

title: fix(engine): edit.puppetWarp allocates bookkeeping for the whole destination area for a far finite pin destination
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

`edit.puppetWarp` accepts pin destinations that are finite but arbitrarily far from the canvas, and the puppet renderer enumerates every tile of the destination rectangle and allocates a tile rectangle, a triangle bin and a lookup entry for each. The renderer clamps the mesh bounds to ±2^20 px and adds a one-pixel margin when forming the destination rectangle, which keeps the enumeration finite, but it does not check an aggregate work or allocation budget. For a pin dragged to `[1048576, 1048576]` on a filled 64×64 layer, the destination spans 17,623,204 tiles, and the renderer must allocate at least about 846 MB of bookkeeping before it renders any pixels. The command does not reject the request first.

## Steps to reproduce

Command form, at the baseline under Runtime or environment (the layer must have content, because Puppet Warp returns an empty layer unchanged):

1. `file.new {"width":64,"height":64}`, then `layer.new.layer {}`.
2. Fill the layer: `edit.fill {"contents":"color","color":"#669933"}`.
3. Run `edit.puppetWarp {"pins":[{"src":[4,4],"dst":[4,4]},{"src":[60,60],"dst":[1048576,1048576]}],"interpolation":"bilinear"}`.
4. Both pins are finite, so `puppet_params` accepts them, and the renderer sizes its tile, bin and lookup collections from the deformed mesh's destination bounds.

title: fix(engine): slice.divide accepts up to a million parts with no total budget, and listing them is quadratic
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

`slice.divide` clamps `horizontal` and `vertical` only to 1..1000 each, so a single request is accepted for up to 10^6 parts, and no check limits the total part count or the work and memory it implies before the parts are created. On a regular grid of P parts, resolving the slice list is quadratic in P: `slice.list` (and every other caller of `slices::resolve`) scans the stored rectangles for every grid cell and does linear id lookups for every stored slice. A probe on the baseline shows `slice.list` time growing with the part count, and at P = 10^6 the static scan count is about 5×10^11 rectangle visits, with 216 MB of inline slice records alone. The quadratic id search that the baseline's divide loop also performed was removed upstream in commit `3ad26e3` (#749); the accepted count, the allocation and the quadratic resolve remain.

## Steps to reproduce

At the baseline under Runtime or environment, through `Session::execute`:

1. `file.new {"width":1000,"height":1000}`.
2. `slice.new {"rect":[0,0,1000,1000]}`, and read the slice id from `slice.list`.
3. `slice.divide {"slice":<id>,"horizontal":n,"vertical":n}`; the clamp accepts any `n` up to 1000, and a 1000×1000 slice is large enough for `n = 1000`.
4. `slice.list {}` and time it.

The verifier ran steps 1-4 in a temporary engine integration test with `n` in 2, 20, 30, 40, 60 and 80, each in a fresh session, timing `slice.divide` and `slice.list` separately, asserting that both the returned count and the listed count equal n², and checking the 2×2 result. The maximum request (`n = 1000`) was not run.

## Expected behavior

AGENTS.md "Never crash" requires allocations sized by input to be capped, and Rule 9 requires a command's `run` closure and anything it calls to "validate params, check bounds before indexing or dividing, and reject absurd sizes before allocating". author: AndrewJFleming

In Photoshop, Alt-clicking a layer mask thumbnail opens the grayscale mask canvas. You can then paste copied image content directly into that mask using Ctrl+V, preserving grayscale values and smooth gradients.

Current PhotoCraft behavior:

Create a layer mask and Alt-click its thumbnail.

Copy a selection containing grayscale image data.

Press Ctrl+V, or use Edit → Paste Special → Paste Into.

PhotoCraft creates a new raster layer instead of modifying the active mask.

Expected behavior:

When the layer mask is the active editing target, pasting should write clipboard image data into the mask's grayscale pixels, preserving luminance and gradients, without creating a new layer.

Add the Perspective Crop tool named in the roadmap: place four corners over a keystoned subject and commit a rectangular document crop with the perspective straightened, as one history step.

## Problem to solve

Photographing a building or a page usually leaves converging verticals, and Photoshop's Perspective Crop tool corrects that in the crop gesture itself. PhotoCraft's Crop tool is rectangular only: the toolbar groups `Tool::Crop` with Slice and Slice Select, `crates/ui-egui/src/crop_ui.rs` draws, moves and resizes a rectangular frame, and the canvas commits that rectangle as x, y, width and height to `image.crop`, whose parameters have no quad or perspective mode. Perspective Warp (`edit.perspectiveWarp`) is a different operation: it deforms the targeted layer's content and does not combine rectification with a document crop. The roadmap names Perspective Crop among the missing tools and in its near-term priority list.

## Proposed behavior

Add a Perspective Crop tool to the toolbar's Crop group, backed by an engine command so the UI, CLI, control channel and MCP share it (the repository's "everything is a command" rule).

The options bar has W and H fields (pixels) and a Clear button: with both fields filled, the output is exactly W × H; with only one filled, the other follows the default rule's aspect ratio. Resolution (ppi) is unchanged.

title: feat(ui): Color Replacement tool on the toolbar
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

Add the Color Replacement tool to the desktop UI. The engine already implements it as `paint.colorReplacement`, and the README lists Color Replacement among PhotoCraft's tools, but there is no selectable Color Replacement tool, canvas stroke routing or options bar, so mouse users cannot use a capability that agents and the CLI can.

## Problem to solve

The README's "34 tools" box lists "Color Replacement" next to Brush, Pencil and Mixer Brush, and the engine's brush module describes itself as covering "the Brush/Pencil/Mixer Brush/Color Replacement tools" and registers `paint.colorReplacement`. The desktop UI has no way to use it: the `Tool` enum and `Tool::ALL` have no Color Replacement entry, the toolbar's Brush group holds only Brush, Pencil and Mixer Brush, `ui.set` cannot select it because tool names resolve only through `Tool::ALL`, and the retouch stroke dispatcher has no branch for it. UI translation catalogs already carry a "Color Replacement" label, but nothing uses it. The capability therefore exists on the CLI, control channel and MCP as a command, but not as a canvas tool.

## Proposed behavior

Expose the existing command as a tool, with no new pixel algorithm.

title: feat(ui): Color Sampler tool and Info panel sample points

title: feat(io): open and save DPX (SMPTE 268M) frames
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

Add DPX as a raster format: open and save Digital Picture Exchange frames in the descriptor, bit-depth and packing combinations listed below, keeping 10- and 12-bit code values exact and the header fields a film or TV pipeline relies on.

## Problem to solve

The roadmap lists DPX as pending format work: the M11 status row ends with "JP2 / DICOM / DPX / C2PA pending", and the M11 scope names "remaining formats (JP2, DICOM, DPX…)". PhotoCraft has no DPX reader or writer: the codec registry has no DPX format, detection does not recognise the `SDPX` or `XPDS` magic numbers, export by extension fails for `.dpx` because the extension is not registered, and the Open and Save As choices do not list it. A `.dpx` frame a colourist hands over cannot be opened, and PhotoCraft cannot produce one.

## Proposed behavior

Supported matrix (proposed):

| Read | Descriptor | Bits | Packing |
|---|---|---|---|
| Luma | 6 | 8, 10, 12, 16 | 8 and 16: 0; 10: 0, 1 (method A) or 2 (method B); 12: 0 or 1 (method A) |
| RGB | 50 | 8, 10, 12, 16 | as above |
| RGBA | 51 | 8, 10, 12, 16 | as above |

- Writing uses descriptor 6, 50 or 51 to match the document (Grayscale, RGB, RGB + alpha), packing 1 (method A) for 10- and 12-bit, packing 0 for 8- and 16-bit, no run-length encoding, and big-endian (`SDPX`) byte order. A Gray + alpha document is written as Luma with the alpha dropped and a fidelity warning.
- Reading accepts both byte orders: big-endian (`SDPX`) and little-endian (`XPDS`).
- Other descriptors (for example ABGR, CbCr or composite video), run-length-encoded image data, floating-point samples and other bit depths return the codec's unsupported-format error naming the field and value.

Sample mapping:

- 8- and 16-bit code values become 8- and 16-bit document samples unchanged.
- 10- and 12-bit code values `c` become 16-bit document samples `round(c × 65535 / (2^b − 1))`, where `b` is the bit depth. Writing at 10 or 12 bits uses the inverse, `round(v × (2^b − 1) / 65535…

title: feat(io): attach and inspect C2PA Content Credentials on export and open
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

Let an export carry a signed C2PA Content Credentials manifest, and let opening or inspecting a file report an existing manifest's signature, asset-binding and signer-trust results, so provenance travels with the image and can be checked from the editor and from automation.

## Problem to solve

The roadmap names C2PA as planned, unfinished work: `docs/roadmap.md:26` ends the M11 row with "JP2 / DICOM / DPX / C2PA pending", and `docs/roadmap.md:150` gives M11 the scope "remaining formats (JP2, DICOM, DPX…), C2PA". Nothing in the tree creates, interprets or verifies a manifest today.

Two metadata models are involved. The codec-level `Metadata` struct (`crates/codecs/src/image.rs:114`) carries EXIF, XMP, DPI, free-form text and, opaquely, Photoshop image resources and layered-TIFF layer data; the flat exporter fills only EXIF, XMP and DPI (`crates/io/src/flat.rs:233`). The document model (`crates/doc/src/lib.rs:634`) additionally keeps raw PSD image resources and raw PSD global blocks (`psd_global_blocks`, line 641), so a PSD's `CAI ` block can sit in document state as opaque bytes. Nothing reads those bytes as a manifest, reports what they claim, checks their signature or binding, or writes a manifest into any export.

A user can therefore neither sign an export nor tell whether an image they were sent carries valid Content Credentials, and an agent cannot do either through the command registry.

## Proposed behavior

- The export paths (File › Export As, and Save As or Save a Copy where the format can hold a manifest) gain a Content Credentials choice that embeds a standards-conforming C2PA manifest signed with a signer identity the user has configured. The Export As dialog already has a Metadata choice (PR #733), which is one natural place for it.
- A request to sign with no configured signer is refused with an error that names the missing signer, in the dialog and headlessly, and writes no file. An export that does not request credentials is unchanged…

title: feat(automation): run Crop and Straighten Photos through automation
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

Let the automation surfaces run File › Automate › Crop and Straighten Photos (`file.automate.cropAndStraightenPhotos`), which splits a scanned page into one new document per photo. The desktop control channel, the headless JSON-lines server and the MCP server refuse it today, although it reads and writes no files.

`docs/architecture.md:239` states the seam's litmus test: "**Litmus test for the seam:** `apps/photocraft-cli` and the automation server must be able to do *everything* the GUI does, except pointer painting, which they do by replaying `PointerEvent` streams through tools." `README.md:222` repeats the promise: "The UI, the CLI, the JSON control channel and the MCP server all call the same commands, so anything you can click, a script or an AI agent can do too."

The automation policy rejects `file.automate.cropAndStraightenPhotos` before dispatch because its id is absent from the explicit allow-list in `crates/automation/src/workspace.rs:152-170`. This request changes the authorization decision for that command only.

From source reading, the command works only on the open document. It is a live menu item (`crates/ui-egui/src/menu_catalog.rs:45`) whose spec takes no parameters, `{} → one new document per photo found on the scan`, with `enabled: has_doc` (`crates/engine/src/photo_cmds.rs:818`). Its handler (`crates/engine/src/photo_cmds.rs:733`) ignores its parameters, flattens the active document in memory, detects the photos, and adds one in-memory document per photo; it calls no file-loading helper. title: feat(vector): Freeform Pen and Curvature Pen tools
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

Add the two Photoshop Pen variants to the Pen tool group: the Freeform Pen, which draws a path freehand and fits it to a Bézier path, and the Curvature Pen, which builds a smooth curve from successive clicks.

## Problem to solve

The roadmap names both tools as missing and puts the Pen variants first among missing tools. `docs/roadmap.md:73` records "~20 Photoshop tools missing: … Freeform/Curvature Pen, Add/Delete Anchor Point tools, …", and `docs/roadmap.md:105` lists as a priority "**Missing tools,** starting with the Pen variants (Direct Selection landed, #790), Patch / Content-Aware Move, Pencil, Rotate View, Perspective Crop."

Only one Pen behaviour exists. The Pen tool (`Tool::Pen`, `crates/ui-egui/src/state.rs:103`, key `P` at `:268`) adds one corner or smooth anchor per click or drag: `pen_down` (`crates/ui-egui/src/vector_ui.rs:127`) appends a knot or closes on the first anchor, `pen_move` (`:141`) drags the last knot's mirrored handles, `pen_up` (`:152`) ends the handle drag, and `pen_commit` (`:159`) writes the result. Nothing collects a freehand pointer trace for curve fitting, and nothing recomputes smooth handles from successive click positions. The Pen toolbar group holds only `Tool::Pen` (`crates/ui-egui/src/panels.rs:37`), and the `Tool` enum (`crates/ui-egui/src/state.rs:64`, with `Tool::ALL` at `:117`) has no variant for either tool, so `ui.set` cannot select one either.

- Freeform Pen: dragging draws a freehand path shown live; on release the traced points are fitted to a Bézier path within the documented fitting tolerance and committed the way the Pen commits.

title: pencil tool cursor parity
author: zsrobinson
body:
The pencil tool doesn't quite match the UX of the pencil tool in Photoshop.

**Expected behavior (Photoshop):** the cursor when using the pencil tool *does not* snap to the grid, as it makes it difficult to tell where within a pixel your cursor actually is. the system cursor is also hidden and completely replaced by the pencil cursor, and has a small crosshair in the middle. larger pencil sizes display and draw as a pixelated circle.

**Actual behavior (PhotoCraft):** the cursor snaps to the grid, and does not hide the system cursor. larger pencil sizes display as a square but draw as a pixelated circle.

title: `Ctrl + I` and `Image -> Adjustments -> Invert` invert layer pixels instead of active layer mask

## Description
When working with layer masks, attempting to invert the mask using the keyboard shortcut (`Ctrl + I` / `Cmd + I`) or the menu path (`Image -> Adjustments -> Invert`) modifies the layer's image pixels instead of inverting the active layer mask. This happens even when the layer mask thumbnail is explicitly selected in the Layers panel.

## Steps to Reproduce

2. Click directly on the **layer mask thumbnail** in the Layers panel (ensuring the mask thumbnail has the active selection border around it, not the image thumbnail).

## Expected Behavior
The active layer mask should be inverted (black becomes white, white becomes black), leaving the original image pixels untouched.

The image pixels on the layer are inverted instead of the selected layer mask.

- **App:** PhotoCraft (Early Alpha)
- **Component:** Layer Masking / Image Adjustments Focus

title: Pattern Preview does not display a seamless four-way repeating preview
author: zystoo
body:
## Description

View > Pattern Preview does not show the image as a seamless repeating tile.

In Photoshop, enabling Pattern Preview repeats the document horizontally and vertically around the original canvas. This makes it possible to paint across the canvas boundaries and immediately see whether the pattern is seamless.

In PhotoCraft, enabling Pattern Preview does not display the surrounding repeated tiles, so I cannot preview or edit a four-way seamless pattern.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create or open a small image.
2. Select View > Pattern Preview.
3. Paint or place an object near one edge of the canvas.
4. Observe the canvas around the original document boundary.

## Current behavior

The canvas does not show the image repeated on all four sides. Content crossing one edge is not visibly wrapped to the opposite edge.

## Expected behavior

- Repeat the document horizontally and vertically around the original canvas.
- Show neighboring tiles outside the original canvas boundary.
- Content crossing the left/right or top/bottom edge should wrap automatically.
- Painting near an edge should update all visible neighboring tiles in real time.
- The original document boundary should remain visible.

This should behave similarly to Photoshop’s View > Pattern Preview workflow.

## Environment

- Operating system: macOS
- PhotoCraft version: [0.3.0]

title: Layer via Copy keeps the selection active, so a following Free Transform moves only the selection (and leaves a residue when feathered)
author: sunboaooo-blip

title: Layer bounds are not recomputed after Free Transform of a selection (still include the old position)
author: sunboaooo-blip
body:
### Summary
After moving a layer's pixels with `edit.transform` **while a selection is active**, the layer `bounds` reported by `doc_inspect` cover the union of the old and new positions, even though the old area is fully transparent. Transforming the same layer with no selection gives correct bounds (`[110,10,40,40]`), so the selection-transform path seems to skip the bounds update. Agents use `bounds` to locate content and check for leftovers, so stale bounds look like residue.

### Steps (MCP / control channel, headless)
```jsonc
doc_new {"width":200,"height":100,"background":"#000000"}
select.rect {"x":10,"y":10,"width":40,"height":40}
paint.gradient {"from":[0,0],"to":[1,0],"colors":["#ff0000","#ff0000"]}
layer.new.layerViaCopy {}                        // selection stays active (see #1096)
edit.transform {"matrix":[1,0,0,1,100,0]}        // transforms the selection; result rect [10,10,50,50]
select.deselect {}
layer.setProps {"layer":<Background id>,"visible":false}
document.pixel {"x":20,"y":20}    // → [0,0,0,0]  old area is empty
document.pixel {"x":120,"y":20}   // → [1,0,0,1]  content now at x 110..150
doc_inspect                       // new layer "bounds": [10,10,140,40]
```

### Expected
`bounds` = `[110,10,40,40]`, the tight box of the non-transparent pixels after the transform (as Photoshop's layer bounds and `layer.bounds` in scripting report).

### Actual
`bounds` = `[10,10,140,40]`, the union of the old and new boxes.

### Notes
- Control: inserting `select.deselect {}` before `edit.transform` gives correct bounds `[110,10,40,40]`.
- Seen repeatedly on larger documents too, e.g. a full-width strip moved by +800 px reported `[600,0,1224,1024]` instead of `[1400,0,424,1024]`.

### Environment
PhotoCraft 0.3.0 (`photocraft-0.3.0-linux-x86_64.AppImage`, SHA256 verified), Ubuntu 26.04, driven headless via `photocraft-cli mcp`.

title: fix(ui): "Save" in the unsaved-changes prompt closes a layered TIFF before it is written
author: ElmoBlatch
body:
**Where:** `crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs:843-846` (`save_as`), `discard_ui.rs:121-134`, `tiff_options_ui.rs:66-75`

`save_as` parks the write behind the TIFF Options prompt and returns `Ok`. `discard_ui::save` treats
that as saved and `advance()` closes the document (or quits). The prompt later calls
`write_document`, which writes whichever document is active.

**Steps:** dirty untitled layered document → ⌘W → Save → name it `x.tif` → OK in TIFF Options.
**Actual:** the document is closed unsaved; the next tab is written to `x.tif`, or the save fails with "no document".
**Expected:** the close waits for the TIFF prompt, and the write targets the document that asked.

Found by code reading on `main` at `eec4af6`. The close-before-write part is reproduced with a test (see the comment below); the later write to the wrong document is not.

title: fix(ui): cancelling a Place / copy transform undoes the last edit of another document
author: ElmoBlatch
body:
**Where:** `crates/ui-egui/src/transform_tool.rs:227-233` (`take_back_made`), `:539-554` (`end_if_left`, `cancel`)

When the transform's layer is not in the active document, `end_if_left` calls `cancel`, and
`take_back_made` runs `session.undo()` + `history.clear_redo()` on the active document.

**Steps:** drop a file onto document A (transform opens) → click document B's tab.
**Actual:** B loses its latest history step with no redo; A keeps the placed layer.
**Expected:** the transform is bound to its document and cancels there.

Found by code reading on `main` at `eec4af6`, then reproduced with a test using a ⌥⌘T copy (see the comment below); the dropped-file case is untested.

title: fix(engine): closing a non-active document changes the active document
author: ElmoBlatch
body:
**Where:** `crates/engine/src/lib.rs:387` (`Session::close`)

`self.active = Some(index.min(len - 1))` uses the closed index, whichever tab was active.

**Steps:** open A, B, C with C active → `file.close {"document":0}`.
**Actual:** B becomes active.
**Expected:** C stays active; the index only shifts when the active document itself closes.

Found by code reading on `main` at `eec4af6`, then reproduced with a test (see the comment below).

title: fix(format): a document holding a NaN or infinite float saves to a .pcraft that cannot be reopened
author: ElmoBlatch
body:
**Where:** `crates/format/src/store.rs:522` (`serde_json::to_vec_pretty`)

serde_json writes non-finite floats as `null`, which does not deserialize into the manifest's
non-`Option` float fields. Nothing sanitizes on import or save. Sources include a PSD `expA` block
(`crates/io/src/adjust_map.rs:197`) and descriptor doubles.

**Actual:** import works, save and autosave report success, every later load fails with a JSON error.
**Expected:** non-finite values are rejected or sanitized at import, or the save fails.

Found by code reading on `main` at `eec4af6`, then reproduced with a test (see the comment below).

title: fix(engine): filters ignore layer locks
author: ElmoBlatch
body:
**Where:** `crates/engine/src/filters.rs:179-192` (`has_filterable_layer`), `run_filter`

`has_filterable_layer` checks only the layer kind, and `filters.rs` never consults locks.

**Steps:** lock pixels (or lock all) on a raster layer → `filter.blur.gaussianBlur`.
**Actual:** the layer is rewritten. With lock-transparency, blurs change alpha.
**Expected:** refused with a "layer is locked" error, as painting is.

Found by code reading on `main` at `eec4af6`, then reproduced with a test (see the comment below). Flame, Tree, Picture Frame (`render_cmds.rs:107`) and
`path.fill` (`vector_cmds.rs:967`) look the same.

title: fix(engine): Delete, Cut and Image › Adjustments write to pixel-locked layers
author: ElmoBlatch
body:
**Where:** `crates/engine/src/edit_cmds.rs:119` (`clear_area`), `:285` (`auto_adjust`), `commands.rs:194` (`destructive_adjust`)

These call `surface_mut()` directly with no `effective_locks` check.

**Steps:** lock pixels on a layer → `edit.clear {}` or any `image.adjustments.*`.
**Actual:** pixels change.
**Expected:** refused.

Found by code reading on `main` at `eec4af6`, then reproduced with a test (see the comment below).

title: fix(engine): Paint Bucket and Gradient ignore lock-transparency
author: ElmoBlatch
body:
**Where:** `crates/engine/src/paint_cmds.rs:57`, `:105`

Both do `let (surf, _) = target_surface(...)`, discarding the transparency-lock flag.

**Steps:** lock transparency on a layer with a transparent region → `paint.bucket` or `paint.gradient`.
**Actual:** transparent pixels become opaque.
**Expected:** alpha is preserved, as `edit.fill` does.

Found by code reading on `main` at `eec4af6`, then reproduced with a test (see the comment below).

title: fix(engine): Flatten Image produces a Background that fails the Background checks
author: ElmoBlatch
body:
**Where:** `crates/engine/src/commands.rs:627-637`, `extra_cmds.rs:46` (`is_background`)

Flatten sets only `locks.transparency`; `is_background` also requires `locks.position`.

**Steps:** `layer.flattenImage` → `edit.clear` with a selection.
**Actual:** Delete punches transparency, `layer.new.layerFromBackground` is disabled, and the layer can be moved.
**Expected:** the flattened layer behaves as a Background.

Found by code reading on `main` at `eec4af6`, then reproduced with a test (see the comment below).

title: fix(engine): select.rect with mode subtract or intersect and no selection selects the rectangle
author: ElmoBlatch
body:
**Where:** `crates/engine/src/commands.rs:409-413`

`("subtract", None)` and `("intersect", None)` fall through to `_ => shape`.

**Steps:** no selection → `select.rect {"mode":"subtract", ...}`.
**Actual:** the rectangle is selected.
**Expected:** the selection stays empty.

Found by code reading on `main` at `eec4af6`, then reproduced with a test (see the comment below).

title: fix(engine): layer.delete can remove a document's last layer
author: ElmoBlatch
body:
**Where:** `crates/engine/src/commands.rs:470`

The single-layer path calls `doc.remove(id)` with no guard; the multi-select path refuses with
"a document must keep at least one layer".

**Steps:** one-layer document → `layer.delete {"layer":id}`.
**Actual:** `layers == []`, `active_layer == None`.
**Expected:** the same refusal as the multi-select path.

Found by code reading on `main` at `eec4af6`, then reproduced with a test (see the comment below).

title: fix(photocraft): a non-UTF-8 argument panics at startup
author: ElmoBlatch
body:
**Where:** `apps/photocraft/src/main.rs:134`, `apps/photocraft-cli/src/main.rs:4`

Both use `std::env::args()`, which panics on a non-Unicode argument.

**Steps (Linux):** `photocraft-cli convert $'caf\xe9.png' out.png`, or open such a file from a file manager.
**Actual:** panic before any window or error message.
**Expected:** `args_os()` and a normal error, per the never-crash rule.

Found by code reading on `main` at `eec4af6`, then reproduced with the CLI (see the comment below); the desktop app was not launched.

title: fix(photocraft): a control request that times out still runs later
author: ElmoBlatch
body:
**Where:** `apps/photocraft/src/control_server.rs:91`, `crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs:901-905` (`drain_control`)

After the 60 s `recv_timeout` the client gets `"timeout"`, but the request stays queued and
`drain_control` executes it, ignoring the failed reply send.

**Steps:** minimise the window on macOS (frames stop) → send `engine.execute` → receive `timeout` → retry → restore the window.
**Actual:** every queued copy runs; a timed-out `app.quit` closes without a prompt.
**Expected:** a timed-out request is cancelled.

Found by code reading on `main` at `eec4af6`. The queued-request-still-runs part is reproduced with a test (see the comment below); the real 60 s timeout, the minimised-window trigger and `app.quit` are untested. Related to #1007 but a different path.

title: fix(codecs): an ASCII PGM/PPM header pre-allocates four times the Limits budget
author: ElmoBlatch
body:
**Where:** `crates/codecs/src/codecs/pnm.rs:158`

`Vec::<u32>::with_capacity(n)` runs before any raster byte is read; `limits.check` budgeted 1-2 bytes per sample.

**Input:** the 19-byte file `P3\n32768 32768\n255\n`.
**Actual:** reserves capacity for about 12 GiB before reading any sample. Under an 8 GB address-space limit the process aborts (`memory allocation of 12884901888 bytes failed`); on a 64 GB machine with default overcommit it returns an error instead.
**Expected:** capacity bounded by the bytes remaining in the file.

Found by code reading on `main` at `eec4af6`, then reproduced under a memory limit (see the comments below).

title: fix(engine): Clone Stamp and Healing Brush slice out of bounds for a far source offset
author: ElmoBlatch
body:
**Where:** `crates/engine/src/retouch_cmds.rs:199-203` (`clone_sample`), `crates/paint/src/retouch.rs:52-54`

`rect.translate(off)` saturates, so the sampled region is smaller than `rect`; `r.rect = rect`
then relabels it full-size and `Region::px` indexes past the buffer.

**Input:** `paint.cloneStamp {"points":[[10,10]],"source":[3e9,0]}`.
**Actual:** panic.
**Expected:** `Err`.

Found by code reading on `main` at `eec4af6`, then reproduced with a test (see the comment below). #716 fixed the rotated-source branch (`source_rect`); this is the pure-translation branch. Should be covered by `panic_hunt`.

title: fix(compose): the Lab-mix flag is cleared, not restored, after compositing a tile
author: ElmoBlatch
body:
**Where:** `crates/compose/src/lib.rs:107-109`, `:116-118`, `:124-126`

`LAB_MIX` is set to `lab` then unconditionally to `false`. A nested rayon job (for example
`gradient_fill::render`) can let a worker steal another tile, which clears the flag mid-tile.

**Actual:** in a Lab document with a gradient fill layer, some 256 px tiles mix in sRGB, varying between renders.
**Expected:** save and restore the previous value, as `with_cmyk_space` does.

Found by code reading on `main` at `eec4af6`, then reproduced intermittently with a test (see the comment below): whole tiles differ between identical renders. The work-stealing explanation itself is not confirmed.

title: fix(compose): Color Lookup's table-size guard overflows
author: ElmoBlatch
body:
**Where:** `crates/compose/src/adjust.rs:206`

`(*size as usize).pow(3) * 3` is unchecked on a file-derived `size`. It can wrap to a small value,
pass the length check, and index past the table.

**Input:** a `.pcraft` manifest with `size: 4194304` and a short `lut`.
**Actual:** panic.
**Expected:** `checked_pow` / `checked_mul` and skip the adjustment.

Found by code reading on `main` at `eec4af6`, then reproduced with a test that builds the adjustment in memory (see the comment below); the `.pcraft` file trigger is untested.

title: fix(algo): Nearest Neighbor averages when reducing
author: ElmoBlatch
body:
**Where:** `crates/algo/src/resample.rs:88`

The nearest path is taken only when `scale >= 1.0`; reductions fall through to the box filter.

**Steps:** 1 px checkerboard → Image Size 50% with Nearest Neighbor.
**Actual:** uniform 0.5 grey.
**Expected:** one source sample per output pixel at any scale.

Found by code reading on `main` at `eec4af6`, then reproduced with a test (see the comment below).

title: fix(compose): split shape layers are rasterised at 8-bit in 16- and 32-bit documents
author: ElmoBlatch
body:
**Where:** `crates/compose/src/shape_split.rs:51` (`let fmt = PixelFormat::RGBA8;`)

**Steps:** 16-bit document → stroked shape with a gradient fill and a layer effect or clipped layers.
**Actual:** the fill is quantised to 256 levels; 32-bit values clip at 1.
**Expected:** the document's pixel format.

Found by code reading on `main` at `eec4af6`, then reproduced with a test (see the comment below).

title: fix(ui): Edit › Toolbar… has no effect on the toolbar
author: ElmoBlatch
body:
**Where:** `crates/ui-egui/src/prefs_ui.rs:1209-1231`, `panels.rs:17`, `:54`

The dialog writes `prefs.toolbar.hidden`, but the toolbar is drawn from the constant
`TOOL_SECTIONS`. Nothing outside the prefs model reads `toolbar.hidden` or `toolbar.order`.
Not in the scorecard's unread-settings list.

Found by code reading on `main` at `eec4af6`, then reproduced with a test (see the comment below).

title: fix(ui): seven options-bar and History buttons discard their click
author: ElmoBlatch
body:
**Where:** `crates/ui-egui/src/panels.rs:524`, `:527`, `:532`, `:772`, `:2020-2022`

Each is `let _ = icons::button(...)`: airbrush build-up, smoothing options, symmetry options,
crop overlay, and History's Delete current state, Create new snapshot, and Create new document
from current state.

**Expected:** wire each to its command, or hide it until one exists.

Found by code reading on `main` at `eec4af6`. The four options-bar buttons are reproduced with a test (see the comment below); the three History footer buttons are not, and rest on the call sites discarding the click.

title: fix(ui): Paint Bucket "All Layers" is never sent
author: ElmoBlatch
body:
**Where:** `crates/ui-egui/src/panels.rs:713`, `canvas.rs:2574`, `crates/engine/src/paint_cmds.rs:38-72`

The checkbox edits `tool_options.sample_all_layers`; the `paint.bucket` params omit it and the
engine has no such parameter.

Found by code reading on `main` at `eec4af6`, then reproduced with a test (see the comment below).

title: fix(ui): several View toggles change only their checkmark
author: ElmoBlatch
body:
**Where:** `crates/ui-egui/src/view_cmds.rs:172-182`, `:516-518`, `:544`

No code outside `view_cmds.rs` and `state.rs` reads `show.target_path`, `show.brush_preview`,
`show.mesh`, `show.edit_pins`, `show.artboard_guides`, `pixel_aspect` or `pixel_aspect_correction`.

**Expected:** the canvas honours them, or the items are disabled.

Found by code reading on `main` at `eec4af6`. Pixel Aspect Ratio and its Correction are reproduced with a test (see the comment below). The `show.*` flags rest on the fields having no reader; the Target Path render check is inconclusive.

title: fix(ui): the Graphic and Web, Pixel Art and Motion workspaces are identical to Essentials
author: ElmoBlatch
body:
**Where:** `crates/ui-egui/src/menus.rs:1090-1095`

The "Graphic and Web" arm returns the same tuple as the default arm; the other two hit the default.

Found by code reading on `main` at `eec4af6`, then reproduced with a test (see the comment below).

title: fix(prefs): integrations.allow_agent_control and control_port are never read
author: ElmoBlatch
body:
**Where:** `crates/engine/src/prefs.rs:698-705`, `apps/photocraft/src/main.rs:120-140`

The control server starts only from `--control` / `PHOTOCRAFT_CONTROL_PORT`. Unticking the
preference does not stop it and the port preference is ignored. The scorecard lists both as
unread (#217, UI-217-4); this asks for the toggle to gate the server, since users will read it as a security switch.

Found by code reading on `main` at `eec4af6`. Not tested by running the app: this rests on neither field having a reader outside `prefs.rs`, and on the server being started only from `--control` / `PHOTOCRAFT_CONTROL_PORT` in `apps/photocraft/src/main.rs`.

title: Proposal: install Google Fonts from inside PhotoCraft (and where to host the font index)
author: kntrttm
body:
## Summary
I'd like to add a "Find More" tab to the font menu, like Photoshop's Adobe Fonts tab, plus
"download missing fonts" in Type › Resolve Missing Fonts…, backed by Google Fonts.
One click downloads the font, verifies it and registers it with the text engine.
Before I write the networking part I need two decisions from maintainers:
whether this kind of network access is acceptable at all, and where the font index should live.

## Design (short)
- **Index**: a JSON list of Google Fonts families, generated from `google/fonts` at a pinned commit.
  Each entry has family, category, subsets, licence, and per file: path, size, sha256, axes and
  PostScript names.
  It is **not embedded** in the app (the wasm has about 1 MB of headroom under the 24 MiB gate).
  The app fetches it on first use from a URL whose sha256 is pinned in the code, the same way
  `corpus_pins.rs` pins the corpora.
- **Font files**: TTFs from `google/fonts` at the same pinned commit, served by jsDelivr
  (`cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/google/fonts@<sha>/…`), with raw.githubusercontent.com as fallback.
  Every file is checked against the index's sha256 and parsed before it is written.
- **Engine**: `type.fonts.catalog`, `type.fonts.install` (a background job with progress and
  cancel), `type.fonts.installed`, `type.fonts.remove`. They work the same from the UI, the CLI and MCP.
