title: Misleading warning `could not find these libraries the X11 session needs: libxkbcommon-x11.so.0. Starting anyway.` when library exists
author: Samueru-sama
body: I packaged PhotoCraft as an Anylinux-AppImage [here](https://github.com/pkgforge-dev/PhotoCraft-AppImage), this makes the app able to work on any linux system regardless of the libc or even if the host is FHS at all. Running the AppImage on alpine linux it works, but I get this warning: **The app works** but it says: ``` photocraft: warning: could not find these libraries the X11 session needs: libxkbcommon-x11.so.0. Starting anyway. Install them with: Debian/Ubuntu: sudo apt install libxkbcommon-x11-0 Fedora: sudo dnf install libxkbcommon-x11 ``` This is because of https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/issues/201 a check that runs `ldconfig -p` was added, which fails here since there is no `ldconfig -p` in musl systems. **Using `ldconfig -p` to check for libraries is wrong and unreliable**, just see: https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/112417 https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/142020#issuecomment-3590632764 and cpython eventually just deprecated this function because it was broken. If you need to check for a library, just try to `dlopen` the library and let the dynamic linker do the discovery, [example.](https://github.com/lseurttyuu/GPU-T/blob/3f7bb3e5a42238bdf565543fd293c481e2633836/Services/Utilities/GpuFeatureDetection.cs#L592-L633)

**Summary**
Add AI image generation that runs fully on your own machine. You'd load community model files, like the checkpoints and LoRAs on Civitai, and generate straight into a document or onto a new layer.

**Why**
PhotoCraft is offline, open source and GPU-accelerated, so generating locally fits the project. No cloud API, no account and no per-image cost. Many artists already have big libraries of `.safetensors` models from Civitai and Hugging Face.

- Optional: use a ComfyUI or A1111 server the user already runs, instead of a built-in engine (related: #584)

**Possible implementation routes**
1. **Built-in Rust engine**: e.g. [`candle`](https://github.com/huggingface/candle) or `diffusion-rs` (stable-diffusion.cpp bindings), keeping the app pure Rust
2. **Backend bridge**: talk to a local ComfyUI or A1111 HTTP API, the way Krita AI Diffusion does. Less work, and it supports every model type
3. Expose it through the existing command/MCP layer so agents can use it too

**Related:** #584, #219

### Description
`photocraft-0.3.0-linux-x86_64.flatpak` (`ai.storyteller.photocraft`, 0.3.0) shows tofu `□□` for many Simplified Chinese menu items. Some items (`文件/图像/文字/窗口/帮助`) render, others don't. Screenshot crop (435x50): menu bar `文件 □□ 图像 □□ 文字 □□ □□ □□ 窗口 帮助`.

- App is static Rust + egui, no fontconfig. It searches hardcoded paths like `/usr/share/fonts/opentype/noto/NotoSansCJK-Regular.ttc`, `/usr/share/fonts/truetype/wqy/...`, `DroidSansFallbackFull.ttf` (strings in `/app/bin/photocraft`).

### Steps to reproduce
1. On Debian 13 (LANG=zh_CN.UTF-8) install `photocraft-0.3.0-linux-x86_64.flatpak` as system.
2. Launch `photocraft`, look at top menu bar.

Menu uses system Noto Sans CJK SC like the native `.deb` does (#185).

Partial tofu, only shared JP/Han glyphs render.

title: Contribution proposal: Windows pen input and movable panel workspace
author: Kindleshard
body:
# Windows pen input and movable panel workspace: tested reference implementation

We have a local reference implementation for several Windows pen-input and panel-workspace improvements and would like to contribute the parts that are still useful upstream.

The implementation is based on commit `47f9306fd06d5dee11acb84b108606f4c867222a` (Open HEIC/HEIF photos). These observations and test results apply to that checkout plus our changes; we have not reproduced all of the original problems on today's main branch. This is a contribution proposal, rather than a claim that every issue remains present in current main.

## Pen input and brush cursor

- Hide the native arrow when the canvas requests a brush-size outline, and restore the normal cursor outside the canvas. Cover additional document windows and preserve unrelated custom cursor images.
- Open the brush picker on the pen's secondary-button press, including a held or moving barrel-button gesture, without interfering with Alt brush resizing or layer picking.
- Preserve Windows Ink `PEN_FLAG_BARREL` during hover and contact. A small safe-Rust mapping in a local winit 0.30.13 patch emits right-button transitions while preserving tip pressure and hover; barrel contact must not also become a left-button press. Release state on leave/cancel and reset on focus loss.
- A user verified that the Wacom pen's right-click worked with the resulting Windows build after it had failed while mouse right-click worked.

The dependency patch and its provenance are documented in `vendor/winit/PHOTOCRAFT-PATCH.md`. The new mapping does not add unsafe code; existing dependency FFI remains unchanged. Vendoring is the current reference packaging, and we welcome a preferred upstream dependency strategy.

## Movable panels

- Detach tabs into resizable floating groups inside the app, reorder tabs, regroup them, move whole groups and dock them again.
- Show a translucent snapshot of the dragged panel at the cursor without re-running interacti…

title: Web: File > Place Embedded does nothing with an open document (v0.3.0)
author: suibianbab
body:
## Summary

In the PhotoCraft v0.3.0 Web build, **File > Place Embedded…** has no visible effect after opening a PNG. No file chooser appears and no layer is added. **File > Open…** works in the same session, and copying from a second document into the first with **Select > All**, **Edit > Copy**, **Edit > Paste** does add a separate pixel layer.

## Reproduction

1. Start the official PhotoCraft v0.3.0 Web build.
2. Open any PNG so a document is active.
3. Choose **File > Place Embedded…**.

**Expected:** A file chooser opens; the selected image is placed into the current document as an embedded Smart Object layer.

**Actual:** No chooser, new layer, status message, or error appears.

**Environment:** Windows 11 (10.0.26200), Chromium-based Codex in-app browser. Reproduced both in the standalone Web page and when embedded in a same-origin iframe. Tested with the unmodified official v0.3.0 JS/WASM release assets.

## Possible cause (source inspection, not yet confirmed by an upstream debugger)

In [apps/photocraft-web/src/web.rs](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/v0.3.0/apps/photocraft-web/src/web.rs#L149-L161), the Web pick_open service starts AsyncFileDialog, queues a selected file in the general open inbox, and immediately returns None. The [file.placeEmbedded handler](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/v0.3.0/crates/ui-egui/src/view_cmds.rs#L802-L808) expects pick_open to return (name, bytes) synchronously and returns early on None. This appears to prevent the chosen file from reaching file_cmds::place_bytes. The asynchronous dialog may also lose the browser's user activation before it can open.

## Workaround

Open the second image as a document, select all and copy it, switch back to the first document, then paste. This creates a separate pixel layer, although it is not equivalent to an embedded Smart Object.

title: Crash opening a 32-layer PSD: egui-wgpu panics "Failed to create staging buffer for index data"
author: Thundras
body:
**Environment:**
- PhotoCraft v0.3.0 (official release build)
- Windows, AMD Radeon RX Vega, Vulkan backend (discreteGpu), AMD proprietary driver 25.8.1

**Document:** 2554x3611 px PSD, 730 MB, 32 layers, plain pixel layers (no layer styles/effects)

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Open the file with "Use GPU" enabled (Preferences > Performance).
2. Loading progress bar reaches 100%, then the process exits silently - no error dialog, no Windows Event Viewer entry.

**Actual behavior:** Process exits with code 101 (an unhandled Rust panic unwound out of `main`). The panic text isn't visible under normal use because PhotoCraft is a GUI-subsystem binary - stderr isn't attached to a parent console even when launched from one; had to capture it via `Start-Process -RedirectStandardError`.

```
thread 'main' (5328) panicked at C:\Users\runneradmin\.cargo\registry\src\index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f\egui-wgpu-0.36.2\src\renderer.rs:984:17:
Failed to create staging buffer for index data. Index count: 38145. Required index buffer size: 152580. Actual size 164760 and capacity: 164760 (bytes)
```

**Workaround:** Disabling "Use GPU" (CPU compositor) opens the same file without issue - ruling out memory as a factor (tested with "Memory usage mb" raised from the 8192 default to 24000 on a 32 GB system; no effect on the GPU-enabled crash).

**Note:** this panics inside the vendored `egui-wgpu` 0.36.2 dependency's own UI-rendering index-buffer logic, not PhotoCraft's compositor code - looks unrelated to #1154.

title: [ Feature Request ] => Perspective Crop ✨
author: Overlord15
body:
## ✨ Feature Request: Perspective Crop

**Labels (suggested):** `enhancement`, `feature-request`, `crop-tool`, `good first discussion`
**Priority:** High

---

### Summary
Add a **Perspective Crop** tool to Photocraft that lets users select an arbitrary four-corner region of an image and warp it into a straight, rectangular result. This corrects photos taken from the wrong angle or point of view (POV).

### Problem / Motivation
People often snap photos at an angle: documents on a desk, whiteboards, book pages, signboards, framed art, or product shots. The result is a skewed, trapezoid-shaped subject. The standard rectangular crop can't fix this, so users have to leave Photocraft for another tool, or stack several transform steps by hand and still get an imperfect result.

Perspective cropping is one of the most commonly used crop operations in everyday photo editing. Without it, Photocraft is missing a feature users expect from a Photoshop alternative.

### Proposed Solution
Add a **Perspective Crop** option in the Crop tool group (alongside the standard crop).

**User flow**
1. User selects **Perspective Crop** from the toolbar or the Crop tool options.
2. Four draggable corner handles appear on the image (default: inset slightly from the image edges).
3. User drags each corner to match the corners of the real-world object (e.g. the four corners of a page).
4. A live overlay shows the selected quadrilateral, with the outside area dimmed.
5. User presses **Enter** or clicks **Apply**. The selected region is warped into a flat rectangle.
6. **Esc** or **Cancel** exits without changes.

- Draggable corner handles with a magnifier/zoom loupe for precise placement

title: [Feature Request] Publish PhotoCraft on winget
author: LeftTwixWand
body:
## Request

Publish PhotoCraft on [winget](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/package-manager/winget/) so Windows users can install and update it with:

```
winget install --id LearningMachines.PhotoCraft -e
```

`winget search photocraft` finds no package today (checked 2026-10-08 against the winget and Microsoft Store sources). The download page only links GitHub release artifacts.

## Why the current installers already fit

The Windows release is a signed, per-machine WiX MSI (`packaging/windows/photocraft.wxs`):

- Product name `PhotoCraft`, manufacturer `Learning Machines LLC`
- Stable `UpgradeCode` `D9660F32-2D0A-4ABE-B73D-17BE25F1542C`, with `AllowSameVersionUpgrades`
- Installs into Program Files, adds a Start Menu shortcut, and registers App Paths for `photocraft`
- Current release (v0.3.0) ships x64, x86, and ARM64 MSIs at stable GitHub release URLs, for example `photocraft-0.3.0-windows-x64.msi`

winget installs an MSI silently. The portable zips can stay off the manifest; the MSI is the package people should get from `winget install`.

## Suggested package

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| PackageIdentifier | `LearningMachines.PhotoCraft` |
| PackageName | PhotoCraft |
| Publisher | Learning Machines LLC |
| License | MIT OR Apache-2.0 |
| Homepage / LicenseUrl | https://getartcraft.com/apps/photocraft and the repo `LICENSE-MIT` / `LICENSE-APACHE` |
| Installers | the three release MSIs (`x64`, `x86`, `arm64`), scope `machine` |

`Storytold.PhotoCraft` is the other reasonable id (the GitHub org). `LearningMachines.PhotoCraft` matches the Manufacturer string already burned into the MSI, which is what winget and Apps & Features show.

## Keeping it current

A one-time PR to [microsoft/winget-pkgs](https://github.com/microsoft/winget-pkgs) covers 0.3.0. title: fix(layers): a new adjustment layer ignores the active selection (no layer mask)
author: Oldrich333
body:
> Agent-written on behalf of @Oldrich333 · agent: hive-admin/main · model: anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 · origin: owner-requested

## Summary
A new adjustment layer created while a selection is active gets no layer mask. Photoshop masks a new adjustment layer with the active selection (the selection becomes the layer mask). Scripts and agents that follow the Photoshop workflow (select → New Adjustment Layer) get an unmasked adjustment over the whole image.

## Runtime or environment
- PhotoCraft 0.3.0 release (`photocraft-0.3.0-linux-x86_64.tar.gz`, SHA256 verified against `SHA256SUMS.txt`), `photocraft-cli`, headless, Linux x86_64.
- Same code on `main` (e5e3e39): `new_adjustment` in `crates/engine/src/commands.rs` inserts the layer without reading `doc.selection`.

## Steps to reproduce
```sh
photocraft-cli run --new '{"width":400,"height":300,"background":"white"}' \
  --cmd select.rect --params '{"x":50,"y":50,"width":100,"height":100}' \
  --cmd layer.newAdjustmentLayer.hueSaturation --params '{"hue":40,"saturation":20}' \
  --out c1.pcraft
photocraft-cli info c1.pcraft --compact
```

## Expected behavior
The new `Adjustment` layer has a mask that reveals the 100×100 selection (`"hasMask": true`), the same result as running `layer.layerMask.revealSelection` on it.

## Actual behavior
- `run` → `{"command":"layer.newAdjustmentLayer.hueSaturation","result":{"layer":3}}`
- `info` → `"hasSelection":true,"selectionBounds":[50,50,100,100]`; layer 3 `"kind":"Adjustment","hasMask":false`.
- Control: appending `--cmd layer.layerMask.revealSelection` → layer 3 `"hasMask":true`.

## Notes
- Applies to every `layer.newAdjustmentLayer.*` command; new fill layers probably follow the same Photoshop rule.
- Related, not a duplicate: #1123 (operations on an existing mask).

title: fix(type): run, convert and info give no warning when text falls back from a missing font
author: Oldrich333
body:
> Agent-written on behalf of @Oldrich333 · agent: hive-admin/main · model: anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 · origin: owner-requested

## Summary
Text in a font that is not installed renders in a fallback face with no warning from `run`, `convert` or `info`. The missing font is detectable (`type.resolveMissingFonts` returns it), but only when the caller asks. An agent or script that renders a client PSD cannot tell that its PNG/JPG preview uses different glyphs and metrics than the original. VectorCraft already warns in this case (vectorcraft#319, vectorcraft PR #395: "exports warn when type in a missing font is written in the fallback font").

## Runtime or environment
- PhotoCraft 0.3.0 release (`photocraft-0.3.0-linux-x86_64.tar.gz`, SHA256 verified), `photocraft-cli`, headless, Linux x86_64; system fonts: Liberation, DejaVu; Arial not installed.

## Steps to reproduce
```sh
photocraft-cli run --new '{"width":600,"height":200,"background":"white"}' \
  --cmd type.create --params '{"x":20,"y":100,"text":"Hello Arial","font":"Arial","size":48,"color":"#000000"}' \
  --out c2.psd
photocraft-cli info c2.psd --compact
photocraft-cli convert c2.psd c2.png
photocraft-cli run c2.psd --cmd type.resolveMissingFonts --out c2_run.png
```

## Expected behavior
`run`, `convert` and `info` report the substitution, e.g. a `warnings` entry `{"kind":"missing_font","font":"Arial","used":"<fallback>","layers":[…]}` in the JSON result and one line on stderr for `convert`, as VectorCraft exports do.

## Actual behavior
- `run` (type.create with `"font":"Arial"`) → ok, no warning; `type.fonts {"family":"Arial"}` → `{"faces":[]}`.
- `info c2.psd --compact` → `"warnings":[]`, stderr empty.
- `convert c2.psd c2.png` → exit 0; stderr only `warning: 2 layer(s) flattened; layers, masks and blend modes are not kept`.
- `type.resolveMissingFonts` → `{"missing":["Arial"]}` (so the information exists).
- A nonexistent family (`"font":"NoSuchFontXYZ"`) is accepted silently too.

title: Linux build not compatable with VFX Reference Platform out of the box.
author: flipphillips
body:
### Description:

Launching the pre-packaged photocraft on a VFX Reference Platform machine (e.g., Rocky 9) [https://vfxplatform.com/linux/](https://vfxplatform.com/linux/) complains about wrong GLIBC version - 

```
λ photocraft --help
  photocraft: /lib64/libm.so.6: version `GLIBC_2.35' not found (required by photocraft)
```

### Notes: 

I'm sure that this limitation is described in the documentation somewhere, however, since the VFX Reference Platform is a sort of defacto-standard industry wise, I'm guessing you'll see a lot of use in that context. 

I'm further sure that flatpak and other solutions exist, but thought I'd point this out for future development issues.

λ photocraft --help
  photocraft: /lib64/libm.so.6: version `GLIBC_2.35' not found (required by photocraft)

### Cause of the Error

  • Your OS: Rocky Linux 9.8 (RHEL 9 family) ships with glibc 2.34.
  • The Package: The PhotoCraft 0.3.0 RPM was built on a system with glibc 2.35+ (Ubuntu 22.04 / newer Fedora).
  • The Conflict: PhotoCraft linked against hypot and hypotf in libm.so.6 using the GLIBC_2.35 symbol tag. Rocky Linux 9 provides these exact standard math functions under
  GLIBC_2.2.5. Every other library dependency in the binary already requires glibc 2.34 or older.
  ──────
  ### Resolution Applied

  The ELF version requirements for photocraft and photocraft-cli were patched so hypot/hypotf resolve against libm.so.6's GLIBC_2.2.5 version, eliminating the artificial
  GLIBC_2.35 blocker.

  The patched binaries have been installed into ~/.local/bin/ (which takes precedence over /usr/bin in your $PATH):

  • ~/.local/bin/photocraft
  • ~/.local/bin/photocraft-cli

title: Hidden ruler guides still intercept clicks and can be moved or deleted
author: DWAA1660
body:
## Report
Ruler guide lines remain interactive after they are hidden. Clicking or dragging where an invisible guide lies captures the guide instead of selecting or moving the layer beneath it. The guide can be moved, and the reporter says it may also be accidentally deleted.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Open a document with a visible layer.
2. Drag a guide from a ruler across the layer.
3. Hide the guides using the guide visibility control.
4. Use the Move tool to click/drag the layer at the hidden guide’s previous position.
5. Show the guides again to check whether the guide moved.

The invisible guide intercepts the pointer and is dragged instead of the intended layer. Accidental guide deletion is also reported; the exact deletion gesture was not specified.

## Expected behavior
Hidden guides should not capture clicks, drags, or guide-removal gestures. Layer selection/movement should work through their positions. Hiding and showing guides should preserve their positions. Visible, unlocked guides should remain draggable, and visible locked guides should respect their lock state.

## Suggested regression coverage
Cover horizontal and vertical guides with visibility disabled: the same pointer gesture should act on the layer and leave guide positions/count unchanged. Include visible-guide dragging as a control. Check hiding guides via their visibility toggle and any global Extras toggle that also hides them.

## Provenance and limits
User-reported PhotoCraft behavior, October 8, 2026. Not independently reproduced. OS, PhotoCraft version/build, and exact hide command were not provided. The steps above make the reported interaction concrete for verification.

Searched existing issues and PRs for hidden/invisible guides and guide hit-testing; no matching report or fix was found.

Speaking from my experience, which may not be extensive, I almost never need two instances of a graphics editor running. title: Free Transform: the W/H fields hard-clamp scale to 10000% (engine accepts more)
author: realjonnysax
body:
## Summary

The Width/Height fields in the Free Transform options bar hard-clamp scale to ±10000%. Large documents regularly need more — scaling a 2000-px overlay tile onto a 100000-px-wide stitched mosaic needs 5000%+, and larger tiles or canvases go past 10000%.

The transform engine itself has no scale limit: `edit.transform` accepts arbitrary matrices (its own tests use 1e9). The clamp is UI-only.

## Where

`crates/ui-egui/src/transform_tool.rs`, `transform_fields` (main @ e5e3e397):

```rust
// lines 1313-1323
let (mut w, mut h) = (sx as f32, sy as f32);
lbl(ui, "W:");
let rw = crate::widgets::value_field(ui, &mut w, -10000.0..=10000.0, "%", 66.0);
...
lbl(ui, "H:");
let rh = crate::widgets::value_field(ui, &mut h, -10000.0..=10000.0, "%", 66.0);
```

`value_field` → `number_edit` builds `egui::DragValue::new(value).range(range)` (`crates/ui-egui/src/widgets.rs:189-191`), so typed and scrubbed values clamp into the range.

Adjacent finding: the X/Y fields in the same bar clamp to **±30000 px** (lines 1302/1304) — below PhotoCraft's own 300000-px document limit (`artboard_cmds.rs:138`), so positions in a very large document are also unreachable by typing.

## Repro

1. Open a document larger than ~10000 px on a side (e.g. a stitched mosaic)
2. Select a smaller layer, run Free Transform
3. Type 15000 in W% → it applies as 10000

## Use case

Large-area light and electron microscopy stitches at the University of Pittsburgh Center for Biologic Imaging — mosaics tens of thousands of pixels wide with reference/overlay layers that must be scaled onto them. Free Transform on those overlays routinely needs >10000%.

## Suggested fix

Raise the W/H range (e.g. ±100000, or at least consistent with the 300000-px document limit); consider raising X/Y to the document limit too.

## Workaround

`edit.transform {"matrix": [k,0,0,k,0,0]}` via the CLI/JSON control channel accepts any scale (15000% = `[150,0,0,150,0,0]`).

title: macOS: save/export to writable SMB/NAS share fails with “Operation not supported (os error 45)”
author: joeteshima
body:
## Summary

PhotoCraft 0.5.0's CLI/MCP cannot export a PNG or save a native document to a writable SMB-mounted NAS share. Ordinary writes and POSIX fsync succeed on the same share, while a direct macOS F_FULLFSYNC probe fails with errno 45.

## Environment

- Mac mini, Apple silicon (arm64)
- macOS 27.0, build 26A428
- Official PhotoCraft 0.5.0 macOS release and CLI installed on local storage
- Writable SMB share mounted under `/Volumes/<share>/`

## Reproduction

1. Mount a writable SMB share and create a test folder.
2. Start `photocraft-cli --automation-read-root "/Volumes/<share>/craft-test" --automation-write-root "/Volumes/<share>/craft-test" mcp`.
3. Use MCP `doc_new` to create a 64 × 64 document.
4. Call `doc_export` with `{"path":"photo.png","format":"png"}`.
5. Also try `doc_save` with `{"path":"photo.pcraft"}`.

Both operations failed in our tests. The captured export error was:

```text
I/O: automation write `verification/nas-file-check/photo.png` failed (Uncategorized): Operation not supported (os error 45)
```

Repeating outside the agent execution sandbox produced the same failure.

## Filesystem comparison

| Operation on the same share | Result |
|---|---|
| Ordinary file write | Success |
| POSIX fsync | Success |
| fcntl(fd, F_FULLFSYNC), macOS command 51 | errno 45: Operation not supported |

[RealFs::write_new](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/main/crates/format/src/atomic.rs) calls `File::sync_all()` and propagates errors. title: Mouse cursor lag — SurfaceConfig::HIGH_THROUGHPUT is wrong default for an image   editor
author: VoronBrothers-VoronBrothers
body:
## Problem

    PhotoCraft has noticeable mouse cursor latency (~50-70ms) on Linux X11 with NVIDIA GPU. The crosshair/brush
    cursor trails behind the physical mouse position, making precise painting difficult. This occurs in both
    release and debug builds.

    ## Root cause

    eframe's default `WgpuConfiguration` uses `SurfaceConfig::HIGH_THROUGHPUT`:
    - `present_mode: PresentMode::AutoVsync`
    - `desired_maximum_frame_latency: Some(2)`

    This queues up to 2 frames in the GPU pipeline before presentation, adding ~32ms of latency at 60Hz on top of
    the X11/NVIDIA driver's own presentation delay. Total input-to-cursor-display latency reaches 3-4 frames.

    ## Expected behavior
    For an image editing application where cursor precision is critical, `SurfaceConfig::LOW_LATENCY` should be
    used:
    - `present_mode: PresentMode::AutoVsync` (keep vsync for smoothness)
    - `desired_maximum_frame_latency: Some(1)` (reduce pipeline queue to 1 frame)

    This cuts latency by ~16ms with no practical FPS impact for a GUI app.

    ## Suggested fix

    In `main.rs`, override the default wgpu surface config in `NativeOptions`:

    fn native_options() -> eframe::NativeOptions {
    let mut options = eframe::NativeOptions { /* ... */ };

    // Use low-latency presentation for responsive cursor
    tracking:
    // HIGH_THROUGHPUT (default) queues 2 frames; LOW_LATENCY queues
    1.
    options.wgpu_options.surface = egui_wgpu::SurfaceConfig::LOW_LATENCY;

    options
    }

    ## Environment
    - OS: Kubuntu 26.04, KDE Plasma X11
    - GPU: NVIDIA RTX 5060 Ti (proprietary driver 595.91.07)
    - wgpu: 30.0.1, eframe: 0.36.2
    - App version: 0.5.0

    ## Impact
    This affects ALL users on X11 with discrete GPUs (NVIDIA/AMD). The effect is most noticeable during brush
    strokes and fine cursor positioning. On high-refresh-rate displays (144Hz+) it's slightly less bad but still
    present.

title: fix(docs): crates/codecs/README.md still says WebP is written lossless only
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

The codec crate's README says PhotoCraft cannot write lossy WebP, but v0.5.0 does: a `--quality` conversion writes a lossy VP8 WebP. The book's raster-formats page already describes the lossy encoder, so the two documents now disagree.

## Runtime or environment

The official macOS universal CLI from the v0.5.0 release (tag commit `e5e3e397523b4db6a016dd19526e4c68514fcc72`, also `main` on 2026-10-08), on macOS 27.0.1 arm64. `photocraft-cli --version` prints:

```text
photocraft-cli 0.5.0 (e5e3e3975, 2026-10-08)
```

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create a 12×8 RGBA PNG with every pixel (200,40,90,128), for example with Pillow: `python3 -c "from PIL import Image; Image.new('RGBA',(12,8),(200,40,90,128)).save('alpha.png')"`.
2. Run `photocraft-cli convert alpha.png default.webp` and `photocraft-cli convert alpha.png lossy.webp --quality 70`.
3. Read the chunk type at byte offset 12 of each file (`xxd -s 12 -l 4 <file>`), and for `lossy.webp` also the `VP8 ` chunk that follows the `VP8X` header.
4. Compare with `crates/codecs/README.md`, the WebP row of the capability matrix and the "Lossy WebP" bullet.

The codec README describes what the codecs do in the default build. ## Summary

In the desktop app's Export As dialog, a Scale that changes the height but not the rounded width is ignored: the dialog shows the scaled size, and the exported file has the original size. Observed with a 1 × 100 and a 1 × 200 document exported at 50%, which the dialog labels 1 × 50 and 1 × 100 and which are written as 1 × 100 and 1 × 200.

## Runtime or environment

2. File › Export › Export As (⌥⇧⌘W). Keep Format PNG.

title: Monitor Profile detection fails and leaks raw ICC profile bytes into error text (scientific-notation display ID)
author: misterlumiere
body:
On macOS, PhotoCraft's display-profile detection fails for me, which causes two visible problems:
1. A persistent notice card ("Display profile not used") fills a large portion of the window with a wall of raw base64 text instead of a short message.
2. Edit › Color Settings shows the same raw dump inline in "Monitor profile in use: …".

**Root cause**, traced in `apps/photocraft/src/monitor_profile.rs`:

- The AppleScript helper (`SCRIPT`) builds each display's line as `n & tab & ...` where `n` is `NSScreenNumber as integer`. For my display, this `CGDirectDisplayID` is large enough that AppleScript's string coercion renders it in scientific notation (e.g. `2.077748985E+9`) instead of a plain integer.
- `parse_reply()` parses that field with `id.trim().parse::<u32>()` (around line 124), which rejects scientific notation, so the `let-else` discards the whole display row via `continue`.
- With only one physical display (MacBook built-in Retina), discarding that row leaves `displays` empty, which trips:
  ```rust
  return Err(format!("couldn't read the display list: {first}"));
  ```
  where `first` is the **entire raw unparsed line** — id, frame, and the full base64-encoded ICC profile, tab-separated (line ~140).
- That raw string then propagates untouched into `MonitorStatus.reason`, and gets surfaced verbatim in both the Color Settings summary (`crates/ui-egui/src/monitor_status.rs::note()`) and as a Notice (`monitor_status::apply()` → `notices::post()`), whose line-count cap (`MAX_LINES = 8`) doesn't help since it's one unbroken line that just word-wraps to fill the window.

Net effect: color management for this display silently falls back to sRGB (it's not just a cosmetic bug — the canvas isn't using my display's actual P3 profile).

**Suggested fix:**
1. Make display-ID parsing robust to scientific notation (either force plain-integer formatting in the AppleScript, e.g. an explicit text coercion that avoids scientific notation, or parse the Rust side via `f64::fro…

title: Security checkup of the project
author: alexpyattaev
body:
Awesome project, like the vibe of it! To keep you guys safe, here are some ideas how to harden the supply chain a bit. Hope you find these helpful!

## Findings

1. High — unpinned executable downloaded beside Azure signing secrets

packaging/windows/sign.ps1:73 downloads latest `Microsoft.Trusted.Signing.Client` package without version or checksum, loads its DLL into `signtool`, and exposes Azure credentials through environment.

Compromised NuGet package could steal signing credentials or alter signed binaries. Pin exact package version and verify hash/signature before loading.

2. High — release actions using mutable tags

Signing jobs use mutable action tags before secret-bearing steps:

- .github/workflows/release.yml:76: `actions/checkout@v4`
- Line 83: `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable`
- Line 86: `Swatinem/rust-cache@v2`
- Windows equivalents at lines 143–153
- Artifact actions also use mutable tags

Compromised action could modify scripts, binaries, PATH, or runner state before signing secrets become available. Pin every release action to commit SHA.

3. Medium — downloaded release tools lack integrity checks

Examples:

- `nfpm` downloaded then installed: .github/workflows/release.yml:214
- `trunk` archive piped into `tar`: .github/workflows/release.yml:357
- Moving `continuous` AppImage tool downloaded and executed: packaging/linux/package.sh:109
- Rustup piped to shell in FreeBSD job

Those jobs mostly lack signing secrets, but compromise could infect release artifacts. Pin versions and verify SHA-256.

title: Free Transform: allow blend mode and opacity edits during the transform, like Photoshop
author: realjonnysax
body:
Photoshop lets you change a layer's blend mode and opacity while Free Transform is active — the canvas preview updates live. PhotoCraft refuses the edit (*"Commit or cancel the transform first"*, `transform_tool.rs:594`) until the transform is committed.

Two problems:

1. **Parity** — adjusting blend/opacity mid-transform is part of the standard workflow (e.g. tuning how an overlay sits while scaling it onto a mosaic). Having to commit first breaks the loop.
2. **Discoverability** — a lingering session (handles off-screen on a huge canvas) makes the sliders look simply dead, with no hint why. Enter commits, but on huge layers the commit itself runs a multi-second resample first, so it feels stuck twice over.

The compositor already re-plans on blend/opacity changes, so applying them live during the transform preview should fall out of the existing pipeline.

Environment: v0.3.0, Windows. Real-world case: large stitched mosaics with overlay layers ([realjonnysax/photocraft-crash-samples](https://github.com/realjonnysax/photocraft-crash-samples), context in #1015).

title: New Document: localized preset titles overflow their cards
author: SckraT
body:
## Bug
In **File › New** (New Document dialog), long translated preset titles are drawn past the edges of their preset cards.

The most visible case is the Russian UI: the first card on the default **Recent** tab, `Default Photoshop Size` → «Размер Photoshop по умолчанию», overflows the card on both sides as soon as the dialog opens. Other languages have the same problem, e.g. es «Tamaño predeterminado de Photoshop» and some it / pt-br titles.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Set the interface language to Russian (or start with a `ru` system locale).
2. Press Ctrl+N.
3. Look at the «Размер Photoshop по умолчанию» card on the «Недавние» tab.

**Expected:** the title stays inside the card.
**Actual:** the title is centred on the card and spills past both edges.

## Cause
In `crates/ui-egui/src/new_doc_ui.rs`, cards have a fixed width (`card = vec2(164.0, 112.0)`) and the title is painted with:

```rust
ui.painter().text(pos2(r.center().x, r.top() + 72.0), Align2::CENTER_CENTER, tl!(p.0), FontId::proportional(12.0), t.text);
```

`Painter::text` lays out a single line with no wrapping or clipping, so any string wider than about 150 px overflows. English strings happen to fit. Some translations (cs «Výchozí velikost», ja «既定サイズ») look like they were shortened to work around this.

## Proposed solution
- Lay the title out with a `LayoutJob`: `wrap.max_width = card.x - 12`, `wrap.max_rows = 2`, `halign = Align::Center`. Draw it with `painter.galley(...)`, centred vertically between the page icon and the size line.
- Move the size line down slightly (top + 90 → top + 97) so two-line titles don't collide with it. The 112 px card height is enough.
- If a title still doesn't fit in two lines, elide it with `…` and show the full name as a hover tooltip on the card.
- Add a unit test that every preset title in every language fits the card width in ≤ 2 lines without eliding, so a future translation can't regress this silently.

The fix is UI-only, so translations don't need to change.…

title: PSD type layers written without pixels (ag-psd, GIMP) open empty; their PostScript font name is reported missing although installed
author: diegochagas
body:
## What happens

A PSD whose type layers were written by [ag-psd](https://github.com/Agamnentzar/ag-psd) (and by GIMP's PSD exporter, and the GIMPhoto `psd-text` plug-in, which uses ag-psd) opens in PhotoCraft 0.5.0 with every type layer **empty**: nothing on the canvas, Properties shows W 0 px × H 0 px, the status bar says "Could not transform: the layer is empty" when you try to move one. The text, font, size and paragraph settings are all read correctly (the Character panel and `photocraft-cli info` show them). Photoshop and GIMP render the same file fine.

The same file also reports its font as missing although it is installed: the layer's font is `CCWildWords-Regular` (PostScript name, installed, listed by *Type › List Fonts* as family `CCWildWords`), but PhotoCraft looks for the family "CC Wild Words" and *Replace All Missing Fonts* replaces it.

## Reproduce

Any PSD with a type layer and no image data for it (such writers leave the channels empty and rely on Photoshop re-rendering the type on open). Headless:

```sh
photocraft-cli info page.psd --compact
# every Type layer: "bounds":[0,0,0,0], "text":{"font":"CC Wild Words","sizePt":7.68,"text":"Viver é maravilhoso!"}
photocraft-cli convert page.psd page.png     # no text in the PNG
photocraft-cli run page.psd --cmd type.replaceAllMissingFonts --out page2.png
# {"missing":["CC Wild Words"],"replaced":7}  and now the text shows, in the default font
```

Fonts: `CCWildWords-Regular.ttf` installed in `~/.local/share/fonts`; `fc-query` says family `CCWildWords`, PostScript `CCWildWords-Regular`; `photocraft-cli run page.psd --cmd type.fonts` lists `CCWildWords`.

1. `crates/io/src/psd_import.rs`: for a `TySh` layer the importer always sets `t.cache = Some(record_surface(...))`, so a record without pixels becomes an **empty cache**, and the compositor draws the cache (`Layer::surface()`); nothing renders the layer from its model until it is edited.

title: Add RTL (right-to-left) language support (Persian, Arabic, Hebrew, Urdu)
author: mzi2020
body:
## Summary

PhotoCraft currently has no way to render text or layout in right-to-left (RTL) mode. Users who write in Persian/Farsi, Arabic, Hebrew, Urdu, and other RTL languages can't use the app properly, since text direction, alignment, and UI layout all assume left-to-right.

## Problem

- Text added to images/templates is laid out left-to-right, so RTL text appears misaligned, with punctuation and numbers in the wrong places.
- There is no option to switch text direction (LTR / RTL / auto).
- Alignment options ("left" / "right") are physical rather than logical, so they don't flip for RTL content.
- The UI itself (toolbars, panels, menus, icons) can't be mirrored for RTL locales.
- Mixed content (e.g. Persian text with English words or numbers) isn't handled with proper bidirectional (bidi) behavior.

## Expected behavior

1. A **text direction** setting (LTR / RTL / Auto-detect) for text elements.
2. Logical alignment options ("start" / "end") in addition to left/right/center.
3. Correct bidi rendering for mixed-direction text, including numbers and punctuation.
4. An optional **RTL UI mode** that mirrors the layout (panels, toolbars, directional icons) based on locale or a manual toggle.
5. Support for RTL-friendly fonts and correct glyph shaping/joining for Arabic-script languages (letters must connect properly).

## Suggested approach

- Use the CSS `direction` property and `dir="rtl"` / `dir="auto"` on text containers.
- Prefer CSS logical properties (`margin-inline-start`, `padding-inline-end`, `text-align: start`) over physical left/right.
- If text is drawn on a canvas, set `ctx.direction` and make sure the text shaping engine handles Arabic-script joining.
- Add an i18n layer with a locale flag that controls UI mirroring.

## Why this matters

Hundreds of millions of people use RTL languages. Without this support, PhotoCraft is effectively unusable for them, and even basic captions or watermarks come out broken.

## Additional context

Happy to help tes…

title: feat(ui): Edit › Stroke… dialog with Width, Color, Location and Blending options
author: eduardomineo
body:
## Summary

Give Edit › Stroke… Photoshop's Stroke dialog: Width, Color, Location (Inside, Center, Outside)
and Blending (Mode, Opacity, Preserve Transparency). Today the menu item runs `edit.stroke`
immediately with fixed defaults, so the user can't choose any option and often sees no change.

## Problem to solve

`edit.stroke` is implemented in the engine (`crates/engine/src/extra_cmds.rs:117`, registered at
`:610`) with `width` (1–250), `color` (default foreground), `location` (default `center`) and
`opacity`. The UI exposes none of them. `menus.rs` opens a dialog for `edit.fill` when it comes
without params (`crates/ui-egui/src/menus.rs:347`), but `edit.stroke` has no such arm and falls
through to `app.run(id, params)` (`:464`) with empty params. The Edit menu entry
(`crates/ui-egui/src/menu_catalog.rs:96`) and the canvas context menu entry
(`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas_tool_menu.rs:60`) both take this path.

With those defaults, Stroke draws a 1 px foreground-colour band. Without a selection it follows the
active layer's opaque edge. A fully opaque layer, such as a new document's Background, has no such
edge inside the canvas: `sel::expand` and `sel::contract` of an all-ones mask both return all ones,
so the band is empty and the command succeeds without changing a pixel or showing a message.

The generic parameter dialog (`crates/ui-egui/src/filter_dialog.rs`) can't stand in. `parse_spec`
has no colour kind, so `"color":"#rrggbb|[r,g,b,a]"=foreground` would be offered as a choice
between the literal strings `#rrggbb` and `[r,g,b,a]`, and a choice starts at its first value, so
Location would open at Inside instead of Center.

The engine also lacks two of Photoshop's options: `edit.stroke` takes no blend `mode` and no
`preserveTransparency`. It follows the layer's transparency lock instead
(`doc.effective_locks(id).transparency`). `edit.fill` already supports both.

## Proposed behavior

- Edit › Stroke… and the canvas context menu's Stroke… open a Stroke dialog w…

title: Pen Tool - Missing handle control on last point and "Make Selection" options
author: onikoge
body:
Hello!

I'd like to report two missing features related to the Pen Tool in PhotoCraft and VectorCraft.

1. Handle control on the last point while drawing

The issue:
In most vector and raster editors (Photoshop, Affinity Designer, Illustrator, etc.), you can adjust the bezier handles of the last placed point without interrupting the curve you're drawing.

In Affinity, clicking the pen on the last point resets the outgoing handle — the point becomes a corner point, so the next segment can be straight or its curvature defined by the next point.

In Photoshop, the same is done by clicking with Alt held down.

What happens in PhotoCraft
This functionality is currently unavailable. As a result, the Pen Tool loses much of its flexibility — you can't switch between smooth and corner points on the fly without breaking the path.

Suggestion:
Add (or restore) the ability to control the last point's handle while drawing — matching Affinity (click on point) and Photoshop (Alt + click). This would make the Pen Tool fully functional and on par with reference editors.

2. "Make Selection" options (Selection from Path)

The issue:
In Photoshop, when converting a path into a selection, the Make Selection dialog offers:

Feather — softens the mask edges;

Anti-aliased — smooths jagged edges;

Operation: New Selection, Add, Subtract, Intersect with the existing selection.

What happens in PhotoCraft / VectorCraft:
There is no equivalent dialog or set of operations — the path either can't be converted to a selection, or it is converted without control over feathering and boolean operations with the current mask.

Suggestion:
Add a "Make Selection" feature with Feather, Anti-alias, and Add / Subtract / Intersect modes — matching Photoshop's behavior.

Thank you!

title: [Feature request]: Android support with a touch-first mobile UI
author: MrMR-711
body:
Summary

I would love to see PhotoCraft support Android devices, with a responsive, touch-friendly interface designed specifically for phones and tablets.

PhotoCraft's goal of becoming an open-source alternative to Photoshop is exciting. Android support could make the project accessible to users who do not have access to a desktop computer, while also extending its reach to tablet users who want to edit images on the go.

Motivation

Simply compiling the existing desktop application for ARM64 would not be enough to make PhotoCraft practical on a phone. A desktop interface designed for a mouse and a large display can be difficult to use on a small touchscreen.

The goal should be to make PhotoCraft genuinely usable on mobile devices, rather than merely making the desktop binary run on Android.

Proposed scope

1. Android compatibility

- Investigate a viable Android build and packaging workflow, ideally producing an installable APK.
- Review platform-specific requirements for windowing, graphics, file access, clipboard operations, and application lifecycle.
- Reuse the existing Rust engine and editing functionality wherever practical, avoiding unnecessary duplication.

2. Responsive, touch-first interface

- Adapt the interface to phone and tablet screen sizes while preserving the existing desktop experience.
- Use collapsible panels, compact toolbars, and contextual controls to maximize canvas space on phones.
- Provide touch-friendly controls and appropriately sized interaction targets.
- Make layers, properties, tools, dialogs, and menus accessible on narrow screens.
- Support canvas gestures such as pinch-to-zoom and two-finger panning, while keeping painting and other editing gestures predictable.

3. Mobile editing workflow

- Integrate Android's file picker and storage mechanisms for opening, saving, and exporting images.
- Consider memory usage, GPU compatibility, battery consumption, and performance on mobile hardware.

title: Packaged the Crafting Apps for omapak — and six metainfo templates have broken screenshots
author: joniler
body:
Hi — a heads-up rather than a request, and one bug report that's yours to fix if you want it fixed.

We've packaged twelve of the Crafting Apps for [omapak](https://omapak.org), an open Flatpak repo, and the submissions are open as PRs now: PhotoCraft 0.5.0, LightCraft 0.4.0, VectorCraft 0.6.0, PdfCraft 0.4.0, DesignCraft 0.4.0, EffectCraft 0.6.0, FilmCraft 0.4.0, GridCraft 0.3.0, WordCraft 0.3.0, DeckCraft 0.3.0, CADCraft 0.3.0, SoundCraft 0.3.0.

Filing on this repo rather than opening twelve issues, since the packaging and the bug below are shared across all of them.

## How they're packaged

Each manifest is your own `packaging/linux/flatpak/ai.storyteller.<app>.bundle.yml` — the one behind the `.flatpak` you attach to every release — unchanged except for the sources. Those become the release tarball per arch (x86_64 and aarch64), pinned by sha256, with `x-checker-data` pointed at your releases API. So we ship the same binaries you publish, and when you tag a release the version, URL and digest get bumped automatically and the result is rebuilt without anyone here editing a manifest.

Runtime, command, `finish-args`, `add-extensions` and the install steps are all yours, untouched, comments included.

We deliberately didn't use the from-source manifests: `cargo-sources.json` would need regenerating from `Cargo.lock` on every release, which flatpak-external-data-checker can't do, so automatic release tracking wouldn't actually work.

ArtCraft itself isn't in the set — its releases ship only `.dmg`/`.exe`/`.msi`, so there's no Linux artifact to package.

title: Affinity export: write .af documents that Affinity opens
author: callmeBalloch
body:
Native Affinity import landed in #1607 (see also #1126; VectorCraft: storytold/vectorcraft#667). Writing Affinity files is not implemented. It needs:

- A writer for the container (header, `#FAT`/`#FT2` tables, zlib/zstd entries, CRCs, the `Thmb` preview record) and the object stream in `doc.dat`, with the version, class and field tags Affinity expects.
- A decision on what is written:
  - our own layers mapped back to Affinity's;
  - unknown records from an imported file carried through unchanged (a round trip);
  - or a minimal document that Affinity is known to accept.
- **Validation in Affinity itself.** Every file written must be opened in Affinity 2 and 3, on macOS and Windows, compared against our render, and saved again by Affinity. No contributor on this has had an Affinity installation so far. Until someone can run those checks, export stays "unsupported": shipping files nobody has opened in Affinity would risk users' work.

The `synth` builders in `crates/affinity` write containers our reader accepts, but they are test fixtures, not an exporter: Affinity has never opened their output.

title: Affinity import: effects, adjustments, brushes, master pages and other remaining gaps
author: callmeBalloch
body:
Native import (#1607) reports each of these in the open warning, but doesn't import them yet. They are listed roughly by how often they came up in 176 of the 189 distinct public sample documents (an earlier run):

- [ ] Layer effects (shadows, glows, outlines, bevels…) and live filters.
- [ ] Adjustment layers.
- [ ] Brush and pressure strokes (imported as plain strokes).
- [ ] Master pages and their instances (Publisher).
- [ ] Symbols and embedded documents as live content (they come in as Affinity's cached picture).
- [ ] Special shapes: cloud, heart, cog, callouts, arrows… (imported as their bounding ellipse).
- [ ] Transparency gradients, fill opacity and bitmap fills.
- [ ] Conical gradients (imported as circular).
- [ ] Corner types other than round; stars with rounded points.
- [ ] Several fills or strokes on one object (one of each is used).
- [ ] Text: outlined or scaled text, fields (page numbers…), frames with columns or a curved outline.
- [ ] Documents in CMYK, Lab, grey or 16/32-bit (opened as 8-bit RGB). Per bflatastic's review on #1607:
  - [ ] Convert colour through `photocraft-cms`: Lab and CMYK through a transform, not `Color::to_rgb` (`io/src/affinity.rs`).
  - [ ] Keep the depth of 16-bit pixel layers instead of reducing them to 8-bit (`raster.rs`).
- [ ] Affinity-only blend modes (Average, Negation, Reflect, Glow, Erase).

Each item should come with a public, permissively licensed sample (added to the pinned corpus manifest) and a ceiling in the corpus test.

title: Web build: an embedding API to open and save documents from the host page
author: wangbingjie1
body:
### What
A small API so a page that embeds the PhotoCraft web build (for example in an iframe) can hand it a document and get the edited document back.

### Why
We run PhotoCraft headless through `photocraft-cli mcp` inside an AI agent's sandbox, and want people to open the same document in the web build to touch it up by hand. Today the web build opens files only through File › Open or drag-and-drop (the inbox in `WebShell`, `apps/photocraft-web/src/web.rs`), and saving always triggers a browser download (`services()` → `write` → `download()`), so the host page can neither load a document nor receive the result.

FilmCraft already has this shape (`window.filmcraft`, `apps/filmcraft-web/src/api.rs`), and so does EffectCraft.

### Proposal (the shape is yours to choose)
- `open(bytes, name)`: open `.pcraft`, PSD or PNG from an ArrayBuffer.
- `save(format)`: return `.pcraft` (single-file ZIP), PSD or PNG bytes to the caller instead of downloading.
- A change notification (an event or `isDirty()`), so the host knows when to offer saving.
- Optional: `request(method, params)` routed through `ControlRequest` / `PhotocraftApp::with_control`, the same methods as the desktop control channel.
- Exposed as `window.photocraft`, plus a `postMessage` mirror for cross-origin embedding, with the allowed parent origin passed in (e.g. `?embed=<origin>`).
- `info()` with the app and `.pcraft` format versions, so a host can keep the CLI and the web build on the same version (`FormatError::TooNew`).

Happy to test a branch against our host.

title: Web build: load CJK fonts next to the wasm so Chinese text renders
author: wangbingjie1
body:
### What
In the web build, Chinese, Japanese and Korean text in type layers and in the UI renders as empty boxes.

### Why it happens
On wasm, `Sources::system()` in `crates/ui-egui/src/cjk_fonts.rs` has no system fonts to read, and the web build embeds no craft-fonts, because the wasm has to stay under the 24 MiB gate in `packaging/web/package.sh` (#237). `crates/text/build.rs` already notes that the web build keeps no Japanese font until craft-fonts can be served next to the wasm instead of inside it.

### Proposal
- Serve font files next to the wasm and fetch them lazily on the first missing glyph for a script.
- Include a Simplified Chinese face (for example Noto Sans SC, OFL). The Japanese craft-fonts faces don't cover many Simplified Chinese characters.
- Let the embedding page add fonts too (e.g. `addFont(bytes)` in the embedding API proposed in #1614), for hosts that serve their own fonts.

The same gap exists in the siblings: storytold/pdfcraft#381 and storytold/pdfcraft#234, storytold/filmcraft#40, storytold/lightcraft#425.

title: Release: a standalone Linux CLI archive
author: wangbingjie1
body:
### What
Publish `photocraft-cli-<version>-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` (and aarch64) next to the existing `photocraft-cli-<version>-macos-universal.zip`, listed in `SHA256SUMS.txt`.

### Why
On Linux the CLI ships only inside the desktop packages (`packaging/linux/package.sh` installs `usr/bin/photocraft-cli` next to the app; the v0.5.0 x86_64 tarball is about 67 MB). Servers, CI and AI agent sandboxes only need the headless CLI, which has no GPU or display dependencies. A CLI-only archive makes it a small, verifiable download.

### Nice to have
State the minimum glibc in the release notes (the Linux release builds on `ubuntu-22.04` runners, so glibc 2.35, as `release.yml` notes), or ship a static musl build.

title: MCP: an MCP Apps view (ui://) for document previews
author: wangbingjie1
body:
### What
Attach an MCP Apps UI resource (`_meta.ui.resourceUri` → `ui://photocraft/...`, MIME `text/html;profile=mcp-app`) to tools such as `doc_render_preview` and `doc_inspect`, so MCP Apps hosts can show an interactive preview: the rendered image, the layer list, and a few actions that call the existing tools.

### Why
Today `photocraft-cli mcp` returns images and JSON only. With a small view, people can see and steer what the agent is doing without leaving the chat, even when no desktop app is running.

### Notes
- Keep the view light, without wasm: some hosts block WebAssembly and workers inside MCP App iframes and cap the HTML resource size.
- The full web editor as an MCP App could come later, on top of the embedding API proposed in #1614.

title: Automation: a 12 MP photo needs ~790 MiB to open, adjust and export headless
author: wangbingjie1
body:
### What
In headless automation (`photocraft-cli mcp`), peak memory for everyday photos is many times the image size, so a typical phone photo does not fit in the memory caps agent sandboxes put on tool processes.

### Measurements
photocraft-cli 0.5.0, linux-x86_64 release, headless MCP, Debian 13; peak RSS = VmHWM of the server process. Under a 512 MiB cgroup limit (swap off) the process is OOM-killed in the cases marked ✗.

Single-layer photo: `doc_open` → brightness/contrast via `command_run` → export JPEG

| Photo | Peak RSS | Time | 512 MiB cap |
|---|---|---|---|
| 12 MP (4000×3000) | 791 MiB | 2.6 s | ✗ killed during the brightness step |
| 24 MP (6000×4000) | 1,571 MiB | 4.3 s | ✗ |

New document + 3 fill layers + Gaussian blur + save `.pcraft` + export PSD

| Canvas | Peak RSS | 512 MiB cap |
|---|---|---|
| 2000×1500 | 212 MiB | ✓ |
| 3000×2000 | 408 MiB | ✓ |
| 4000×3000 | 586 MiB | ✗ (during PSD export) |
| 6000×4000 | 964 MiB | ✗ |

For the 12 MP photo, an 8-bit RGBA buffer is about 46 MiB, so the peak is roughly 17× the image. We have not profiled where it goes; full-resolution copies kept for undo, per-step adjustment buffers and export encoding are the usual suspects.

### Proposals
- An option to bound or disable undo history in headless sessions (agents rarely undo; they re-open the saved file).
- Process adjustments and export in tiles or strips so peak memory stays a small multiple of the image size.
- A memory budget option (e.g. `--memory-budget 512M`) that fails a command with a clear tool error instead of being OOM-killed mid-call.
- Document the expected peak memory per megapixel for headless use.

Related: #212 (recovering from out-of-memory), #49 (very large images).

title: feat(web): Publish the browser build at an official URL
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

Every release already attaches a host-ready static site (`photocraft-web-<ver>.zip`), and the README lists the web as a supported platform, but the project hosts no copy of it. Publish the web build at an official URL, keep it updated from CI, and link it from the README, so anyone can try PhotoCraft in a browser with one click.

## Problem to solve

The README says the whole engine and UI compile to WebAssembly and lists "Web" next to macOS, Windows, Linux and FreeBSD. To actually run the browser version today, a person has to download the release zip, unzip it, and serve it with a static file server or the Docker image described in `packaging/web/README.md`. That is a larger step than installing the desktop app, and it is the opposite of what a browser build usually offers: a link that opens the app.

The pieces needed to host it already exist and work:

- `release.yml`'s `Web (wasm)` job builds the site with `packaging/web/package.sh` on every release; the last three release runs of that job took 5 to 7 minutes.
- `apps/photocraft-web/Trunk.toml` sets `public_url = "./"`, and `package.sh` rejects any root-absolute URL in `index.html`, so the site works under a sub-path such as a project Pages URL (`https://<owner>.github.io/<repo>/`).
- `packaging/web/README.md` › Required server settings says the app needs no `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy` or `Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy` headers, so a plain static host with HTTPS is enough.

I served the unmodified v0.5.0 release zip with `python3 -m http.server` from a nested path (`/project/photocraft-web-0.5.0/`) and opened it in Chromium: the wasm loaded, the console logged `wgpu backend BrowserWebGpu` and `event handlers installed`, and the page removed its loading placeholder.

## Proposed behavior

- An official HTTPS URL serves the PhotoCraft web build. GitHub Pages for this repository is the lowest-effort option, since the build already runs on GitHub Actions; another static host the project controls also sa…

title: feat(ci): Build the web app and run its wasm size gate on pull requests
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

Pull-request CI never builds `apps/photocraft-web` or runs the 24 MiB wasm size gate in `packaging/web/package.sh`; only the release workflow does. Add a pull-request check that runs the real web build and its gate, so a change that breaks the web app or pushes the wasm over the limit fails on its own PR instead of at release time.

## Problem to solve

`packaging/web/package.sh` fails the build when a `.wasm` file exceeds 24 MiB (Cloudflare's per-file cap is 25 MiB) or when `index.html` contains root-absolute URLs. Its comment states the intent: fail "well before that so a regression shows up here, not at upload time." That script runs only in `release.yml`'s `Web (wasm)` job.

The `wasm32 check` job in `ci.yml` runs `cargo xtask wasm`, which is `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` on the L0 to L5 crates, `photocraft-ui-egui`, and the standalone crates. `xtask/src/layers.rs` classifies `photocraft-web` as `Exempt`, so the web app crate itself is not checked, and no pull-request job runs `trunk build --release`, wasm-opt, the relative-URL check or the size gate.

The wasm size has moved quickly and close to the gate. Measured from each release's `photocraft-web-<ver>.zip`:

| Release | Published | `_bg.wasm` bytes | MiB | Headroom to 24 MiB gate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| v0.2.0 | 2026-10-05 | 27,072,762 | 25.82 | over (gate did not exist yet; issue #198) |
| v0.3.0 | 2026-10-07 | 24,710,609 | 23.57 | 0.43 MiB |
| v0.5.0 | 2026-10-08 | 22,602,197 | 21.56 | 2.44 MiB |

The gate was added with the fix for #198, when the wasm measured 18.8 MiB. Two days later v0.3.0 shipped within 0.43 MiB of it. A pull request in that window that added half a MiB of wasm would have passed every PR check and failed only in the release workflow, after merge, blocking the release.

## Proposed behavior

- A CI job on pull requests runs the same web build the release uses (`packaging/web/package.sh`, or `trunk build --release` plus the same checks) and fails the PR whe…

title: JPEG: resolution stored in EXIF is ignored (opens at 72 ppi instead of the camera's 300), and saving writes a contradicting JFIF density
author: switch87
body:
## Problem

A JPEG straight from a Nikon D3200 opens in Photoshop at **300 ppi** and in PhotoCraft at **72 ppi**. The two apps then disagree on print size, and sizes in cm/inch, Image Size and type sizes in pt differ for the same file.

The camera stores its resolution only in **EXIF** (IFD0 `XResolution` / `YResolution` = 300, `ResolutionUnit` = inches) and writes no JFIF APP0 segment. PhotoCraft's JPEG reader (`crates/codecs/src/codecs/jpeg.rs`) takes the resolution only from the JFIF APP0 density, so with no JFIF segment it falls back to 72 ppi. Many phone and camera JPEGs are like this.

## Saved files contradict themselves

Saving that photo again as JPEG from PhotoCraft writes a JFIF segment with 72 ppi and keeps the original EXIF block with 300 ppi. `exiftool` on the result:

```
[JFIF]  XResolution    : 72
[IFD0]  XResolution    : 300
[IFD0]  ResolutionUnit : inches
```

Readers then pick one or the other. The same photo saved from Photoshop as PSD carries 300 ppi everywhere.

## Expected

- **Open:** take the resolution from EXIF IFD0 (`XResolution`/`YResolution`, with `ResolutionUnit` 2 = inch, 3 = cm) when the file has no usable JFIF density, as Photoshop does. A JFIF segment with unit 0 (aspect ratio only) counts as "no density". Where both are present and disagree, follow Photoshop's precedence; Photoshop's own APP13 ResolutionInfo (`0x03ED`) wins when present.
- **Save:** the written JFIF density and the EXIF resolution kept from the source agree with the document's resolution. Either update the EXIF tags or leave them out.

## Environment

PhotoCraft main (0.5.x), Linux. Test file: an unedited Nikon D3200 JPEG (EXIF only, 300 ppi).

title: Web build: Save for Web (Legacy) never downloads the file, and the dialog reuses the previous document's size
author: mindmeltde
body:
Found while using the browser build (self-hosted web build from `main` at 9d3447b, Chrome on macOS).

## 1. Save for Web writes nothing in the browser

**Steps:** open an image in the web build → File › Export › Save for Web (Legacy)… → OK.
**Expected:** the optimized file downloads, like Export As does.
**Actual:** no download. The command fails silently from the user's point of view.

**Cause:** `save_for_web` writes through the engine's `write_file` (`crates/engine/src/web_cmds.rs:741`), whose wasm32 variant only returns `cannot write …: no file system on the web` (`crates/engine/src/file_cmds.rs:95`). On the web, `pick_save` already turns the suggested name into a download name, but the bytes never reach `services.write` (the browser download in `apps/photocraft-web/src/web.rs`). Export As goes through `services.write` (`crates/ui-egui/src/export_dialog.rs:246`) and works.

**Suggestion:** on the web, have the dialog run the estimate/optimize path and hand the bytes to `services.write` (one file, or one download per slice plus the HTML). Also surface the error instead of failing silently.

## 2. The dialog opens with the previous document's dimensions

**Steps:** open document A and open Save for Web (the dialog computes its estimate) → cancel → open document B (different pixel size) → Save for Web.
**Expected:** width/height (and the preview) reflect document B.
**Actual:** the dialog starts with A's size.

**Cause:** `save_for_web` stores `last_web = Some(p.clone())` before the estimate early-return (`web_cmds.rs:733`), so every estimate saves `width`/`height`/`percent`, and `open_web` (`crates/ui-egui/src/file_ui.rs:183`) restores everything except `path`/`dir`. Remembering format/quality across documents matches Photoshop; carrying over the image size doesn't.

**Suggestion:** exclude `width`, `height` (and probably `percent`) from the restored settings, and only update `last_web` on an actual save.

Thanks for the great work on the web build — we use it dai…

title: Move the Discord promotion out of primary UI into the Help menu
author: mroxso
body:
## Problem

PhotoCraft currently promotes its community Discord in several high-visibility places in the app's primary UI:

1. **Start screen** — a large, styled primary "Join us on Discord" button sits directly below the New/Open document actions (`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`, `discord_button(app, ui, 190.0)`).
2. **Title bar** — a "Discord" button with icon is shown in the top bar whenever the window is wide enough (`crates/ui-egui/src/panels.rs`, gated on `DISCORD_ROOM`).
3. **About dialog** — the same prominent primary button appears there (`crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs.rs`).

While a community link is valuable, placing it at this prominence level reads as marketing inside a professional creative tool rather than as part of the product. It competes for attention with the core actions users actually came for (creating and opening documents), and it sets PhotoCraft apart from comparable editors (Photoshop, Affinity, GIMP, Krita), none of which surface a chat-platform invitation in the workspace chrome. For a tool people may use in client-facing or screen-shared settings, a persistent "Join us on Discord" button also looks unpolished.

## Proposed change

Keep the Discord link discoverable, but move it out of the primary UI:

- **Remove** the "Discord" button from the title bar and the primary-styled button from the start screen.
- **Keep** the existing `Help › Join the ArtCraft Discord…` entry (`crates/ui-egui/src/menus.rs`) as the canonical location — it already exists, so this is mostly subtraction.
- In the **About dialog**, replace the primary button with a modest text link in the existing link row, so the community remains one click away without the visual weight.

This also simplifies the layout code (the `DISCORD_ROOM` width gating and associated title-bar tests in `titlebar.rs` can go away) and reduces the i18n surface, since the "Join us on Discord" string is currently duplicated across all language packs.

## Impact

- No functionality is lost — the Disc…

title: Color Lookup layers from a PSB open disabled with no warning
author: theriseandfallofitall
body:
> Agent-written on behalf of @theriseandfallofitall · model: claude-opus-5-5 · origin: owner-requested

title: Adding a layer gets slow once a document has ~100 layers
author: theriseandfallofitall
body:
> Agent-written on behalf of @theriseandfallofitall · model: claude-opus-5-5 · origin: owner-requested

At around 105 layers, creating a new layer lags noticeably (large PSB). Adding a layer should take the same time at any layer count.

**Suspects:** `Session::edit` clones the document for history on every edit (`crates/engine/src/lib.rs:451-475`, `:458`), so check the clone is shallow (COW tiles) and not O(layers × tiles). Also `surface_fingerprint` walks every tile of each layer every frame (`crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs:1359`). Add a `perf/budgets.toml` scenario: new layer at 10/100/500 layers.

title: Invert freezes the app on large layers (serial, untiled, on the UI thread)
author: theriseandfallofitall
body:
> Agent-written on behalf of @theriseandfallofitall · model: claude-opus-5-5 · origin: owner-requested

**Steps:** 6336×7920 PSB, Image ▸ Adjustments ▸ Invert (Ctrl+I), especially on a layer with large transparent areas.
**Actual:** Windows greys the window ("Not Responding") for several seconds, then it recovers.

**Cause:** `adjust_surface` (`crates/engine/src/pixels.rs:11-58`) processes the whole `content_bounds` as one buffer in a serial per-pixel loop (no tiles, no rayon, no empty-tile skip), run synchronously by `destructive_adjust` (`crates/engine/src/commands.rs:285-312`). This hits every `image.adjustments.*` command. **Fix:** per-tile parallel, skip empty tiles, and run as a job (`crates/engine/src/jobs.rs`) with progress. Related: #1561, #211.

title: Lasso selections come out faceted on large documents
author: theriseandfallofitall
body:
> Agent-written on behalf of @theriseandfallofitall · model: claude-opus-5-5 · origin: owner-requested

On the 6336×7920 PSB, freehand lasso selections are made of long straight segments: ~100–200 screen px at 125% zoom (screenshots available). The lasso appends a point for every `PointerMoved` it gets (`crates/ui-egui/src/lasso_ui.rs:180-199`, no decimation), so the points are lost upstream. Windows coalesces mouse moves while the UI thread is busy, so slow frames give sparse input.

**Fix:** keep frames fast during the drag (see #1771, #1772, #1774, #1343), and consider high-rate input (raw input / `GetMouseMovePointsEx`) for lasso, brushes and pen. **Done when:** the lasso stays smooth on a 50 MP document.

title: Fill freezes the app on large documents; crash guard does not cover command dispatch
author: theriseandfallofitall
body:
> Agent-written on behalf of @theriseandfallofitall · model: claude-opus-5-5 · origin: owner-requested

**Steps:** 6336×7920 PSB at 125%: Ctrl+A, Ctrl+Backspace (fill background), twice.
**Actual:** "Not Responding" for several seconds each time, then it recovers.

**Cause:** `edit.fill` (`crates/engine/src/fill_cmds.rs:16,86`) is tiled and parallel (`:265`) but runs synchronously on the UI thread. Run it through the job API (`crates/engine/src/jobs.rs`, as `filters.rs:221` and `edit_menu_cmds.rs:381` do). A full-canvas solid fill should be a cheap per-tile write.

**Also:** `crash_guard::guard` (`apps/photocraft/src/crash_guard.rs:20`) wraps only file import/export (`apps/photocraft/src/services.rs:244,257`). AGENTS.md "Never crash" requires the same safety net around command dispatch.

title: Help ▸ Record Issue: capture steps, timings, logs and screenshots for bug reports
author: theriseandfallofitall
body:
> Agent-written on behalf of @theriseandfallofitall · model: claude-opus-5-5 · origin: owner-requested

A one-click recorder for reproducible bug reports. Start, reproduce, Stop, then review and save a bundle:
- the command journal for that span (`Session::journal`, `crates/engine/src/lib.rs:273`), in the same `[[id, params]]` shape as actions, so it replays with `actions.play` / `photocraft-cli run`

- a generated `issue.md` (steps, timings, links to screenshots; expected/actual left for the user), with "Copy as GitHub issue"
- raw layer pixels never included unless ticked; also exposed as a control/MCP command for agents

title: MCP tool schemas: `items: true` (ui_pointer) and `$ref`/`$defs` (command_batch) rejected by strict LLM providers
author: fangooer
body:
## Summary

Two tool definitions emitted by `photocraft-cli mcp` use JSON Schema constructs that are valid per JSON Schema 2020-12 but get rejected by stricter tool-schema validators used by some LLM providers. When these tools are part of the request, the **whole request fails before inference**.

## What happens

With the MCP tools loaded, chat requests to Moonshot Kimi-K3 (via Volcano Ark) fail with:

```
tools.function.parameters is not a valid moonshot flavored json schema,
details: <At path 'properties.events.items': items must be an object>
```

Two constructs are affected:

1. **`ui_pointer`** — `properties.events` is declared as `{"type": "array", "items": true}`. `items: true` is legal in draft 2020-12, but many provider-side validators require `items` to be a schema object.
2. **`command_batch`** — `properties.steps.items` uses `{"$ref": "#/$defs/RunParams"}` together with `$defs`. `$ref`/`$defs` are also commonly unsupported by strict tool-schema validators.

## Repro

- `photocraft-cli v0.3.0` and `v0.5.0` (macOS universal build), MCP over stdio.
- Fetch `tools/list`, put the emitted `ui_pointer` definition into a chat-completions `tools` array, send it to a strict validator (Kimi-K3 via Volcano Ark in our case) → HTTP 400 at parameter validation.
- Replace `items: true` with a concrete object schema in the same request → HTTP 200. This isolates the cause to the schema shape, not the endpoint.

## Suggested fix

- Emit a concrete object schema for `ui_pointer`'s `events.items`, e.g. `{"type":"object","properties":{"kind":{"type":"string","enum":["down","move","up"]},"x":{"type":"number"},"y":{"type":"number"},"pressure":{"type":"number"}},"required":["kind","x","y"]}`.
- Inline `$defs`/`$ref` in `command_batch`'s `steps.items` (embed the `RunParams` object directly) — or emit plain object schemas without `$defs` entirely, since MCP tool schemas travel to arbitrary providers with varying validator strictness.

Happy to test a fix. Meanwhile we run a smal…

title: [UX/Enhancement] Font Picker: dynamic height collapse on search and missing keyboard navigation
author: slimetbh
body:
### Problem Description

Currently, the Font Picker has two usability issues that slow down typography workflows:

1. **Dynamic Dropdown Shrinking:** When filtering fonts via the search input, the picker container resizes dynamically to fit the filtered results. This layout shift makes the UI jump and degrades the user experience.
2. **Lack of Arrow Key Navigation:** Users cannot cycle through fonts using the keyboard (`ArrowUp` / `ArrowDown`), requiring manual mouse selection for every font change.

### Proposed Solution

- **Stable Dropdown Height:** Set a fixed height (or `min-height` with `overflow-y: auto`) for the font list viewport so the dropdown dimensions remain consistent regardless of how many search results match.
- **Photoshop-like Keyboard Navigation:** 
  - Allow navigating up and down the filtered font list using the `ArrowUp` and `ArrowDown` keys while the search field is focused.
  - Apply real-time preview on the canvas (or immediately select the font) as the active list item changes.

### Expected Behavior
A stable, non-jumping picker container and quick keyboard-driven font iteration matching standard graphic editor ergonomics (Photoshop, Figma).

title: Dropped image layer disappears from the main document when opening its Smart Object contents for edit
author: subtilicus
body:
**What happens**
Drag an image onto the canvas (it is placed as an embedded Smart Object and Free Transform starts on it). Without committing the transform, choose Edit Contents (double-click the layer thumbnail). The placed layer is removed from the main document.

**Cause**
A drop leaves a Free Transform session open on the placed layer, marked `MadeLayer::Place`. Edit Contents makes the child document active, and `transform_tool::end_if_left` sees a different active document and calls `cancel`, which runs `take_back_made` and undoes the place in the parent.

**Fix**
In `end_if_left`, when the session is a pending place and its document is still open, end the session without undoing the place; the layer stays, untransformed. Regression test: `editing_the_contents_of_a_dropped_file_keeps_the_layer` in `crates/ui-egui/src/transform_tool.rs`. Not yet confirmed to fail without the fix; clippy, `cargo xtask layers` and `cargo xtask wasm` not yet run.

title: Brush: a tap (press and release without moving) paints a full-size blob and ignores pen pressure
author: FluorescentLava
body:
## Summary
With a pen tablet, pen pressure is applied correctly to strokes that involve movement, but a tap that is released without moving paints a large dab as if the pressure were at maximum, regardless of how hard the pen was pressed.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Select the Brush tool with a pressure-sensitive preset (or in Brush Settings set Shape Dynamics › Size Control and/or Transfer › Opacity Control to Pen Pressure).
2. Tap once with very light pressure and release immediately without moving the pen. Repeat with firm pressure.
3. Then press and hold the pen, drag slowly for a short distance, and release.

## Expected behavior
A tap dab reflects the pen pressure at contact: small/faint for a light tap, larger/more opaque for a firm tap, as in Photoshop.

## Actual behavior
- Tap and release without moving: a large blob (<full brush size / full opacity>) every time, regardless of pressure.
- Press, hold, then draw a short slow segment: pressure is respected along the segment, and no blob appears.
So the blob only appears when the pen is released without any movement.

## Notes
- PR #943 (draft) describes a similar symptom: tap dabs use a hard-coded pressure of 1.0 instead of the stylus pressure, and fast taps may start and end between two UI frames. I have not verified whether this is the cause here.
- Possibly related: #1302 (large blobs on stylus release, macOS).
- Screen recording attached: taps at light vs. firm pressure, then a short slow stroke.
