Found by reading the source at main `dd41598`. Not run in the GUI.

`zoom_step` in `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs:648-652` has a step table that ends at 32.0, but the zoom clamp allows up to 64.0 (`MAX_ZOOM` in `zoom_tool.rs:17`). For a zoom between 32 and 64 there is no larger step, so `unwrap_or(32.0)` returns 32.0. Zoom In (Ctrl+=) and a Zoom tool click then zoom out.

For example, at 40x, `zoom_step(40.0, 1)` returns 32.0.

The existing test `zoom_steps_monotone` (`canvas.rs:4495`) asserts `zoom_step(32.0, 1) == 32.0`, so it encodes the same behaviour.

Possible fix: add 64.0 to `STEPS` and fall back to `z` (not 32.0) when no larger step exists.

title: Horizontal ruler loses its ticks when View > Flip Horizontal is on
author: stueydubs
body:
Found by reading the source at main `dd41598`. Not run in the GUI.

In `crates/ui-egui/src/rulers.rs:234` the horizontal ruler takes its visible range as `(xf.to_doc(top.left_top())[0], xf.to_doc(top.right_top())[0])` and then loops `while v <= u1`. With View > Flip Horizontal, `ViewXform::to_doc` negates x (`canvas.rs`, `to_doc`), so `d0 > d1` and the loop never runs. The horizontal ruler should lose all its ticks and labels in a flipped view.

`visible_doc_rect` (`canvas.rs:1144`) already handles this by taking the min and max over the corners. The ruler could do the same.

title: image.size without a resample filter returns the new size but does not apply it
author: stueydubs
body:
Found by reading the source at main `dd41598`.

In `crates/engine/src/image_cmds.rs:148`, `image.size` returns early when no resample filter is chosen: `let Some(filter) = resample else { return Ok(()) };`. That return happens before `doc.size` is set. At line 172 the command still returns `{"width": nw, "height": nh}`.

A caller that passes `resample: "none"` (or whatever maps to `None`) with a new width and height gets a result saying the canvas is now `nw x nh`, but only `resolution` was applied.

Either apply the size without resampling, or return the actual document size, or reject the combination with an error.

title: --control exits with status 0 when token or workspace setup fails
author: stueydubs
body:
Found by reading the source at main `dd41598`.

In `apps/photocraft/src/main.rs:240-241` and `254-255`, when control authentication or the automation workspace cannot be configured, the app prints an error and then does `return Ok(())`. The process exits with status 0 and no control server is running. A script that launched PhotoCraft with `--control` sees success.

The control port parse failure just above these (`--control` port) exits with `std::process::exit(2)`, so the two paths disagree. The same exit code (or at least a non-zero one) would let scripts detect the failure.

title: RAW readers truncate EXIF orientation to u16 before the 1..=8 range check
author: stueydubs
body:
Found by reading the source at main `dd41598`.

The RAW readers parse the EXIF orientation tag like this: `t.tag_uint(&ifd0, tag::ORIENTATION).map(|o| o as u16).filter(|o| (1..=8).contains(o))`. `tag_uint` returns `Option<u32>` (`crates/raw/src/tiff.rs:299`), so the `as u16` cast runs before the range check. A tag value of 65538 truncates to 2 and passes the filter. It should be rejected and fall back to 1.

Affected lines: `cr2.rs:292`, `rw2.rs:169`, `orf.rs:149`, `dng.rs:261`, `tiffep.rs:212` (all under `crates/raw/src/`).

Low impact: a malformed file gets an unexpected rotation. Filtering on the `u32` first, then casting, fixes all five.

title: unhex accepts a leading '+' in a hex pair (from_str_radix)
author: stueydubs
body:
Found by reading the source at main `dd41598`.

`unhex` in `crates/format/src/convert.rs:57-65` decodes each pair with `u8::from_str_radix(s.get(i..i + 2).unwrap_or("x"), 16)`. `from_str_radix` accepts a leading `+`, so a pair like `"+5"` decodes as `0x05` instead of failing as corrupt hex.

A malformed hex string therefore loads as valid data. Checking that both characters are ASCII hex digits before calling `from_str_radix` would fix it.

author: kayrockscreenprinting
body:
## What PhotoCraft shows (macOS)

Closing a document with unsaved changes opens a dialog titled "Unsaved changes", with the buttons in one row labelled **(D)on't Save**, **(C)ancel**, **(S)ave**. On Windows and Linux the labels are **(Y)es**, **(N)o**, **Cancel**. The key letters come from #533, which fixed #480 (answering the prompt from the keyboard).

![PhotoCraft](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kayrockscreenprinting/photocraft/22115bbb660840e6aba2e8b3a78cb9dab92827cb/discard-prompt-photocraft-mac.png)

## What Photoshop shows (macOS)

The standard macOS alert:
- the app icon, with the question as a bold heading ("Save changes to the Adobe Photoshop document "Untitled-1" before closing?");
- the buttons stacked vertically: **Save**, **Don't Save**, **Cancel**;
- no key letters in the labels.

![Photoshop](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kayrockscreenprinting/photocraft/22115bbb660840e6aba2e8b3a78cb9dab92827cb/discard-prompt-photoshop-mac.png)

## Why

AGENTS.md sets the goal as 1:1 Photoshop parity in look and behaviour. The printed key letters stand out as non-native next to Photoshop's prompt and other Mac dialogs.

title: Allow editContents / convertToLayers on embedded smart objects over the control channel
author: eduafbr
body:
# Allow `editContents` / `convertToLayers` on embedded smart objects over the control channel

## Problem

Over the desktop control channel (and the MCP bridge), these commands are refused:

```
{"id":1,"method":"engine.execute","params":{"command":"layer.smartObjects.editContents","params":{"layer":19}}}
→ {"id":1,"ok":false,"error":"automation command `layer.smartObjects.editContents` uses ambient filesystem paths and is disabled; use capability-scoped document methods"}
```

`layer.smartObjects.convertToLayers` fails with the same error.

So automation can't reach layers inside a smart object, even when the smart object is **embedded** in a document that was opened through `app.open` under the automation read root.

## Use case

A print template PSD has one smart object per product. Each smart object holds nested smart objects (a top/bottom copy for printing), and the product photo is a pixel layer two levels down:

```
template.psd
└─ Products / "Product A"   (embedded smart object)
   └─ "Front"             (embedded smart object)
      └─ "Photo"          (pixel layer: the product photo)
```

Exporting that photo currently needs a person to double-click each smart object in the Layers panel. Once the inner document is open, the rest works over the control channel (`layer.setProps`, `image.duplicate`, `image.trim`, `app.save`).

## Why the embedded case seems safe

For an **embedded** smart object, the contents are already inside a document the session has opened. Double-clicking in the UI opens them as a new in-memory document, and nothing is read from or written to disk. Saving or closing that document updates the parent in memory too. Nothing seems to touch an ambient path.

The risk the rule guards against looks specific to **linked** smart objects, whose contents are an external file at an arbitrary path.

## Proposal

Over the control channel / MCP:

1. **Embedded smart objects:** allow `layer.smartObjects.editContents` (open contents as a new in-memory d…

title: Importing a large ABR brush library can cause extremely high memory usage and lose folder hierarchy
author: Sansui233
body:
Importing a large ABR brush library can cause extremely high memory usage.

People who use digital painting software often have fairly large brush libraries. For example, after importing Krenz's brush pack, I opened a new blank canvas immediately after starting PhotoCraft, and memory usage was already close to **4 GB**.

Could the brush system consider:

* Caching generated brush thumbnails to disk instead of keeping all rendered thumbnails in memory.
* Rendering/loading brush thumbnails only when the corresponding brushes are about to become visible in the brush panel (lazy loading / virtualization).
* Releasing thumbnails that are no longer visible when appropriate.

There is also a separate issue with the **ABR folder hierarchy**.

ABR brushes can contain nested folders/categories, but after importing them into PhotoCraft, the second-level folders disappear and all brushes are flattened into a single level. The original hierarchy should ideally be preserved when importing an ABR file.

So there are two issues here:

1. **Very high memory usage when importing large ABR libraries**, potentially several GB even with a blank canvas.
2. **Nested ABR folder hierarchy is lost**, with brushes being flattened into a single level.

title: fix(gpu): parity test adjustment_layers fails on NVIDIA: the 1/255 tolerance has no f32 slack
author: Sir-Starch
body:
## Runtime or environment

`main` at `dd41598d`, Arch Linux x86_64 (kernel 7.2.9), Rust stable 1.98.0 (1.97.1 behaves the same), `cargo test` in the default dev profile. Vulkan loader 1.4.363.0. The machine has three Vulkan adapters, and the result depends on which one the test picks:

- NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4080 SUPER, proprietary driver 615.71.09
- AMD Raphael iGPU, RADV (Mesa 26.2.4)
- llvmpipe / lavapipe (Mesa 26.2.4, `vulkan-swrast`)

## Summary

`cargo test -p photocraft-gpu --test parity` fails on NVIDIA, on every run (18 of 18 in isolation), and passes on RADV and on lavapipe (3 of 3 each). The failing test is `adjustment_layers`:

```text
thread 'adjustment_layers' panicked at crates/gpu/tests/parity.rs:142:62:
Hue/Saturation Normal: max diff 1.00/255 at (18,23): cpu [0.46666667, 0.9019608, 0.89411765, 1.0] gpu [0.46666664, 0.89803916, 0.8941176, 0.99999994]
```

The reported difference is exactly one 8-bit step, which is what `const TOL: f32 = 1.0 / 255.0` is meant to allow. The GPU result is not wrong by more than the documented parity tolerance; the check has no room for f32 rounding, so it rejects a result that sits on the limit.

## Steps to reproduce

On a machine whose Vulkan loader offers an NVIDIA adapter, and with the NVIDIA ICD as the only or the preferred driver:

```sh
cargo test -p photocraft-gpu --test parity adjustment_layers
```

To see the dependence on the adapter on a machine that has several, restrict the loader to one driver file (adjust the paths to your distro):

```sh
VK_DRIVER_FILES=/usr/share/vulkan/icd.d/nvidia_icd.json cargo test -p photocraft-gpu --test parity adjustment_layers   # fails
VK_DRIVER_FILES=/usr/share/vulkan/icd.d/radeon_icd.json cargo test -p photocraft-gpu --test parity adjustment_layers   # passes
VK_DRIVER_FILES=/usr/share/vulkan/icd.d/lvp_icd.json    cargo test -p photocraft-gpu --test parity adjustment_layers   # passes

title: ABR import flattens the brush folder hierarchy (phry section ignored)
author: davidmann4
body:
Split out of #1843 (that issue now tracks the memory use).

## Problem

ABR files from Photoshop CC keep their brush folders. PhotoCraft drops them: every preset in an imported `.abr` goes into a single group named after the file. Nesting is lost, and so are single-level folders. Exporting Photoshop 25.1's default brush set produces an ABR with 4 folders (8, 6, 6 and 8 presets); the import code below puts all 28 into one flat group.

## Cause

- `crates/psd/src/abr.rs` skips the `phry` section on purpose (`// Preset hierarchy (groups) and tool presets: not needed for the tips.`).
- `crates/io/src/abr_map.rs` puts every preset in `group` (the file name).
- `BrushPreset.group` is a single string, so the preset store (`index.json`, one `.pcbrushes` file per group) and the Brushes tab only know one level.

## Format (observed on a v6.2 ABR exported by our own Photoshop 25.1)

`phry` = version `u32` (16) + ActionDescriptor whose `hierarchy` key is a list of objects, read as a token stream:

- `Grup` { `Nm  ` (name, TEXT), `zuid` (uuid, TEXT) }: opens a folder
- `preset` {}: the next preset of the `desc` section's `Brsh` list, in order
- `groupEnd` {}: closes the current folder

Nested folders should be nested `Grup`/`groupEnd` pairs (to confirm with a nested oracle). Presets outside any `Grup` are at the top level.

## Proposed work

1. `psd`: parse `phry` into a tree (or a folder path per preset). Don't panic on mismatches: unbalanced `groupEnd`, more or fewer `preset` tokens than `desc` presets, a depth limit. Keep the current flat import as the fallback, with a warning.
2. Model: nested groups for brush presets (e.g. a group path), with a migration so existing stores still load.
3. `io::abr_map`: put the ABR's folders under the file-name group (or, as in Photoshop, import the folders themselves at the top level; decide by checking Photoshop's behaviour).
4. Store and Brushes tab: nested folders (expand/collapse, drag and drop, rename, delete), like Photoshop's Brushes…

title: PhotoCraft becomes unresponsive when opening files or new window or dialogue on Linux (Wayland/Hyprland)
author: recremsa

PhotoCraft should remain responsive when opening, interacting with, and closing any window or dialog. Opening a window should not trigger an application-not-responding warning.

Opening any window or dialog from within PhotoCraft causes the application to appear unresponsive. Hyprland displays an application-not-responding warning while the window is open. Closing the window restores responsiveness.

title: Native Wayland file drag-and-drop without waiting for winit 0.31 (patched winit 0.30, works on niri)
author: MixaDoDs
body:
Follow-up to #386 and #1840: native file drag-and-drop on Wayland can work today, with no wait for egui to move to winit 0.31.

### Why the current workaround fails on niri

The X11 preference / `WAYLAND_DISPLAY=` route doesn't fix niri. niri runs X11 apps through **xwayland-satellite**, and that doesn't bridge drag-and-drop between Wayland clients and X11 clients. So dropping a file from Nautilus onto PhotoCraft does nothing in both modes. The only way to make it work is for the Wayland window to accept the drop itself.

### How to do it (working branch)

Branch: https://github.com/MixaDoDs/photocraft/tree/wayland-dnd (2 commits on top of `15737e1`)

1. **`9fe46f3`**: vendor `winit 0.30.13` unchanged into `patches/winit` (so the next diff shows only the patch).

title: Crop tool: a pending crop leaks into other documents (New, Open, switching tabs)
author: davidmann4
body:
Photoshop treats a pending crop as a modal state: you can't create a new document while a crop box is still open. In PhotoCraft the crop box stays active, and it carries over to whichever document becomes active.

### Steps to reproduce
1. File › New (any size).
2. Pick the Crop tool (C) and drag a crop box. Don't commit.
3. File › New again.
4. The new document is still in cropping mode, with the crop box from the first document drawn over it. Pressing Enter crops the **new** document to that box.

Switching to another document tab or opening a file while a crop is pending probably does the same.

### Expected
- A pending crop belongs to the document it was drawn on. It never shows on or applies to another document.
- As in Photoshop, File › New (and the other commands Photoshop blocks during a crop) aren't available while a crop is pending, or the crop is cancelled first. Which commands Photoshop blocks, and whether it asks to apply the crop when you switch documents, still needs checking in Photoshop before fixing.

### Cause (from reading the code)
`UiState::crop_rect` / `crop_angle` (`crates/ui-egui/src/state.rs`) are global, not per document, and nothing resets them when the active document changes. `canvas.rs` draws the frame over the active document, and `commit_crop` applies it there.

PhotoCraft 0.5.0 / main

title: Mouse Text Selection in Single Line Input Fields
author: JoaCHIP
body:
Scenario: Fill text into any single line input field like for instance the layer name.
Point at the middle of the text string and hold down the left mouse button to start selecting text.

**Expected behavior:** Moving the mouse to the left should select text to the left side of the starting point. Moving the mouse right should select text on the right side of the starting point.

**Observed behavior:** Moving the mouse up selects text to the left side of the starting point. Moving the mouse down selects text on the right side of the starting point. Text selection is basically rotated 90°.

Notice: This behavior is actually correct for multi line text fields. But not for single line text fields. My suspicion is that the UI framework has to be told whether each text field is single or multi line, so that it can choose the correct corresponding mouse behavior. For reference, here is an example of the same problem with a work-around demonstrated in Qt: https://github.com/JoaCHIP/TextSelectionQt

title: Let an embedding app hide the icon rail and the in-window menu bar
author: rossaai
body:
## The need

We are testing PhotoCraft's egui UI, `PhotocraftApp`, embedded in a prototype of our own app, compiled to WebAssembly and run in the browser. The prototype offers a simple view and the full view, and switches between them by setting `app.ui.panels`, `app.ui.dock` and `app.ui.tool`. This works for the toolbar, the options bar, the status bar and every dock group. The `dock` flag from #1388 hides the dock groups and the rail together.

Two parts of the window have no flag:

- the right dock's icon rail, which `panels::right_dock` always draws while the dock is shown
- the title bar with the in-window menus, which `PhotocraftApp::ui` always draws outside full-screen mode

So a simple view that keeps some dock groups keeps the rail, and an app that draws its own bar shows two menu rows. #1614 asks for a related embedding API for the web build, to open and save documents. It does not cover these two parts.

## Proposal

Two fields on `state::Panels`, `rail` and `menu_bar`, both `true` by default and `#[serde(default = "yes")]`. `right_dock` and `PhotocraftApp::ui` check them. `dock`, Tab and ⇧Tab keep working as they do. Saved settings and the default UI do not change, and `ui.set {"panels": {...}}` accepts them as it accepts the other panel flags. No menu item and no command, as for `toolbar_double`.

Hiding the title bar also hides what else it holds: the document title, the workspace switcher, the search, theme and Discord buttons, the window drag area, and PhotoCraft's own caption buttons where it draws them. That seems right for an embedding app, which owns its window and its bar.

A branch with the change and tests is ready: `rossaai:rossa/embedding-panels`. Would you take it as a pull request, or would you prefer another shape, for example one `embedded` flag or a builder option on `PhotocraftApp`?

title: Menus: a submenu whose items are all disabled still looks enabled
author: kayrockscreenprinting
body:
### What happens

A submenu whose items are all disabled still shows its header as enabled. For example, with a crop pending (#1918 / #1957), every item under File › Export, Automate, Scripts and Import is greyed, but the four headers look available and open to a list of greyed items.

### Photoshop

Photoshop greys such headers. Checked in Photoshop 27.11 on macOS with a crop pending: Export, Automate, Scripts and Import are greyed in the File menu, as are Image › Mode and Adjustments.

### Where

- In-window menus: `menus::render_level` enables a submenu when `any_enabled || !child.is_empty()`, so any non-empty submenu stays enabled. That line dates from the first work-in-progress commit.
- Native macOS menu: `native_menu::Node::Submenu` has no enabled flag, so the backend can't grey a header.

### Question before a PR

Greying all-disabled headers everywhere would match Photoshop and the macOS convention. But it also hides the contents of submenus whose items are all unimplemented, if keeping those browsable was the intent of the current rule. Is a global change wanted, or only during modal states such as a pending crop or transform?

I'm happy to send the PR either way (both renderers, plus a test over `menu_catalog`).

title: Large layered saves (TIFF / PSD→PSB) block the UI with no progress indicator
author: realjonnysax
body:
## Summary

Saving a large layered document (layered TIFF, or a PSD that auto-writes as PSB) blocks the whole UI until the write completes — minutes for multi-GB documents, with no progress feedback. The save itself works: it completes and shows the expected auto-PSB warning.

Photoshop shows a percentage-completed in the file tab during saves; PhotoCraft shows nothing, so Windows declares the app **"Not Responding"** for the duration. The only feedback is a note at the bottom right *after* it finishes.

## Where

`PhotocraftApp::write_document` (`crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs:855-876`) calls `export(...)` and `write(...)` synchronously on the UI thread, straight from the save dialog flow (`save_as` → the layered-TIFF options park → continue → `write_document`). The export path has no progress callback — the whole layered encode (every layer plane) runs inline.

## Repro

1. Open a large layered document (e.g. a multi-GB stitch)
2. File › Save As — layered TIFF (answer the options) or PSD (auto-writes PSB past the size limit)
3. The UI freezes with no feedback for minutes (Windows: "Not Responding"), then completes with the auto-PSB warning and the bottom-right saved note

## Environment

v0.5.0, Windows. Large stitched mosaics from a microscopy workflow ([realjonnysax/photocraft-crash-samples](https://github.com/realjonnysax/photocraft-crash-samples)).

## Suggested direction

A progress indicator (percentage in the title bar or file tab, like Photoshop) during layered saves — and/or running the encode off the UI thread so the app stays responsive. The auto-PSB warning and the bottom-right saved note are expected and fine.

title: Auto-Blend Layers › Stack Images: fuse the merged layer per pyramid level by region energy, with halo control
author: ragtux
body:
## What

Edit › Auto-Blend Layers with `method: "stack"` (Stack Images, focus stacking) and Seamless Tones and Colors builds the merged "Blended" layer by taking the full-resolution one-hot masks from `pyramid::stack_weights` (box-blurred |∇²L| winner per pixel) and running them through the Burt–Adelson multiresolution spline (`pyramid::blend`). So the merged layer is only as good as the per-pixel mask: a wrong pick in the mask (a flat area, noise, the smoothing radius straddling a depth edge) is baked into every scale of the result, and a bright object's defocused glow in the other layers is blended in around its silhouette.

## Proposal

Fuse the stack on the Laplacian pyramid itself, the "multifocus composite" of Adelson, Anderson, Bergen, Burt & Ogden (*Pyramid methods in image processing*, RCA Engineer 1984): per pyramid coefficient, keep the layer with the most band-pass energy at that scale, then expand-and-add, so the blending between layers happens in the reconstruction. Selection rules from Wang & Chang (*A Multi-focus Image Fusion Method Based on Laplacian Pyramid*, J. Computers 6(12), 2011): maximum region energy (3×3 binomial window of L² on luminance) for the band-pass levels and local deviation + entropy for the residual, generalised to N layers.

Plus halo control: the levels coarser than a guide level (quarter resolution) do not pick winners but take the mean of the layers weighed by the guide's region energy to a power (REDUCEd to each level's size), so coarse structure follows the layers the guide found sharp and the defocused glow stays out. A `haloControl` parameter (0 = off … 8) on `edit.autoBlendLayers`, default 2.

The masks stay as they are (per-pixel pick, what the Layers panel shows); only the merged layer changes, and only for the stack method. Panorama is untouched.

This is a port of the fusion in [lapstack](https://github.com/ragtux/LAPSTACK) (MIT, mine), rewritten on PhotoCraft's `pyramid::Level` / `reduce` / `expand`, interleaved any…

title: Many filters preview at 1/4 resolution.  For some, the final result is 1/4 scale (smaller / finer than expected)
author: bradtchapman
body:
I tested some **filters** on a photograph with fine detail and noticed how the preview appears to be 1/4 resolution of the original image, possibly for performance reasons.  After setting the parameters on some filters, the final effect does not appear as expected.  In fact, the final result was approximately 1/4 the scale I was expecting based on the preview.  

I zoomed in and out on the image during preview, and that's how I discovered the 1/4 scale.  The image looked highly pixelated at 100%, and I screenshotted / measured it to determine the exact scale.

I think the underlying issue is that some effects are being applied to the preview at 25% scale, so the effect **appears** 4x larger in preview than it will actually appear in the final result.  As far as I can tell, previews for basic lighting and color correction is done at 100% scale.  And I don't think the original app scaled previews to 25% resolution under any circumstances, so using a 25% scale preview in ArtCraft just feels wrong.

Some filters tested where the preview was low-res (1/4), and final result appeared **1/4 scale** relative to preview:
- Distort > Ripple
- Stylize > Diffuse
- Stylize > Oil Paint
- Render > Flame
- Render > Fibers
- Pixelate > Mezzotint

Filters tested where preview was low-res (1/4), effects in preview appeared accurate to scale, and the final result was rendered at the expected scale:
- Pixelate > Color Halftone
- Pixelate > Crystallize
- Pixelate > Pointillize* (preview did not render anything below 8 px)
- Render > Light
- Sharpen > Unsharp Mask

Unsharp Mask is a good case for understanding the render flow of the effect to the 25% preview scale (and figuring out why it's happening at all).

title: Auto-Align Layers fails on focus and exposure brackets: add a direct intensity-based registration
author: ragtux
body:
## What

Edit › Auto-Align Layers registers layers by matching Harris / steered-BRIEF features between them (Photomerge's registration). That is right for a panorama, but on layers that nearly coincide — a focus bracket, an exposure bracket, a burst — it fails outright. On an 8-frame focus bracket (2070×1378, a still life shot on a Z 8 with a 105 mm macro) `edit.autoAlignLayers` with any projection returns

```
Auto-Align couldn't find enough matching detail between the layers
```

The frames are the same view with sub-pixel shifts, a little rotation and up to 6.7 % of scale from focus breathing, and much of each frame is defocused: there is nothing distinctive to match and nothing to verify. Focus stacking (Auto-Blend › Stack Images) needs exactly these layers aligned first.

## Proposal

A direct, intensity-based registration as a second path of `edit.autoAlignLayers`: the pose that makes the warped target look like the reference, found coarse-to-fine on a Gaussian pyramid of the luminance with a bounded Nelder-Mead search; the cost is the RMS of the mean-removed difference over the pixels both layers cover (so exposure changes don't count). The pose is a similarity (shift, scale, rotation about the centre), with aspect and shear for an affine fit and two perspective terms for a projective one, so it maps onto the existing projections: Reposition → translation, Collage and Auto → similarity, Perspective → projective (Cylindrical and Spherical stay feature-based). Layers register outward from the reference, each to the previous one aligned, starting from its pose. The pose is resolution independent, so the search stops a few levels short of full resolution (finest level ≤ 2048 px) and the full-resolution cost is never paid.

A `registration` parameter: `auto` (default) tries features first and falls back to intensity when there is nothing to match, `features` and `intensity` force one. The result reports which was used. The rest of the command (warping, masks, undo…

title: [Bug] Windows: app appears to close immediately on launch — startup blocks loading a large crash-recovery autosave
author: theriseandfallofitall
body:
### What happens
Launching PhotoCraft (Start-menu/desktop shortcut, or double-clicking a `.psd`/`.psb`) seems to close
immediately: no window appears. Launching again gives the same result. In Task Manager each attempt is
actually still running (several hundred MB to 3.5 GB each, "Not Responding"), but it never shows a window.
After a few tries there were 5 `photocraft.exe` processes.

### Cause
`%APPDATA%\Photocraft\Recovery` held a 403 MB crash-recovery autosave (`.pcraft`, revision 246) of a
1 GB `.psb`. At startup the recovery service (`apps/photocraft/src/services.rs`, `recover`) loads every
recovered document synchronously **before the first frame**, with no progress or cancel. Recovery entries
are kept until the document is saved or closed, so **every** launch reloads it and hangs again.

Moving the `Recovery` folder aside → the app opens in seconds.

### Where in the code (main @ 2515fa7c)
- [`crates/ui-egui/src/prefs_ui.rs#L115-L131`](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/2515fa7c/crates/ui-egui/src/prefs_ui.rs#L115-L131): `prefs_ui::load` calls `services.recover()` on the UI thread during the first frame (when `file_handling.recover_on_launch`, default `true`, [`crates/engine/src/prefs.rs#L347`](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/2515fa7c/crates/engine/src/prefs.rs#L347)).
- [`apps/photocraft/src/services.rs#L170-L173`](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/2515fa7c/apps/photocraft/src/services.rs#L170-L173): the `recover` service, which collects every entry before returning.
- [`crates/format/src/autosave.rs#L209-L211`](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/2515fa7c/crates/format/src/autosave.rs#L209-L211) and [`#L247`](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/2515fa7c/crates/format/src/autosave.rs#L247): `RecoveryStore::recover` → `load_path` decodes each whole `.pcraft` bundle up front.

Likely fix: show the window first, then load recovery entries on a worker thread with progress (#210), or ask "Recover N documents?" …

title: Add a System theme option that follows the macOS light/dark appearance
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

Add a System choice to PhotoCraft's interface theme setting that follows the macOS light/dark appearance live, so the app changes with the rest of the desktop when macOS switches appearance automatically.

## Problem to solve

macOS can switch between Light and Dark appearance automatically (System Settings → Appearance → Auto changes it at sunset and sunrise), and many Mac apps offer a "System" theme choice that tracks it.

PhotoCraft offers only manual interface themes. PhotoCraft → Appearance (and Preferences → Interface) lists "Pro (Dark)", "Pro (Medium Gray)" (the default), "Studio (Dark)", "Studio (Light)" and "Classic", stored as `interface.theme` in `preferences.json`. The palette is chosen only from that preference; no code path reads the OS appearance.

Because PhotoCraft only has manual choices, a user whose macOS appearance switches automatically has to change the app theme by hand at least twice a day, or leave it mismatched with every other app.

## Proposed behavior

Add System to the existing theme choice. With System selected, the app applies a light theme while macOS is in Light mode and a dark theme while it is in Dark mode, both at launch and immediately when the OS appearance changes while the app is open. The saved choice stays System; only the displayed theme changes. The existing manual choices keep working as they do today.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The theme control offers a System choice (for example "System" or "Use system setting") alongside the existing manual choices, and every place that exposes the theme (PhotoCraft → Appearance, Window → Theme and Preferences → Interface) shows it.
2. With System selected, the app starts in its light theme when macOS is set to Light and in its dark theme when macOS is set to Dark.
3. With System selected and the app running, changing the macOS appearance, including the scheduled change made by macOS Appearance "Auto", switches the whole interface (panels, menus, dialogs and custom-pain…

title: [Bug] Linux (GNOME): pointer stays a spinning "starting" cursor after launch (startup notification never completed)
author: 0xmedic
body:
### What happens
On Ubuntu 26.04 (GNOME), launching PhotoCraft from the dock or the app grid leaves the mouse pointer as GNOME's spinning "app is starting" cursor after the window has already appeared. It keeps spinning until GNOME's startup-notification timeout ends it, which is long enough to be distracting on every launch.

The window works normally during that time; only the pointer is wrong.

### Cause
The desktop entry asks the desktop for startup notification, but the app never completes it.

- [`packaging/linux/ai.storyteller.photocraft.desktop#L10`](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/11a2b724/packaging/linux/ai.storyteller.photocraft.desktop#L10) sets `StartupNotify=true`. GNOME then shows the busy cursor and passes the app a startup token: `XDG_ACTIVATION_TOKEN` on Wayland, `DESKTOP_STARTUP_ID` on X11.
- The busy cursor ends when the app hands the token back: on Wayland by activating its first window with the token (`xdg_activation_v1`), on X11 by sending the startup-notification `remove:` message. If neither happens, the cursor stays until the compositor times out.
- Nothing in the app reads or uses that token. There are no references to `XDG_ACTIVATION_TOKEN`, `DESKTOP_STARTUP_ID`, `ActivationToken` or `startup_notify` anywhere in `apps/`, `crates/` or `packaging/`. The window is built in [`apps/photocraft/src/main.rs#L71-L90`](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/11a2b724/apps/photocraft/src/main.rs#L71-L90) without an activation token.
- winit 0.30.13 (pinned in `apps/photocraft/Cargo.toml`) does not do this on its own: the application must read the token (`winit::platform::startup_notify::EventLoopExtStartupNotify::read_token_from_env`) and pass it to the window (`WindowAttributesExtStartupNotify::with_activation_token`). As far as I can tell eframe 0.36 doesn't do it for us either and `egui::ViewportBuilder` has no field for it (I haven't confirmed this against eframe's source).

There is also a related mismatch on X11:

title: Proposal: clarify task-specific reading in contributor guidance
author: ha1des
body:
AI assistance: Codex · Model: gpt-6-astra · Reasoning effort: ultra · Accountable: @ha1des

Make it clearer which documentation contributors need for a task.

## Proposed change

Add a “Read when” column to the existing orientation table in `AGENTS.md`. Keep `AGENTS.md` and `docs/contributing.md` as the starting point; select other sections by the behaviour or interface affected. Update the README entry to match.

Specialist rules remain binding. Architecture requirements apply even to changes inside one crate; protocol requirements apply when changing automation APIs. Revisit the selection when the task expands.

This is a documentation change: existing rules stay in place and remain binding.

## Why

The [existing orientation](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/9d1713cfb625392b15e7d63da82a33be63dfbfd5/AGENTS.md#L3-L18) says “Read this file first, then `docs/`”, without saying when the listed documents apply. Explicit reading conditions would make the relevant guidance easier to find.

## Validation

- Review the diff for preserved rules and working links.
- Walk through four examples: a UI change, a heavy image operation within one crate, a PSD fix, and an automation API change. Check that each still selects the required guidance and checks.
- If actual reading is compared, assess individual requirements as well as reading volume and report omissions. No measured saving is claimed without such evidence.

## Tracking

The performance-reporting proposal has been split into #6523 so the two changes can be assessed separately. Both are already implemented in #2174; this issue now tracks only task-specific reading.

Related but distinct: #2094 / #2920 covers PR validation details; #5380 / #5388 covers shared progress and remaining-work notes.

title: Proposal: clarify three PR review details in contributing docs
author: ha1des
body:
AI assistance: Codex · Model: GPT-6.1 Sol (`gpt-6.1-sol`) · Reasoning effort: high · Accountable: @ha1des

## Goal

Help maintainers assess PRs with three short hints in `docs/contributing.md`:

- State the revision that check results apply to.
- Distinguish checks not run or unavailable from checks that failed.
- State any open decisions requiring maintainer input.

Example: “Checked `abc1234`: unit tests passed; GPU checks unavailable (no adapter). Open decision: should this setting be exposed in the UI?”

## Non-goals

- No handoff template, separate record, pilot or required PR section.
- No changes to `AGENTS.md`, automation, reviewer loops or CI gates.
- Instruction cleanup and AI provenance remain separately decidable in #2092.

## Done when

The three hints are documented and accepted by maintainers. Existing PR descriptions can provide this information; no duplicate record is needed.

title: Perf: full composite of tall documents with Transparency Shapes Layer off is ~10-20x slower than the floor
author: davidmann4
body:
Follow-up to #1909 / #2076. #2076 bounds the **memory** of effect maps for layers with Transparency Shapes Layer off (PSD `tsly` = 0) on tall documents; it doesn't make the **full composite** faster. This issue collects the measurements and the optimization options, to discuss separately from that fix.

## Measurements
Compose only, release, Windows 11. Synthetic 1920 × 103675 RGB/8 page, N raster layers (1200 × 120 opaque blocks), each with a 6 px Outside Stroke. Full `render_bands` = 23 bands of ~1920 × 4352 px. "Map builds" = `prepare_effects` run band by band on its own.

| Page | N | Full render | Map builds | Effect compositing (rest minus floor) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| No effects (floor) | 3 / 10 | 1.77 s / 1.83 s | 0 | 0 |
| Stroke, tsly on | 3 / 10 | 1.87 s / 2.10 s | 0.02 s / 0.07 s | ~0.1 s / ~0.2 s |
| Stroke, tsly off | 3 | 17.0–21.5 s | 13.5 s | ~1.7–6 s |
| Stroke, tsly off | 10 | 41.8–42.3 s | 17.0 s | ~23 s |

Times are the same before and after #2076 (21–22 s at N = 3); the memory fix didn't slow it down.

## Root cause
- `empty_in` (`crates/compose/src/lib.rs` ~:840) skips a layer with effects only when its bounds plus the effect reach miss the tile. With tsly off, `layer_bounds` returns the whole canvas (`lib.rs` ~:603 via `advanced::shapeless`, `advanced.rs` ~:83), so no tile is ever skipped.
- `prepare_effects` (`lib.rs` ~:497) therefore rebuilds every tsly-off layer's maps for every band (~0.6 s per build: `local_coverage` plus two serial chamfer passes, `effects.rs` ~:214, ~:1193), and every tile composites every such layer (map crops, work buffer, per-pixel passes), which grows with N.
- Any tsly-off layer also sends the whole document to the CPU compositor (`advanced_active`, `advanced.rs` ~:78), so in the app each full refresh pays this cost (22–60 s per layer-adding command on the test page).

## What tsly off renders (from the code, not yet checked against Photoshop)

title: Chisel bevel: a size change at 250 px costs 230 → 450 ms on 12 MP (GPU canvas)
author: Sir-Starch
body:
Follow-up to #2006, as requested there.

## Problem
Since #2006 a bevel size change costs about twice as much on the GPU canvas at large sizes. RTX 4080 SUPER, 12 MP, ms per size change (command + 4 frames), before → after:

| scene | size 9–12 | 50 | 250 |
|---|---|---|---|
| ellipse | 86 → 96 | 114 → 141 | 234 → 395 |
| text | 89 → 139 | 117 → 205 | 230 → 448 |

300 stars at 250: 292 → 495; 36 MP ellipse at 250: 567 → 751. The new `bevel_bench` rows (P52–P59, #2118) reproduce the trend (p50, 9 reps; runs vary by about 20%): ellipse GPU at 250 305 → 460 ms, text GPU at 250 238 → 557 ms.

## Where the time goes
- Nearly all of a step is the CPU effect-map phase (shape + distance fields; `PHOTOCRAFT_FX_TRACE=1`): 225 of 229 ms before and 521 of 525 ms after, 12 MP ellipse, size 250.
- Single thread, 12 MP ellipse, size 250: the plain fields take 290 ms, the new ones 664 ms. The neighbour search and `edge_distance` are 324 ms of that; on 300 stars 525 of 927 ms. They scale with edge length × size: the refinement covers a band of 2·reach around every edge, which at size 250 is most of these maps.
- The two distance transforms (268 of the 290 ms) run over the whole region at any size; they are the same before and after.
- The GPU band halo is `reach + 9` with `reach = ceil(size) + 2`, so at size 250 a 128-row band is computed from a window about 5× its height.

## Ideas (none measured)
1. The GPU path calls `sharp_edges` once per field kind (twice); share it.
2. Refine only where the plain distance can still change the shading noticeably, or cap the refined depth, instead of the whole `reach`.
3. Compute the fields only within `reach` of an edge; the transforms cover the whole region today.
4. Bigger bands at large reach to cut the halo recompute.
5. In the GPU path, grow existing fields instead of recomputing them when the size increases (a shrink already keeps them).

Any of these must keep the fields bit-identical (see the fingerprint approach in #2006) or say what c…

title: Supported theme file: let the desktop supply colors (all Crafting Apps)
author: NobleDoodle
body:
PhotoCraft can already take its colors from a JSON file (`theme::live`, `PHOTOCRAFT_THEME_FILE`), but only in debug builds. Making that a supported feature in release builds would let desktop theming tools (Omarchy's palette, pywal, base16 and others) theme PhotoCraft without patches. Adopting it across the Crafting Apps would answer #1206 ("Themes on all apps") too.

**Proposal**

- Read `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/photocraft/theme.json` (and/or a shared `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/craft/theme.json`) in release builds, re-reading it when it changes, as `theme::live` does now.
- Show it as a "Custom" entry in Window › Theme while the file exists.
- A small shared set of names (`background`, `surface`, `border`, `text`, `textDim`, `accent`, `accentText`, `danger`, `warning`) that each app maps onto its own tokens, plus optional per-app token names, so one file can theme every Crafting App.
- Keep the current rules: `#rrggbb` values only, unknown keys ignored.

Related: #2074, #1206; storytold/lightcraft#589, storytold/vectorcraft#825, storytold/pdfcraft#446.

I'm happy to send a PR for PhotoCraft if this direction works for you.

title: UI Scale incorrectly affects image zoom and rendering
author: xAMOKx
body:
The UI Scale setting incorrectly scales the image content along with the application interface.

I verified this by taking a screenshot of PhotoCraft, creating a document with the screenshot's exact pixel dimensions, and pasting it into the document.

At 150% UI Scale, the screenshot content only matches the actual interface dimensions at approximately 66.6% image zoom.

At 100% UI Scale, the screenshot content matches perfectly at 100% image zoom.

Expected behavior:
UI Scale should affect only the application interface. Image zoom should remain independent, with 100% representing a 1:1 pixel mapping.

Actual behavior:
UI Scale also affects image rendering, causing 100% image zoom to effectively become 150% when UI Scale is set to 150%.

Impact:
This breaks accurate image scaling and likely contributes to blurry image rendering due to unnecessary interpolation.

title: Copy/Paste is fundamentally broken in certain editing contexts
author: xAMOKx
body:
In Photoshop, copy and paste operations are context-sensitive. They respect the active layer, pixel selection, channel, or mask.

In PhotoCraft, this functionality is incomplete.

Examples:
- Copying the Green channel and pasting it into the Quick Mask does not work as expected. Instead, a new layer is created.
- Copying the fully selected mask of an adjustment layer is not possible. The clipboard remains unchanged, so subsequent paste operations insert previously copied content.

Expected behavior:
Copy and paste should support the active editing context, including color channels, alpha channels, layer masks, and Quick Masks.

Impact:
Channel-based and mask-based editing workflows are impaired or unavailable.

title: Brush interpolation and smoothing problems
author: artcraftfan1
body:
When using the brush with smoothing, Photoshop interpolates smoothly between the registered cursor positions, instead of connecting points with straight lines. 

PhotoCraft does connect them with straight lines when smoothing is enabled or high.

There is probably a limitation of how many cursor positions can be registered while drawing. That's why they need to be interpolated. Photocraft currently seems to be doing this linearly while PS offers a more smooth interpolation.

Disabling smoothing completely (ticking off in pen settings) gives a similiar corner-effect in PS. But enabling it with 0% already interestingly creates a smooth interpolation.

The brush "appears" to be interpolating more by slowing down, but if the cursor is moving faster than the cursor registration we are still getting linear edges, which is very undesirable on a quick curved brush stroke.

Also, the photocraft brush smoothing option in the brush settings interface does also not have a checkmark available unlike the other options in the brush settings like shape dynamics, scattering, texture, etc.

The smoothing feature needs to be revamped, and a better form of interpolation introduced, optimally speaking.

Maybe relevant: #2057

The same file opens as `Users/me/a.png`. The sibling apps (VectorCraft, FilmCraft, LightCraft, PdfCraft, EffectCraft) all take absolute paths. PdfCraft's `--root` also takes absolute paths and checks that each one is inside the root.

## Impact
Every agent has to remove the root prefix from the paths it already holds. Agents hit this on their first call, and it's easy to get wrong on Windows.

## Repro (Windows 11, photocraft-cli 0.5.0, e5e3e3975)
- Absolute path -> rejected (above)
- Relative `Users/...` -> opens
- `../escape.png` -> correctly rejected (keep this)

## Suggested fix
Canonicalise an absolute path and accept it when it lies under a configured root, as `pdfcraft-cli mcp --root` does. Keep rejecting device/stream prefixes and anything that resolves outside the roots.

title: Stereo 3D: PhotoCraft ignores the stereo pair in MPO, JPS and PNG sTER files (we measured it, and we have a patch)
author: danielcamposramos
body:
Hi, I am Daniel Ramos. I work on a stereo 3D edition of SparkyLinux, and I use PhotoCraft because it is pure Rust and openly licensed.
I tested PhotoCraft 11f6f00 on Debian testing with our own MPO, JPS and PNG `sTER` files (red left eye, blue right eye), so a swapped or missing eye shows.

**What we measured**
- An MPO opens as one layer with the left eye only; the right eye is dropped silently.
- A JPS or a PNG with `sTER` opens as one flat packed layer, in stored order.
- Nothing writes MPF, the JPS descriptor or `sTER`; saving `.mpo` or `.jps` fails with "unknown file format"; the Open filter lacks both.

**The offer**
We wrote the change in your style and under your rules (new Rust, MIT OR Apache-2.0, no GPL code), citing CIPA DC-007-2009, the VRex JPS descriptor and PNG Extensions 1.4.0 section 3.6, with tests built byte by byte from those specifications:
- a stereo file opens as one document with both eyes side by side, so edits apply to both;
- it saves back as MPO, JPS or PNG with its mark kept;
- Save As offers MPO and JPS, and the `.pcraft` file keeps the stereo flag.

Is a pull request welcome?
We built and tested this with Claude and checked every result by running it. Whatever you decide, thanks for building this in the open.

title: Tests: cut the local test loop ~2.5× (debuginfo, nextest, fewer test binaries)
author: davidmann4
body:
## Summary

Most of the time we spend "running tests" is spent **linking test binaries**, plus running 190 test binaries **one after another**. The tests themselves are fast. Two low-risk changes would cut the full local loop roughly in half, and a third (structural) one would cut it further.

All numbers below were measured on `main` (c63d04a0): Windows 11, 32 threads, rustc 1.99, warm `target/`. CI runners (4 cores, Linux) were not measured; their gains will be smaller.

## Where the time goes

| What | Number |
|---|---|
| Test binaries `cargo test --workspace` builds | **261** (incl. 41 examples) |
| Integration-test files (= separate binaries) | io 41, engine 27, ui-egui 19, codecs 17 |
| Link time per ui-egui integration-test binary | **~39 s CPU** each, even for a 2-test file |
| PDB size per test binary (full debuginfo) | io **239 MB**, ui-egui **588 MB** |
| `cargo test --workspace` wall time (build already done) | **297 s**, of which 251 s is binaries running serially |
| Same tests, summed per-test CPU time | longest single test is 26 s |

`cargo test` runs one binary at a time, so a 32-core machine sits mostly idle while it runs.

## Proposal 1: `debug = "line-tables-only"` for the dev profile (measured)

CI already sets `CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG: line-tables-only` (`ci.yml`). Locally we still build full debuginfo.

Rebuild of the engine test binaries after touching `crates/engine/src/lib.rs`, 3 runs each:

| Setting | Time |
|---|---|
| today (full debuginfo, link.exe) | 23 s · 23 s · 23 s |
| `debug = "line-tables-only"` | **11 s · 11 s · 11 s** |
| `debug = 0` | 10 s · 10 s · 9 s |
| `line-tables-only` + `rust-lld` | 10 s · 9 s (≈ no extra gain) |

For `photocraft-io` the same edit cycle went from 17.5 s to 7 s, and each PDB from 239 MB to 64 MB.

Panic backtraces keep file and line numbers. What we lose is inspecting local variables in a debugger; anyone who needs that can set `CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=true` for that session.

title: ci(web): photocraft-web.wasm (26.9 MiB) exceeds 24 MiB limit in web build size gate
author: Hathor875
body:
## Problem
In PR #1689 (commit `d502c5d`), the `web build and wasm size gate` check was added to PR CI and `main`. It enforces:
```bash
MAX_WASM_BYTES="${PHOTOCRAFT_WASM_MAX_BYTES:-25165824}" # 24 MiB
```
However, with recent additions merged to `main`, the uncompressed `photocraft-web-*.wasm` output size is **26,907,579 bytes (~25.66 MiB)** under the default `wasm-release` profile (`opt-level = "s"`).
As a result, `web build and wasm size gate` currently fails across all pull requests in the repository.

## Solution
Update `[profile.wasm-release]` in `Cargo.toml` to use `opt-level = "z"` (optimize aggressively for size) for the general crates, while preserving `opt-level = 3` overrides for all performance-critical imaging and pixel crates:
- `photocraft-raster`
- `photocraft-color`
- `photocraft-cms`
- `photocraft-compose`
- `photocraft-algo`
- `photocraft-paint`

## Verification
With this configuration, `trunk build --release` shrinks the wasm binary from **26,915,128 bytes (25.66 MiB)** down to **25,071,795 bytes (23.9 MiB)**, bringing it under the 24 MiB threshold without impacting raster/rendering performance. `packaging/web/package.sh` passes.

title: CMYK is written as sRGB RGB when the document has transparency (TIFF and JPEG export; PSD is correct)
author: r-neuschulz
body:
## Problem

Converting a document to CMYK with `image.mode.cmyk` and exporting it to **TIFF or JPEG** silently produces an **RGB** file whenever the document carries transparency. The separation itself is correct — the command returns the coated profile and `info` reports `"mode":"Cmyk"` for the live document — but the writer converts back to sRGB on the way out. PSD export is unaffected and keeps CMYK, so this is in the flat-format writers.

The only signal is one warning among several:

```
warning: Cmyk composite written as sRGB RGB (colour-managed conversion)
```

In a headless or batch prepress run that is easy to miss, and the file that lands looks perfectly fine while having lost the separation (300% TAC, medium GCR) that the job depends on.

## Repro

`photocraft-cli 0.5.0 (e5e3e3975, 2026-10-08)`, official Windows x64 MSI. Commands in POSIX sh quoting.

Control — flat document, no transparency:

```sh
photocraft-cli run --new '{"width":8,"height":8}' \
  --cmd image.mode.cmyk --out flat.tif --format tif
photocraft-cli info flat.tif --compact   # "mode":"Cmyk"   correct
```

Same document plus one empty layer, which gives it an alpha channel:

```sh
photocraft-cli run --new '{"width":8,"height":8}' \
  --cmd layer.new.layer --cmd image.mode.cmyk --out alpha.tif --format tif
photocraft-cli info alpha.tif --compact  # "mode":"Rgb"    wrong
```

An 8x8 document with two layers is enough. Across formats:

| export format | flat document | document with transparency |
|---|---|---|
| `.tif` | Cmyk | **Rgb** |
| `.jpg` | Cmyk | **Rgb** |
| `.psd` | Cmyk | Cmyk |

On the real document this came from (12000x16000, one pixel layer with a mask) the TIFF tags confirm it is RGB with alpha rather than a separation:

| tag | written | expected for CMYK |
|---|---|---|
| `PhotometricInterpretation` (262) | 2 (RGB) | 5 (Separated) |
| `SamplesPerPixel` (277) | 4 (RGBA) | 4 (CMYK) |
| `ICCProfile` (34675) | 652 bytes (sRGB) | the CMYK profile (236 KB) |

In the Layers panel's right-click menu (and the Layer menu) whether an item is **enabled** is decided by the **active** layer, while the command runs on the **selection**, or, for some commands, only on the active layer. With several layers selected this gives three kinds of wrong behaviour.

title: History state should bundle actions together to avoid taking up states too quickly
author: cwshields
body:
Bundling actions is something Photoshop does well to avoid the user bloating history state. 

For example, in Photoshop, when moving a layer with the arrow keys, you move it by one pixel and if you do 5-15 in quick succession, then press undo, it will undo the last 5-15, but in PhotoCraft, it saves each pixel movement as a state, and you have to undo for every pixel. Even when the arrow key is held down, you still have to undo for every pixel the layer is moved.

In my opinion, this should be a preference setting to allow for both options because both can be useful for different projects.

title: FWIW: Changes Adobe has said they'll make to PS—and changes they won't make yet
author: geraldblank
body:
I tried the PhotoCraft alpha, and I’m impressed with the progress you’ve already made! It appears the alpha is a reverse-engineer of Photoshop v27.0.
**In v27.1, the Adjustments now include Camera Raw-style lighting and color adjustments, as well as Clarity and Dehaze.**

**FWIW: Here’s a recent Adobe Community post, describing how they intend to overhaul some of the core PS code:** https://community.adobe.com/the-evolution-of-photoshop-835/introducing-the-tech-of-nextgen-engine-1641818

**A couple of quotes from the page:**
**“See edits to anything in Layers in the context of your full composition”
“Edit compositions of any complexity without having to merge layers or create Smart Objects.” That will be a biggie when it happens—maybe in v28.0?**

How well we integrate open source AI models into PhotoCraft may be the deciding factor for many users. The Adobe Community is full of comments from frustrated users who simply want Gen AI tools which DON’T turn their 4K-resolution still images into mush. These users express their willingness to give up more AI credits for the capability to use Gen AI with higher-resolution images.

Thus far, Adobe’s response to those cries and pleas is” Our servers “can’t handle higher-resolution files”. Therefore, my current workflow is to export 4K still images to Black Forest Labs’ Flux 3 models, if the images need AI work.

But if we gain the ability to create a new PhotoCraft layer with the AI app of our choice—while staying in PhotoCraft — that will give Adobe a run for their money!

title: Feature Request: Add native Wayland support for Linux
author: jasperwoodchuck
body:

Add native Wayland support as a first-class display backend on Linux, allowing PhotoCraft to run directly on Wayland compositors instead of relying on X11/Xwayland.

## Motivation
Native Wayland support would improve integration with modern Linux desktop environments and reduce reliance on the X11 compatibility layer.

## Proposed Behavior
- Allow users to select native Wayland as a display backend in Preferences.
- Use native Wayland when available and selected.
- Preserve X11/Xwayland as a compatibility option for features that still depend on it.
- Ensure display initialization and backend selection behave consistently across supported Wayland compositors.

## Additional Context
The current Linux display server preference offers Auto and X11. A dedicated Wayland option would give users more control over which display system PhotoCraft uses.

title: Feature Request: Add Solo Layer Mode
author: jasperwoodchuck
body:
## Description

Add a Solo Layer Mode that temporarily isolates a selected layer by hiding other layers in the document.

## Proposed Behavior

- Provide a way to enable Solo Mode for the selected layer.
- Hide other layers while Solo Mode is active, without permanently changing their visibility settings.
- Restore the previous visibility states when Solo Mode is disabled.
- Allow users to toggle Solo Mode on and off without losing their current layer selection.
- Handle switching the selected layer while Solo Mode is active consistently.

## Motivation

When working with complex documents, isolating a layer often requires manually hiding and restoring multiple layers. Solo Mode would make inspecting individual layers faster and reduce accidental changes to layer visibility.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Users can isolate the selected layer with a dedicated control or shortcut.
- Other layers are hidden without losing their original visibility states.
- Disabling Solo Mode restores the previous visibility states.
- Solo Mode works correctly with nested layer groups.
- Undo/redo and document saving behave consistently with the existing visibility system.

## Additional Context

This feature is intended as a temporary inspection mode rather than a permanent change to layer visibility.

title: Feature Request: Add a Dedicated Drawing Workspace

Unlike the existing canvas-only mode, this workspace should retain relevant tools and panels instead of hiding the entire UI.

- Provide a dedicated Drawing Workspace that users can switch to when working on illustrations.
- Keep essential drawing tools readily accessible, such as brushes, colors, brush settings, and layers.
- Hide or minimize unrelated panels and controls that are not relevant to drawing.
- Allow users to customize which panels and tools appear in the workspace.
- Preserve the document state and restore the previous workspace when switching back.

## Motivation

The existing canvas-only mode hides most of the interface, which can be inconvenient when drawing because users still need frequent access to brushes, colors, brush settings, and layers.

A dedicated Drawing Workspace would provide a less cluttered interface without sacrificing access to essential tools, making illustration workflows more efficient.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Users can switch between the default workspace and the Drawing Workspace.
- Essential drawing tools and panels remain accessible.
- Unrelated UI elements are hidden or minimized.
- Switching workspaces does not alter the document or layer state.
- The workspace integrates with existing panel management and customization features.

title: Feature Request: Add a Before-and-After Comparison View
author: jasperwoodchuck
body:
## Description

Add a before-and-after comparison view that allows users to compare the current editing result with the original image or a saved editing snapshot.

## Proposed Behavior

- Provide a way to enter a comparison mode without modifying the document.
- Support a split view with a movable divider to compare the two versions.
- Allow users to compare against the original image or a saved snapshot, where supported.
- Provide a convenient way to exit comparison mode and return to normal editing.
- Keep the comparison view synchronized with the document's canvas zoom and position.

## Motivation

When editing photographs or adjusting colors, users often need to evaluate how their changes affect the image. A dedicated comparison view would make it easier to assess edits without repeatedly undoing and redoing operations.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Users can compare the current result against a supported reference state.
- The comparison divider can be moved to inspect different parts of the image.
- Entering and leaving comparison mode does not modify the document.
- Canvas zoom and navigation remain consistent between both views.
- The original image or reference snapshot remains unchanged.

## Additional Context

The comparison interface should integrate with PhotoCraft's existing document and snapshot architecture where possible. The reference state and behavior should be clearly defined to avoid confusion about which version is being displayed.

title: Feature Request: Add Perspective Drawing Assistants
author: jasperwoodchuck
body:
## Description

Add perspective drawing assistants that help users create accurate perspective lines when drawing or painting. Users should be able to place guides on the canvas and use them to guide their strokes.

## Proposed Behavior

- Support configurable perspective guides, including one-point, two-point, and three-point perspective where practical.
- Allow users to position and adjust vanishing points and associated guide lines.
- Provide an option for brush strokes to follow or snap to the active perspective guides.
- Allow users to enable, disable, and remove individual assistants.
- Display guides as non-destructive overlays that do not become part of the exported artwork.
- Preserve perspective assistant settings with the document, where supported.

## Motivation

Drawing objects, buildings, environments, and other scenes in perspective can require substantial manual alignment. Perspective assistants would help users produce more consistent results while keeping their attention on the artwork.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Users can create, move, edit, and remove perspective assistants.
- Supported perspective configurations guide brush strokes as expected.
- Guides remain separate from the artwork and do not appear in exported images.
- Users can temporarily hide or disable assistants without deleting them.
- Assistant settings persist when reopening a saved document, where supported.

## Additional Context

The implementation should follow PhotoCraft's existing tool and canvas architecture. Perspective guides should remain optional and should not interfere with normal brush behavior when disabled.

title: Feature Request: Add Searchable Panel Navigation
author: jasperwoodchuck
body:
## Description

Add a panel search feature that allows users to quickly find and open panels by name instead of navigating through menus.

## Proposed Behavior

- Provide a searchable interface for finding available panels.

- Show an appropriate message when no matching panels are found.

## Motivation

As PhotoCraft grows and introduces more panels and tools, finding a specific panel through menus can become inconvenient. Searchable panel navigation would make the interface easier to navigate and reduce the time spent searching for features.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Users can search available panels by name.
- Search results update as the query changes.
- Selecting a result opens or focuses the corresponding panel.
- Keyboard navigation and selection are supported.
- Empty queries and searches with no results are handled clearly.
- Existing panel visibility, docking, and workspace behavior remain intact.

## Additional Context

The feature should reuse PhotoCraft's existing panel catalog and UI architecture where possible. If a general command palette already exists, consider extending it with panel-search functionality rather than introducing a separate search system.

title: Feature Request: Add an Advanced Node-Based Brush Creator
author: jasperwoodchuck
body:
## Description

Introduce an advanced, node-based brush creator that allows users to design custom brushes by connecting modular nodes in a visual graph.

The system should let users define how brush properties, input-device data, textures, procedural patterns, and other supported parameters interact to determine the appearance and behavior of a brush stroke.

Unlike a conventional brush editor, which exposes a fixed set of controls, a node-based editor would allow users to build custom brush behaviors by combining and reusing individual components. For example, users could combine pen pressure with a size-mapping node, use stroke direction to control brush rotation, or combine procedural noise with a texture input to produce more varied brush marks.

The node-based editor should complement PhotoCraft's existing brush system rather than replace the conventional brush editor. Users who only need basic brush customization should still be able to work with familiar controls, while advanced users could use the graph editor to create more complex brushes.

## Motivation

Brush engines often expose many independent settings, but more complex brush behaviors require those settings to interact in specific ways. A fixed collection of controls can limit how users combine inputs and effects, while making advanced behavior difficult to configure and understand.

A node-based brush creator would provide a visual and extensible way to define these relationships. Users could inspect how brush properties are calculated, combine supported operations, reuse components, and experiment with new brush behaviors without requiring changes to the application's source code.

Potential use cases include:

- Creating pressure-sensitive brushes with nonlinear size and opacity responses.
- Combining multiple textures to create natural-looking painting tools.
- Using stroke direction, pen tilt, or rotation to control brush orientation.
- Introducing controlled randomness into brush size, rotatio…

title: Bug: Artboards in Affinity Documents Are Imported as a Single Document
author: jasperwoodchuck
body:
## Description

When opening an Affinity document (`.af`), PhotoCraft imports the artwork as a single document instead of preserving and opening the individual artboards separately.

This prevents users from accessing the original artboard structure and working with the imported designs as individual artboards.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create or open an Affinity document (`.af`) containing multiple artboards.
2. Open the file in PhotoCraft.
3. Inspect how the document and its artboards are imported.

## Expected Behavior

PhotoCraft should preserve the individual artboards from the imported Affinity document, including their boundaries, dimensions, and associated artwork, to the extent supported by the importer.

Each artboard should remain individually identifiable and editable using PhotoCraft's existing artboard functionality.

## Actual Behavior

The imported document is presented as a single document rather than preserving the individual artboards from the original Affinity file.

## Motivation

Artboards are commonly used to organize multiple related designs within one document. Preserving them during import would allow users to continue editing multi-artboard projects without manually separating the artwork or reconstructing the original layout.

## Additional Context

This issue concerns importing existing artboards from Affinity documents, not implementing artboard functionality in PhotoCraft.

The importer should preserve the source document's artboard structure where the `.af` format and PhotoCraft's existing import architecture permit it.

title: Feature Request: Add Multiple Color Picker Views
author: jasperwoodchuck
body:
## Description

Add options to switch between different color picker views in PhotoCraft, allowing users to choose the color selection interface that best suits their workflow.

The current color picker uses a two-dimensional color gradient alongside a vertical hue bar. Providing alternative views would give users more flexibility when selecting colors and make different color-selection methods accessible from the same interface.

## Proposed Behavior

- Provide a way to switch between different color picker views.
- Consider supporting the following views:
  - **Saturation and Value:** A two-dimensional gradient for adjusting saturation and brightness while selecting a hue.
  - **Hue and Saturation:** A two-dimensional gradient for adjusting hue and saturation while keeping brightness fixed.
  - **RGB:** Separate controls for red, green, and blue channels.
  - **HSV/HSB:** Controls for hue, saturation, and value or brightness.
  - **HSL:** Controls for hue, saturation, and lightness.
  - **Color Wheel:** A circular interface for selecting hue and adjusting saturation, with an appropriate secondary control for brightness or lightness.
- Preserve the currently selected color when switching between views.
- Keep color selection synchronized across all views.
- Provide clear visual indicators for the currently selected color and the active view.
- Allow users to switch views without losing their current selection.

author: MazenGit
body:
## Use case

I want an agent to **read from a photo library that must never be written to**, while **saving only to a working folder**, and to be able to open its own earlier work from that working folder too. That needs two read roots (library and working folder) and one write root (working folder).

Today `--automation-read-root` accepts one folder, and if the flag is repeated only the last value is used, silently. That forces a choice between the two folders:

- make the library the read root, and the agent can no longer read back anything it saved in the working folder; or

Make `--automation-read-root` **repeatable and accumulating**, so that a path resolves if it is under any of the given read roots. A single write root is fine for my use case, so `--automation-write-root` can stay as it is.

If accumulation is not wanted, then at minimum reject a repeated flag with an error (or document that the last one wins), so the dropped root is not silent.

title: Colour palettes taken from LGPL desktop stylesheets (Adwaita) vs. the "permissively licensed" asset rule

body:
`ATTRIBUTION.md` says third-party assets must be permissively licensed and keep their licence file next to them. Solarized Dark (#2098, MIT) follows that.

The Adwaita and Adwaita Dark themes (#1823) use libadwaita's named colours (header bar, sidebar, window, dialog, accent blue, destructive red). The PR said so openly, but libadwaita is LGPL-2.1+, and there is no `ATTRIBUTION.md` row or licence file for it. The licence wasn't discussed in the PR. Only RGB values are used, no code or files.

Questions for the maintainers:
1. Do RGB values taken from an LGPL stylesheet count as third-party assets under that rule?
2. If yes: add attribution rows, re-derive the values as our own, or remove the themes?
3. What is the policy for future themes that match a desktop? KDE Breeze (#2276) has the same situation: its colour schemes are LGPL-2.0-or-later.

title: Current .af artboard properties import as ordinary masked shapes
author: callmeBalloch
body:
Current Affinity 3 `.af` files can open as editable masked shapes on one canvas while all of their native artboards are lost.

Tested upstream main: `1f84f19caf30c9725e820e47d806c090397bb331` (PhotoCraft 0.6.0), macOS Apple Silicon. The problem is also present in the installed 0.6.0 app's reader.

The reader recognizes only `ShpN` nodes with `ABEn = true`. Current documents can mark boards with an `aprp` object referenced by `phrp`, without that legacy flag. Those nodes currently fall through to ordinary shape import, so the document has no artboard groups. The normal single-canvas view, missing board names and disabled board-specific operations follow from that lost model data.

Reproduction uses an original in-memory synthetic version-12 document: two 16×16 boards at x=0 and x=24, each with oversized red rectangle content. Give each board `phrp -> aprp` and `ABEn = false`. Import through `photocraft_io::import`. Expected: two named artboards with separate bounds and clipped editable children. Actual: zero artboards. Replacing the marker with legacy `ABEn = true` preserves both boards. Converted `PCrv` boards with the current properties fail too; unrelated `phrp` property classes must remain ordinary shapes.

The regression tests in the forthcoming fix exercise that synthetic input, all three supported archive compression methods, exact board/pixel preservation through `.pcraft` and PSD, and movement with undo/redo. The current-property cases fail on unchanged upstream while the legacy and unrelated-property controls pass.

Cross-check: VectorCraft's merged AF.4 PR [#763](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/pull/763) already recognizes `phrp`/`aprp`. PhotoCraft's merged [#1778](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/pull/1778) and open [#2137](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/pull/2137) do not contain this recognition change. This is distinct from VectorCraft's already merged artboard edge-containment fix [#894](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft…

title: Every redraw takes ~10 s on a 50 MP PSB with several feathered masks: combined-mask cache thrashes and rebuilds each mask single-threaded
author: theriseandfallofitall
body:
## Summary

On a 6336×7920 (50 MP) 8-bit PSB with 47 layers and **five feathered pixel masks** (two at the
maximum 1000 px), every canvas refresh takes ~10 s on the UI thread. Changing a layer's blend mode
freezes the app for ~10 s each time; opening the file also freezes for a while after the progress
bar reaches 100%. During the freeze one CPU core is at 100% and the GPU is idle (RTX 3070, ~2% util).

## Environment

- PhotoCraft 0.6.0 dev build, `main` @ fc42f81f42919ad420aec66cc2bd30f0ab20fc5c, `cargo run --release`
- Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 Laptop GPU (Vulkan, driver 617.42), 16 threads
- GPU canvas active (`perf.timings.gpu: true`, `lastRefresh: "gpu-rect"`)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open a ~50 MP document with at least three layers whose pixel masks have Properties › Feather > 0
   (mine: feathers of 1000, 1000, 12.4, 4.6 and 1.8 px; one is on a pass-through group).
2. Change any layer's blend mode (or anything else that triggers a refresh).

**Expected:** the GPU refresh takes milliseconds (it does: 14 ms once fewer feathered masks are visible).
**Actual:** ~10 s per refresh, every time, not just the first.

## Measurements (control channel, `ui.inspect` → `perf.timings`)

| State | `compositeMs` after a blend change |
|---|---|
| All layers visible (5 feathered masks) | 10 078 – 11 017 |
| Group "ShadowedBg" hidden (removes 3 feathered masks → 2 left) | **14** |
| Hide any single child of that group (≥3 still left) | 7 844 – 10 758 |
| Disable the group's own mask | 8 831 |

`gpuUploads` doesn't change across refreshes (no page re-upload thrash). Process CPU stays at
exactly one core (100%) for the whole refresh; GPU utilisation 1–8%.

## Cause

`Planner::mask_use` calls `photocraft_compose::masks::combined_mask` for every feathered mask on
every plan, i.e. every refresh. The result is a full-canvas single-channel **f32** surface
(50 MP × 4 B ≈ 200 MB, plus the accounted pixel-mask input). The combined-mask cache is capped at
512…

title: Proposal: agents check for and post "I'm working on this." before fixing an issue
author: davidmann4
body:
## Problem

Agents (and people) from different contributors keep fixing the same issue in parallel. Duplicates waste contributor time and review time.

In the last 300 PRs, 9 issues got two competing PRs, and 4 of those pairs are still both open:

| Issue | PRs |
|---|---|
| #2288 | #2321, #2331 (both open) |
| #2302 | #2322, #2327 (both open) |
| #2326 | #2336, #2343 (both open) |
| #974 | #2005 (merged), #2053 (open) |
| #1905, #1918, #1985, #2124, #2237 | one merged, one closed as duplicate |

Contributors can't assign themselves (that needs triage rights), and `AGENTS.md` has no "check whether it's taken" step, so most agents just start coding.

## What already works

Contributors have converged on a convention by themselves: a plain **`I'm working on this.`** comment on the issue (#2812, #2825, #2832, #2837, #2844, …), and a comment releasing it when they give up (#2735). It needs no permissions, no bot and no workflow: anyone with read access can post and read it.

The only missing piece is that agents don't know about it. They read `AGENTS.md` first, so that is where it goes.

## Proposal: one short section in `AGENTS.md` (docs only, no bot)

Add this under **4. Picking work**:

> ### Claiming an issue
>
> Before you start on an issue, check that nobody else has:
>
> 1. Read the issue's comments (`gh issue view N --comments`). If a comment **starts with** `I'm working on this` and is less than **72 hours** old, or its author has since linked a PR or posted progress, the issue is taken: pick another one.
> 2. Check for an open PR that fixes it (`gh pr list --search "N in:body" --state open`, or the issue's *Development* sidebar). If there is one, the issue is taken.
> 3. Otherwise claim it **before writing code** by commenting exactly `I'm working on this.` (one line; add details after it if useful).
> 4. Put `Fixes #N` in your PR so the claim and the PR link up.
> 5. If you stop, comment `Releasing my claim.` so the issue is free again.
>
> A claim older than…
