title: GPU canvas: inverting a layer mask leaves tile-sized blocks un-inverted (stale default pixel)
author: theriseandfallofitall
body:
## Summary

Make a feathered selection, add an adjustment layer (its mask gets the selection), then invert the
mask. The canvas shows a staircase of rectangular blocks along the edges where the mask is still the
old value. The document is correct: a saved/flattened PNG has no blocks (CPU compositor), and a full
GPU refresh (toggling the layer's visibility) still shows them, so it's the GPU compositor's resident
mask texture.


## Environment

- PhotoCraft 0.6.0 dev build, `main` @ fc42f81f42919ad420aec66cc2bd30f0ab20fc5c, `cargo run --release`
- Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 Laptop GPU (Vulkan), GPU canvas

## Steps to reproduce (control channel; same with the Lasso tool in the UI)

```json
{"command":"file.new","params":{"width":6336,"height":7920,"background":"#808080"}}
{"command":"select.lasso","params":{"points":[[1000,1000],[5000,1500],[4500,6500],[1500,6000]],"feather":1000}}
{"command":"layer.newAdjustmentLayer.curves","params":{"points":[[0,0],[128,230],[255,255]]}}
{"command":"select.deselect"}
{"command":"image.adjustments.invert","params":{"target":"mask"}}
```

**Expected:** the corners show the Curves result (230) everywhere outside the feathered area.
**Actual (canvas):** stepped blocks of the un-inverted value (128) in the corners and along the edges.
`app.save` of the same document: corners are 230 everywhere, largest neighbour difference 1/255 (no steps).

## Cause

`Compositor::sync` decides whether a resident layer/mask texture is stale from its region, kind,
format and CMYK space only, and records `default_nonzero` once when the texture is created. Tiles the
surface doesn't store (the mask's far-away constant area) are written only at creation, as the default pixel.
Inverting the mask flips its **default pixel** (0 → 1) without touching those absent tiles, so they're
neither "changed" nor "gone" and keep the old default on the GPU. The blocks are exactly the
missing tiles.

## Where in the code

https://github.com/storytold/…

title: Opening card: a long file name wraps the title and pushes the percentage and Cancel button outside the card
author: theriseandfallofitall
body:
## Summary

While a document opens, the canvas shows an "Opening {name}" card. With a long file name the title
wraps to two lines and the bottom row (percentage + Cancel) is drawn below the card's bottom edge,
on the backdrop.


## Environment

- PhotoCraft 0.6.0 dev build, `main` @ fc42f81f42919ad420aec66cc2bd30f0ab20fc5c, `cargo run --release`
- Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200, English UI, default UI scale

## Steps to reproduce

1. File › Open a large file with a long name, e.g. `a7rv-test_2024_02_17_shot_30_3705.psb` (1.1 GB PSB, so the card stays up).
2. Look at the card while it decodes.

**Expected:** everything inside the card; a long name truncated with "…" (full name on hover) or the card grows to fit.
**Actual:** title wraps to two lines; "100%" and Cancel sit ~20 px below the card's bottom edge.

## Cause

`open_card` paints a fixed 340×132 card and lays the content out in `card.shrink(18.0)` with no
height constraint. Title (semibold 14) + message + bar + button row only fit when the title is one
line; a wrapped title (long names, or longer translations of "Opening {name}" / the job message)
overflows downwards.

## Where in the code

- https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/fc42f81f42919ad420aec66cc2bd30f0ab20fc5c/crates/ui-egui/src/jobs_ui.rs#L550-L578
  (fixed size at L556, title label at L560)

## Likely fix

- Title on one line: `egui::Label::new(..).truncate()` (egui shows the full text on hover), same for
  the job message.
- And/or size the card to its content: reserve the background with `ui.painter().add(Shape::Noop)`,
  lay out the child, then set the card rect from `child.min_rect().expand(18.0)`.
- Check with `cargo run -p photocraft-ui-egui --example snapshot` using a long name and a long
  translation (e.g. `de`, `ru`).

## Workaround

None needed: cosmetic. Cancel still works (also Esc).

**Retested on `main` @ 29d5f791** (2026-10-10): `crates/ui-egui/src/jobs_ui.rs` unchanged since the commit above; same card.

back in). The Gradient tool, brushes and Invert on the same mask work.

## Environment

- PhotoCraft 0.6.0 dev build, `main` @ 29d5f791d52cd54e411611a609fbc56949e0c653
- Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200

## Steps to reproduce

1. New document, Layer ▸ New Adjustment Layer ▸ Curves (it gets a mask).

title: No command targets a layer's mask (Photoshop "select the mask channel"): mask targeting is shell-only state
author: theriseandfallofitall
body:
## Summary

In Photoshop, clicking a mask thumbnail (or pressing ⌘\) targets the mask, and actions record it as a
`select` of `Chnl.Msk`; every later step then edits the mask. In PhotoCraft the mask target lives only
in the UI shell (`app.ui.mask_target`, settable over the desktop control channel with
`ui.set {maskTarget}`). There's no engine command for it: `channel.target {"channel":"mask"}` is
rejected ("must be \"composite\", a colour channel name or an alpha channel"). So the headless server,
the CLI, MCP and PhotoCraft's own recorded actions can't "target the mask, then run commands"; each
command needs its own `"target":"mask"`. A replay of one of my Photoshop actions has about 12 such steps.

## Environment

- PhotoCraft 0.6.0 dev build, `main` @ 29d5f791d52cd54e411611a609fbc56949e0c653

## Steps to reproduce

```json
{"command":"layer.newAdjustmentLayer.curves","params":{}}
{"command":"channel.target","params":{"channel":"mask"}}
```

→ invalid parameters error.

## Where in the code

- `channel.target` accepts composite, colour channels and alphas only, although the channel reader already knows `"mask"`/`"layermask"` (L248): https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/29d5f791d52cd54e411611a609fbc56949e0c653/crates/engine/src/channel_cmds.rs#L216-L250
- Shell-only state: `crates/ui-egui/src/channels_panel.rs:295`, `crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs:474-477`. The engine half is `ToolState::target_mask`: https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/29d5f791d52cd54e411611a609fbc56949e0c653/crates/engine/src/lib.rs#L273-L287

## Likely fix

Accept `"mask"` / `"vectorMask"` in `channel.target` (fail if the active layer has none), keep the
target on the session (the engine already tracks `mask_targeted` for the colour swap), and let the
`follows_target` commands read it, so the shell, CLI, MCP and actions share one mask target. Journal
it so recorded actions replay it.

title: Rename Layer trims leading/trailing spaces (New Layer keeps them), so names don't round-trip with Photoshop
author: theriseandfallofitall
body:
## Summary

`layer.renameLayer` stores `name.trim()`: renaming a layer to `"black skin bw "` stores
`"black skin bw"`. `layer.new.layer {"name":"abc "}` keeps the trailing space, so the two commands
disagree. Photoshop keeps spaces in layer names: one of my actions renames a layer to
`black skin bw ` and later selects it by that exact name, which fails after a PhotoCraft rename.

## Environment

- PhotoCraft 0.6.0 dev build, `main` @ 29d5f791d52cd54e411611a609fbc56949e0c653

## Steps to reproduce

```json
{"command":"layer.new.layer","params":{"name":"a"}}
{"command":"layer.renameLayer","params":{"name":"black skin bw "}}
```

`ui.inspect` → the layer is named `"black skin bw"`.

**Expected:** `"black skin bw "`, as given (reject only an all-whitespace name).

## Where in the code

https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/29d5f791d52cd54e411611a609fbc56949e0c653/crates/engine/src/layer_multi_cmds.rs#L1046-L1055 (`map(str::trim)` at L1048)

## Likely fix

Use the trim only for the emptiness check (`filter(|n| !n.trim().is_empty())`) and store the name
unchanged. The Layers panel's inline rename can keep trimming what the user types; the command shouldn't.

title: fix(automation): MCP bridge — idle connection dies after 30s, call timeout races the app deadline, no retry for reads
author: ahmedhosnypro
body:
## Problem

`photocraft-cli mcp --bridge` (and any `BridgeClient` consumer) keeps **one persistent TCP connection** to the desktop app's control server, but the app closes idle control connections after **30 seconds** (`IO_TIMEOUT`, `crates/automation/src/security.rs:23`, applied in `configure_stream`). An automation agent routinely thinks for longer than that between tool calls, so the first call after a pause fails:

```
bridge: `ui.inspect` failed: bridge: connection closed by the app; operation may have completed; inspect state before retrying
```

Three further defects stack on top:

1. **Timeout race — 60/60/60.** The app's per-request reply deadline is 60s (`apps/photocraft/src/control_server.rs`, `deadline = Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(60)`), the bridge's call timeout is also 60s (`crates/automation/src/bridge.rs`, `timeout: Duration::from_secs(60)`), and typical MCP clients also cut at ~60s. The bridge's error loses the race (or is never delivered at all), so the agent sees a bare `Request timed out` with zero diagnostics.
2. **No retry, even for pure reads.** On any transport failure the bridge returns "operation may have completed; inspect state before retrying" — correct for edits (#1007 forbids resending a possibly-applied edit), but wrong for idempotent getters, where a reconnect + single retry is always safe.
3. The result is that a healthy app + a paused agent produces scary errors, and a busy/not-responding app produces undiagnosable ones.

## Evidence

Observed repeatedly in a 2026-10-10 automation session driving the desktop app through the MCP bridge: single-call failures with the message above after every >30s pause; later, while the app was (unbeknownst to us) not drawing frames, every bridge call surfaced only the MCP client's `Request timed out` — the bridge never returned its own error inside the window.

## Proposed fix (`crates/automation/src/bridge.rs`)

- Track `last_used: Instant` beside the connection; if >25s since last use (…

title: fix(app): app.save encodes on the UI thread — the window and control channel freeze during a save
author: ahmedhosnypro
body:
## Problem

`app.save` over the control/MCP channel encodes and writes the document **inline on the UI thread**: `save_automation` (`crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs`) calls `services.export(...)` and the automation writer synchronously, and `drain_control` runs it inside the egui frame update. While a large document encodes:

- the window freezes (no frames are drawn),
- every other control request (including `ui.inspect`) queues behind it, and
- a save that takes >60s overruns the control server's reply deadline, so the caller receives `timeout` while the save is still running.

The UI's own File › Save already runs the identical work as a **background job** (#2017, `jobs_ui::start_save`): the worker encodes and writes, the window keeps drawing, the document is locked, `Outcome::AfterJob` lets control requests wait on the job. `save_automation` bypasses all of that machinery.

## Evidence

2026-10-10 automation session: saving a 12–15 layer, 1920×1080 PSD (~16–19 MB) over `app.save` froze every control request for over 60s; the caller got `timeout`; the same file saves in ~1s once the encode is not competing with the frame loop.

## Proposed fix

title: fix(automation): the bare control "timeout" error can't distinguish a slow command from an app that stopped drawing frames
author: ahmedhosnypro
body:
## Problem

The control server replies `{"ok": false, "error": "timeout"}` when a request gets no reply within its 60-second deadline. That single string covers two very different situations:

1. **The request was queued but never dispatched** — the app's window was not drawing frames (display asleep, window fully occluded on Wayland, or the frame loop wedged by a long inline operation). Nothing is running; nothing will ever reply.
2. **The command is genuinely still running** — a long job, or an inline operation like `app.save` (see companion issue) that overruns the deadline while doing real work.

An automation agent cannot tell "wait longer" from "check your display / window state", which turns a diagnosable condition into hours of misdirected debugging. In our session this exact ambiguity cost ~2h: a healthy app behind a sleeping display produced `timeout` for every request for over 3 hours, while we chased nonexistent app bugs.

## Proposed fix

- `apps/photocraft/src/control_server.rs` (the serve thread's `recv_timeout` fallback) and the `drain_control` expired-request rejection (`crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs`): replace `"timeout"` with an actionable message, e.g.:
  `"timeout: no reply in 60s — the command may still be running, or the app was not drawing frames (display asleep, window fully occluded, or a long operation blocked the frame loop)"`
- Update the exact-match assertions in the existing control tests (`crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs`, the `drain_control` timeout test) to the new string.
- `docs/control-protocol.md`: document the deadline semantics and the message.

## Acceptance criteria

- Both timeout sites return the actionable message.
- Existing timeout tests updated and passing; no other reply shapes change.

title: feat(automation): app.open cannot open directory .pcraft — the native on-disk format — over control/MCP
author: ahmedhosnypro
body:
## Problem

`app.open` over the control/MCP channel cannot open `.pcraft` files written in the **directory** form — which is the native on-disk format the app's own File › Save and crash recovery produce. `AuthorizedWorkspace::read` opens the path and rejects anything that is not a regular file (`crates/automation/src/workspace.rs`):

```
{"ok": false, "error": "automation read path is not a regular file: `x.pcraft`"}
```

So an agent that saves/receives a native `.pcraft` directory cannot open it in the running app; the only workaround is round-tripping through `photocraft-cli convert`. The single-file (ZIP) `.pcraft` form still opens fine through the bytes path.

## Proposed fix

The format crate already abstracts storage behind `Source { fn get(&self, path: &str, max: usize) -> Result<Vec<u8>> }` (`crates/format/src/store.rs`) with a `DirSource` implementation — the seam exists, it is just not public and not reachable from the capability-scoped workspace.

- `crates/format`: expose `pub trait ByteSource` (the current `Source`) and `pub fn load_bytes_source(&dyn ByteSource, &LoadOptions) -> Result<Document>`; `DirSource`/`ZipSource` become internal impls.
- `crates/automation`: `AuthorizedWorkspace::open_pcraft(&self, path) -> Result<Document, _>` — open the `.pcraft` subdirectory through the held cap-std root (`Dir::open_dir`), implement `ByteSource` over bounded reads (`photocraft_format::read::read_all`), and call `load_bytes_source`. Requires a `photocraft-doc` dependency (L1; automation already sits above it in the layer graph).
- `crates/ui-egui`: a `Services::automation_open_pcraft` hook; `control.rs`'s `app.open` tries the directory form for `.pcraft` paths first, and falls back to the existing bytes path when the path is a regular file (ZIP form keeps working). Success mirrors `import_automation_document` (document added, `opened_from` recorded, notices shown).
- `docs/control-protocol.md`: document directory `.pcraft` support in `app.open`.

## Acceptanc…

title: feat(cli): PHOTOCRAFT_CONTROL_PORT as mcp/serve fallback
author: ahmedhosnypro
body:
## Problem

The desktop app reads its control port from `PHOTOCRAFT_CONTROL_PORT` (set by launchers and agent tooling that start the app with `--control`). But `photocraft-cli mcp` (bridge mode) and `photocraft-cli serve` only take the port from explicit flags (`--bridge`, `--port`). An agent that starts the app with the env variable then launches an MCP bridge without flags gets a **headless** MCP server with an empty session instead of the running app — silently the wrong backend — or must duplicate the port on every command line.

## Proposed fix

`PHOTOCRAFT_CONTROL_PORT` as the fallback for both subcommands, mirroring the desktop app's own `--control` handling:

- `photocraft-cli mcp`: no `--bridge` → bridge to `127.0.0.1:$PHOTOCRAFT_CONTROL_PORT` (headless when the variable is unset).
- `photocraft-cli serve`: no `--port` → serve on `$PHOTOCRAFT_CONTROL_PORT` (stdio when unset).
- A bad value (non-numeric) is an error naming the variable and the offending value, following the #701 pattern; an empty value counts as unset.

## Acceptance criteria

- Unit tests: parse + empty/unset semantics for both subcommands (`env_control_port_tests`).
- USAGE text and `docs/control-protocol.md` / `docs/development.md` updated to name the fallback.

(Fix already implemented and tested locally; PR incoming.)

title: tracking: control requests starve when the window gets no frame callbacks (display asleep / fully occluded on Wayland)
author: ahmedhosnypro
body:
## Problem (tracking — needs an architectural decision; no fix attached yet)

Control requests are drained inside the egui frame update (`drain_control` in `crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs`), and the control server wakes the loop with `ctx.request_repaint()` when a request is queued (`apps/photocraft/src/control_server.rs`). On Wayland, **if the compositor stops delivering frame callbacks, the frame update stops running entirely** — so control requests (TCP and MCP alike) queue until their 60s deadline rejects them, even though the app process is completely healthy.

Two reproducible triggers:

- **Display asleep (DPMS off):** KWin sends no frame callbacks to any window. Every control request times out with `{"ok": false, "error": "timeout"}` for as long as the display is off.
- **Window fully occluded:** same effect while another window covers the app.

## Evidence (2026-10-10 automation session)

- With the display DPMS-off, `ui.inspect` returned the timeout error for over 3 hours across multiple app restarts; we misdiagnosed it as a wedged app and killed/restarted healthy processes, rewrote working code paths, and burned ~2h.
- `kscreen-doctor --dpms on` revived the channel **instantly** (fps 20.8 on the next request); every previously "wedged" operation then worked: a 15-layer PSD `app.open` in 3.6s, an 18.9 MB `app.save` in ~1s.
- `ctx.request_repaint()` from the server thread does not break the loop out of the no-frame-callback state (it is already called on every queued request).

## Why this matters

Automation agents are expected to drive the desktop app for hours; a screen blanking (laptop lid, idle timeout, another fullscreen session) makes the app look dead while it is fine. This also masks/compounds the diagnostics problem in the companion issue about the bare `timeout` error.

## Directions to consider (not decided)

1. **Off-thread drain for read-only getters** (`ui.inspect`, `document.inspect`, `session.inspect`, `engine.commands`, `jobs.list`): these are …

title: Render › Tree and Picture Frame fail from their dialogs: whole numbers arrive as floats
author: davidmann4
body:
**What happens.** Filter › Render › Tree… and Filter › Render › Picture Frame… fail as soon as the dialog runs them, both in the live preview and on OK, with:

```
invalid type: floating point `1.0`, expected u32
```

**Why.** The schema dialog keeps every numeric field as a JSON float. So it sends `{"baseTreeType": 1.0, "lightDirection": 3.0, ...}` and `{"frame": 1.0, "lines": 1.0, ...}`. `TreeSpec` and `FrameSpec` (`crates/algo/src/render2.rs`) declare those fields as `u32`, and serde rejects a float for a `u32`. A caller that sends integers works: the control channel, MCP, or the CLI with `{"baseTreeType": 1}`.

**Expected (Photoshop).** Both dialogs preview and apply the chosen tree or frame.

**Found by** the preview sweep in #2494, which had to convert the dialog's values to integers before it could measure these two filters. Other commands whose params deserialize integers through serde may have the same problem.

title: Filter Gallery: zoomed-out preview shows strokes and textures too large
author: davidmann4
body:
**What happens.** In Filter › Filter Gallery…, when the preview is zoomed out below 100 % on a large image, the filter's strokes, grain and textures look several times larger and coarser than what OK applies. Examples: Graphic Pen, Charcoal, Reticulation, Stained Glass, Spatter.

**Why.** `gallery_ui::update_preview` (`crates/ui-egui/src/gallery_ui.rs`) samples every k-th source pixel, with k = ceil(1/zoom), and runs the filter on that reduced image with unscaled params. The gallery filters size their strokes, grain and textures in pixels, so on a 1/k image every feature comes out k times too large. This is the gallery window's own preview path. The schema-dialog path for `filter.gallery.*` previews at full resolution since #2494.

**Expected (Photoshop).** The Filter Gallery preview at any zoom shows what OK applies, scaled down: the result is filtered at full resolution and then displayed at the zoom level.

**Measured** (mean absolute RGB difference between a 1/4 preview and the full-resolution result downsampled by 4, from the #2494 sweep): Graphic Pen 0.460, Charcoal 0.367, Reticulation 0.337, Stained Glass 0.264, Chalk & Charcoal 0.173, Spatter 0.106.

Related: #2063, #2207, #2494.

title: Proposal: shared universal GUI framework for *craft apps
author: szponciciel04
body:
### Context
We have multiple `*craft` apps (photocraft, vectorcraft, and more). Each has its own `ui-egui` crate, but they duplicate much of the same UI plumbing:

- app shell layout (docks, panels, toolbar, status bar)
- theme / design tokens and common widgets
- menu and command wiring (`engine -> UI`)
- settings / state persistence
- control channel and screenshot support for testing
- desktop + web targets

Today every UI fix or improvement has to be ported separately in each app, and the apps slowly drift apart in UX.

### Proposal
Create a shared universal GUI framework, e.g. `craft-ui`, that provides:

1. Reusable app shell: layout, theme, common panels and dialogs.
2. Small trait to plug in app-specific logic, e.g. `CraftEngine: commands(), menus(), state()`.
3. Shared settings store, test and screenshot helpers.

Each app would then keep only a thin adapter: its own tools, menus and panels built on top of `craft-ui`. Domain logic stays untouched in each app.

### Benefits
- Less duplicated UI code, one place for fixes.
- Consistent UX across all *craft apps.
- Faster bootstrap for new *craft apps.

title: Curved shapes report bounds one pixel too wide (float32 coverage residue in vector rasterizer)
author: deadmeu
body:
## Summary

Shape layers with curved edges (ellipse, rounded rect, star, custom paths…) report bounds one
pixel wider than the shape. An exact 600×600 ellipse shows **W 601 / H 600** in Properties, and
`shape.info` returns `"bounds":[660,240,601,600]`. Rectangles are exact.

## Reproduce

```sh
photocraft-cli run --new '{"width":1920,"height":1080}' \
  --cmd shape.create --params '{"kind":"ellipse","rect":[0,0,100,100],"fill":"#0000ff"}'
```

| kind | rect | bounds |
|---|---|---|
| rect | `[0,0,100,100]` | `[0,0,100,100]` ✅ |
| ellipse | `[0,0,100,100]` | `[0,0,101,100]` ❌ |
| ellipse | `[660,240,600,600]` | `[660,240,601,600]` ❌ |
| ellipse | `[10.5,10,100,100]` | `[10,10,102,100]` ❌ (should be 101) |

Seen on 0.6.0 (dev build), Linux.

## Cause

In `crates/vector/src/raster.rs`, each row's cell accumulator (`RowState::acc: Vec<f32>`)
is prefix-summed in `render_into`. A left boundary adds coverage and a right boundary subtracts
it. For curved (non-axis-aligned) edges the two don't cancel exactly in `f32`, so the pixel just
past the right edge is left with a tiny positive value. `*o = sum.clamp(0.0, 1.0)` keeps it, and
the shape's content bounds count any coverage above 0.

A probe on a 100×100 ellipse found 21 non-zero pixels in column 100, max **8.94e-8**, and
none in row 100. Rows below the shape have no active edges and are zero-filled exactly, which
is why only the width is affected.

## Suggested fix

- In `render_into`, snap near-zero coverage to 0 (e.g. `if sum < 1e-6 { 0.0 }`, well below a
  16-bit step), and optionally accumulate in `f64`.
- Add a regression test: a 100×100 ellipse reports bounds `[0,0,100,100]`.
- Check the other `Rasterizer` users (selections made from paths, vector masks, strokes) for the
  same residue.

title: WebAssembly plug-ins never appear under Filter › Plug-ins when the UI language is not English
author: tmtmtomato
body:
## Summary

With the UI language set to anything but English, an installed WASM filter plug-in is loaded (`plugin.list` reports it with `failed: []`) but never appears in the **Filter › Plug-ins** menu — only "Install Plug-in…" is shown. Switching the UI language to English (no restart needed) makes the item appear immediately.

## Root cause

`crates/ui-egui/src/plugin_ui.rs::insert_menu_items` registers the plug-in items with a **localized** menu path:

```rust
let path: Vec<String> = vec![tl!("Filter").into(), tl!("Plug-ins").into()];
```

while `crates/ui-egui/src/menus.rs::menu_bar` filters top-level items by raw equality against the English `TOP_MENUS` constants:

```rust
let mine: Vec<&MenuItem> = items.iter().filter(|i| i.path.first().map(String::as_str) == Some(top)).collect();
```

With a Japanese UI the item's path is `["フィルター", "プラグイン"]`, it never matches `"Filter"`, and the item is dropped at render time (the submenu/flyout path matching has the same problem). Other dynamically inserted submenus in the same file (File › Open Recent) use raw English segments — `vec!["File".into(), "Open Recent".into()]` — and render correctly.

The unit test `installed_plugins_appear_under_filter_plugins_and_run` doesn't catch this because tests run with the default English language, where `tl!("Filter") == "Filter"`.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Install any `.wasm` filter plug-in (Filter › Plug-ins › Install Plug-in…, or set the additional plug-ins folder in Edit › Preferences › Plug-ins).
2. Set the UI language to a non-English language (e.g. Japanese) in Edit › Preferences › Interface — or start with it already set.
3. Open Filter › Plug-ins: only "Install Plug-in…" is shown.
4. Switch the language back to English: the plug-in item appears.

The item is present in `ui.menu.list` (control channel) with path `["フィルター","プラグイン"]` even while it is missing from the rendered menu.

## Expected

Loaded plug-ins are listed under Filter › Plug-ins regardless of the UI language.

title: Desktop app.save retargets the document to flat exports (PNG/JPEG), unlike headless (#1547)
author: deadmeu
body:
## Summary

In the desktop app, `app.save` with a flat format (PNG, JPEG, …) treats the export as a save of
the document: the tab is renamed to the exported file and the document's path points at it. The
headless MCP server handles this correctly since #1547: a flat export is a copy and leaves the
document's path and name alone. The desktop path was missed.

This also affects MCP in bridge mode, since `doc_save` there goes through `app.save`.

## Reproduce

1. Start the app with a control port and an automation write root:
   `photocraft --control 9876 --control-token-file <token> --automation-write-root <dir>`
2. Bridge MCP to it: `photocraft-cli mcp --bridge 127.0.0.1:9876 --control-token-file <token>`
3. With a layered, unsaved document open, call `doc_save {"path": "flat.png"}`.
4. Call `session_list`.

**Expected:** the document keeps its name and `path` (`null` for an unsaved document), and it's
still marked as having unsaved changes, as in headless mode.

**Actual:** the document is renamed to `flat.png` and its `path` is `flat.png`.

The same sequence against the headless server (`photocraft-cli mcp --automation-write-root <dir>`)
behaves correctly: `flat.png` leaves the path unchanged, and only a `.pcraft` save retargets it.

## Cause

`save_automation` in `crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs` (~L1124) calls `state.saved_to(target)` after
every write, whatever the format. `saved_to`'s doc comment (`crates/engine/src/file_cmds.rs`)
says callers "must not call this for a copy or export". The headless equivalent
(`crates/automation/src/headless.rs`, ~L149–164) only calls it for PSD, PSB and `.pcraft`, and the
interactive File › Save path skips it for copies via the `copy` flag in `saved()`.

## Impact

- The tab and document are renamed to the export, and later saves target the export's path.
- From reading the code (not reproduced): `saved_to` also sets `saved_revision = revision`, so
  the document is marked as having no unsaved changes. Closing it after a flat export…

title: Automation preview: allow an opt-in region for documents over the 64 Mi pixel source budget
author: KnottyDyes
body:
Headless automation previews (`doc_render_preview` over MCP, `doc.render` over JSON-lines) refuse any document
whose canvas exceeds `MAX_RENDER_SOURCE_PIXELS` (64 Mi pixels) whenever filesystem access is scoped:

```
automation preview source exceeds 67108864 pixels
```

That's a common print size: a 24 × 36 in poster at 300 ppi is 7200 × 10800 = 77.76 MP. An agent editing such a document
can't look at it at all over MCP. Running without roots doesn't help, because the server then has no file access.

The current behaviour is deliberate (`budgets.rs`: "Oversized requests fail rather than silently downscale"), and
that seems right. So I'd like to propose an explicit, opt-in alternative rather than any automatic downscaling:

- An optional `rect` (`x`, `y`, `width`, `height` in integer document pixels) on `doc_render_preview`, its
  `render_preview` alias, and `doc.render`.
- Only that region is composited, through the existing `photocraft_compose::render_reduced_rect`, and the source
  budget is checked against the region's area.
- Without `rect`, behaviour and errors are unchanged. Bridge mode rejects `rect`, since bridge previews are window
  screenshots.

One known limit: the final composite is region-scoped, but some layer-effect intermediates still span their
whole layer and effect area. Memory isn't strictly proportional to the rectangle.

I have an implementation with tests: 14 new regression tests, and the automation crate's suite and clippy are clean.
Happy to open a PR if this direction works for you, or to adjust the parameter shape first.

title: Add configurable canvas size limits and progressive preview for large documents in headless mode
author: peter-research
body:
## Summary

Make the headless render preview limits (`MAX_RENDER_SOURCE_PIXELS`) configurable and add a progressive / tiled preview mode so large documents can still be inspected without filesystem access (related to open issue #2582).

## Motivation

Current hard limit of 64 Mi pixels blocks automation workflows on large canvases. A configurable limit plus a downscaled or tiled preview path would improve usability for MCP / JSON-lines automation.

## Proposed changes

- Environment variable or CLI flag to override the pixel limit.
- Optional progressive renderer that returns a low-resolution overview first, then tiles on demand.
- Clear error messages that suggest the new controls.
- Tests covering both the override and the progressive path.

---
Contribution proposal.

title: **Linux / Wayland / GNOME 50: the pen does not click in either mode (v0.6.0)**
author: JeoftonCostaDeveloper
body:
Tested v0.6.0 (`0c72d9542`, AppImage, SHA256 matches `SHA256SUMS.txt`) after #1070 was merged. Neither the Xwayland path nor native Wayland gives a working pen on this setup. Details below in case they help.

**Setup**
- Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS, GNOME Shell 50.1, mutter 50.1-0ubuntu2.4, Xwayland 2:24.1.10
- Wayland session only (no Xorg session is installed or offered at login)
- Huion T172 (USB `256c:006e`), kernel 7.0.0-38-generic, `hid_uclogic` driver loaded
- The tablet works at the OS level: the system cursor follows the pen. Xwayland exposes `xwayland-tablet stylus` / `eraser` / `pad`, and the stylus device has an `Abs Pressure` valuator (0-65535).

**1. Default (Xwayland, selected automatically by #1070): pen moves the cursor but never clicks in the app**
- stderr shows `photocraft: pen found; opening the window through Xwayland, where the pen works`, so the detection works.
- Pen clicks are never delivered to the app window.

**2. `PHOTOCRAFT_NATIVE_WAYLAND=1`: same symptom** (cursor moves, no click). Expected, since winit 0.30 does not bind `zwp_tablet_v2`.

**Where the events get lost (path 1)**
I ran `xinput test-xi2 --root` while tapping and dragging the pen over the window:
- The X server does see the pen: 24 `ButtonPress` (detail 1) from the `xwayland-tablet stylus` device, with many distinct pressure values on the valuator.
- Every one of those events has `windows: root 0x374 event 0x374 child 0x0`, i.e. no client window under the pointer. The root coordinates fall inside the target window.
- To rule out PhotoCraft, I repeated the same thing with a plain `xev` window (`DISPLAY=:0`): it received **zero** events from the pen, not even Enter/Motion. Mouse events reach it normally.

So on this stack the pen events end up at the Xwayland root and never reach any X11 client. That looks like a compositor/Xwayland delivery problem rather than anything in PhotoCraft's own X11 code, but it means the #1070 workaround does not help on GNOME 50 / mutter 50.1.

**Sugges…

title: Web build: one Ctrl/Cmd+V pastes twice when the clipboard holds text
author: vangel76
body:
Found by reading the code (eframe 0.36.2 web input + `crates/ui-egui/src/shortcuts.rs`), not yet reproduced in a browser.

### Steps
1. Web build: open a document, make a selection, Edit > Copy (Ctrl/Cmd+C).
2. Have some text on the OS clipboard as well (any text copied in another app / browser tab), or just copy as above in a browser that puts text there.
3. With the canvas focused, press Ctrl/Cmd+V.

### Expected
One pasted layer, like on desktop.

### Actual (from the code)
Two pasted layers. eframe's web runner forwards the `keydown` as `Event::Key { key: V, pressed: true, modifiers: command }` (it deliberately doesn't prevent default for Ctrl/Cmd+C/V/X), and the browser then fires its `paste` event, which eframe turns into `Event::Paste(text)` when the clipboard holds text. Both land in the same frame. `shortcuts::clipboard_keys` passes the key press through and also turns the `Paste` event into a second ⌘V press, so `edit.paste` runs twice.

The same applies to Ctrl/Cmd+X (key press + `cut` event: the second Cut runs on the now empty selection) and Ctrl/Cmd+C.

Desktop is unaffected: egui-winit drops the key press when it emits `Copy`/`Cut`/`Paste`.

title: Convert to Smart Object with several layers wraps them in a group inside the contents (Photoshop keeps them at the top level)

body:
**Steps**
1. Create two pixel layers, select both in the Layers panel.
2. Layer › Smart Objects › Convert to Smart Object.
3. Layer › Smart Objects › Edit Contents.

**Expected (Photoshop)**
The embedded document holds the two selected layers at its top level, in their stacking order. (Converting a single selected group keeps that group as-is.)

**Actual**
The contents hold one group, named after the top selected layer, with the two layers inside it.

**Code pointer**
`convert` in `crates/engine/src/smart_cmds.rs` wraps the selected top-level layers in a temporary `Layer::group(..)` and passes it to `layer_to_smart`, so the wrapper group ends up in the nested document. The existing tests in `crates/engine/src/smart_cmds/tests/selection.rs` assert this wrapper (`inner.layers[0].children()`).

title: Load Files into Stack › Create Smart Object wraps the layers in a group inside the contents

body:

1. File › Scripts › Load Files into Stack with three images and "Create Smart Object after Loading Layers" on (`file.scripts.loadFilesIntoStack` with `"createSmartObject": true`). The same happens with File › Scripts › Statistics, with or without "Attempt to Automatically Align Source Images".
2. Edit Contents of the resulting smart object.

**Expected (Photoshop)**

**Actual**
The contents hold one group named after the first file, with the loaded layers inside it.

**Cause**
Both call sites put the layers in a temporary group before they call `layer_to_smart`:
- `crates/engine/src/file_cmds.rs` `load_files_into_stack` (the `createSmartObject` branch)
- `crates/engine/src/automate_cmds.rs` `statistics` (the `align` branch)

title: Move tool: with Auto-Select, the drag's bounding box and snapping follow the previously selected layer
author: vangel76
body:
With **Auto-Select** on (the default), the Move tool's drag box and its snapping use the layers that were selected **before** the press, not the layer that Auto-Select picks and that actually moves.

This is the box drawn while dragging, which is the only feedback when Preferences › Interface › "Show bounding box when dragging layer" is on.

**Steps**
1. Make a document with two painted layers, A and B. Select B.
2. Move tool, Auto-Select on. Press on A's pixels and drag.
3. Repeat with an empty layer (or a group) selected instead of B.

**Expected (Photoshop):** the box outlines A and follows it. Snapping and smart guides align A's edges, and A is not a snap target for itself.

**Actual:**
- With B selected, the box drawn is B's bounds moving with the pointer while A moves. Snapping aligns B's edges, so A lands at the wrong place.
- With an empty layer or a group selected, no box is drawn at all, only the arrow, and the drag doesn't snap.

**Code pointer:** `canvas::tool_event` runs `snap_ui::filter_event` (and with it `snap_ui::begin`, which takes `moving_rect` from `selected_layers()` and excludes them from the targets) before the Move tool's press handler runs `layer.pickAt`. `snap_ui::draw` then draws that stale rect.

Related: #2413 / #2565 (the View › Show › Layer Edges outline during a Move). That's a different overlay.

title: Copy/Paste with no selection should keep type, shape and group layers (Photoshop's layer-based copy)
author: vangel76
body:
Holding ⌘ (Ctrl) turns a painting tool (Brush, Eraser, …) into a temporary Move tool, and ⌘ with a marquee or lasso outside the selection moves the layer as the Move tool does. In Photoshop such a drag behaves exactly like the Move tool, including smart guides and snapping.

In PhotoCraft the layer moves, but the drag gets no moving bounding box and doesn't snap (no smart guides to other layers' edges, no guide or grid snapping). With a marquee it snaps the pointer like a marquee corner instead of the layer's bounds.

**Steps**
1. New document, two layers with content apart from each other; View › Show › Smart Guides on.
2. Select the Brush tool, hold ⌘ (Ctrl) and drag one layer so its edge comes near the other's.

**Expected:** the Move tool's box and magenta smart guides; the edge snaps.
**Actual:** no box, no snapping.

**Cause:** `snap_ui::begin` (crates/ui-egui/src/snap_ui.rs) picks the snap gesture from `app.ui.tool`, the selected tool, rather than the tool the press acts as (`tool_override` / ⌘ in `canvas::tool_event`, `canvas::command_moves_layer`).

title: CI: Actions cache is over the 10 GB limit, so the perf nightly's cache is always evicted
author: 1Git2Clone
body:
The repo's Actions cache is at 11.7 GB, over GitHub's default 10 GB per-repo limit. The per-job breakdown, the command and the run evidence are in https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/pull/2575#issuecomment-6099878374.

**Effect:** GitHub evicts the least recently used entries. CI on main restores its caches all day, so they survive. The perf nightly's cache is used once a day, so it's always the first to go: every scheduled nightly so far found no cache and rebuilt from scratch.

**Cause:** `ci.yml`'s test job keeps three generations per OS (5.63 GB on Linux and 3.37 GB on Windows as of 3e000bc1). `rust-cache` saves a new entry whenever the `Cargo.lock` hash changes, and the older ones stay until they're evicted.

**Possible fixes:**
- Delete superseded generations after a save, keeping the newest entry per job (Actions cache API or `gh cache delete`).
- Save the test caches less often than on every push to main.
- Raise the repo's cache limit: storage above 10 GB costs $0.07 per GB-month, so 15 GB is about $0.35/month ([docs](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/dependency-caching#increasing-cache-size)).

Found while working on #2575.

title: Edit › Cut with a single colour channel targeted clears every channel of the layer
author: vangel76
body:
With a single colour channel (e.g. Red) targeted in the Channels panel, **Edit › Cut** ignores the target: it puts the whole layer (all channels) on the clipboard and clears the selected area in **every** channel of the layer, making it transparent (or filling it with the background colour on the Background).

**Expected (Photoshop):** Cut with one channel targeted copies only that channel (as grayscale) and clears the selection in that channel alone; the other channels and the layer's transparency stay as they were.

**Cause:** `edit.cut` (`crates/engine/src/edit_cmds.rs`) is not one of the commands whose target follows the Channels panel (`routed()` in `crates/engine/src/channel_cmds.rs`), so no colour restriction applies to its clear step, and `copy()` ignores the channel target.

**Steps:** File › New (RGB) → fill red → Channels panel: target Red → Select All → Edit › Cut → the Background turns the background colour in all channels instead of only the Red channel changing.

Related: #2680 / #2307 (Copy and Paste with a channel targeted; PR #2695 explicitly leaves Cut for a follow-up).

title: PSD/PSB import: an unreadable Lr16/Lr32 block silently drops every layer
author: vangel76
body:
**Steps:** open a 16- or 32-bit PSD/PSB whose layers are stored in the global `Lr16`/`Lr32` block (as the format requires for those depths), where that block can't be parsed. For example, a layer count larger than the records that follow.

**Actual:** the open succeeds with no warning. The document has one "Background" layer in Normal mode, built from the merged composite, and every layer is gone. If the file was saved without Maximize Compatibility, that composite is blank. Saving again writes a new `Lr16` and also keeps the unreadable one from the original global blocks, so the saved file contains two `Lr16` blocks.

**Expected:** a warning saying the layers couldn't be read and only the merged image was opened (the same pattern as the #1763 adjustment warning). The unreadable block should be kept for saving without producing a duplicate `Lr16`/`Lr32`.

**Where:** `crates/psd/src/file.rs` `PsdFile::from_bytes` drops the parse error (`&& let Ok(info) = LayerInfo::read_body(..)`), and `crates/io/src/psd_import.rs` never checks for an unconsumed `Lr16`/`Lr32`/`Layr` block.

Reproduced on `main` 2d6154a: export a 16-bit PSB, replace the layer info with an `Lr16` block that holds only a count of 2 and 10 zero bytes, then import it. The result is `[("Background", Normal)]` with no warnings, and a re-export holds two `Lr16` blocks.

Found while investigating #1764.

title: Edit › Clear (Delete) with a single colour channel targeted clears every channel of the layer

body:

2. Click the Red channel in the Channels panel.

title: Printing not working (CUPS errors, no Windows support)
author: rafi612
body:
### Problem

`File > Print…` renders the document but can't send it to the printer. Depending on the install, one of these appears in the status bar:

- **Flatpak:** `could not run 'lp' (CUPS): No such file or directory` — always. The sandbox has no `lp` client.
- **Native Linux:** `lp failed: lp: Error - No default destination.` — when no default printer is configured and the `Printer` field is left empty (the dialog default).
- **Windows:** `could not run 'lp' (CUPS): …` — always. The code spawns Unix `lp`, which doesn't exist on Windows.

A temp `*-print-*.pdf` is left behind in each case, and the settings are not remembered.

## Repro

1. Open any document.
2. `File > Print…`, leave `Printer` empty, click `Print`.
3. See the status-bar error (variant depends on install type).

PDF generation itself works — only spooling is broken. Filling `Save as PDF` in the same dialog and printing the PDF from the OS works fine.

## Expected

- Detect printers and the default before spooling; validate the `Printer` field instead of passing raw CUPS errors through.
- Handle "printer exists but no default" gracefully (use the only printer, or ask to pick/set one) — before writing the temp PDF.
- Clean up the temp PDF and keep `Save as PDF` as a working fallback.

## Proposed fix

Replace the `lp`-subprocess spool (`crates/engine/src/print_cmds.rs:spool_pdf`) with a real backend behind a platform seam (engine keeps PDF rendering only):

- **Unix:** [`cups_rs`](https://crates.io/crates/cups_rs) — typed discovery, job options (copies, media, orientation, duplex), categorized errors. Note: Unix-only, needs system `libcups` + `bindgen` at build time, so it must be a `cfg(unix)`-gated dep to keep the wasm check green.
- **Windows:** [`printers`](https://crates.io/crates/printers) — the only one of the two covering Windows (winspool). Note: PDF-over-RAW depends on the driver, otherwise it needs host Ghostscript — needs a spike test with our generated PDF first.
- **Flatpak:** neither …

title: Proposal: Decouple UI feature availability and layout from visual themes
author: genrichh93-ui
body:
Summary

Currently, PhotoCraft's visual themes also influence parts of the application's UI layout and the visibility or presentation of certain controls.

For example, switching from the default Pro (Dark) appearance to a light appearance selects a theme from the Studio, Classic, or Adwaita family. This can substantially change the interface rather than simply switching its colors.

I propose separating three concerns:

  1. Feature availability — which tools, panels, and actions the application supports.

  2. UI layout — how those features are arranged and presented (Pro, Studio, Classic, etc.).

  3. Visual appearance — colors, contrast, borders, typography styling, and light/dark variants.

The goal is to make PhotoCraft's functionality consistent across themes while allowing users to change appearance without unexpectedly changing their workspace.

Motivation

While testing PhotoCraft on GNOME/Linux, I noticed that switching from the dark Pro interface to a light theme also changes several UI elements:

  • Overlapping square foreground/background color swatches become round color chips.

  • Panel styling and toolbar layout change significantly.

  • Some toolbar controls and panel groups are presented differently depending on the selected theme.

These differences are not inherently bad. The Studio interface is a valid design in its own right.

However, visual appearance and workspace layout are different user preferences

title: Edit › Clear (Delete) with an alpha channel targeted changes the layer instead of the channel
author: vangel76
body:
With an alpha channel (e.g. "Alpha 1") targeted in the Channels panel, Edit › Clear (Delete) changes the active layer and leaves the alpha channel alone. The same happens in Quick Mask mode: Delete clears the layer instead of the mask.

**Steps**
1. File › New, Channels › New Channel filled white (Alpha 1 is targeted).
2. Set the background colour to black, make a rectangular selection.
3. Edit › Clear (or press Delete).

**Expected (Photoshop):** the selected area of Alpha 1 is filled with the background colour (as gray), the layer is untouched, one undo step. In Quick Mask mode, Delete fills the mask with the background colour.

**Actual:** the layer's pixels inside the selection are cleared to the background colour; Alpha 1 is unchanged.

`edit.clear` is not routed to the channel target (unlike Edit › Fill), and it is disabled when the active layer is not a pixel layer even though a channel is targeted. Related: #2720 / #2730 (colour-channel target).

title: Moving a selection outline snaps the pointer instead of the selection's edges
author: vangel76
body:
With a marquee or lasso tool, dragging inside an existing selection moves the selection outline (and ⌘-drag cuts the selected pixels into a floating piece and moves that). In Photoshop the moved outline's **bounds** (edges and centre) snap to guides, document edges and layer edges, the same as the Move tool snaps a layer's bounds.

PhotoCraft does something else:
- Rectangular/Elliptical Marquee: the **pointer** snaps as if it were drawing a new marquee corner. The outline jumps by however far the pointer moved to reach a target, so its edges usually end up next to the guide instead of on it.
- Lasso: nothing snaps at all.

**Steps** (View › Snap on, the default):
1. New 400×300 document, add a vertical guide at x = 220.
2. Rectangular Marquee: select 100,100 – 150,140.
3. Drag from inside it 68 px to the right, so the outline's right edge comes within 2 px of the guide.

**Expected:** the right edge lands on the guide (selection 170–220).
**Actual:** the pointer snaps to the document centre (x = 200), and the selection ends at 175–225, past the guide.

title: Quick Mask: with no selection the whole canvas is treated as selected, and Select All is lost on exit
author: JohnSabol55
body:
## Case 1: Quick Mask with no selection (Color Indicates Selected Areas)

**What I did**
1. Open any document and make sure nothing is selected.
2. Press `Q` to enter Quick Mask.
3. Right-click the **Quick Mask** channel in the Channels panel and choose **Color Indicates Selected Areas**.

**What was expected**
Quick Mask starts empty, with no overlay, because nothing is selected. Painting adds to the selection, so the painted area is the selection when Quick Mask is left. 

**What happened**
The whole canvas is covered by the red overlay, as if everything were selected. To select a small area I have to paint away everything I do not want, or press Ctrl+I to invert the mask first. That works, but it is an extra step that a normal "nothing selected" start should not need.

---

## Case 2: Select All, then Quick Mask round trip

**What I did**
1. Open any document and press `Ctrl+A` (to select the whole canvas).
2. Press `Q` to enter Quick Mask, then press `Q` again to leave it.

**What was expected**
The whole canvas is selected, as it was before entering Quick Mask. Entering Quick Mask turns the selection into a mask and leaving turns it back, so a full selection should survive the round trip like any other selection.

**What happened**
There is no selection at all after `Q`, `Q`.

---

Both Color Indicates settings behave the same in these cases. With a real selection made with a selection tool, entering and leaving Quick Mask works correctly.

## Cause (as far as I can tell from the source)

In `crates/engine/src/channel_cmds.rs`:
- `quick_mask_from` fills the Quick Mask channel solid white when there is no selection. White means selected, so with **Selected Areas** the overlay covers everything.
- `selection_from` turns any all-white mask back into "no selection". A real Select All, which is also all white, therefore becomes no selection.

So "nothing selected" and "everything selected" cannot be told apart.

## Suggested fix

- With no selection, start the mask …

title: Normal Brush Tip cursor ring is too large for soft brushes (old falloff formula)
author: vangel76
body:
With Preferences › Cursors › Painting Cursors = **Normal Brush Tip**, the brush ring should sit on the tip's 50 % opacity contour (Adobe: "restricts the cursor size to areas of the brush stroke that have 50 % or more opacity").

Since #2167 the soft falloff in `photocraft_paint::tip_falloff` is `(1 - t²)⁴`, where `t` runs from the hard core (`hardness · r`) to the edge `r`. Its 50 % point is at `t = sqrt(1 - 0.5^¼) ≈ 0.399`, so the contour is at `r · (h + 0.399 · (1 - h))`.

The cursor (`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`, the `NormalTip` branch) still uses `r · (0.5 + 0.5 · h)`, the 50 % point of the old smoothstep falloff. The ring is too large for soft brushes:

| size 21, hardness | ring drawn | true 50 % contour |
|---|---|---|
| 0 % | 5.25 px | 4.19 px |
| 25 % | 6.56 px | 5.77 px |
| 50 % | 7.88 px | 7.34 px |
| 75 % | 9.19 px | 8.92 px |
| 100 % | 10.5 px | 10.5 px |

Fix: derive the ring radius from the paint crate's own falloff (a small helper that inverts it), so the cursor and the engine can't drift apart again.

title: Windows CI: save_dialogs_remember_where_each_document_was_last_saved fails on main (hard-coded / separators)
author: Sir-Starch
body:
`cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui` fails on `windows-latest` on current `main`:

```
file_dialog::tests::save_dialogs_remember_where_each_document_was_last_saved
  panicked at crates\ui-egui\src\file_dialog\tests.rs:299:5
  left:  "/proj\\result.png"
  right: "/proj/result.png"
```

Seen on `main` itself (run https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/actions/runs/38072256347, commit c287ecab, an unrelated change) and on every PR rebased onto it (for example #2335, which only adds themes). The test came with #2421.

**Cause:** `pick_save` builds the suggested path with `Path::join`, which is correct and uses `\` on Windows, but the test compares against hard-coded `/` strings (`/proj/result.png`, `/renders/again.png`, `/renders/third.png`, ...). So it is the test that is POSIX-specific, not the behaviour.

**Possible fix:** build the expected values with `Path::new("/proj").join("result.png")` (and the same for the other directories) instead of literals, or normalise separators before comparing.

Most CI runs on `main` get cancelled by the next push, so this red result is easy to miss.

Happy to send the small test fix if that helps.

title: Batch and droplets reject actions that contain recorded view steps (unknown command)
author: vangel76
body:
**What happens**

An action recorded in the desktop app can contain view steps (`view.zoomIn`, `view.zoomOut`, `view.fitOnScreen`, `view.actualPixels`): the shell records them (`actions_cmds::shell_view_command`). Running that action with File › Automate › Batch or Create Droplet fails before any file is processed:

```
unknown command `view.zoomIn` in the action
```

because both validate every step against the engine's command registry, and view steps are shell-only.

**Repro (engine)**

```rust
s.execute("file.automate.batch", json!({"steps": [["view.zoomIn", {}], ["image.imageRotation.90cw", {}]], "input": dir, "output": out}))
// Err(BadParams { msg: "unknown command `view.zoomIn` in the action" })
```

Same for `file.automate.createDroplet` with those steps.

**Expected (Photoshop)**

Batch and droplets run actions with zoom/fit steps fine; the view steps have no effect on the processed files.

**Fix idea**

Batch and Create Droplet skip the shell's view steps (as #2746 does for recorded saves), so the rest of the action runs.

title: ⌘-drag with a painting tool moves the whole layer instead of the selected pixels when driven via the control channel
author: vangel76
body:
With an active selection, ⌘-drag with a painting tool (the temporary Move tool, #2248) floats and moves the selected pixels in the app, as the Move tool does (#578). Driven through the control channel / MCP (`ui.pointer` with `command: true` on the events), or from tests, the same drag moves the whole layer instead.

**Steps:** transparent document, paint two squares, select one, Brush tool, `ui.pointer` drag with ⌘ from inside the canvas.

**Expected:** the selected pixels float and move, the rest of the layer stays (as with ⌘ physically held).

**Actual:** nothing floats; the whole layer moves.

**Cause:** `move_ui::moves_selected_pixels` asks `app.active_tool()`, which only sees the held-key override (`tool_override`) that the canvas sets while ⌘ is down. `canvas::tool_event` resolves ⌘ from the event's modifiers into the Move tool, but the selected-pixels checks inside it (and in `move_lock::blocked`) still see the Brush.

Actual: the Eraser Mode dropdown only offers Brush and Pencil.

title: Content-Aware Spot Healing takes ~300–800 ms per small dab on large documents
author: vangel76
body:
A single Content-Aware Spot Healing click costs 0.4–0.8 s on a large document, even for a 50 px spot, while Proximity Match and Create Texture take about 10 ms at the same size. Photoshop heals small spots almost instantly.

**Measured** (`retouch_bench`, release, 6016×6016 8-bit RGB, one single-dab stroke through `Session::execute`; the machine was under load, so the numbers are noisy):

| size | contentAware | proximityMatch | createTexture |
|---|---|---|---|
| 50 | 441 ms | 10 ms | 10 ms |
| 100 | 524 ms | 26 ms | 27 ms |
| 200 | 722 ms | 71 ms | 124 ms |
| 300 | 796 ms | 231 ms | 305 ms |

**Where the time goes** (`perf`): about 72 % is in `photocraft_algo::inpaint::onion_peel`, the initial fill at the coarsest pyramid level of `inpaint::complete`. For each pixel on the hole's front it scans **every** valid source patch in the window (the full 7×7 SSD with no early exit) to pick the best one. The pyramid shrinks the hole to about four patches across, and the sampling window is about four times the hole, so this exhaustive scan costs about the same at every brush size (~600 hole pixels × ~10 000 sources × 49 pixels). PatchMatch (`Solver::dist`, `vote`) accounts for most of the rest.

The sampling window itself is already bounded: `content_aware::sampling_window`, about 4× the dab. The cost is the exhaustive initialisation, not the window. Content-Aware Fill, Remove, Patch and Content-Aware Move also call `inpaint::complete`, so they pay the same cost.

**Expected:** a small Content-Aware dab should feel instant (well under 100 ms), and the healed pixels should not change.

title: Batch, script steps and droplets report success when a step fails inside a nested action
author: vangel76
body:
An action step that plays another action (`actions.play`) returns `Ok` with a `failed` entry when a step inside the called action fails. Headless and desktop action playback catch this (`actions_cmds::nested_failure`), but other step runners don't:

- **File › Scripts › Browse** (`file.scripts.browse`) and **Script Events**: the failure is ignored. The script reports `"ok": true` and keeps running the later steps.
  Repro: an action `Bad` with the step `layer.delete {"layer": 999999}`, then `file.scripts.browse {"steps": [["actions.play", {"action": "Bad"}], ["image.imageRotation.90cw", {}]]}` → `ok: true`, and the rotation runs.
- **File › Automate › Batch** and **Run Droplet**: each file runs in a scratch session that has no actions, so a batched action containing a nested action call fails on every file with `no action named 'Bad'`, even when the called action exists. Once nested calls can run, a failure inside them also has to land in the batch's `errors` instead of the file being saved as a success.

Expected (Photoshop): a failing step inside a called action stops the script, and Batch reports the file as an error (Errors: Stop / Log Errors to File) instead of saving it as a success.

title: photocraft-cli batch: an action that plays another action fails for every file
author: vangel76
body:
**What happens**

`photocraft-cli batch --actions <file>` runs each input file in a fresh headless session with no actions loaded, so an action step that plays another action (`actions.play`, Photoshop's "Play Action" step) fails on every file:

```
FAIL  in/a.png: `actions.play`: invalid parameters for `actions.play`: no action named `Rotate`
FAIL  in/b.png: …
0 succeeded, 2 failed
```

There is also no way to hand the CLI the called action: `--actions` only takes one action's steps, and passing the Actions panel's own `actions.json` (`{"version": 1, "actions": [{"name", "steps"}…]}`) fails with `step needs "command"`.

**Expected (Photoshop)**

Batch plays the chosen action (Set + Action) with its whole set available, so nested Play Action steps work. A failure inside the called action makes that file an error instead of a saved result.

**Fix idea**

`batch --actions` also accepts an Actions set, with `--action <name>` picking the action to play; every per-file session gets the whole set, and a failed nested step (`actions_cmds::nested_failure`) fails the file. Same problem as #2779 for the in-app Batch (fixed there by #2783).

title: Filter › Neural Filters: Photo Restoration on a local model (repair scratches, stains and specks of scanned prints)
author: diegochagas
body:
## What

Photoshop's **Filter › Neural Filters › Photo Restoration**: a scanned print with blotches, stains, scratches and dust specks is repaired in one step, with *Photo Enhancement*, *Enhance face* and *Scratch reduction* sliders, and the result can go to a new layer. PhotoCraft has nothing under this menu yet: `crates/ui-egui/src/menu_catalog.rs` has no `Filter › Neural Filters…` entry at all, so `docs/parity.md` counts 627/627 while Photoshop's Filter menu has one more item.

## Why now

The roadmap grades AI at ~0% and #41 keeps *generative* features on hold until a provider interface lands. Photo Restoration is not generative in that sense: no prompt, no new content, only damage repair of existing pixels. It fits the `ImageProvider` seam proposed in #730 (edit with mask) and the local backends asked for in #584, #1996 and #2682, and it works offline on the user's own GPU.

## Proposed behaviour

- `filter.neuralFilters.photoRestoration` (new catalog entry `Filter › Neural Filters…`, Photoshop's position after *Camera Raw Filter*). Params: `enhance` 0–100, `enhanceFace` 0–100, `scratchReduction` 0–100, `output: "currentLayer" | "newLayer"` (default new layer, like Photoshop's Output menu).
- The model only repairs damage: compare input and output, build a mask of the changed pixels (dilated a few px, feathered), and apply the model's pixels **only inside that mask**. Everything else stays the original, so grain, colour and sharpness of the undamaged print are untouched. Output as a new layer with that mask, so the user can paint the mask to undo a repair.
- Runs as a background job (progress, cancel, one history step), respects the selection, works at 8/16/32-bit by converting at the provider boundary.
- Without a configured local provider the menu item is enabled but reports "no local model backend configured" with a link to Preferences; off the wasm path entirely (`cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))`).

## Backend

A local **ComfyUI** HTTP backend behind the p…

title: Select Subject, Object Selection and Remove Background with a local segmentation model (BiRefNet / SAM 2), heuristic as fallback
author: diegochagas
body:
## What

**Select › Subject**, the **Object Selection** tool and the Properties panel's **Remove Background** exist (`crates/engine/src/smartselect_cmds.rs`, `select.object`, `crates/engine/src/cutout_cmds.rs`), but they are heuristic. `docs/parity-estimate.md` says so: "heuristic Select Subject/Sky vs Adobe's ML". On real photos (hair, fur, thin straps, low contrast with the background) the heuristic mask is far from Photoshop's, and Remove Background inherits every error as a layer mask.

This issue proposes running the three on a **local segmentation model** when one is available, keeping the current code as the fallback:

| Command | Model | Prompt |
|---|---|---|
| `select.subject` | BiRefNet (dichotomous segmentation, state of the art for "the subject") | none |
| `select.object` (Object Selection tool, box drag; Shift adds, Alt subtracts) | SAM 2.1 | the dragged box |
| `layer.removeBackground` (Quick Action) | BiRefNet | none; mask becomes the layer mask, not applied |

## How

- A `SegmentationProvider` trait next to the `ImageProvider` of #730 (or in the same crate): `subject(image) -> mask`, `object(image, box|points) -> mask`. One local **ComfyUI** HTTP backend (the address configured per #6067; BiRefNet and SAM 2 run as ComfyUI nodes, no weights shipped). Transport behind a trait, so tests use a fake provider.
- The three commands gain `"backend": "auto|classical|model" = "auto"`: *auto* uses the model when a backend is configured and reachable, else the classical path, and the result JSON says which ran. Nothing changes for existing scripts or the wasm build (model path is `cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))`).
- Masks come back as 8-bit alpha at the image size; the existing refine step of `layer.removeBackground` (smart radius) still applies. Selections respect the current combine mode (new, add, subtract, intersect).
- Timing: BiRefNet on a mid-range GPU is ~1 s for a 24 MP photo (the model runs at 1024² and the mask is upscaled with edge-aware refinem…

title: feat(codecs): open JPEG XL (.jxl) images with a pure-Rust decoder
author: diegochagas
body:
## What

PhotoCraft cannot open **JPEG XL** (`.jxl`) files. `crates/codecs/README.md` states "AVIF decoding and JPEG XL are unavailable", `Format` in `crates/codecs/src/format.rs` has no `Jxl` variant, and I found no issue for it (#1047 is JPEG 2000, #463 is AVIF). JPEG XL is the format Apple ships in iOS 17+ cameras (ProRAW and HEIF alternatives), Chrome re-enabled it in 2025, and GIMP, Krita, darktable and Affinity read and write it.

## Proposed

Read support first, as HEIF is done today:

- A `jxl` cargo feature (official builds enable it) wrapping a **pure-Rust decoder**: [`jxl-oxide`](https://github.com/tirr-c/jxl-oxide) decodes the full JPEG XL spec (modular and VarDCT, including lossless-JPEG recompression) with no C code and no `unsafe` in its public path; licence to be confirmed against MIT OR Apache-2.0 before adding (it is dual-licensed MIT/Apache-2.0 as of its current releases). Wrap it in a small optional crate `crates/jxl` like `crates/heif` (panic-guarded, `Limits` on dimensions and memory) so a decoder bug can't take the app down.
- `Format::Jxl`: extension `jxl`, MIME `image/jxl`, detection by the bare codestream signature `FF 0A` and the ISOBMFF container (`0000000C 4A584C20 0D0A870A`). Entry in `ASYMMETRIC_EXCEPTIONS`: write stays unsupported until a pure-Rust encoder exists (libjxl is C++).
- Depths: 8 and 16-bit integer and float samples kept (JXL is float internally; map to U8/U16/F32 as TIFF does), gray and RGB with alpha, embedded ICC profile and EXIF/XMP boxes passed to the document, first frame of an animation.
- Fuzz target `crates/codecs/fuzz/fuzz_targets/decode_jxl.rs` with a timeout, as `decode_heif.rs`; a tiny pinned test corpus (the public conformance images are CC0) checked by sha256 like `xtask/heif-corpus.sha256`.
- `docs/file-format-parity.md`, the README Formats paragraph and `crates/codecs/README.md` updated in the same change.

I'd like to implement this.

title: Neural Filters: Modern Photo (colorize and enhance an old photo as a modern camera shot, on a local model)
author: diegochagas
body:
## What

A **Neural Filters › Modern Photo** filter: an old photo (faded, soft, black and white or yellowed) is re-rendered by a local image-edit model as if taken today with a modern phone camera: sharp, clean, true colours, black and white comes back in colour. The result is a new layer above the original, never a destructive edit.

Photoshop's nearest items are *Neural Filters › Colorize* and the *Photo Enhancement* slider of *Photo Restoration*; this filter covers both in one pass and goes further on detail. If the maintainers prefer strict parity, the same backend gives *Colorize* for free and I can split that out as its own command.

## Depends on

A local model provider (see #2787 and #41 / #730 / #2682): this is the second filter on the same `Filter › Neural Filters…` entry and the same ComfyUI backend, so it adds a command and a dialog, not infrastructure. Non-generative in the #41 sense: no prompt from the user, no new content beyond re-rendering the same picture.

## Proposed behaviour

- `filter.neuralFilters.modernPhoto`, params: `colorize: bool = true`, `strength` 0–100 (how far from the original the model may go; implemented as a blend with the source), `output: "newLayer" | "currentLayer"` (default new layer).

title: Droplets don't include the actions their Play Action steps call, so they fail outside the app
author: vangel76
body:
`file.automate.createDroplet` saves only the chosen action's own steps. If that action contains a Play Action step (`actions.play` of another action), the droplet fails on every file when it runs outside the session that made it: `photocraft-cli droplet` and the droplet's `.command` shim run `file.automate.runDroplet` in a fresh session with no actions, so each file reports `no action named …`.

Photoshop droplets run standalone. A droplet should carry the actions its Play Action steps call (transitively), and `runDroplet` should load them into the per-file batch sessions. Older droplet files without them should keep working.

Related: #2779 / #2783 (nested failures in batch), #2786 (CLI `batch --actions`).

title: fix(theme): late Linux initial appearance does not repaint the idle window
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

When the first Linux portal Read finishes after the host startup wait, PhotoCraft publishes the appearance without waking the UI. An idle Auto window can keep its initial dark fallback after a valid Light result is available, until another event causes a frame.

## Runtime or environment

Audited `storytold/photocraft` main at `706c730cd20b951080033c6e1166c260f40fe5dd`. Native Linux Auto path with a working desktop portal and a valid Light Read reply delayed beyond the 250 ms startup wait but within the 2-second method timeout. Cargo.lock selects egui/eframe/egui-winit 0.36.2, winit 0.30.13 and zbus 5.19.0. The supplied probe copies the service worker into a controlled substitute; it does not launch PhotoCraft or use real D-Bus.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Select Sync with system and a saved Light-family theme. Let the native Linux startup portal Read remain pending beyond the service's 250 ms wait.
2. Execute the initial frame while the host reader returns unknown, register the egui context, and allow unrelated startup activity to finish. Use an otherwise idle window with saved preferences and no pending retries.
3. Release a valid portal Light reply before the Read method timeout. Supply no later portal signal or user input.
4. Compare the host reader's new Light answer with repaint requests and the still-idle displayed palette.

These are source-established app steps. The supplied controlled worker probe held Read past the actual startup wait, registered a real egui repaint callback, released Light and saw zero callbacks. It did not display a Linux app window. This drafting investigation inspected the exact worker/probe and outputs but did not rerun them.

## Expected behavior

Once a supported portal returns Light after startup, Auto must wake the idle UI and apply the saved Light palette without another OS event or user action. [Current UI design contract](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/706c730cd20b951080033c6e1166c260f40fe5dd/docs/ui-d…

title: fix(theme): Linux appearance change before subscription leaves a stale result
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

PhotoCraft reads the Linux portal appearance before subscribing to SettingChanged. A single valid change in that gap is lost, leaving the cached host appearance stale even on later app frames when no subsequent portal change occurs.

## Runtime or environment

Audited `storytold/photocraft` main at `706c730cd20b951080033c6e1166c260f40fe5dd`. Native Linux Auto path with a working desktop portal; initial Read returns Light, then a change to Dark occurs before subscription completes. Cargo.lock selects zbus 5.19.0 and winit 0.30.13. The supplied extracted-worker probe uses a controlled portal substitute, not a real session bus or launched app.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start the Linux service with Sync with system selected and a working portal. Complete its initial Read with Light.
2. Before PhotoCraft installs the SettingChanged match, change the portal value to Dark and emit that single valid change.
3. Allow subscription to complete. Send no second change. Call the cached host reader on later app frames.
4. Verify the answer remains Light even though the portal is now Dark.

The timing case is source-established. The supplied substitute probe pauses at the exact Read-to-subscribe boundary, changes its controlled state before subscription, then observes cached Light afterward. It models the separately verified no-retention contract for signals before the match exists. No real D-Bus change or native app reproduction was executed, and this drafting investigation did not rerun the probe.

Auto must retain and apply a single valid Linux appearance change during initialization, without requiring a second OS event or user input. title: Web build: File › Open opens only one of several selected files
author: vangel76
body:
In the web build, File › Open lets you pick only one file. `apps/photocraft-web/src/web.rs` calls `rfd::AsyncFileDialog::pick_file()` and ignores the request's `multiple` flag, and `FileDialogAnswer` can only carry the contents of one file (`Contents(name, bytes)`).

Found while checking #2780. Dropping several files onto the web page already opens all of them; only the Open dialog is affected.

title: wasm32: dead-code warnings in photocraft-cms (PAR_MIN_PIXELS, PAR_CHUNK_PIXELS) and photocraft-engine (OPENABLE)
author: vangel76
body:
On `wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `main` emits three dead-code warnings:

```
$ cargo check -p photocraft-engine --target wasm32-unknown-unknown
warning: constant `PAR_MIN_PIXELS` is never used   --> crates/cms/src/transform.rs:513
warning: constant `PAR_CHUNK_PIXELS` is never used --> crates/cms/src/transform.rs:514
warning: constant `OPENABLE` is never used         --> crates/engine/src/file_cmds.rs:118
```

Their only users (`par_rows` / `par_inplace`, the rayon path, and `list_images`) are `#[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]`, but the constants are not gated. CI stays green because `cargo xtask wasm` runs plain `cargo check` without `-D warnings`, but `cargo clippy --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -- -D warnings` fails for these crates, and the warnings show up in every web build.

Fix: gate the constants with the same `cfg` as their users. No behaviour change.

title: Proposal: Integrate Nik Collection-style local adjustment tools (Viveza & U Point technology) with ML Issue Detection & Personalized Automation
author: olesme
body:
### Description

#### Context & Real-World Retouching Scenarios

Global edits (curves, white balance, exposure) work well for the overall frame, but photographic retouching mostly consists of localized, highly repetitive adjustments targeting specific visual issues across key image regions:

- **Portrait & Beauty Retouching:**
  - **Eyes:** Brightening the eye region, opening up harsh eye-socket shadows, and slightly boosting iris contrast/structure.
  - **Lips & Skin:** Warming up lip saturation, softening skin texture without losing natural pores, and flattening harsh directional shadows or bright hot-spots across the face.
  - **Hair & Details:** Adding selective micro-contrast to hair details or popping catchlights in the eyes.
- **Landscape & Outdoor Photography:**
  - **Sky & Dynamic Range:** Recovering blown-out or washed-out skies through complex tree branches or architectural frames.
  - **Foreground Accents:** Boosting saturation and warmth on selective patches of sunlight on foliage or rocks without affecting shadowy backgrounds.

Doing this with traditional brush masks or layers takes minutes per photo, requiring constant zoom adjustments, edge feathering, and cleanup.

The **Control Point approach** (pioneered by Nik Collection's Viveza / U Point technology) simplifies this by letting the user click directly on a target area. The tool samples the color, hue, and luminance under the point and creates a dynamic local mask for matching pixels within a radius — turning complex edge masking into a single click and slider drag.

---

title: Canvas selection and layer context menus close immediately on quick right-clicks on macOS
author: zi-ger
body:
Related to #2360, which reports the same behavior in the Brush Preset picker. This issue covers the selection context menu and the Move tool’s canvas layer menu, outside the scope of #2772.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open a document with a visible layer.
2. Select the Rectangular or Elliptical Marquee tool and create a selection.
3. Open the canvas context menu with a two-finger trackpad click.
4. Dismiss it by clicking outside.
5. Try opening it again. The menu briefly appears and immediately closes.

The same behavior occurs when right-clicking over a visible layer on the canvas with the Move tool (V).

### Expected behavior

The menu stays open until an action is chosen, Escape is pressed, or a later click occurs outside it.

### Investigation

Automated full-UI tests reproduced the dismissal with:

- Rectangular and Elliptical Marquee
- Lasso, Polygonal Lasso, and Magnetic Lasso
- Magic Wand and Object Selection
- Move tool’s canvas layer menu

It reproduces with and without an active selection when secondary-button press and release arrive in the same frame at fractional coordinates. Slower clicks and clicks aligned to whole pixels stayed open.

Both menu implementations can treat the opening press as an outside click after rounding the menu position. For example, an opening press at `x=457.5` falls outside a menu whose left edge rounds to `x=458`, immediately dismissing it. This matches the cause identified for #2360.

Quick Selection uses the Brush Preset picker and passed these probes with the fix from #2772 applied.

title: Performance: repeated Select Subject on 24 MP over budget (P29: ~690 ms vs 100 ms)
author: vangel76
body:
Scorecard row **P29 "Select Subject on 24 MP, repeated"** (part of #211): budget ≤ 100 ms p95, the 2026-10-05 baseline measured 559 ms p50 / 693 ms p95 (`perf_scenarios` row `Select Subject 24 MP (repeat)`).

Running Select Subject again on an unchanged document recomputes everything: the composite (or layer) is resampled to the working resolution, SLIC superpixels, the saliency optimisation and GrabCut run again, and the result is re-cut at full resolution. Photoshop answers the second call near-instantly.

Proposal: remember the last subject mask, keyed by the pixels it was computed from (the same tile-pointer comparison `same_pixels` the session already uses for damage, so selection-only edits such as Deselect keep it valid) and by the sampled target (composite vs. active layer). A repeat returns the cached mask and still applies the selection mode (replace/add/subtract/intersect). One entry for the whole session, held weakly so it never keeps a closed or edited document's tiles alive. Results stay bit-identical.
