title: Performance: Select › Modify › Feather/Smooth on 24 MP over budget (P27 357 ms, P26 ~250 ms vs 100 ms)
author: vangel76
body:
Part of #211 (scorecard rows P26 and P27, `perf/budgets.toml`).

**Budget:** Select › Modify › Feather and Select › Modify › Smooth on a 24 MP photo (radius 50) should take ≤ 100 ms p95.
**Measured** (`docs/scorecard.md`, `perf/baseline.json`): P27 Feather p50 122 ms, p95 357 ms; P26 Smooth p50 100 ms, p95 216 ms (max 251 ms).

**Where the time goes** (release, 6000×4000, the `perf_scenarios` ellipse selection, best of 7 on a 16-core machine):

| stage | Smooth | Feather |
|---|---|---|
| read the selection into an f32 mask (parallel) | 3.6 ms | 3.6 ms |
| the blur itself (`selection_blur`, already parallel and radius-independent) | 9 ms | 15 ms |
| store the result as a GRAY8 selection (`selection::combine`) | 9 ms | 9 ms |
| **whole command** | **86 ms** | **87–140 ms** |

The ~60 ms gap is in the engine glue around the blur, which runs on one thread:

- `selection_cmds::modify` always copies the mask into a padded buffer (`pad_mask`, per sample with bounds checks) and copies the result back out (`crop_mask`, a `flat_map` collect). It does this even when the padding is 0, which is the usual case: a selection clear of the canvas edge. That is two serial passes over 24 M floats.
- `combine` builds a full-canvas byte buffer, scans it once more to see whether it is empty, and then copies it into tiles one tile at a time on a single thread.

**Plan:** skip the copies when there is no padding, and pad or crop row by row when there is. Build the selection tiles in parallel directly from the mask, sharing one tile for fully selected tiles. The results stay bit-identical; existing oracle tests and a new one check this.

title: Performance: duplicating a 12 MP layer takes ~500–700 ms (P8/P9, budget 100/20 ms)
author: vangel76
body:
Part of #209 (performance budgets). Scorecard rows **P8** "Duplicate a 12 MP layer (first)" (budget 100 ms) and **P9** "(repeat)" (budget 20 ms) were measured at 508/699 ms and 406/627 ms (p50/p95) in the 2026-10-05 baseline (M4 Pro, load average ~290 during that run).

### Breakdown (`perf_scenarios --only "duplicate 12 MP"`, release, Linux, RTX 5090, upstream/main 5a1f6eef)

| Part | Time |
|---|---|
| `layer.duplicate` itself (`Session::execute`: layer clone, history step, `same_pixels`) | 0.1–0.3 ms |
| Canvas refresh afterwards | everything else |

- The copy is already cheap: `Layer::duplicate` clones the surface's `BTreeMap<TileCoord, Arc<Tile>>`, so the copy shares every tile with its source (no pixel copy), and the history step holds the old document by `Arc`.
- The refresh is the cost: `Session::edit` reports no damage (`last_damage = None`) for any edit that changes pixels, so the canvas recomposites the **whole 20 MP document** (`gpu-full`, 19.96 MP) for a copy that only draws in its own 12 MP. The new layer id also means its tiles are uploaded again (204 tile uploads), but that is a small part.
  - GPU compositor: ~15–35 ms CPU-side per refresh (wgpu pass encoding and driver work) + 1–6 ms GPU wait. P8 p50/p95 34/39 ms, P9 24/28 ms on a quiet machine.
  - CPU compositor (`--cpu`): P8 ~400 ms, P9 ~500 ms.
- Undo of the duplicate (not timed) is also a full recomposite: `step_damage` treats any added non-empty layer as unbounded.

### Proposed fix

Report bounded damage for Duplicate Layer: the walk `step_damage` already does (pair layers by id, compare tiles by pointer), extended so a layer only the new document has contributes its `photocraft_compose::change_bounds` when it is self-contained (not an adjustment / pass-through group holding one, not a new clipping base for clipped layers above it, no video or excluded channels inside). Anything else (canvas size changes from artboard copies, clipping changes, …) still recomposites everything. Results stay …

title: Performance: elliptical (and rectangular) marquee selection on 24 MP is written pixel by pixel
author: vangel76
body:
Part of #211 (performance on large documents).

## Problem

Making a marquee selection on a 24 MP document is slow. Photoshop makes it instantly.

`select.rect` with `ellipse: true` builds the shape one pixel at a time on a single thread: four corner tests plus, on the edge, 16 sub-samples, then `Surface::write_pixel` (a tile lookup and copy-on-write check) for every selected pixel. Fully selected tiles aren't shared either: each one is a separate 64 KB copy.

The `add`, `subtract` and `intersect` modes (rectangle and ellipse) go through a local `combine` in `crates/engine/src/commands.rs`. It reads both selections over the whole canvas into `f32` buffers, maps them and writes the result back. That's 3 × 24 M floats (about 290 MB) for every Shift-drag or Alt-drag.

Rectangle in `replace` mode is already fast: `fill_rect` shares the full tiles.

## Measurements

6000×4000 document, release build, end-to-end `select.rect` timing, best of 5 (`cargo run --release -p photocraft-engine --example bench_marquee`):

| Case | Time |
|---|---|
| rectangle replace 5800×3800 | 15 ms |
| ellipse replace 5800×3800, anti-aliased | 583 ms |
| ellipse replace 5800×3800, no anti-alias | 496 ms |
| ellipse 8000×6000 dragged past the canvas | 900 ms |
| ellipse, feather 20 | 1.05 s |
| rectangle add | 316 ms |
| ellipse add / subtract / intersect | 367 / 425 / 333 ms |

## Proposed fix

- Build the ellipse a row at a time. Each pixel row is a run of fully selected pixels with anti-aliased pixels at each end. Only the edge pixels get the exact per-pixel coverage test, so the bytes stay identical. Tiles are built in parallel, and fully selected tiles share one copy-on-write tile.
- Combine two selections tile by tile in parallel through a 256×256 byte table, with the same per-pixel results. Tiles that come through unchanged stay shared, and there's no full-canvas temporary buffer.

PhotoCraft is AI-positive by design. Every action is a command, and the MCP server can already drive the running app. Teaching takes more than driving. title: Security: RAW lossless-JPEG intermediate allocation misses its documented limit
author: coygeek
body:
PhotoCraft camera raw import has an allocation-limit gap in the lossless-JPEG intermediate decoding path. Static source review indicates that this intermediate does not apply the documented per-buffer decode budget. An untrusted raw file may therefore cause memory use beyond the configured limit.

Component: `photocraft-raw`, RAW lossless-JPEG decoding. Reviewed source: [commit a3d2a6d](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/tree/a3d2a6d486e138c648cd56442c1e4ebddb76287c).

Expected invariant: check each decoded buffer against the configured allocation limit before allocating it, and return a format error when it exceeds the limit. Please apply that invariant to intermediate buffers while preserving valid camera-file layouts.

This report is based on source review only. No runtime validation was performed, and process termination or loss of unsaved work has not been established.

This is a minimal non-exploitable summary under `SECURITY.md`. Please use #913 to establish a private follow-up channel for further technical details.

title: fix(psd): bound parse-time merged-image ZIP validation
author: coygeek
body:
Source review identified inconsistent resource-limit enforcement in PhotoCraft's PSD/PSB merged-image ZIP validation. This can cause excess work during import of untrusted documents.

Expected behavior is that validation respects the existing decoded-data resource budget before unnecessary work, while preserving checksum validation and supported large PSB files. Please reconcile the validation budget with the existing decode limits and retain compatibility checks for valid documents.

Reviewed source: [commit a3d2a6d](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/commit/a3d2a6d486e138c648cd56442c1e4ebddb76287c), affected component [crates/psd/src/compression.rs](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/a3d2a6d486e138c648cd56442c1e4ebddb76287c/crates/psd/src/compression.rs).

This is a source-only review. Runtime impact has not been validated at this revision. No test input or reproduction instructions are included. See [#913](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/issues/913) for the requested private follow-up channel.

title: Security: enforce linked Smart Object file authority consistently
author: coygeek
body:
A source-only review of PhotoCraft at [a3d2a6d](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/commit/a3d2a6d486e138c648cd56442c1e4ebddb76287c) found a remaining authorization gap in linked Smart Object handling in the native engine and PSD export component. Document-provided references can lead to file access without the authority expected by the documented automation workspace policy, which can affect file confidentiality and process availability.

The expected invariant is that opening or processing a document does not independently grant authority to its external references. Explicitly user-selected linked assets should continue to work. Source resolution should consistently enforce the applicable read authority and bounded regular-file handling across editing and exporting.

This assessment comes from source review only. No runtime validation was performed, and broader consequences remain unverified. Please coordinate the detailed report privately through the channel requested in [#913](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/issues/913). This summary contains no reproduction steps or attachments.

title: Performance: brush dab p95 on large 16/32-bit documents over budget (P13 146 ms, P16 161 ms)
author: vangel76
body:
Part of #209 (scorecard rows **P13** and **P16**).

The 2026-10-05 baseline has P13 "Brush dab on a 15000×10000 16-bit document" at p50 6.4 / **p95 146 ms** (budget 80) and P16 "Brush dab on a 32-bit document with 20 layers" at p50 21.5 / **p95 161 ms** (budget 100).

## Breakdown

Measured per dab on upstream/main (`perf_scenarios`, release, Ryzen 7 7800X3D + RTX 5090, under load from other builds), command vs GPU canvas refresh timed separately:

| | command (`paint.stroke`) | GPU refresh |
|---|---|---|
| P13 16-bit | p50 0.4 / p95 0.7 ms | p50 1.1 / p95 5 ms |
| P16 32-bit | p50 0.4 / p95 0.8 ms | p50 2.6–6 / p95 6–20 ms |

The command is cheap. The time goes to the GPU refresh, and the slow dabs are the ones that **grow the painted layer's tile bounds**. `photocraft_gpu::Compositor::sync` keys a resident layer page by its region (the layer's tile bounds inside the page cell). A dab on a part of the layer that had no tiles changes that region. The page is then treated as stale: a new texture is created and **every stored tile of the layer in that cell is converted and uploaded again**, not just the tiles the dab touched. With per-dab logging, the refresh cost grows with the number of tiles re-uploaded (1 tile ≈ 3 ms, 8 tiles ≈ 14–20 ms on the 32-bit document). In the scenario the dabs walk diagonally across a mostly empty layer, so almost every timed dab grows the bounds. That's why P16's p50 is 3× P13's.

32-bit tiles also take the slow general conversion path: decode into a float buffer, then `to_rgba` and `f32_to_f16` per pixel. 16-bit RGB/gray tiles have a table fast path. In the profile, `to_rgba` + `Surface::read_region` were about 60 % of CPU samples during the 32-bit dab loop.

Note on the p95 values: with n = 15, p95 is the max sample. The baseline was recorded at load average 225–290 on a 14-core machine, so one descheduled dab can set the row. P13 measures p95 ≈ 5 ms here.

## Plan

- When only a resident page's region changes, keep its texels: copy t…

title: Performance: pasting a 12 MP layer recomposites the whole document (P10/P11)
author: vangel76
body:
Part of #209 (performance budgets). Scorecard rows **P10** "Paste a 12 MP layer (first)" (budget 100 ms) and **P11** "(repeat)" (budget 20 ms) were measured at 1232/3136 ms and 445/1174 ms (p50/p95) in the 2026-10-05 baseline (M4 Pro, heavily loaded).

### What happens

`edit.paste` (and Paste in Place, which shares it) inserts the pasted layer through `Session::edit`, which reports no damage for an edit that changes pixels (`last_damage = None`). So the canvas recomposites the **whole 20 MP document** after every paste, although the pasted layer only draws in its own 12 MP. The paste command itself is cheap (0.3–5 ms: the clipboard surface shares its tiles, the history step holds the old document by `Arc`).

Measured on `perf_scenarios --only "paste 12"` (release, Linux, RTX 5090, machine under load):

| Row | GPU p50 / p95 | CPU compositor p50 / p95 |
|---|---|---|
| P10 paste (first) | 59 / 74 ms | 1249 / 1467 ms |
| P11 paste (repeat) | 52 / 69 ms | 1268 / 1487 ms |

Paste Into / Paste Outside go through `edit.paste` and then add the layer mask in further coalesced steps, which also report no damage.

### Proposed fix

Same as Duplicate Layer in #2883 / #2884: capture the document before the paste and report the damage with `note_insert` (the `step_damage` walk extended to self-contained added layers), so only the pasted layer's bounds are recomposited. Anything not self-contained (a new clipping base, video, excluded channels) still recomposites everything. Results stay identical.

title: [Feature Request] AppImage desktop shortcut check
author: Ferase
body:
## Main Issue

The AppImage automatically creates a desktop shortcut every time it is run, regardless of if it exists or not. While a very helpful feature especially for when new AppImages of PhotoCraft are released, there is a glaring problem with this approach.

Because it always creates a new shortcut no matter if it did previously or not, it will remove any environment variables, launch options, or other modifications the user applies to this shortcut. For example, I use a Wayland graphics backend, thus I need to pass `WAYLAND_DISPLAY=` to the program to allow drag-and-drop to work. When doing this and running the program via that shortcut, drag-and-drop will be enabled, but only for that session. Now that it was started, it will write a new shortcut over the original one I just altered, essentially undoing my change.

I'll also note that using AppImage managers like AppManager does not help. I know I could try other options, such as opting out of new `.desktop` file writes via `PHOTOCRAFT_NO_DESKTOP_INTEGRATION=1`, but given not all users utilize zsync updates and the filenames of AppImages are naturally different because of versioning, the functionality of a shortcut being created on startup is a good and helpful feature. I just think more overhead is required.

Maybe a check for this shortcut should be done first before writing a new one. For new versions, perhaps it can ask the user once if they want to update their shortcut. There are a few different approaches that could work here, but I feel that some action should be taken given that losing custom settings for a shortcut can be frustrating and not all users would want to disable the shortcut writing and updating altogether.

title: Security: RAW lossless-JPEG intermediate sample buffer is not charged against max_alloc
author: coygeek
body:
# RAW lossless-JPEG intermediate sample buffer is not charged against `max_alloc`

## Summary

In the shipped camera-raw import path, the assembled image plane is checked against the codec `Limits`, but the separately sized lossless-JPEG intermediate sample buffer is not. A raw file can therefore drive a single decode buffer past the documented per-buffer `max_alloc` budget before any `Limits` error is returned. This is a source-only assessment at the pinned revision below; no runtime measurement was performed.

- Component: `photocraft-raw`, DNG and TIFF/EP lossless-JPEG (`Compression::LosslessJpeg`) decoding, reached from `crates/io`'s raw import.
- Reviewed revision: [`1a59f6f6a336b17ae7016558ffc107c1b27df4fb`](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/tree/1a59f6f6a336b17ae7016558ffc107c1b27df4fb).
- Historical attribution: first identified from source review at `d7df9d8`; the affected code is unchanged at the reviewed revision.

## Expected invariant

`photocraft-raw` documents that sizes are checked against `Limits` before allocating and defines `max_alloc` as the maximum bytes of one buffer:

title: fix(psd): bound parse-time merged-image ZIP validation by MAX_DECODED_BYTES
author: coygeek
body:
# PSD/PSB parse-time merged-image ZIP validation is not bounded by `MAX_DECODED_BYTES`

## Summary

`photocraft-psd` implements a decoded-size budget, `MAX_DECODED_BYTES`, and applies it on the decode path. The parse-time validator for the merged-image ZIP/ZIPPrediction stream uses the uncapped declared total as its only work bound instead, so it can inflate far past the budget before reporting an error. An untrusted PSD/PSB can therefore cause parse-time decompression work proportional to the file size times the zlib expansion ratio at open time. This is a source-only assessment at the pinned revision below; no runtime measurement was performed here.

- Component: `photocraft-psd`, merged-image ZIP validation (`validate_planes`), reached from `PsdFile::from_bytes`.

author: coygeek
body:
# Linked Smart Object sources are read with ambient authority

## Summary

A document can carry a linked Smart Object whose source path is an arbitrary host path. When the engine re-renders or exports that layer, it resolves the path through the general file reader with ambient authority, outside the capability-scoped read path the automation workspace uses. A document received from elsewhere can therefore cause a read of a file the user never chose, and the read is neither confined to the document's folder nor restricted to regular files. title: [Feature Request] Copy & paste layer masks (within and between documents)
author: KW1-greysky
body:
**Summary**
I’d like better ways to reuse layer masks:

Alt + drag a mask thumbnail onto another layer to copy it (like Photoshop).
Copy & paste masks via menu/shortcut, so masks can also be transferred between documents.

**Current behavior**
Within a document, I can work around this by putting layers into a group and masking the group. That doesn’t help when only some layers need the mask, and there’s no way to move a mask to another document at all, so I have to recreate it by hand.

**Desired behavior**

Alt + drag (within a document)

Alt (Option on Mac) + drag a mask thumbnail onto another layer → mask is copied, original stays.
Drag without Alt → mask is moved (optional, matches Photoshop).

Copy & paste (within and across documents)

Select a mask → Copy Mask (e.g. via right-click on the mask thumbnail or Edit menu).
Select a layer, in the same or another document → Paste Mask.
If the documents have different dimensions, the mask should be pasted centered (or with an option to scale it to the canvas).

For both

If the target layer already has a mask, ask whether to replace it.

Why this matters
Applying the same mask to several layers or reusing a selection across related images (e.g. a series shot from the same angle, or exposure blends) is a very common workflow. Group masks only cover part of this, and transferring masks between documents is currently not possible as far as i tested it. Both features would save a lot of repetitive work.

Thanks for considering it!

# Windows release signing client is downloaded unpinned and unverified

## Summary

The Windows release signing script downloads `Microsoft.Trusted.Signing.Client` from an unversioned NuGet URL and loads it without any version, digest or package-signature check. This is a release-tool provenance hardening gap: the client used to produce release signatures is not bound to an approved identity or integrity value. title: PSD: public psd_to_document and layered TIFF skip the group-depth preflight
author: coygeek
body:
# PSD: public `psd_to_document` and layered TIFF skip the group-depth preflight (defense-in-depth)

## Summary

The normal PSD/PSB file-open path rejects layer-group nesting deeper than `MAX_GROUP_DEPTH` before conversion. The public converter `psd_to_document` and its layered-TIFF caller do not run that preflight: they build the full `LayerNode` tree from the file's layer records and only then cap document conversion. This report asks for a consistent preflight as defense-in-depth. It is a hardening proposal, not a confirmed vulnerability: the parser bounds layer records to 32767, so the deepest possible tree is ~16383 levels, and a focused stack test shows recursive `Drop` at that depth completes within a 2 MiB thread stack. Source-only review at the pinned revision below.

- Component: `crates/io/src/psd_import.rs` (`psd_to_document`), `crates/io/src/tiff_layers.rs` (`import_layered`), `crates/io/src/flat.rs` (layered TIFF entry).

title: AI Denoise (Camera Raw › Detail) on a local model
author: diegochagas
body:
## What

Noise is the cleanup every photo editor is asked for first, and Photoshop does it with a model: **Camera Raw › AI Denoise** (and *Enhance*). JPEG Artifacts Removal is #6065 (split out at ticket-craft's request). PhotoCraft has **Filter › Noise › Reduce Noise** (`crates/engine/src/filters_ext.rs`: strength, preserve details, reduce colour noise, sharpen details), a classical filter that blurs texture along with the noise at high strength.

`docs/gaps.md` G15 lists Neural Filters as missing; #2313 names denoising among the first uses of downloadable models.

## Proposed

- **Filter › Noise › AI Denoise…** (Camera Raw's name; also reachable from the Camera Raw Filter's Detail panel): one *Amount* slider, output to the current layer or a new one. Runs on the local model provider (shared with #2787 / #2788 / #2942 / #6065) with an open restoration model: SCUNet or NAFNet-style denoisers run as ComfyUI nodes and take a `sigma`/strength parameter; a diffusion image-edit model is not needed.
- Tiles large images with overlap, respects the selection, converts at the provider boundary (8-bit sRGB tiles in, the document's depth and profile out) and never touches a pixel outside the selection.
- Without a backend it falls back to Reduce Noise with a note. Headless under the automation policy.
- Tests: a fake provider; tiles and seams; selection respected; 8/16/32-bit; `panic_hunt`. For an honest quality check, a synthetic noisy image (known clean source + Gaussian noise) and the PSNR gain over Reduce Noise, measured and recorded.

Prior art: GIMP-ML's denoiser and the OpenVINO plug-ins' super-resolution/denoise are what GIMP users install for this. I'd like to implement this here once the provider seam exists.

body:
## What

**Filter › Neural Filters › Style Transfer** applies the look of a reference image (brush strokes, palette, texture) to the photo, with *Strength*, *Style Opacity*, *Brightness*, *Saturation*, *Preserve Color* and *Focus Subject*. PhotoCraft has no Neural Filters entry at all (`crates/ui-egui/src/menu_catalog.rs` lists none, see #2787), and nothing like style transfer among its filters; Filter Gallery's Artistic looks are hand-written approximations of a few fixed styles.

## Proposed

- `filter.neuralFilters.styleTransfer` with Photoshop's controls: a reference image (a file, or another open document) plus a few bundled public-domain presets, *Strength* (how far the result goes from the photo; implemented as a blend with the source so it re-blends without re-running the model), *Preserve Color* (take the result's luminance only, keep the photo's chroma), output to a new layer by default.
- Runs on the local model provider (shared with #2787 / #2788): a style-transfer graph in ComfyUI (IP-Adapter style reference with an open image-edit model, or a classical neural style transfer node) with the reference image uploaded alongside the photo; nothing leaves the machine.
- *Focus Subject* reuses the segmentation of #2788 to apply the style to the background only.
- Without a backend the item reports it; headless under the automation policy. Tests: a fake provider, the strength re-blend, Preserve Color, selection, `panic_hunt`.

Prior art: GIMP-ML ships a style-transfer model; it is among the AI features GIMP users add through plug-ins. Lower priority than the restoration, segmentation, upscale and denoise issues, filed so the Neural Filters set is complete.

title: image.canvasSize: a misspelled anchor lands between two anchors instead of the documented default
author: Erica4fr
body:
## Summary

`image.canvasSize` with an `anchor` outside its documented list does not fall back to the
documented default: `anchor_factors` decides each axis separately, with different rules, so a
misspelling can produce an anchor that is not one of the nine. `"topleft"` anchors top-centre and
`"TopLeft"` anchors left-centre, both reported as `ok`.

## Problem to solve

The command documents `"anchor":"topLeft|top|topRight|left|center|right|bottomLeft|bottom|bottomRight"="center"`.
Measured on a 0.6.0 dev build at ec03c602 (release build, Arch Linux), through
`photocraft-cli serve`, resizing a 64×48 document to 100×80 and reading the `offset` the command
returns, one fresh document per call:

```text
anchor         offset     anchors at
"topLeft"      [0, 0]     top-left        (correct)
"topleft"      [18, 0]    top-CENTRE      not one of the nine
"TopLeft"      [0, 16]    left-centre     silently a different anchor
"TOPLEFT"      [18, 16]   centre          the default
"bottomleft"   [18, 32]   bottom-CENTRE   not one of the nine
"bottomright"  [18, 32]   bottom-CENTRE   not one of the nine
"bottomRight"  [36, 32]   bottom-right    (correct)
"middle"       [18, 16]   centre          the default
"NOPE"         [18, 16]   centre          the default
```

Three spellings of the same intent give three different results, and two of them are anchors the
command does not offer. A caller that writes `"topleft"` gets a canvas anchored somewhere that is
neither what it asked for nor the documented default, with no error.

The cause is in `anchor_factors` (`crates/engine/src/image_cmds.rs`), which resolves the two axes
independently and with different matching rules:

```rust
let x = if a.contains("Left") || a == "left" { 0.0 }
        else if a.contains("Right") || a == "right" { 1.0 }
        else { 0.5 };
let y = if a.starts_with("top") { 0.0 }
        else if a.starts_with("bottom") { 1.0 }
        else { 0.5 };
```

title: Select and Mask: Refine Edge Brush (TOOL-214-1)
author: vangel76
body:
Part of #214 (scorecard TOOL-214-1, docs/gaps.md G7).

Select and Mask (`select.refineEdge`) has Radius / Smart Radius, Smooth, Feather, Contrast, Shift Edge, Decontaminate Colors and the Output To choices, and (with #2970) its view modes, but no **Refine Edge Brush**. In Photoshop that tool (R in the Select and Mask workspace) paints the areas where edge refinement happens: brushing over hair or fur adds them to the refinement border, so fine detail beyond the radius band is picked up; Alt-painting removes the refinement there and restores the original edge.

Proposal:
- Engine: a `refineStrokes` param on `select.refineEdge`: `[{"points":[[x,y],…],"size":px,"mode":"add|subtract"}]`, applied in order. Added areas become unknown for the matting (guided filter) and take its result; subtracted areas keep the original edge. Agent-drivable and recordable like every other param; bad strokes are rejected, never a panic.
- UI: a Refine Edge Brush toggle (R) with Size in the Select and Mask dialog; with it on, dragging on the canvas paints strokes (Alt subtracts), shown live in the current view; Show Edge includes the painted area.

title: Type menu: Anti-Alias › None is never checked, and the checks ignore the edited type layer
author: vangel76
body:
In Photoshop, Type › Anti-Alias lists **None, Sharp, Crisp, Strong, Smooth**, then Windows LCD and Windows, and both Type › Anti-Alias and Type › Orientation check the current value of the type layer you're working on.

On `main` (d9ae73e9):

1. **Anti-Alias › None is never checked and sits last.** `menu_catalog.rs` has no entry for `type.antiAlias.none`, so the item comes from the engine's command list. It's added at the end of the Type menu, so it appears below Windows in the submenu instead of first. Engine-only items are also built with `checked: None`, so a layer set to None shows no checkmark anywhere in the submenu.
2. **The checks follow only the active layer.** `view_cmds::type_checked` reads `active_layer`, while the options bar, Properties and the Type menu commands themselves act on the layer being edited, or else on a selected type layer (`type_tool::target`). If the active layer isn't a type layer (for example, a type layer and a pixel layer are selected), the menu shows no check while the options bar shows the type layer's value.
3. **Without a type layer, the items stop being check items** (`None` rather than `Some(false)`). That changes the item kind, so the native (macOS) menu has to be rebuilt (see the note in `menus::checked`).

Expected: None is first in Anti-Alias, and the current anti-aliasing and orientation of the layer the Type controls show are checked in both the in-window menu bar and the native menu.

title: Type: variable font axis sliders; optical size follows the type size (TYPE-218-4)

title: Tests: panic_hunt reports type.create as hung when the first system font scan takes over 4 s
author: vangel76
body:
`cargo test -p photocraft-engine --test panic_hunt -- --ignored` fails now and then on a busy machine with `1 commands panicked or hung`, then passes on a rerun.

**Cause.** The test gives each command 4 s of wall-clock time on a fresh 24×16 document. The first command that lays out text, `type.create` with `{}`, also starts the process-wide text engine (`photocraft_text::shared()`). That scans every system font directory once (about 1,000 font files on the machine where this was measured). With a load average of about 35 on 16 cores, that first call took **5.2 s** in one run and **3.5 s** in another. Every other command, and `type.create` with the other three param sets, stayed under 0.3 s. So the test reports a one-time startup cost as a hang of `type.create`, whenever the font scan happens to go over 4 s.

Evidence: 6 plain runs passed in 25–40 s each. Two instrumented runs logged each `execute` that took longer than 300 ms. The only ones were `type.create <- {}`, at 5177 ms and 3489 ms.

**Fix.** A real hang is reproducible, and one-time lazy setup is not. So a command that times out is run once more on a fresh session, and it counts as hung only if the second run also times out. The failure message already names the command and params; it now also says that both runs timed out. The 4 s deadline stays the same: it is still more than 10 times what any command needs on a loaded machine.

title: Select and Mask: Output To New Document (TOOL-214-1)
author: vangel76
body:
Part of #214 (scorecard row TOOL-214-1).

Photoshop's Select and Mask › Output Settings › Output To offers six targets: Selection, Layer Mask, New Layer, New Layer with Layer Mask, **New Document** and **New Document with Layer Mask**. `select.refineEdge` (crates/engine/src/smartselect_cmds.rs) supports the first four. It rejects anything else with "output must be selection|layerMask|newLayer|newLayerWithMask".

**Expected**
- `output: "newDocument"` opens a new document with the same size, mode, depth, resolution and ICC profile as the source. It holds one layer: the active layer's pixels, cut out by the refined selection (decontaminated when Decontaminate Colors is on).
- `output: "newDocumentWithMask"` does the same, but keeps the full pixels and puts the refined matte on that layer as a layer mask.
- The source document stays as it was: no history step, its layers stay visible and its selection is kept. The new document becomes the active document.
- Both outputs appear in the Select and Mask dialog's Output choice and are translated in every UI catalog.

title: feat(doc): keep video layer frames in .pcraft
author: Sir-Starch
body:
A video layer's frame stack lives in memory only (`VideoData` in `crates/doc/src/video.rs`: "`.pcraft` persistence of the stack is a follow-up"). A saved document keeps the current frame as the layer's raster content, so reopening it loses the other frames. This shows up as soon as footage is loaded, for example an animated GIF (#2999, #572).

Proposed: store the frames and the source in the `.pcraft` container, with the same limits and malformed-input tests as the other layer data, and round-trip tests.

I'm planning to work on this after #2999 is merged.

title: feat(doc): per-frame delays for video layers and animated GIF
author: Sir-Starch
body:
The timeline has one frame rate (`Timeline.fps`), but a GIF stores a delay per frame. #2999 loads every GIF frame into a video layer and picks the most common delay as the rate, so a GIF with varied delays plays at the wrong speed, and Render Video to GIF writes one delay for all frames.

Needs a per-frame duration in the frame model (`VideoData` / `Timeline`) and its use in playback and in the GIF writer. This changes the timeline model, so I'd like a maintainer's opinion on the shape before writing it. Related: #572.

title: feat(export): play animations in the Save for Web preview
author: Sir-Starch
body:
Save for Web has no playback of an animated GIF: #572 asks for "playback in main window and the save for web legacy panel". With #2999 a GIF can be loaded into a video layer and the encoder already writes animated GIFs (`encode_gif_animated`), but the Save for Web preview shows a still frame.

Proposed: play the document's timeline in the preview at the timeline rate, with a play/pause control. Depends on #2999; per-frame delays would be a separate issue.

title: Type: the system font scan runs on the UI thread (all platforms)
author: vangel76
body:
## What happens

The first time the Type tool is chosen, the app freezes while all installed fonts are scanned. Nothing starts that scan earlier, and it runs on the UI thread on every platform. With many fonts installed the freeze is long: #2518 reports more than 60 seconds on macOS.

## Code path

- `photocraft_text::shared()` (`crates/text/src/lib.rs`) is a `OnceLock`. Its first call builds `TextEngine::with_system_fonts()`, which scans every system font directory.
- Choosing the Type tool draws its options bar. `type_tool::options_bar` calls `font_picker`, which evaluates `&families()` on every frame. `families()` calls `photocraft_text::shared()`, so the full scan runs inside the first frame that shows the Type tool.
- The Character panel (`type_sections` → `font_picker`/`styles`) and the Glyphs panel and Character/Paragraph Styles family menus (`type_panels_ui.rs`: `family_picker`, `glyphs_panel`) reach `shared()` the same way.
- Engine type commands (`type.create` and the others) also call `shared()`. They run on a user action, not every frame.

## Relation to #2518 / #2644

#2644 makes macOS discovery itself faster by switching to CoreText. This issue is complementary and covers all platforms: it is about *where* the scan runs, not *how* fonts are discovered. Linux and Windows directory scans with large font folders hit the same first-frame stall, and even a fast CoreText pass still runs inside a UI frame.

## Proposed fix

- Start the scan on a background thread at app startup (native only; the web build has no system fonts and no threads).
- Add a non-blocking accessor (`photocraft_text::try_shared()`).
- While the scan runs, the per-frame font menus (options bar, Character, Glyphs, Character/Paragraph Styles) show a disabled "Loading fonts…" box instead of blocking.
- Engine commands that need fonts keep waiting for the scan, since they run on a user action.

Refs #2518, complements #2644.

title: Release dmg: bundled .app fails `codesign --verify --deep --strict` due to empty `com.apple.FinderInfo` xattrs
author: pdaw-cowork
body:
**Environment**
- PhotoCraft v0.5.0 universal dmg, macOS Apple Silicon
- The same pattern was observed in the universal dmgs of the other craft apps (FilmCraft, VectorCraft, LightCraft, EffectCraft, DesignCraft, PdfCraft).

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Mount the universal `.dmg` and copy the `.app` out (or check the mounted app).
2. `codesign --verify --deep --strict --verbose=2 PhotoCraft.app`
3. For comparison: `spctl --assess --type execute -vv PhotoCraft.app` and `xcrun stapler validate PhotoCraft.app`.

**Expected**
`codesign --verify --deep --strict` passes, like `spctl` and `stapler`.

**Actual**
Strict verification fails with `resource fork, Finder information, or similar detritus not allowed`. `spctl` (Notarized Developer ID) and `stapler validate` both pass. Empty `com.apple.FinderInfo` attributes are present on resource files inside the bundle (e.g. the `.icns` and the license `.txt`).

**Workaround confirmed**
On a copy of the app, removing only `com.apple.FinderInfo` (`xattr -d com.apple.FinderInfo <file>` on the affected files) makes `--strict` pass; the signature stays valid.

**Suggested fix**
Strip extended attributes in the packaging step before signing (`xattr -cr "$APP"`, or `ditto --norsrc --noextattr`), and add `codesign --verify --deep --strict` as a CI check on the final dmg contents.

**Impact**
Low for Gatekeeper, but strict verification tools and some MDM/integrity checks flag the bundle.

title: Actions: commands that run other commands record them twice
author: vangel76
body:
## What happens

A command that runs other commands through `Session::execute` journals those inner calls as well as its own entry. Action recording copies every replayable journal entry, so the recorded action contains the outer command **and** its inner steps, and playback applies them twice.

Example: Image › Analysis › Straighten Layer on the Background runs `image.rotation.arbitrary` and `image.crop` itself.

1. `actions.record` `{"name": "Level"}`
2. `image.analysis.rulerTool` `{"start": [10, 30], "end": [70, 25]}`
3. `image.analysis.straightenLayer` `{}`
4. `actions.stop`

Recorded steps on `main`:

```
["image.analysis.rulerTool", "image.rotation.arbitrary", "image.crop", "image.analysis.straightenLayer"]
```

Playing the action on a fresh copy of the starting document runs 4 steps: it rotates and crops, then Straighten (the ruler is still there) rotates and crops a second time. The result differs from the direct run.

The same applies to every journaled command that calls `s.execute` (for example Transform Again on a copy records `layer.duplicate` + `edit.transform` + the wrapper; `file.scripts.browse`, `file.automate.batch` and droplets record each inner step plus the call). Edit › Transform › Again was fixed on its own in #1440. #3039 trims the journal by hand for `path.stroke`.

## Expected

As in Photoshop, the action records the command the user ran, once. Playback gives the same document as the direct run.

## Cause

`Session::dispatch` → `after_command` pushes every successful journaled command, nested or not, and nested commands finish (and journal) before the outer one.

title: Artboards: a board moved left of or above the canvas origin ends up off-canvas
author: vangel76
body:
**What happens**

Moving an artboard left of or above the canvas origin leaves it partly (or fully) off-canvas. This happens with a Move tool drag left/up past the origin, or with `layer.artboard.set` and a negative `x`/`y`. A board moved right or down grows the canvas (#1531, #2389), but the canvas never grows left or up.

**Steps**

```
file.new {"width": 100, "height": 80}
layer.new.artboard {"rect": [10, 10, 40, 40]}
layer.translate {"dx": -60, "dy": -30}
```

The board is at (-50, -20)…(-10, 20) and the canvas is still 100×80 at the origin, so the part left of and above the origin is cut off.

**Expected (Photoshop)**

An artboard document grows in every direction. Everything (boards, their contents, guides) shifts right/down by the overhang, and the canvas grows to show the board. All of this happens in the move's single undo step.

**Cause**

`artboard_cmds::fit_canvas` only grows the canvas to `max(x1)`/`max(y1)` of the boards. It never shifts the document for a negative `x0`/`y0`.

title: Content-Aware Move: Transform On Drop (TOOL-213-4)
author: vangel76
body:
Scorecard row **TOOL-213-4** (Content-Aware Move tool) is `partial`. Missing piece: **Transform On Drop**.

In Photoshop the Content-Aware Move tool has a **Transform On Drop** checkbox in the options bar. When it is on, dropping the moved patch shows a transform box around it; you can scale and rotate the patch, and the content-aware blend is computed with the transformed patch when you commit (Enter / ✓). Esc cancels the whole move.

Today `paint.contentAwareMove` only takes a translation (dx/dy) and the tool commits immediately on drop.

Plan:
- Engine: `paint.contentAwareMove` gains optional transform params (scale/rotation of the patch around its centre), validated (finite, sane ranges, `Err` instead of panic), so agents and recorded actions can drive it.
- UI: a "Transform On Drop" checkbox in the options bar (remembered like other tool options); after the drop a transform box (scale/rotate handles) appears; Enter commits, Esc cancels; one undo step.

Part of #213.

title: Curves: pencil mode (draw the curve) and Smooth (UI-217-15)
author: vangel76
body:
Scorecard row UI-217-15 (`scorecard/ui.toml`): "Curves: smoothing / pencil mode, black/grey/white eyedroppers, tooltips" is partial. The black/gray/white point eyedroppers landed in #873; what's missing:

- **Pencil mode**: Photoshop's Curves dialog and Properties panel can switch from point editing to drawing the curve freehand ("Draw to modify the curve"). The result is an arbitrary 256-entry map per channel, not a point curve.
- **Smooth**: in pencil mode, the Smooth button smooths the drawn map (each click smooths more).
- **Edit points**: switching back converts the drawn map into a point curve.
- **Tooltips** on the mode buttons and Smooth.
- **PSD**: the `curv` block's first byte is the map flag (psd-tools reads it as `is_map`; a map stores 256 bytes per channel instead of a point list). `crates/io/src/adjust_map.rs` treats that byte as padding, so a pencil-drawn Curves layer from Photoshop is misread (the map bytes are parsed as point counts), and we can't write one.

Plan: a `pencil` flag on `Adjustment::Curves` (serde default), maps stored as 256 points evaluated piecewise-linearly, `image.adjustments.curves` / adjustment-layer params `pencil` + 256-value channel arrays + `smooth`, PSD read/write of the map form, and the editor UI.

title: Actions: recording Last Filter records the wrapper, which fails or applies another filter on playback
author: vangel76
body:
## What happens

Recording an action while pressing Filter › Last Filter (⌥⌘F) records the wrapper step `filter.lastFilter {}`, not the filter it applied. Playback then depends on the playing session's journal:

- In a new session, or after a restart, the step fails: `command filter.lastFilter is not available right now: no filter applied yet`.
- In a session where another filter ran since, the step applies *that* filter instead of the recorded one.

Reproduce (engine):

```
file.new {width:16,height:16}
filter.other.offset {horizontal:3}
actions.record {name:"F"}
filter.lastFilter {}
actions.stop
actions.get {action:"F"}      → steps [["filter.lastFilter",{}]]
# in a new session with the action loaded:
actions.play {action:"F"}     → failed: "no filter applied yet"
```

## Expected

The action records the filter that ran, with its settings (Offset, horizontal 3), the way Photoshop records the filter event. Edit › Transform › Again already does this: it records the concrete `edit.transform` (#1440).

## Cause

`filter.lastFilter` is a journaled, replayable command whose `run` looks up the last filter in the session journal and calls `run_filter` directly. The concrete filter is never journaled.

title: fix(type): text replacement changes an All-locked type layer
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

Replacing a type layer's text through `type.edit` succeeds after All lock has been enabled. Both tested builds change the original text, so this lock does not prevent the demonstrated content edit. Undo restores the original text in the tested case.

## Steps to reproduce

Use either CLI build listed under Runtime or environment, with Arial available. This executed command creates a synthetic 128 by 128 transparent document and uses the newly created type layer as the active layer:

```sh
photocraft-cli run --new '{"width":128,"height":128,"background":"transparent"}' --cmd type.create --params '{"text":"a","x":20,"y":20,"size":12,"font":"Arial"}' --cmd type.info --params '{}' --cmd layer.setProps --params '{"locked":true}' --cmd type.edit --params '{"text":"b"}' --cmd type.info --params '{}'
```

For the unlocked control, omit the `layer.setProps` command. For the unlock-before-edit control, insert `--cmd layer.setProps --params '{"locked":false}'` immediately before `type.edit`. Both controls were executed on both builds and successfully replaced the text with `b`.

## Expected behavior

All lock must prevent changes to the type layer's text. The locked replacement must fail and leave the original text `a` unchanged. The same replacement must remain available when the layer is unlocked.

Both tested builds exit 0 with empty standard error. The first `type.info` returns text `a`; `type.edit` succeeds and the second `type.info` returns text `b` on the same layer. Setting the lock returns success before the replacement. The locked and unlocked cases therefore permit the same content change.

title: Content-Aware Scale: transform box with live preview (TOOL-214-7)
author: vangel76
body:
Scorecard row TOOL-214-7 (`scorecard/tools.toml`, part of #214) is `partial`: Edit › Content-Aware Scale (`edit.contentAwareScale`) opens a parameter dialog.

Photoshop has no dialog: Content-Aware Scale puts a transform box (like Free Transform) on the layer or selection. The options bar has the reference point X/Y, W/H, Amount, Protect (an alpha channel) and Protect Skin Tones. Dragging a handle shows a live preview, Enter commits and Esc cancels. The box only scales and moves: no rotate, skew or distort.

Plan:
- Edit › Content-Aware Scale from the menu opens a scale-only Free Transform box over the layer content (or the selection).
- The options bar shows Amount, Protect and Protect Skin Tones next to X/Y and W/H.
- The preview runs the same seam carving on a reduced copy in the background, and a new drag cancels the stale run.
- Enter runs `edit.contentAwareScale` with the box's size and position as one history step. The command gains optional `x`/`y` params for where the result goes.
- With params, the command still runs directly (actions, CLI, MCP).

title: Numeric fields: arithmetic and units, scrubby labels, double-click reset (UI-217-13)
author: vangel76
body:
Scorecard row UI-217-13 (scorecard/ui.toml, part of #217) is partial. On main, value fields already evaluate arithmetic (#726, #2252) and the field itself scrubs, but:

- **Units in expressions:** typing `1in` or `2cm + 10` into a px field (or `10px` into a pt field) is rejected. Photoshop converts a typed unit into the field's unit at the document resolution; `50%` in a percent field is rejected too (`%` is read as modulo).
- **Scrubby labels:** dragging a field's label (options bar `Size:`, `Opacity:`, adjustment slider rows) does nothing; in Photoshop it scrubs the value (Shift ×10, Alt fine) with the scrubby cursor.
- **Double-click reset:** only Color Balance and Camera Raw sliders reset on double-click; the other adjustment sliders and filter dialog sliders have known defaults but ignore it.

Expected: all three in the shared widgets (`widgets::value_field`, `slider_row`), so every field benefits. Bad input (`1/0`, `1e400`, `((((`, unknown units, unicode) is rejected and keeps the old value.

title: Layers panel: Shift+Plus/Minus cycle blend modes; effects dragged onto the Trash are deleted (UI-217-14)
author: vangel76
body:
Scorecard row **UI-217-14** ("Layers panel: wheel steps blend modes, drop on New/Trash duplicates/deletes, checker behind art") is marked `partial`, but on `main` its three listed parts are already there:

- the wheel over the Layers panel's blend-mode dropdown steps the modes (#1961, #1747);
- a layer row dropped on the footer's New Layer / Group / Delete buttons duplicates / groups / deletes it (#965, #736);
- pixel layer thumbnails draw a checkerboard behind the art (`panels.rs`, `widgets::checker`).

Two related Photoshop behaviours are still missing:

1. **⇧+ / ⇧− cycle blend modes.** In Photoshop, Shift+Plus and Shift+Minus step to the next / previous blend mode: the Brush's or Pencil's mode while a painting tool is active, the Gradient's mode with the Gradient tool, and otherwise (Move, the selection tools…) the active layer's mode. Nothing happens on these keys today.
2. **Effects dragged onto the Trash.** Dragging a layer's "Effects" row onto the Layers panel's Delete button clears its layer style, and dragging a single effect row there deletes only that effect. Effect rows can be dragged onto other layers today (#1719), but a drop on the Trash does nothing.

Scope: both of these run through engine commands (`layer.setProps`, `tools.setBrush`, `layer.layerStyle.clear` with an optional `effect` index), so agents can drive and record them. The scorecard row gets updated too.

title: Puppet Warp: mesh follows the object outline (TOOL-214-6)
author: vangel76
body:
Edit › Puppet Warp builds its mesh from square grid cells that touch the layer's opaque pixels (`algo/puppet.rs` `build_mesh`), so the mesh outline is a staircase up to a cell outside the shape, and shapes closer together than about one cell are glued into one mesh: pinning one drags the other.

In Photoshop the mesh follows the layer's outline (grown or shrunk by Expansion), with Density setting the triangle size.

Plan: build the mesh from a signed distance field of the opaque region offset by Expansion; grid vertices near the outline snap onto it and boundary triangles are cut along it (2D isosurface stuffing), so the mesh edge follows the outline and stays conforming. Opaque content is never cut away. Scorecard row TOOL-214-6 (part of #214).

title: Shortcuts: brush size and hardness keys don't work on a German keyboard layout
author: vangel76
body:
On a German keyboard layout the brush keys can't be used the way Photoshop's German keyboard shortcuts work.

**Photoshop (German layout):** `Ö` makes the brush smaller and `#` makes it bigger (the keys US users know as `[` and `]`). ⇧Ö and ⇧# change the hardness.

**PhotoCraft:**
- `Ö` and `#` do nothing. egui has no key for `ö` or `#`, so it reports the physical key (`;` and `\` in US terms), which no shortcut matches. ⇧# types `'` and arrives as the Quote key.
- The only way to reach `[` / `]` is AltGr+8/9 (⌥5/⌥6 on the Mac). On the Mac and on Windows that press carries ⌥ (Ctrl+Alt on Windows), and the shortcut match rejects it, so `tools.decreaseBrushSize` / `increaseBrushSize` and the hardness keys can't be reached at all.

Opacity digits and ⌘+ / ⌘− are fine on a German layout (digits use the physical key, and Ctrl+`+` arrives as `+`).

**Expected:** On a German layout `Ö` / `#` step the brush size and ⇧Ö / ⇧# the hardness, as in Photoshop. Edit › Keyboard Shortcuts overrides still apply.

In PhotoCraft they exist only in the Image › Adjustments › Curves dialog (#873); the Properties editor of a Curves adjustment layer has none, so scorecard row UI-217-15 stays `partial`.

Expected: the three eyedroppers in the Curves Properties editor; with one armed, a click on the image samples the image the layer adjusts and sets that point on the layer's curve as one undoable `layer.setAdjustment` step (recordable and drivable by agents). Esc or picking another tool disarms it.

title: Layers panel: drag a mask onto the Trash asks to apply or delete it
author: vangel76
body:
**Photoshop:** If you drag a layer mask thumbnail onto the Layers panel's Delete (Trash) button, Photoshop asks "Apply mask to layer before removing?" and offers three buttons:
- **Apply** applies the mask to the layer's pixels (Layer › Layer Mask › Apply).
- **Delete** throws the mask away.
- **Cancel** keeps the mask.

**PhotoCraft:** A layer's mask thumbnail can't be dragged on its own. A drag that starts on the mask thumbnail drags the whole layer row, and dropping it on the Trash deletes the **whole layer**, not just its mask.

The engine already has both commands, `layer.layerMask.apply` and `layer.layerMask.delete`.

**Expected:** Dragging the mask thumbnail onto the Trash opens the Apply / Cancel / Delete prompt, and nothing changes until you answer. Clicking the Trash with the mask targeted should stay as it is now (it deletes the mask immediately; see #2197).

title: Levels: black/gray/white point eyedroppers (dialog and Properties)
author: vangel76
body:
Photoshop's Levels has Set Black Point / Set Gray Point / Set White Point eyedroppers, both in the Image › Adjustments › Levels dialog and in a Levels adjustment layer's Properties panel. PhotoCraft's Levels has none in either place; only Curves has them (dialog: #873; Properties: #3110 / #3115).

Expected: the same three pickers for Levels. The black/white pickers set the input black/white level per channel from the sampled colour, and gray neutralises it through per-channel gamma. They should be drivable through an `eyedropper` param on `image.adjustments.levels` / `layer.newAdjustmentLayer.levels` / `layer.setAdjustment`, reusing the Curves sampling (`adjust_params::eyedropper_sample`, which samples below the layer for adjustment layers) and the Properties picker (`layer_picker.rs`).

title: Layers panel: dragging the vector mask thumbnail to the Trash deletes the whole layer

title: Vanishing Point: on-canvas plane editor (Create/Edit Plane, grid, paste on OK) (TOOL-214-14)
author: vangel76
body:
Part of #214 (scorecard row TOOL-214-14: "Vanishing Point window: draw and edit planes, paste, clone in perspective").

**Today:** Filter › Vanishing Point… (`filter.vanishingPoint`, `crates/engine/src/vp_cmds.rs`) does planes, paste onto a plane and perspective cloning, but in the app it only opens the generic parameter dialog: you have to type plane corner coordinates as JSON. Nothing is drawn on the canvas, and a self-intersecting or dented quad is accepted silently.

**Photoshop:** the Vanishing Point window has a Create Plane tool (four clicks define a plane) and an Edit Plane tool (drag corner and edge nodes, the edge nodes extend the plane along its perspective). The plane's grid is drawn at the Grid Size and turns yellow or red when the plane's perspective is doubtful or invalid (blue when valid). A copied image pasted into the window drops onto the plane in perspective.

**This piece:** a dialog-mode plane editor on the canvas:
- Create Plane (C): four clicks; Edit Plane (V): drag corners, drag edge midpoints to extend/shrink the plane in perspective, Delete removes the selected plane.
- The plane grid at a Grid Size field, coloured valid / questionable / invalid.
- With something on the clipboard, OK (↩) pastes it onto the selected plane at a draggable position and width, as one `filter.vanishingPoint` history step (optionally on a new layer). The planes go into the command's params, so actions record them and agents can drive the same thing.
- The engine rejects a non-convex quad with an error instead of warping along it.

Clone stamp, marquee and tear-off (Ctrl-drag an edge) in the window stay for later.

title: Feature request: self-hosted "cloud documents": autosave, version history and hand-off editing on storage you own (local/NAS, Google Drive, OneDrive, S3/R2 via rclone)
author: fernandodilland
body:
## TL;DR
Photoshop's cloud documents give autosave, version history and "invite to edit", but only inside Adobe's cloud. Please add an open equivalent: a central "Save target" where a native `.pcraft` document is autosaved and versioned on storage the user owns, with hand-off editing between people and, later, live co-editing. Opt-in, no vendor server, no telemetry.

## How Photoshop does it
- Cloud documents (.psdc) save automatically as you work and create a new version at each autosave. A Version History panel lets you revert, and documents can be used offline and sync when you reconnect.
- "Invite to edit" is asynchronous: a collaborator can take over only after the active editor exits and saves, so two people never edit at once. Shared documents don't count toward the invitee's storage.
- Adobe has also run a live co-editing beta for Photoshop.

## What PhotoCraft has today (README only)
Native `.pcraft`, PSD/PSB, copy-on-write 256x256 sparse tiles, deterministic replayable brush strokes, recordable Actions, 500+ commands (UI/CLI/control channel/MCP), a web build, and a Docker recipe for self-hosting the web build.

## Proposal
**Phase 0:** autosave + crash recovery (atomic writes, recovery prompt, `file.autoSave`). Large documents must autosave without blocking the GPU compositor.
**Phase 1, Save target:** shared building blocks below, with a **manifest + content-addressed chunk** layout for `.pcraft`: immutable tile/layer chunks plus a small manifest. Autosave uploads only the tiles that changed (copy-on-write already tells us which). The manifest is the "head" pointer, replaced with `If-Match`.
**Phase 2, version history:** each saved manifest is a version; named versions; retention and garbage collection of unreferenced chunks. PSD stays an interchange/export format, not the sync format.
**Phase 3, hand-off editing (Photoshop's "invite to edit" without the cloud):** a lease with TTL and heartbeat; "X is done, take over" notification via the target; conflict…

title: AppImage: Allow direct access to bundled CLI and MCP without extraction
author: newyorkthink
body:
## Problem

PhotoCraft 0.7.0 AppImage already includes `usr/bin/photocraft-cli`, including MCP support, but the AppImage entry point always launches the graphical application.

Running:

```bash
./photocraft-0.7.0-linux-x86_64.AppImage mcp
```

opens the GUI instead of starting the MCP server. The argument is interpreted as a file path.

## Root cause

The current `packaging/linux/AppRun` always executes:

```bash
exec "$APPDIR/usr/bin/photocraft" "$@"
```

There is no supported direct entry point for the bundled `photocraft-cli`.

## Requested fix

Please allow users to launch the bundled CLI and MCP directly through the original AppImage, without:

- Extracting the AppImage
- Manually mounting the AppImage
- Installing a separate DEB or CLI
- Creating additional wrapper scripts

For example, provide a supported CLI selector such as:

```bash
./photocraft-0.7.0-linux-x86_64.AppImage --cli mcp
```

The exact interface is up to the maintainers.

## Expected behavior

1. Normal AppImage execution continues to launch the GUI.
2. A documented CLI option directly launches the bundled `photocraft-cli`.
3. MCP works through stdio for AI agents.
4. All CLI arguments are forwarded correctly.
5. No extraction, persistent installation, or additional dependencies are required.
6. Existing AppImage desktop integration remains unaffected.

The CLI is already bundled and functional. This request concerns exposing it through the AppImage entry point, not implementing a new MCP server.

Related: #2904.

title: Automation: export through the roots — layersToFiles, dataSetsAsFiles and variableDataSets (the other half of #2810)
author: switch87
body:
#2810 asked for two things; PR #3215 does the placing half (`doc.place`). This is the export half, which is still refused **for paths inside the granted roots**, because all three commands take ambient paths:

- `file.export.layersToFiles {dir, format, prefix?, visibleOnly?}` → needs the **write** root
- `file.export.dataSetsAsFiles {dir, format, dataSets?, naming?}` → needs the **write** root
- `file.import.variableDataSets {path, delimiter?}` → needs the **read** root (a CSV)

Today the only workarounds are `image.applyDataSet` + `doc.save` once per data set, and showing one layer at a time and saving once per layer.

## What already exists

Both halves of each counterpart are already in the tree, so this is mostly plumbing:

- **In-memory export:** `file_cmds::save_doc(doc, path, opts)` is `encode(doc, path, opts)` + `write_file(path, bytes)`. An in-memory core (`layers_to_bytes(s, p) -> Vec<(name, bytes)>`, same for data sets) can be shared by the command and the new method, so the two can never drift — the command keeps writing the returned bytes to `dir`.
- **Capability-scoped writes:** `AuthorizedWorkspace::export_sequence(dir)` already returns an `ExportSequence` with `write(name, bytes)`, `commit()` and `cleanup()`, plus `create_new` (no overwrites), single-component names, and cleanup of everything it created when a step fails.
- **Capability-scoped reads:** `AuthorizedWorkspace::read`, which `doc.place` (#2810) just used the same way.

## Proposed methods

Same shape as `doc.place`: the method resolves the path through the root and hands the bytes to an in-memory engine entry point; the ambient command keeps its refusal.

| JSON-RPC | MCP | Params |
|---|---|---|
| `doc.exportLayers` | `doc_export_layers` | `{dir, format?, prefix?, visibleOnly?, index?}` plus the export options `save_doc` already takes → `{files, count}` |
| `doc.exportDataSets` | `doc_export_data_sets` | `{dir, format?, dataSets?, naming?, index?}` → `{files, count}` (colliding filenames…

title: Feature Request: Add Python Scripting API
author: jasperwoodchuck
body:
PhotoCraft already has a CLI, but Python scripting could make complex automation easier without requiring users to write Rust or chain CLI commands manually.

Potential use cases:
- Batch editing and exporting images.
- Automating layer operations, filters, and adjustments.
- Processing multiple documents with custom logic.
- Creating reusable scripts and workflows.
- Integrating PhotoCraft into Python-based image-processing pipelines.

Expose supported editing operations through a Python API that interacts with PhotoCraft's existing engine and command system.

The implementation should include documentation, examples, and clear error handling. A future scripting interface could support both standalone Python scripts and integration with the CLI.

title: Zoom and Hand tools: right-click the canvas for the zoom menu (Zoom In/Out, Fit on Screen, Fill Screen, 100%, 200%, Print Size)
author: LloydNicholson
body:
In Photoshop, right-clicking the canvas with the **Zoom** tool (the magnifying glass) or the **Hand** tool opens a view menu. From it you can zoom to a set level or fit the image to the window without going to the View menu or the options bar.

In PhotoCraft, right-clicking the canvas with either tool does nothing.

### Expected

Right-click inside the image with the Zoom or Hand tool selected opens:

- Zoom In
- Zoom Out
- ---
- Fit on Screen
- Fill Screen
- ---
- 100%
- 200%
- Print Size

Zoom In and Zoom Out zoom around the point you right-clicked, the same way a Zoom tool click does, and they follow Preferences › Tools › Zoom Clicked Point to Center. Rows grey out like their View menu twins (for example, Zoom In at the maximum zoom). Right-clicking the pasteboard (outside the image) still opens the pasteboard colour menu.

### Notes

- Every row except Fill Screen already exists as a View command (`view.zoomIn`, `view.zoomOut`, `view.fitOnScreen`, `view.actualPixels`, `view.twoHundredPercent`, `view.printSize`). Fill Screen is the Hand tool's options-bar button.
- `docs/context-menu-parity.md` lists this as a P1 gap ("Hand, Zoom … No tool menu"). The checklist in #217 includes "Canvas right-click menu (tool-specific, like Photoshop)".
- The order above is a best guess. `docs/context-menu-parity.md` asks for a Photoshop capture before the menu is called 1:1.

title: Feature Request: Add Non-Destructive Boolean Operations for Vector Shapes
author: jasperwoodchuck
body:
Add non-destructive Boolean operations for vector shapes, allowing users to combine shapes without permanently modifying their original geometry.

Supported operations should include:
- **Union** — combine shapes.
- **Subtract** — remove one shape's area from another.
- **Intersect** — keep only overlapping areas.
- **Exclude** — remove overlapping areas from the result.

Unlike destructive Boolean operations, the original shapes should remain editable. Users should be able to move, resize, or replace the source shapes and have the result update automatically.

This would make vector editing more flexible and support workflows such as icon design, complex illustrations, and shape-based artwork.

title: Feature Request: Add Raster-to-Vector Image Tracing
author: jasperwoodchuck
body:
Add an Image Trace feature to convert raster images into editable vector paths.

Users should be able to:
- Trace images into vector shapes.
- Adjust detail, path accuracy, and color count.
- Choose between black-and-white, grayscale, and color tracing.
- Preview the result before applying it.
- Edit the generated paths after tracing.

This would be useful for converting logos, sketches, icons, and illustrations into scalable vector artwork.

The traced output should remain editable within PhotoCraft's existing vector workflow.

title: Feature Request: Add Variable-Width Vector Strokes
author: jasperwoodchuck
body:
Add support for variable-width strokes so users can adjust the thickness of a vector path at different points along its length.

Users should be able to:
- Add and adjust width points along a path.
- Control stroke thickness and transitions between points.
- Create tapered ends for calligraphy, lettering, and illustrations.
- Edit the width profile after drawing.

The result should remain an editable vector path rather than being converted into a raster image. This would make PhotoCraft more useful for vector illustration and expressive linework.

title: Feature Request: Show Live Preview When Docking Panels
author: jasperwoodchuck
body:
When dragging a panel to a new docking position, PhotoCraft shows a blue outline indicating where the panel will be placed instead of displaying a live preview of the layout change.

It would be helpful to show the panel in its target position while dragging, so users can see how the layout will look before releasing it.

**Expected behavior**
- Display a live preview of the panel in the target position.
- Update the surrounding layout as the panel is dragged.
- Keep the existing docking indicator as a fallback if live previews are not feasible.

title: Feature Request: Add Options to Hide or Expand Scrollbars
author: jasperwoodchuck
body:
Add settings to control scrollbar visibility and behavior across the application.

Users should be able to choose between:
- **Always visible** — keep scrollbars expanded at all times.
- **Auto-hide** — show scrollbars only when needed.
- **Hidden** — hide scrollbars entirely.

These options would let users customize the interface to their preference, especially when working with panels where scrollbars take up valuable space.

title: Timeline: implement Photoshop-style frame-animation mode
author: theriseandfallofitall
body:
Verified against the current Timeline implementation.

The Timeline panel currently provides a document-level FPS/duration playhead with play/pause, previous/next frame, and scrubbing. It does not provide Photoshop frame-animation mode.

Missing frame-animation behaviour:
- Make Frames From Layers and a frame strip
- per-frame duration/delay and visibility state
- select, duplicate, delete, reorder, copy/paste, and reverse frames
- Tween frames, loop count, and onion-skin controls

`layer.new.frameFromLayers` is a masked layout-frame command, not timeline frame animation. The data model contains one global timeline rather than a collection of animation frames, so this requires document/engine support rather than only UI wiring.

Acceptance criteria:
- a document can enter frame-animation mode and create frames from layers;
- each frame persists its delay and layer visibility state;
- playback respects per-frame delays and loop settings;
- Tween produces interpolated frames with undo/redo;
- the UI and automation can drive the feature.

title: Dust & Scratches: avoid pixelated live preview on large documents
author: theriseandfallofitall
body:
Verified in the live filter preview path.

Dust & Scratches is absent from the full-resolution preview allow-list. The application therefore uses the normal proxy preview target (2,500,000 pixels). On a 24 MP document this can be about one quarter of the source dimension, and after upscaling the affected preview looks visibly blocky/pixelated at practical Dust & Scratches radii.

The final command still applies the filter at full resolution, so the result is correct; the defect is misleading low-quality interactive feedback. Users can currently work around it by disabling Low Resolution Previews in Preferences > Performance.

Expected behaviour:
- Dust & Scratches preview is full resolution, or uses a high-quality progressive/tiled preview that is not visibly pixelated at normal inspection zoom;
- preview parameters match the final operation;
- maintain responsiveness and make any reduced-quality preview explicit if one is unavoidable.

Add a regression test that places this filter on the intended preview-quality path.

title: Feature Request: Add Dedicated Pixel Art and Game Asset Tools
author: jasperwoodchuck
body:
Add tools designed for pixel artists and game asset creation, covering tilesets, sprite sheets, palette management, and seamless textures.

### Proposed Features

- **Tilemap Editor:** Arrange reusable tiles into grid-based levels, with support for multiple layers and tile collision properties.
- **Seamless Tile Preview:** Display a live, repeating preview of the canvas to help create seamless textures.
- **Sprite Sheet Slicer:** Split sprite sheets into individual sprites using configurable grids or transparent gaps, with manual adjustment.
- **Indexed Color Mode:** Restrict artwork to a fixed palette and allow global color replacement while preserving palette indices.
- **Pixel-Perfect Symmetry:** Draw mirrored artwork along configurable axes without introducing unwanted pixels or uneven edges.
- **Tile Seam Detection:** Highlight potential mismatches along tile edges and provide a repeating preview to help identify visible seams.

### Goals

These tools should make PhotoCraft more useful for creating pixel art, game sprites, tilesets, and textures without requiring separate applications for common workflows.

Where possible, features should integrate with existing editing tools and support exporting assets in formats commonly used by game engines.

Implementation can be split into smaller stages, starting with seamless tile preview and sprite sheet slicing before moving to the more involved tilemap editor and indexed color mode.

title: Feature Request: Add Traditional Frame-by-Frame Animation Tools
author: jasperwoodchuck
body:
Add a dedicated frame-by-frame animation workflow to PhotoCraft, allowing artists to create hand-drawn animations directly within the application.

### Proposed Features

- **Animation timeline:** Create, duplicate, delete, and reorder frames.
- **Onion skinning:** Display previous and next frames with adjustable opacity and frame range.
- **Playback controls:** Play, pause, loop, and adjust frame rate.
- **Per-frame editing:** Draw and erase directly on individual frames.
- **Layer support:** Organize animation frames into layers for more complex scenes.
- **Frame timing:** Set individual frame durations to control animation timing.
- **Preview controls:** Adjust playback range and loop the animation while editing.
- **Export:** Export animations as GIFs, video, or image sequences.

### Goals

The animation workflow should feel natural to artists familiar with traditional hand-drawn animation. It should support rough sketches, clean linework, and finished artwork without requiring users to manage each frame as a separate document.

The implementation should integrate with PhotoCraft's existing drawing tools and layer system. A good starting point would be a timeline, frame management, onion skinning, and real-time playback, with more advanced features added later.

title: Feature Request: Add Advanced Color Harmony and Palette Generation
author: jasperwoodchuck
body:
Add a color harmony tool that generates coordinated palettes from a selected base color.

**Proposed features**
- Generate complementary, analogous, triadic, split-complementary, and tetradic palettes.
- Allow users to adjust hue, saturation, and lightness.
- Preview palette colors and copy their HEX, RGB, or HSL values.
- Save generated palettes for reuse across projects.
- Allow individual colors to be locked while regenerating the remaining palette.
- Support importing and exporting palettes.

The tool should integrate with PhotoCraft's existing color picker and palette workflow, making it easier to create consistent color schemes for illustrations, paintings, and design work.

title: Interface: an Enable Animations preference (UI-217-10)
author: vangel76
body:
Part of #217 (scorecard row UI-217-10: "Appearance: animation toggle, canvas pattern toggle per theme, start-screen recents").

The issue asks to "toggle UI animation". There is no such preference: menus, popups and collapsing sections always fade/slide over egui's `animation_time` (1/12 s), and scroll areas animate their jumps. #1218 asked for the same thing ("an option to completely disable these kinds of time-wasters", a reduced-motion mode); #3251 fixes that issue's submenu part and leaves this request out.

Proposal: Preferences › Interface › **Enable animations** (`interface.enableAnimations`, on by default). Off sets egui's `animation_time` to 0 and turns off scroll animation in both the dark and light styles, live, re-applied after a theme change. Agents can set it with `prefs.set`; it is saved with the other preferences.

The other two parts of the row are elsewhere: the canvas pattern toggle is #2317 (#2264), and the Home screen already lists recent files (#2691).

title: View: guides stay level on a rotated canvas instead of turning with the image
author: vangel76
body:
### Description

With View › Rotate View (or the Rotate View tool) at a non-zero angle, guides are still drawn as screen-level lines: a vertical guide at x = 500 px is drawn as a vertical screen line through the screen position of document point (500, 0). It no longer marks x = 500 anywhere else on the image, while hit-testing (Move tool, ⌘-drag) and snapping still use the document coordinate, so the guide you see and the guide you grab are in different places.

In Photoshop, guides are locked to document coordinates and turn with the canvas when the view is rotated.

### Steps to reproduce

1. File › New, 2100 × 1500 px.
2. View › Rulers, drag a vertical guide to x = 500.
3. Rotate the view to e.g. -119° (Rotate View tool, Angle field).

### Expected

The guide is drawn along document x = 500, i.e. rotated with the image.

### Actual

The guide stays a vertical screen line, crossing the image at the wrong place.

Found while fixing #3233 (rulers on a rotated canvas); `draw_guides` in `crates/ui-egui/src/rulers.rs`.

title: Vanishing Point: tear off perpendicular planes and the Stamp tool (TOOL-214-14)
author: vangel76
body:
Follow-up to #3122 / #3133 (on-canvas Vanishing Point plane editor).

The Vanishing Point window can draw and edit planes and paste onto them, but two parts of Photoshop's window are still missing:

- **Tear off planes:** Ctrl/Cmd-dragging an edge node should tear off a perpendicular plane (90° by default). Dragging the new plane's far edge node sets its depth, and Alt-dragging it sets its angle. The torn plane should follow its parent and reach `filter.vanishingPoint` as `{"from", "edge", "angle", "depth"}`.
- **Stamp tool (S):** Alt-clicking a plane should set the source, and painting should clone in perspective (Diameter, Hardness, Opacity, Aligned) with a live preview. The strokes should be applied on OK as the command's `clone` param, so the whole session is one history step.

The engine already supports torn-off planes and perspective clone strokes. Its `clone` param still needs input validation and caps (stroke and point counts, finite numbers).

Out of scope: the window's Marquee tool and the Stamp's Heal modes (Off/Luminance/On). The engine has no heal mode yet.

Scorecard row: TOOL-214-14.

title: Smart Filters: paint the filter mask directly, with undo (FILE-215-3)
author: vangel76
body:
Scorecard row FILE-215-3 (`scorecard/file_compat.toml`, part of #215): "Filter mask can be painted directly, with undo".

On `main` a smart object's filter mask can only come from the selection when the first smart filter is added (`smart_cmds.rs` `add_smart_filter`). It can't be targeted or painted afterwards:

- The swatch on the Smart Filters row of the Layers panel is drawn but not clickable.
- `paint.stroke` and the other pixel commands have no filter-mask target. On a smart object without a layer mask they're refused ("active layer is a Smart Object layer without a mask").
- ⌥-click can't show the filter mask on its own.

Photoshop: clicking the filter mask thumbnail targets it. The painting tools, fills, filters and adjustments then edit it (black hides the smart filters there), with one undo step per stroke. ⌥-click shows the mask alone and ⇧-click disables it. The mask already persists through .pcraft and PSD (`FEid`).
