title: `layer.smartObjects.warp`: on a skewed smart object the mesh is mapped onto the bounding frame, not the contents, so an identity mesh shrinks the contents
author: pandapknaepel
body:
## Summary

`layer.smartObjects.warp` with `style: "custom"` and `mesh.points` in document px works as expected while the smart
object sits on an axis-aligned rectangle. When the smart object has a skewed or perspective placement (after
`edit.transform` with `quad`, or from a PSD's `nonAffineTransform`), the mesh is not applied to the contents but to a
larger frame **B**: the bounding rectangle of the `rect` corners mapped back into content space. The knots `us`/`vs`
are also measured in B. Result: a mesh that should leave the layer unchanged shrinks the contents into the middle of
the quad.

This matters for mockups: replaced contents on a skewed product photo (mug, box side) end up anywhere from a few px to
far away from where the warp should put them.

## Steps to reproduce

that content `(u, v)` lands at `x = 600 + 800u`, `y = 500 + 200u + 800v`. Then apply a warp whose control points are
exactly that placement (bicubic patches with evenly spaced control points reproduce an affine map exactly), with an
extra knot at `v = 0.25` so the knot handling is visible too.

```sh
# 1) placement only
photocraft-cli run --new '{"width":2000,"height":2000,"background":"white"}' \
  --cmd file.placeEmbedded --params '{"path":"uv-grid-1000.png","scale":100,"center":[1000,1000]}' \
  --cmd edit.transform --params '{"layer":6,"quad":[[600,500],[1400,700],[1400,1500],[600,1300]]}' \

title: Question: `file.export.saveForWebLegacy`: `matte` defaults to white – semi-transparent pixels in PNG-8/GIF get lightened, unlike Photoshop's scripted Save for Web
author: pandapknaepel
body:
## Summary

`file.export.saveForWebLegacy` uses `matte: "#ffffff"` by default. With PNG-8 (or GIF) and transparency on, partly
transparent pixels are blended with the matte before they get 1-bit transparency, so a soft black shadow turns into
grey pixels. Images exported for the web on non-white backgrounds then show a light halo. Photoshop's scripted Save for
Web (`ExportOptionsSaveForWeb` with PNG-8 and the remaining options at their defaults) gave us no matte: the shadow
pixels stayed pure black, alpha only 0 or 255.

## Steps to reproduce

`soft-shadow.png`: 256 × 64 px, black, alpha falling from 255 (left) to 0 (right).

```sh
photocraft-cli run soft-shadow.png \
  --cmd file.export.saveForWebLegacy --params '{"format":"png8","path":"sfw-default.png"}' \
  --cmd file.export.saveForWebLegacy --params '{"format":"png8","matte":"none","path":"sfw-none.png"}'
```

Pixels at y = 10 (ImageMagick `%[pixel:p{x,10}]`):

| x (source alpha) | default (`matte` white) | `matte: "none"` |
|---|---|---|
| 0 (255) | srgba(2,2,2,1) | srgba(0,0,0,1) |
| 64 (191) | srgba(66,66,66,1) | srgba(0,0,0,1) |
| 128 (127) | transparent | transparent |

Default export: 129 colours, 1472 bytes; `matte: "none"`: 2 colours, 197 bytes.

## Expected

Same as Photoshop's scripted Save for Web with default options: no matte unless one is asked for (or at least the
documented default matches whatever Photoshop uses for the chosen format/preset).

## Actual

White matte by default; dark semi-transparent pixels are lightened (grey fringe).

## Environment

- Windows 10 Pro 22H2 (10.0.19045), x64
- `photocraft-cli 0.7.0 (792616159, 2026-10-11)`, headless `run`

## Workaround we use

Pass `"matte": "none"` explicitly.

title: PSD import hangs on an annotation entry with length 0
author: davidmann4
body:
A malformed global `Anno` block makes PSD import hang, then abort when allocation fails. The abort is not a panic, so the last-resort guard can't keep the document.

**Where:** `crates/io/src/annotations_map.rs`, `parse_entries`. When an entry's length is 0, `end == start` and `r.p = end` puts the cursor back on the same entry. With a count of `0xFFFFFFFF` the loop runs about 4.3 billion times and pushes an entry each time. A `txtA` entry with length 0 loops the same way. Every PSD open calls this (`psd_import.rs`, `notes_from_blocks`).

**Repro:** a PSD whose global `Anno` block is these 16 bytes: `00 02 00 01 FF FF FF FF 00 00 00 00 73 6E 64 41` (version 2.1, count 0xFFFFFFFF, one entry with length 0 and type `sndA`).

**Expected:** the block is treated as unreadable and kept raw (the #944 behaviour), and import finishes. An entry's length includes itself and the 4-byte type, so anything under 8 is invalid.

Found while reading the code on `main`. I'm fixing it in #4117.

title: Swatches: an HSB value beyond f32 range is stored as NaN and resets all presets on the next launch
author: davidmann4
body:
`swatches.add {"color":{"model":"hsb","values":[1e39,100,100]}}` returns Ok.

**Where:** `crates/engine/src/presets/swatches.rs`, `SwatchColor::from_param`. The value passes the finiteness check as f64, then `as f32` turns it into infinity, and `inf.rem_euclid(360)` gives NaN. The NaN is written to the preferences file as `null`.

**What goes wrong:** on the next launch, `load_presets_json` fails to deserialize the whole `Persisted` blob because of that one `null`. Every user preset (gradients, styles, shapes, tool presets, document presets, swatches) falls back to the defaults, and the next save overwrites the user's presets with them.

**Expected:** a BadParams error for numbers outside f32 range, and the library stays unchanged. This is the same class as #4044.

Found while reading the code on `main`. I'm fixing it in #4118.

title: Layer effects keep stale maps after toggling Transparency Shapes Layer or a child's Blend If
author: davidmann4
body:
The effect-map cache key (`layer_identity` in `crates/compose/src/lib.rs`) hashes a layer's pixels, masks, fill opacity and effects, but not `layer.advanced` or `layer.blend_if`. Both change the shape effects are built from:
- With Transparency Shapes Layer off, the whole layer becomes the effect shape.
- A styled group's shape is its children's composite, and a child's Blend If changes it.

**Repro:** a layer with a transparent hole and an outside Stroke. Turn Transparency Shapes Layer off (Blending Options). The stroke keeps rimming the hole until Edit › Purge. The same happens with a group's Drop Shadow after a child's Blend If changes.

**Expected:** the effects update right away. The GPU path falls back to the CPU in both cases, so the stale result shows on screen.

Found while reading the code on `main`. I'm fixing it in #4119.

title: Layer Style dialog turns an Inner Glow's Source: Center into Edge on OK
author: davidmann4

**Repro:** a layer with an Inner Glow whose Source is Center (`layer.layerStyle.innerGlow {"source":"center"}`, or from a PSD). Open Layer › Layer Style.

**What goes wrong:**
- The Source dropdown shows Edge, and the preview renders Edge.
- Clicking OK with no edits stores Edge.

**Where:** `crates/ui-egui/src/layer_style.rs`, `values_of()`. It starts from the defaults (`"source": "edge"`) and never loads the glow's source. The engine's `overlay_effect` then writes Edge.

**Expected (Photoshop):** the dialog shows Center, and OK keeps it.

Found while reading the code on `main`. I'm fixing it in #4120.

title: Auto-Select picks the layer below when the mask has reduced density
author: davidmann4
body:
`layer.pickAt` (Move tool Auto-Select, the right-click layer list and the Move rollover highlight) reads the raw mask pixel. The compositor applies the mask's density (`LayerMask::value`, `1 - density*(1-v)`), but picking does not.

**Repro:**
1. Create a layer filled red.
2. Layer Mask › Hide All, then set the mask's Density to 0 in Properties. The layer is now fully visible.
3. `layer.pickAt {"x":5,"y":5}` returns the Background. At 50% density the layer is half visible and still never picked.

**Where:** `crates/engine/src/pick_cmds.rs`, `layers_hit`.

**Expected:** picking follows what is visible, so the red layer is picked.

Found while reading the code on `main`. I'm fixing it in #4121.

title: Find and Replace Text: backward Change/Find keeps finding the text it just replaced
author: davidmann4
body:
**Repro:** a type layer reading "cat dog cat", with Edit › Find and Replace Text set to Find "cat", Change To "Cat", backward.
1. Find finds the second "cat" (8..11).
2. Change/Find replaces it and finds (8..11) again, forever. The first "cat" is never reached.

This happens whenever the replacement still matches the search, for example the common case-insensitive change of capitalisation.

**Where:** `crates/engine/src/edit_menu_cmds.rs`, `find_replace`. After a replace, the cursor is set to the end of the replacement. A backward search then starts after the text it just replaced.

**Expected:** a backward Change/Find moves on to the previous match.

Found while reading the code on `main`. I'm fixing it in #4122.

**What goes wrong:** the command succeeds and adds a smart filter, plus a history step, to the locked layer. Other filters, such as Gaussian Blur, refuse with "layer … is locked".

**Where:** `crates/engine/src/distort_cmds.rs`, `run_on_layer`. The smart-object branch returns through `add_smart_filter` before `check_locks` runs.

title: Count tool: Marker Size and Label Size fields have no effect
author: davidmann4
body:
**Repro:** select the Count tool and type 8 into Marker Size (or change Label Size) in the options bar. The markers don't change.

**Where:**
- `crates/ui-egui/src/analysis_ui.rs` sends `{"markerSize": ms.round(), "labelSize": ls.round()}` with f32 values, so the JSON holds 8.0.
- `count.setGroup` (`crates/engine/src/analysis_cmds.rs`) reads them with `as_u64()`, which returns None for floats.
- The command returns Ok and changes nothing. The engine test sends integers, so it doesn't catch this.

**Expected:** the sizes apply. The engine should also accept integral numbers sent as floats, as agents and actions send them.

Found while reading the code on `main`. I'm fixing it in #4124.

title: Double-clicking another layer's effect row opens Layer Style for the active layer

**What goes wrong:** Layer Style opens filled from A, and OK edits A.

**Where:** `crates/ui-egui/src/panels.rs`, `effect_rows`. The handler calls `layer_style::open(app, kind)`, which always uses the active layer. The right-click menu on the same row selects the row's layer first, so the two paths disagree.

title: Layers panel shows no lock icon for Lock Image Pixels or the artboard lock

**What goes wrong:**

**Where:** `crates/ui-egui/src/layer_row_ui.rs` (`reserved_width`, `indicators`) and the Studio lock button in `crates/ui-egui/src/panels.rs` test `transparency || position || all`. `simple_lock_toggle` in the same file tests `transparency || pixels || position || artboard || all`.

title: photocraft-cli serve: an invalid "index" silently targets the active document
author: davidmann4
body:
In the JSON-lines server (`photocraft-cli serve`), `index_of` in `crates/automation/src/rpc.rs` turns any `index` that isn't an unsigned integer (`"0"`, `-1`, `0.5`, `true`) into None, and None means "the active document".

**Repro:**
1. `doc.new` twice, so document 1 is active.
2. `{"method":"doc.close","params":{"index":"0"}}` replies ok and closes document 1, the unsaved active one.

`doc.save` with `"index": -1` likewise saves the active document. The MCP server types `index` as `Option<usize>` and rejects these, so the two front ends disagree.

**Expected:** a bad-request error, and nothing is closed or saved.

Found while reading the code on `main`.

title: Image Size / Canvas Size resize large documents on OK without any edit when the unit isn't pixels
author: davidmann4
body:
**Repro:**
1. Set Preferences › Units & Rulers › Rulers to Points.
2. Open a 40000×1000 px document at 72 ppi.
3. Image › Image Size. Width shows 30000 pt instead of 40000, and with Constrain on the height becomes 750.
4. Press OK without touching anything: the image is resized to 30000×750. Canvas Size crops in the same way.

The same happens in mm or in at low resolutions.

title: Content-Aware Move (Move mode): moved object isn't blended, result looks like two patches swapped
author: Lincontrol
body:
Found in a first-look video of PhotoCraft 0.7 on macOS: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0j57nAQjisI

**What happens**
With the Content-Aware Move tool in **Move** mode, the reviewer moved a person and other objects to a new spot on a beach photo. The result:
- The moved patch keeps its original brightness, so it looks too bright in one place and too dark in another.
- The area around the object (sand from the old spot) is pasted along with it.
- The old spot is filled with a straight copy of nearby content.
In the reviewer's words it looked like the two areas were "just flipped". **Extend** mode and the **Remove** tool gave clearly better results on the same photo.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Open a photo with a gradual lighting change (e.g. beach, sky, wall).
2. Content-Aware Move tool, Mode: Move, default Structure and Color.
3. Loosely lasso an object and drag it to an area with different brightness.

**Expected**
Like Photoshop: the moved object adapts to its new surroundings with no visible patch edge, and the hole is filled plausibly.

**Where I think it comes from** (`crates/engine/src/retouch_cmds/content_aware_move.rs`)
- `land` copies the eroded core of the selection **pixel for pixel**. Only a fixed ~6 px band (`band_width` for Structure 3–7) is re-synthesised.
- The only tone fit is a single global gain/bias per channel (`level_transform`), scaled by `color_amount(color)`. **Color defaults to 0** (`cam_color: 0.0` in `crates/ui-egui/src/state.rs`), and `color_amount(0)` returns `Adapt::NONE`, so by default there is no colour adaptation at all. - No gradient-domain blending is used, although `poisson::seamless_clone` (`crates/algo/src/poisson.rs`) is already used by the healing tools.
- The hole at the old spot is filled with `fill_with` (Content-Aware Fill PatchMatch, large 15–40 px patches, no grow). The Remove tool, which looked much better, uses `remove::remove_with` with a sma…

title: Eraser/brush stroke jumps: first press draws a long line to a far point
author: Lincontrol
body:
Found in a first-look video of PhotoCraft 0.7 on macOS: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0j57nAQjisI

**What happens**
The reviewer painted with the Brush on a new layer and changed brush size with `[` / `]`. Then they selected the original image layer (Background) and started erasing. The first press drew a long straight erase stroke to a point far away, "without me moving my mouse". Undo fixed it, and the next strokes were fine.

(The white instead of a checkerboard was expected: erasing on a layer with locked transparency paints the background colour, as in Photoshop.)

**Steps to reproduce (not confirmed, best guess)**
1. Brush tool on Layer 1, paint a stroke; use `[`, `]` (or `⇧[` / `⇧]`).
2. Click the Background layer in the Layers panel.
3. Eraser tool, press and drag on the canvas somewhere else.
4. Sometimes the first segment runs from the end of the previous stroke to the new press point.

**Most likely cause**
This looks exactly like Photoshop's ⇧-click "connect to last point" firing without the user holding Shift:
- `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs` (`ToolEvent::Down` for paint tools): when `mods.shift` is set, `app.last_stroke_end` is inserted as the stroke's first point.
- `last_stroke_end` is only checked against the **document**, not the layer or tool (`lib.rs`, set at the end of every stroke). So the end of the brush stroke on another layer is still used after switching layers and tools.
- If Shift is reported as still down on the press (a lost Shift key-up on macOS after `⇧[`/`⇧]` or a focus change, or Window › Modifier Keys sticky Shift), the press becomes a connect-line.

I checked other candidates and they look fine: pointer moves outside the stroke are dropped, smoothing repeats the last point, tablet input only supplies pressure, and stroke points are in document coordinates.

**Suggestions**

2. Clear `last_stroke_end` when …

title: Gradient tool icon (two overlapping circles) is hard to recognise
author: Lincontrol
body:
Found in a first-look video of PhotoCraft 0.7 on macOS: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0j57nAQjisI

**What happens**
The reviewer, who knows Photoshop, couldn't find the Gradient tool for a while. The icon shows two overlapping circles, which reads as a Pathfinder/blend icon, not as a gradient. Quote: "I don't know why there's a really weird icon for the gradient tool… It was really confusing to me."

title: Contour (.shc) files: long names split UTF-16 surrogates, and a 1024-unit name can't be read back
author: davidmann4
body:
Two bugs in `crates/psd/src/shc.rs`:

1. **Writer:** `c.name.encode_utf16().take(MAX_NAME_UNITS)` can end on a lone high surrogate. A contour named 1023 × "a" followed by an emoji is saved as ill-formed UTF-16 and reads back with U+FFFD. `aco.rs` and `ase.rs` use the shared `crate::io::utf16_units` for exactly this. Reachable through saving user-named contours (`contour_to_shc`).
2. **Reader:** the "count left out the null" check tests `units.last()` on the vector after it was capped at `MAX_NAME_UNITS`. Our own writer saves a 1024-character name as count 1025 plus a null. The reader then consumes the next point count (`00 00`) as the null, the stream shifts by 2 bytes, and parsing fails with `UnexpectedEof`.

**Expected:** the writer cuts at a character boundary, and anything the writer produces parses back.

Found while reading the code on `main`.

author: ametadot
body:

We are developing a multi-image Filmstrip for PhotoCraft's Camera Raw workspace, following established industry-standard RAW development workflows and terminology.

The goal is to allow users to open, preview, navigate and adjust multiple photographs within a single Camera Raw session before opening them as PhotoCraft documents.

This should be a general RAW and JPEG capability, independent of camera manufacturer or file format, using PhotoCraft's existing supported image decoders.

Proposed functionality

Vertical Filmstrip: A left-side thumbnail browser showing photographs in the current Camera Raw session, with active-image highlighting, filenames, file extensions, show/hide controls and an adjustable Filmstrip width.

Multi-image navigation: Switch between photographs while retaining independent adjustment settings and preview state.

Open Images / Cancel: Open the intended photographs into PhotoCraft while ensuring Cancel discards uncommitted changes.

Document staging: Photographs awaiting acceptance should not appear as ordinary editable PhotoCraft documents or tabs before Open Images is selected.

RAW and JPEG compatibility: Support multiple photographs in one Camera Raw session, including DNG, NEF, CR2, ARW and other supported RAW formats, with JPEG support included in the intended workflow.

File preservation: Original RAW and JPEG files and associated metadata must remain unchanged during preview and cancellation.

The multi-image workflow should support non-destructive XMP metadata handling, with independent adjustment settings for each photograph.

XMP reading: Detect associated .xmp sidecar files and load supported Camera Raw adjustment settings where available.

title: Cryptomatte: IDs stored in the .blue/.alpha channels are dropped, so mattes get holes
author: davidmann4
body:
Each Cryptomatte RGBA set holds two (ID, coverage) pairs: `.red/.green` and `.blue/.alpha` (Cryptomatte spec; the reference Nuke `cryptomatte_utilities.py` reads both). `crates/codecs/src/codecs/exr_cryptomatte.rs` (`split_stream`, `decode`) only recognises `red`/`r` and `green`/`g`, so every second rank is lost.

**Repro:** the Psyop sample `testGrid_CryptoObject.exr` has `CryptoObject00..02.{red,green,blue,alpha}` (6 ranks); only 3 are decoded. Objects stored at ranks 1, 3, 5 vanish from the matte at edges and overlaps.

Matching is also case-sensitive, so `.R/.G/.B/.A` (as some renderers write them) aren't recognised.

**Expected:** both pairs per channel set are decoded, with case-insensitive suffixes.

Found while reading the code on `main`.

body:
CMYK samples are ink amounts (1 = full ink), but two Stylize filters treat them like RGB light values:

- **Find Edges** (`crates/algo/src/stylize.rs`, `find_edges`): `v = 1 - |gradient|/4`. In flat areas that sets every ink to 100%, so a flat CMYK 10/10/10/10 document turns solid black. Photoshop gives 0/0/0/0 (white).
- **Solarize** (`crates/algo/src/lib.rs`): `if v > 0.5 { 1 - v }` inverts the channels with more than 50% ink (the shadows). CMYK 10/20/80/90% gives 10/20/20/10; Photoshop gives 90/80/80/90 (it inverts the channels below 50% ink, the highlights).

Trace Contour already handles this with `fxutil::subtractive(ctx)`.

**Expected:** both filters give Photoshop's results on CMYK; RGB is unchanged.

Found while reading the code on `main`; both CMYK results were checked against Photoshop.

title: Rotate View turns the image against the pointer when View › Flip Horizontal is on
author: davidmann4
body:
**Repro:** View › Flip Horizontal, then the Rotate View tool (R). Drag clockwise around the centre: the image turns counter-clockwise, away from the hand. A trackpad rotate gesture is reversed the same way.

**Where:** `ViewXform::to_screen` rotates first and then mirrors x, so in a flipped view increasing `rotation` by d turns the image by -d on screen. The compass overlay in `crates/ui-egui/src/rotate_view.rs` already accounts for the flip, but `drag` (`delta = wrap_deg(pointer_deg(p) - start)`) and the trackpad delta in `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs` don't.

**Expected (Photoshop):** the image follows the pointer (and the trackpad gesture) whether or not the view is flipped.

Found while reading the code on `main`.

title: Brush resize HUD (Alt+right-drag / Ctrl+Alt-drag) mixes up size and hardness in a rotated view

**Where:** `crates/ui-egui/src/brush_resize.rs`, `update`: the drag delta is taken in document coordinates. It corrects for View › Flip Horizontal but not for the view rotation (or pixel aspect).

**Expected (Photoshop):** the HUD is screen-relative: horizontal changes the size, vertical changes the hardness, whatever the view rotation.

Found while reading the code on `main`.

title: Brush cursor: a shaped tip's outline doesn't turn or flip with a rotated or flipped view
author: FinnNk
body:
**What happens:** with a shaped brush tip (a sampled tip, or a round tip with less than 100% roundness or an angle), the cursor traces the tip's outline (#3467). On a rotated canvas (Rotate View, R) or a flipped one (View › Flip Horizontal), the outline keeps the document's orientation, but the stroke turns with the view. So the cursor no longer shows what will be painted.

**Photoshop:** the brush cursor turns and mirrors with the view, so it always matches the dab.

**Steps:** Brush tool, roundness 30%, angle 30°. Rotate the view 90° with R: the cursor outline doesn't turn, but a dab does.

The outline also ignores View › Pixel Aspect Ratio Correction, which stretches the stroke.

title: Make Brushes its own dockable panel
author: artcraftfan1

## Description
Make the Brushes window a separate panel that can be docked, moved, and grouped with other panels, matching Photoshop's behavior.

## Current behavior
The Brushes window is currently integrated into the Brush Settings window as its second tab. Selecting Window → Brushes opens the Brush Settings window instead of a separate panel.

- The Brushes panel is independent of Brush Settings.
- It can be docked, moved, reordered, and grouped with other panels.
- It can be opened independently through Window → Brushes.
- It can be hidden and reopened without affecting Brush Settings.

- `crates/ui-egui/src/brush_panel.rs`
- `crates/ui-egui/src/brush_picker.rs`
- `crates/ui-egui/src/brushes_tab.rs`
- `menus.rs` (`window.panel.brushes`)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Brushes exists as a separate panel.
- [ ] The panel supports docking, moving, and grouping.
- [ ] Window → Brushes opens the independent Brushes panel.
- [ ] The panel can be hidden and reopened independently of Brush Settings.

title: Feature request: AI Seamless Blending for imported layers, integrated with Generative Fill

## Summary

Please add AI-powered Seamless Blending for imported image layers, integrated with text-prompt Generative Fill.

The main use case is placing an object or person from one image into another scene and asking AI to make it look naturally photographed there, while keeping the document editable.

## Suggested workflow

1. Open a background image.
2. Import another image onto a separate layer, then position and resize it.
3. Select the imported layer (or its mask/selection) and choose **AI Seamless Blend**.
4. Optionally provide a prompt, such as: "Blend this person naturally into the scene. Match the warm light from the left and add a realistic contact shadow."
5. Preview the result, adjust the strength or prompt, and accept a variation.

## Expected blending behavior

Use the surrounding scene as context to:

- Match lighting direction, intensity, and color temperature.
- Create or adapt realistic contact and cast shadows.
- Harmonize colors, exposure, contrast, and saturation.
- Adjust perspective where needed to make the placement believable.
- Refine edges and transitions, avoiding halos or an obvious pasted-on appearance.
- Preserve the imported subject's identity and important details unless the prompt explicitly requests changes.

## Preserve editability

Keep the original background and imported layer intact. Put generated changes on separate layers with editable masks, or an equivalent non-destructive structure. Users should be able to refine masks, adjust opacity, hide or remove the result, and regenerate without flattening the document. Limit changes to the selected area and any explicitly allowed surrounding blend region.

## Text-prompt Generative Fill

The same workflow should also support selecting an area and describing what to add, replace, or remove. For example: "Add a small plant on this table, matching the room's lighting and perspective." Return the generated result on a separate masked layer, with variations and the ability to revise t…

title: 32-bit text rasterization clips HDR and signed color components
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
On main `184c226`, `TextEngine::render` with an RGB text style `[2.5, -0.25, 0.5]` and `PixelFormat::RGBA32F` produces `[1.0, 0.0, 0.5]` at covered pixels. A fractional-coverage pixel in the reproduction is `[1.0, 0.0, 0.5, 0.72021484]`.

The character style supports float components (including through the array form of `type.create` / `type.setStyle`), but `crates/text/src/render.rs` unconditionally clamps the unpremultiplied color channels to `[0,1]`. This loses intensity and signed channel information in the rendered text cache before subsequent editing or export. Integer output should remain bounded; finite float colors should retain their range.

Reproduced with bundled text and a failing regression on current main, independently of display profiles or system fonts. This is separate from #4302's ordinary pure RGB report and #1630's text-gamma change when converting a type layer to a pixel layer: the values here are already clipped in the text engine's float surface before compositing.

A small correction and regressions are prepared locally: opaque/translucent float text retains its authored components, while 8/16-bit output remains bounded. Full text tests, Clippy, layering and WebAssembly checks pass; corpus and performance validation are still in progress before submitting the PR.

Prepared with Codex assistance; credit jonathnwxh.

title: Engine commands silently ignore unknown params (`layer.hideLayers {"ids":[4]}` toggles the active layer instead)
author: Mart95Dev
body:
## Summary

Engine commands accept unknown keys in `params` and silently ignore them. A misspelled or misremembered parameter doesn't produce an error: the command runs with its defaults, often on a different target than intended, and reports success. This matters most for automation (CLI `run`, `serve`, MCP, control channel), where an agent guessing a parameter name gets no signal that it guessed wrong.

The `ui.*` methods already reject unknown fields (`docs/control-protocol.md`: "an unknown field … is an error naming the parameter, and nothing is queued or applied"). Engine commands don't: `grep deny_unknown_fields crates/engine/src` finds nothing.

## Reproduction

`example.psd` from psd.rb's test files (https://github.com/layervault/psd.rb/blob/master/spec/files/example.psd). It has groups "Version A" (id 5, visible), "Version B" (id 9, hidden) and "Version C" (id 13, hidden). The active layer on open is id 13.

```
$ photocraft-cli run example.psd --cmd layer.hideLayers --params '{"ids":[4]}' --out out.png
{"command":"layer.hideLayers","result":null}          # exit 0
```

The intended parameter is `{"layer": 4}`, the type layer inside "Version A". With `ids` ignored, `layer.hideLayers` toggles the **active** layer: "Version C" is hidden, so it gets *shown*. `out.png` is the green Version C composited over Version A, the opposite of hiding something.

Two more examples:

```
$ photocraft-cli run example.psd --cmd layer.hideLayers --params '{"nimportequoi":42}' --out out.png
{"command":"layer.hideLayers","result":null}          # exit 0

$ photocraft-cli run example.psd --cmd layer.newAdjustmentLayer.curves --params '{"pointz":[[0,0],[64,40],[192,220],[255,255]]}' --out out.png
{"command":"layer.newAdjustmentLayer.curves","result":{"layer":14}}   # exit 0, identity curve: the typo'd points were dropped
```

## Expected

An error naming the unknown key, like the `ui.*` methods:

```
error: `layer.hideLayers`: unknown parameter `ids` (expected: layer)
```

The pa…

title: Tools other than Brush/Pencil/Fill convert a CMYK foreground through sRGB (follow-up to #4196/#4344)
author: vangel76
body:
Follow-up to #4196 / #4339 (Edit > Fill) and #4344 / #4347 (Brush, Pencil). #4339 makes `tools.setColors` remember a CMYK pick (`foregroundCmyk`) and Edit > Fill write those inks; the other consumers of `tools.foreground` / `tools.background` still convert the sRGB stand-in, so a pick like pure cyan 100/0/0/0 (outside sRGB) comes out as roughly 100/28/0/17 in a CMYK document.

Every consumer, and whether the picked inks should apply:

Flat colour written straight into the target's pixels (inks apply):
- `edit.fill*` / Alt+Backspace: done in #4339
- `paint.stroke` / `paint.pencil`: done in #4347
- `paint.bucket` (solid colour, not pattern): TODO
- `edit.stroke` (Edit > Stroke band): TODO
- Background colour written into pixels: Delete/Cut on the Background (`clear_selected`), Canvas Size / Crop / Rotate Canvas extension (`extensionColor` "background"), Magic Eraser on locked transparency: same mechanism applies, left for a later PR to keep this one small

Only feeds a blend, mix or interpolation (sRGB stand-in is correct, no change):
- `paint.gradient` / gradient fills: stops are interpolated in RGB, so intermediate pixels are not the picked inks anyway
- Filters Clouds / Difference Clouds: interpolate fg to bg per pixel
- Mixer Brush, Smudge finger painting, Color Replacement, Background Eraser (protect foreground / sampling), Magic Wand colour range: the colour is a mix input or a comparison key, not a pixel value
- Photo Filter, Color Range foreground sample: colour operation parameters

Non-pixel property (no pixels written at this point):
- Type tool text colour, shape/vector fill and stroke colours: stored on the layer and rasterised by the compositor
- History Brush: no colour

title: PSD: Photoshop Frame layers open without their stroke (frame imports as an empty group)
author: Nmarello
body:
**Version:** photocraft-cli 0.7.0 (macOS universal release), and main at `d43db3e1` (0.8.2). macOS 27.0.1, Apple M4.

### What happens

A Photoshop **Frame** (Frame tool, K) with a stroke opens with no stroke. Since the frame is empty, nothing is drawn at all. Photoshop's own composite shows the stroked frame.

Repro file: I made it in Photoshop 27.9 for this report, and I can contribute it to photocraft-corpus. It's 800×600 RGB 8-bit sRGB on a white background, with one elliptical frame. The frame has an 8 px red Inside stroke set in Properties and nothing placed in it.

```sh
photocraft-cli run frame.psd --cmd layer.flattenImage --out photocraft.png   # white canvas only
sips -s format png frame.psd --out photoshop.png                             # red ellipse (Photoshop's merged image)
```

`photocraft-cli info` lists `Frame 1` as a `Group` with `bounds: null`, `hasVectorMask: true` and no children.

### How Photoshop stores it

From this file: the frame is a layer group (`lsct` 1 … `lsct` 3, section blend `pass`). Its top record carries these blocks:

| Block | Holds |
|---|---|
| `vsms` | the frame outline as a vector mask |
| `vogk` | the live ellipse |
| `vstk` | the stroke, in the same layout as a shape layer's |
| `frgb` | a descriptor with `framedGroupRect`, `framedGroupType`, `LockPPI`, `PreferredResolution` and `framedGroupPath…` |

PhotoCraft already imports `vsms` as the group's vector mask (`apply_vector_mask` in `psd_import.rs`). `vstk`, though, is only read for shape layers (`vector_map.rs`), so the stroke never reaches the document. The blocks do survive a re-save (`convert frame.psd out.psd` keeps `vsms`/`vogk`/`vstk`/`frgb`), so Photoshop still shows the frame afterwards. The gap is only in what PhotoCraft draws.

### Proposed fix

- Give groups an optional frame stroke, e.g. `Group::frame_stroke: Option<ShapeStroke>`.
- Import it from `vstk` on group records with `parse_vstk`.
- Draw it along the group's enabled vector-mask path, above the group…

title: Type: fall back to installed Indic fonts for document text (TYPE-218-3)
author: vangel76
body:
Part of #218 (scorecard row TYPE-218-3).

**Photoshop behaviour:** text in a font that lacks a script's glyphs falls back to an installed font that has them (missing glyph protection), so Devanagari, Bengali, Gurmukhi, Gujarati, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam and Sinhala show real letters.

title: GPU compositor: a Blend If layer sends the whole document to the CPU compositor
author: FinnNk
body:
**What happens:** if any layer in an RGB or grayscale document has Blending Options › Blend If set, the GPU planner refuses the whole document (`plan.rs` `check_blend_if`: "Blend If on `…` (composited on the CPU)"). Every canvas refresh of that document then runs the CPU compositor, for every edit to any layer, not just edits to the Blend If layer.

**Cost** (release build of `main` at `d43db3e1`, `perf_scenarios` layered group, RTX 4090 laptop; the CPU numbers come from `--cpu`, which is the path such documents take):

| Edit | GPU compositor | CPU compositor |
|---|---|---|
| Change layer opacity | 3.4 ms | 93 ms |
| Toggle visibility | 3.3 ms | 63 ms |
| Move styled layer 10 px | 18 ms | 201 ms |
| Move tool drag frame, full-canvas layer | 93 ms | 531 ms |

Blend If is common in retouching and compositing PSDs (blending skies, luminosity blending), and one such layer is enough to slow every edit by 15–27×.

**Proposal:** composite Blend If on the GPU. `compose::apply_blend_if` is a per-pixel weight from the layer's own colour ("This Layer", its content with masks) and the backdrop beneath it ("Underlying Layer"), through the Gray/R/G/B ranges, followed by a premultiplied mix of the composite back towards the backdrop. That's the existing `Lerp` mix with a computed weight: retain the backdrop, composite the layer as now, render its own content (with masks) into a slot, and mix with the ranges in the pass parameters. No document or format change, and the same evaluation as the CPU compositor within the GPU path's usual tolerance.

Scope: Blend If only, in RGB, Grayscale and Duotone (where `blend_if_active` applies it). Documents that also use Advanced Blending keep the CPU path.

title: Compose: vector-mask cache keyed by a temporary clone's address serves the wrong mask
author: vangel76
body:
`RenderVectorMasks::values` (crates/compose/src/lib.rs) caches compiled vector masks keyed by the address of the `&VectorMask` it is given. `hiding_mask` and `effects_source` (crates/compose/src/advanced.rs) pass it addresses of temporary clones. The clone is dropped, the next clone reuses the address, and the map never evicts, so a different layer's mask is served from the cache (and entries pile up).

Repro: 12x8 RGB doc, white Background, two full-canvas layers A (blue) and B (green), each with an Inside stroke effect and `vector_mask_hides_effects = true`. A's vector mask is a polygon covering x<6, B's covers x>=6.

Expected: pixel x=2 blue, x=9 green.
Actual: x=2 green, x=9 white, with both `render` and `render_tiled(.., 3)` (layer B is composited with A's mask).

Fix: key the cache by mask content instead of a temporary's address.

title: Compose: arithmetic overflow and unbounded allocation on hostile coordinates (never-crash)
author: vangel76
body:
Found by a read-only audit of `crates/compose` against the never-crash rules (AGENTS.md section 3). All of these panic in debug/test builds (wrap silently in release) or allocate without bound on hostile numbers.

- `masks.rs` `build_mask`: `x0.floor() as i32 - 2` / `x1.ceil() as i32 + 2` overflow when path control points are about +-1e30 (the cast saturates to i32::MIN/MAX).
- `effects.rs` `Map::shifted`: `x - fx as i64` overflows for a layer-style distance of +-1e30 (only the margin is clamped, not the distance).
- `pattern.rs` `Tile::sample`: `x0 + dx` overflows for a huge pattern phase (x0 = i64::MAX after the saturating cast).
- `proxy.rs` `downsample`: `x1 * k`, `oy * k` can overflow near i32::MAX.
- `lib.rs` `render_tiled_with`: `rect.width() as i32 <= tile` wraps negative for widths >= 2^31 and takes the single-tile path with a huge allocation; nothing caps the rect size at all (canvas can be 300000 px per side).
- `adjust.rs` `lut3d_sample` (pub): panics for `n < 2` (`n - 1`, `n - 2` underflow) and indexes past a short table.

title: Text: non-finite numbers and negative indices from PSD files are not sanitized
author: vangel76
body:
Self-found while auditing `crates/text` against the never-crash rules. None of these panic, but hostile or corrupt PSD data silently corrupts text.

- EngineData accepts `inf`, `nan`, `1e999` as reals; `char_style`/`para_style`, the FillColor reader and the warp reader pass them into font size, leading, tracking, scales, indents, colour and warp. Text then silently disappears (inf size, NaN alpha) or a zero size is saved back.
- `dpi > 0.0` lets `inf` through (layout, lib, psd, psd_styles), so `size_pt / k` is inf and `format_real` writes `0.0`.
- `psd_styles.rs` casts negative `Parent` / `TheNormal*` / `DefaultStyleSheet` indices with `as usize` (huge value), which suppresses the `Name` fallback; `psd.rs` already uses `usize::try_from`.
- `served.rs::sri` accepts `+` in hex digits via `from_str_radix`.
- `raster.rs::Coverage::line` casts f64 to f32 without re-checking finiteness.

Plan: sanitize at the boundary (non-finite -> field default), require finite dpi, reuse the checked index handling, validate hex digits, re-check finiteness after the cast. Finite in-range values keep their behaviour.

title: Text: layout is O(chars x runs) on documents with many style runs
author: vangel76
body:
Laying out a text layer with many style runs does super-linear work. A layer with 90,000 one-character runs (30,000 x "ab ") stalls far beyond 10 s in a debug build.

Causes in `crates/text/src/layout.rs` (upstream/main d43db3e1):

- `style_at` (`run_starts.iter().rposition(..)`) is called per character (synthetic caps / caps handling), so layout is O(chars x runs).
- `small_caps` is rebuilt for every paragraph by calling `fonts.selected_face_has_feature` for every style, even when the style's `caps` is not `SmallCaps`. Each call does a family lookup and a font table probe, so this is O(paragraphs x runs) font probes.

Related, not part of the fix: `psd.rs` `para_of`, `psd_styles.rs` `run_at` and the per-tab tail rescan at layout.rs `~799` have similar shapes.

Planned fix (narrow): `style_at` becomes a binary search with identical results, and `small_caps` is computed once per layout and only probes the font for styles that use `Caps::SmallCaps`.

Found by a read-only audit.

title: Compose: effect-map cache key is recomputed for every tile (provably redundant work)
author: vangel76
body:
## Problem

`effect_maps` (`crates/compose/src/lib.rs`) computes the cache key of a layer's effect maps with `layer_identity`: a `format!("{:?}")` of the whole effects block, of the vector mask and of fill/adjustment content, a walk over every tile of the layer's pixels and mask, and, for a group, the same for every child, recursively.

The identity depends only on the layer, not on the tile, yet `effect_maps` runs it again on every call. It is called once per render tile for every layer with effects (`composite_layer_effects`, `composite_atop_any`), plus once per layer in `prepare_effects`. A render of T tiles therefore builds the same identity T + 1 times per effect layer, and each build is linear in the layer's tile count (so the total grows with tiles x layer tiles).

## Proposed fix

Compute the identity once per layer per render. The memo lives in the render's `Ctx` (one render's lifetime) and is only used for layers that are part of the document being rendered: the document is borrowed for the whole render, so such a layer's address cannot be reused by another object (unlike the temporary clones made by `effects_source`, which keep taking the existing path). The cache key itself is the same function of the same inputs, so output is unchanged.

## Not covered

Other redundant work found in the same audit is left alone because open PRs rewrite the same code: the per-tile key in `masks.rs` `combined_mask` and `shape_split.rs` `split` (#2028, #3446, #3409), the outside-stroke buffer clones in `effects.rs` (#3650, #4231), and the backdrop/content re-renders in `advanced.rs` / `lib.rs` clipped-layer paths (#4040, #3193).

Tests: an equivalence test (tiled vs single-tile, cold vs warm, U8/U16/F32) and a counter test showing the identity is built once per layer per render instead of once per tile. No timing claims.

title: [Feature Request] Self-hosted cloud sync for workspace preferences and projects (SFTP, WebDAV, S3, other ?)
author: darkstudio
body:
Description:
💡 **Context & Vision**
Proprietary creative suites often lock collaboration, document storage, and profile synchronization behind their own closed cloud infrastructure.

To give the Craft suite (Photocraft, Vectorcraft, etc.) a major competitive edge while staying true to open-source principles, I propose adding a self-hosted, protocol-agnostic cloud synchronization system. This would allow users to connect their own storage infrastructure to sync workspace configurations, browse remote project files, and save directly to their private cloud.

🛠️ **Proposed Solution**
Integrate a Cloud / Remote Storage settings panel where users can configure their own server credentials:

Connection parameters: Server URL/Host, Port, Username, Password, or Key/Token (depending on the protocol chosen).

**Key Capabilities**:
Preferences & Workspace Sync (Opt-in checkboxes):

[x] Sync Preferences to Cloud (shortcuts, color themes, tool options).

[x] Sync Window & Panel Layout (workspace positions across different devices).

**Cloud Document Workflow**:

Open recent documents directly from the configured remote storage. 

Open document directly from configured remote storage on a custom dialog box (a dialog box that list cloud doculents).

For both dialog box: Possibility to switch documents presentation on different style (list,details, miniature).


Provide a choice in the Save / Save As dialog: Save Locally or Save to Cloud.

title: Select › Color Range: Skin Tones (and Detect Faces) are missing
author: switch87
body:
## What

Photoshop's **Select › Color Range** has a **Skin Tones** entry in its Select menu, with a **Detect Faces** checkbox. PhotoCraft's `select.colorRange` doesn't. The dialog leaves Skin Tones out on purpose (`crates/ui-egui/src/color_range_ui.rs`: "Skin Tones is left out: the engine has no skin-tone model"), and the engine refuses `{"select": "skinTones"}` as an unknown preset.

## Use case

Recolouring a garment on a model photo: select the shirt, then add a fill layer or Hue/Saturation. To take the skin out of a lasso selection you would subtract Skin Tones. The closest thing available today is subtracting `reds`. That keeps only half the skin out: the hue family is weighted by chroma, so the low-saturation skin shadows along the armholes stay selected and get recoloured with the shirt.

## Proposal

- `select.colorRange {"select": "skinTones"}`: a skin-tone model from published work (a chroma region in YCbCr, as in the skin-detection literature), not a hue family, with a soft luminance gate so near-black and near-white pixels drop out. **Fuzziness** widens or narrows the region, as it does for Sampled Colors. The selection modes, Invert and Sample All Layers work as they do for the other presets.
- The dialog gets the Skin Tones entry, with Fuzziness enabled.
- **Detect Faces** needs a face detector, which PhotoCraft doesn't have yet (that belongs with the local models of #2788 / #4098). Until then, `detectFaces: true` is refused with a message that says so, instead of being silently ignored. A later PR can add it on top.

I'm working on this.

title: Replace Color: Localized Color Clusters (and Range) are missing, so near-white backgrounds shift with a cream colour
author: switch87
body:
## What

Photoshop's **Image › Adjustments › Replace Color** has **Localized Color Clusters** with a **Range** slider, the same as Select › Color Range. With it on, a colour only matches near the places it was sampled, so the same colour elsewhere in the photo stays as it is. PhotoCraft's `image.adjustments.replaceColor` only takes `color`, `fuzziness`, `hue`, `saturation` and `lightness`: it matches the colour everywhere in the image. `select.colorRange` already has `localized`/`range` and positioned eyedropper samples (`points`), so the algorithm is there.

## Repro

`photocraft-cli` 0.7.0. The photo is a product shot of a man in a cream (`#E7E1CA`) mesh tank top on a near-white (`#FCFDF7`) background:

```
photocraft-cli run arm_2.png --cmd image.adjustments.replaceColor \
  --params '{"color":"#E7E1CA","fuzziness":150,"hue":180,"saturation":80}' --out x.png
```

The shirt turns blue as intended, but the background shifts as well. In a 150×600 strip of pure background left of the model, 1,636 of 90,000 pixels change at Fuzziness 150 and 943 at Fuzziness 100. The skin goes grey-blue too. Lowering Fuzziness keeps the background, but then the shirt's shadowed folds stay cream. A localized match (sampled on the shirt) is the way out of that trade-off, as it is in Photoshop.

(I checked that an active selection is respected: with the left half selected, the right half is unchanged pixel for pixel. That part works.)

## Proposal

- Engine: `replaceColor` takes the Color Range sampling params: `points` (eyedropper positions), plus `localized: bool = false` and `range: 0..100 = 100`, with the same meaning and code as in `select.colorRange`. Without `points` the colour is matched everywhere as today, so automation that sends only `color` is unchanged.
- Dialog: Localized Color Clusters and Range, using the canvas eyedropper from #4247 (which records where the colour was picked). I'll do the engine part first and the dialog part once #4247 is in, so the two don't conflict.…

title: Add an enable checkbox to Smoothing in Brush Settings
author: artcraftfan1
body:
## Summary

Add an enable checkbox to the **Smoothing** section in the Brush Settings panel, matching the behavior of other toggleable brush-setting sections in Photoshop.

Currently, Smoothing is configured without an enable checkbox (`SECTIONS` marks it as `false`), so users cannot toggle it on or off through the section list in the same way as other settings.

## Expected behavior

- [ ] Smoothing displays an enable checkbox in the Brush Settings section list.
- [ ] Clicking the checkbox toggles Smoothing on or off.
- [ ] Clicking the Smoothing row follows the panel's existing interaction rules, keeping section selection and enable-state toggling consistent.
- [ ] The checkbox accurately reflects whether Smoothing is enabled.
- [ ] Existing Smoothing settings are preserved when toggling the section off and back on, consistent with other brush-setting sections.

## Implementation notes

- Check the `SECTIONS` definition and section-list rendering in `crates/ui-egui/src/brush_panel.rs`.
- Inspect how other sections define and render their enable checkboxes.
- Ensure the change works with the existing brush-settings state and persistence behavior.
- Keep the implementation compatible with the project's native and WebAssembly builds.

## Acceptance criteria

- Smoothing has a visible, functional enable checkbox.
- Toggling the checkbox updates the enabled state correctly.
- The options pane reflects the enabled state.
- No regressions to other brush-setting sections.
- Relevant tests pass.

## Scope

This issue covers adding the Smoothing enable checkbox and its expected toggle behavior. Brush-specific disabled states and other Photoshop-parity improvements can be handled separately.

title: Brush Settings: Improve Pressed-State Feedback for List Items
author: artcraftfan1
body:
## Overview

PhotoCraft currently lacks some of the visual feedback Photoshop provides when interacting with checkbox-based entries in the Brush Settings panel.

Although selecting and focusing list entries works correctly, the absence of a visible pressed state makes interactions feel less responsive and reduces visual parity with Photoshop.

This issue investigates whether that feedback can be reproduced within PhotoCraft's existing UI and theming architecture.

## Observed Behavior

### 1. Clicking an Already-Selected Element

| Interaction | Photoshop | PhotoCraft |
|---|---|---|
| Click an already-selected element | The checkbox darkens slightly, indicating that it is interactive. | No visible feedback occurs. |

### 2. Pressing a List Entry

| Interaction | Photoshop | PhotoCraft |
|---|---|---|
| Mouse-down | The checkbox mark darkens to indicate a pressed state. | No visual indication is shown. |
| Mouse release | The checkbox is checked, and the corresponding list entry receives focus. | The checkbox is toggled, and the corresponding list entry receives focus correctly. |

The primary discrepancy is therefore **visual feedback during interaction**, rather than the underlying selection or focus behavior.

### 3. On the go-ahead

There are four distinct Checkbox states. The label text stays the same.
Unselected: The checkbox is unselected.
Unselected and pressed: The checkbox shows the unselected look, but a bit darker.
Selected: The checkbox is selected.
Selected and pressed: The checkbox shows the selected look, but a bit less opaque.

Pressing the label counts as pressing the checkbox. The label text doesn't change.

## Key Consideration: Theme Integration

In Photoshop, checkbox darkening when its label is pressed appears to be part of a broader theming and interaction-state behavior. It is not necessarily a special effect implemented specifically for the Brush Settings panel.

Matching this behavior in PhotoCraft may require integration with shared UI co…

title: Preserve full filenames in document tabs instead of truncating them
author: egofree71
body: When many documents are open, PhotoCraft aggressively shrinks the visible document tabs, causing filenames to become heavily truncated (e.g. `clip...`, `cmy...`, `emp...`). This makes it difficult to identify and switch between documents, especially when several filenames share the same prefix. Although hovering over a tab displays the full filename in a tooltip, having to inspect tabs individually is inconvenient. ### Current behavior - PhotoCraft reduces tab widths significantly when many documents are open. - Filenames become heavily truncated and difficult to distinguish. - Some documents are already moved to the overflow menu (`»`). - The **Window** menu provides a complete list of all open documents. ### Expected behavior I suggest following Photoshop's approach: - **Never truncate document tab filenames.** Keep their full names visible. - When there is insufficient horizontal space, hide additional tabs rather than shrinking the visible ones. - Always keep the active document's tab visible. - Display **all open documents** in the overflow menu (`»`), not only the hidden ones, as Photoshop does. The last point would complement the existing **Window** menu by providing a more convenient way to switch between documents directly from the tab bar. ### Why this matters Document tabs should allow users to identify files at a glance. Showing fewer tabs with readable filenames is more useful than showing many tabs with labels that are too truncated to distinguish. PhotoCraft already has the necessary overflow mechanism, so this would primarily be an improvement to the existing tab layout and overflow behavior. ### Screenshots - PhotoCraft: heavily truncated document tab names. - Photoshop: readable document tab names and a complete document list in the overflow menu.

title: GPU canvas: refreshes on DX12 take 2–3× as long as on Vulkan (cause not yet known)
author: FinnNk
body:
**What happens:** on DX12, the default backend on Windows (`gpu_startup.rs`), every GPU canvas refresh regenerates the display mips through scratch textures (`gpu_canvas.rs` `regenerate_mips`, the `res.separate_mip_targets` branch):
- one is created per display tile and per mip level, each the **whole level's size**;
- each is then cleared in full, although only the damaged rectangle is drawn and copied back.

Level 1 of an 8192² display tile is 4096², which is 64 MiB at RGBA8 or 128 MiB at RGBA16F.

The separate targets exist because "some Intel DX12 drivers corrupt reduced previews when both are mip levels of the same texture". But the flag is set for every DX12 adapter:

```rust
res.separate_mip_targets = rs.adapter.get_info().backend == wgpu::Backend::Dx12;
```

This runs after every refresh (each brush dab, slider tick and Move frame) on every Windows machine using DX12.

**Measured:** release `perf_scenarios` on `main` at `d43db3e1`, on an RTX 4090 laptop. The same exe was run with `WGPU_BACKEND` switched, two alternating runs each, 15 reps. The machine was under other load, so allow ±30 %.

| Row | Vulkan p50 | DX12 p50 | Peak RSS, Vulkan → DX12 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Brush dab, 16-bit 15000×10000 | 1.64 / 3.52 ms | 5.28 / 5.14 ms | 204 → 726 MB |
| Brush dab, 32-bit, 20 layers | 3.20 / 3.72 ms | 7.39 / 7.17 ms | 553 → 1202 MB |

I haven't yet measured how much of that gap the scratch textures account for; part of it may be general DX12 overhead. I'll measure it with the workaround disabled before changing anything.

**Proposed fix:** size each scratch texture to the damaged rectangle at its level, since the copies are already per rectangle. Alternatively, keep one pooled scratch texture per level and format, so it isn't allocated and cleared in full on every refresh. Either way the separate-resource property the Intel workaround needs is kept, so output is unchanged.

I'm working on a fix and will open a PR.

title: Edit › Copy reads the copied area into f32 and rebuilds every tile instead of sharing them
author: FinnNk
body:
**What happens:** Edit › Copy, and Layer via Copy / Cut with a selection, build the clipboard surface in `edit_cmds.rs` `lift` like this:
1. read the whole copied area into an `f32` buffer (`allocation::read_region(src, area, …)`);
2. multiply in an `f32` read of the selection, when there is one;
3. write everything back into new tiles.

That is 16 bytes per RGBA pixel (about 366 MiB at 24 MP), plus the mask. The clipboard then shares no tiles with the layer, although tiles are `Arc`-shared copy-on-write and fully selected tiles are already shared.

Paste is already cheap: with zero offset it clones the clip.

**Measured:** a probe calling the commands on `main` at `d43db3e1`, on a 6000×4000 RGBA8 full layer, release build, 7 reps, Windows. The machine was under other load, so allow ±30 %.

| Operation | p50 |
|---|---|
| Copy, no selection | 349 ms |
| Copy, Select All | 643 ms (419–694) |
| Paste, for comparison | 0.19 ms |

The transient peak is about 460 MiB (estimated from the buffer sizes). The clipboard also keeps a separate full copy that history accounting doesn't count.

**Proposed fix:** build the clip tile by tile.
- Reuse the source `Arc<Tile>` where there is no selection, or the selection tile is fully selected, and the source tile already has the clip's format.
- Skip fully unselected tiles.
- Compute only the partially selected edge tiles.
- Convert opaque (no-alpha) sources one tile at a time.

The clip comes out pixel-identical, so Paste and Paste in Place are unchanged.

I'm working on a fix and will open a PR.

title: Fill, Stroke and Clear copy tiles outside the selection, inflating every history step
author: FinnNk
body:
**What happens:** `fill_cmds.rs` `blend_into` serves Edit › Fill, Edit › Stroke, Clear on a channel and its other callers. It takes every tile in the selection's bounding box and runs each one through `Arc::try_unwrap` or a clone, then `blend_tile` and `Arc::new`.

The only short-cut is for a solid colour that fully covers a tile. A tile whose selection mask is entirely zero is still deep-copied. History keeps the old document, so `try_unwrap` always fails. Every step therefore stores duplicates of tiles it didn't change.

**Measured:** a probe on `main` at `d43db3e1`, release build, Windows.

- **Edit › Stroke 4 px on Select All, on a full 20 MP layer:** +82.5 MB of retained pixel memory, and 555 ms. The stroke only touches the ring of about 74 boundary tiles, roughly 18.5 MB at 256 KiB per tile. So about 64 MB per step is duplicates (estimated from the tile grid, 22 × 15 tiles).
- **Fill of a 4000×3000 ellipse:** +26 MB. Here the waste is the corner tiles.

**Proposed fix:** in `blend_into`'s per-tile closure, keep the original `Arc` when the tile's selection mask is entirely zero, or when the blend can't change it. This mirrors how fully covered solid tiles are already handled. Output is identical, and both the history steps and the time spent shrink.

I'm working on a fix and will open a PR.

title: Navigator and Channels thumbnails run full-resolution CPU composites on the UI thread after edits
author: FinnNk
body:
**What happens:** even with the GPU canvas, two panels still composite the document on the CPU, on the UI thread, after edits.

- **Navigator** (`canvas.rs` `navigator_texture`):
  - A one-step edit with known damage calls `compose::render_reduced_damage`. That composites the whole damage rectangle at full resolution, then averages it down to 512 px.
  - Any other step calls `thumbnail_buffer(doc, 512)`. It uses a proxy only when `proxy_faithful(doc)` holds, so any layer effect or vector mask means a full-document, full-resolution CPU composite.
- **Channels** (`lib.rs` `channel_thumbs`):
  - It is keyed by the document snapshot, so every edit rebuilds the composite with `compose::thumbnail(&doc, 56)`. That includes selection-only steps such as a marquee or Deselect.
  - Each rebuild allocates new textures with `load_texture` instead of updating the existing ones.

Both panels are off by default, but many Photoshop users keep them open.

**Measured:** a probe on `main` at `d43db3e1`, using the #209 layered document (5472×3648), release build, Windows. Allow ±30 % for noise from other load.

| Operation | p50 |
|---|---|
| Navigator update after an opacity change on one styled panel (damage 1428×1276) | 126–137 ms |
| Navigator update after an opacity change on a full-canvas layer | 700 ms |
| Navigator full rebuild, `thumbnail_buffer(512)` | 697 ms |
| Channels `thumbnail(56)` (the document has effects, so no proxy) | 659 ms |

The canvas itself does the same opacity edit in 3.4 ms on the GPU. So with either panel open, the UI thread spends far longer on the thumbnail than on the edit. With Channels open, a marquee drag and release costs about 0.66 s.

**Proposed fix**, in steps:
1. **Channels:** rebuild only when pixels change (`layer_multi_cmds::same_pixels`), so selection-only steps reuse the image, and update the existing textures instead of loading new ones. Output is identical.
2. **Navigator, and the Channels composite, on the GPU canvas:** derive the image f…

title: Launch and preference changes can block the UI thread on the system font scan
author: FinnNk
body:
**What happens:** `Session::apply_prefs` (`engine/src/prefs.rs`) sets the text engine's missing-glyph protection through `photocraft_text::shared().lock()`. `shared()` is `SHARED.get_or_init(new_shared)`. Its own documentation says the first call scans the installed fonts and blocks until the scan is done, and that per-frame code should use `try_shared` instead.

`apply_prefs` runs:
- at launch, when a preferences file exists, while the background `warm_fonts` scan started in `apps/photocraft/src/main.rs` is still running;
- on every preferences change.

On a machine with many fonts, the first frame can therefore wait for the rest of the scan.

**Impact:** estimated, not yet measured. The wait is whatever remains of the font scan at that point: typically hundreds of milliseconds to seconds on Windows with 1–3k fonts, and much longer on some Macs, according to the code's comments. I'll measure a real launch before and after the fix.

**Proposed fix:** use `try_shared()`. When the engine isn't ready yet, keep the setting pending and apply it when the scan finishes, in `new_shared`. Guard the pending value with a mutex so a late change isn't lost. The setting behaves exactly as before; only the moment it's applied changes.

I'm working on a fix and will open a PR.

title: Touch-Screens in Brush Mode: One finger, two fingers not detected.
author: leafnie
body:
In programs like Krita and Photoshop, one or two finger input on a touch screen will behave like so:

Krita:
- One Finger: Drags the canvas around.
- Two Fingers: Drags, zooms, and rotates canvas simultaneously.

PS 26 Default Settings:
- One finger: Nothing
- Two Fingers: Drags and zooms simultaneously. Rotation requires a certain finger gesture. Feels clumsy.

While in brush mode, Photocraft currently does this:

- Two Fingers: Zooms, no dragging, and draws on one of the fingers, all at once.

title: Add DDS (DirectDraw Surface) import/export support
author: bennybullTT
body:
Summary
Add support for opening and saving DirectDraw Surface (.dds) files.

Use case
DDS is the standard texture format for game development and modding. Right now I have to convert DDS files with a separate tool before I can edit them in PhotoCraft, and convert them back afterwards. Photoshop handles this through the NVIDIA Texture Tools plugin.

Proposed behavior

title: Duotone and live-adjust previews deep-clone the document several times per frame
author: FinnNk
body:
**What happens:** `canvas.rs` `display_doc` runs 3–4 times per frame, from `navigator_texture`, `ensure_texture`, `ensure_gpu` and `draw_beyond_canvas`. It deep-clones the document in two cases:

- **Duotone documents:** `canvas.rs:1075` → `mode_cmds.rs:528-533` clones the document on every call, before any cache check. This happens on every frame, even though the result is keyed by a constant.
- **Live adjustment previews:** `canvas.rs:1061-1072` does `(*st.doc).clone()` on every call while an adjustment slider is being dragged.

Cloning a `Document` rebuilds every layer's tile `BTreeMap` (an atomic increment per tile, no pixel copy). It also deep-clones groups' children, and copies owned blobs such as XMP.

Two panels also clone a layer every frame just to read a couple of fields:
- `channels_panel.rs:66` clones the active layer when it has a mask (a whole subtree for a masked group), but only uses its `id` and `mask`.
- `panels.rs:3177` clones an adjustment layer while Properties shows it, but only reads `visible` and `clipped`.

`prefs_ui.rs:598` also walks every layer each frame (`link_watch::linked_files`, a path `Vec` per layer), to find links in the active document.

**Impact:** estimated from the code. The cost is O(layers × tiles) per clone, three to four times per frame, on Duotone documents and during every adjustment drag. That's up to milliseconds per frame on large layered documents.

**Proposed fix:**
- Memoise the Duotone and live-adjust display documents per (document id, revision, preview parameters), and share the `Arc`.
- Borrow instead of cloning in the two panels.
- Cache the link scan per revision.

Output is unchanged.

I'm working on a fix and will open a PR.

title: Info panel recomposites every colour sampler through the command dispatcher on every frame
author: FinnNk
body:
**What happens:** while the Info tab is visible, `panels.rs:1771` runs `session.execute("view.colorSamplers.list")` on every redraw. Each sampler goes through `sample_cmds::sample_color` → `photocraft_compose::render(doc, 1×1)`. That composites one pixel through the whole layer stack, with a fresh pattern set and `Ctx`, plus the full command-dispatch overhead (parameter clone, preconditions, `catch_unwind`). There can be up to 10 samplers, and nothing is cached by revision.

Layers with local effects make it worse: each 1-pixel render builds its own clipped effect-map entry, which also crowds the global effect cache.

**Impact:** estimated. Tens of microseconds per sampler per frame normally; more with effects, and the effect cache gets polluted.

**Proposed fix:** cache the readouts per (document id, revision, sampler points, display settings), and call the readout function directly rather than dispatching a command each frame. Output is unchanged.

I'm working on a fix and will open a PR.

title: GPU compositor can keep a closed document's pages and effect maps resident
author: FinnNk
body:
**What happens:** `GpuCanvas::retain` (`gpu_canvas.rs:637-650`) frees compositor memory for closed documents by calling `forget_doc`. It only does so for ids still in `res.docs`. Three paths remove a document's `res.docs` entry while keeping the compositor and whatever it already uploaded:
- line 442: `DocTextures::new` failed;
- line 513: a fresh render failed with a non-fault error after uploading pages;
- line 539: the document no longer fits the canvas budget, for example after Canvas Size grows a document that was already composited.

If the document is then closed, its resident pages, effect maps and lower-stack cache entries are never released. They are only evicted when another document pushes the budgets over (`gpu/lib.rs:1014-1057`). With no other GPU document in use, they stay resident indefinitely.

(The panic path at line 497 is not affected: it drops the whole compositor.)

**Impact:** estimated. Up to the resident budget, potentially GBs of VRAM, after closing a large document that went down one of those paths.

**Proposed fix:** add `Compositor::retain_docs(live)`, which drops residents, effect maps and prefix entries of documents that aren't open, and call it from `GpuCanvas::retain`.

I'm working on a fix and will open a PR.

title: Memory outside every budget: pinned effect-cache layers, the shape split cache and History snapshots
author: FinnNk
body:
Three caches hold pixels that no memory budget counts and, in two cases, that Purge doesn't free:

1. **Effect cache pins whole layers** (`compose/lib.rs:1573`, `FxEntry { maps, _pin: layer.clone(), bytes }`). `bytes` counts only the maps. After the layer is edited, the pinned old tiles stay alive until the entry is evicted. For a group with effects, the pin is a deep clone of the subtree. Purge All does clear it.
2. **Shape stroke-split cache** (`compose/shape_split.rs:20-66`). It holds up to 32 entries, each with two canvas-size surfaces plus the pinned shape cache. It has no byte cap, and Purge doesn't clear it (`edit_menu_cmds.rs:261-276` purges only the effect, mask and smart caches). At 24 MP, 32 entries can reach GBs.
3. **History panel snapshots** (`history_cmds.rs:24-30`, stored in `DocState::snapshots`). The number of snapshots is unlimited, they aren't counted in `History::pixel_bytes` or trimmed, and Purge doesn't free them. A "Merged Layers" snapshot is a full flattened copy.

**Impact:** estimated. Memory use can grow beyond the configured budgets without showing in the memory readout, worst on large documents with stroked shapes or many snapshots.

**Proposed fix:**
- Count the effect cache's pinned bytes, or pin only what is needed.
- Give the shape split cache a byte cap and a Purge hook.
- Count snapshot-only tiles in the history readout, using the existing seen-set approach so shared tiles aren't double-counted.

I'm working on a fix and will open a PR.

title: Mode and depth conversion un-share copy-on-write tiles
author: FinnNk
body:
**What happens:** `Surface::map_color` and `convert` / `try_convert` (`raster/lib.rs:737-801`) convert per tile coordinate through `tile_mut`. ICC mode conversion (`color_cmds::convert_surface`, `color_cmds.rs:553-580`) does the same, plus a staging buffer the size of all the tiles.

A tile shared across many coordinates, such as a `fill_rect` background where every tile is one `Arc`, is therefore converted and stored once per coordinate.

**Impact:** estimated from the tile counts. Converting a white 24 MP background turns one shared tile into 384 separate tiles: +96 / 192 / 384 MiB at 8 / 16 / 32-bit. For a very large canvas filled with `fill_rect`, conversion can explode memory. It happens on every Image › Mode or bit-depth change.

**Proposed fix:** group tile coordinates by `Arc` identity, convert each distinct tile once, and insert the same `Arc` at every coordinate. The GPU upload already does this (`gpu/lib.rs` `convert_tiles`). Output is unchanged.

I'm working on a fix and will open a PR.

title: Lasso and polygon selections build full-canvas f32 masks
author: FinnNk
body:
**What happens:** `polygon_selection` (`selection_cmds.rs:588-602`) rasterises lasso and polygon selections over `doc.bounds()`. `sel::polygon` allocates a `w × h` f32 mask (`algo/selection.rs:770-772`), and the optional feather runs over the whole canvas. Add, Subtract and Intersect then read the previous selection into a second full-canvas f32 buffer before `combine` (`selection.rs:138-157`). That's about 96 MB per buffer at 24 MP, whatever the polygon's size.

#3959, merged as 63fd5ec7, sped up the edge scan and says the full-document mask allocation remains.

**Measured:** 60.8 ms p50 for a 2000-point lasso spanning 400 px on a 20 MP document (`main` at `d43db3e1`, before #3959).

**Proposed fix:** rasterise within the polygon's bounding box, inflated by 1 px plus the feather radius, and combine through the existing `combine_region` (`selection.rs:374`, already used by marquee selections). The aim is the same mask; the edges at the bounding box will be checked against the current result.

I'm working on a fix and will open a PR.

title: Filters applied through a selection look up the selection one pixel at a time
author: FinnNk
body:
**What happens:** `mix_selection` (`algo/lib.rs:1207-1241`) calls `sel.pixel(x, y)[0]` for every output pixel. `Surface::pixel` (`raster/lib.rs:278-282`) allocates a `Vec` and does a tile `BTreeMap` lookup each time. Its callers are the tiled filter paths (`algo/lib.rs:1098, 1182`) and Motion Blur (`blur/motion_apply.rs:172`).

**Impact:** estimated. One allocation plus one map lookup per pixel is about 24 million at 24 MP, plausibly hundreds of ms on every filter applied with an active selection.

**Proposed fix:** read the selection once per tile into a buffer (`read_region_into`) and index it, the same way the original pixels are already read. Output is unchanged.

I'm working on a fix and will open a PR.

title: Brush strokes clone the brush settings, including sampled tip bitmaps, on every pointer event
author: FinnNk
body:
**What happens:** `StrokeRenderer::tail_preview` (`paint/render.rs:835-877`) clones `self.generator` before checking whether there's anything to draw. It then clones `self.ctx`. Both hold a `BrushSettings`: in `DabBuilder`, in the optional `DualBuilder` (`dynamics.rs:456-457, 590-591`), and in `BrushContext` (`render.rs:147-152`).

A sampled tip is `TipShape::Sampled(GrayTile { data: Vec<u16> })` (`brush.rs:85`), so a large sampled or dual brush copies its tip bitmaps two to four times per pointer push. Callers are `brush_cmds.rs:602` (each push), `retouch_cmds.rs:418`, `render.rs:666` and `stroke_trail.rs:96`.

#2379 makes stroke rendering faster and skips the tail on alternate pushes, but doesn't remove the clone.

**Impact:** estimated. Several MB copied per pointer event for large sampled tips (a 2500² tip is about 12 MB), on the hot path of every stroke.

**Proposed fix:** hold tip bitmaps behind an `Arc` (or the settings as `Arc<BrushSettings>`) in the builders and context, so the clones are pointer copies. Output is unchanged.

I'm working on a fix and will open a PR.

title: XMP and raw PSD blobs are deep-copied on every edit and history state
author: FinnNk
body:
**What happens:** `Metadata.xmp: Option<String>` (`doc/lib.rs:818`), `Duotone.psd_raw: Option<Vec<u8>>` (`doc/mode.rs:61`) and `Adjustment::Unsupported { raw: Vec<u8> }` (`doc/adjust.rs:285-288`) are owned buffers. Their siblings (`exif`, `psd_resources`, the layer `psd_raw`) are already `Arc`.

Every `Session::edit` clones the document, and history keeps one document per state. An XMP packet (hundreds of KB to MBs in files with long DocumentAncestors lists) is therefore duplicated per history state without being counted, and per frame by the Duotone preview clone.

**Impact:** estimated. Negligible for most files; MBs × history states for files carrying large XMP.

**Proposed fix:** store them as `Arc<str>` / `Arc<[u8]>` like their siblings. Behaviour is unchanged.

I'm working on a fix and will open a PR.

title: GPU memory budget ignores the GPU's own memory
author: FinnNk
body:
**What happens:** the GPU canvas budget (`gpu_canvas.rs:1142-1157`) comes from system RAM: `memory_budget` is the Memory Usage allowance minus the active document's pixels, capped at RAM / 4 and floored at 512 MB; `canvas_budget` is RAM / 4. Nothing looks at the adapter's own memory.

On a discrete GPU with less VRAM than a quarter of system RAM (an 8 GB card in a 64 GB machine, say), the compositor can plan for more resident data than the card holds. The driver then over-commits and pages instead of the compositor evicting in a controlled way.

(#3814 covers the history budget and detecting RAM. Its Windows RAM-detection point is already fixed on `main` by #3189, `detect_physical_memory` with `GlobalMemoryStatusEx`. It doesn't cover VRAM.)

**Impact:** estimated. Stutter or driver paging on mid-range discrete GPUs with large documents, instead of the compositor's own eviction.

**Proposed fix:** clamp the budgets by the adapter's memory where the platform reports it:
- DXGI `QueryVideoMemoryInfo` on Windows;
- `recommendedMaxWorkingSetSize` on Metal;
- `VK_EXT_memory_budget` on Vulkan.

Keep the RAM-based value where none is available. wgpu has no portable query, so this needs small platform-specific code.

I'm working on a fix and will open a PR.

title: Select › Sky selects a plain white or light-grey studio background as overcast sky
author: switch87
body:
## What

`select.sky` selects a near-white product or studio background as sky, even though the photo has no sky. Its colour prior counts *bright and nearly neutral* as overcast sky (`segment/sky.rs`, `colour_prior`'s `white` term). A seamless backdrop starts at the top edge, so it seeds the region growing and floods the whole background. `photocraft-cli` on `main` (`select.sky` → `{"coverage": 0.79}`) with a 300×200 image of a dark disc on `#F2F2F0`:

```
photocraft-cli run white_bg.png --cmd select.sky
```

Photoshop's Select › Sky leaves such a photo unselected.

## Proposal

A sky doesn't reach the bottom of a photo, but a backdrop does. When the region found also covers most of the bottom rows **and** is nearly neutral in colour (an overcast-looking white or grey, not a blue sky), treat it as a background and select nothing. Blue sky that reaches down, as in a photo taken upward, is unaffected.

I'm working on this.

title: PSD/PSB save: 16-bit files include padding in the Lr16 length, so Unity PSD Importer fails ("Incorrect length for InfoLayers")
author: sun-studios
body:
## Summary

When PhotoCraft saves a **16-bit** document as PSD or PSB, the length field of the `Lr16` tagged block includes its trailing padding bytes. Photoshop writes that length unpadded and pads *after* the block. Readers that check the block length exactly, such as Unity's 2D PSD Importer, reject the file and lose every layer.

8-bit saves are not affected. Their layers go in the regular Layer Info section, where padding inside the length is normal.

## Environment

- PhotoCraft 0.8.2 (Windows 10; reproduced with both `photocraft.exe` and `photocraft-cli.exe`)
- Unity 6000.3.22f1 with `com.unity.2d.psdimporter` 12.0.2

## Reproduction (no source file needed)

```sh
photocraft-cli run --new '{"width":64,"height":48,"depth":16,"mode":"rgb","background":"transparent"}' \
  --cmd layer.new.layer --cmd edit.fill --params '{"use":"foreground"}' \
  --cmd layer.new.group --out repro16.psd
```

| Output | Where the layers are | Declared length | Actual layer data | Padding inside the length |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `repro16.psd` | `Lr16` block | 1528 | 1526 | 2 bytes ❌ |
| `repro16.psb` | `Lr16` block | 1976 | 1974 | 2 bytes ❌ |
| `repro8.psd` / `repro8.psb` | Layer Info section | (padded) | — | fine (this is allowed there) |

"Actual layer data" means the layer count, the layer records and all channel image data.

A real 16-bit PSB character rig saved by PhotoCraft fails to import in Unity:

```
Failed to import file Assets/<…>.psb. Error: Incorrect length for InfoLayers.
  at PhotoshopFile.InfoLayers..ctor (...) in .\Library\PackageCache\com.unity.2d.psdimporter@…\Editor\PSDPlugin\PsdFile\Layers\LayerInfo\InfoLayers.cs:85
  at PhotoshopFile.LayerInfoFactory.Load (...) in ...\PsdFile\Layers\LayerInfo.cs:62
  at PhotoshopFile.PsdFile.LoadLayerAndMaskInfo (...) in ...\PsdFile\PsdFile.cs:361
```

Unity bundles the Paint.NET PSD plugin as its reader. That reader loads the layers from `Lr16`, then requires the stream position to equal `start + length` exactly. Its own com…
