title: Layer comps lose their appearance (blend mode, opacity) in PSD and layered TIFF
author: switch87
body:
## What

A layer comp's **Appearance** (blend mode, opacity, and layer style) survives a `.pcraft` save but not PSD or layered TIFF. After a round trip, applying a comp brings back each layer's visibility and position, but not its blend mode or opacity. `crates/io/src/comps_map.rs` says so itself: "comp appearance is not written to PSD; `.pcraft` keeps it". Its `cmls` `layerSettings` writes only `enab` and `Ofst`.

## Repro (`photocraft-cli`, current `main`)

```
photocraft-cli run --new '{"width":64,"height":64}' --cmd layer.new.layer \
  --cmd layer.setProps --params '{"blend":"multiply","opacity":0.4}' --cmd layerComp.new --params '{"name":"A"}' \
  --cmd layer.setProps --params '{"blend":"normal","opacity":1}'    --cmd layerComp.new --params '{"name":"B"}' \
  --out c.psd          # or c.pcraft, or c.tif --tiff-layers
photocraft-cli run c.psd --cmd layerComp.apply --params '{"comp":"A"}' --out a.pcraft
photocraft-cli info a.pcraft
```

| saved as | Layer 1 after applying comp A |
|---|---|
| `.pcraft` | Multiply, 0.4 |
| `.psd` | Normal, 1.0 |
| `.tif --tiff-layers` | Normal, 1.0 |

## What it needs

The keys Photoshop uses for a comp's appearance in a layer's `cmls` `layerSettings` (next to `enab`/`Ofst`) aren't in the public PSD specification. A Photoshop-authored oracle in **photocraft-corpus** would let this be done properly and tested: one layer with different blend modes, opacities, fill opacities and a layer style across two or three comps captured with *Appearance* on. I haven't claimed this, since it needs that file first.

title: Content-Aware Fill / Move leave a tinted blotch in a smooth gradient (Color Adaptation default and high)
author: switch87
body:
## What

Filling a hole in a smooth vertical gradient (a clear sky: each row one colour) leaves a visible **tinted blotch**, purple and green, even though copying rows unchanged would be invisible. It happens at Color Adaptation **Default** and **High**; **None** and **Very High** are clean. Measured on current `main` with a 400×120 sky gradient and a 60×40 selection:

| Color Adaptation | worst channel error in the fill (of 255) |
|---|---|
| None | 0 |
| Default | 14 |
| High | 27 |
| Very High | 1 |

## Cause

`inpaint::fit` fits each channel as `gain · source + bias`. The gain is the ratio of the patches' standard deviations, clamped to the level's range, and the bias is then clamped to `±bias`. On a nearly flat patch that ratio is noise, so the gain often sits at its limit (1.1 for Default). Because the gain scales about zero, it moves a bright mean (≈ 0.7) by ≈ 0.07, more than Default's ±0.04 bias can bring back. Each channel ends up off by a different amount, and that is the tint. Very High's ±0.14 bias happens to cover it.

I'm working on this. (#1366 is about Content-Aware Fill's quality in general; this is one specific, measurable artefact.)

title: macOS: droplets can't run because `photocraft-cli` isn't included in the app
author: Brad-Toms
body:
**Version:** PhotoCraft 0.8.2 (macOS, [your macOS version], iMac)

**Problem**
File → Automate → Create Droplet writes a `.pcdroplet` file and a `.command` file. The `.command` runs:

    exec "${PHOTOCRAFT_CLI:-photocraft-cli}" droplet '/path/to/X.pcdroplet' "$@"

The macOS build doesn't include `photocraft-cli`. `which photocraft-cli` returns "not found", and PhotoCraft.app/Contents/MacOS only contains the `PhotoCraft` binary. So the droplet can't run at all.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Record an action (for example Fit Image followed by Canvas Size).
2. File → Automate → Create Droplet, with the output set to a writable folder.
3. Double-click the generated `.command`, or drop images onto it.
4. Result: `photocraft-cli: command not found`.

**Expected**
Droplets run on macOS. Ideally they'd be generated as a small `.app`, like Photoshop droplets, so you can drag and drop images onto them in Finder. Finder won't accept drops on a `.command` file even when the CLI is installed.

**Other issues found along the way**
- **Unwritable default paths:** Create Droplet defaults to the relative paths `./Name.pcdroplet` and `./droplet-output`. On macOS they resolve to a read-only location, and saving fails with `Read-only file system (os error 30)`. Defaulting to an absolute path, such as ~/Desktop or ~/Documents, would avoid this.
- **Quick Export breaks Batch:** a recorded `file.export.quickExport` step is saved with empty params (`{}`). In Batch it makes the run stop with no output and no obvious error. With the step disabled, Batch works fine.

title: [Feature] Bidirectional hover highlighting between Layers panel and Canvas (Photoshop parity)
author: safvanedge
body:
### Summary
In Photoshop, there is a smooth bidirectional visual connection between the Layers panel and the Canvas/Artboard during rollover/hover:
1. **Hovering a layer in the Layers panel** displays a bounding outline/box in the accent color around that layer on the canvas, allowing the user to immediately identify which canvas element corresponds to the hovered layer.
2. **Hovering a layer on the Canvas** (via Move Tool auto-select rollover) highlights the corresponding layer row in the Layers panel with a subtle fill overlay.
3. **Already selected layers** do not receive an extra overlay tint when hovered (they retain their clean selected appearance).
4. The hover overlay in the Layers panel uses a clean fill (no stroke border), matching Photoshop's modern flat UI aesthetics and design tokens.

### Proposed Behavior
- When moving the pointer over any unselected layer row in the Layers panel:
  - The row receives a subtle hover tint (`t.hover` + `t.accent` fill).
  - Its bounding box on the canvas is outlined with the blue accent stroke (`1.5 pt Outside`), irrespective of the currently selected tool.
- When hovering over an element on the canvas with Auto-Select rollover enabled:
  - The layer is outlined on the canvas (existing behavior).
  - The corresponding row in the Layers panel highlights simultaneously.
- If a layer is already selected, hovering over it does not draw an extraneous blue overlay over the selection background.

### Expected Parity
Matches Photoshop 2026's layer panel rollover and auto-select hover feedback.

### Status
I have implemented this feature locally following PhotoCraft's design tokens (`theme::Tokens`), clean-room guidelines, and added unit tests in `move_hover.rs` (3/3 tests passing). Ready to open a PR if the maintainers would like to have this!

title: Brush tool is choppy
author: Iron-Foot
body:
## Fast brush strokes render as polygons: dabs are placed along straight segments between input samples

**Summary**
Drawing quickly with the Brush turns curves into visible straight segments with corners. Slow strokes look fine. The same gesture in Photoshop stays a smooth curve at any speed. Same result with a Wacom tablet and the built-in trackpad.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. New canvas, Brush tool, default round brush, default Smoothing (10%)
2. Draw a fast circle or S-curve
3. Draw the same shape slowly and compare

**Expected:** a smooth curve regardless of speed.
**Actual:** a polyline; faster strokes give fewer, longer segments.

**Environment**
- PhotoCraft: main @ a7919b2
- MacBook Pro M4 Max, latest macOS, 120 Hz display
- Input: Wacom tablet and built-in trackpad (identical results)

**Cause (from the source)**

1. **Dabs are interpolated linearly between samples.** `PathWalker` walks a polyline: every dab between two input points is placed with `lerp_pt`, a straight-line interpolation ([dynamics.rs L262–L310](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/a7919b24e1a418d80f35ae98a02f603628e7753e/crates/paint/src/dynamics.rs#L262-L310)). The `Smoother` doesn't help either: both the exponential and pulled-string modes move along straight lines toward the pointer ([dynamics.rs L96–L120](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/a7919b24e1a418d80f35ae98a02f603628e7753e/crates/paint/src/dynamics.rs#L96-L120)). So any gap between samples becomes a straight segment, and fast strokes have big gaps.

2. **The sample rate is probably capped by macOS mouse coalescing.** The canvas already feeds every `PointerMoved` event from each frame to the tool ([canvas.rs L3268–L3311](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/a7919b24e1a418d80f35ae98a02f603628e7753e/crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs#L3268-L3311)), so PhotoCraft itself isn't dropping events. But AppKit coalesces mouse and tablet drag events by default, and nothing in the repo calls `NSEvent.setMouseCoalescingEna…

title: Layered TIFF: mixed-order TySh transforms become enormous or NaN; selecting/editing text corrupts rendering or crashes
author: TheSeanLavery
body:
A Photoshop-authored Intel-order layered TIFF initially looks correct in PhotoCraft, but selecting a text layer can change/disappear its text, and entering text editing can crash. The text affine matrix is decoded using the wrong byte order.

## Reproduction and environment

- macOS Apple Silicon, native PhotoCraft built from Sean's fork main `14c612c24b270ff62aaddd38bf64776c823f6003` (0.8.2).
- TIFF creator metadata: Adobe Photoshop 27.11 on Windows.
- 2550 × 3300 RGB8 at 300 DPI, 41 layer records, six editable type layers.
- Open the layered TIFF, select a type layer, then enter Edit Type.
- No source-file save or manual font-size edit was made.

The original artwork is private and is not attached. A synthetic regression fixture can reproduce the byte layout without distributing it.

## Measured cause

Its TIFF `TySh` blocks have a **little-endian version and six affine doubles, followed by a big-endian text version/descriptor, then little-endian warp version/descriptor and bounds** (offset 50: `00 32`; offset 52: `00 00 00 10`). The TIFF transcoder assumes the descriptor follows the container byte order; it fails at offset 60 and retains the block as foreign-order `MIB8` data.

The PSD importer then passes those retained bytes to `photocraft_text::psd::parse_tysh`, which reads the matrix as big-endian. The big-endian descriptor parses successfully, so correct text styles are combined with invalid geometry:

- One horizontal scale: valid `1.8054202887117468`, imported `1.315776645269349e62`.
- One rotated layer term: valid `-2.01242653341062`, imported `3.935562794632577e177`.
- Another matrix contains NaN; another has a term around `1.4759871577491642e307`.
- All six point sizes import correctly (48, 28.6443, 12.4723, 10.3170, etc.; `pxPerPt=4.1666665`). This is not a uniform DPI/font-size conversion error.

The saved Photoshop pixel caches hide the problem on open. Selecting the headline made it disappear, with `invalid parameters for type.setStyle: size must be…

title: PSD: Indexed Color, Bitmap and Duotone documents are not saved in their own mode
author: switch87
body:
I'm working on this; the PR follows right away.

## What

Saving an Indexed Color, Bitmap or Duotone document as PSD converts it: Indexed is written as RGB, and Bitmap and Duotone as Grayscale, each with a warning (`Indexed document written as Rgb`, …). A Duotone opened from a PSD loses its inks on the way back, although PhotoCraft keeps them (`Duotone::psd_raw`).

Repro on current `main`:

```
photocraft-cli run --new '{"width":32,"height":32}' --cmd image.mode.grayscale --cmd image.mode.duotone --out d.psd   # header mode 1 (Grayscale)
photocraft-cli run --new '{"width":32,"height":32}' --cmd image.mode.indexedColor --out i.psd                       # mode 3 (RGB), 3 channels
photocraft-cli run --new '{"width":32,"height":32}' --cmd image.mode.grayscale --cmd image.mode.bitmap --out b.psd  # mode 1, 8-bit
```

## What the PSD specification allows

- **Indexed (mode 2):** one plane of palette indices, with the Color Table as Color Mode Data (256 reds, 256 greens, 256 blues). Resource 1046 holds the table length and 1047 the transparent entry.
- **Bitmap (mode 0):** 1 bit per pixel, 1 = black.

Neither mode has layers in Photoshop. A Duotone's ink block is undocumented, but an imported one can be written back as it was, over the grey plate. A duotone whose inks were set in PhotoCraft has no such block and stays Grayscale for now.

title: CJK UI fallback uses NotoSansCJK-VF.ttc default Thin (100) so CJK looks thin
author: apicalshark
body:
### Summary
CJK glyphs in PhotoCraft UI (panels / layer names) look abnormally thin on Fedora when only the variable font is installed. Latin UI looks normal.

### Environment
- PhotoCraft `0.8.2 (d43db3e15, 2026-10-12)` from `/bin/photocraft`
- Fedora 44, GNOME 50, Wayland
- Fonts installed:
  - `google-noto-sans-cjk-vf-fonts-2.004-11.fc44` only
  - `google-noto-sans-cjk-fonts` (static) NOT installed
- `fc-list` only shows:
  - `/usr/share/fonts/google-noto-sans-cjk-vf-fonts/NotoSansCJK-VF.ttc`

### Steps to reproduce
1. On VF-only system, launch `photocraft`
2. Open any doc with CJK layer names / UI, e.g. `圖片`, `文件`
3. Compare CJK stroke weight vs Latin / vs GNOME / vs Chromium

### Actual
CJK renders at Thin weight.

Log (`~/.config/photocraft/logs/photocraft.log`):

> `photocraft_ui_egui::cjk_fonts: UI font fallback: registered /usr/share/fonts/google-noto-sans-cjk-vf-fonts/NotoSansCJK-VF.ttc (face 3) as system-cjk-0`

### Expected
CJK fallback renders at Regular (wght 400).

### Root cause
`crates/ui-egui/src/cjk_fonts.rs` loads the TTC file directly, bypassing fontconfig, in this probe order:

`.../google-noto-sans-cjk-fonts/NotoSansCJK-Regular.ttc` → `.../google-noto-sans-cjk-vf-fonts/NotoSansCJK-VF.ttc` → ...

On VF-only systems it picks `face 3` (= `Noto Sans CJK TC`) raw.

That VF has:

fvar: wght min 100, default 100, max 900
  Thin 100, Light 300, DemiLight 350, Regular 400, Medium 500, Bold 700, Black 900

verified with `fontTools.TTCollection`. `fc-query`:

index 3: "Noto Sans CJK TC" weight 0 (Thin)
index 262147 (0x40003): "Noto Sans CJK TC Regular" weight 80

fontconfig correctly instantiates `Regular`, but egui/epaint (`ab_glyph`/`fontdb` without variation instancing) rasterizes the default outlines = `Thin 100`.

Hence only CJK looks thin.

### Suggested fix
- Instantiate VF at `wght=400` when loading `NotoSansCJK-VF.ttc` (e.g. `fonttools varLib.instancer` / `fontdb` variation coords), or
- Prefer / bundle static `Regular`, or warn on VF-only syste…

title: Save for Web: JPEG uses 4:2:0 chroma up to quality 89; Photoshop switches to 4:4:4 above 50
author: switch87
body:
I'm working on this; the PR follows right away.

## What

Save for Web writes JPEG with 4:2:0 chroma subsampling up to quality 89 (`subsampled = quality < 90` in `crates/codecs/src/web.rs`). Photoshop's Save for Web switches to full 4:4:4 chroma above quality 50.

I measured this on Photoshop 2025 (26.5) by saving the same image at many qualities and reading the luma sampling factors in each file's SOF marker:

| | 4:2:0 | 4:4:4 |
|---|---|---|
| Save for Web, quality 0–100 | 0, 10, 20, 30, 40, 49, **50** | **51**, 60, 70, 80, 90, 100 |
| Save As, quality 0–12 | all of them | none |

So in PhotoCraft, the Save for Web presets "JPEG High" (60) and "JPEG Very High" (80) smear colour edges that Photoshop keeps sharp. File › Save As already matches Photoshop: 4:2:0 at every quality.

title: PhotoCraft does not restore saved window position on Linux Mint with multiple monitors
author: pixelmicke-cmyk
body:
# PhotoCraft does not restore saved window position on Linux Mint with multiple monitors

## Description

PhotoCraft saves its window position correctly in `ui.ron`, but does not restore that position when the application is restarted.

This happens on Linux Mint 22.3 Cinnamon with four monitors connected.

Other applications, such as Google Chrome, remember their window positions correctly.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start PhotoCraft.
2. Move its window to the desired monitor (monitor 3).
3. Close PhotoCraft normally.
4. Check the saved window position in `~/.config/photocraft/ui.ron`.
5. Restart PhotoCraft.
6. Check its actual window position using `wmctrl -lG`.

## Expected behavior

PhotoCraft should reopen on the same monitor and at approximately the same position where it was closed.

## Actual behavior

PhotoCraft opens at a different position, sometimes outside the visible screen area.

For example:

**Saved position after closing:**
```
outer_position_pixels:Some((x:2048.0,y:1228.0))
```

**Actual position after restarting:**
```
X=520, Y=300
```

The intended monitor starts at X=1920, Y=1080.

Manually repositioning PhotoCraft using `wmctrl` works correctly.

## System information

- OS: Linux Mint 22.3 Cinnamon
- Display system: X11
- GPU: NVIDIA
- Monitors: Four displays
- Window manager: Cinnamon/Muffin

## Relevant source code

In `apps/photocraft/src/main.rs`, the native window options include:

```rust
centered: true,
persistence_path: services::config_dir().map(|dir| dir.join("ui.ron")),
window_builder: Some(Box::new(restored_window)),
```

Could there be an interaction between the centered window setting, eframe's saved window geometry, and multi-monitor positioning on Linux?

The saved coordinates appear correct, but the window is not restored to those coordinates.

Thank you!

title: [Bug] Image dropped while another image is in Free Transform stays hidden until that transform is applied

body:
**Describe the bug**
When dragging and dropping image files into the document **one at a time**, a new image does not appear while the previous image is still in Free Transform. It only appears after the previous Free Transform is applied with Enter.

For example, when dropping 3 files in separate drops:

- Image 2 does not appear until Free Transform of image 1 is applied

Either of the following would be reasonable:

title: Background layer takes an opacity, blend mode and (via Select and Mask) a layer mask
author: switch87
body:
I'm working on this; the PR follows right away.

## What

The Background layer takes an opacity, fill opacity and blend mode through `layer.setProps`, and a layer mask through Select and Mask (output: Layer Mask). In Photoshop the Background can't have any of these: setting one turns it into a normal layer, "Layer 0", first.

I observed this in Photoshop 2025 (26.5): `backgroundLayer.opacity = 50` leaves a normal "Layer 0" at 50 %, and so does adding a layer mask. PhotoCraft already does this conversion (`extra_cmds::background_to_layer`) for moving, transforming, erasing, styles and Layer › Layer Mask. `layer.setProps` and Select and Mask's Layer Mask output don't.

Repro:

```
photocraft-cli run --new '{"width":32,"height":32,"background":"white"}' \
  --cmd layer.setProps --params '{"opacity":0.5,"blend":"multiply"}' --out a.pcraft
photocraft-cli info a.pcraft   # "Background", opacity 0.5, Multiply: still the locked Background
```

title: info: a smart object embedded in a PSD is reported as linked, with a uuid as its path
author: switch87
body:
I'm working on this; the PR follows right away.

## What

`info` (and the control channel's document state) reports a smart object whose file is **embedded** in a PSD as `linked`, with the file's `Idnt` uuid as its path:

```
photocraft-cli run --new '{"width":32,"height":32,"background":"white"}' --cmd layer.new.layer \
  --cmd edit.fill --params '{"contents":"color","color":"#ff0000"}' \
  --cmd layer.smartObjects.convertToSmartObject --out so.psd
photocraft-cli info so.psd
#  "smartSource": {"kind": "linked", "path": "095b540d-6bae-d530-b38c-560d27575ab5"}
```

The file is in the PSD (a `liFD` item in the global `lnk2` block, `Layer 1.psb`). Internally, PSD import keeps every placed layer as `SmartSource::Linked { path: <uuid> }` on purpose, so duplicates share the file and export stays byte-stable. The report then calls it linked and gives a path that is no path.

## Proposed fix

When the uuid has an embedded file in the preserved blocks, report `{"kind": "embedded", "fileName": "Layer 1.psb", "uuid": "…"}`, found without copying the file's bytes. The model stays as it is.

title: Smart Objects › Export Contents ignores the extension: out.png holds .pcraft/.psb data
author: switch87
body:
I'm working on this; the PR follows right away.

## What

`layer.smartObjects.exportContents` writes the smart object's file as it is, whatever the path's extension. Exporting to `out.png` gives a `.pcraft` (zip) or `.psb` file named `out.png`:

```
photocraft-cli run --new '{"width":32,"height":32,"background":"white"}' --cmd layer.new.layer \
  --cmd edit.fill --params '{"contents":"color","color":"#ff0000"}' --cmd layer.smartObjects.convertToSmartObject \
  --cmd layer.smartObjects.exportContents --params '{"path":"out.png"}'
file out.png   # Zip archive data
```

## Proposed fix

When the path has the contents' own extension (or none), keep writing the file as it is. With another extension, open the contents and export them in that format, the way File › Export does, and report `"converted": true` with the export's warnings. An unknown extension is an error.

title: Flat export: a Lab document with one layer warns that its layers were flattened
author: switch87
body:
I'm working on this; the PR follows right away.

Exporting a Lab document that has only its Background to a flat format (TIFF, PNG, JPEG, …) warns `1 layer(s) flattened; layers, masks and blend modes are not kept`, although nothing is flattened. RGB, Grayscale and CMYK documents with one layer don't get the warning.

```
photocraft-cli run --new '{"width":16,"height":16,"background":"white"}' --cmd image.mode.lab --out lab.tif
warning: 1 layer(s) flattened; layers, masks and blend modes are not kept
warning: Lab composite written as sRGB RGB (colour-managed conversion)
```

The cause is in `crates/io/src/flat.rs`. Lab skips the native single-layer path, because the codecs have no Lab layout, and goes through the composite, and the composite path always adds the flatten warning. The second warning, about the sRGB conversion, is correct.

title: PNG: 300 ppi reopens as 299.9994 (pHYs rounding)
author: switch87
body:
I'm working on this; the PR follows right away.

A PNG saved at 300 ppi reopens at 299.9994 ppi, and one saved at 72 ppi at 72.009. `pHYs` stores whole pixels per metre, so 300 ppi becomes 11811 px/m, and the decoder converts that back exactly.

Photoshop 2025 writes the same 11811 px/m for 300 ppi and reads it back as **300** (observed). The ppi that was meant is the whole number that rounds to the stored value. A value no whole ppi rounds to, such as 11812 px/m (300.0248 ppi), should stay as it is.

title: Feature request: Add keyboard mnemonics (Alt + letter) for menu navigation
author: bjornsyse
body:
PhotoCraft currently seems to lack Windows-style menu mnemonics (underlined access keys).

In most Windows desktop applications, you can navigate menus entirely using the keyboard. For example:

Alt + F opens the File menu.
Pressing an underlined letter activates the corresponding menu item.
Pressing Alt reveals the available access keys.

Expected behavior:

- Support Alt + letter navigation for main menus.
- Display underlined letters for menu items, preferably when Alt is pressed.
- Allow navigating nested menus without using the mouse.

Why this matters:

This is a well-established Windows UI convention that makes menu navigation much faster for keyboard-oriented users. It also improves accessibility and consistency with other desktop applications.

Since PhotoCraft uses egui, I noticed that native-style menu mnemonics aren't currently supported out of the box (see egui issues (https://github.com/emilk/egui/issues/429) and (https://github.com/emilk/egui/issues/2831)) 

I understand this might require either an application-level implementation or upstream support in egui. Either way, I think it's an important usability feature, especially for a desktop application aiming to provide a familiar Photoshop-like workflow.

title: info: adjustment layers are reported as the internal model (snake_case, 0..1), not the params their commands take
author: switch87
body:
I'm working on this; the PR follows right away.

`info` / `document.inspect` reports an adjustment layer as a serde dump of the internal model:

```json
"adjustment": {"Levels": {"master": {"in_black": 0.0, "in_white": 1.0, "gamma": 1.0, "out_black": 0.0, "out_white": 1.0}, "per_channel": [...], "black": {...}}}
```

The Rust enum name is the key, the fields are snake_case, and the values are in 0..1. The adjustment commands take something else: `{"inBlack": 0..255, "inWhite": …, "red": {…}}`. A script that reads a layer's adjustment can't feed it back into `layer.newAdjustmentLayer.levels` or `image.adjustments.levels`. `adjust_params::to_params`, the inverse of `from_params`, already produces the command form.

## Proposed fix

Report `{"kind": "levels", "params": <to_params>}`. Nothing in the repository reads the old form.

title: TIFF: EXIF is dropped on export and not read on import (no Exif/GPS directory support)
author: switch87
body:
I'm working on this; the PR follows right away.

## What

A flat TIFF export drops EXIF: `warning: EXIF not supported; it will be dropped`. A JPEG with camera data saved as TIFF loses exposure, ISO, date taken and GPS. Reading a TIFF that has EXIF (from a camera, Photoshop, exiftool, …) doesn't pick it up either. The TIFF codec has no Exif directory (`FormatCaps` for TIFF: `exif: false`).

TIFF is EXIF's own container: IFD0 points to the Exif directory (tag 34665) and the GPS directory (34853), with the descriptive tags (Make, Model, Artist, …) in IFD0 itself. Photoshop reads and writes it that way.

Layered TIFFs keep EXIF as Photoshop resource 1058 (#1545). Only PhotoCraft reads it there; exiftool and Photoshop's File Info don't see it.

## Plan

- **Write:** a TIFF writes the EXIF block's Exif and GPS directories as directories of its own, and IFD0's descriptive tags as IFD0 tags. Values are copied as bytes (reordered when the byte orders differ), so unknown tags survive.
- **Read:** a TIFF with an Exif or GPS directory builds an EXIF block from them.

title: [Bug] Engine commands run while a modal dialog is open
author: stobados
body:
A command sent through the bridge is applied to the document while an adjustment dialog is still open. The person then sees a changed canvas behind a dialog that still shows its starting values.

**Environment:** macOS 27.2 (26B5101f), Apple M1, 8 GB. PhotoCraft 0.8.2. Mode: Desktop app, bridge.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Start: `photocraft --control 7995 --control-token-file TOKEN`; connect with `photocraft-cli mcp --bridge 127.0.0.1:7995 --control-token-file TOKEN`
2. `doc_new {"width": 600, "height": 400, "background": "#3366cc"}`
3. `ui_menu_invoke {"id": "image.adjustments.hueSaturation"}`: the dialog opens (`ui_inspect` lists dialog 1)
4. `command_run {"id": "image.adjustments.invert"}`

**Expected:** The command is refused with a clear error while a modal dialog is open, or the dialog is cancelled first.

**Actual:** It succeeds. History becomes `["Open", "Invert"]` and the canvas turns ochre behind the Hue/Saturation dialog, which still reads 0 / 0 / 0.

Related: #1556 fixed this for `ui.menu.invoke`. Engine commands sent with `command_run` still run under the dialog in 0.8.2.

_Found and reproduced with Claude Code (an AI agent) on the versions listed: every step above was actually run, not inferred._

title: TIFF: Lab (CIELab) files don't open, and Lab documents are saved as sRGB
author: switch87
body:
I'm working on this; a draft PR will follow soon, since it is a bigger change.

## What

PhotoCraft can't open a Lab TIFF. Photoshop 2025 saves a Lab document as TIFF with PhotometricInterpretation CIELab (8), and opening such a file (8 or 16 bits) fails:

```
error: codec: Tiff: Photometric interpretation CIELab with bits per sample [8, 8, 8] is unsupported
```

The other way round, a Lab document saved as TIFF is converted to sRGB (`Lab composite written as sRGB RGB`), although TIFF stores Lab as it is.

## Plan

- **Codecs:** a Lab channel layout (Lab / Lab + alpha) with the same sample values as PhotoCraft's Lab documents, plus Lab ⇄ RGB conversion for formats without Lab.
- **TIFF read:** CIELab, 8 and 16 bits. a and b are signed in the file and become PhotoCraft's offset form. The file opens as a Lab document.
- **TIFF write:** a Lab document with a single plain layer is written as CIELab TIFF, at its own depth.
- **Other formats:** unchanged, the sRGB conversion with its warning.

title: Feature proposal: Photoshop Generator-style event hooks for third-party subscriptions
author: wojzj57
body:
Hi maintainers,

We would like to integrate PhotoCraft with external tools and workflows, and need an event subscription mechanism that lets third parties receive notifications as users edit.

The existing commands, control channel, and MCP capabilities address how to ask the editor to perform an operation. We also need to know what a user has just done in the editor, so external tools can respond to editing changes without continuously polling.

We would like to use **Photoshop Generator's event notification model** as a reference. For example:

- `imageChanged`: describes document and layer changes, including pixel changes, layer properties, and structural changes.
- `toolChanged`: notifies clients when the selected tool changes.

Adobe's public documentation can serve as a reference for event semantics and fields: [Generator JSON event format](https://github.com/adobe-photoshop/generator-core/wiki/JSON-event-format) and [Photoshop Kevlar API Additions for Generator](https://github.com/adobe-photoshop/generator-core/wiki/Photoshop-Kevlar-API-Additions-for-Generator).

We would like PhotoCraft to offer a similar subscription capability, covering:

| Event category | Changes we need to observe |
| --- | --- |
| Image and layers | Committed brush strokes or filters, layer additions/deletions, property changes, transforms, etc. |
| Pixel selection | Selection creation, modification, clearing, and restoration through undo/redo |
| Layer selection | Changes to the selected layer set and active layer, separately from pixel selection |
| Tools | Changes to the currently selected tool |
| History | New history states, coalesced updates, undo/redo, deletion/clearing, trimming, and snapshot changes |
| Document lifecycle | Creation, opening, activation, successful saving, and closing |

Separate selection and history events could use PhotoCraft-defined contracts. We are not claiming that all of these categories are existing Generator events with the same names.

title: PSD: Photo Filter colors from Photoshop CS2 files are decoded wrong
author: detunized
body:
> [!NOTE]
> Found by an AI agent that compared PhotoCraft's renders of my old Photoshop CS2 files with Photoshop's own exports. It may need to be verified again.

PhotoCraft main (d43db3e, built from source), macOS. Follow-up to #3777 and #3790.

**Problem**

A version 3 `phfl` block stores the filter color as XYZ relative to the D50 white (X / 0.9642, Y, Z / 0.8249). PhotoCraft reads it as absolute XYZ and then clamps it to sRGB. Every Photo Filter from a CS2 file gets a slightly wrong color, and a filter outside sRGB, like Cooling Filter (82), loses most of its effect.

**Where**

`crates/io/src/adjust_map.rs`, `parse_photo_filter`, lines 530 to 536.

**Possible fix**

Multiply by the white point before converting (`[x * 0.9642, y, z * 0.8249]`) and keep the color unclamped, as XYZ or linear RGB, until `photo_filter_matrix`. The Warming Filter (85) test from #3790 uses a computed XYZ; a real CS2 file stores (15548, 12029, 0).

**Evidence**

- Decoded relative to the white point, every stored color in my files is exactly a Photoshop preset: Yellow #F9E31C (PhotoCraft reads #FFE03A), Blue, Warming Filter (85), Cyan, Cooling Filter (82).
- Against Photoshop's own exports: 118 files with the Yellow filter go from 0.91 to 0.77 of 255 on average with the corrected color, none worse. `blinds02.psd` (Cooling Filter 82) is 4.0 of 255 off now.

![Photo Filter](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/934ce75d-cc23-459a-bf60-1f646d3f3364)

**Repro**

```
photocraft-cli convert photo-filter-cooling82.psd out.png
```

**Attached**

- [`photo-filter-cooling82.psd.zip`](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33380248/photo-filter-cooling82.psd.zip), [`photo-filter-yellow.psd.zip`](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33380257/photo-filter-yellow.psd.zip): a test chart under the Photo Filter layer exactly as Photoshop CS2 saved it. Only the fill was raised to 100%.
- [`blinds02-small.psd.zip`](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33380261/blinds02-small.psd.zip) an…

title: Color Balance: Preserve Luminosity changes the brightness when more than one midtone slider is moved
author: detunized
body:
> [!NOTE]
> Found by an AI agent that compared PhotoCraft's renders of my old Photoshop CS2 files with Photoshop's own exports. It may need to be verified again.

PhotoCraft main (d43db3e, built from source), macOS. Follow-up to #3423 and #3443.

**Problem**

With Preserve Luminosity on and two or three midtones sliders moved, PhotoCraft shifts all three channels too far, so the image gets darker or lighter. With one slider it matches Photoshop.

**Where**

`crates/compose/src/adjust.rs:576`, `color_balance_channel`. Every midtones slider adds its own +a/2 or -a/2 term, so the exponent for channel c is `sum(a)/2 - a_c`.

**Possible fix**

Use `(max(a) + min(a))/2 - a_c`, the same max/min rule the shadows and highlights branches already use. I fitted this to Photoshop's exports of my files, so the exact rule could still be a close variant; a Photoshop measurement with large sliders would settle it. `crates/gpu/src/plan.rs:1633` uses the same function.

**Evidence**

- Test chart with midtones Cyan/Red +30 and Yellow/Blue +30: the average lightness of the gray ramp drops from 128 to 118. With the fix it is 125.
- Against Photoshop's own exports: `experiencemusicproject03.psd` 4.25 to 0.82 of 255, `bigdig.psd` 1.74 to 0.81, `tractors09.psd` 1.80 to 0.77.

![Color Balance](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d11e3d2a-be43-431c-a586-aa8c2a02b1fc)

**Repro**

```
photocraft-cli convert color-balance.psd out.png
```

**Attached**

- [`color-balance.psd.zip`](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33380321/color-balance.psd.zip): the test chart with the Color Balance layer (made in PhotoCraft).
- [`experiencemusicproject03-small.psd.zip`](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33380325/experiencemusicproject03-small.psd.zip) and [`experiencemusicproject03-photoshop-small.png`](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d8aa900a-a438-4353-aca7-78ab65b5c7a5): a real Photoshop CS2 file and Photoshop's export, 900x600.

title: Hue/Saturation: color range edits fade out on low saturation pixels
author: detunized
body:
> [!NOTE]
> Found by an AI agent that compared PhotoCraft's renders of my old Photoshop CS2 files with Photoshop's own exports. It may need to be verified again.

PhotoCraft main (d43db3e, built from source), macOS.

**Problem**

Edits to a color range (Reds, Yellows, ...) are scaled down for pixels with low saturation, when max minus min of R, G, B is below 0.25. Photoshop applies the full edit at every saturation, so muted colors like wood, skin or haze shift less in PhotoCraft.

**Where**

`crates/compose/src/adjust.rs:163`, the same in `crates/gpu/src/compose.wgsl:635`:

```rust
let chroma = ((c[0].max(c[1]).max(c[2]) - c[0].min(c[1]).min(c[2])) * 4.0).min(1.0);
```

multiplies the range hue, saturation and lightness.

**Possible fix**

Drop the factor. Only exact grays (max == min) have no hue, and they already don't change.

**Evidence**

- `boston15.psd` (Yellows hue -16): Photoshop shifts yellow pixels by -16° at every saturation. PhotoCraft's shift follows -16 × min(4 × saturation, 1) almost exactly (chart in the image).
- Without the fade, `boston15.psd` goes from 0.83 to 0.69 of 255 against Photoshop's export. This is not #4089: master and Colorize edits from my files render right.

![Hue/Saturation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bab099e5-5296-4706-90bf-a8c72f2bb877)

**Repro**

```
photocraft-cli convert hue-saturation.psd out.png
```

**Attached**

- [`hue-saturation.psd.zip`](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33380364/hue-saturation.psd.zip): a yellow saturation ramp with a Hue/Saturation layer, Yellows hue -60 (made in PhotoCraft).
- [`boston15-small.psd.zip`](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33380369/boston15-small.psd.zip) and [`boston15-photoshop-small.png`](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5072777e-d7fe-4650-94a8-7d384a70917a): a real Photoshop CS2 file and Photoshop's export, 900x600. Its Photo Filter is affected by #4940, so set that layer to #f9e31c first to compare only the Hue/Saturation part.

title: PSD: Gradient Fill layer from Photoshop CS2 runs at a different angle on a non-square canvas
author: detunized
body:
> [!NOTE]
> Found by an AI agent that compared PhotoCraft's renders of my old Photoshop CS2 files with Photoshop's own exports. It may need to be verified again.

PhotoCraft main (d43db3e, built from source), macOS.

**Problem**

`leaf.psd` has a linear Gradient Fill layer with angle -66.5 on a 3504x2336 canvas. PhotoCraft draws it at -66.5°, but in Photoshop's export it runs at about -62.5°. Setting the angle to -62.45 in PhotoCraft makes the render match Photoshop's export: 3.00 of 255 off before, 0.58 after.

**Where**

I'm not sure. The direction comes from `fill_gradient_layout` / `gradient_layout` (`crates/compose/src/fill_layout.rs:21`) and `gradient_t` (`crates/compose/src/effects.rs:1015`), which use the stored angle as it is.

**Possible cause**

tan(62.45°) / tan(66.5°) = 0.833 on a 3:2 canvas, so Photoshop may apply the angle in a differently scaled space. This is my only file with a gradient fill, and it may be specific to CS2. A gradient fill at -66.5 on a 3:2 canvas in current Photoshop would show which.

![Gradient Fill](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/74d02616-eb4e-4056-bb82-1926a848c19e)

**Repro**

```
photocraft-cli convert gradient-fill.psd out.png
photocraft-cli run gradient-fill.psd --cmd gradient.fill.set --params '{"layer":3,"angle":-62.45}' --out photoshop-direction.png
```

**Attached**

- [`gradient-fill.psd.zip`](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33380423/gradient-fill.psd.zip): the Gradient Fill layer exactly as Photoshop CS2 saved it, over a white background, 900x600.
- [`leaf-small.psd.zip`](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33380452/leaf-small.psd.zip) and [`leaf-photoshop-small.png`](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2759626b-622e-429e-9834-2eee0bd3318c): the real photo and Photoshop's export, 900x600.

title: Dependencies: update ruzstd for RUSTSEC-2026-0344
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment

Audit finding 1/32. **High availability priority; high confidence in affected dependency exposure**. Source reviewed at [6f85054288a5](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/commit/6f85054288a564f9fbbccb99268ffdb34e581584). Static source review only; no runtime reproduction, hostile-input execution, or resource-exhaustion testing was performed. Confidence refers to the source evidence, not observed failure frequency.

## Evidence and impact

[`Cargo.lock:5451-5457`](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/6f85054288a564f9fbbccb99268ffdb34e581584/Cargo.lock#L5451-L5457) resolves `ruzstd 0.9.0`. The public [RUSTSEC-2026-0344 advisory](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0344.html) lists versions before `0.9.1` as affected by a decompression denial-of-service defect. PhotoCraft uses this decoder in `crates/format/src/store.rs` and `crates/affinity/src/container.rs`.

Opening an affected document through those import paths may exhaust resources or trigger a decoder panic. PhotoCraft-specific failure was not reproduced. This is not a claim of memory corruption, RCE, or unauthenticated network reachability.

## Recommended remediation and validation

Require and resolve `ruzstd >= 0.9.1`, retain application decoding limits, run dependency-advisory checks and native/Affinity roundtrips, and adopt a safely bounded decoder regression.

This public report intentionally contains only the already-public advisory and affected components. No malformed samples or reproduction payloads are attached, in accordance with SECURITY.md.

title: Save-and-close can discard edits made by Save Document hooks
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment

Audit finding 2/32. **High data-loss priority; high confidence; synchronous-save path**. Source reviewed at [6f85054288a5](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/commit/6f85054288a564f9fbbccb99268ffdb34e581584). Static source review only; no runtime reproduction, hostile-input execution, or resource-exhaustion testing was performed. Confidence refers to the source evidence, not observed failure frequency.

## Source evidence

- [`crates/ui-egui/src/discard_ui.rs:181-215`](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/6f85054288a564f9fbbccb99268ffdb34e581584/crates/ui-egui/src/discard_ui.rs#L181-L215): synchronous completion accepts `Ok(_) => !app.save_options_open() && !app.saving()` without rechecking the document's dirty state. The deferred `saved_document` path does check it.
- [`crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs:1452-1512`](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/6f85054288a564f9fbbccb99268ffdb34e581584/crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs#L1452-L1512): saving records the serialized revision and then executes Save Document hooks.

## Conditions and impact

A dirty document is saved from the close prompt through synchronous services, and a Save Document hook edits that document after serialization. The prompt can advance and close it although the hook's edits were never written. This concerns synchronous saves, not all save paths; automation suppresses these hooks.

## Remediation

Release the prompt only after checking the original DocId and its current dirty state. Use the same completion invariant for synchronous and deferred saves.

## Suggested regression

A Save Document hook adds a layer. Save through the close prompt and assert that the document remains open and dirty. Include no-hook and background-save controls. Related closed #1098 addresses pending save options, not post-save hook edits.

title: Close All and Quit use a stale inventory of dirty documents
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment

Audit finding 3/32. **High data-loss priority; high confidence; hook-dependent**. Source reviewed at [6f85054288a5](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/commit/6f85054288a564f9fbbccb99268ffdb34e581584). Static source review only; no runtime reproduction, hostile-input execution, or resource-exhaustion testing was performed. Confidence refers to the source evidence, not observed failure frequency.

## Source evidence

- [`crates/ui-egui/src/discard_ui.rs:53-63`](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/6f85054288a564f9fbbccb99268ffdb34e581584/crates/ui-egui/src/discard_ui.rs#L53-L63) snapshots dirty document IDs once.
- [`crates/ui-egui/src/discard_ui.rs:139-176`](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/6f85054288a564f9fbbccb99268ffdb34e581584/crates/ui-egui/src/discard_ui.rs#L139-L176) closes answered documents, then enables exit or invokes the parked close command without rebuilding that inventory.

## Conditions and impact

During the multi-document workflow, a save/close hook dirties an initially clean document or creates a new dirty document. It is absent from the original inventory, so final Close All/Close Others/Quit can discard its work without asking. No modal escape is required.

title: Rasterize Smart Object can replace unavailable uncached content with transparency
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment

Audit finding 4/32. **High data-integrity priority; high confidence**. Source reviewed at [6f85054288a5](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/commit/6f85054288a564f9fbbccb99268ffdb34e581584). Static source review only; no runtime reproduction, hostile-input execution, or resource-exhaustion testing was performed. Confidence refers to the source evidence, not observed failure frequency.

## Source evidence

- [`crates/engine/src/extra_cmds.rs:710-730`](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/6f85054288a564f9fbbccb99268ffdb34e581584/crates/engine/src/extra_cmds.rs#L710-L730) ignores `refresh_layer` failure for an uncached smart object, falls back to `content_pixels`, then replaces the layer with raster content and removes smart-object PSD blocks.
- [`crates/engine/src/smart_cmds.rs:477-490`](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/6f85054288a564f9fbbccb99268ffdb34e581584/crates/engine/src/smart_cmds.rs#L477-L490) can fail to produce a cache.
- [`crates/compose/src/lib.rs:822-826`](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/6f85054288a564f9fbbccb99268ffdb34e581584/crates/compose/src/lib.rs#L822-L826) produces no pixels for missing smart-object pixel content.

## Conditions and impact

Rasterize an uncached smart object whose linked source is unavailable or whose embedded source cannot be decoded. The operation can succeed as transparent raster content rather than preserve the source representation and report an error. Undo may recover the layer while history is retained; saving persists the replacement.

## Remediation

Propagate refresh errors and require a usable cache before destructive conversion. A successful refresh return without a cache must also fail without mutation.

## Suggested regression

Missing linked and invalid embedded sources without caches must return an actionable error with unchanged layer content, metadata, history and serialization. Include valid-cache success.

title: Concurrent directory-bundle saves can remove objects required by the winning manifest
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment

Audit finding 6/32. **High conditional integrity risk; high mechanism confidence, medium desktop reachability confidence**. Source reviewed at [6f85054288a5](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/commit/6f85054288a564f9fbbccb99268ffdb34e581584). Static source review only; no runtime reproduction, hostile-input execution, or resource-exhaustion testing was performed. Confidence refers to the source evidence, not observed failure frequency.

## Source evidence

- [`crates/format/src/store.rs:730-755`](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/6f85054288a564f9fbbccb99268ffdb34e581584/crates/format/src/store.rs#L730-L755) snapshots existing objects and prepares one writer's reference set.
- [`crates/format/src/store.rs:815-829`](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/6f85054288a564f9fbbccb99268ffdb34e581584/crates/format/src/store.rs#L815-L829) publishes its manifest and then removes objects absent from that writer's set, without a bundle-wide cross-process lock.

## Conditions and impact

Two independent stores/processes save different snapshots to the same directory bundle. Writer A removes object X; writer B retains X and publishes the winning manifest before A's cleanup removes X. Both can report success while the final manifest references a missing object.

`&mut self` protects one Store instance, not independent stores or processes. Same-process UI overlap was not established; ordinary serialized saves are not implicated.

## Remediation

Coordinate the entire publication/garbage-collection transaction across writers, including reader lifetime considerations, or use immutable generations with coordinated reclamation.

## Suggested regression

Use deterministic barriers around two writers' publication and cleanup. Require serialization/rejection or a final loadable bundle containing all manifest-referenced objects. No destructive concurrency test was performed during this audit.

title: Security review: deep tiled EXR intermediate allocation admission
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment

Source reviewed at [6f85054288a5](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/commit/6f85054288a564f9fbbccb99268ffdb34e581584). A static review of `crates/codecs/src/codecs/deep_exr.rs` found an intermediate allocation-admission gap in deep tiled EXR import. Certain untrusted documents may consume memory beyond the configured importer allowance. Actual exhaustion or process termination has not been reproduced.

Recommended direction: apply checked size arithmetic and allocation admission to intermediate decoding buffers, including fallback paths and scratch space. Suggested regression: use a small injected allocation allowance to verify rejection before allocation, alongside valid deep-EXR controls.

title: Security hardening: aggregate working-memory admission for tiled RAW decoding
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment

Audit finding 8/32. **Potential high availability risk; high retention confidence, medium impact confidence**. Source reviewed at [6f85054288a5](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/commit/6f85054288a564f9fbbccb99268ffdb34e581584). Static source review only; no runtime reproduction, hostile-input execution, or resource-exhaustion testing was performed. Confidence refers to the source evidence, not observed failure frequency.

## Minimal public report

Static review of `crates/raw/src/sensor.rs` found no aggregate working-memory admission covering retained tile-decoding intermediates and destination storage. Resource-heavy input may therefore require substantially more peak memory than an individual allocation limit suggests. No exhaustion was attempted or measured.

Important qualification: `Limits::max_alloc` is explicitly a **per-buffer** limit. This is a request to bound aggregate working memory, not a claim that the documented per-buffer contract is violated. Existing single-buffer fixes in #2925 and #2897 do not provide that aggregate guarantee.

Recommended direction: bounded decode-and-scatter batches or an explicit operation-wide budget. Suggested regression: many individually admissible intermediates under a small aggregate test budget, plus normal tiled-file controls.

Detailed input relationships are withheld in accordance with SECURITY.md; coordinate private source evidence through #4819.

title: Security hardening: account for materialized raster memory during Affinity import
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment

Audit finding 9/32. **High potential availability risk; high accounting confidence**. Source reviewed at [6f85054288a5](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/commit/6f85054288a564f9fbbccb99268ffdb34e581584). Static source review only; no runtime reproduction, hostile-input execution, or resource-exhaustion testing was performed. Confidence refers to source evidence, not observed failure frequency.

## Minimal public report

Static review of `crates/affinity/src/model.rs` and `crates/affinity/src/raster.rs` found that archive extraction accounting does not also admit aggregate materialized raster storage and temporary planes. Inputs within extraction and per-layer limits can still cause high overall memory pressure. No exhaustion was measured.

`max_total` documents **extracted bytes**, not process memory. This report concerns a missing materialization budget, not incorrect extraction accounting.

Recommended direction: separately admit cumulative decoded pixels and peak temporary buffers before allocating, with fallible allocation. Suggested regression: several ordinary small layers under an injected aggregate budget, checking graceful rejection and valid single-layer behavior.

Per SECURITY.md, detailed triggering representations are withheld publicly. Please coordinate private evidence through #4819. No malicious document is attached.

title: Web save clears unsaved protection after requesting an unconfirmed download
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment

Audit finding 11/32. **High conditional data-loss priority; high state-transition confidence, medium browser-outcome confidence**. Source reviewed at [6f85054288a5](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/commit/6f85054288a564f9fbbccb99268ffdb34e581584). Static source review only; no runtime reproduction, hostile-input execution, or resource-exhaustion testing was performed. Confidence refers to source evidence, not observed failure frequency.

## Source evidence

- [`apps/photocraft-web/src/web.rs:385-432`](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/6f85054288a564f9fbbccb99268ffdb34e581584/apps/photocraft-web/src/web.rs#L385-L432): browser saving dispatches an anchor click and returns `Ok(())` without observing download completion.
- [`crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs:1452-1504`](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/6f85054288a564f9fbbccb99268ffdb34e581584/crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs#L1452-L1504): writer success records a saved revision.

## Conditions and impact

If the browser blocks the download, the user cancels its prompt, or persistence subsequently fails, the editor can appear clean despite no saved copy. title: Security review: preserve confidential-file permissions throughout atomic replacement
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment

Static review of atomic writing in `crates/format/src/atomic.rs` and automation writing in `crates/automation/src/workspace.rs` found that confidential-file access restrictions are not consistently maintained throughout replacement. Under particular local filesystem permission configurations, another local principal may gain access to document bytes. No disclosure experiment was performed.

Suggested regression: inspect both intermediate and final permissions under controlled creation defaults, including failure injection and platform-specific access-control behavior.

title: Security review: special-file-safe admission for automation workspace reads
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment

Audit finding 13/32. **Medium; high confidence in blocking-open ordering; runtime hang unmeasured**. Source reviewed at [6f85054288a5](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/commit/6f85054288a564f9fbbccb99268ffdb34e581584). Static source review only; no runtime reproduction, hostile-input execution, or resource-exhaustion testing was performed. Confidence refers to source evidence, not observed failure frequency.

## Minimal public report

Review of `crates/automation/src/workspace.rs` and headless request dispatch found that workspace file admission can encounter a blocking filesystem operation before rejecting an unsupported file type. Under specific authorized-root contents, an authenticated operation may stall shared automation progress.

Recommended direction: use platform-appropriate nonblocking, capability-relative admission and validate the opened handle rather than relying solely on a race-prone pathname check. Suggested regression: bounded-completion special-file tests for flat and bundle reads, followed by an independent request proving continued responsiveness.

This is not a demonstrated capability escape or authentication bypass. Triggering filesystem arrangements are withheld publicly in accordance with SECURITY.md; private coordination is requested through #4819.

title: Security hardening: absolute deadline for unauthenticated control connections
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment

Audit finding 14/32. **Medium local availability risk; high static confidence**. Source reviewed at [6f85054288a5](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/commit/6f85054288a564f9fbbccb99268ffdb34e581584). Static source review only; no runtime reproduction, hostile-input execution, or resource-exhaustion testing was performed. Confidence refers to source evidence, not observed failure frequency.

## Minimal public report

The authentication/connection-admission paths in `crates/automation/src/security.rs`, `crates/automation/src/rpc.rs`, and `apps/photocraft/src/control_server.rs` do not establish an absolute authentication-completion deadline independent of connection activity. A local principal able to connect may consume admission capacity without authenticating.

Recommended direction: bound total pre-authentication lifetime and input, release permits on expiry, and preserve useful authenticated-client timeout behavior. Suggested regression: injectable short deadlines showing that pre-authentication activity cannot indefinitely extend admission and that legitimate clients can connect after expiry.

No authentication bypass or remote reachability is claimed. Detailed connection sequences are withheld under SECURITY.md; coordinate privately through #4819. Related #2487 concerns authenticated bridge timeout behavior, not this admission property.

title: Security hardening: validate trust properties of existing control-token files
author: PierrunoYT
body:

title: Autosave: salvage committed sidecar-less bundles before orphan cleanup
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment

Audit finding 16/32. **Medium recovery/data-loss risk; high confidence in ordering gap**. Source reviewed at [6f85054288a5](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/commit/6f85054288a564f9fbbccb99268ffdb34e581584). Static source review only; no runtime reproduction, hostile-input execution, or resource-exhaustion testing was performed. Confidence refers to source evidence, not observed failure frequency.

## Source evidence

- [`crates/format/src/autosave.rs:168-200`](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/6f85054288a564f9fbbccb99268ffdb34e581584/crates/format/src/autosave.rs#L168-L200): a bundle is committed before its recovery sidecar is published; discovery depends on sidecars.
- [`crates/format/src/autosave.rs:288-325`](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/6f85054288a564f9fbbccb99268ffdb34e581584/crates/format/src/autosave.rs#L288-L325): sufficiently old sidecar-less bundles are swept after the 24-hour age threshold.

## Conditions and impact

A first autosave commits a valid bundle, then the process stops or sidecar publication fails. Recoverable work is absent from the recovery inventory and can later be deleted as an orphan. Not all orphans are valid, and deletion requires the age conditions.

This is a focused follow-up to closed #3489, which identified orphan accumulation and requested cleanup. Its cleanup is present; the remaining distinction is a **valid committed bundle** versus an incomplete bundle. This report does not ask to undo orphan cleanup generally.

## Remediation

Discover/validate committed sidecar-less bundles and synthesize recovery metadata, or make discoverability part of publication. Preserve valid recovery data while continuing to clean genuine partial bundles.

## Suggested regression

Inject failure after manifest commit but before first sidecar publication. Recovery must discover the document, and aged cleanup must retain it. Include incomplete-orphan cleanup and active-writer controls.

title: Saving reports success despite failed directory durability flushes
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment

Audit finding 17/32. **Medium conditional data-loss risk; high ignored-error confidence**. Source reviewed at [6f85054288a5](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/commit/6f85054288a564f9fbbccb99268ffdb34e581584). Static source review only; no runtime reproduction, destructive testing, or resource-exhaustion testing was performed. Confidence refers to source evidence, not observed failure frequency.

## Source evidence

- [`crates/format/src/atomic.rs:198-205`](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/6f85054288a564f9fbbccb99268ffdb34e581584/crates/format/src/atomic.rs#L198-L205): after publication, `let _ = fs.sync_dir(&dir)` discards the directory-sync result and returns success.
- [`crates/format/src/store.rs:550-565`](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/6f85054288a564f9fbbccb99268ffdb34e581584/crates/format/src/store.rs#L550-L565) also ignores the directory durability result.

## Conditions and impact

On a filesystem requiring a successful directory flush for durable publication, rename may succeed while the flush fails. A later power/system failure can then lose the supposedly saved entry. Distinguish published-but-durability-uncertain from complete success and pre-publication failure. Notify callers and retain recovery/required old objects until required flushes succeed; do not pretend publication can always be rolled back.

title: GPU pattern cache identity omits surface default pixels and source format
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment

Audit finding 19/32. **Medium rendering correctness risk; high confidence**. Source reviewed at [6f85054288a5](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/commit/6f85054288a564f9fbbccb99268ffdb34e581584). Static source review only; no runtime reproduction, destructive testing, or resource-exhaustion testing was performed. Confidence refers to source evidence, not observed failure frequency.

## Source evidence

- [`crates/gpu/src/lib.rs:1513-1537`](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/6f85054288a564f9fbbccb99268ffdb34e581584/crates/gpu/src/lib.rs#L1513-L1537): pattern identity includes ID/name, dimensions, document mode and tile addresses/coordinates, but not surface default pixels or source format.
- [`crates/format/src/convert.rs:593-604`](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/6f85054288a564f9fbbccb99268ffdb34e581584/crates/format/src/convert.rs#L593-L604): native pattern loading permits default-only surfaces with no populated tiles.

## Conditions and impact

A persistent compositor encounters same-key, same-dimension patterns with no allocated tiles but different default pixels. They receive the same identity despite producing different pixels, so a cached texture can show stale pattern fills/effects. Source-format changes are also not represented. Document mode **is** included; no on-disk corruption is established.

## Remediation

Include all pixel-defining fields, or use a stable comprehensive content/revision identity. Consider source-tile lifetime if retaining address-based identity; address reuse itself is not runtime-verified here.

## Suggested regression

Render two small same-key default-only patterns with different defaults and compare GPU output with the CPU oracle. Cover source-format and COW-edit changes. Related #2422 concerned a different default-pixel cache; #4780 concerns Pattern Stamp behavior.

title: Failed multi-step rasterization can leave earlier edits committed
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment

Audit finding 23/32. **Medium conditional integrity risk; high confidence in non-atomic behavior**. Source reviewed at [6f85054288a5](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/commit/6f85054288a564f9fbbccb99268ffdb34e581584). Static source review only; no runtime reproduction, destructive testing, or resource-exhaustion testing was performed. Confidence refers to source evidence, not observed failure frequency.

## Source evidence

- [`crates/engine/src/extra_cmds.rs:692-708`](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/6f85054288a564f9fbbccb99268ffdb34e581584/crates/engine/src/extra_cmds.rs#L692-L708) commits content conversion before a fallible vector-mask subcommand.
- [`crates/engine/src/extra_cmds.rs:758-790`](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/6f85054288a564f9fbbccb99268ffdb34e581584/crates/engine/src/extra_cmds.rs#L758-L790) iterates selected/all layers with early error propagation and no overall rollback.
- [`crates/engine/src/lib.rs:659-669`](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/6f85054288a564f9fbbccb99268ffdb34e581584/crates/engine/src/lib.rs#L659-L669) commits each successful edit immediately.

## Conditions and impact

If a later substep fails after an earlier conversion succeeds, the outer operation returns an error while leaving partial rasterization in the document. History coalescing combines undo entries but does not provide transaction rollback. This is a conditional error-path finding, not a claim of authorization bypass or a reproduced UI failure.

## Remediation

Prepare the operation against one snapshot and commit once, or implement complete compound rollback including document, targeting, history and journal state.

## Suggested regression

Inject a later nested-command failure after one successful conversion, both within content-plus-mask work and across selected layers. The public command should leave state unchanged on error; successful multi-layer operation should remain one history step. Keep tests bounded…

title: Scale Marker compound rollback can leave a dangling layer target
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment

Audit finding 24/32. **Medium conditional state-integrity risk; high confidence**. Source reviewed at [6f85054288a5](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/commit/6f85054288a564f9fbbccb99268ffdb34e581584). Static source review only; no runtime reproduction, destructive testing, or resource-exhaustion testing was performed. Confidence refers to source evidence, not observed failure frequency.

## Source evidence

- [`crates/engine/src/analysis_cmds.rs:177-205`](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/6f85054288a564f9fbbccb99268ffdb34e581584/crates/engine/src/analysis_cmds.rs#L177-L205): `compound` saves `prior = st.layer_target()` but the failure branch restores document, history and samplers without restoring that target.
- [`crates/engine/src/analysis_cmds.rs:1112-1135`](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/6f85054288a564f9fbbccb99268ffdb34e581584/crates/engine/src/analysis_cmds.rs#L1112-L1135): Scale Marker selects a newly created bar before a fallible nested text-creation step.

## Conditions and impact

If the nested text step fails, rollback removes the bar from the document while targeting can still reference its ID. Later commands then encounter inconsistent active/selected-layer state. No downstream crash or wrong-layer edit has been demonstrated.

## Remediation

Restore the saved complete layer target and reconcile associated selection/channel/coalescing state when rolling back.

## Suggested regression

Inject failure in the nested text step through the public command path. Compare original document, history, journal, active layer, selected layers and anchor; then execute an ordinary layer command successfully.

Closed #932 addressed a different Scale Marker height-clamp panic. Its guard is present and is not the subject of this report.

title: Security review: checked ICC parser arithmetic on 32-bit targets
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment

Audit finding 25/32. **Medium architecture/build-dependent risk; high confidence in unchecked arithmetic**. Source reviewed at [6f85054288a5](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/commit/6f85054288a564f9fbbccb99268ffdb34e581584). Static source review only; no runtime reproduction, hostile-input execution, or resource-exhaustion testing was performed. Confidence refers to source evidence, not observed failure frequency.

## Minimal public report

Review of `crates/cms/src/profile.rs` found input-derived count/offset calculations that precede complete arithmetic validation on 32-bit targets, including wasm32. Depending on build overflow behavior, this can produce a panic or wrapped offsets. No allocation-limit bypass, memory corruption or successful incorrect-profile acceptance has been established.

Recommended direction: validate counts before calculations and use checked multiply/add for complete record extents and field offsets. Suggested regression: small synthetic malformed-count cases through the public parser on 32-bit checked and release builds, plus valid multilingual-record controls.

Specific triggering values and detailed parser paths are withheld under SECURITY.md; coordinate private evidence through #4819. This finding must not be generalized to a proven exploit on every target.

title: Investigate RAW Deflate stream-completion validation
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment

Audit finding 26/32. **Potential Medium correctness risk; medium confidence in acceptance behavior, high confidence status is ignored**. Source reviewed at [6f85054288a5](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/commit/6f85054288a564f9fbbccb99268ffdb34e581584). Static source review only; no runtime reproduction, hostile-input execution, or resource-exhaustion testing was performed. Confidence refers to source evidence, not observed failure frequency.

## Source evidence

[`crates/raw/src/sensor.rs:243-274`](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/6f85054288a564f9fbbccb99268ffdb34e581584/crates/raw/src/sensor.rs#L243-L274) invokes `Decompress::decompress` with `Finish`, handles errors, then uses produced bytes without requiring the returned status to be `StreamEnd`. Checked segment-size admission is present.

## Unverified condition and potential impact

If the resolved backend returns nonterminal success while producing enough samples, the importer may accept incomplete or excess-output compressed streams. The exact backend acceptance behavior has **not** been verified. This is an investigation, not a confirmed corrupt-file acceptance, decompression bomb, or allocation-limit bypass.

## Recommended investigation/remediation

Test the resolved backend's completion semantics. Require completed streams and output lengths consistent with supported packing; explicitly define any policy for trailing compressed input.

## Suggested regression

Bounded cases for a valid complete stream, incomplete/truncated stream, excess decoded output, and supported packing variants. Verify observable parser errors rather than only absence of panics. No malformed samples or triggering byte sequences are attached.

Related #2925 concerns lossless-JPEG allocation accounting, not Deflate stream completion.

title: Security hardening: aggregate plug-in memory admission across parallel bands
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment

Audit finding 27/32. **Medium conditional availability risk; high confidence in per-instance budget scope**. Source reviewed at [6f85054288a5](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/commit/6f85054288a564f9fbbccb99268ffdb34e581584). Static source review only; no runtime reproduction, hostile-input execution, or resource-exhaustion testing was performed. Confidence refers to source evidence, not observed failure frequency.

## Minimal public report

Static review of `crates/plugins/src/runtime.rs` and `crates/plugins/src/apply.rs` found per-instance guest-memory limits without equivalent operation-wide admission across native parallel filter bands. A resource-heavy installed plug-in can therefore consume multiple instance allowances simultaneously, in addition to host buffers. Actual peak memory/exhaustion was not measured.

Fuel, deadlines, per-instance limits and the absence of ambient imports remain relevant protections. This is not a sandbox escape; running a plug-in is required, and the wasm band path has different concurrency.

Recommended direction: reserve aggregate memory and derive instance concurrency from a shared budget. Suggested regression: bounded reservation accounting with a benign fixture, including release on error/cancellation and successful multi-band controls.

Detailed stress configurations are withheld under SECURITY.md; coordinate through #4819. Related #52 and #662 describe plug-in architecture but do not establish aggregate memory admission.

title: Text rasterization: budget peak working bytes, not only pixel count
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment

Audit finding 28/32. **Medium conditional availability risk; high allocation-accounting confidence; exhaustion unmeasured**. Source reviewed at [6f85054288a5](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/commit/6f85054288a564f9fbbccb99268ffdb34e581584). Static source review only; no runtime reproduction, hostile-input execution, or resource-exhaustion testing was performed. Confidence refers to source evidence, not observed failure frequency.

## Text-specific follow-up to #212

The general fallible-allocation work in #212 covers import and several editing operations. This narrower tracker covers `crates/text/src/render.rs`, `crates/text/src/raster.rs`, and `crates/io/src/text_import.rs`: the pixel-count limits do not directly bound the peak bytes of overlapping text-rendering buffers. The peak depends on channels, accumulation/coverage storage and rendering variants.

A large otherwise admitted text render may require more working memory than the process can provide; no exhaustion was attempted and no failing document is claimed.

Recommended direction: admit peak bytes for simultaneously live buffers, use fallible allocation, and consider bounded-region rendering. Suggested regression: small injected allowances across RGB/CMYK, depths and faux-bold, verifying graceful failure and preservation of existing document/cached appearance.

This is a component-specific follow-up rather than a duplicate proposal for general OOM handling. Exact input constructions and resource-amplification details are withheld under SECURITY.md; coordinate private evidence through #4819.

title: Web file ingestion: bound input bytes and read concurrency before decoding
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment

Audit finding 29/32. **Medium conditional browser availability risk; high static confidence**. Source reviewed at [6f85054288a5](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/commit/6f85054288a564f9fbbccb99268ffdb34e581584). Static source review only; no runtime reproduction, hostile-input execution, or resource-exhaustion testing was performed. Confidence refers to source evidence, not observed failure frequency.

## Minimal public report

Review of file acquisition in `apps/photocraft-web/src/web.rs` found no pre-read file-count/aggregate-byte admission for multi-file selection, and no equivalent admission/concurrency budget for queued dropped-file reads. Decoder limits occur after acquisition and cannot by themselves bound those retained input buffers.

This requires user selection/drop; arbitrary remote injection and actual tab exhaustion were not established. Picker reads are sequential but retain results until delivery; they should not be described as all running concurrently.

Recommended direction: validate available metadata before reading, bound cumulative bytes/concurrency, process incrementally, and release buffers promptly. Suggested regression: fake readers proving rejection before reads and bounded queued work, with normal multi-file and cancellation controls.

No oversized sample is attached. Further stress details are withheld under SECURITY.md and can be coordinated through #4819. Related #2802 introduced multi-file behavior rather than a resource budget.

title: PSD decode_channel should validate its index before range arithmetic
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment

Audit finding 30/32. **Low API-robustness risk; high confidence; application reachability unestablished**. Source reviewed at [6f85054288a5](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/commit/6f85054288a564f9fbbccb99268ffdb34e581584). Static source review only; no runtime reproduction, hostile-input execution, or resource-exhaustion testing was performed. Confidence refers to source evidence, not observed failure frequency.

## Source evidence

[`crates/psd/src/image_data.rs:37-46`](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/6f85054288a564f9fbbccb99268ffdb34e581584/crates/psd/src/image_data.rs#L37-L46) decodes merged image data, then evaluates `all.get(index * plane..(index + 1) * plane)` without first checking `index < header.channels`.

## Conditions and impact

An invalid sufficiently large public-API index can overflow checked arithmetic rather than return `PsdError`. In wrapping builds it may produce an unintended range. No application path accepting such an index was established; this is not a demonstrated file-triggered editor crash.

## Remediation

Reject invalid indices before decoding and use checked offset arithmetic. Preserve ordinary out-of-range error behavior without wasting decode work.

## Suggested regression

Against a tiny valid PSD, cover valid channels, the first out-of-range index and the maximum API index. Invalid calls must return errors without panic in checked and release builds. No hostile document or exploit is required.

title: panic_hunt misses command panics caught by Session dispatch
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment

Audit finding 31/32. **Low test-quality risk; high confidence; not a standalone vulnerability**. Source reviewed at [6f85054288a5](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/commit/6f85054288a564f9fbbccb99268ffdb34e581584). Static source review only; no runtime reproduction, hostile-input execution, or resource-exhaustion testing was performed. Confidence refers to source evidence, not observed failure frequency.

## Source evidence

- [`crates/engine/tests/panic_hunt.rs:25-37`](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/6f85054288a564f9fbbccb99268ffdb34e581584/crates/engine/tests/panic_hunt.rs#L25-L37): the harness ignores `Session::execute`'s returned result and checks only whether its outer `catch_unwind` succeeded.
- [`crates/engine/src/jobs.rs:662-666`](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/6f85054288a564f9fbbccb99268ffdb34e581584/crates/engine/src/jobs.rs#L662-L666): dispatch already catches command panics and converts them into an error result.

## Conditions and impact

A command panics internally but the production safety net catches it. The outer harness sees no unwind and counts the case as successful, so the claimed command-level never-panic gate misses that defect. Production containment still works; the finding concerns regression detection.

## Remediation

Expose a typed internal-panic error or test-only panic observer and make panic-hunt fail on that signal while continuing to accept ordinary validation errors. Avoid brittle matching on incidental error-message text.

## Suggested regression

A controlled panicking test command must be contained by normal dispatch but rejected by the harness classification. Include a legitimate invalid-input error control.

Closed #2994 addressed timeout/font-initialization flakiness, not this swallowed-panic blind spot.

title: Crop: a turned crop rotates the whole canvas, so small rotated crops take ~1 s
author: davidmann4
body:
## Problem

A turned crop (Crop tool with the frame rotated, i.e. `image.crop` with an `angle`) is much slower than an upright one. Cropping a small box out of a 3859×2594 photo with one extra layer takes about a second in the app, while Photoshop does it instantly and an upright crop of the same box takes ~11 ms.

`rotated_crop` rotates the **whole canvas** (every layer, mask and channel) with Image Rotation › Arbitrary and only then crops to the frame. With Delete Cropped Pixels on (the default), almost all of that rotated work is thrown away straight after.

Measured on the Great Wave scan (3859×2594) + a duplicated layer, release build:

| Crop | Time |
|---|---|
| Upright 512×442 | 11 ms |
| Turned 3°, 512×442 | 541 ms (in the app: 1.03 s, 978 ms of it in Rotate Canvas) |
| Turned 3°, 3000×2000 | 621 ms |

A second, smaller cost: Rotate Canvas fills the Background with a canvas-sized `f32` buffer (`fill.repeat(w × h)`, ~190 MB for this canvas) before compositing the rotated pixels over it.

## Expected

A turned crop that deletes the cropped pixels costs about what the frame holds, not what the canvas holds.
