title: Free Transform snaps the object to a repositioned reference point when resizing
author: ultimaKV
body:
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e58d6fa3-4fb4-4078-80fa-7e89b9af8129

Free Transform behaves incorrectly after manually repositioning the transformation reference point.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Select a layer or object.
2. Enter Free Transform with `Ctrl+T`.
3. Move the transform reference point to a different position.
4. Use `Shift+Alt+Left Click` to drag a transform handle to resize the object around the new reference point.

### Actual behavior

When resizing begins, the object suddenly snaps toward the repositioned reference point. The object appears to become centered on the reference point before being resized around it.

This unexpectedly changes the object's position and makes it difficult to resize accurately around a custom pivot.

### Expected behavior

Moving the reference point should only change the anchor or pivot used by the transformation.

The reference point should remain fixed at its new location, and the object should resize toward or away from that point without jumping, snapping, or becoming centered on it.

This should work similarly to Photoshop, where repositioning the transform reference point changes the origin of the transformation without moving the object when resizing begins.

**Environment:** PhotoCraft 0.8.2 (official Flatpak `ai.storyteller.photocraft`), Arch Linux (Omarchy), **Wayland / Hyprland 0.56.2**, NVIDIA.

**Summary:** Copying an image from a browser (Chromium) and pasting into PhotoCraft does nothing — no new layer, no canvas paste.

**The clipboard is fine — verified:**
- `wl-paste --list-types` →
```
text/x-moz-url
text/html
image/png
chromium/x-internal-source-rfh-token
chromium/x-source-url
```

**Expected:** Ctrl+V pastes the clipboard image onto a new layer; "New from clipboard" sizes to the image.

Related: #741 (macOS), #2629 (Windows) — this is the Linux/Wayland counterpart.

title: PSD fonts reported missing although installed: PostScript names BMDoHyeon and Daum_SemiBold are guessed as "BM Do Hyeon" / "Daum_Semi Bold"
author: uhoyeun-code
body:
**Version:** PhotoCraft 0.8.2, Windows 11 x64 (portable build, `photocraft-cli` and the app).

**What happens**
PSDs made in Photoshop with two free Korean fonts open with those fonts reported missing, although both are installed (per-user, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Fonts`, registered under HKCU) and PhotoCraft lists them in `type.fonts`.

| Font file | name table: family / PostScript | Name in the PSD | What PhotoCraft looks for |
|---|---|---|---|
| BMDOHYEON_ttf.ttf (BM DoHyeon, Woowahan Brothers) | `BM DoHyeon` / `BMDoHyeon` | `BMDoHyeon` | `BM Do Hyeon` |
| Daum_SemiBold.ttf (Daum font, Kakao) | `Daum_SemiBold` / `Daum_SemiBold` | `Daum_SemiBold` | `Daum_Semi Bold` |
| Daum_Regular.ttf | `Daum_Regular` / `Daum_Regular` | `Daum_Regular` | resolves fine |

`type.fonts` lists the installed families as `BM DoHyeon` and `Daum`.

**Repro**
```
photocraft-cli run thumbnail.psd --cmd type.resolveMissingFonts
{"result":{"missing":["BM Do Hyeon"]}}
warning: font 'BM Do Hyeon' is not installed; text may render using a fallback face
```
It looks like the PostScript name is split into words (`DoHyeon` -> `Do Hyeon`, `SemiBold` -> `Semi Bold`) and the guessed family is then compared with the installed family names, instead of matching the PostScript name against the installed faces' PostScript names (which match exactly).

**Workaround attempts**
- `type.resolveMissingFonts` with `{"map":{"Daum_Semi Bold":"Daum"}}` clears the warning, but the run ends up as family `Daum` and the SemiBold weight appears to be lost.
- `{"map":{"BM Do Hyeon":"BM DoHyeon"}}` reports `replaced`, but after saving to PSD and reopening, `BM Do Hyeon` is reported missing again (the file stores `BMDoHyeon`, which is guessed the same way on reopen).

**Expected**
A PSD run whose PostScript name exactly equals an installed face's PostScript name resolves to that face (and its weight), without a family-name guess.

Possibly related: #608 (open PR, "resolve PostScript faces beyond family-name gues…

title: [Feature Request] Add "Pixel Perfect" to Pencil Tool & Add "Palettize Map","Index Colors" Non-Destructive Adjustment Layer or Filter
author: homable80-bit
body:
### 🎯 Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
Some people sometimes use Photocraft as part of their workflow for creating pixel art.

Currently, Photocraft lacks some essential, industry-standard tools required for efficient pixel art and HD index painting workflows.

**Pencil Tool Limitation**s: The Pencil Tool currently lacks both a "Pixel Perfect" feature. Drawing freehand lines often creates unwanted L-shaped pixel clusters (jaggies), requiring tedious manual cleanup.

**Lack of Non-Destructive Indexing/Dithering**: Currently, there is no effective way to non-destructively map a painting to a specific palette and the colors on the color picker while applying stylized dithering, making the HD index painting workflow highly destructive and difficult to iterate.

### 💡 Describe the solution you'd like
I would like to request two major additions tailored for pixel artists and index painters:

**1. "Pixel Perfect" Mode for the Pencil Tool**

- Algorithm & Behavior: Implement an algorithm similar to the 'Pixel Perfect' feature found in Aseprite. When enabled, it should automatically filter out the extra diagonal pixels that create L-shapes during continuous freehand strokes, ensuring clean, 1-pixel wide line art.
- UI/UX (Top Options Bar): The layout of the top options bar for the Pencil Tool should closely resemble Aseprite's approach.
- Separation from Stabilizer(Smoothing): Since the pencil tool currently lacks the 'Pixel Perfect' feature, when implemented, the "Pixel Perfect" toggle must be distinctly separated from the "Stabilizer" options in the top UI. They serve entirely different purposes (clean pixel placement vs. smooth stroke trajectories) and should not be bundled together.

**2. "Palettize Map" Non-Destructive Filter**

- Behavior: Add a non-destructive adjustment layer or filter similar to Krita's "Palettize Map" (It is recommended to also include "Index Colors"). This will allow artists to paint smoothly and non-destructively map…

title: PhotoCraft: Inaccurate Multiply Blend Mode calculation compared to industry standards (Gamma/Linear color space issue)
author: awehbe74-design
body:
First, congratulations on this amazing, lightning-fast open-source suite! The performance and UI familiarity of PhotoCraft are incredible. However, I found a specific issue regarding the Multiply Blend Mode, which is crucial for digital restoration workflows (such as restoring comic book pages and blending paper textures).

Steps to reproduce:

Import a clean, restored line art image (black lines on a pure white background).

Add a textured background layer (e.g., newspaper or paper grain) on top.

Set the top layer's blend mode to Multiply.

Expected behavior:
The texture should blend smoothly with the underlying image, preserving the contrast, brightness, and deep dark lines without looking washed out or flat (similar to how Affinity Photo or Photoshop handle it).

Current behavior:
The Multiply mode looks somewhat opaque and muddy, failing to blend properly and washing out the overall brightness and contrast of the image. It feels like the color space/gamma calculation during the blending operation might be treating pixels directly in sRGB without proper linear-space conversion or alpha handling.

OS: Windows

title: I should be able to remap keyboard shortcuts according to usual conventions.
author: awiebe
body:
On Linux I may want to use PC or Mac style shortcuts.  

- The tool and panel management architecture should understand that I may want to map arbitrary key combinations to certain commands
- I may want to use a specific modal conventions for some tools without individually specifying for all tools. For example I may want constrain aspect and clone move combinations to be consistent.
- I should be able to import and export my keymap preferences.
- I should be able to pick from reasonable preset defaults of the usual PC and Mac styles.
- I should be able to set commands easily with a table that has a checkbox for the modifiers (use the modifiers given in the USB specification), in combination with any letter, number, named or function key with or without shift.
- If a key combination conflicts with another combination in the program, it should be highlighted a different color, and there should be a way to filter the table to show only conflicting mappings
- If a key combination does not have any meaning in the global application context, but does have meaning modally, then it is not a conflict if two separate modes share a combo, although I don't think this actually happens in photoshop, but it is a good idea to have this infrastructure for the *Craft suite.
- It should be possible to load a plugin that can report when a key combination conflicts with key combos reserved outside the application for example by the system.  A builtin plugin should be available to do this for windows and macos since these combos are known.  For example the mac version of the plugin would know that gui+shift+q is not a valid combinations because the loginwindow will interpret that as a logout.  SDImilarly cmd+tab, and cmd+~, and cmd+space should not be overridden.
- Some combinations are conventional and should not be overridden under normal circumstances. For example in the mac keymap cmd+; is preferences, cmd+s is save, cmd+z is undo, cmd+q is quit, cmd+h is hide.  It should be possibl…

title: Feature request: Optional "Low-Quality Preview While Editing" setting for low-end PCs
author: EGAN-xyz
body:
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a29ccb3b-5b7d-4cad-8a17-81888addd958

[###](url) Summary
I would like to suggest an optional setting that lets users choose between
real-time full-quality preview and a faster, lower-resolution preview while
editing. Thank you for PhotoCraft, it already runs great on weak computers!

### Background
I have seen several users complain that when applying color adjustments or
scaling/resizing images, the preview becomes pixelated for a moment until
the operation is confirmed, and then returns to full quality. This is a
known trade-off in many editors, and while it bothers some people, it
could actually help users on weak hardware.

### The idea
Add a setting (for example in Preferences > Performance):

  [ ] Use low-resolution preview while editing (faster on low-end PCs)

When ENABLED:
- While dragging a layer, adjusting colors, or transforming/scaling an
  image or layer, the editor renders a reduced-resolution (pixelated)
  preview to reduce CPU/integrated-GPU load.
- When the user confirms (OK / releases the mouse), the result is
  rendered at full quality.

When DISABLED:
- The editor shows the instant full-quality preview, as it does today.

### Why an option, not a forced behavior
- Users on low-end CPUs and integrated graphics (like mine) get a much
  smoother experience.
- Users who dislike the temporary pixelation can simply turn it off and
  keep seeing the true-quality preview in real time.
- Everyone chooses what fits their hardware and workflow.

### Environment
- PhotoCraft version: [(0.8.2)]([url]([url](url)))
- OS: Windows (10)
- CPU: AMD A4-5000 (4 cores, 1.5 GHz)
- RAM: (write yours)
- GPU: AMD Radeon HD 8330 (integrated)

Thanks again for the great work!

title: Tracking: print-scale performance (150 MP+, CMYK, multi-GB PSB)
author: davidmann4
body:
Can PhotoCraft handle the files an advertising agency works with for print campaigns: posters and billboards at 150 MP and up, CMYK, 16-bit, dozens of layers, multi-GB PSB? This issue tracks what still stands between main and that workload, with the test or bench that proves each item. It complements #209, #210 and #211 (the budgets) and #216 (file-compatibility measurement).

## Where main stands (measured 2026-10-13)

`perf_scenarios` in release on main at 6f850542 (Windows 11, 32 threads, RTX 5070 Ti, idle machine, 15 reps). The committed baseline in `docs/scorecard.md` dates from 2026-10-05; about 25 perf PRs have merged since, and it no longer reflects main.

| Row | Budget (p95) | Baseline 2026-10-05 | Main today (p95) |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 move styled layer | 25 ms | 535 | 19 ✅ |
| P2–P5 opacity / fill / blend / visibility | 10–20 ms | 423–467 | 4–5 ✅ |
| P6 / P7 undo move / redo property | 25 ms | 530 / 212 | 13 / 3 ✅ |
| P8 / P10 duplicate / paste 12 MP (first) | 100 ms | 699 / 3136 | 24 / 26 ✅ |
| P9 / P11 duplicate / paste 12 MP (repeat) | 20 ms | 627 / 1174 | 24 / 24 ⚠️ → 19.5 / 19.7 ✅ after #5288 (2026-10-14) |
| P12 nudge in a 150-layer document | 30 ms | crashed | 4.5 ✅ |
| P13 / P14 dab / move on 15000×10000 16-bit | 80 ms | 146 / 4318 | 1.5 / 18 ✅ |
| P16 / P17 dab / move on 32-bit, 20 layers | 100 ms | 161 / 681 | 3.4 / 17 ✅ |
| P18 open 20 MP layered PSD | 1000 ms | 2794 | 361 ✅ |
| P33 brush dab on A4 300 ppi CMYK | 6 ms | 235 | 9.1 ❌ |

So the interactive layer operations are in good shape. The gaps for print-scale work are memory (no scratch disk), files larger than anything we measure, and CMYK painting.

## Checklist

**Memory and huge documents**
- [ ] Scratch disk: tiles spill to disk past the memory budget (#4185, claimed by @itsF4LCON). Test: spilled tiles read back bit-identical, including copy-on-write copies under concurrent reads.
- [x] Large PSB: full CPU redraws leave the UI thread, visible part first (#4024 / #5001, merged 2026-…

title: Tests: generated large-file fixtures (20 MP, 150 layers, 2 GB PSD, 4-5 GB PSB) and a P20 number (FILE-216-2)
author: davidmann4
body:
Part of #5106 (scorecard FILE-216-2, part of #216).

## What's missing on main

FILE-216-2 is `partial`: `crates/psd/examples/big_psb.rs` writes 4–5 GB PSB fixtures and `crates/io/examples/big_psb_check.rs` opens them, and `crates/io/tests/large_psb.rs` is an opt-in test with a 2.5 GB merged image. There is no generated 2 GB PSD, no 150-layer layout PSD and no 20 MP layered fixture, and nothing reads them in tests or benches. Scorecard P20 ("Open a 2 GB PSD / 4–5 GB PSB") stays `not measurable` for the same reason.

Photoshop's limits these fixtures should sit at: PSD up to 30,000 px per side and 2 GB; PSB (Large Document Format) up to 300,000 px per side.

## Proposal

- A fixture generator (testkit or the `psd` crate, generated at test time and never committed): a 20 MP layered PSD, a 150-layer layout PSD (mixed small layers, groups, masks, a few effects), a PSD just under the 2 GB cap, and the existing 4–5 GB PSB.
- Opt-in tests (`#[ignore]` or a feature, like `large_psb.rs`) that generate each one, open it through `photocraft_io`, check the layer count, size and merged pixels, and re-save it.
- A bench row for P20 in the existing large-file bench, so `cargo xtask perf` reports a number (opening in the background with progress, editable afterwards); update `perf/budgets.toml` and the scorecard.
- Flip FILE-216-2 in `scorecard/file_compat.toml` with the evidence.

title: Performance: brush dab on A4 300 ppi CMYK over budget (P33: 9.1 ms vs 6 ms)
author: davidmann4
body:
Part of #5106 (scorecard P33, #211).

## Numbers

`perf_scenarios --only CMYK` in release on main at 6f850542 (Windows 11, 32 threads, RTX 5070 Ti, idle, 15 reps):

| Row | Budget | p50 | p95 |
|---|---|---|---|
| brush dab on A4 300 ppi CMYK + refresh | 6 ms | 5.23 ms | 9.11 ms |

This is the only interactive scenario in #209/#211 still clearly over budget on main. For comparison, a 60 px dab on a 15000×10000 16-bit RGB document takes 1.5 ms p95 (P13), so the extra cost is most likely in the CMYK-specific part of the dab-to-screen path (the CMYK → display conversion of the damaged area, or a cache that misses on CMYK). To be measured before changing anything.

## Proposal

- Measure the stages of one dab (paint, composite, CMYK → display, upload) with a throwaway probe and fix the measured cost.
- The displayed pixels stay bit-identical: keep the current path as the oracle in a test.
- Before/after p50/p95 in the PR; set `enforce = true` in `perf/budgets.toml` only if p95 sits under budget with margin.

title: [BUG] Distortion tools break layer deletion, history (Ctrl+Z), and leak layers across projects
author: Caio13Vinni
body:
### Describe the bug
When applying **any distortion tool** (e.g., Puppet Warp, Liquify, Free Transform distortions) to a layer, several critical layer and history management issues occur:

1. **Undo fails:** Pressing `Ctrl + Z` no longer reverts the distortion or any subsequent actions.
2. **Project leak:** The distorted layer unexpectedly bleeds/leaks into other open project tabs or canvases.
3. **Deletion failure:** In specific cases (such as Puppet Warp), the layer cannot be deleted after distortion.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Open a project with an image layer.
2. Select the layer and apply any distortion tool (Puppet Warp, Liquify, etc.).
3. Try to undo the action by pressing `Ctrl + Z` -> *Nothing happens / action is not reverted*.
4. Open or switch to another active project tab/canvas -> *The distorted layer leaks or displays inside the other project*.
5. (For Puppet Warp) Try to delete the layer via keyboard or context menu -> *Layer is not removed*.

### Expected Behavior
- `Ctrl + Z` should undo any applied distortion and revert the layer state properly.
- Layers and transformations must remain strictly isolated to their original project/canvas document.
- Layers should remain deletable after applying any distortion tool.

### Environment
- **OS:** Arch Linux (x86_64)
- **App Version:** [Insira a versão do PhotoCraft/Photopea/App aqui, ex: v1.2.0 ou Web/Browser version]
- **Browser / Runtime:** [Ex: Ghostty / Chromium / Firefox / Brave - insira seu navegador]
- **Display Server / WM:** Wayland / X11 (Hyprland / custom WM)

### Additional Context
- No error dialogs appear in the UI when `Ctrl + Z` fails or when trying to delete the layer.
- Applying any distortion tool appears to break the active document context, causing state mutation to leak into global window state instead of remaining scoped to the active canvas.

title: Require CI to pass before merging into `main`, and enable auto-merge
author: Higgs32584
body:
## Summary

Protect `main` so a pull request can only merge after CI passes, and turn on GitHub's auto-merge so a maintainer can approve a PR once and have it merge by itself when the checks go green.

## Current state

- `main` has no branch protection and no required status checks (the only ruleset in the repository is `release`). A PR with failing or still-running CI can be merged.
- Auto-merge is not available on pull requests, so a maintainer has to come back after CI finishes (the `test` jobs take a while) to press Merge.

## Why

- A red PR can land on `main` by accident, and every branch based on it then inherits the failure.
- Contributors and maintainers both wait on CI. With auto-merge, a maintainer reviews, clicks "Enable auto-merge", and moves on; the PR merges when the checks pass, or stays open if they fail.
- The same applies after a contributor pushes a fix for a failed run: nobody has to remember to return to the PR.

## Proposal

1. **Required status checks on `main`** (branch protection rule or ruleset: "Require status checks to pass before merging").
2. **Allow auto-merge** (Settings › General › Pull Requests › "Allow auto-merge").
3. **One aggregate check to require**, rather than the individual jobs. `ci.yml` picks its jobs per PR: `select platforms` runs `test (windows-latest)` only when platform-sensitive paths change, and `web build and wasm size gate` only when the web build's inputs change. A required check that never starts stays "Expected" forever and blocks the PR, so `test (windows-latest)` cannot be required directly.

   Add a final job to `ci.yml`, for example `ci passed`, that:
   - `needs` every other job (`platforms`, `test`, `corpus`, `wasm`, `web`, `fuzz`),
   - runs with `if: always()`,
   - fails if any needed job failed or was cancelled, and passes when they succeeded or were skipped (`fuzz` is skipped on pull requests).

   Then require only `ci passed`.

## Open questions for maintainers

- Should required checks also dem…

title: UX: Compact UIs
author: awiebe
body: In general photoshop was invented when screen real-estate was at a premium, and was designed with professionals in mind. Its UI is finely tuned to balance legibility and and compactness so that the user can move their mouse the least possible to change tool selection or get through a menu. There is no UI design where there is a "big friendly button" with lots of padding space. And the buttons especially in the toolbar are crisp to make it obvious where each button is especially in older versions. Photocraft should consider this snappiness to be an important feature, not a visual afterthought. Here is the evolution of the photoshop toolbar Notice how up until some modern ugly redesigns it is very oblivious if your button is over the tool button you want. Also when if you click and hold a tools button it snaps open instantly because you know what you're doing, and the 2 up toolbar is the usual default mode.

title: Touchpad pinch gesture fails to zoom the canvas
author: FluorescentLava
body:
**Description**

When using a touchpad, the two-finger pinch gesture does not zoom in or out of the canvas. Instead, the canvas only pans along either the horizontal or vertical axis.

**Steps to Reproduce**
1. Open the canvas in PhotoCraft.
2. Place two fingers on the touchpad.
3. Perform a pinch-in or pinch-out gesture to zoom the canvas.

**Expected Behavior**

The canvas should zoom in or out according to the pinch gesture, similar to standard touchpad zoom behavior in other canvas-based applications.

**Actual Behavior**

The canvas only moves horizontally or vertically instead of zooming. The pinch gesture appears to be interpreted as a pan or scroll operation rather than a zoom gesture.

title: Dissolve layer blend mode has no visible effect
author: FluorescentLava
body:
**Description**

The Dissolve layer blending mode does not appear to work correctly. Enabling it produces no noticeable visual difference compared to the Normal blending mode.

**Steps to Reproduce**
1. Open an image in PhotoCraft.
2. Select a layer and change its blending mode from **Normal** to **Dissolve**.
3. Compare the rendered result with the Normal blending mode.

**Expected Behavior**

The Dissolve blending mode should produce its characteristic dithered transparency effect, distributing opaque and transparent pixels based on the layer's opacity.

**Actual Behavior**

The rendered result appears identical to the Normal blending mode, suggesting that the Dissolve blending mode has not been implemented correctly or is not being applied during rendering.

**Additional Notes**

Please verify that the Dissolve blending mode is correctly implemented in the rendering pipeline, including its interaction with layer opacity.

Although #3195 addresses Dissolve rendering in specific scenarios, this issue remains reproducible in v0.8.2.

title: Reports should be written by a validating program, not agents.  The agent can write the program to do this, but it should be a CI tool
author: awiebe
body:
`ui-parity.md` reads like a spaghetti of feels about various features.  It should read more like a specification and a Requirements Trackability matrix.  The generation of these should be done by a skill which actually runs a validation program it should not be what the agent hallucinates to be the case.

- A requirement is an atomic logical assertion stated in the positive voice.  You cannot test for the absence of something only its presence.  A test for absence must be time bounded.  
- An [RTM ](https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/software-testing/requirement-traceability-matrix/)is a table which maps a requirement to a test.
- A specification is a document which fully enumerates all requirements so that there is a definition for when the software is behaving as expected.


The specification should be grouped by parts of the program, and should be arranged as a hierarchical bulleted list.  Requirements may be given a shortname to make them easier to refer to if that helps with workflow.

An example of requirements statements would be as follow

### Rectangular selection tool  (1/5 20%) [TOOL-RECSEL]
- [ ] The rectangle selection is a tool mode selectable from the toolbar [TOOL-RECSEL]
  - [ ] The tool changes the selection state by replacing, adding, removing, unironing or intersecting a rectangular region with the current selection depending on mode or held modifier keys [TOOL-RECSEL-MODES]
  - [ ] The mode of the tool is shown in the tool properties window at the top of the UI [TOOL-RECSEL-INSPECTOR]
  - [ ] The mode of the tool defaults to replacing mode [TOOL-RECSEL-DEFAULTS]
  - [x] The icon for rectangular selection in the toolbar is a stippled rectangle [TOOL-RECSEL-ICON]

title: Vector: hostile paths can exhaust memory when flattened, dense dashes erase strokes, huge coordinates give NaN edges
author: vangel76
body:
Three robustness bugs in `crates/vector`, found while reading the crate:

1. **Unbounded flattening memory.** `flatten::pieces` lets every cubic split into up to 65536 pieces and `flatten_subpath` / `fill_rasterizer` / `stroke_rasterizer` put no cap on a whole path. Paths that never pass `validate_shape` reach these functions: vector masks imported from PSD (`vmsk`), compose vector masks, SVG import, effect outlines. Example: in a 1000 px document the segment `p0=(0,0) c1=(128000,-128000) c2=(-128000,128000) p1=(1000,1000)` flattens to ~6400 points; a 4 MB `vmsk` made of such segments asks for ~1e9 points and can abort the process on allocation.
2. **Over-budget dashes erase the stroke.** When `stroke::dash_polyline` hits its 100000-step guard it returns an empty list, so the whole stroke disappears (e.g. an SVG `stroke-dasharray="0.5 0.5"` on a 60000 px path). It should keep the dashes made so far and draw the rest solid.
3. **Huge finite coordinates produce NaN edges.** In `raster::Rasterizer::add_component`, coordinates around ±1e308 overflow `dxdy` to infinity, and `x_at` then returns NaN or infinity for that edge.

Expected: hostile paths render with bounded memory, a dense dash pattern never removes the stroke, and huge coordinates never produce NaN.

title: PSD: pattern memory budgets are per pattern, mixed-depth pattern channels are accepted, slice ids wrap
author: vangel76
body:
Found in a read-only audit of crates/psd (follow-up to #3652 / #3686).

1. **Pattern zero-padding budget is per pattern only** (`patterns.rs` `read_pattern`). `MAX_PADDED_PATTERN_BYTES` (512 MiB) and the decoded-bytes cap are counted per pattern; nothing totals them across one `Patt`/`Pat2`/`Pat3` block, a `.pat` file (up to 100000 patterns), several pattern global blocks in one PSD, or the `patt` sections of an `.abr` (whose shared sample budget doesn't count patterns). A gray pattern with a 23170x23170 rectangle and one 1x1 raw channel is about 100 input bytes and commits 512 MiB of zeros; N copies get the process OOM-killed.
2. **Pattern channels with different depths are accepted** (`read_pattern`): `PsdPattern.depth` becomes the last channel's depth while earlier planes keep their own size, so the parsed pattern can't be written back (`write_pattern_block` then re-parse fails; the fuzz target `fuzz/fuzz_targets/patterns.rs` expects it to).
3. **Slice descriptor numbers wrap** (`slices.rs` `d_int` and callers): `LargeInteger`/`Double` values are cast with `as i32`/`as u32`, so a sliceID of 2^32+5 reads as 5 (and the v6 trailing descriptor then attaches its outsets to slice 5); bounds/outsets out of the i32 range wrap.

Expected: one budget per top-level parse (abr patterns charged to the abr budget), mixed channel depths rejected, out-of-range numbers rejected or clamped instead of wrapped.

title: PSD import: ResolutionInfo with cm display units opens at 2.54x the resolution (300 ppi becomes 762 ppi)
author: vangel76
body:
`crates/io/src/psd_import.rs` multiplies the ResolutionInfo (resource 1005) `hRes`/`vRes` by 2.54 when `hResUnit`/`vResUnit` is 2 (cm). Per the Adobe Photoshop File Formats Specification (ResolutionInfo: Fixed 16.16 `hRes` in pixels per inch, followed by the *display* unit), the stored value is always pixels per inch; the unit only says how Photoshop displays it. `photocraft_codecs::resolution::photoshop_resolution` already reads it that way ("Fixed 16.16 hRes / vRes are pixels per inch whatever display unit follows them").

Evidence from Photoshop-authored files in the psd-tools corpus (fetched by `cargo xtask corpus --all`): `artboard.psd` stores hRes = 300.0 with hResUnit = 2, `empty-layer.psd`/`.psb` and `empty-group.psd` store 72.0 with unit 2. Round ppi values, not 118.11 / 28.35 px/cm. PhotoCraft opens `artboard.psd` at 762 ppi and the others at 182.88 ppi. Since the type engine converts points with the document resolution, text in such files is affected too.

Fix: read `h_res()`/`v_res()` as ppi whatever the unit; correct the `psd::ResolutionInfo` doc comment; update the two tests that assert the conversion (`tests/resolution_axes.rs`, `tests/psd_structure.rs::resolution_in_cm_converted`).

Found in an audit of `crates/io`.

title: io: unchecked usize arithmetic on file-derived sizes in PSD import (overflows on 32-bit / wasm32)
author: vangel76
body:
Several file-derived sizes in `crates/io` are multiplied without overflow checks. `usize` is 32 bits on wasm32, where these wrap (release) or panic (debug):

- `psd_import.rs` `unicode_names`: `at + n * 2` with `n` a u32 from resource 1045 (alpha channel names).
- `psd_import.rs` `psd_to_document_with`: `let n = w * hh` (header allows 300000x300000) and `h.row_bytes() * hh` for the merged planes. A 1-bit Bitmap plane can decode within the budget while `w * hh` does not fit in 32 bits.
- `adjust_map.rs` `parse_gradient_map`: `at += 4 + be32(d, at)? as usize * 2` (gradient name length).

Fix: `checked_mul`/`checked_add` and stop (or skip with a warning) when they overflow.

Found in an audit of `crates/io`.

title: Vector: stroke expansion has no point budget (dashed round-cap strokes can reach ~1e8 points)
author: vangel76
body:
Stroke expansion in `crates/vector/src/stroke.rs` has no point budget after flattening.

`stroke_polygons` emits one round cap per dash end and one round join per corner. A round cap is a full circle tessellated with `ceil(TAU / arc_step(hw, tol))` points; `arc_step` is clamped at 0.01 rad, so a wide stroke gets ~629 points per cap. The dash step guard in `dash_polyline` (100k steps) is per polyline, so a dashed, round-capped stroke can produce ~50k dashes per subpath, each with two ~629-point caps: on the order of 1e8 points (gigabytes) from one stroke, and more with many subpaths.

Reachable from imported data that is not validated: SVG `stroke-dasharray` with round caps and PSD `vstk` stroke styles (shape strokes rendered through `stroke_rasterizer`).

Expected: a total budget for the stroke outline. Under the budget the output is unchanged; above it round caps and joins degrade to fewer segments (and the dash step budget is shared by all subpaths), but no stroke is dropped.

Found while working on #5195.

title: [Bug Report] [PhotoCraft] Object disappears during Ctrl + T transform when a mask is applied
author: ticket-craft
body:
### Description

Hello ArtCraft Team 💙

I'm experiencing an issue when using Ctrl + T to transform an object that has a mask applied to it.

When I press Ctrl + T, the object disappears, but the transform bounding box and outlines remain visible. The object reappears when I press Enter to confirm the transformation or Esc to cancel it.

This happens whether I select the mask itself or the object that the mask is applied to. The issue appears to be related to objects with masks, as I don't experience the same problem with objects without masks.

Steps to reproduce:

- Open a project containing an object with a mask applied.
- Select the object or its mask.
- Press Ctrl + T.
- The object disappears while the transform outlines remain visible.
- Press Enter or Esc, and the object reappears.

**Expected behavior** : The object should remain visible while using Ctrl + T.

title: feat(channels, io): Spot Color channels and multichannel CMYK TIFF export for print/UV RIP workflows
author: ModularKarma1
body:
### Summary

Add first-class support for **Spot Color Channels** (`New Spot Channel...`, `Channel Options`, `Merge Spot Channel`) in the document model, compositor, and PSD/TIFF codecs so PhotoCraft can be used in professional print, screen printing (serigraphy), and UV/DTF large-format plotter workflows.

Currently, commercial RIP software (such as Onyx, SAi FlexiPRINT, Caldera, and Honsoft) relies on **CMYK TIFF or PSD files containing additional Spot Channels** (typically named `White`, `W1`, `Varnish`, `Gloss`, or Pantone spot names) to drive specialty ink heads on hybrid UV and packaging printers.

---

### Current Behavior & Limitations

1. **Alpha vs. Spot Channel distinction:** The `Channels` panel currently supports composite color channels and standard Alpha channels, but lacks `Spot Channel` properties:
   - Custom ink/channel name (e.g., `White`, `Varnish`)
   - Display preview color (RGB/CMYK/Lab representation for on-screen preview)
   - `Solidity` percentage (0–100% ink opacity simulation in the canvas composite)
2. **TIFF Extra Channels dropped on export:** As noted in the codec matrix, the TIFF encoder currently writes at most a single transparency channel and discards additional alpha/spot channels. Exporting a CMYK document with `White` and `Varnish` masks to `.tif` strips the extra plates needed by the RIP.

---

### Proposed Implementation Scope

#### 1. Document Model & Command Registry
- Extend the channel model to distinguish between **Alpha** (mask/selection) and **Spot** (specialty ink plate) channels.
- Wire commands in the registry:
  - `channel.newSpotChannel` (with Name, Color, and Solidity 0–100%)
  - `channel.channelOptions` (switching between Masked Areas, Selected Areas, and Spot Color)
  - `channel.mergeSpotChannel`

#### 2. CPU Reference Oracle & `wgpu` Compositor
- When a Spot Channel is visible alongside composite channels, composite the spot plate over the canvas using its preview color and `Solidity` value without altering the…

title: filter.render.fibers does nothing on an empty layer

`filter.render.fibers` on an empty (fully transparent) layer does nothing: the layer stays empty, and a following `edit.transform` on it fails with `nothing to transform`.

In Photoshop, Filter › Render › Fibers fills the layer regardless of its content (it renders from the foreground/background colours and doesn't read the existing pixels).

2. `filter.render.fibers` with default params.
3. The layer is still transparent; `edit.transform` reports `nothing to transform`.

**Workaround:** fill the layer first, then run Fibers.

Found while scripting a texture; version 0.8.2 (dev build, current main).

title: layer.setProps: opacity above 1 is clamped silently (layerStyle uses 0..100)
author: switch87
body:
`layer.setProps {"opacity": 55}` is accepted without an error and sets the layer to 100 %. Values above 1 are clamped silently.

`layer.setProps` takes opacity as 0..1, while the `layerStyle.*` commands take 0..100. Mixing the two scales is easy when scripting, and the silent clamp hides the mistake: the result looks plausible (an opaque layer) instead of failing.

**Expected:** either reject values outside 0..1 with an error that names the range (`opacity must be 0..1, got 55`), or use one scale across commands. A clear error seems the least disruptive.

Version 0.8.2 (dev build, current main).

title: select.colorRange "blues" misses muted navy (#3d3f54)
author: switch87
body:
`select.colorRange {"select": "blues"}` returns an empty selection on a muted navy area. The test image was a billiard cloth photographed in normal light, average colour `#3d3f54` (hue ≈ 235°, saturation ≈ 28 %, brightness ≈ 33 %).

The hue is squarely blue, so it's the saturation/brightness gate of the preset that drops it. Photoshop's Blues preset is also weighted towards saturated colours, so this needs checking against Photoshop on the same pixels before deciding what the right output is. Filing it so it gets checked.

**Steps:** fill a layer with `#3d3f54` (or open a photo of dark blue cloth) and run `select.colorRange {"select": "blues"}`; the selection is empty.

Version 0.8.2 (dev build, current main).

title: select.colorRange: sample points outside the active selection are refused
author: switch87
body:
`select.colorRange` with `points` refuses sample points that lie outside the active selection.

In Photoshop, Color Range with an active selection limits the *result* to that selection, but you can still sample colours anywhere in the image. Here the samples themselves are rejected, so you can't, for example, pick a colour from a reference area and select it only inside the selection.

**Expected:** accept sample points anywhere in the document and only clip the resulting selection to the active selection.

Version 0.8.2 (dev build, current main).

title: select.object fails silently on an empty active layer
author: switch87
body:
`select.object` fails silently when the active layer is empty. It defaults to `sampleAllLayers: false`, finds nothing on the empty layer, and returns without an error. The failure only shows up at the next `select.saveSelection`, which then complains about an empty selection.

This happens easily when scripting: you add a new layer and then run the selection on the photo below.

title: a_system_arabic_face_renders_both_samples fails when an installed font claims Arabic but has blank glyphs
author: prekabreki
body:
## Context
The test, added with the Arabic font-menu sample (#2535), picks the first installed family whose character map covers the Arabic sample and expects that sample to render.
A font can map those characters to empty glyphs. On one Linux machine, the free decorative font "Black Mountain" (`BlackMountain-vmlBZ.ttf` in `~/.local/share/fonts`) sorts first: its layout has bounds, but the ink rect is empty, so `render` correctly returns `None`. The test then panics with `Arabic sample` at `font_preview.rs:253`, on clean `main` (99e11388).
The app is fine; the font menu just omits the Arabic sample for that font. The test's assumption is the bug, and it turns `cargo test` red for any contributor with such a font installed.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The test picks the first candidate family whose Arabic sample actually renders (`images(..).arabic.is_some()`), and skips with its existing message if none does.
- [ ] For that family it still asserts the sample's size and that it has ink.
- [ ] It still exercises every candidate through `images()` without panicking.

## Files / where this lives
- `crates/ui-egui/src/font_preview.rs`: test `a_system_arabic_face_renders_both_samples` (line 244)

## How to verify
- `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib a_system_arabic_face_renders_both_samples`
- It only reproduces with a blank-glyph Arabic-claiming font installed (for example Black Mountain, a free download). Without one, the test passes both before and after.

## Constraints
- Test-only change; `sample_texts` and `render` behaviour stay as they are.
- Never commit a font to reproduce it (AGENTS.md › fonts).

## ⚠ Danger zones (review focus)
- Don't let the fix weaken the test into always skipping: on a machine with Arabic fonts that render (DejaVu Sans, Vazirmatn), it must still assert a real Arabic sample.

## Notes
- Executor: cheap.

title: Linked Masks follow-up: Puppet Warp Live Preview, Smart Objects, and further tool testing
author: TomerFaraj
body:
First of all, thank you for the immediate fixes regarding the linked masks in #4989
Following up on the remaining edge cases and recent PR notes, here are some findings regarding how these tools should handle linked masks:

**1. Puppet Warp Live Preview & Mesh Calculation (Raster Layers):**
I checked how the original Photoshop handles this on raster layers: it builds the mesh only around the visible (unmasked) areas, and essentially crops/discards the hidden pixels outside the mask during the calculation. Currently, the live preview ignores the mask and builds the polygons around the entire unmasked image.

**2. Smart Objects (and other non-raster layers):**
The linked mask behavior still needs an implementation for Smart Objects (and potentially other non-raster layer types). I think implementing this on Smart Objects should actually be simpler, since it doesn't have the same complex questions of "what to do with the live preview" or "how to lay the polygons" destructively.

**3. Further Testing on Other Manipulation Tools:**
Regarding the other tools mentioned previously (like Perspective Warp with active selections, and Content-Aware Scale), I think similar linked-mask logic applies to them as well. I don't have Photoshop myself, so I'm just putting it out there—these tools are a bit complex, and some high-quality testing should be done to make their behavior whole, usable, and identical to the expected industry standard.

title: Linux Wayland: a virtual keyboard (RustDesk) is taken for a pen, so the window opens through Xwayland and is blurred at fractional scales
author: dutraroberto
body:
## Summary

On a Wayland session with a fractional display scale, the PhotoCraft UI is blurred even after #1237. The cause is not the scale logic. PhotoCraft opens its window through Xwayland because it detects a pen that does not exist: a uinput virtual keyboard (RustDesk's here) advertises `BTN_TOOL_PEN`, and `has_pen` in `apps/photocraft/src/tablet.rs` treats any device with that key as a pen (#639).

## Environment

- Zorin OS, GNOME Shell 46.0, Wayland session
- LG 4K display (3840×2160) at 125% fractional scale
- RustDesk installed; no pen tablet, pen display, or touchscreen attached
- PhotoCraft 0.8.2 built from `main` at `99e11388`
- Preferences: UI Scale = Auto, Linux display server = Auto

## Steps to reproduce

1. On a Wayland desktop set to a fractional scale (125%), have a uinput keyboard that advertises every key code (installing RustDesk creates one).
2. Start PhotoCraft from a terminal with no extra environment variables.

## Actual behavior

stderr prints:

    photocraft: pen found; opening the window through Xwayland, where the pen works (PHOTOCRAFT_NATIVE_WAYLAND=1 keeps Wayland)

The window is an X11 client. `xlsclients` does not list it, but `xwininfo -root -tree` does:

    0x1e00004 "PhotoCraft": ("" "ai.storyteller.photocraft")  3072x1696+0+32

The Xwayland screen is the logical size (3072×1728, `Xft.dpi: 120`), so the app renders at 1.25 pixels per point into a 3072 px wide window and the compositor enlarges it by 1.25 to 3840 px. The whole UI is blurred, and it is effectively at about 156% instead of 125%.

## Expected behavior

With no pen attached, the window opens on native Wayland and the UI is sharp at the system's fractional scale.

## Cause

The only device with `BTN_TOOL_PEN` on this machine is the virtual keyboard. It has no absolute axes (no `EV_ABS`, no `B: ABS=` line):

    I: Bus=0003 Vendor=1234 Product=5678 Version=0111
    N: Name="RustDesk UInput Keyboard"

title: PSD save: a document that compresses under 2 GB is still written as PSB (raw-size estimate)
author: davidmann4
body:
Part of #5106 (print-scale performance; found while measuring the large-file fixtures of #5107 / #5109).

## What goes wrong
Re-saving the generated 2.02 GB PSD fixture as `.psd` writes a **PSB** file, although the written file is only 1.75 GB, well under the 2 GB PSD limit.

`psd_size_exceeds_limit` → `estimate_psd_size` in `crates/io/src/psd_export.rs` sums the **uncompressed** size of every layer, mask and merged-image plane (plus fixed and per-layer overhead) and switches to PSB when that sum is over `PSD_MAX_FILE_SIZE` (2 GiB). The writer then RLE-compresses the channels, so the real file is often much smaller than the estimate. Any document whose raw pixel data is a bit over 2 GB but compresses below it is saved as PSB, which many tools that read PSD (and older Photoshop workflows that expect `.psd`) can't open. The same estimate is used by `multichannel_map.rs`.

## Expected
Photoshop's PSD format is limited to 2 GB per file; larger documents must be saved as Large Document Format (PSB). The decision should rest on the size of the file that would actually be written, so a document whose encoded PSD fits in 2 GB stays a PSD, and only one that really exceeds 2 GB falls back to PSB (the auto-PSB behaviour of #212 stays).

## Proposal
- Keep the cheap estimate as a fast path where it is conclusive (raw size under the limit → PSD; even the best-case compressed size over the limit → PSB).
- In between, decide on the encoded size (e.g. encode the channel data, which is compressed anyway, then pick the version from its real length), without a second full encode or doubled peak memory where avoidable.
- Tests: a synthetic document whose raw estimate is over a (test-lowered) limit but whose encoded size is under it stays PSD; one whose encoded size is over it becomes PSB; the 2 GB fixture test in `crates/io/tests/large_files.rs` (opt-in) checks the re-save stays PSD once #5109 lands.

title: Performance: repeat duplicate / paste of a 12 MP layer over budget (P9 / P11: 24 ms vs 20 ms)
author: davidmann4
body:
Part of #5106 (print-scale performance), scorecard perf rows P9 and P11.

## Numbers
`perf_scenarios` in release on main (6f850542, Windows 11, 32 threads, RTX 5070 Ti, idle, 15 reps), measured for #5106:

| Row | Scenario | Budget (p95) | Main (p95) |
|---|---|---|---|
| P8 / P10 | duplicate / paste a 12 MP layer, first time | 100 ms | 24 / 26 ms ✅ |
| P9 / P11 | duplicate / paste a 12 MP layer, **repeat** | 20 ms | 24 / 24 ms ❌ |

The repeat cases cost the same as the first ones, so nothing is reused between the first and the second duplicate/paste; the remaining cost is still to be measured (copy-on-write tile sharing, history snapshot, thumbnail or canvas refresh after the command are candidates).

## Proposal
Measure the stages of the repeat case first (release, `perf_scenarios --only "<P9/P11 scenario>"`, a throwaway probe for stage timings), fix the measured cost, keep results bit-identical (old path as the oracle in a test), and record before/after p50/p95 with machine load. Set `enforce = true` in `perf/budgets.toml` only if p95 is under budget with margin.

title: Web build: ship the wasm as compressed parts so the 24 MiB gate stops blocking PRs (tested on Cloudflare Pages)
author: zuujiscom
body:
## Summary

The 24 MiB gate in `packaging/web/package.sh` exists because Cloudflare Pages and Workers static assets reject any uploaded file over 25 MiB (#198). It is a limit on one file on one kind of host, not on what a browser can load. `main` sits about 150 KB under it, so any feature PR can fail CI on size alone (#2213, #3904, #3907; most recently #5186).

This proposes packaging the wasm as several small gzip files that the page reassembles while it loads. No file is ever near 25 MiB, however large the app grows, and Cloudflare Pages keeps working. I tested it with the real app on Cloudflare Pages.

It is an alternative to #4304, which removes the gate and asks hosts with a per-file cap to look elsewhere.

## Measurements

`main` at 99e11388, `trunk build --release`, macOS arm64, Rust 1.99:

| Form | Bytes |
|---|---:|
| `photocraft-web-<hash>_bg.wasm` (what the gate measures) | 25,018,540 |
| gzip -9 | 11,402,023 |
| Brotli -q 11 | 8,773,572 |

## What I tested

`docs/contributing.md` says never hand-write JS, so the loader is a small Rust crate, not a script.

1. Built the site as above, gzipped the wasm and split it into two files (6,000,000 and 5,402,023 bytes) listed in `app/parts.txt` (first line a marker, `photocraft-parts 1`), next to the app's own generated `photocraft-web.js`.
2. Added a bootstrap crate, `apps/photocraft-web-boot` (about 220 lines; `wasm-bindgen`, `web-sys` and the workspace's `flate2`). The page loads it through the loader Trunk already generates. It fetches the parts in order, pipes them through an identity `TransformStream` into `DecompressionStream("gzip")`, wraps the result in a `Response` typed `application/wasm`, and passes it to the app's generated `init` (imported with `#[wasm_bindgen(raw_module = "./app/photocraft-web.js")]`), so the browser still compiles while streaming. It builds to 94,179 bytes of wasm and 25,249 bytes of generated glue (38,772 and 20,914 without the `flate2` fallback described below); `clippy -D warnin…

title: History panel: the trash button can't delete a snapshot
author: davidmann4
body:
Split out of the History panel tracker #2966.

**What happens:** in the History panel the trash button always deletes the current history state (`history.deleteState`, `fn history` in `crates/ui-egui/src/panels.rs`). A snapshot can only be deleted with right-click › Delete. Clicking a snapshot returns the document to it as a new state, but the snapshot doesn't stay selected, so there is nothing for the trash to act on. Dragging a snapshot row onto the trash does nothing.

**Repro:**
1. Open any document, paint a stroke.
2. Click the camera button in the History footer → "Snapshot 1".
3. Click "Snapshot 1", then click the trash button.
4. The latest history state is deleted; "Snapshot 1" is still there.
5. Drag "Snapshot 1" onto the trash: nothing happens.

**Expected (Photoshop):** clicking a snapshot selects it (highlighted like the current state). The trash button, and the panel menu's Delete, then delete the selected snapshot instead of a state. Dragging a snapshot (or a state) onto the trash deletes it too.

The engine already has `history.deleteSnapshot {snapshot}` (#3545), so this is panel work: remember the selected snapshot, route trash / Delete / drop-on-trash to it, and harness tests for each.

title: Curves cannot be applied to non-colour channels
author: hidoba
body:
Two main things:
1. in Photoshop you can apply a curve using Ctrl/Cmd+M or a menu to any channel including color channels and non-color channels such as layer mask, saved selection, quick mask. In Photocraft currently it's only possible to apply a curve to a color channel.
2. in Photoshop whenever you open curves with a single channel selected, the curves window has only that channel in the channels popup. In Photocraft it contains all color channels.

I'm working on a fix and will open a PR.

**More details on expected behaviour**
- Colour components retain their corresponding curve colour—for example, Green has a green curve.
- Non-colour channels display their exact name from the Channels panel, including custom names, and use a neutral, untinted curve regardless of their overlay colour.

**Related work**

- [#4615](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/issues/4615) / [PR #4648](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/pull/4648): isolated channel transforms.
- [#2307](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/issues/2307) / merged [PR #2695](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/pull/2695): copying and pasting individual channels.
- Merged [PR #1078](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/pull/1078): pasting into targeted masks, alpha channels and Quick Mask.

title: Default active tool on startup should be Move tool (Photoshop parity)
author: safvanedge
body:
### Photoshop Parity / Expected Behavior

In Photoshop, the default active tool when the application is launched and before any tool is selected is the **Move tool** (`V`), which sits at the very top of the primary toolbar.

### Current Behavior

In PhotoCraft (`crates/ui-egui/src/state.rs`), `UiState::default()` initializes:

```rust
impl Default for UiState {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            tool: Tool::Brush,
            ...
```

As a result, launching PhotoCraft or creating a new document starts with the Brush tool active instead of the Move tool.

### Proposed Fix

Change `UiState::default().tool` from `Tool::Brush` to `Tool::Move` so that PhotoCraft defaults to the Move tool on launch, matching Photoshop's toolbar layout and standard behaviour.

title: Performance: Blend mode hover preview chugs
author: EuphoricPenguin
body:
When you hover to preview blend modes, performance tanks in the program. I'm not terribly sure what Photoshop does to avoid this problem, but a quick-and-dirty solution would just be to render the preview at a reduced resolution until the user selects an option. Another would be to render the preview over the view window with the gray background masked rather than the full res image, which would probably have a similar compute savings benefit. In most cases, the user's view will be a lower resolution than the full image. The final computation could then happen when the option is selected.

This feature was added in #1081 for reference.

title: Modernize History into a professional branching revision workspace
author: TheSeanLavery
body:
## Objective
Turn PhotoCraft History into a professional revision workspace: a fast, legible timeline for exploring alternatives, restoring exact document states, and understanding storage and recovery. The visual direction should feel modern and precise, with restrained typography, clear branch relationships, useful previews, and accessible controls rather than decorative effects.

## Existing fork capabilities to preserve
Inventory inspected from `TheSeanLavery/photocraft` main at `14c612c24b270ff62aaddd38bf64776c823f6003` on October 13, 2026. Existing behavior is the starting point, not a proposal to rebuild it.

| Capability | Current behavior / boundary |
|---|---|
| Shared memory and scratch cache | Copy-on-write document snapshots; 4 GiB managed RAM target shared across open documents; background spilling into compressed content-addressed native-format objects; deduplication and shared allocations on restore. This is a managed payload target, not a process RSS ceiling. |
| Unlimited retention | Unlimited action history and available-space scratch retention enabled by default; demand-grown storage, no fixed action-count or 8 GiB ceiling. Explicit numeric preferences select bounded compatibility mode. |
| Failure-aware storage | Failed writes, disk exhaustion and bounded writer backpressure preserve existing history. Further edits can be rejected before mutation; Retry storage retries admission. Read/decode failures leave the document and cursor unchanged. |
| Compact raster moves | Independently undoable integer translations retain a shared immutable source plus small offset descriptors. Unsupported masks/effects/content and coordinate cases use exact snapshots; paint strokes preserve changed tiles. |
| Branch preservation | Editing after undo retains the alternative path; stable state IDs, parent IDs and branch IDs identify states independently of row positions. Undo/redo follows the selected path. |
| Direct navigation | `history.jump` restores one destinati…

- The toolbox count is stale everywhere it appears. `docs/gaps.md` G6 lists Color Replacement, Add Anchor Point, Delete Anchor Point and Art History Brush as missing, but the first three are in the `Tool` enum on `main` (`crates/ui-egui/src/state.rs`; landed in #1045 and #1044). title: Docs: headline numbers disagree with each other and with the code
author: Higgs32584
body:
Some figures in the hand-written docs are stale or contradict other docs:

- **Oracle floor.** `ROADMAP.md` focus item 1 says "Photoshop-oracle floor 133 → 200+ of 256". `docs/gaps.md` G1 says 145 of 258, and the floor in `crates/io/tests/corpus.rs` (`PHOTOSHOP.pass_floor`) is 145.
- **Open issues.** `ROADMAP.md` "Why alpha" says 579 open issues; there are 953 (2026-10-13).
- **Workspace size.** `docs/architecture.md` "Current state" says ~393,000 lines of Rust in ~1,020 files and ~5,460 `#[test]` functions. `main` has ~539,000 lines in ~1,310 `.rs` files and ~8,040 `#[test]` functions.
- **Layer filters.** `README.md` lists "layer filters" as a feature. Only the Kind filter exists (five toggle buttons, Pro themes); the "Kind" box next to them is a static label (`crates/ui-egui/src/panels.rs`, `Sense::hover()`), and the other Photoshop filter types are not implemented (see #5048).

title: Docs: architecture.md's design principles no longer describe the UI layer
author: Higgs32584
body:
`docs/architecture.md` still states two goals from the 2026-09-30 design plan that the code has moved away from, and its "Deviations from the plan" list doesn't mention them:

- **"The UI can be swapped without touching the core."** The core still doesn't depend on egui (enforced by `cargo xtask layers`), but `crates/ui-egui/src` now has ~290 hand-written egui modules; `transform_tool.rs` alone is ~4,900 lines of tool logic written against egui types. Swapping toolkits would mean rewriting the largest crate. The same doc's current-state summary already says "UI toolkit: decided: egui/eframe".
- **Principle 3, "Data describes the UI … not about 150 bespoke dialogs."** Most dialogs and tool interactions are bespoke egui code (`*_ui.rs`), not generated from parameter schemas or overlay primitives.

Decision needed: either restate these as current principles (and track the work to get back to them), or record them as deviations so contributors and agents don't design against a goal the project has dropped.

title: Docs: progress-doc status lines have grown into change logs
author: Higgs32584
body:
The status line at the top of each progress doc (`> **Last reviewed:** … · **Last updated:** … · **Change:** minor (…)`) is meant to say what the latest change was. In practice each update prepends its note and nothing is removed, so the `Change:` parenthetical has become a running log. In `docs/gaps.md` it lists over a dozen separate changes; `docs/ui-parity.md` and `docs/target-app-parity.md` are similar.

The same information is already in each doc's "Revision history" table, so the status line could carry only the latest change. Worth confirming against craftrules `standards/progress-docs.md` and then trimming them once.

title: Docs: ROADMAP.md and docs/roadmap.md overlap and are easy to confuse
author: Higgs32584
body:
There are two roadmap files: `ROADMAP.md` (the one-page parity summary: stage, headline numbers, dimensions, focus) and `docs/roadmap.md` (milestones M0–M12, alpha gate, current focus, releases). Both carry a "current focus" list and release information, they are updated separately, and they have drifted (for example the release list in `docs/roadmap.md` stopped at 0.6.0 while `ROADMAP.md` had other figures).

Options: rename `ROADMAP.md` to say what it is (a parity summary), or merge the overlapping sections so each fact lives in one place and the other file links to it.

title: AGENTS.md: the required dev-log entry goes to a gitignored, local-only file
author: Higgs32584
body:
`AGENTS.md` §5 asks every contributor to "append a terse entry to `log/devlog.md` (what landed, numbers, what's still open)", and §4 tells agents to pick work from the "Still open" bullets of recent entries. But `/log` is in `.gitignore` (§7 also says "`log/` (local, gitignored)"), so an entry only exists on the machine that wrote it. For outside contributors and fresh clones the log is empty, and the "how the next agent picks up" purpose doesn't work.

Either track a shared log (or move the "still open" notes into issues or PR descriptions, which are already shared), or drop the requirement for contributors outside the maintainers' machines.

title: Docs: hour estimates are calibrated on 1,004 merged PRs; recalibrate or date them
author: Higgs32584
body:
`ROADMAP.md`, `docs/gaps.md` and `docs/target-app-parity.md` give remaining effort in "Opus 5.5 agent wall-clock hours … calibrated from this repository's 1,004 merged PRs" (2–9 h per checklist item, 8–20 h per format or subsystem). That calibration is from around 2026-10-10; several times as many PRs have merged since, so the per-item rates (and every hour range built on them) may no longer hold.

Suggest re-running the calibration on current merge data, or at least stating the date it was taken next to each estimate table.

title: Reduce avoidable work across large PSD parsing, loading and first display
author: TheSeanLavery
body:
Opening large PSDs still performs avoidable copying, decompression, intermediate rendering and display work. Track the related changes together so parser ownership, tile storage, upload lifetimes and render-cache behavior remain consistent.

Context: PR #2575 reported a 36 MP opening regression, but its historical comparison spans many commits. A separate fixed-file experiment does not identify one culpable commit. On a Ryzen 7950X3D / RTX 3090, the current fork and historical reference are effectively tied before optimization (~621/623 ms); the retained import prototype measures ~250 ms. Complex eight-layer PSD: ~287 → 136 ms. These are in-memory import + full-canvas GPU completion measurements, excluding disk, GPU initialization and UI presentation; not an exact replay of CI P44.

## Sequential implementation plan

- [x] Harden and retain concurrent channel decoding, direct RGBA8 plane-to-tile assembly, reduced interleave copies and prevalidated bounded RLE row decoding.
- [x] Upload native RGBA8/GRAY8 tile bytes directly instead of copying them into an owned conversion buffer. Preserve shared tile deduplication and ordered writes.
- [x] Introduce a borrowed/shared-byte import representation to avoid parser-owned copies of compressed layer channels and merged-image data; keep the existing owned PSD API and byte-stable round trips.
- [x] Fuse ordinary raster Content + Blend passes to avoid intermediate full-resolution writes/reads. Preserve a fallback for effects, clipping, channel restrictions and other complex semantics.
- [x] Investigate adaptive first-open prefix-cache admission. Compare opening plus subsequent edits; do not permanently disable useful editing caches merely to improve the opening timer.
- [x] Remove single-channel mask intermediates and avoid materializing Photoshop-rendered bitmap masks that the importer immediately discards. Preserve real-mask precedence and malformed-channel warnings.
- [x] Reuse already-decoded merged planes on flattened imp…

title: Suggestion: module-level reviewers and a public path to becoming a maintainer
author: nevicia2010-hub
body:
### Suggestion

Could PhotoCraft pilot module-level reviewers and publish a path for trusted contributors to become maintainers?

I use several Craft apps and have submitted fixes. Community contributions are growing quickly, and the recent integration batches show substantial effort to review and combine them. A small group still appears to handle much of the final integration in the public records; those records do not reveal the full team or any internal plans.

A lightweight pilot could help spread that work:

1. **Publish an opt-in area/reviewer map.** For example: RAW/Camera Raw and masks, PSD/file compatibility, rendering/performance, text/fonts, and native UI. List a contact and a backup where volunteers are available, with uncovered areas left visible. Start with a few areas; a short document is enough, with CODEOWNERS optional later.
2. **Start with review responsibility.** Experienced contributors could reproduce reports, check regressions and review changes in their area before receiving write access. Publish how someone volunteers, what evidence builds trust, and how maintainers decide on additional permissions. Review assignments and merge authority can develop separately.
3. **Keep cross-cutting decisions coordinated.** Changes to shared interfaces, dependencies, security, packaging or releases would still go through the appropriate core maintainers. Area reviewers could prepare focused, tested batches and identify interactions between PRs.
4. **Make the next action visible.** A few labels such as “needs reviewer”, “needs author update”, “needs maintainer decision” and “ready for integration” would help volunteers direct their effort.

Related discussions already address parts of the coordination problem: #3561 proposes avoiding duplicate work, [DesignCraft #259](https://github.com/storytold/designcraft/issues/259) shows contributors helping with focused review and integration, and [craft-libs #94](https://github.com/storytold/craft-libs/issues/94) di…

title: Pen input from Sunshine/Moonlight virtual pen (Apple Pencil on iPad)
author: BluePhi09
body:
## Request
Pen input should work when PhotoCraft runs on a PC that is streamed to an iPad with **Sunshine (host) + Moonlight (client)** and drawn on with an Apple Pencil.

Moonlight forwards Apple Pencil input (pressure, tilt, hover, eraser) to Sunshine, which injects it on the host as a virtual pen device (uinput tablet on Linux, Windows pen injection on Windows). PhotoCraft sees it as an ordinary tablet pen, so the existing pen paths have to handle it.

## What exists today (from reading the repo)
- `crates/tablet` + `crates/ui-egui/src/stylus.rs`: pressure, tilt, rotation, eraser end via AppKit (macOS) and XInput2 (Linux X11).
- Windows: pressure only (WM_POINTER via winit); no tilt, rotation or eraser (#2285).
- Linux Wayland: no native `zwp_tablet_v2`; a pen only works through Xwayland (#79), and the pen does not click on GNOME 50 (#2622) or KDE (#2297).

## To check / do
- Test the Sunshine virtual pen on Linux (X11, Wayland via Xwayland, native Wayland) and Windows hosts and note which of pressure, tilt, hover and eraser arrive in PhotoCraft.
- Native Wayland tablet-v2 support, since the virtual pen is a libinput tablet tool.
- Tilt, rotation and eraser on Windows.
- Hover (proximity) events should move the brush cursor without painting.
- Document the Sunshine/Moonlight setup once it works.

## Related
#79, #759, #1302, #2285, #2297, #2622, #4620, #3294

title: Dropdowns: the Blend Mode menu opens with a scrollbar because popups are capped at 420 pt
author: davidmann4
body:
Every dropdown popup is capped at a fixed 420 pt (`egui::ComboBox ... .height(420.0)` at `crates/ui-egui/src/widgets.rs:1326` and `:1523` on main), so lists longer than that get a scrollbar even when the window has plenty of room. The Layers panel's Blend Mode menu (27 modes) is the most visible case: it opens with a scrollbar next to it.

That scrollbar is misleading together with #1747: the wheel over the open list steps the blend mode (as Photoshop does) instead of scrolling, so it looks like the list is broken ("the dropdown doesn't scroll, the blue selection bar jumps"). Reported publicly by a user.

**Photoshop:** the Blend Mode menu opens at full height, every mode visible, no scrollbar, as long as it fits on the screen.

**Expected:** dropdown popups are as tall as their items, up to the visible part of the window, and only scroll past that. `widgets::menu_scroll` (`widgets.rs:1475`) already does this for context menus (`work_area::visible_rect`, `MENU_MIN_HEIGHT`) and could be reused.

**Done when:** a test opens the Layers panel's Blend Mode dropdown in a tall window and finds all modes laid out without a scroll area offset/scrollbar, and a short window still scrolls.

title: Dialogs have no close (×) button in their title bar
author: davidmann4
body:
Dialogs drawn by the shared renderer (`crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs.rs`, `show()`: a title label + hairline, draggable title band since #1921) have no close button in the title bar. The only ways out are Cancel/OK or Esc. A few separate windows have no title bar at all and no close box either, e.g. Check Spelling (`type_panels_ui.rs:762`, `.title_bar(false)`). Reported publicly by a user ("a modal dialog doesn't even have a close button").

**Photoshop (Windows):** modal dialogs (Image Size, Gaussian Blur, Levels, …) have a title bar with a close (×) button; clicking it is the same as Cancel. On macOS Photoshop's modal dialogs have no close button, so this should follow the platform.

**Expected:** on Windows (and Linux), every modal dialog shows a × at the right end of its title band that cancels exactly like Cancel/Esc (same revert of live previews, same history behaviour). Dragging the title band keeps working.

**Done when:** a test opens a dialog through the shared renderer, clicks the × and gets the same result as Cancel; Check Spelling gets the same close box.

Please check the exact Photoshop look/behaviour by hand before building; this was written from the report and code reading.

title: Reset caret blink phase on navigation and typing in Type tool
author: safvanedge
body:
### Description

When editing text with the Type tool, the caret blinks at a steady ~0.53s cadence (`(time * 1000.0 / 530.0) as i64 % 2 == 0`).

However, because the blink phase was tied purely to absolute wall clock time, when navigating with arrow keys (or typing) while the rhythm happened to be in its "off" (invisible) half-cycle, the caret movement was visually hidden until the clock reached the next "on" half-cycle.

### Photoshop & Expected Behaviour

In Photoshop and standard OS text controls, pressing an arrow key, typing, or clicking immediately resets the caret blink phase to **visible (solid)**. The caret remains continuously visible while actively navigating or typing, and only resumes blinking after user input pauses for ~0.53s.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create or open any text layer with the Type tool.
2. Tap the left/right arrow keys across characters.
3. Observe: depending on the wall-clock phase, the caret is invisible while jumping between characters.

title: Restore previous tool on commit/cancel when text editing is started via double-click
author: safvanedge
body:
### Description

In PhotoCraft, double-clicking a text layer with the Move tool (`V`) or double-clicking a text layer thumbnail in the Layers panel begins an inline text editing session and switches `app.ui.tool` to `Tool::Type` (`edit_at` / `edit_active`).

However, when the user commits (`Ctrl+Enter`, Enter on numpad, or clicking Commit) or cancels (`Escape`), the application remained stuck on `Tool::Type` instead of returning to the tool that initiated the edit (`Tool::Move`).

### Photoshop & Expected Behaviour

In Photoshop:
1. When double-clicking text while on the Move tool, Photoshop enters text editing.
2. When committing with `Ctrl+Enter` or canceling with `Escape`, Photoshop returns to the **Move tool**.
3. Returning to the Move tool immediately re-displays the transform bounding box (if "Show Transform Controls" is enabled) and allows arrow keys to nudge the layer.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Select the Move tool (`V`).
2. Double-click any text layer on the canvas to edit it.
3. Press `Ctrl+Enter` to commit the text edit.
4. Observe: the active tool remains `Tool::Type` instead of returning to `Tool::Move`.

```
──────
Lighten, Screen, Color Dodge, Linear Dodge (Add), Lighter Color
──────
Overlay, Soft Light, Hard Light, Vivid Light, Linear Light, Pin Light, Hard Mix
──────
Difference, Exclusion, Subtract, Divide
──────
Hue, Saturation, Color, Luminosity
```

For a group layer, Pass Through comes first, in the first group.

**PhotoCraft (main):** `panels.rs:2243` builds the list from `blend_options(..)` and shows it through `widgets::dropdown_wheel_hovered`, which draws one `selectable_label` per option with no separators. The options bar's Mode dropdowns (Brush/Pencil/Gradient, `panels.rs:1266`, `panels.rs:3751`) go through the same widget.

**Expected:** separator lines between the groups above. The separators only change how the list looks. Wheel stepping (#1747), arrow keys, type-ahead (#1481), press-drag-release and Shift+Plus/Minus keep stepping through the modes in the same order, never landing on a separator.

**Done when:** a test opens the Layers Blend Mode dropdown and finds a separator between each pair of groups (5 in total), and the existing wheel, keys and type-ahead tests still pass unchanged.

Related: #5495, where the list opens at full height.

title: [Bug Report] [PhotoCraft] AppImage gets no menu entry when AppImageLauncher is installed
author: oddvalue
body:
## What happens

With AppImageLauncher installed, the 0.8.2 AppImage gets no launcher at all. Nothing shows up in the app menu, and after a launch `~/.local/share/applications` has no PhotoCraft entry.

I hit this upgrading from 0.3.0. When I deleted the old AppImage, AppImageLauncher removed its `appimagekit_*-PhotoCraft.desktop`, as it should. 0.8.2 never got a replacement.

## Why

Since #3641 (the #3623 fix), AppImageLauncher and AppRun each wait for the other to create the entry.

1. `ai.storyteller.photocraft.desktop` ships `X-AppImage-Integrate=false`, so appimagelauncherd skips the AppImage:
   ```
   Integrating: /home/jim/Applications/photocraft-0.8.2-linux-x86_64.AppImage
   WARNING: AppImage shall not be integrated, skipping
   ```
2. AppImageLauncher sets `DESKTOPINTEGRATION=AppImageLauncher` on every AppImage it launches through its binfmt bypass, including ones it declined to integrate. I confirmed this in `/proc/<pid>/environ` of another running AppImage. `packaging/linux/AppRun` (line 44) reads any non-empty `DESKTOPINTEGRATION` as "an external integrator owns this AppImage", so it doesn't write `ai.storyteller.photocraft.desktop`. If one exists from an earlier run, it deletes it.

Test 7 in `packaging/linux/apprun-test.sh` asserts the current behaviour: with `DESKTOPINTEGRATION=AppImageLauncher`, no entry gets written.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Install AppImageLauncher with the daemon on (the default).
2. Put `photocraft-0.8.2-linux-x86_64.AppImage` in `~/Applications` and launch it.
3. Run `ls ~/.local/share/applications | grep -i photocraft`. It returns nothing, and PhotoCraft isn't in the menu.

Environment: Ubuntu 26.04.1, AppImageLauncher 3.0.0-beta-2 (gha287~96cb937).

## Possible fix

PhotoCraft opts out of external integration, so `DESKTOPINTEGRATION=AppImageLauncher` doesn't tell AppRun that anything integrated it. AppRun could drop the `DESKTOPINTEGRATION` check and keep only the existing scan for a `.desktop` file whose `Exec=` already …

title: Text selection highlight is hidden while holding Command/Ctrl in Type tool
author: safvanedge
body:
### Summary
1. While editing text with the Type tool, holding the Command/Ctrl modifier key (for example, when pressing `Ctrl + A` to select all text, or performing shortcuts like `Ctrl + X` / `Ctrl + C`) causes the active text selection highlight and caret to disappear until `Ctrl` is released.
2. In addition, the temporary transform box displayed when holding `Ctrl` while typing drew an extra 3px shadow stroke, blue accent color, and center pivot crosshair, making it look over-bold and inconsistent with Photoshop. In Photoshop, holding `Ctrl` while editing type displays a crisp 1px dark bounding box with white handles (dark border), preserves the text baseline underline, and does not draw a center pivot circle.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Select the Type tool and click on the canvas (or double-click an existing text layer with the Move tool) to begin editing text.
2. Type some text.
3. Press `Ctrl + A` and keep `Ctrl` held down.

### Expected Behavior
- The selected text displays its selection highlight immediately while `Ctrl` is held down.
- The transform frame uses a clean 1px dark border with white square handles (matching Photoshop's Type Ctrl-transform appearance), without an exaggerated 3px shadow or unneeded pivot crosshair.

### Observed Behavior
While `Ctrl` is held, the selection highlight is completely invisible (only the temporary type-transform bounding box is rendered). The highlight only appears after `Ctrl` is released.

### Root Cause
In `crates/ui-egui/src/type_tool.rs:draw_overlay`:
```rust
    let mods = crate::workspace_ui::sticky_mods(app, painter.ctx().input(|i| i.modifiers));
    if crate::type_transform::draw(app, painter, xf, mods) {
        return;
    }
```
When `mods.command` is true (`Ctrl`/`Cmd` held), `type_transform::draw` draws the transform box and handles, and returns `true`. The early `return;` bypassed the remainder of `draw_overlay`, suppressing the drawing of the active selection polygon, caret, and baseline underline.

title: CI: PR runs wait 23–48 min queued for runners — demand (~5,000 runner-min/h) exceeds the free-tier 20-job ceiling
author: ahmedhosnypro
body:

Measured on 2026-10-13 (UTC), from the public Actions API: - **Live snapshot (16:10 UTC):** across active CI runs, **106 jobs queued / 6 executing**, 37 CI runs in `queued`/`in_progress`. - A *successful* PR run ([#8194](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/actions/runs/38414072002), `issue-4963`) took **87 min wall**, of which its `test (ubuntu-latest)` job **queued for ~48 min** and then executed in 38.7 min. `wasm32 check` waited 39 min to run for 1.9 min; `corpus tests` waited 23 min to run for 11 min. - Cancelled runs confirm it: [#8149](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/actions/runs/38417722889) was created 14:55 and its 9-second `select platforms` job never got a runner before cancellation **54 minutes later** (job had zero executed steps; `started_at` is stamped at queue time). - Run creation rate on 2026-10-13: 32 → 11 → 39 → **57 → 61 runs/hour** (12:00→16:00), mostly PRs from the parallel agent fleet, each spawning 5–7 jobs. At ~60 runs/h × ~5 jobs × ~25–40 min, demand is **~4,000–5,000 runner-minutes/hour** against a ceiling of **20 concurrent jobs × 60 = 1,200 runner-minutes/hour**. The backlog can't drain; observed execution concurrency was even below 20 (~6). ## Evidence 1 — a PR run is 5–7 parallel jobs, but the queue is the gate ```mermaid flowchart LR PR["PR opened or pushed"] --> Queue["Runner queue

title: Paragraph text with 60% horizontal scale wraps too early, leaving large unused space after PSD text re-render
author: RDuomer
body:
## Summary
PhotoCraft 0.8.2 on Windows x64 can show paragraph text wrapping prematurely after editing/resizing imported PSD paragraph text with character horizontal scale below 100%. The result is substantial unused space on the right of the paragraph box and a taller paragraph.

## Suggested minimal reproduction
Please test with a newly created synthetic paragraph, without any user artwork:
1. In Photoshop, create a paragraph text box with several sentences of placeholder text.
2. Set all character runs to 60% horizontal scale, with zero paragraph indents.
3. Save as PSD and open in PhotoCraft 0.8.2.
4. Enter text editing and drag a paragraph-box resize handle.
5. Compare line breaks and used width with Photoshop and with 100% horizontal scale.

This synthetic reproduction has not yet been executed as an automated test. The report is prompted by observed early wrapping during imported PSD paragraph editing.

## Expected
Line breaking should account for effective horizontally scaled character advances and make appropriate use of the available paragraph width.

## Suspected cause: public source inspection
In v0.8.2 crates/text/src/layout.rs, available paragraph width is passed to layout.break_all_lines(avail) before horizontal_scale is applied to cluster/glyph advances later in layout. style_props does not appear to pass horizontal_scale into shaping/line breaking. This suggests that a paragraph can be broken using unscaled advances and then rendered compressed, leaving unused space.
