title: Group Layers (Ctrl+G) should create group collapsed by default
author: safvanedge
body:
### Summary
In PhotoCraft, grouping selected layers (`Layer ▸ Group Layers` / `Ctrl + G` / `layer.groupLayers`) creates a new group that is expanded (`expanded: true`) by default in the Layers panel, keeping all child layers visible and expanded.

### Comparison with Photoshop (Target Parity)
In Adobe Photoshop, when you select multiple layers and press `Ctrl + G` (or `Layer ▸ Group Layers`), the newly created group folder is created **collapsed by default** (`> Group 1`). 

This immediately cleans up and condenses the Layers panel. If the user wants to see or work with the child layers inside, they click the disclosure triangle to expand it.

### Current Implementation
In `crates/engine/src/layer_multi_cmds.rs:1233`:
```rust
let gid = doc.insert_above(Some(top), Layer::group(name, vec![]));
```
`Layer::group` initializes `expanded: true` by default. When grouping layers via `layer.groupLayers`, the new group remains expanded rather than collapsed.

### Expected Behavior
`layer.groupLayers` should create the group with `expanded: false` (collapsed), matching Photoshop's layer grouping behavior.

title: [Feature Request] Commit text editing when clicking a layer in the Layers panel
author: remidesbois1
body:
Currently, when editing a text layer in PhotoCraft, clicking a layer row in the Layers panel does not automatically commit the active text edit. Users must manually press Escape or use another commit action before switching layers.

In Photoshop, clicking a layer in the Layers panel automatically commits the current text edit.

## Expected Behavior

While a text layer is being edited:

1. **Clicking the currently edited layer** in the Layers panel should commit the text edit, exit text editing mode, and keep the same layer selected.
2. **Clicking a different layer** should commit the text edit, exit text editing mode, and select the clicked layer.
3. The changes must be preserved, and the text must remain editable as a text layer.

This should work with a regular single click on the layer row, including its name or thumbnail.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create or select a text layer.
2. Enter text editing mode and type or modify some text.
3. Click the same text layer in the Layers panel.
4. Observe that the text editing session remains active instead of being committed.
5. Repeat by clicking another layer.

## Expected Result

title: [Feature Request]  Quick Warp Brush On Canvas
author: 0nnix
body:
Hi — first, two things I genuinely love about Photocraft and hope never change:

Paste-to-new-document on the Welcome screen. Open Photocraft, hit Ctrl+V, and it creates a document sized to the clipboard and pastes immediately. No "New Document" dialog, no picking resolution, no "create from clipboard" step. This is something I always wanted in other editors and it's already here. Please keep it.
The clean-slate advantage. You're building from scratch, which means you're not bound by legacy architecture. That's exactly why I'm writing this.
The request: a Quick Warp Brush that lives on the canvas.

In Photoshop, Liquify is a separate modal window. It's powerful, but for small adjustments it's painful: you leave the canvas, wait for the window to open, re-enable the backdrop, re-set the parameters, do a tiny nudge, close it, and come back. When all you wanted was to slightly pull a hand, a corner, or a face while still seeing the full composition.

The Smudge tool is not a substitute — it smears pixels instead of warping them. Different operation.

**What I'd love to see:**

A Quick Warp Brush on the canvas that reuses the Liquify engine you already have — same warp quality, same math, no modal dialog. Push, pull, pinch, bloat, twirl, directly on the layer, in place.

Quick Warp Brush (on canvas): fast, in-place nudging with full Liquify-quality warping. No dialog, no re-initialization, no parameter reset.

title: fix: saved workspaces never appear in the Workspace menu or switcher
author: drewaltukhov
body:
### What happens

After saving a layout with **Window › Workspace › New Workspace…**, the saved workspace doesn't appear anywhere in the UI where you could switch back to it:

- **Window › Workspace** lists only the six built-in workspaces (Essentials, Photography, Painting, Pixel Art, Graphic and Web, Motion), then Reset / New / Delete.
- The **workspace dropdown in the top bar** lists the same six.

The save itself works. The workspace is stored in preferences and becomes current, and its name shows up in **Delete Workspace…**. But once you switch to a built-in workspace, the UI has no way back to the saved one. The only route is the control protocol (`window.workspace.select {"name": "…"}`).

None of the presets shows a check mark while the saved workspace is current, so nothing indicates which workspace is active.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Arrange some panels.
2. Window › Workspace › New Workspace…, enter a name, OK.
3. Open Window › Workspace (or the top-bar workspace dropdown).

**Expected:** the saved workspace is listed (in Photoshop, custom workspaces appear in the Workspace menu and switcher), checked while it is current, and selectable.
**Actual:** only the six presets are listed.

Seen on macOS with the native menu bar.

### Where it comes from (as of c699e3c)

- `crates/ui-egui/src/menu_catalog.rs:730-741`: the Window › Workspace submenu is a static list of the six presets.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/panels.rs:639-646`: the top-bar dropdown options are a hard-coded array of the same six.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/menus.rs:840-843` + `workspace_name()` (`menus.rs:133-143`): check marks only map preset ids.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/workspace_ui.rs:216-226`: `select_workspace` already handles saved names (`window.workspace.select`), so the backend is there. It just isn't wired to any menu item or to the dropdown.

title: Deleting the last smart filter keeps its filter mask, so the next smart filter is clipped to the old selection
author: davidmann4
body:
## What goes wrong
`layer.smartFilter.delete` removes the filter from `smart_filters` but never clears `filter_mask` when the list becomes empty. `add_smart_filter` only creates a mask from the current selection when `filter_mask.is_none()`, so the next smart filter reuses the old mask.

## Repro
1. Convert a layer to a smart object.
2. Select the left half and run Gaussian Blur: the filter mask is the left half.
3. Run `layer.smartFilter.delete {}`: no filters remain, the mask stays.
4. Select the right half and run Gaussian Blur again: the blur lands on the **left** half. With no selection the new filter is still clipped to the old mask.

## Where
`crates/engine/src/smart_cmds.rs` `delete_filter` (and the single-filter move in `transfer_filters`). `layer.smartFilter.clearSmartFilters` and moving all filters already clear the mask.

## Expected
As in Photoshop: deleting the last smart filter removes the filter mask too; the next filter gets a mask from the current selection (or none).

title: Lens Correction, Adaptive Wide Angle and Camera Raw Filter add smart filters to locked smart objects
author: davidmann4
body:
## What goes wrong
On a smart object with Lock All (or locked pixels), `filter.lensCorrection`, `filter.adaptiveWideAngle` and `filter.cameraRaw` succeed and add a smart filter plus a history step.

## Repro
1. Convert a layer to a smart object and lock it (Lock All).
2. Run `filter.lensCorrection {"distortion":10}`.
3. It returns OK and a Lens Correction smart filter is added.

## Where
`crates/engine/src/lens_cmds.rs` `run_filter`: the `LayerContent::Smart` branch returns before the `locks.all || locks.pixels` check. Generic filters (`filters.rs`) check locks first; #4123 fixed the same gap for Liquify, Puppet Warp and Perspective Warp.

## Expected
The command is refused with a "layer is locked" error, nothing is added, no history step.

title: Image › Trap changes the pixels of locked layers
author: davidmann4
body:
## What goes wrong
`image.trap` writes to the active layer without checking its locks, so it changes a layer with Lock All, locked pixels, or one inside a locked group.

## Repro
1. CMYK document with a pixel layer; lock the layer (Lock All).
2. Run `image.trap {"width":1}`.
3. It returns `{"trapped":true}` and the pixels change.

## Where
`crates/engine/src/trap_cmds.rs`: neither `run` nor `enabled` calls `check_pixels_unlocked`, unlike other pixel edits.

## Expected
The command is refused with a "layer is locked" error and the pixels stay unchanged.

title: New Guide Layout turns Rows on by itself and adds guides at the top and bottom
author: davidmann4
body:
## What goes wrong
With the default layout (columns 8, rows 0), View › Guides › New Guide Layout… shows Rows **checked** after the first frame, and OK adds horizontal guides at the top and bottom of the canvas.

## Repro
1. Open View › Guides › New Guide Layout… with defaults.
2. The Rows checkbox becomes checked without any input; the preview shows top/bottom guides.
3. Click OK: horizontal guides are added. Alt+Reset triggers it again.

## Where
`crates/ui-egui/src/guide_layout_ui.rs` `number()`: the (disabled) Rows "Number" field is drawn with range `1.0..=1000.0`. egui's DragValue clamps the existing value 0 → 1 and reports a change, which is written to `f["rows"]`; the checkbox falls back to `positive(f, "rows")`.

## Expected
Opening the dialog changes nothing: Rows stays off and OK adds only the column guides.

title: FITS: a 32-bit image with a value above 2.0 reopens almost black
author: davidmann4
body:
## What goes wrong
A 32-bit document saved as FITS reopens almost black when any sample is above 2.0.

## Repro
1. 32-bit grayscale image with samples `[0.5, 3.0]` (one hot highlight).
2. Save as FITS, reopen.
3. Samples are `[0.5/65535, 3/65535]`: black. No warning on save.

## Where
`crates/codecs/src/codecs/fits.rs`: the writer stores F32 samples unclamped (the module doc promises `BITPIX = -32, 0..1`); the reader picks the white point from the data maximum (`max <= 2.0 → 1`, `<= 65535 → 65535`). `fidelity.rs` only warns `RangeClipped` for float → integer saves.

## Expected
A FITS save round-trips: values are stored in the documented 0..1 range (with a range-clipped warning when HDR values had to be clipped), and the file reopens as it looked when saved.

title: Feature Request: Enhancement of the Brush Engine inspired by Paint Tool SAI, Black Ink, and Procreate
author: NeytJA
body:
Hi PhotoCraft Team,

First of all, thank you for building such an incredible open-source project! The performance and the pure Rust architecture look extremely promising.

Since PhotoCraft is currently in early alpha and aiming to become a powerful tool for creators, I would love to suggest an area for deeper improvement: the brush engine. While the current feature list mentions solid foundational brush mechanics, digital artists heavily rely on organic, highly responsive, and customizable stroke dynamics.

It would be absolutely amazing if the brush engine could take inspiration from software known for their legendary brush feel and specialized rendering:

• Paint Tool SAI: Renowned for its unparalleled, ultra-smooth line stabilization (mathematical smoothing) and realistic color blending/bleeding that feels like real paint.
• Black Ink: Famous for its generative, node-based brush system that allows creating non-traditional, algorithmic, and highly stylized brushes.
• Procreate: Celebrated for its dual-brush combination system and fluid, low-latency performance with Apple Pencil / modern tablets.
• Corel Painter / Clip Studio Paint: Great examples of rich physics-based particle brushes and deep texture integration.

Focusing on unique brush math, powerful stabilizer algorithms, and customizable blending profiles would attract not just photo editors, but a huge community of digital painters and concept artists to the ArtCraft ecosystem.

Thank you for your hard work, and looking forward to seeing how PhotoCraft evolves!

title: Type: Editing an existing text layer resets subscript formatting (e.g., C₂ becomes C2)
author: cherry-hur-47
body:
When editing an existing type layer that contains subscript formatting (such as chemical formulas like C₂), entering text edit mode (clicking the text with the Type tool) strips the subscript formatting and converts the glyph back to regular full-size text (C2).

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Open a PSD document containing a text layer with subscript text (or create text with a subscript character).
2. Select the Horizontal Type Tool (T).
3. Click into the text layer to place the caret and edit the text.
4. Observe the subscript character.

### Expected Behavior (Photoshop Parity)
The character should retain its subscript character styling, baseline shift, and font size scaling during active text editing, exactly as in Adobe Photoshop.

### Actual Behavior
The subscript formatting is stripped, and the character immediately reverts to a standard baseline character (e.g., C₂ reverts to C2).

title: Shortcuts: Repeatedly pressing a tool shortcut cycles through the tool group instead of requiring Shift
author: cherry-hur-47
body:
Pressing a tool's shortcut key repeatedly cycles through all tools within that tool group (e.g., pressing 'V' cycles between Move and Artboard; pressing 'B' cycles through Brush, Pencil, Mixer Brush, etc.). 

In Photoshop, pressing a primary tool shortcut key selects that specific tool and keeps it active. Cycling through tools in the same group should require holding `Shift + [Key]` (e.g., `Shift + V` or `Shift + B`), or strictly adhere to the "Use Shift Key for Tool Switch" preference.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Select any tool that has a sub-group (e.g., Move Tool 'V' or Brush 'B').
2. Press the shortcut key repeatedly on the keyboard.
3. Observe that the active tool cycles to the next tool in the group without holding Shift.

### Expected Behavior (Photoshop Parity)
- Pressing a shortcut key once should select the primary tool and keep it active on subsequent presses.
- Cycling through tools in the same group should require `Shift + [Shortcut Key]`.

### Environment
- PhotoCraft v0.9.0
- OS: Windows 10/11 (x64)

title: Temporary Files in Roaming Profile (Windows)
author: JoaCHIP
body:
When working with large images, PhotoCraft leaves a very large amount of "tile" files in the AppData/Roaming/PhotoCraft/Recovery folder. This is not the correct way to use the Roaming folder on Windows, which may be automatically synced in a business setting, and may even be restricted in maximum storage allowed due to things like group policies, Active Directory, RDP servers, cloud hosting etc.

Just like any other operating system, Windows has a %TEMP% environment variable that shows where to put temporary files.

Using this will also make it easier to clean up the disk in case PhotoCraft is prevented to do so itself.

title: count.deleteGroup on a group before the active one changes which group is active
author: davidmann4
body:
## What goes wrong
`count.deleteGroup` removes a count group but does not shift `active_count_group` when the removed group comes before the active one. The index then points at the next group, so the active group silently changes and the next `count.add` lands in the wrong group.

## Repro
1. Create count groups A, B, C, D and make C (index 2) active.
2. `count.deleteGroup {"group": 0}`.
3. Active index is still 2, which is now D. The next `count.add` adds to D instead of C.

Only the API/CLI/MCP and actions hit this; the Count panel deletes the active group.

## Where
`crates/engine/src/analysis_cmds.rs`, `count_delete_group`: `active_count_group = active_count_group.min(n - 1)` with no shift.

## Expected
The active group stays the same group (C, now index 1), as in Photoshop where deleting another count group doesn't change the selected one. Deleting the active last group selects the new last group.

title: Image > Adjustments on a locked smart object still add a smart filter
author: davidmann4
body:
## What goes wrong
Every `image.adjustments.*` command (and Shadows/Highlights) on a smart object goes through `adjust_as_smart_filter`, which adds the smart filter with no lock check. On a Lock All smart object `image.adjustments.invert` returns Ok and adds a smart filter. On a locked raster layer the same command is refused (`paint_surface` -> `check_pixels_unlocked`), and generic filters on smart objects are refused too.

## Repro
1. Place a smart object, lock it with Lock All.
2. Run `image.adjustments.invert` (or Shadows/Highlights).
3. A smart filter is added to the locked layer.

## Where
`crates/engine/src/adjust_cmds.rs`, `adjust_as_smart_filter`: `s.edit(label, |doc, _| add_smart_filter(doc, id, sf, ...))` without `check_pixels_unlocked`.

## Expected
The command is refused on a locked layer, like Photoshop (adjustments are greyed out on a fully locked layer) and like PhotoCraft's own filters on smart objects.

title: Interpret Footage and New Video Layer from File store fps 0, negative or infinite
author: davidmann4
body:
## What goes wrong
`layer.interpretFootage` and New Video Layer from File take the `fps` param as `f as f32` with no check. fps 0 or -5 is stored on the video layer, and a finite JSON value like `1e39` becomes `inf`; the next .pcraft save then fails (`format/src/finite.rs` refuses non-finite values).

## Repro
1. Create a video layer.
2. `layer.interpretFootage {"fps": 1e39}` (or `0`, `-5`).
3. The layer stores inf/0/-5 fps; with inf, saving the document as .pcraft fails.

## Where
`crates/engine/src/video_cmds.rs`, `interpret_footage` (`v.fps = f as f32`) and the new-from-file path (`p.get("fps")...map(|f| f as f32)`). `timeline_cmds.rs` already has `fps_param` (finite, > 0, <= MAX_FPS) for the timeline commands.

## Expected
Invalid frame rates are refused with an error, as the timeline frame-rate commands already do; Photoshop's Interpret Footage only accepts positive frame rates.

title: type.pasteLoremIpsum ignores "layer" when the active layer isn't a type layer
author: davidmann4
body:
## What goes wrong
`type.pasteLoremIpsum` decides whether to insert into existing text by looking at the *active* layer (`has_text(s)`), while the insert itself targets `p["layer"]`. With a type layer T and a pixel layer active, `type.pasteLoremIpsum {"layer": T, "at": 0}` creates a new type layer and leaves T unchanged.

## Repro
1. Create a type layer T, then `layer.new` (a pixel layer becomes active).
2. `type.pasteLoremIpsum {"layer": <T id>, "at": 0}`.
3. A new type layer is created; T is unchanged.

## Where
`crates/engine/src/type_extra_cmds.rs`, `paste_lorem`: `if has_text(s).is_ok() && ...`.

## Expected
The placeholder text is inserted into T at the given position. An explicit `layer` that isn't a type layer returns an error instead of silently doing something else.

title: Properties > Document W/H resizes tiny documents when the rulers are in inches
author: davidmann4
body:
## What goes wrong
The Properties panel's Document W/H fields use `value_field(ui, &mut v, 0.01..=300_000.0, ...)`. egui clamps the *existing* value to the range, the field reports `changed()`, and `image.canvasSize` runs. A 1x1 px document at 300 ppi with rulers in Inches shows 0.0033 in, which is clamped to 0.01 in = 3 px: just showing the panel makes the document 3x3 px with two history steps and no user edit (at 2400 ppi up to 23 px).

The New Document dialog has the same range: 1 px at 300 ppi, switch the unit to Inches -> width becomes 3 px.

## Repro
1. New document 1x1 px, 300 ppi; set rulers to Inches.
2. Open Properties with nothing selected (Document section).
3. Document is now 3x3 px; history has canvas-size steps.

## Where
`crates/ui-egui/src/doc_props_ui.rs` (Document W/H value_field range), `crates/ui-egui/src/new_doc_ui.rs` (W/H value_field_units range).

## Expected
Displaying a value never edits the document. Photoshop shows small sizes in inches without changing the pixel size. The pixel result is already clamped to >= 1 px afterwards, so the lower bound can be 0.

title: Add a splash screen that shows while PhotoCraft is loading
author: netoverlord
body:
## Summary

PhotoCraft takes longer to start as the app grows. During that time there is no feedback, so it's unclear whether the app is loading or has frozen. Add a splash screen that shows right after launch and stays until the main window is ready, as Adobe Photoshop does.

## Current behavior

- After launching PhotoCraft, the user waits with nothing (or an empty window) on screen until the main window appears.
- As the app gets bigger, this wait gets longer.
- Users can't tell whether the app is starting, stuck or has crashed, and may launch it a second time.

## Expected behavior

- A splash window appears immediately on launch, before the main window.
- It's a small, borderless window, centered on the screen, with:
  - **Left side:** the PhotoCraft logo, the app name and version, and a loading status line (e.g. "Loading plugins…", "Initializing…")
  - **Right side:** artwork (an illustration or image representing PhotoCraft)
- Optionally, a thin progress bar or a loading animation.
- When the app is ready, the splash closes and the main window opens.
- It also appears when launching with a file (double-click, "Open with").

## Why this matters

- It tells users the app is starting, even when startup is slow.
- It prevents double launches and "is it frozen?" confusion.
- It's a familiar pattern for large creative apps and gives a more polished first impression.
- It buys time for further startup improvements (lazy loading, caching), which would still help on their own.

## Suggestions

- The splash should be lightweight, and shown before the heavy initialization starts, so it doesn't add to the wait.
- Artwork could be replaced in later versions, or rotate between several images.
- Optional: a setting or command-line flag to turn it off (e.g. `--no-splash`).

title: Feature Request: Subtract Front Shape (Path Operations)
author: sloptop-the-terrible
body:
**What**

Add a **Subtract Front Shape** path operation (Photoshop's Path Operations / Illustrator's Pathfinder → Minus Front): boolean-subtract the topmost shape from the shape below it, live and non-destructive.

**Why**

Photoshop's Pen / shape tool Path Operations menu is: New Layer, Combine Shapes, Subtract Front Shape, Intersect Shape Areas, Exclude Overlapping Shapes, Merge Shape Components. PhotoCraft doesn't have the boolean set yet.

For vector and vexel work, Subtract Front Shape is the workhorse — cutting holes and negative space out of a shape by stacking a second shape on top, without rasterizing or hand-painting a mask.

**Behaviour**

- Select two or more shape layers → Subtract Front Shape subtracts the frontmost shape's area from the shapes below.
- Stays live: moving or editing either shape updates the result.
- Also applies within a single shape layer's subpaths (subtract a newly drawn path from the existing path).

**Related**

Part of the broader path-operations request in #1397.

title: Layer Mask From Transparency / Mask All Objects keep the Background and build 8-bit masks in 16/32-bit documents
author: davidmann4
body:
## What goes wrong
1. `layer.mask.fromTransparency` and `layer.maskAllObjects` assign `layer.mask` directly, without `background_to_layer_for_mask`, which every other add-mask path calls (Hide Selection, the generic set-mask commands, Select and Mask). A document with only a Background → `layer.maskAllObjects {}` → the layer is still `is_background` and carries a mask, which a Background can't have.
2. The masks start from `LayerMask::hide_all()` / `reveal_all()`, which are 8-bit. #3359 routed the other mask paths through `mask_at_depth`; these (and Hide Selection) were missed. In a 16-bit document a layer with a smooth alpha ramp → From Transparency → the alpha is quantised to 256 levels in the mask (banding), and since the pixels are then made opaque the 16-bit alpha is lost.

## Repro
- Open a flat photo (Background only) → Layer > Layer Mask > Mask All Objects → Layers panel still shows "Background" with a mask.
- 16-bit document, layer with alpha 0.5003 → Layer > Layer Mask > From Transparency → mask sample is 8-bit (≈ 0.5020).

## Where
`crates/engine/src/layer_menu_cmds.rs`: `mask_from_transparency`, `hide_selection`, `mask_all_objects`; `mask_at_depth` in `crates/engine/src/commands.rs`.

## Expected
As in Photoshop, adding a mask to the Background first turns it into a normal layer ("Layer 0"), and the mask keeps the document's bit depth.

title: Preset Manager brush rename/delete leaves the current brush preset dangling and allows duplicate names
author: davidmann4
body:
## What goes wrong
`edit.presetManager` renames and deletes brush presets directly (`b.name = new; b.builtin = false` / `presets.remove(i)`), skipping what `brush.presets.rename` and `brush.presets.delete` do: refuse a duplicate name, and move or clear the current preset.

- `brush.presets.setCurrent {"name":"Chalk"}`, then Preset Manager rename "Chalk" → "Chalky", then `brush.presets.update {}` fails with "no brush preset named `Chalk`".
- Preset Manager rename "Soft Round" → "hard round" is accepted although "Hard Round" exists; `brush.presets.delete {"name":"Hard Round"}` then removes both.

## Where
`crates/engine/src/edit_menu_cmds.rs`, `preset_manager` (rename/delete for `"brushes"`). Siblings: `brush_preset_cmds.rs` (rename), `brush_cmds.rs` (delete).

## Expected
Renaming or deleting a brush in the Preset Manager behaves like the same action in the Brushes panel: duplicate names are refused, and the current preset follows the rename or is cleared on delete.

title: PSD: Transparency Shapes Layer off is ignored for a layer's own blend mode (Color Dodge at 53%)
author: kenny-t-vo
body:
**PhotoCraft 0.9.0** (macOS universal, `photocraft-cli convert`).

Photoshop composites a layer with Transparency Shapes Layer off (Blending Options; `tsly` 0 in the PSD) differently from the same layer with it on, even when the layer has no effects. PhotoCraft draws the two the same, as Photoshop draws the one with the option on. In `crates/compose` (v0.9.0), `transparency_shapes` is read only for effects and knockouts: `effect_shape` (`lib.rs:751`), `knockout_shape` (`advanced.rs:127`), and the isolation tests at `advanced.rs:78` and `:84`, which need effects or a knockout. A layer's own blending never reads it.

**Repro.** `dodge-tsl-off.psd` (below, gzip and base64, 70 KB) was made in Photoshop 2026, as follows:
- a document of 200 × 100 px in sRGB, its background filled with (90, 110, 130);
- one layer: an ellipse with radii 40 × 30 px, feathered 15 px, filled with (200, 150, 80);
- the layer set to Color Dodge at 53% opacity, with Transparency Shapes Layer off.

The same document with the option on is the control. The Photoshop values below come from Photoshop's own PNG export of each document.

```
base64 -d dodge-tsl-off.psd.gz.b64 | gunzip > dodge-tsl-off.psd
photocraft-cli convert dodge-tsl-off.psd out.png --format png
```

Along the row y = 50:

| x | Photoshop, option off | PhotoCraft, option off | Photoshop and PhotoCraft, option on |
|---|---|---|---|
| 100 | (177, 180, 158) | (171, 181, 159) | (171, 181, 159) |
| 125 | (146, 150, 149) | (150, 163, 152) | (150, 163, 152) |
| 145 | (102, 121, 136) | (113, 130, 138) | (113, 130, 138) |

Over the whole image, PhotoCraft is 3.3/255 from Photoshop on average with the option off, and at most 15. With it on, it is 0.1/255, and at most 1.

- **Expected:** the layer composited with the option off as Photoshop composites it.

**Where it bites:** a render of ours has a Color Dodge layer at 53% with this option off. Where that layer lies, PhotoCraft draws the image lighter and warmer than Photoshop does, by 5.4/25…

title: Perf: full Document clone and tree walk in duplicate_selected and paste_selected regress layer operations (P8 +44%, P9 +30%, P11 +50%)
author: zachshallbetter
body:
Commits 3e90c81e3 and 7107c8004 introduced full `Document` clones and tree comparisons in `duplicate_selected` and `paste_selected` (`crates/engine/src/layer_multi_cmds.rs`):

```rust
let before = s.active().ok_or(EngineError::NoDocument)?.doc.clone();
...
note_insert(s, &before);
```

While calculating `insert_damage` avoids full canvas recomposition when adding bounded layers, cloning the entire document hierarchy on every duplication and paste before running recursive pairwise tree walks regressed multiple benchmarks on 12 MP layers:
- P8 (`duplicate 12 MP layer, first`): 299 ms -> 430 ms (+44%)
- P9 (`duplicate 12 MP layer, repeat`): 303 ms -> 394 ms (+30%)
- P11 (`paste 12 MP layer, repeat`): 301 ms -> 452 ms (+50%)

Fix: Track inserted layer IDs and calculate their bounds directly without cloning the full `Document` state beforehand.

title: Suggestions for Improving PhotoCraft
author: macreatiive-crypto
body:
Hello PhotoCraft Development Team!

I am a Brazilian user testing PhotoCraft as an alternative to Photoshop for professional graphic design work, especially large-format printing, party decoration panels, and printed materials.

I would like to share a few suggestions that could significantly improve the user experience.

1. Customizable Tool Cursors

Currently, the cursor remains a crosshair even when the Move Tool is selected. I would appreciate the option to use an arrow cursor similar to Photoshop's, making it easier to identify the pointer position and move elements accurately.

It would also be helpful to allow users to choose different cursor shapes for each tool, such as an arrow, a precision crosshair, or other appropriate shapes depending on the tool's function.

2. Brush Size and Coverage Area Preview

I am experiencing an important issue when using the Brush Tool: the circular outline indicating the brush diameter and coverage area does not appear correctly, even when the brush cursor is configured to display the normal brush tip.

In Photoshop, users can see the circle corresponding to the brush size and press Caps Lock to toggle between the circular brush outline and a precision crosshair.

It would be very useful for PhotoCraft to support the same behavior, allowing users to clearly preview the area that will be affected before painting. This would greatly improve precision when working with large-format artwork, retouching, masks, and detailed edits.

3. Independently Adjustable Toolbar Icon Size

The toolbar icons take up a considerable amount of visual space. It would be helpful to have an option to reduce icon sizes independently of the scaling applied to text, menus, and other interface elements.

This would allow users to create a more compact toolbar and free up valuable workspace.

4. Classic Interface Option

I would appreciate a classic interface style featuring less rounded buttons and panels, compact icons, and a layout closer to tradition…

title: GPU: a styled group's effects ignore the group's vector mask and children's Blend If
author: davidmann4
body:
On the GPU compositor, a group with a layer style (e.g. Stroke) keeps drawing the effect around the **old** shape after the group's own vector mask changes, or after a child's Blend If / Advanced Blending changes. The CPU compositor updates correctly.

**Repro**
1. Raster layer inside a group; add a Stroke to the group (GPU canvas).
2. Add or move a vector mask on the group, or set the child's Blend If "This Layer" black point to 128.
3. The stroke still follows the previous outline.

**Where**
`crates/gpu/src/fx.rs` `group_key` (used by `sync_fx` in `gpu/src/lib.rs`): the group arm hashes the children and `layer.mask`, but not the group's own `layer.vector_mask`; the per-child `walk` hashes visibility, opacity, blend, content, masks and effects, but not `blend_if` or `advanced`. The group effect shape uses all of them, and group tiles have no damage sources, so the cached distance field is never rebuilt.

**Expected**
Like Photoshop and our CPU compositor (`compose::layer_identity`): the group's effects follow the group's current composite, so any of those edits redraws the stroke.

title: Studio/Adwaita/Breeze options bar clamps Brush and Eraser size to 2500 px
author: davidmann4
body:
In the Studio / Adwaita / Breeze themes, the Brush and Eraser options-bar **Size** field clamps the brush to 2500 px, although the brush picker, the `]` key, the Pencil field and the engine allow up to 5000 px (`MAX_BRUSH_SIZE`).

**Repro**
1. Studio theme, Brush tool.
2. Set the size to 4000 px with the brush picker or `]`.
3. On the next frame the options bar's field clamps the value to 2500 px and commits it: the brush paints at 2500 px.

**Where**
`crates/ui-egui/src/panels.rs`: `widgets::value_field(ui, &mut b.size, 1.0..=2500.0, "px", 76.0)` in the non-Pro options bar (the Pencil arm right above uses `MAX_BRUSH_SIZE`). egui's drag value clamps the existing value to its range.

**Expected**
Photoshop's brush size goes up to 5000 px everywhere; the field should accept and keep it in every theme.

title: Selecting a scaled type layer shrinks its text: the Character fields clamp the shown size to 1296 pt
author: davidmann4
body:
## What goes wrong
Selecting a type layer that was scaled with Free Transform silently changes its font size (and leading), adding a history step, although the user edited nothing.

The Character fields show the size as it appears on the canvas (`size_pt × transform scale`). They are drawn with egui `DragValue` ranges of `0.1..=1296` pt (size) and `0.1..=5000` pt (leading). egui clamps an *existing* value that lies outside the range on the first frame and reports the field as changed, so the UI sends `type.setStyle` with the clamped value.

## Repro
1. New document, Type tool, type some text at 200 pt.
2. Free Transform, scale 1000 %, commit (the size now shows as 2000 pt).
3. Select the layer with the Character/Properties panel visible (or the Type tool active).

Result: the text shrinks to 129.6 pt (1296 / 10) and History gets an entry. The same happens at the low end: 8 pt scaled to 5 % shows 0.4 pt, below the options bar's minimum of 1 unit, so the Type tool raises it.

## Where
`crates/ui-egui/src/type_tool.rs`: Character panel Font size and Leading fields (`num_field(..., 0.1..=1296.0 ...)`, `0.1..=5000.0`), and the options bar size field (`value_field(..., unit..=1296.0 * unit ...)`).

## Expected
Showing a value never changes the document. Only a real edit by the user is clamped to the field's range; a value already outside the range is displayed as is.

title: Flatten All Layer Effects bakes with the default Global Light and drops Pattern Overlay / Pattern Fill
author: davidmann4
body:
## What goes wrong
Scripts › Flatten All Layer Effects (and Flatten All Masks) bake each layer through `photocraft_compose::render_layer`, which renders without the document's context:

- `light: GlobalLight::default()`: a Drop Shadow / Bevel that uses Global Light is baked at the default angle instead of the document's, so the shadow jumps when the effects are flattened.
- `PreparedPatterns::new(&[], ..)`: no patterns are available, so a Pattern Overlay vanishes and a Pattern Fill layer with effects bakes transparent (content lost).
- `canvas: rect` (the layer area inflated for the effects) instead of the document bounds, so a Gradient Fill layer lays its gradient out on the wrong frame.

## Repro
1. Document with Global Light set to 0° (Layer › Layer Style › Global Light).
2. Pixel layer with a Drop Shadow that uses Global Light (distance 10, size 0).
3. File › Scripts › Flatten All Layer Effects.

Result: the composite changes; the shadow moves to the default 90°/120° direction. With a Pattern Overlay, the overlay disappears.

## Where
`crates/compose/src/lib.rs` `render_layer` (no document context) and `crates/engine/src/file_cmds.rs` `bake`.

## Expected
Flattening layer effects leaves the composite unchanged: the baked pixels match what the document showed before (document Global Light, patterns, canvas, colour mode and depth).

title: Gradient/Pattern Fill layers accept angle 1e39 or phase 1e39, and the document can no longer be saved
author: davidmann4
body:
## What goes wrong
`layer.newFillLayer` with a gradient `{"angle": 1e39}`, `gradient.presets.apply` with `{"angle": 1e39}`, or a pattern fill with `{"angle": 1e39}` / `{"phase": [1e39, 0]}` stores an infinite value (`as f32` of a finite JSON number beyond f32 range). Rendering then takes cos(inf) = NaN, and `.pcraft` save and autosave are refused by `format/src/finite.rs` ("... is NaN or infinite"). An angle of 450 is stored as 450 instead of 90.

## Where
- `crates/engine/src/commands.rs` (`layer.newFillLayer`, `f32_or(p, "angle", 90.0)`)
- `crates/engine/src/presets/gradients.rs` (`gradient.presets.apply`, `unwrap_or(90.0) as f32`)
- `crates/engine/src/pattern_cmds.rs` (`placement`: angle/phase `as f32`, shared by fill and paint commands)

## Expected
Like the sibling `gradient.fill.set` (gradient_fill_cmds.rs): non-finite values are rejected and angles are normalised to (-180, 180], as Photoshop's angle fields do.

title: Place Scale Marker: the label overlaps the bar on documents above 72 ppi
author: davidmann4
body:
## What goes wrong
`image.analysis.placeScaleMarker` lays out the bar height, the text height and the baseline as if `fontSize` were pixels, but it passes the size to `type.create`, which takes points (scaled by resolution / 72). At 300 ppi a 12 pt label is 50 px tall while only 15 px are reserved, so the label overlaps the bar (and with text at the bottom it can run off the canvas). At 72 ppi points and pixels match, which is why the existing tests pass.

## Where
`crates/engine/src/analysis_cmds.rs`, `place_scale_marker` (`bar_h`, `text_h`, `baseline` from `font_size`).

## Expected
Photoshop's Measurement Scale Marker font size is in points; the label sits clear of the bar at any resolution.

title: Image Size and Canvas Size ignore Preferences > Point/Pica Size (Traditional 72.27)
author: davidmann4
body:
## What goes wrong
With Preferences > Units & Rulers > Point/Pica Size set to Traditional (72.27 points/inch), the rulers, Info panel, shape dialog and layer properties use 72.27 (`units_and_rulers.point_size.per_inch()`), but Image Size and Canvas Size hard-code 72 points and 6 picas per inch. A 723 px document at 72 ppi reads 725.7 pt in the rulers but 723 pt in Image Size, and typing a size in points resizes by the wrong amount.

## Where
`crates/ui-egui/src/sizing.rs` (`to_unit` / `from_unit` hard-code 72.0 and 6.0).

## Expected
In Photoshop the Point/Pica Size preference defines the point (and pica = 12 points) for every point/pica field, Image Size and Canvas Size included.

title: PSD: layers under unclosed group dividers past the depth cap are dropped instead of hoisted
author: davidmann4
body:
## What goes wrong
`PsdFile::layer_tree` hoists the layers under a group divider that never gets a matching folder record to the enclosing level. `layer_tree_max_depth` drops them instead once the unclosed dividers are nested past `max_depth`: frames beyond the cap collect nothing, so when the unclosed frames are hoisted at the end there is nothing left to hoist. Records `[a, </Layer group>, b, c]` give `a, b, c` from `layer_tree()` but only `a` from `layer_tree_max_depth(0)`, so a malformed file with many unclosed dividers loses layers on import.

## Where
`crates/psd/src/tree.rs`, `layer_tree_max_depth`.

## Expected
The depth cap only trims the children of groups that are actually nested too deep; layers under unclosed dividers are hoisted as `layer_tree` does.

title: [Deps/CI] No dependency-update automation runs, so advisories and action pins drift with no owner
author: Emin-ACIKGOZ
body:
### Summary

No automated dependency-update tool runs on this repository. Cargo dependencies, the `Cargo.lock` lockfile and GitHub Actions pins are updated only when a contributor notices.

### Current behavior

- **No update automation.** `.github/dependabot.yml`, `renovate.json` and `renovate.json5` are all absent.
- **Git dependencies are pinned to immutable revisions by hand:** `craft-ui` at `Cargo.toml:13` and `craft-print` at `Cargo.toml:41` point at `storytold/craft-libs` by `rev`.
- **Actions are mostly on mutable tags:** `actions/checkout@v4` (×9), `Swatinem/rust-cache@v2` (×6), `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable` (×6), `actions/upload-artifact@v4` (×3), `actions/cache@v4`.
- **Open advisories in the locked graph:** #4952 (`ruzstd` RUSTSEC-2026-0344) and #4983 (`paste`/`rustybuzz`/`ttf-parser`, unmaintained). Both are still open.

### Motivation

- **Security.** Known-vulnerable or unmaintained crates (#4952, #4983) stay unfixed until a contributor updates them by hand.
- **Supply chain.** Mutable action tags change without review (see #2939).
- **No owner.** Updates happen only when a contributor notices.

### Additional context

1. **CI builds with `--locked`** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`). A dependency-update bot must commit the `Cargo.lock` change, or its PRs fail the build.
2. **Cargo git dependencies are unevenly supported.** Dependabot has long-standing gaps for git-based Cargo deps and does not update `Cargo.toml` for them (dependabot-core #7079, #8689). Renovate's Cargo manager supports `git-refs`/`git-tags`/`github-tags` datasources, so it can move the pinned `craft-libs` revisions. This is the one capability difference that affects the choice in `Cargo.toml:13,41`.

### Related issues

- **#4060** adds a `cargo-deny` advisory gate and SAST — complementary (it *blocks* known-vulnerable deps); this issue is update automation. Not a duplicate.
- **#2939 / #2936 / #1372** cover pinning and the umbrella checkup; this issue keeps pins and deps current.

title: Panel Layout: Resolve Panel Duplication, Enable Multi-Column Support, and Improve Docking Mechanics
author: TycusArt
body: ### Current Behavior: - The UI currently duplicates panel elements. For example, the "Color" icon and "Color" panel are displayed simultaneously. Clicking an icon in the left toolbar simply expands or collapses the duplicated panel on the right. - The layout is rigidly restricted to an icon column on the left and panel column on the right. - While panels can be dragged individually, advanced docking capabilities for precise workspace organization would be great. ### Expected Behavior: - Each panel exists independently in either a collapsed icon state or an expanded state. - Clicking a collapsed panel icon should expand only that specific panel. Clicking the small double-arrow icon in the top right corner should expand or collapse the entire column. - Multi-Column Layouts: As many panel columns as the user needs, supporting combinations of collapsed and expanded columns. This is useful for scenarios such as widescreen users can have multiple fully expanded columns, while laptop users can have partly or fully collapsed columns. - In a collapsed column, each group of icons should have a handle bar above to allow dragging whole group and a separator below. - Context-sensitive Drag-and-Drop Docking: 1. Drop a panel between columns or at the outer edges to create a new column containing only that panel. The panel's current collapsed or expanded state should be carried over. 2. Drop a panel inside a group should add it to that group. Dropping a panel below the separator should create a new group containing only that panel.

title: Improve Gaussian Blur and filter-dialog preview performance with GPU execution
author: schmidtzoltan
body:
## Problem

(Part of  #3934.)

Filter-dialog previews currently execute the filter on the CPU, flatten the result on the CPU, and then upload it for display. Large previews and changes to expensive filters can take long enough to delay feedback.

The desktop app already runs preview calculations on a worker and discards stale requests. The GPU compositor renders document chunks to a texture, but does not currently execute filter kernels.

## Scope

This issue focuses on GPU execution for interactive filter previews, beginning with Gaussian Blur and Unsharp Mask. It covers preview calculation and display; applying filters to document pixels remains on the existing engine command path.

Relevant code:

- `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`: `ensure_filter_preview` manages preview requests, workers, and publishing results.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/filter_dialog.rs`: `preview_document_for_target` creates a proxy document and executes the filter command.
- `crates/engine/src/filters.rs`: `params_for` maps command IDs to `FilterParams`.
- `crates/algo/src/blur.rs`: Gaussian Blur uses an exact separable kernel for small radii and three box passes for larger radii.
- `crates/algo/src/sharpen.rs` and `crates/algo/src/sharpen/exact.rs`: CPU Unsharp Mask implementations.
- `crates/gpu/src/lib.rs`: `Compositor::render` sends rendered chunks to a caller-provided sink.
- `crates/gpu/src/plan.rs`: GPU composition planning and adjustment shader support.

## Desired outcome

Gaussian Blur and Unsharp Mask previews can use the GPU where supported, with the existing CPU path available as a fallback. The preview continues to honor proxy scaling, alpha, selection and target behavior, and does not publish results for stale requests.

The implementation can establish whether filtered output can flow into GPU composition without a full readback and re-upload. GPU results should be compared with the CPU reference, and preview latency measured on representative large documents.

title: Lock Transparency paints too strongly on semi-transparent pixels
author: davidmann4
body:
**What goes wrong**
With Lock Transparent Pixels (or Fill's *Preserve Transparency*), PhotoCraft composites source-over and then restores the old alpha. The colour is therefore weighted by the source-over alpha instead of the source alpha, so semi-transparent pixels get too much of the new colour. Opaque and fully transparent pixels are unaffected, which is why existing tests pass.

**Repro**
1. New transparent layer, Edit > Fill white at 50% opacity (alpha 128).
2. Edit > Fill black at 50% with Preserve Transparency.
3. Photoshop: (127,127,127,128). PhotoCraft: (85,85,85,128).

**Where**
- `crates/paint/src/retouch.rs` `over_native` (lock branch divides by the source-over alpha but keeps the old one)
- `crates/engine/src/fill_cmds.rs` `blend_tile` (keep_alpha)
- `crates/algo/src/paint.rs` `composite_area` (`o[3] = d[3]` after a source-over composite: gradient, bucket)
- `crates/paint/src/render.rs` brush, non-Normal modes

**Expected**
Source-atop when the alpha is kept: `Co = (1 - as)·Cb + as·B(Cb, Cs)`, alpha unchanged.

title: Lens Flare darkens 32-bit HDR pixels above 1.0
author: davidmann4
body:
**What goes wrong**
Filter > Render > Lens Flare screens the flare over the image with `c = 1 - (1 - c)·(1 - a)`. For 32-bit pixels above 1.0, `(1 - c)` is negative, so the flare *darkens* them: a 2.0 pixel under a = 0.5 becomes 1.5, and at the flare core (a = 1) any value becomes 1.0.

**Repro**
New 32-bit RGB document, fill with RGB (2, 2, 2) (exposure +1), run Lens Flare. Every pixel the flare touches drops below 2.0; the core clips to 1.0.

**Where**
`crates/algo/src/render.rs`, end of the lens flare pixel loop (`c[k] = 1.0 - (1.0 - c[k]) * (1.0 - a.min(1.0))`).

**Expected**
Adding light never lowers a channel: `c += a·max(1 - c, 0)` gives the same result for c ≤ 1 and leaves brighter HDR values alone (8/16-bit output unchanged).

title: CMYK: Duplicate Channel, Load Selection, Split and Merge Channels use inverted ink values
author: davidmann4
body:
**What goes wrong**
CMYK pixels are stored as ink (1 = full ink), while the Channels panel (and Photoshop) shows each channel as a tone where white means no ink. Several channel commands copy the raw ink values, so they come out inverted:
- On a white CMYK document, duplicating the Cyan channel gives an all-black alpha channel (Photoshop: white).
- Load Selection from Cyan selects nothing (Photoshop: everything).
- Split Channels gives black grayscale documents; Merge Channels of white grayscale documents gives a black CMYK document.
- Copy/paste of a single CMYK channel (`channel_clip.rs`) has the same polarity issue.

**Where**
`crates/engine/src/channel_cmds.rs` (`ref_planes` / `native_pixels`, `split`, `merge`), `crates/engine/src/channel_clip.rs` (copy/paste).

**Expected**
Read and write CMYK channels as tone (`1 - ink`), like Photoshop.

title: Multichannel PSD: alpha-type channels import and save inverted
author: davidmann4
body:
**What goes wrong**
`crates/io/src/multichannel_map.rs` inverts every Multichannel plane into ink on import (`1.0 - decode(..)`) and back on export (`1.0 - v[0]`). DisplayInfo then turns some planes (kind 0/1, *Selected/Masked Areas*) into alpha channels (`spot = None`), but their values stay inverted. Everywhere else alpha channels are stored as-is (`psd_import.rs`, `psd_export.rs`, `channel.toMultichannel`).

**Repro**
- A Multichannel PSD with a white *Selected Areas* channel imports as 0: Load Selection selects nothing.
- RGB document with a white alpha channel → Image > Mode > Multichannel → save as PSD: the alpha plane is written black.

**Where**
`crates/io/src/multichannel_map.rs` import (~line 50 and the DisplayInfo step) and export (~line 94); `crates/compose/src/multichannel.rs` prints alpha-type channels as ink.

**Expected**
Alpha-type channels are stored and read as-is; only spot (ink) channels are inverted.

### Environment

When creating a new group with multiple layers selected, the selected layers should automatically become children of the newly created group, preserving their relative order.

A new, empty group is created, leaving the previously selected layers outside the group.

### Additional Context

This may be intended behaviour rather than a bug. However, automatically grouping selected layers would provide a more intuitive workflow and eliminate the additional step of manually moving layers into the newly created group.

title: Flatpak on Wayland: pen tablet moves the cursor but never clicks (works in the AppImage)
author: pierodev0
body:
## Summary

On a Wayland session, a pen tablet used in the **Flatpak** build moves the cursor inside the PhotoCraft window but **never clicks anything** (no tool select, no canvas click, no menu). The same tablet works correctly in other applications and in the **AppImage** build of PhotoCraft on the same machine.

Root cause: the Flatpak manifest grants `--socket=fallback-x11`, which only exposes the X11 socket when the Wayland socket is **absent**. Under a Wayland session the sandbox therefore sees `DISPLAY` empty, so `pen_needs_xwayland()` never triggers and PhotoCraft stays on **native Wayland** — where `winit 0.30` does not bind `zwp_tablet_v2` and a pen has no working input (#639, #79). The AppImage works because on the host `DISPLAY` is always set (Xwayland), so it takes the Xwayland path.

## Environment

- **PhotoCraft version:** 0.9.0 (Flatpak, system install, `flatpak install ai.storyteller.photocraft`, no extra parameters)
- **OS:** Arch Linux (Omarchy)
- **Compositor / session:** Hyprland (Wayland); Xwayland is present on the host (`Xwayland :0 -rootless ...`)
- **Tablet:** XP-Pen Deco 01 V2 (libinput tablet tool; works in other apps and in the PhotoCraft AppImage)

## Steps to reproduce

1. On a Wayland session (Hyprland, and the same applies to GNOME/KDE), install the PhotoCraft Flatpak with its default permissions.
2. Attach the XP-Pen and hover it over the PhotoCraft window: the cursor moves.
3. Touch/tap any UI element or the canvas with the pen.

## Expected vs actual

- **Expected:** the pen clicks/activates elements (as it does in the AppImage and in other apps).
- **Actual:** the cursor moves, but the pen never produces a click. A mouse works fine.

## Evidence

Permissions of the installed Flatpak:

```

[Context]

title: [Docs] No CHANGELOG and no release-notes generation
author: Emin-ACIKGOZ
body:
### Summary

The repository has no `CHANGELOG.md` and no automated release notes. Change history lives only in GitHub Releases.

### Current behavior

- `CHANGELOG.md` is absent.
- Releases are cut frequently with hand-written GitHub Release notes.
- Commit messages are not Conventional Commits (the repository uses `Area: description`), so `release-please` would require a commit-style migration.

### Motivation

- A single versioned history is easier to scan than many release pages, and helps users, packagers and distributors.
- Reduces the manual effort of writing notes each release.

### Open questions

1. Is a repository CHANGELOG wanted at all, given GitHub Releases already exist?
2. Which approach: (a) a Keep a Changelog file updated per release, (b) generated from merged pull request titles/labels, or (c) Conventional Commits plus `release-please`?
3. If (c), do we accept migrating the commit style from `Area: description` to Conventional Commits?

title: [Community] No code of conduct is published
author: Emin-ACIKGOZ
body:
### Summary

The repository has no `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md`. There is no published standard for behaviour in issues, pull requests or discussions.

### Current behavior

- `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md` is absent (both at the root and under `.github/`).
- GitHub's community health profile reports the code of conduct as missing.
- `docs/contributing.md` states contribution rules but not a conduct standard.

### Motivation

- With 315 commit authors and 1,050 open issues, a shared, published standard is the baseline for a healthy community.
- It gives maintainers a stated basis to moderate and reduces ad-hoc decisions.

### Additional context

- The common choice is the [Contributor Covenant](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/) v2.1 (translations available).
- Needs a private enforcement contact; conduct reports usually want a separate address from the security channel in #4819.

### Related issues

- #5439: module-level reviewers and a maintainer path.
- #4819: private reporting channel.

### Open questions

1. Contributor Covenant v2.1, or a shorter custom text?
2. Which contact(s) should receive reports?

title: [Community] No issue templates or issue chooser
author: Emin-ACIKGOZ
body:
### Summary

There is no `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/`, so new issues arrive unstructured, and GitHub's community profile lists issue templates as missing.

### Current behavior

- `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/` is absent; there are no issue forms and no `config.yml` chooser.
- Issues are free-form. The audit-style issues carry their own structure, but reporters are given no prompt.

### Motivation

- 1,050 open issues with heavy duplication.
- Structured intake (OS, version, repro steps) reduces back-and-forth and near-duplicates.
- Fills the community-profile gap.

### Additional context

An issue form is a YAML file under `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/`. GitHub turns the chosen form into the new-issue body, and the form can set the issue's labels. Proposed files:

- `bug_report.yml` (label `bug`): required fields for OS, PhotoCraft version or commit, build type, steps to reproduce, and expected vs actual behaviour.
- `feature_request.yml`: the problem and the behaviour requested.
- `config.yml`: settings for the template chooser, including `contact_links` that route security reports to `SECURITY.md` and general questions to the Discord.

### Related issues

- #3561: claiming issues so PRs do not collide.
- #2993: closing done/duplicate tickets.
- #5439: triage labels.

### Open questions

1. Which templates to ship first: bug, feature, question?
2. Disable blank issues, or keep an "open a blank issue" escape?

title: [CI] OpenSSF Scorecard is not run on the repository
author: Emin-ACIKGOZ
body:
### Summary

The repository does not run OpenSSF Scorecard, so its supply-chain posture is not continuously measured or published.

### Current behavior

- No `.github/workflows/scorecard.yml`; no published score.
- Gaps Scorecard would surface: unprotected `main` (#5118), Actions referenced by mutable tags (#2939), and, until #5760, no dependency-update tooling.

### Motivation

- A weekly, third-party score keeps supply-chain regressions visible and gives users a signal when assessing the project.
- It is cheap: one workflow, using the official action.

### Additional context

- Convention: `ossf/scorecard-action` on a `schedule` and `branch_protection_rule` trigger, SARIF uploaded to code scanning, `publish_results: true` (needs `id-token: write`).
- It reads GitHub **Repository Rules** with the default token; classic branch protection needs a PAT.

### Related issues

- #5118: require CI before merging into `main`.
- #2939 / #2936: pin release/signing actions.
- #5760: dependency-update automation.

### Open questions

1. Show the Scorecard badge on the README, or keep the results internal?

title: [Legal] No SPDX license headers or REUSE metadata in source
author: Emin-ACIKGOZ
body:
### Summary

Source files carry no SPDX license identifiers, so per-file licensing is not machine-readable.

### Current behavior

- Zero `SPDX-License-Identifier` headers in the tree.
- The project is `MIT OR Apache-2.0` (`Cargo.toml`, `LICENSE-MIT`, `LICENSE-APACHE`).

### Motivation

- Machine-readable per-file licensing helps downstream users, packagers and distributors, and pairs with the license policy planned in #4060.
- Removes ambiguity for any file added from a third party.

### Additional context

- Convention: a one-line `// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT OR Apache-2.0` at the top of each source file, or REUSE metadata (`.license` files / `REUSE.toml`), checkable with a `reuse lint` CI job.
- `Cargo.toml` already declares the crate license; per-file headers are the complement.

### Related issues

- #4060: dependency vulnerability and licence policy gate.

### Open questions

1. Per-file SPDX headers, REUSE metadata, or neither (rely on `Cargo.toml`)?

title: [CI] No stale issue/PR automation for the open backlog
author: Emin-ACIKGOZ
body:
### Summary

There is no stale-bot or auto-close workflow, so inactive issues and pull requests accumulate without a nudge.

### Current behavior

- No `actions/stale` (or equivalent) workflow exists.

- #3561: claiming issues / reducing collisions.
- #5439: triage labels.

2. Warn then close, or close directly?

The repository has a priority label family plus GitHub's defaults and several one-off labels, but no type or status axes and no prefix that says which axis a label belongs to.

- Priority labels exist: `priority: critical`, `priority: high`, `priority: medium`, `priority: low`.

title: GPU canvas runs out of memory at ~2 GB VRAM on an 8 GB card: layer resident textures are created past the budget, and one OOM drops the GPU for the session
author: theriseandfallofitall
body:
## Summary

Opening a 9290×6194 16-bit layered PSB (~98 layers) on an 8 GB RTX 3070 Laptop GPU with Memory usage 16000 MB (budget 7426 MB) hits an out-of-memory error on the first composite, at a VRAM peak of 2.1 GB. The log shows one `Out of Memory` followed by 526 validation errors on `pc_compose_layer` textures within 4 ms: the per-layer resident textures from `sync` are created without any check, so the budget and eviction never stop creation before the device runs out, and the failed textures poison every later call. Because the canvas watches the device, that one error faults the GPU for the session: CPU fallback, 13 s redraws, GPU idle, and "Retry GPU" needs a restart.

This is not "budget larger than the card" (7426 MB is below 8 GB) and no single allocation exceeds a device limit; the evidence points to many resident textures created in one pass with no error scope, no count against the budget before allocating, and no retry.

Measured on the same file, fresh launch each time (`ui.inspect` `perf.timings` and the log):

| Memory usage | `gpuBudgetMb` | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 4096 MB | 512 | GPU alive; "layers exceed the GPU memory budget; full refresh on the CPU", 14.3 s redraw |
| 12000 MB | 3426 | GPU alive; same CPU fallback, 13.9 s redraw, VRAM 1.9 GB |
| 16000 MB | 7426 | `Out of Memory` + 526 `pc_compose_layer` errors; GPU off for the session, 13.0 s redraw |
| 50000 MB | 16309 | same `Out of Memory` |

So on this file no setting gets a GPU-drawn canvas: below what the layers need the canvas falls back to the CPU, and above it the device runs out of memory and the GPU is gone until restart.

Related: #4536 (budget ignores the card's memory; PR #5234 caps it at 3 GB here, which does not add an error scope or retry), #1015 (very large documents run the GPU out of memory).

## Environment

- PhotoCraft built from main @ 8d840eab, Windows 11, 64 GB RAM, NVIDIA RTX 3070 Laptop (8 GB, driver 617.42, Vulkan, discreteGpu) + Intel UHD, Memory usage 16000 MB
-…

title: Export As: Resample menu for the exported size, incl. Nearest Neighbor (FILE-215-18)
author: davidmann4
body:
Part of #215 (scorecard FILE-215-18). Related: #4676 (Export As layout; this covers only its Resample control).

## What's missing on main
File › Export As always resamples with Bicubic when the export scale or pixel size differs from the document (`crates/ui-egui/src/export_dialog.rs`, `export_document`: `image.imageSize` with `"resample": "bicubic"`). There is no Resample choice in the dialog, so pixel art and hard-edged graphics can't be exported at 200 % / 400 % with Nearest Neighbor, and the scorecard row stays partial ("Missing: Export As nearest-neighbour scaling"). The engine already supports every method: `image.imageSize` takes `nearest`, `bilinear`, `bicubic`, `bicubicSmoother`, `bicubicSharper`, `bicubicAutomatic`.

## Photoshop's behaviour
Export As › Image Size has a **Resample** menu next to Width, Height and Scale, with Bicubic Automatic, Bicubic, Bicubic Smoother, Bicubic Sharper, Bilinear and Nearest Neighbor (Adobe help: "Export settings and export location preferences", https://helpx.adobe.com/photoshop/desktop/save-and-export/export-files-to-different-formats/export-settings-and-export-location-preferences.html). It resamples only the exported copy; the document is unchanged.

## Proposal
- Export As gets a `resample` setting (`bicubicAutomatic|bicubic|bicubicSmoother|bicubicSharper|bilinear|nearest`, default Bicubic Automatic) applied to the exported copy; unknown values are rejected with an error, never a panic. Agent-drivable through the same path the dialog uses.
- A Resample dropdown in the Image Size section of the dialog; the choice is remembered with the other Export As settings (`seed_remembered` / confirm).
- The preview and the size estimate use the chosen method.
- Tests: Nearest Neighbor at 200 % reproduces each source pixel as a 2×2 block (8 and 16 bit); the setting survives the remembered-settings round trip; a bad value is an error; the document is untouched.

title: Shapes: Density and Feather on shape layers (TOOL-214-12)
author: davidmann4
body:
Part of #214 (scorecard TOOL-214-12, the "shape feather" part; on-canvas corner radii are done or in #5834).

## What's missing on main
A shape layer has no Density or Feather. `ShapeLayer` (`crates/doc/src/vector.rs`) holds `path`, `fill`, `stroke`, `live` and has no mask parameters, so its edge can't be softened non-destructively and the shape can't be faded outside its path. Ordinary vector masks already have both (`VectorMask { density, feather }`, `layer.vectorMask.edit`, the compositor blurs them in `crates/compose/src/masks.rs`), but they don't apply to a shape layer's own path. The scorecard row says "Missing: shape feather".

## Photoshop's behaviour (measured)
In Photoshop a shape layer is a fill layer whose path is its vector mask; the layer descriptor carries `vectorMaskDensity` and `vectorMaskFeather`, edited in Properties › Masks. Measured with a script on a new 200×200 white document holding a black 100×100 rectangle shape layer (50..150):
- **Feather 10 px:** the edge becomes a symmetric soft ramp centred on the path. Row 100, x = 30..72 step 3: 249, 242, 232, 216, 195, 170, 142, 113, 85, 60, 39, 23, 13, 6, 2; the centre stays 0.
- **Density 50 %:** the fill shows at half strength *outside* the path (128 over white), full strength inside, with a hard edge.
The fill and the stroke stay editable; nothing is rasterized.

## Proposal
- Density and feather for shape layers in the document model (`#[serde(default)]`, so older `.pcraft` files load unfeathered at 100 %), in `.pcraft` and in PSD (the vector mask density/feather mask parameters Photoshop writes for the layer).
- The compositor applies them to the shape exactly like a vector mask (the same `feather_sigma` blur, density lifting the outside), CPU and GPU agreeing (or the GPU falling back).
- Engine: drivable through the vector-mask edit command (or a shape equivalent) with `density` 0..100 and `feather` 0..1000 px; one history step; NaN, negative or out-of-range values → `Err`, never a panic.

title: macOS Dock icon loses Liquid Glass appearance due to runtime icon override
author: demo-nic
body:
### Description

On macOS, PhotoCraft appears to override its bundled application icon at runtime, preventing the Dock from displaying the native, macOS-version-specific appearance of the icon.

The application bundle contains PhotoCraft.icns, which is referenced by CFBundleIconFile in Info.plist. macOS can apply its native icon rendering and appearance effects, including the Liquid Glass style introduced in newer macOS versions, to the bundled icon.

However, PhotoCraft also sets a runtime window icon through egui::ViewportBuilder::with_icon(), using a PNG image. This appears to override the bundled icon, causing the Dock to display the runtime-provided image instead of the system-rendered application icon.

As a result, the Dock icon may lose the native Liquid Glass appearance and other system-managed visual treatments appropriate to the installed macOS version.

### Relevant code

In apps/photocraft/src/main.rs, the native window options include:

```
viewport: egui::ViewportBuilder::default()
    .with_icon(app_icon::window_icon())
    .with_app_id(APP_ID)
```
The runtime icon is loaded from assets/app-icon/photocraft-1024.png in apps/photocraft/src/app_icon.rs.

Meanwhile, the macOS packaging process already includes assets/app-icon/photocraft.icns in the application bundle.

### Expected behavior

On macOS, PhotoCraft should use its bundled .icns application icon and allow the operating system to apply its native icon rendering and appearance effects, including Liquid Glass where supported.

The runtime window icon should not override the bundled application icon or prevent macOS from presenting it with the appropriate system-managed appearance.

Runtime icon behavior on other platforms should remain unchanged.

### Proposed solution

Consider omitting .with_icon(app_icon::window_icon()) when running PhotoCraft as a packaged macOS application, while retaining the existing behavior on other platforms and, if necessary, for direct development builds.

title: Feature request: Unify pen (and eyedropper) cursors with the code-drawn style used by Hand and Zoom
author: VimiummuimiV
body: ## Unify tool cursors with the code-drawn style of Hand and Zoom ### Problem In PhotoCraft 0.9.0 the pen tools use the full toolbar icons as cursors. These icons already contain extra marks (plus, minus, freehand squiggle, etc.), so the cursors look visually noisy and inconsistent with each other. In addition, the cursor icons have background bleed — the canvas background and other UI backgrounds slightly show through in places, making them look dirty. Hand and Zoom already use a clean, simple style that is drawn directly in Rust code. The eyedropper currently looks okay only by chance, because its icon happens to be simple. ### Proposal Please draw the pen cursor (for all pen tool variants) and, ideally, the eyedropper cursor **directly in code**, in the same style and technique as the current Hand and Zoom cursors. - One simple pen glyph for all pen modes. - Same visual language, weight and rendering approach as Hand / Zoom. - Fully opaque, no background bleed. - Dynamic plus/minus indicators (where needed) should continue to be drawn separately in code, the same way other tools already do it. - Keep the existing Caps Lock → crosshair behaviour. ### Why - Consistent look across all custom cursors. - Cleaner and less noisy at small sizes. - No more background showing through. - Easier to maintain than a set of near-identical SVG icons with baked-in marks. Hand and Zoom already prove that the code-drawn approach works well. It would be good to extend the same style to the pen tools (and eyedropper).

title: PSD: image resources 1092/1097 are guides v2 (with colour) and guide GUIDs; export keeps them stale after guide edits
author: bramheerink
body:
## Summary

Image resources **1092** and **1097** are undocumented (not in Adobe's spec; ag-psd lists 1092 as `// ???` in `src/imageResources.ts`, psd-tools has no entry for either). From the existing corpora they decode as **Grid and Guides v2 with a colour per guide (1092)** and **a GUID per guide (1097)**.

PhotoCraft regenerates 1032 from the document but writes 1092 and 1097 back verbatim (`keep_imported_resource` returns true for them), so after any guide edit the saved PSD carries two guide lists that disagree. Decoding 1092 would also close the gap noted in #3553 ("PSD export keeps guide positions only"): guide colours could be written to and read from PSD.

## Layout (from 748 PSD/PSB files in psd-tools, ag-psd and photocraft-corpus)

**1092**, same header as 1032 but version 2:

```
u32 version        = 2
u32 grid cycle h   = 576   (1/32 px, as in 1032)
u32 grid cycle v   = 576
u32 guide count
per guide, 9 bytes:
  i32 position     (1/32 px)
  u8  direction    (0 = vertical, 1 = horizontal)
  u8  unknown      (always 0 in the corpora; a flag such as locked?)
  u8  r, g, b      (always 74,255,255 = #4AFFFF, Photoshop's default Cyan)
```

In all 367 files that have 1092, its positions and directions equal 1032's exactly, in the same order.

**1097**:

```
u32 count                       (equals 1092's guide count in every file)
per guide:
  u32 36, 36 ASCII bytes        GUID of the guide, e.g. "e65283a8-8acd-4b4d-b336-cc13199cb73d"
  u32 0                         (always 0)
  u32 36, 36 ASCII bytes        a second GUID, always 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000
                                (guess: the artboard the guide belongs to)
```

A file without guides has `00 00 00 00` (334 ag-psd files).

## Reproduction (PhotoCraft 0.9.0)

Using `psd-tools/tests/psd_files/clipping-mask4.psd` (two guides):

```
photocraft-cli run clipping-mask4.psd --cmd view.clearGuides --out cleared.psd
photocraft-cli run clipping-mask4.psd --cmd view.newGuide \
    --params '…

title: PSD export: guide resources 1092/1097 are kept stale after guide edits
author: bramheerink
body:
Split from #5965.

## Problem

PhotoCraft regenerates image resource 1032 (Grid and Guides) from the document on PSD export, but writes the undocumented resources **1092** (guides v2) and **1097** (one GUID per guide) back verbatim from the imported file, because `keep_imported_resource` returns true for them. After any guide edit the saved PSD carries two guide lists that disagree.

Both resources describe the same guides as 1032: in all 367 corpus files (psd-tools, ag-psd, photocraft-corpus) that have 1092, its positions and directions equal 1032's in the same order, and 1097's count equals 1092's. The layout is in #5965.

## Reproduction (PhotoCraft 0.9.0)

With `psd-tools/tests/psd_files/clipping-mask4.psd` (two guides):

```
photocraft-cli run clipping-mask4.psd --cmd view.clearGuides --out cleared.psd
photocraft-cli run clipping-mask4.psd --cmd view.newGuide \
    --params '{"orientation":"horizontal","position":40}' --out added.psd
```

| file | 1032 | 1092 | 1097 count |
|---|---|---|---|
| original | (512,0) (512,1) | (512,0) (512,1) | 2 |
| cleared.psd | *absent* | (512,0) (512,1) | 2 |
| added.psd | (512,0) (512,1) (1280,1) | (512,0) (512,1) | 2 |

## Expected

The saved guide resources agree with the document. If Photoshop 2026 prefers 1092 when present (likely, as it is the newer form, but not verified), guides cleared in PhotoCraft currently come back in Photoshop and guides added in PhotoCraft are missing.

## Suggested fix

Never keep 1092/1097 verbatim next to a regenerated 1032. Simplest: drop both when the guides differ from the imported ones (or always). Fuller: regenerate them from the document, which #5967 (guide colours) needs anyway.

title: PSD: read and write guide colours via image resource 1092 (guides v2)
author: bramheerink
body:
Split from #5965. Follow-up to #3553, which notes "PSD export keeps guide positions only".

## Problem

Photoshop stores a colour per guide in the undocumented image resource **1092** (Grid and Guides, version 2). PhotoCraft reads guides from 1032 only, so guide colours in a PSD are lost on import, and PhotoCraft's own per-guide colours (`Guides.colors`, #3553) are not written to PSD.

## Layout of 1092 (from 748 corpus files; see #5965)

```
u32 version        = 2
u32 grid cycle h   = 576   (1/32 px, as in 1032)
u32 grid cycle v   = 576
u32 guide count
per guide, 9 bytes:
  i32 position     (1/32 px)
  u8  direction    (0 = vertical, 1 = horizontal)
  u8  unknown      (always 0 in the corpora)
  u8  r, g, b      (always 74,255,255 = #4AFFFF, Photoshop's default Cyan)
```

Companion resource **1097**: `u32 count`, then per guide a length-prefixed (u32 36) ASCII GUID, a u32 0, and a second length-prefixed GUID that is always all zeros. A file without guides has `00 00 00 00`.

## Suggested change

- Import: read 1092 when present (position, direction and colour into `Guides.colors`), falling back to 1032.
- Export: write 1032 and 1092 from the document (1092 with the preference colour for guides without their own), plus 1097 with a fresh GUID per guide and a zero second GUID.

## To confirm with the Photoshop oracle generator

1. a guide with a non-default colour (the RGB bytes);
2. a locked guide, and one from New Guide Layout (the unknown byte);
3. guides on an artboard (the second GUID in 1097; artboards also list `guideIndeces`, see #722);
4. a file whose 1032 and 1092 disagree, to see which one Photoshop shows.

title: [Community] No issue forms for bug reports and feature requests
author: Emin-ACIKGOZ
body:
### Summary

There are no YAML issue forms, so bug reports and feature requests arrive free-form and often miss the details needed to act on them.

### Current behavior

- `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/` has no `bug_report.yml` or `feature_request.yml`.
- New issues are unstructured; reporters are given no prompt for OS, version, reproduction steps or expected behaviour.
- GitHub's community profile lists issue templates as missing.

### Motivation

- Structured intake reduces back-and-forth and near-duplicate reports (see #2993).
- Fills the community-profile gap.

### Additional context

- Issue forms are YAML files under `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/`; the chosen form becomes the issue body and can set the issue's labels.
- Suggested bug form fields: OS, PhotoCraft version or commit, build type, steps to reproduce, expected vs actual behaviour, attachments.
- Suggested feature form fields: the problem, and the behaviour requested.

### Related issues

- #5820: split from.
- #2993: closing done/duplicate tickets.
- Sibling repositories: storytold/gridcraft#894, storytold/lightcraft#648.

### Open questions

1. Which templates to ship first: bug and feature, or also a question or task form?

title: [Community] No issue chooser with contact links
author: Emin-ACIKGOZ
body:
### Summary

There is no `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml`, so the new-issue chooser offers no links to the security policy or the community chat.

### Current behavior

- `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml` is absent.
- There are no `contact_links`, so security reports and questions have no dedicated entry point in the chooser.

### Motivation

- Routes vulnerability reports to `SECURITY.md` and general questions to the Discord instead of into the issue tracker.
- Reduces misfiled issues.

### Additional context

- `config.yml` controls the template chooser and can define `contact_links` (for example to `SECURITY.md` for private vulnerability reports and to the Discord for questions).
- It can also set `blank_issues_enabled`.

### Related issues

- #5820: split from.
- #4819: private security reporting channel.
- #5819: code of conduct.

### Open questions

1. Disable blank issues, or keep an escape hatch?

title: PSD: inventory of undocumented and unread fields in the test corpora
author: bramheerink
body:
PhotoCraft keeps unknown PSD data verbatim, which preserves it on round trips. This is an inventory of what in the existing corpora is still undocumented, or documented but not read by PhotoCraft, as of PhotoCraft 0.9.0.

**How it was made.** Read-only scans of the 748 PSD/PSB files in the three corpora PhotoCraft already pins (psd-tools `tests/psd_files`, ag-psd `test/`, photocraft-corpus `photoshop/`): every tagged block, image resource and descriptor key, compared with the PhotoCraft source (a key that appears nowhere in `crates/` is counted as unused) and with what psd-tools and ag-psd name. Text keys were decoded by pairing each `Txt2` style or paragraph run with the same run in the layer's `TySh` EngineData, where keys have names, and looking for one-to-one value maps.

Every tagged-block key and image resource in the corpora is already recognised by PhotoCraft, except resources 1092/1097 (#5966, #5967). What is left sits inside blocks.

## A. Format unknown (no project documents it)

| # | Where | What is unknown | Example file | Determinable from existing files |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | `GdFl` / `GrFl` / gradient map, `GrdF = ClNs` | **Photoshop's noise-gradient synthesis**: how `RndS` (seed), `Smth` (roughness, 0–4096), `ClrS`, `VctC` (restrict colours), `ShTr` (add transparency), `Mnm `/`Mxm ` produce the colours. PhotoCraft skips noise gradients (`adjust_map.rs`), and psd-tools only approximates them ("without reproducing Photoshop's noise synthesis"). | psd-tools `gradient-styles.psd`: five noise fills with the same seed 9052369 and varying roughness, restrict colours, transparency and ranges, plus Photoshop's composite | Yes: seed, parameters and Photoshop's composite are all in the file |
| A2 | `Txt2` style run keys | No known meaning: 10 14 17 21 22 31–34 36 39–51 56–62 65–69 71–78 80–84 86 88 91 92 (constant in the corpora), and **70, 87** (vary: 87 is 100 in most runs, 0 / 5.53 / 0.08 in ag-psd `read/text-path-26`, `read/alias`, `read-write/fl…
