title: Nikon D4: 12-bit NEFs open 2.6 stops darker than 14-bit (profile white level ignores bit depth)
author: odgrim
body:
### What is wrong
The measured Nikon D4 profile (`crates/raw/src/cameras.rs`) sets the saturation level to 15520 for every D4 NEF, but that level was measured on 14-bit files. The D4 also writes 12-bit NEFs (lossless, lossy and uncompressed) whose samples only reach about 4095, so they are scaled by a level four times too high and open about 2.6 stops darker than the same scene at 14 bits. Nothing warns about it.

This is in v0.9.0 and on `main`. It only affects the D4: other bodies take their white level from the file, and a D800E 12-bit and 14-bit pair matches within 0.01 stop.

### How to see it
Public CC0 D4 files from raw.pixls.us (one scene, 4992x3292), developed with `cargo run --release -p photocraft-raw --example rawinfo -- --ppm`. Mean linear luminance of the ProPhoto output, against the 14-bit lossy file `_DSC2252`:

| File | Bits | vs 14-bit |
|---|---|---|
| `_DSC2258` lossy | 12 | -2.58 stops |
| `_DSC2256` uncompressed | 12 | -2.63 stops |
| `_DSC2260` lossless | 12 | -2.60 stops |

### Expected
A 12-bit D4 frame develops as bright as its 14-bit twin. A 12-bit sample is the 14-bit value shifted right by two, so the level for 12 bits is 15520 / 4 = 3880. The 14-bit result stays unchanged.

title: TIFF import: tiff_exif::read copies overlapping EXIF values without a total cap (62 KB file yields 50 MB)
author: odgrim
body:
### What is wrong
`tiff_exif::read` (`crates/codecs/src/codecs/tiff_exif.rs`) copies the value of every Exif, GPS and descriptive IFD0 entry it keeps (up to 1,024 per directory). An entry's value only has to lie inside the file, so many entries can point at the same bytes: a valid 62 KB TIFF with 1,000 Exif entries of 50,000 bytes each, all at one offset, makes the reader copy 50 MB, and `block()` then builds a second copy. An allocation failure aborts the process, which the panic guards cannot catch.

This runs on every TIFF import, and again on export when the document carries an EXIF block.

### How to see it
Decoding that 62,140-byte TIFF yields 50,012,032 bytes of EXIF. Encoding a TIFF with the same stream as the image's EXIF block writes a 50,012,222-byte file. (Checked on `main` at `4e1e325b`.)

### Expected
Copying is bounded by the stream's size and by a fixed cap, entries that do not fit are left out, and legitimate EXIF (including Nikon maker notes of 100 KB to about 1 MB) still round-trips.

title: GPU mode doesn't start on Raspberry Pi 5 (V3D 7.1): wgpu device limits exceed the adapter's
author: nictoumayan
body:
In GPU mode (fresh settings, `gpuBackend: auto`), PhotoCraft 0.9.0 (arm64 .deb) can't create its wgpu device on this machine. It restarts itself with `--safe-gpu` and runs on the CPU renderer.

**Machine:** Raspberry Pi Compute Module 5 Lite (BCM2712, V3D 7.1.10.2), Debian 13 (trixie), Mesa 26.2.2 (`26.2.2-1~bpo13+0~rpt1`), labwc on Wayland.

```
INFO  [main] photocraft: GPU startup: Plan { backend: Auto, env: None, reason: None, remember: false } (0.06 ms)
ERROR [main] eframe::native::run: Exiting because of error: WGPU error: Limit 'max_inter_stage_shader_variables' value 16 is better than allowed 15
INFO  [main] photocraft: GPU startup: Plan { backend: Cpu, env: None, reason: Some("--safe-gpu: CPU renderer for this launch"), remember: false } (0.06 ms)
```

**Cause:** eframe 0.36's default `WgpuSetupCreateNew::device_descriptor` (egui-wgpu 0.36.2) requests `wgpu::Limits::default()` on every backend except GL, and `downlevel_webgl2_defaults()` on GL, in both cases with `max_texture_dimension_2d: 8192`. It never checks what the adapter offers, so `request_device` fails when the adapter falls short on any single limit. V3D 7.1 falls short on several:

| Limit | requested | V3D 7.1 Vulkan (V3DV) | V3D 7.1 GL |
|---|---|---|---|
| `max_inter_stage_shader_variables` | 16 | 15 (`maxVertexOutputComponents` = 64) | |
| `max_texture_dimension_2d` | 8192 | 7680 | 4096 |

wgpu stops at the first failing limit, so the error only names one of them. egui's own shaders need far less than any of these.

**Fix:** wrap the default descriptor and lower each requested limit to the adapter's where the adapter offers less:

```rust
if let eframe::egui_wgpu::WgpuSetup::CreateNew(setup) = &mut native_options.wgpu_options.wgpu_setup {
    let egui_descriptor = std::sync::Arc::clone(&setup.device_descriptor);
    setup.device_descriptor = std::sync::Arc::new(move |adapter| {
        let mut descriptor = egui_descriptor(adapter);
        descriptor.required_limits = descriptor.required_limi…

title: Nikon NEF: Adobe RGB previews are read as sRGB (maker-note ColorSpace 0x001E is not read)
author: odgrim
body:
### What is wrong
`photocraft_raw::embedded_preview_color_space` (`crates/raw/src/preview.rs`) reads only the EXIF ColorSpace (0xA001, plus Interoperability "R03" for a Sony body set to Adobe RGB). Nikon bodies write no EXIF ColorSpace; they state the colour space of their JPEG rendering only in the maker note, tag 0x001E (1 = sRGB, 2 = Adobe RGB). So for a Nikon NEF with Adobe RGB selected, the colour fit in `photocraft-io` (`preview_profile`, `crates/io/src/raw.rs`) reads the embedded JPEG preview as sRGB and learns its look from the wrong colours.

### How to see it
- In the public raw.pixls.us Nikon set (291 files) the maker note's ColorSpace is 2 on 49 files, 1 on 212, and absent on 30.
- On current `main`, `embedded_preview_color_space` returns `None` for all of these real CC0 files, although their maker notes say Adobe RGB: D700 (`_GDN0446`), D90 (`00001`) and four D4 files (`_DSC2252`, `_DSC2256`, `_DSC2258`, `_DSC2260`). The D40 file `DSC_1842` says sRGB.
- The D700 preview JPEG itself has no EXIF or ICC segment (only DQT, SOF0 and DHT markers), so the maker note is the only statement in the file.

### Expected
When the EXIF states no colour space, the Nikon maker note's ColorSpace is used (1 = sRGB, 2 = Adobe RGB). EXIF still wins when it states one, and the preview's own ICC profile wins over both.

### Not covered here
Tagging the document opened from a preview (HE and other unsupported NEFs open untagged), and refusing BT.2100 previews (0x001E = 4).

title: Feature Request: Comprehensive Perspective Rulers and Drawing Guides
author: homable80-bit
body:
**Description:**
This issue is closely related to #2293. While #2293 proposes adding linear perspective rulers, limiting the feature to only 1- to 3-point linear perspective is insufficient. To provide a complete user experience for different art professionals, the drawing assistant guide system needs to be far more comprehensive.

Different fields have distinct requirements for perspective and drawing guides:

- Comic/Manga Artists: Require 1-6 point linear perspective(and“Multi-Point Perspective”), fisheye,concentric circle rulers, multiple curves, parallel lines, radial lines, radial curves, and parallel curves.
- Illustrators ,Game Artists (Asset/Tilemap Creation)& Animators: Heavily rely on 1-6 point linear perspective(and“Multi-Point Perspective”),fisheye,isometric perspective and similar to Haha o Tazunete Sanzenri's perspective.This refers to how 'using one-point perspective can easily result in unwanted wide-angle distortion in the image. And Hayao Miyazaki once said that perspective is not a point, but a circle.'

Furthermore, basic drawing guides such as straight lines, spline curves, basic shapes and Bézier curves are fundamental tools during the drawing process.

Focusing solely on basic linear perspective (as seen in #2293) overlooks the practical workflows of these user groups. I strongly recommend expanding the scope of the drawing guide features to include these diverse rulers, making the software truly versatile for all creators.

App does not appear in search or app list.

Add desktop database and icon cache update hooks to the RPM `%post` / `%postun` scriptlets:
- `update-desktop-database /usr/share/applications`
- `gtk-update-icon-cache -f -t /usr/share/icons/hicolor`

- OS: Fedora Linux (GNOME / Wayland)
- Installed file: `/usr/share/applications/ai.storyteller.photocraft.desktop`

title: [v0.9.0][Missing Feature] No progress feedback (and slow handling) during Embedded Profile Mismatch on large documents (unlike Photoshop)
author: I-love-craft
body:
**Description:**

In PhotoCraft v0.9.0, when opening a large document with embedded color profile different from workspace, a progress bar is correctly shown during the initial decoding phase. However, after the Embedded Profile Mismatch dialog appears, the following issues occur:

- Choosing “**Convert document’s colors to the working space**” can take several seconds (or more) on large files, with no progress bar or busy indicator. The interface appears frozen.

- Choosing “**Use the embedded profile**” or “**Discard the embedded profile**” is also noticeably slower than in Photoshop and can also cause the UI to freeze several seconds, again without any progress feedback.

The slowdown (especially for “Use the embedded profile” and “Discard the embedded profile”) seems to occur mainly (or only) when the document has an embedded Adobe RGB (1998) profile. The same document previously converted to sRGB IEC61966-2.1 opens nearly instantaneously in PhotoCraft after the initial decoding progress bar.

**Comparison with Photoshop CS2:**

A progress bar is shown while the document is being decoded (before the Embedded Profile Mismatch dialog).

If the user chooses “**Convert document’s colors to the working space**”, a second progress bar is displayed during the conversion.
Choosing “**Use the embedded profile**” or “**Discard the embedded profile**” is nearly instantaneous.

title: [Feature Request] [PhotoCraft] Change stroke tool size with the mouse wheel only (no modifier keys)
author: ensummi
body:
### Description

While a stroke tool is active and the cursor is over the canvas, let the mouse wheel change that tool's **Size** with no modifier keys: scroll up = Size +, scroll down = Size -. Today the size is changed through the brush popup slider (or Alt+right-drag), which interrupts painting.

### Which tools

Every tool that paints a stroke and has a Size setting (`size` 0.5..5000 px in the engine commands):

| Group | Tools |
|---|---|
| Painting | Brush, Pencil, Mixer Brush, Color Replacement |
| Erasing | Eraser (Brush/Pencil erase mode), Background Eraser |
| Retouching | Clone Stamp, Pattern Stamp, Healing Brush, Spot Healing Brush, Remove, History Brush |
| Tone and detail | Dodge, Burn, Sponge, Blur, Sharpen, Smudge |

### Details

- Works while the brush popup is closed, and while hovering over the Size slider or field in the popup.
- Steps scale with the current size: small steps at small sizes (1-20 px), larger steps at big sizes, so going from 5 px to 500 px does not take hundreds of scrolls.
- The tool outline on the canvas and the Size value in the toolbar update live.
- Opt-in or switchable in Preferences, because the plain wheel currently scrolls or zooms the canvas (Alt+wheel zooms, see #304). Also an option to invert the wheel direction.
- Photoshop has no wheel-only resize, so this is an optional convenience, not a parity change. Krita and GIMP offer it.

### Implementation hint

The engine already has `tools.increaseBrushSize` and `tools.decreaseBrushSize` (bound to `]` and `[`). The wheel only needs to trigger those two commands for the active stroke tool.

title: Save history in document: keep the undo history in .pcraft files (opt-in)
author: switch87
body:
I'm working on this.

## Wish

Close a `.pcraft` document, open it again tomorrow, and still be able to step back through the History panel. Today the undo history lives in memory only, so every save-and-close is a point of no return.

This has been asked of Photoshop since 2012 and is still open there: [P: Save with history](https://community.adobe.com/t5/photoshop-ecosystem-ideas/p-save-with-history/idi-p/12249784) (41 replies, the latest in May 2026). Affinity Photo has it as *File › Save History with Document*.

## Proposed behaviour

- A preference, **Save history in document** (Preferences › Performance, next to History States), **off by default**. Off, a save writes exactly the bytes it writes today.
- On, saving to the native `.pcraft` format also stores the document's undo states (labels, the targeted layers, and each state's document). PSD, TIFF and the flat formats are not affected.
- States are stored the way the History panel already keeps them: whole-document snapshots whose tiles are shared copy-on-write. In the bundle they are extra manifests that reference the same content-addressed `tiles/`/`blobs/`, so only the pixels a step actually changed cost space.
- A size limit: at most the History States preference worth of steps, and a byte budget for the tiles only the history needs. The oldest states are left out when the budget is exceeded; the document itself is always saved in full.
- Opening restores the history, so Undo (and the History panel) works right after reopening. Redo states are not stored.
- Failure is never fatal: a missing, unreadable, corrupt or oversized history section is ignored and the document opens as it does today, without history.
- Compatibility: the history is a separate, optional section of the bundle. Older PhotoCraft versions ignore it and open the document as before; files without it open unchanged. The manifest `format_version` does not change.

Snapshots stay session-only, as in Photoshop (#2966 / #3545); this is about …

title: Contributors: keep people.toml sorted alphabetically to stop onboarding merge conflicts
author: 1Git2Clone
body:
## Problem

Every entry in `contributors/people.toml` gets appended to the end of the file, so any two PRs that add a contributor edit the same lines and conflict with each other. Newcomers hit this all the time, often in their first PR. Their actual change is ready to merge, but they still have to rebase and fix the conflict by hand, usually while waiting on review.

Right now, 14 open PRs touch `people.toml`. Of those, 5 conflict with `main` inside `people.toml` itself: #5774, #5609, #5326, #5279 and #5252. The other 9 are mergeable now, but they will start conflicting as soon as another contributor entry lands. #2863 hit the same conflict: it collided with the `[people.sidney]` entry and had to be rebased just for that.

## Proposal

Keep the `[people.*]` tables in case-insensitive alphabetical order by GitHub username:

1. Sort the existing file once. The order isn't shown anywhere, since the About window sorts by first contribution (#369), so this changes nothing users see.
2. Change the header comment to say "add your entry in alphabetical order" instead of "copy this block".
3. Make `contributors.py --add-me` insert the entry in sorted position rather than appending it.
4. Optionally, add a cheap CI check that fails when the tables are out of order, so the order doesn't drift.

With sorted entries, new lines go into different spots in the file, and two PRs only collide when their usernames sort next to each other.

## Scope

The file and `contributors.py` come from the shared craftrules contributors standard, so this probably applies to every *craft repo that has a `people.toml`, not just photocraft.

title: Neural Filters › JPEG Artifacts Removal on a local model
author: diegochagas
body:
Split out of #2943 at ticket-craft's request (that ticket now covers AI Denoise only).

## What

Compression damage is one of the two cleanups every photo editor is asked for first, and Photoshop does it with a model: **Neural Filters › JPEG Artifacts Removal**. PhotoCraft has **Filter › Noise › Reduce Noise** (`crates/engine/src/filters_ext.rs`), a classical filter that cannot undo 8×8 block edges or ringing.

`docs/gaps.md` G15 lists Neural Filters as missing; #2313 names restoration among the first uses of downloadable models.

## Proposed

- **Neural Filters › JPEG Artifacts Removal**: runs on the local model provider (shared with #2787 / #2788 / #2943 / #2942) with a model trained on compression artifacts; the strength maps to *Low / Medium / High* as in Photoshop; keeps the result on a new layer by default.
- Tiles large images with overlap, respects the selection, converts at the provider boundary (8-bit sRGB tiles in, the document's depth and profile out) and never touches a pixel outside the selection.
- Without a backend it reports the missing backend (there is no classical equivalent). Headless under the automation policy.
- Tests: a fake provider; tiles and seams; selection respected; 8/16/32-bit; `panic_hunt`. For an honest quality check, a synthetic image (known clean source + JPEG at quality 30–50) and the PSNR gain over Reduce Noise, measured and recorded.

Prior art: GIMP-ML and the OpenVINO plug-ins are what GIMP users install for this. I'd like to implement this here once the provider seam exists.

title: Neural Filters › Super Zoom: AI upscaling of a selection on a local model
author: diegochagas
body:
Split out of #2942 at ticket-craft's request (that ticket now covers Image Size › Preserve Details 2.0 only).

## What

**Filter › Neural Filters › Super Zoom** enlarges a selection (or the whole canvas) with a model and puts the result in a new document or layer at 2×/3×/4×. PhotoCraft has no equivalent: `docs/gaps.md` G15 lists Super Zoom as missing, and #2313 asks for downloadable models with upscaling as its first use case.

## Proposed

- **Neural Filters › Super Zoom** on the same local model provider as #2942 (ComfyUI's *Upscale Image (using Model)* node with an open ESRGAN-family model such as Real-ESRGAN x2/x4): the selection, or the whole canvas, enlarged at 2×/3×/4× into a new document or layer with the model's result; the classical kernel fills in any size the model does not produce natively. Tiles over the model's tile size, with overlap. Generative Upscale (a diffusion upscale with a prompt) stays with #41.
- Without a configured backend it reports the missing backend.
- Headless too (`photocraft-cli` and MCP), under the automation policy of #2788: the backend URL is a flag or environment variable, nothing is sent anywhere else.
- Tests: a fake provider returning a known enlargement; tiling and overlap seams; 8/16/32-bit sources (the model takes 8-bit sRGB tiles, the result goes back through the document's profile and depth); `panic_hunt`.

Prior art: GIMP users reach for the GIMP Upscale plug-in (Real-ESRGAN) or GIMP-ML's super-resolution for exactly this. I'd like to implement this here once the provider seam exists, right after #2942 since they share the path.

title: Headless AI backend configuration for serve, batch and mcp (backend URL preference, flag, env var, automation policy)
author: diegochagas
body:
Split out of #2788 at ticket-craft's request (that ticket now covers the segmentation model itself). This is the configuration and policy piece that every model-backed command needs headless: #2788, #2787, #2790, #2942, #2943, #2944 and their follow-ups.

## What

Batch cut-outs, restorations and upscales are where a local model matters most, so the model path must work without the window: `photocraft-cli serve`, `batch` and `mcp` need to know which backend to talk to, and headless sessions must not talk to the network unless the user opted in.

## Proposed

- **Backend address is a preference**, not a constant: `127.0.0.1:8188` (ComfyUI) is only the default. ComfyUI Desktop takes another port when 8188 is busy, and the backend may be on another machine on the LAN. Preferences › AI (or Plug-ins) holds the URL; `photocraft-cli` takes it as `--ai-backend <url>` and the `PHOTOCRAFT_AI_BACKEND` environment variable, so `serve`, `batch` and `mcp` use the same backend without a profile.
- **Automation policy**: headless sessions only talk to the network when the user opted in. The configured backend is an explicit allow: `serve`/`mcp` refuse `"backend": "model"` with a clear error until a backend URL is given on the command line or in the preferences, and `command_list` reports which backend `auto` would pick. Nothing is sent anywhere but that URL.
- Shared by every model-backed command through the provider seam (#4098's shared AI layer, craft-libs #69), so each feature adds only its model, never its own transport or settings.
- Tests: the preference, flag and environment variable precedence; `serve`/`mcp` refusing the model backend without an allow; `command_list` reporting the backend; nothing reaches any other host (fake transport).

Measured case (from @HassanJb961's data point on #2788, 0.6.0, `photocraft-cli serve`, Windows 11): a 1080×1080 product photo on a busy, low-contrast background; `layer.removeBackground` returned a full-width band, unusable as a cut-out, w…

title: New Guide Layout: fields lock to px instead of respecting ruler units and custom units
author: safvanedge
body:
### Summary
In Photoshop, the **New Guide Layout** dialog (`View > Guides > New Guide Layout…`) formats its spacing, margin, and size fields according to the document's active ruler unit (as configured in Preferences or right-clicked on rulers / status bar). Users can type any unit (`cm`, `in`, `px`, `pt`, `mm`, `pica`, `%`) or bare numbers without them being forced or immediately converted to pixels while typing.

In PhotoCraft, these fields were previously locked to `px`:
1. Spacing (`gutter`, `rowGutter`) and Margin (`Top`, `Left`, `Bottom`, `Right`) fields forced the `"px"` suffix widget and converted input immediately into pixels.
2. The fields did not open in the active ruler unit.
3. Typing bare values did not append the ruler unit upon lost focus/Tab.
4. Typing values with units without spaces (e.g. `10cm`) did not normalize with a space (`10 cm`).
5. Clicking with the mouse selected all text instead of placing the caret at the clicked point.

### Expected Behavior
- When the dialog opens, fields display values formatted in the document's active ruler unit (`"0.71 cm"`, `"0.28 in"`, `"20 px"`).
- Users can type any supported unit or bare numbers without immediate conversion while typing.
- When navigating to the next field (Tab / lost focus), bare numbers append the active ruler unit, and unspaced units format with a space (`10cm` -> `10 cm`).
- Tabbing into a field selects all text for quick replacement; clicking with the mouse places the cursor without selecting all text.
- Live canvas preview reflects the typed units at document resolution.
- Reopening the dialog displays values converted to the current ruler unit.

title: Pen: Holding Spacebar while dragging an anchor point breaks path and activates Pan/Move
author: cherry-hur-47
body:
When drawing vector paths with the Pen Tool (P), holding Spacebar while clicking and dragging to reposition an active anchor point aborts the path operation and switches to the Hand/Pan tool.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Select the Pen Tool (P).
2. Click and hold the left mouse button on the canvas, dragging to pull out Bézier direction handles.
3. While still holding the left mouse button, press and hold Spacebar.
4. Attempt to move the mouse to reposition the anchor point.

### Expected Behavior (Photoshop Parity)
Holding Spacebar while keeping the mouse button pressed should freeze the Bézier handle angle/length and allow moving the anchor point itself across the canvas. Releasing Spacebar (while still holding the mouse click) should resume adjusting handle angles before finalizing the point.

### Actual Behavior
Pressing Spacebar immediately triggers the Pan/Hand tool, breaks the active Pen stroke, and leaves dangling Bézier control points on the canvas.

### Environment
- PhotoCraft v0.9.0
- OS: Windows 10/11 (x64)

title: Eyedropper: Sampling canvas with an active Layer Mask sets RGB color instead of grayscale intensity
author: cherry-hur-47
body:
Sampling colors with the Eyedropper Tool (I) while a Layer Mask is targeted sets a full RGB color in the Foreground swatch instead of a grayscale luminance value (0–255).

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Open an image with color content.
2. Add a Layer Mask to the active layer and ensure the mask thumbnail is targeted (has the active bracket border).
3. Select the Eyedropper Tool (I).
4. Click on any saturated color area on the canvas (e.g., pure red or blue).
5. Inspect the active Foreground color swatch.

### Expected Behavior (Photoshop Parity)
Because Layer Masks only accept single-channel luminance data, the Eyedropper should sample the luminosity/grayscale value of the clicked pixel and map the Foreground swatch to a neutral gray (K value / 0–255), never an RGB color.

### Actual Behavior
The Eyedropper samples and retains full RGB chromatic data in the Foreground swatch while working inside the Layer Mask.

### Environment
- PhotoCraft v0.9.0
- OS: Windows 10/11 (x64)

title: History snapshots: New Snapshot opens during Free Transform, a cleared name errors, stale first-snapshot thumbnail
author: davidmann4
body:
Found while reviewing #3567 (History panel: New Snapshot dialog and the first snapshot, part of #2966). None of these crash. Line numbers are on #3567's head (70711bb9c).

1. **New Snapshot opens during Free Transform.** `crates/ui-egui/src/panels.rs:3158` calls `snapshot_dialog::open(app)` without the `app.ui.transform.is_none()` check that the plain camera click (`footer_cmd`, line 3163) and the snapshot rows get.
   - Repro: Ctrl+T, then ⌥-click the camera, then OK. A snapshot is taken while the transform is still open.
   - Expected: the click does nothing during Free Transform, as a plain click does. The check belongs in `snapshot_dialog::open`, so the History panel menu (#3534) and the "Show New Snapshot Dialog by Default" option (#3634) are covered too.
2. **A cleared name errors.** `snapshot_dialog::confirm` sends the name field as typed, and `name_param` (`crates/engine/src/history_cmds.rs:113`) rejects an empty or blank string.
   - Repro: ⌥-click the camera, delete the suggested name, OK. The result is "`name` must be a non-empty string".
   - Expected: the default name "Snapshot N".
3. **Stale thumbnail for the first snapshot.** `snapshot_thumbs` is keyed by (DocId, snapshot id), and every document's first snapshot now has id 0. Entries are pruned only for the document being drawn and never on close. A `.pcraft` file keeps its DocId, and `add_document` reuses it when no open document has it.
   - Repro: open a `.pcraft` with the History panel showing, paint, save, close, reopen. The top row shows the old image.
   - Expected: thumbnails of a closed document are dropped.
4. **The first snapshot is taken before served fonts arrive (web build).** It is made in `DocState::new`. `Session::refresh_type_layers` later redraws type layers whose font was fetched on demand, without a history step, and doesn't update the snapshot.
   - Repro: in the web build, open a document whose type layers use a served font and show PhotoCraft's own layout. Click the top History…

title: Type: Pressing Escape while editing text commits changes instead of canceling/reverting
author: cherry-hur-47
body:
Pressing the Escape key while actively editing an existing text layer commits the modifications instead of canceling the edit session and reverting to the previous state.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Select the Horizontal Type Tool (T) and create a text layer with the word `ORIGINAL`.
2. Commit the text (Ctrl + Enter).
3. Click into the text layer again with the Type Tool and append new text: `MODIFIED`.
4. Without clicking away or unfocusing the field, press the Escape (Esc) key.

### Expected Behavior (Photoshop Parity)
Pressing Escape during an active text editing session must cancel all uncommitted changes and immediately restore the text string to its state prior to entering edit mode (`ORIGINAL`).

### Actual Behavior
Pressing Escape commits the newly typed text (`ORIGINAL MODIFIED`) and closes editing mode, providing no way to discard edits.

### Environment
- PhotoCraft v0.9.0
- OS: Windows 10/11 (x64)

title: Quick Mask: Inverting with Ctrl+I paints canvas red and drops selection upon exiting mode (Q)
author: cherry-hur-47
body:
Inverting a Quick Mask using Ctrl + I paints the entire viewport red and completely clears the selection when exiting Quick Mask mode (Q).

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Create a rectangular selection on the canvas using the Rectangular Marquee Tool (M).
2. Press Q to enter Quick Mask mode (the unselected area is covered with the translucent red rubylith mask).
3. Press Ctrl + I to invert the mask.
4. Press Q again to exit Quick Mask mode back to standard selection mode.

### Expected Behavior (Photoshop Parity)
Pressing Ctrl + I inside Quick Mask mode should invert the mask buffer (making the interior red and the exterior clear). Exiting Quick Mask (Q) should produce an inverted selection marquee (the entire canvas selected except the original rectangle).

### Actual Behavior
Pressing Ctrl + I paints the entire canvas solid red, and pressing Q to exit produces no selection marquee at all (the selection is entirely lost).

### Environment
- PhotoCraft v0.9.0
- OS: Windows 10/11 (x64)

title: Render Video sizes frame buffers from document data with no cap
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
Render Video sizes its frame buffers from document-derived data with no cap, so a crafted document can drive unbounded allocation on render. Full evidence, reachability and a ready-to-apply patch are in the parent audit: #5599 (finding 1).

Currently covered by open PRs #5618 and #5670 (not ours — filed by other contributors; we are not duplicating).

title: PSB foreign-order long-key blocks written with a 4-byte length into a little-endian TIFF
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
PSB foreign-order long-key blocks are written with a 4-byte length into a little-endian TIFF structure, corrupting the block. Full evidence, reachability and a ready-to-apply patch are in the parent audit: #5599 (finding 2).

Fix PR: #5600 (regression test included).

title: SVG raster budget missing
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
SVG import rasterises embedded/fallback content with no aggregate decoded-pixel budget, so a crafted SVG can allocate without bound. Full evidence, reachability and a ready-to-apply patch are in the parent audit: #5599 (finding 3).

Currently covered by open PR #5671 (not ours).

title: Affinity decode budget missing
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
Affinity import decodes embedded images and resamples staging buffers with no document-wide budget, so a crafted document can allocate without bound until the process dies. Full evidence and reachability are in the parent audit: #5599 (finding 4).

**Fixed** by #5738 (merged): a 1 GiB decoded-pixel budget with regression tests over both charge sites.

title: Clone Stamp, Healing Brush, Spot Healing and Remove render stroke coverage without Pattern Stamp's size guard
author: saad-mughal435
body:
## Summary

Pattern Stamp refuses a stroke it cannot render: `reject_huge_stroke` bounds the
footprint from the points and brush size before anything is drawn, `reject_bounds`
checks the rendered box, and `MAX_STROKE_PIXELS` sets the allowance. Those three
live in `crates/engine/src/retouch_cmds/pattern_stamp.rs` and are private to that
module.

The other stroke commands reach the same dense conversion with no equivalent
guard:

| Command | Path |
|---|---|
| `paint.cloneStamp` | `retouch_cmds.rs` (Clone Stamp) |
| `paint.healingBrush` | `retouch_cmds.rs` (Healing Brush) |
| `paint.spotHealingBrush` | `retouch_cmds.rs` (`spot_heal_surface`) |
| Remove | `retouch_cmds/remove.rs` |
| `paint.historyBrush` | `retouch_cmds.rs` — tracked separately as #4961 |

## Why the box is not bounded by the canvas

Stroke coverage is accumulated in tiles, so a thin stroke keeps only the tiles it
touches. `StrokeRenderer::dense_coverage()` then materialises the **whole bounding
box** as one `vec![0.0f32; w * h]`, and the retouch paths read a `Region` over the
same box for every channel. The box comes from the stroke's own points, which are
validated against `MAX_COORD` rather than the document, so it is not bounded by
the canvas size.

Both allocations use the infallible `vec!`, so a request that cannot be served
aborts the process rather than returning an error — which *Never crash* in
`AGENTS.md` rules out ("a malformed file, a bad command or MCP param ... must
produce an error the user or agent can act on, never a panic").

These commands are reachable from the JSON control channel and MCP as well as the
UI, so the parameters are the automation surface `SECURITY.md` says to treat as
potentially malicious.

## Suggested fix

Share Pattern Stamp's three guards from the parent `retouch_cmds` module and apply
them in each command: `reject_huge_stroke` before anything is rendered,
`reject_bounds` before the dense region read. The allowance already leaves room
for a stroke running corne…

title: CI: run the tests with cargo nextest
author: davidmann4
body:
**TL;DR: run CI's tests in parallel with cargo nextest and stop at the first failure, so the test jobs (Windows 43.5 min, Linux 35.3) finish sooner and a failing PR frees its runner early. Overlaps #2933, which measured nextest plus skipping examples at 39.8 → 32.6 min on Windows.**

The `test` job is the critical path of every CI run, and most of its test time goes into running test binaries **one after another**. This moves the test steps to `cargo nextest` on the same runners: no new jobs, no extra runner slots. That matters because the queue, not execution, is already the bottleneck (#5543). It brings #2204's measured nextest gain to CI.

Split from the original version of this issue (as asked): running the cheap checks first is #6119, and limiting the craft-fonts pass is #6120 (it uses nextest's filter, so it builds on this one).

## Numbers (public Actions API, 2026-10-15)

Last green `main` run ([38698210256](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/actions/runs/38698210256)):

| Job / step | Time |
|---|---|
| **test (windows-latest)** | **43.5 min** (`cargo test` 38.1) |
| test (ubuntu-latest) | 35.3 min |
| ↳ Test | 16.1 |
| ↳ Test without heif | 2.8 |
| ↳ Test with craft-fonts | 12.8 |
| corpus / web / wasm32 | 9.9 / 6.2 / 1.8 |

In the last 40 failed PR runs, the failing step was a test step in 36 runs on Linux and 29 on Windows. Those jobs went red only after a median of **24 min** (Linux) and **50 min** (Windows): the test binaries run one at a time.

Queue wait from run creation to job start, last 60 runs: median under 1 min, but **p90 is 16–17 min** for the test jobs when many PRs push at once (the 20-concurrent-job cap, #5543). A failing PR that frees its runner sooner helps everyone in that queue.

## Where the time goes

`cargo test` runs about 245 test binaries one at a time (217 integration-test files plus the lib targets). #2204 measured locally that 251 of 297 s of a warm `cargo test --workspace` is binaries running serially, with the cores idl…

title: CI: run clippy, layers and scorecard checks before the tests
author: davidmann4
body:
**TL;DR: show a clippy, layering or scorecard failure after ~3 min instead of ~45, by running those checks before the tests. No extra cost on green runs.**

In the CI `test` job, clippy, `xtask layers` and `scorecard --check` run **after** all the test passes. Together they take about 1.5 min, but a failure in them is reported only after the full test run.

Measured on the last 40 failed PR runs (public Actions API, 2026-10-15): clippy failed in about 15 s, but the job went red **41–48 min** after it started. Format already runs first and goes red at about 2 min.

## Plan

Move clippy, `xtask layers` and `scorecard --check` up, right after Format and before the tests. The steps stay the same, so a green run costs nothing extra. Clippy uses main's warm cache (0.9 min on main today), and a lint failure goes red after a few minutes.

This is deliberately **not** a separate "quick" job that the other jobs wait for:
- it would add its setup time to every green run, to save time on about 4% of failures;
- it would take another runner slot while the queue is already the bottleneck (#5543);
- a parallel quick job can't cancel the slow jobs on fork PRs, because their `GITHUB_TOKEN` is read-only.

Split from #6117 (the CI test-job speedups); related: #5543.

title: CI: run only the font tests in the craft-fonts pass
author: davidmann4
body:
**TL;DR: run only the ~3,800 tests of the 3 crates that read the fonts in the craft-fonts pass, instead of all ~8,900 again (that step takes 12.8 of the Linux job's 35.3 min today).**

The CI step "Test with craft-fonts" builds the workspace with the optional `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR` input and then runs **every** test in the workspace again. On main's last green run it took **12.8 min** of the Linux job's 35.3. But `CRAFT_FONTS` is only read in three crates:

- `photocraft-text` (`craft_fonts.rs`, `fonts.rs`, tests)
- `photocraft-io` (`svg.rs`)
- `photocraft-ui-egui` (`cjk_fonts.rs`)

Engine and the apps only pass text on to those crates.

## Plan

- Keep the exact build selection (`--workspace --locked --features heif`). As the step's comment explains, any other package or feature selection recompiles the dependency graph and runs the runner out of disk.
- Run only the tests of those three packages, with nextest's filter: `-E 'package(photocraft-text) | package(photocraft-io) | package(photocraft-ui-egui)'`. The filter changes what runs, not what is built.

This uses nextest's filter, so it builds on #6117 (nextest in CI). Split from #6117; related: #5543.

title: Channels: a spot channel viewed alone shows ink as white (should be black = 100% ink)
author: ingling
body:
### What happens

A spot channel viewed on its own in the Channels panel (colour channels hidden, only the spot channel's eye on) shows **ink as white**: 100% ink displays white, no ink displays black.

In Photoshop, and in prepress generally, a spot channel's grayscale reads **black = 100% ink, white = 0%**, the same way CMYK plates do. PhotoCraft already shows its CMYK plates that way, but not spot channels.

The overlay with the colour channels on is consistent with the stored data, so the two views disagree. A blue spot channel tints blue exactly where its lone grayscale view is **white**. Anyone building separations by looking at the channel (and painting it the Photoshop way, black = ink) gets inverted ink.

### Steps to reproduce

1. New RGB document. Channels panel › New Spot Channel…, pick a colour such as blue.
2. Paint or fill part of the spot channel.
3. Hide RGB so only the spot channel is visible: note where the image is white and where it is black.
4. Turn RGB back on: the spot colour appears where step 3 showed **white**.

**Expected:** step 3 shows the inked area black (black = 100% ink), and the spot colour appears over the areas that were black.
**Actual:** step 3 shows the inked area white.

Seen on macOS (0.9.0).

### Where it comes from (main at df055f3)

- Spot ink is stored as value 1 = solid ink (`multichannel_map.rs`; `AlphaChannel::overlay_coverage` in `crates/doc/src/lib.rs`: "spot channels show ink where the channel is white").
- `crates/ui-egui/src/channel_view.rs` › `render_with_source`: with no colour channel visible, the channel is drawn with `gray(&first.surface)`, i.e. the raw stored value, so ink shows white. The single-colour-channel branch a few lines below already inverts ink channels ("Ink channels read dark where there is ink"), but only for CMYK.

So the grayscale presentation of spot channels should invert (show `1 - value`), matching CMYK plates and Photoshop. Editing a targeted spot channel should probably use the same co…

title: Text: what a TySh rebuild (`build_tysh`) loses or changes, measured on the corpora
author: varanus-salvator
body:
Every text edit rebuilds the layer's `TySh` with `build_tysh` (`crates/engine/src/type_cmds.rs`, `canvas_geom.rs`). Unedited layers are kept byte-for-byte, so a plain open/save round trip doesn't show these differences; they appear after the first edit.

Two measurements, both on EngineData leaves:

## 1. Rebuild of every text layer

Every text layer in the psd-tools, ag-psd and Photoshop oracle corpora (132 layers, 97 files), passed through `build_tysh` and compared with the original:

- `EngineDict/ParagraphRun/RunArray[]/ParagraphSheet/Properties`: on all 132 layers, these keys are not written back:
  - `WordSpacing`, `LetterSpacing`, `GlyphSpacing`;
  - `HyphenatedWordSize`, `PreHyphen`, `PostHyphen`, `ConsecutiveHyphens`, `Zone`;
  - `EveryLineComposer`, `Hanging`, `Burasagari`, `KinsokuOrder`;
  - `Adjustments` (`Axis`, `XY`).

  The run's `Properties` are rebuilt from the model (`paragraph_properties`), which has no fields for these keys, so non-default values set in Photoshop are lost.
- `ResourceDict/FontSet[]` and `DocumentResources/FontSet[]` are rebuilt from constants (`font_entry`: `Script` 0, `FontType` 1, `Synthetic` 0):
  - `FontType` 2 → 1 on all 132 layers;
  - `Script` 4 → 0 on 35 layers;
  - `Synthetic` 3 → 0 on 13 layers (the faux bold/italic files).
- `EngineDict/AntiAlias` 7 → 3 on 14 layers (`src.psd` layers with the "Windows" anti-alias modes).
- `StyleSheetData/AutoKerning` false → true on 21 layers. The kerning mode is also stored in `Txt2`; not checked whether that compensates.
- `ParagraphSheet/Properties/LeadingType` 1 → 0 on 11 layers.

## 2. Photoshop's own change vs PhotoCraft's

Several oracle files come in families that differ in one setting (`antialias-*`, `paragraph-justify-*`, `paragraph-box-*`, `paragraph-(no-)hyphenation-narrow`, `caps-*`, `tracking-*`). For a pair (A, B), B's text model is applied to A's `TySh` with `build_tysh`, and the fields Photoshop changed between A and B are compared with PhotoCraft's result (`FontSet`…

title: PSD write: verifying PhotoCraft-written files through the Photoshop oracle pipeline
author: varanus-salvator
body:
## Context

The Photoshop oracle corpus (`storytold/photocraft-corpus`) is generated headlessly: `run-jsx.sh` drives Photoshop through AppleScript, and `generate.jsx` saves 258 files. That covers the read direction (Photoshop writes, PhotoCraft reads). The write direction has no Photoshop check yet (FILE-216-4, `docs/gaps.md`: "No test opens our exports in a third-party editor"). A write fix can currently only be verified by someone opening the file by hand.

#6129 shows that the oracle families can already act as a write oracle without Photoshop: for a pair of files differing in one setting, the difference is how Photoshop writes that change, and PhotoCraft's version of the same change can be compared with it. Byte or EngineData equality is stricter than necessary, though: Photoshop may accept a file and interpret it the same while the bytes differ, or accept it and silently interpret it differently. Only Photoshop can say which.

## A verification loop on the existing pipeline

The same `run-jsx.sh` mechanism can close the loop. One possible shape:

1. **Recipes as data.** A recipe is a JSON file in the corpus repo:
   - a base corpus file;
   - a change in two forms: the Action Manager `set` that `generate.jsx` would send, and the PhotoCraft command with its params (`layer.layerStyle.*`, type commands).

   Families can also be produced mechanically: read a layer's descriptor (`textKey`, `layerEffects`, adjustment), change one key, save. Each Photoshop key then gets its own pair, and the byte difference attributes PSD fields to settings, including fields nobody has decoded yet.
2. **Photoshop reference, once.** For each recipe, Photoshop saves B and a descriptor dump (as `dump-text.jsx` does). The references are keyed by Photoshop version and recipe hash, so they are generated once per Photoshop version.
3. **PhotoCraft output, on ordinary CI.** For each recipe, a headless `xtask` imports A, applies the command and exports. This runs on GitHub-hosted runners for …

title: [Feature Request] Add RGB and Realistic Pigment (Mixbox-like) Blending Modes to Mixer Brush
author: homable80-bit
body:
**1. Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Currently, digital painters using the Mixer Brush face a common issue where color blending relies purely on standard digital color spaces. This often results in unnatural, muddy, or desaturated transitions. For example, mixing blue and yellow in standard digital blending often yields a greyish or brown transition rather than the vibrant green a traditional painter would expect. This discrepancy disrupts the intuitive painting workflow for artists transitioning from traditional to digital media.But since some people actually prefer transitions that result in grey or brown, so please provide two different blending modes.

**2. Describe the solution you'd like**
I propose adding a "Color Blending Mode" option specifically for the Mixer Brush tool, featuring at least two distinct algorithms:

Standard RGB Blending: The conventional digital additive/computational mixing for users who prefer standard digital behavior.

Realistic Pigment Blending (Natural Color Mixing): A subtractive or perceptual color mixing algorithm that accurately simulates real-world paint behavior. Ideally, this would use a pigment-based mixing algorithm similar to Mixbox. This would allow colors like cyan and yellow to naturally mix into green, or red and blue into purple without losing saturation, closely mirroring the intuitive mixing engines found in software like Clip Studio Paint (v2.0+ "Perceptual" mixing) and Rebelle.

**3. Describe alternatives you've considered**
Currently, artists must manually select intermediate colors from the color wheel to "bridge" the gradient, or use a combination of complex layer blending modes (like Multiply or Color Burn) and low opacity brushes to simulate pigment mixing. Both workarounds are time-consuming and break the fluidity of the painting process.

title: [Feature Request]Support for OKlch and Okhsl in the Color Picker
author: homable80-bit
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Most digital painting or image editing software (and presumably Photocraft) defaults to traditional HSV or HSL color spaces for their color pickers. However, these color spaces are not perceptually uniform.
For example, in HSL, if you lock the Lightness at 50%, pure yellow (Hue 60) appears extremely bright to the human eye, while pure blue (Hue 240) appears very dark.
This represents a major pain point for artists. When painting ambient lighting or adjusting shadows, artists frequently need to shift the hue. Doing so in HSL/HSV destroys the established values (light/dark relationships) of the artwork, forcing the artist to manually and repeatedly compensate for the lightness shift by eye.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I would like Photocraft to implement OKlch and Okhsl as options in the color picker UI.

- OKlch: Based on the OKLab color space, it offers perceptual uniformity across Lightness (L), Chroma (C), and Hue (h). If an artist locks the "L" value and shifts the hue, the perceived brightness remains strictly identical regardless of the selected color.

- Okhsl: This maps the perceptual uniformity of OKLab onto the familiar cylindrical coordinates of traditional HSL. It provides an intuitive interface for artists who are used to HSL workflows but want the underlying mathematical accuracy of perceptual uniformity.

This feature would allow artists to perform advanced coloring techniques, such as "locking values while shifting hue/chroma," drastically improving color management accuracy.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Current workarounds severely disrupt the creative workflow:
- Using third-party OKlch web tools to generate colors, copying the Hex/RGB codes, and pasting them back into Photocraft.
- Creating a flat grayscale layer set to the "Luminosity" blend mode on top of the canvas to constantly check and correct value shifts manually.

title: Performance: cancelling a Gaussian Blur job over budget (P25: 478 ms vs 200 ms)
author: davidmann4
body:
**TL;DR:** Cancelling a Gaussian Blur job on a 24 MP image can take over 400 ms before the worker stops; the budget is 200 ms.

Part of #210 (scorecard P25, docs/gaps.md G2).

## What's slow on main
Scenario P25, "Cancel a Gaussian Blur job on 24 MP (until the worker exits)", `perf_scenarios` row `cancel Gaussian Blur r 50 job on 24 MP`, metric `max`, budget 200 ms (`perf/budgets.toml`).

Measured on origin/main 4e7a17cd5 (release, `perf_scenarios --cpu --only "cancel Gaussian Blur"`, Windows 11, otherwise idle machine), three runs, n = 8 each:

| run | p50 | max |
|---|---:|---:|
| 1 | 38 ms | 410 ms |
| 2 | 69 ms | 478 ms |
| 3 | 144 ms | 424 ms |

The median is well inside the budget but the worst case is about twice it, so some stretch of the blur runs a long time between `ctl.cancelled()` checks (`crates/algo/src/blur.rs:273`, `:293`). Which stretch is to be measured, not assumed.

## Proposal
- Measure where the cancel latency goes (stage timings from a throwaway probe).
- Check the cancel flag often enough inside the long stretch that the worker exits within budget, without slowing the uncancelled blur.
- Output stays bit-identical: a test compares the uncancelled result against the current path.
- Before/after table in the PR; `enforce` stays `false` unless max is under budget with margin.

title: Preferences: "Save in Background" does nothing (UI-217-4)
author: davidmann4
body:
**TL;DR:** Preferences › File Handling › "Save in Background" does nothing: turning it off should make saves run in the foreground with a progress dialog, as in Photoshop.

Part of #217 (scorecard UI-217-4, docs/gaps.md G9; prefs audit field `file_handling.save_in_background`).

## What's missing on main
`file_handling.save_in_background` (`crates/engine/src/prefs.rs:442`, default `true`) is listed as unread by the scorecard prefs audit. Saves always run as a background job (`crates/ui-egui/src/jobs_ui.rs:252`), whatever the preference says.

## Photoshop's behaviour
- With **Save in Background** on (the default), you keep working while the file is written; progress shows in the document tab and status bar.
- With it off, the save blocks the app and shows a progress window until the file is written. Adobe's own KB uses this as the fix for "View PDF After Saving" opening the PDF before it is complete: with the option off, nothing that follows a save runs before the file is written. (Adobe KB "PDF doesn't automatically open when saved"; Adobe Community "No progress bar when saving".)

## Proposal
- Read the preference where a save starts: on → today's background job; off → the same encode/write runs, but the UI shows a modal progress dialog and takes no document edits until it ends. Anything queued after the save (close, quit) runs only after the file is complete.
- The save itself stays one code path (same encoder, same atomic write, same error reporting); only the waiting differs.
- Tests: with the pref off, a save is complete before the next action runs; with it on, behaviour unchanged; a failing save reports its error in both modes.
- Flip the prefs audit (`cargo xtask scorecard`).

title: Preferences: "Animated Zoom" does nothing, holding the Zoom tool does not zoom (UI-217-4)
author: davidmann4
body:
**TL;DR:** Preferences › Tools › "Animated Zoom" does nothing: with it on, holding the mouse button down with the Zoom tool should zoom continuously, as in Photoshop.

Part of #217 (scorecard UI-217-4, docs/gaps.md G9; prefs audit field `general.animated_zoom`).

## What's missing on main
`general.animated_zoom` (`crates/engine/src/prefs.rs:220`, default `true`) is unread. The Zoom tool steps once per click or zooms by dragging (Scrubby Zoom, `crates/ui-egui/src/zoom_tool.rs`); pressing and holding without moving does nothing more.

## Photoshop's behaviour
- With **Animated Zoom** on, pressing and holding the mouse button with the Zoom tool zooms continuously (in, or out with Alt/Option) until you release.
- With it off, a click steps the zoom.
- **Scrubby Zoom** is a separate Zoom tool option: dragging zooms whatever Animated Zoom says (Adobe Community staff answer).

Sources: Adobe Community "Photoshop animated zoom", online-tech-tips "How to Zoom (In and Out) in Photoshop". The hold rate and anchor will be checked in Photoshop before implementation.

## Proposal
- Zoom tool: a press held still past a short delay zooms continuously around the press point while the button is down (Alt: out), within the `zoom_levels` range; release ends it. Pref off: no hold zoom.
- Scrubby Zoom drags unchanged.
- Tests (UI harness): hold zooms in, Alt+hold zooms out, pref off → only the click step, a drag still scrubs.
- Flip the prefs audit (`cargo xtask scorecard`).

title: Tool options are lost when PhotoCraft quits (UI-217-1)
author: davidmann4
body:
**TL;DR:** Tool options (and each painting tool's brush) are lost when PhotoCraft quits; Photoshop keeps them across launches until you choose Reset All Tools.

Part of #217 (scorecard UI-217-1, docs/gaps.md G9).

## What's missing on main
Tool options live in `UiState.tool_options` (`crates/ui-egui/src/state.rs:510`, `:1250`) and the per-tool brushes in `UiState.tool_brushes` (`state.rs:1149`, synced by `paint_mouse.rs` `sync_tool_brush`). Both are serde types, but nothing saves them, so every launch starts from the defaults. (Fill and Liquify already keep their dialog settings in Preferences.)

## Photoshop's behaviour
Each tool's options-bar settings (brush size and hardness, opacity, flow, mode, tolerance, feather, sample size and so on) are kept between sessions. That is what **Reset Tool** / **Reset All Tools** (right-click the tool icon in the options bar) is for: it returns them to the defaults. Sources: howtogeek "How to Reset Photoshop's Tools Back to Their Defaults", photoshopessentials "How to Reset the Tools and Toolbar".

## Proposal
- Save `tool_options` and `tool_brushes` with the other persisted UI state (at quit, and debounced when they change), restore them at launch. Unknown or old fields fall back to defaults (`#[serde(default)]`); a corrupt store is ignored with a warning, never a panic.
- Reset Tool / Reset All Tools also reset the saved state.
- Scope: tool options only. The Export As / Save for Web / font-recents parts of UI-217-1 are separate (#5838, #3559).
- Tests: round trip of changed options through the store; a missing or corrupt store gives defaults; Reset All Tools clears it.
- Update the UI-217-1 evidence in `scorecard/*.toml`.

title: Preferences: Column Size does nothing, no Columns unit in Image Size (UI-217-4)
author: davidmann4
body:
**TL;DR:** Preferences › Units & Rulers › Column Size (Width, Gutter) does nothing: Image Size should offer a "Columns" width unit that uses it, as in Photoshop.

Part of #217 (scorecard UI-217-4, docs/gaps.md G9; prefs audit fields `units_and_rulers.column_width`, `units_and_rulers.gutter`).

## What's missing on main
`units_and_rulers.column_width` (`crates/engine/src/prefs.rs:670`, default 180) is unread. The size dialogs offer Pixels, Percent, Inches, Centimeters, Millimeters, Points and Picas (`crates/ui-egui/src/sizing.rs:14`), with no Columns unit. (#3549 reads `gutter` for New Guide Layout; this issue is about the Columns unit.)

## Photoshop's behaviour
- Units & Rulers › Column Size sets a column Width and a Gutter (the space between columns), meant for matching a page-layout column.
- Image Size can size the width in **Columns**, an arbitrary unit defined by that preference. Sources: Photoshop Elements help ("Image Size and Canvas Size commands also use this setting"), Teesside University guide "Adobe Photoshop: Resizing an Image".
- The exact conversion (expected: *n* columns = *n* × width + (*n* − 1) × gutter) and which dialogs (Image Size, Canvas Size, New Document) offer Columns will be checked in Photoshop before implementation; the measured values will be added here.

## Proposal
- A Columns width unit in the dialogs Photoshop offers it in, converting through the Column Size preference at the document's resolution; height doesn't get it.
- The engine commands keep taking pixels/physical units; the conversion is in the dialog, so recorded actions stay independent of the preference.
- Tests: conversion both ways for a few column counts; a zero, negative or NaN preference doesn't panic.
- Flip the prefs audit (`cargo xtask scorecard`).

title: Color Overlay with Soft Light renders too bright on a Normal layer with Fill 0%
author: sageford
body:
## Description

A Color Overlay layer style set to **Soft Light** renders significantly brighter in PhotoCraft than in Photoshop when the layer itself uses **Normal** blending and **Fill 0%**.

This is reproducible with a simple two-layer PSD: a solid dark green background and a transparent gradient layer with a yellow Color Overlay.

## Environment

- PhotoCraft: **0.9.0**
- Reference application: **Adobe Photoshop 2025, version 26.5**
- OS: **Windows 11 Pro Insider Preview, build 29683, x64**
- Document size: **940 × 572 px**
- Layer count: **2 pixel layers**

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create a **940 × 572 px** RGB document in Photoshop.
2. Create a bottom pixel layer named `Layer 1` and fill it with **`#04170F`**.
3. Create a pixel layer named `Layer 2` above it.
4. On `Layer 2`, draw a vertical gradient that fades from opaque at the top to transparent below, covering approximately the top **174 px** of the canvas.
5. Set `Layer 2` to:
   - Layer blend mode: **Normal**
   - Layer opacity: **100%**
   - Fill: **0%**
6. Enable **Layer Style → Color Overlay**:
   - Blend mode: **Soft Light**
   - Color: **light yellow**
   - Effect opacity: **100%**
7. Leave the other advanced blending settings at their defaults.
8. Save the document as PSD and open the **same file** in PhotoCraft.
9. Compare the rendered results.

The Soft Light setting is inside **Color Overlay**, not the layer’s own blend mode.

## Expected behavior

The yellow Color Overlay should blend with the underlying `#04170F` background using Soft Light, following the upper layer’s opacity gradient.

The result should match Photoshop: a relatively dark green highlight fading into the background.

## Actual behavior

PhotoCraft produces a bright yellow band fading into the background. Photoshop produces a much darker green result from the same PSD.

PhotoCraft’s output appears consistent with the yellow overlay being composited normally over the background instead of being blended against it using Soft Lig…

title: Linux/Flatpak on GNOME Wayland: mouse pointer invisible over the window (no cursor theme in the sandbox)
author: L-Caetano
body:
### Description

On GNOME 46 (Wayland), the mouse pointer turns invisible whenever it is over the PhotoCraft window when PhotoCraft is installed as a Flatpak. It looks random because it only happens while the pointer is over the app.

### Environment

- Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS, GNOME Shell 46.0 (mutter 46.2), Wayland session
- Intel Iris Xe (TigerLake-LP GT2)
- `ai.storyteller.photocraft` 0.9.0 (Flatpak, user install); the ArtCraft Launcher Flatpak (`ai.storyteller.artcraft-launcher` 0.3.2) shows the same thing
- Host cursor theme: Yaru

### Cause

The user journal fills with winit warnings while the pointer is over the window:

```
WARN  winit::platform_impl::linux::wayland::window::state] Failed to set cursor to Default
WARN  winit::platform_impl::linux::wayland::window::state] Failed to set cursor to Pointer
```

When the compositor doesn't offer the cursor-shape protocol (GNOME 46 doesn't), winit loads the Xcursor theme itself and draws the cursor. Inside the sandbox it finds none:

```
$ flatpak run --command=sh ai.storyteller.photocraft -c 'echo "XCURSOR_PATH=$XCURSOR_PATH"; ls /usr/share/icons'
XCURSOR_PATH=
hicolor
```

The host's themes are mounted at `/run/host/share/icons` (e.g. `/run/host/share/icons/Yaru/cursors`), but nothing points winit there. Theme loading fails and no cursor is drawn.

### Workaround

```
flatpak override --user --env=XCURSOR_PATH=/run/host/share/icons --env=XCURSOR_THEME=Yaru ai.storyteller.photocraft
```

(Replace `Yaru` with your theme, or leave out `XCURSOR_THEME` to use the host's `default` theme.) Undo with `flatpak override --user --reset ai.storyteller.photocraft`.

### Proposed fix

Add `--env=XCURSOR_PATH=/run/host/user-share/icons:/run/host/share/icons` to `finish-args` in both `packaging/linux/flatpak/ai.storyteller.photocraft.yml` and `ai.storyteller.photocraft.bundle.yml`. PR to follow. The ArtCraft Launcher manifest probably needs the same line.

Possibly related: #4190 (cursor vanishes on Zorin OS 18.1, a GNOME-based dis…

title: Hue Curves adjustment layer (Hue vs Hue / Saturation / Luminance) on the canvas, outside Camera Raw
author: switch87
body:
**I'm working on this.**

## Wish

Hue-based curves (Hue vs Hue, Hue vs Saturation, Hue vs Luminance) as an adjustment / adjustment layer on the normal canvas, not only inside Camera Raw. Lightroom and Camera Raw have them as *Point Color* / the HSL mixer, DaVinci Resolve as its *Hue vs Hue / Hue vs Sat / Hue vs Lum* curves. In Photoshop users have to round-trip through the Camera Raw filter for this.

Evidence: the top comment (76 points) in the r/photoshop thread "What feature do you wish Photoshop had?" asks for exactly these curves outside Camera Raw: https://redd.it/pxgz9z

## Plan (medium scope)

- One new adjustment **Hue Curves** (Image › Adjustments and Layer › New Adjustment Layer), with three curves over hue:
  - hue → hue shift (degrees),
  - hue → saturation factor,
  - hue → luminance shift.
- Curves are periodic over 360° (the curve wraps around red at 0°/360°) and interpolate smoothly between points, so colour transitions stay soft.
- Engine command, op, adjustment-layer kind, `.pcraft` save/reopen, undo, MCP/scripting description, Properties panel reusing the existing curves editor.
- PSD: Photoshop has no equivalent adjustment layer, so on PSD export the layer is handled like other PhotoCraft-only adjustment layers (documented in the PR).
- Tests first: red → orange shift leaves blue untouched, saturation down on green, identity is a no-op, periodicity around 0/360°, `.pcraft` round-trip, undo.

title: PSD smart filters Sharpen, Dust & Scratches and Hue/Saturation come in as `psd.unsupportedFilter` and are dropped when the smart object is re-rendered
author: pandapknaepel
body:
## Summary

PSD mockups with these smart filters open fine (the stored composite is shown), but `info` reports the filters as
`psd.unsupportedFilter`. As soon as the smart object is re-rendered (`layer.smartObjects.replaceContents` or
`relinkToFile`), the filters are gone. PhotoCraft already has the matching commands, so only the import mapping seems to
be missing:

| Filter | `filterID` (4CC) | PhotoCraft command |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sharpen | 1399353968 (`Shrp`) | `filter.sharpen.sharpen` |
| Dust & Scratches | 1148417107 (`DstS`) | `filter.noise.dustAndScratches` |
| Hue/Saturation | 1213428850 (`HStr`) | `image.adjustments.hueSaturation` |

This is the same kind of gap as #3673 (Displace).

## Steps to reproduce

PhotoCraft 0.9.0 (c699e3cda, 2026-10-14), macOS 26.6, `photocraft-cli`.

1. A PSD with a smart object that has a Sharpen smart filter.
2. `photocraft-cli info mockup.psd --compact` – the smart object lists

   ```json
   {"command": "psd.unsupportedFilter", "visible": true, "blend": "Normal", "opacity": 1.0,
    "params": {"filterID": 1399353968, "name": "Sharpen", "psd": "00000001000000000008…"}}
   ```

3. `photocraft-cli run mockup.psd --cmd layer.smartObjects.replaceContents --params '{"layer":22,"path":"new.png"}' --cmd file.saveACopy --params '{"path":"out.png","layers":false}'`

**Expected:** the re-rendered smart object is sharpened like before (the filter is part of the smart object).
**Actual:** it is rendered without the filter.

The raw descriptor for Sharpen only holds the filter name and the blend options (`Nm  TEXT "Sharpen"`, `blendOptions`
with `Opct` 100 %, `Md  enum BlnM normal`) – Sharpen has no parameters.

**Impact:** product mockups re-rendered with new artwork look softer than the stored composite; in our mug mockups three
smart objects of one file and the artwork of a second file use Sharpen.

title: PSD import: the Perspective Warp smart filter (`perspectiveWarpTransform`, filterID 708) is `psd.unsupportedFilter` and is lost on re-render
author: pandapknaepel
body:
## Summary

A smart object whose perspective comes from a Perspective Warp smart filter (a poster lying on a table) opens with the
stored composite, but `info` lists the filter as `psd.unsupportedFilter` (filterID 708). After
`layer.smartObjects.replaceContents` the smart object is re-rendered without it: the new artwork stands upright instead
of lying in perspective, and is cut off by the paper mask.

PhotoCraft can already apply the same transform with `layer.smartObjects.perspectiveWarp {planes:[{src, dst}]}`; the
descriptor holds everything needed for it:

- `perspectiveWarpTransform` → `vertices` (VlLs of points, document px) and `warpedVertices` (same count)
- `quads` (VlLs) → each with `indices` (4 × `long` into the vertex lists, clockwise from top-left)

Mapping each quad to `{src: vertices[indices], dst: warpedVertices[indices]}` and creating the filter with
`layer.smartObjects.perspectiveWarp` (then moving it to the original index with `layer.smartFilter.move`) puts the
artwork back in perspective as in the stored composite.

## Steps to reproduce

PhotoCraft 0.9.0 (c699e3cda, 2026-10-14), macOS 26.6.

1. `photocraft-cli info poster.psd --compact` – layer 6: `{"command":"psd.unsupportedFilter","params":{"filterID":708,…}}`
2. `photocraft-cli run poster.psd --cmd layer.smartObjects.replaceContents --params '{"layer":6,"path":"new.png"}' --cmd file.saveACopy --params '{"path":"out.jpg","layers":false}'`

**Expected:** the new contents are warped by the filter, as in the stored composite.
**Actual:** the filter is dropped; the contents are drawn flat.

**Impact:** every mockup that uses this filter needs our own re-creation; without it the product image is wrong.

title: [Bug Report] [PhotoCraft] PhotoCraft Bugs
author: ticket-craft
body:
### Description

Hey! I'd like to report a few issues and suggest some improvements for PhotoCraft:

- **Large File Stability:** When importing or working with large files (around 1.5 GB or more), PhotoCraft can become extremely unstable and crash frequently, even on powerful hardware. Improving stability and memory management when handling large projects would make a huge difference.

- **Camera Raw Filter:** The current Camera Raw Filter feels limited compared to Photoshop. Adding more advanced adjustment tools and providing a more complete, professional editing experience would be a great improvement.

- **Selection Tools & Background Removal:** The selection tools, especially Select Subject and background removal, don't seem as accurate or refined as Photoshop's. Improving edge detection, handling fine details like hair, and overall selection precision would make the workflow much better for professional designers.

- **Layers Panel Auto-Scrolling:** When dragging a layer from the bottom of the Layers panel toward the top, scrolling feels too slow. It would be great to have dynamic auto-scrolling that gradually speeds up the longer the cursor stays near the panel's edges, making it easier to navigate and rearrange layers in large projects.

- **PSD File Compatibility:** I once opened a large PSD file in PhotoCraft successfully, although the application was lagging while handling it. However, when I tried opening the same file in Photoshop, it refused to open and displayed a message saying that the file was created or saved using a different PSD version than the one supported by my current version of Photoshop. It would be worth investigating PSD compatibility and how different applications handle files saved in different PSD formats or versions.

I believe addressing these issues would significantly improve PhotoCraft's stability, compatibility, and overall experience for professional designers.

Thanks for your hard work and for continuing to improve PhotoCraft…

title: Torn-off document views remain duplicated and lose canvas tool input
author: mostyk
body:
## Description
Detaching a document tab into a floating window can leave the same document visible in the main window, and canvas input may not reach the focused floating viewport.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Open at least two documents.
2. Drag one document tab outside the tab strip to detach it into a floating OS window.
3. Check whether it remains visible in the main tab strip or canvas.
4. Focus the floating window and use a canvas tool.
5. Try Window > Arrange > Float All in Windows.

## Expected behavior
The torn-off document is shown only in its floating window, remains active there, and receives canvas input through the focused viewport. Other docked documents stay available in the main canvas and tab strip. Float All creates floating document windows.

Related: PR #5744; original floating-window feature request #3733.

`crates/io/src/smart_map.rs` maps Gaussian Blur, Box Blur, Motion Blur, Unsharp Mask, Add Noise, Median, High Pass, Maximum, Minimum, Mosaic, Emboss, Levels, Curves, the Filter Gallery and a Camera Raw subset. title: Actions: Smart Blur quality is read and written as Hgh/Mdm/Low, codes Photoshop ignores
author: davidmann4
body:
**TL;DR:** A recorded or exported Smart Blur step stores its quality as `Hgh `/`Mdm `/`Low `. Photoshop doesn't understand those codes, so the step plays back with its fallback quality, and Photoshop's own `.atn` files (`SBQH`/`SBQM`/`SBQL`) don't map back to a quality in PhotoCraft.

## Where
`crates/engine/src/atn_cmds.rs:918`:
```rust
const SMART_BLUR_QUALITY: &[(&str, &str)] = &[("Hgh ", "high"), ("Mdm ", "medium"), ("Low ", "low")];
```
used by the `SmrB` event (`F("SmBQ", "quality", Kind::Enum("SmBQ", SMART_BLUR_QUALITY))`). The mode table next to it already uses Photoshop's `SBMN`/`SBME`/`SBMO`.

## Photoshop's behaviour (measured)
Measured in Photoshop by rendering: Smart Blur (radius 6, threshold 60, mode Normal) was applied through Action Manager to the same test image with each quality code, and the pixels were compared.
- `SBQH` and `SBQM` each give a distinct result.
- `Hgh `, `Mdm `, `Low ` and a nonsense code `Xxxx` all give the **identical** image (same hash), i.e. Photoshop ignores them and uses its fallback. `SBQL` gives that same image (low is the fallback).
- The smart filter Photoshop saves for this filter uses enum type `SmBQ` with values `SBQL`/`SBQM`/`SBQH` (see #6298).

## Proposal
- Change the table to `SBQL`/`SBQM`/`SBQH` for writing. On reading, accept both Photoshop's codes and the old `Hgh `/`Mdm `/`Low ` (actions PhotoCraft wrote before this fix), so nothing that loads today stops loading.
- Tests: an `.atn` round trip of every quality writes `SBQ*`; a Photoshop-shaped `SmrB` descriptor with each `SBQ*` reads as the right quality; the legacy codes still read; unknown codes → the existing unknown-value handling, no panic.
- Check the other enum tables in `atn_cmds.rs` against the codes measured for the smart-filter work (#6296–#6305) and report any other mismatch.

body:

## What's missing on main
`crates/io/src/smart_map.rs` has no entry for `filter.pixelate.mezzotint` or `filter.pixelate.colorHalftone`; the engine has both with matching options.

## Photoshop's behaviour (measured)

- **Mezzotint**: filterID `Mztn` 1299870830, class `Mztn`. `MztT` enum `MztT`: `FnDt` Fine Dots, `MdmD` Medium Dots, `GrnD` Grainy Dots, `CrsD` Coarse Dots, `ShrL` Short Lines, `MdmL` Medium Lines, `LngL` Long Lines, `ShSt` Short Strokes, `MdmS` Medium Strokes, `LngS` Long Strokes. title: Actions: Box Blur, Surface Blur, Flatten Image and Black & White steps export event codes Photoshop can't run
author: davidmann4
body:
**TL;DR:** Box Blur, Surface Blur, Flatten Image and Black & White steps exported to `.atn` use event codes Photoshop doesn't run (`BoxB`, `SrfB`, `Fltn`, `BlnW`), so these steps fail with "command not available" when the action plays in Photoshop.

## Where
`crates/engine/src/atn_cmds.rs`: the `ev!` entries for these events have a four-char `code`. Export writes `AtnEvent::Code(code)` whenever the code is non-empty (around `let event = if e.code.is_empty() { AtnEvent::Name(..) } else { AtnEvent::Code(..) }`).

| PhotoCraft command | code written | name in the table |
|---|---|---|
| `filter.blur.boxBlur` | `BoxB` | `boxblur` |
| `filter.blur.surfaceBlur` | `SrfB` | `surfaceBlur` |
| flatten image | `Fltn` | `flattenImage` |
| black & white | `BlnW` | `blackAndWhite` |

## Photoshop's behaviour (measured)
Measured in Photoshop. Each event was run with `executeAction` on a document with a filled pixel layer:
- `BoxB`, `SrfB`, `Fltn` and `BlnW` fail: "General Photoshop error … the command is not currently available".
- `boxblur`, `surfaceBlur`, `blackAndWhite` and `flattenImage` run. The charID `FltI` also flattens.
- `typeIDToStringID(charIDToTypeID(code))` is empty for `BoxB`, `SrfB` and `BlnW`. For `Fltn` it is `flatness`, a property, not the flatten event.
- For comparison, `BlrM` (Blur More) and the other codes in the table do run or resolve to the expected event.

Not checked by running them, because they open dialogs: `GEfc` (Filter Gallery) and `GdMp` (Gradient Map).

## Proposal
- Export these four events under an id Photoshop runs: the name, or the `FltI` code for Flatten Image.
- On import, keep accepting the old codes, so actions PhotoCraft wrote before still load.
- Tests: an export of each step writes the new id; a Photoshop-shaped step with the name (and `FltI`) imports to the right command; the legacy codes still import; unknown ids don't panic.

title: [Bug Report] Help › Search: ← / → switch menus and Space runs a result while typing in the field
author: Higgs32584
body:
Follow-up to #5996 (letters typed into Help › Search ran Help rows by mnemonic; fixed in #6030). The same thing happens with the keys that edit the field, which #6030 doesn't cover:

## Steps to reproduce
1. Click **Help**.
2. Type `levls` in the search field.
3. Press **←** to move the cursor back and fix the typo.

**Expected:** the cursor moves inside the field.
**Actual:** Help closes and **Window** opens. **→** opens **File** instead.

Space has the same problem: with a result lit (the pointer resting on it, or after **↓**), typing a space in the query runs that result.

## Cause
`menu_nav::Nav::keys` handles the open menu's keys after the menu is drawn. It treats ← / → as "switch to the neighbouring menu" and Space as "run the lit row", even while the Help search field has the keyboard. The text field has already moved its cursor or typed the space that frame, and then the menu acts on the same key as well.

## Fix
While a text field in the menu has the keyboard (`ctx.text_edit_focused()`), `Nav::keys` leaves ← / → / Space to it. ↑ / ↓, ↩ and Esc behave as before, so you can still move from the field into the results and run one.

title: Move tool: dragging a large floating selection lags far behind the cursor
author: robertoffmoura
body: ### What happens On a large image, dragging a selection with the Move tool is very laggy: the selected pixels trail well behind the cursor and move in visible jumps. The first press also takes about a second before anything moves. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Open a large photo, e.g. 6016×6016 (36 MP), 8-bit RGB, a single `Background` layer. 2. Rectangular Marquee (M): select about 1/5 of the image (~2700×2700 px, ~7 MP). 3. Move tool (V): drag the selection around. **Expected:** the selection follows the cursor smoothly. **Actual:** about 1 s delay on press, then about 3–4 updates per second while dragging. The first small movements also snap back to the starting position. ### Environment - OS: macOS 14.8.9, Macbook pro 15-inch, 2018 / 2.9 GHz 6-Core Intel Core i9, 32 GB 2400 MHz DDR4 - PhotoCraft: c11ef015 - Document: 6016×6016, 8-bit RGB, 1 layer ### Measurements Release build, instrumented, same document and selection (measured on Linux): | | per event | |---|---:| | Press (cut the selection into a floating piece) | ~1036 ms | | Each drag frame (floating preview) | ~275 ms avg, up to 594 ms | | Drop (`select.drop`) | ~281 ms | ### Cause Cutting the selection and redrawing it each frame copy the whole selected region into flat float buffers on a single thread: about 116 MB per copy, about 230 MB per drag frame. Smaller contributors: - a preview composite is built before the pointer has moved; - the piece snaps to its own starting outline; - the Navigator falls back to a full CPU thumbnail on the first drag frame. ### Fix #6318 makes these operations tile-based and parallel, sharing unchanged tiles instead of copying them. With it, the press takes ~86 ms and each drag frame ~12 ms. Related: #209 (interactive performance targets), #1425 (initial pause when dragging a layer with the Move tool)

title: fix(linux): avoid duplicate AppImage desktop launcher when managed by AM / AppMan
author: Korg1ch
body:
﻿### Problem
When PhotoCraft is installed or managed via the ["AM" / AppMan package manager](https://github.com/ivan-hc/AM), AM manages application launchers using a -AM.desktop suffix (e.g. photocraft-AM.desktop in /usr/local/share/applications or $XDG_DATA_HOME/applications) and symlinks the binary into $PATH (e.g. /usr/local/bin/photocraft).

Because packaging/linux/AppRun's external integrator detection currently only checks whether $appimage matches the raw Exec= line of .desktop files in $XDG_DATA_HOME/applications, it does not detect the existing AM launcher. As reported by @ivan-hc in #3641, this causes PhotoCraft's best-effort integration to write a second launcher alongside photocraft-AM.desktop.

### Expected behavior
- packaging/linux/AppRun should recognize existing AM / AppMan launchers (*-AM.desktop matching photocraft or i.storyteller.photocraft) in $XDG_DATA_HOME/applications, /usr/local/share/applications, or /usr/share/applications (or when m/ppman is present).
- When an AM launcher is detected, AppRun should skip writing a duplicate .desktop entry while continuing to ensure hicolor icons are installed.
