title: CI: merge through a merge queue, so PRs merge only after CI passes on the latest main
author: davidmann4
body:
**TL;DR:** merge PRs through a GitHub merge queue, so whoever merges clicks once and moves on, and GitHub merges each PR only after CI passes on top of the latest main.

## Problem

- `main` has no protection (the only ruleset is `release branch`), so nothing stops a PR with red or still-running CI from merging.
- Waiting for CI by hand doesn't scale: a PR run takes about 50–70 minutes plus the runner queue (45 PR runs were queued at once on 2026-10-15), and there are hundreds of open PRs.
- A PR's green run was against the main of when it ran. Two PRs that are green on their own can still break main together.

## Proposal

Turn on GitHub's [merge queue](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/configuring-pull-request-merges/managing-a-merge-queue) for `main`. A queued PR is tested on top of main plus the PRs queued ahead of it, and merges only when that run is green.

Workflow side (a PR can do this):
1. `merge_group:` trigger in `ci.yml`. Without it a queued PR waits forever.
2. One always-reporting `ci passed` check to require, as #5118 describes. `test (windows-latest)` and the web build run only for some paths, and a required check that never starts blocks the PR.
3. Merge groups pick platforms by changed paths like PRs do, since the queue starts one CI run per queued PR.

Maintainer side (repo settings): a ruleset on `main` that requires `ci passed` and the merge queue. The PR lists the exact settings.

Related: #5118 (require CI before merging), #5543 (runner queue).

title: DX12: building the GPU compositor costs ~8 s on every launch with FXC (1.6 s with DXC, 0.05 s on Vulkan)
author: 00xJS
body:
## What happens

`Compositor::try_new_with_format` builds every pipeline up front (`crates/gpu/src/lib.rs`, `new_with_format`). On DX12, wgpu compiles each one with FXC, which is the default unless a `dxcompiler.dll` sits beside the exe (`gpu_startup.rs` `dx12_compiler`, #712). FXC's output isn't cached between launches, so every DX12 launch pays the full compile again.

The canvas creates the compositor lazily on its first GPU composite, while holding the egui renderer's write lock (`gpu_canvas.rs`, around line 415). So I'd expect this to show up as a freeze when the first document opens. I haven't measured that in the app yet.

## Measured

Setup: Ryzen 5 2600X, Radeon RX 6900 XT, Windows 11, main `2b3d0563` (the gpu crate is unchanged on the current main, `3cb3580a`). A release-build probe creates a fresh device and calls `Compositor::try_new_with_format(Rgba32Float)`, three rounds per configuration:

| | First run | Later runs |
|---|---|---|
| Vulkan | 3.59 s | **0.05 s** (driver shader cache) |
| DX12 + FXC (what ships) | 13.8 s | **8.1–8.7 s** |
| DX12 + DXC (Windows SDK `Redist/D3D/x64/dxcompiler.dll`) | 4.4 s | **1.6–1.7 s** |

A second compositor on the same device costs about 0.06 s on every backend.

The test suite shows the same pattern:
- `photocraft-gpu`'s tests take 554 s on DX12 against 134 s on Vulkan.
- The 64×48 `first_frame_renders` parity test takes about 8 s against about 1 s.

## Who's affected

Windows users on DX12:
- Intel GPUs, where DX12 is the `auto` default;
- anyone whose Vulkan start failed and fell back;
- anyone who switched to DX12 by hand (it was suggested in #2308).

## Options

These are for the maintainers to choose between:

1. **Ship `dxcompiler.dll` beside `photocraft.exe`** in the Windows packages. `dx12_compiler` already loads it by full path, so #712 stays fixed. This needs the DXC release's license added to ATTRIBUTION/NOTICE, and possibly `dxil.dll` too. Measured above: about 5× faster.

title: Affinity import: a self-referencing or shared compound shape aborts with a stack overflow or hangs exponentially
author: Dromares
body:
## Summary

`crates/affinity/src/geometry.rs` `outline()` recurses into every operand of a `Comp` (compound shape) object's `Chld` list with **no depth limit and no visited set**. The tree walk in `model.rs::node` does guard against cycles (`self.active`, `MAX_TREE_DEPTH`), but it does not descend into a `Comp`'s children itself; it hands the compound to `geometry::outline` (`model.rs:459`), which has neither guard. The stream parser lets a shared object reference itself (`stream.rs::shared` registers the key before parsing its fields) and lets many children reference one shared object.

That gives two failures from tiny files:

title: Automation: an uppercase control token is accepted at startup but every client sending it is rejected
author: Dromares
body:
## Summary

`validate_token` accepts uppercase hex, and `server_token` stores the token lowercased (`crates/automation/src/security.rs:166-167` for `--control-token`, `:174` for a token file). But `authentication_reply` (`:108-116`) passes the client's token to `token_matches` (`:100-105`) unchanged, and `token_matches` compares bytes exactly. So a client that sends the token exactly as it was configured is refused. Only the bundled bridge client works, because it lowercases (`bridge.rs:57`).

## Repro

```sh
photocraft-cli serve --port 47391 --control-token 0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF
# (any valid-length uppercase token)
```

Then send the `auth` method with that same token:

- uppercase → `{"error":"authentication required","ok":false}`
- the same token lowercased → `{"ok":true,"result":{"authenticated":true}}`

Same with `--control-token-file` holding uppercase hex: a unit test of `server_token` + `authentication_reply` gives `ok=false` for the file's exact contents.

## Suggested fix

Lowercase (or compare case-insensitively, still in constant time) the supplied token in `authentication_reply`, or reject uppercase in `validate_token` so the mismatch can't happen.

## Duplicate check

None found (token uppercase / case / lowercase / hexadecimal token, open + closed).

Found on PhotoCraft 0.9.0 (c699e3cda, Arch `photocraft-bin`, CachyOS / KDE Plasma Wayland) and confirmed against source at `main` 3cb3580a4.

title: Automation roots: absolute request paths are refused when the root was given through a symlink, `..` or a relative path
author: Dromares
body:
## Summary

The root is stored with `std::path::absolute` (no symlink or `..` resolution; `crates/automation/src/workspace.rs:146-147`), and `request_path` (`:157-171`) compares absolute request paths against it component by component, as text. So the real location of a file inside the root is refused, while the odd spelling of the same path is accepted. It fails closed (not an escape), but it breaks absolute paths for anyone whose root is spelled through a link: macOS `/tmp` → `/private/tmp`, a symlinked home or project dir, or a relative root containing `..`.

## Repro (installed `photocraft-cli` 0.9.0 and a unit test)

| Root given as | Request | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `rootlink` (symlink → `root`) | save to `/…/root/x.png` | `absolute paths must be inside the automation root` |
| | save to `/…/rootlink/y.png` | ok |
| `/…/root/../root` | `/…/root/z.png` | refused |
| | `/…/root/../root/w.png` | ok |
| `../out` | `/…/out/rel.png` | refused |

## Suggested fix

Store the canonicalised root (`std::fs::canonicalize` once, at startup) and canonicalise the request's parent directory before comparing (or compare against both spellings). The capability handle still does the opening, so this doesn't weaken containment. #2176 asked for exactly this ("absolute paths that resolve inside the roots"), but what shipped compares text only.

## Duplicate check

#2176 (closed) added absolute-path support. #2319 shows the same error message, but for repeated roots. Nothing covers this.

Found on PhotoCraft 0.9.0 (c699e3cda, Arch `photocraft-bin`, CachyOS / KDE Plasma Wayland) and confirmed against source at `main` 3cb3580a4.

title: `photocraft --control 0` logs `listening on 127.0.0.1:0` instead of the port actually bound
author: Dromares
body:
## Summary

Port 0 is accepted on purpose (see the test near `apps/photocraft/src/main.rs:163`), but `control_server::start` prints the *requested* port (`apps/photocraft/src/control_server.rs:28`) instead of `listener.local_addr()`. With `--control 0` the OS picks a free port, and nothing tells the client which one. `photocraft-cli serve` already prints the bound address (`rpc.rs`).

## Repro

```sh
photocraft --control 0 --control-token-file /tmp/tok   # isolated HOME
```

- stderr: `photocraft: control server listening on 127.0.0.1:0`
- `ss -ltnp` shows the process actually listening on e.g. `127.0.0.1:44967`

## Fix

Log `listener.local_addr()` (and ideally put it somewhere machine-readable, e.g. next to the token file).

## Duplicate check

Searched control 0 port / ephemeral port / bound port: only #701, a different bug.

Found on PhotoCraft 0.9.0 (c699e3cda, Arch `photocraft-bin`, CachyOS / KDE Plasma Wayland) and confirmed against source at `main` 3cb3580a4.

title: Desktop `--control <port>`: a bind failure is only printed; the app keeps running and exits 0 without a control server
author: Dromares
body:
## Summary

When `TcpListener::bind` fails, `control_server::start` prints the error and returns an empty receiver (`apps/photocraft/src/control_server.rs:21-26`). The GUI keeps running without a control server and the eventual exit status is 0. That's the same silent failure #701 and #1816 fixed for an unparseable port and for bad auth setup (both now exit 2), but the bind path was left out. A supervisor or agent that launched the app to drive it has no way to know it can't connect.

## Repro

1. Hold a port: `python3 -c 'import socket,time;s=socket.socket();s.bind(("127.0.0.1",39937));s.listen();time.sleep(60)' &`
2. Launch: `photocraft --control 39937 --control-token-file /tmp/tok` (isolated HOME).
3. stderr: `photocraft: control server failed to bind 127.0.0.1:39937: Address already in use (os error 98)`, and the process is still running 8 s later.

## Suggested fix

Bind before the window opens (as the parse and token checks already do) and exit with status 2 on failure.

## Duplicate check

#701's body mentions this in passing ("it too returns an `Ok` exit later"), but #701 and #1816 are closed and fixed only the parse and auth paths. Nothing open tracks it.

Found on PhotoCraft 0.9.0 (c699e3cda, Arch `photocraft-bin`, CachyOS / KDE Plasma Wayland) and confirmed against source at `main` 3cb3580a4.

title: Desktop: `--control-token` / `--control-token-file` (and `--automation-*-root`) with no value are silently ignored
author: Dromares
body:
## Summary

In `apps/photocraft/src/main.rs`, a missing value for `--control-token` becomes `None` (`:216`), and `--control-token-file`, `--automation-read-root` and `--automation-write-root` use `args.next().map(..)` (`:218-220`), which is also `None` when the value is missing. Instead of a usage error, the app starts with a freshly generated random token. `photocraft-cli` rejects the same input (`--control-token needs a value`), and the desktop app already exits 2 for a missing `--control` port.

## Repro

```sh
photocraft --control 0 --control-token
photocraft --control 0 --control-token-file
```

Both start the GUI and print `photocraft: control token: <random hex>`, so the caller's intended token or file is silently not used.

Not run, but the same code path: `--automation-read-root` with no value would overwrite a root set through `PHOTOCRAFT_AUTOMATION_READ_ROOT` with `None`.

## Suggested fix

Push a `control_arg_errors` entry ("missing value") for each of these flags, as `--control` does.

## Duplicate check

None found.

Found on PhotoCraft 0.9.0 (c699e3cda, Arch `photocraft-bin`, CachyOS / KDE Plasma Wayland) and confirmed against source at `main` 3cb3580a4.

title: Free Transform / Transform Selection with a huge scale takes 5–7 s instead of being refused (the #3773 budget is bypassed by bounds clamping)
author: Dromares
body:
## Summary

`relative_matrix` (`crates/engine/src/transform_cmds.rs:533-554`) checks that the scale is finite but sets no upper limit. `corner_bounds` (`crates/algo/src/transform.rs:244-254`) then **clamps** the transformed bounds to ±2²⁰ px instead of reporting them as too large, so the result size checked against `MAX_TRANSFORM_PIXELS = 1<<30` (`transform_cmds.rs:265`) is the clamped strip (~3M px wide × the layer height), which passes. The warp then fills that whole strip.

#3773 ("A scale past it is refused rather than clipped") intended huge scales to be refused, but clamping first defeats that check.

## Repro

24×16 document, a layer with content (e.g. after `filter.render.clouds`), and a selection:

| Command | Time | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `edit.transform {"scaleX":1e308}` | 6.9 s | Ok |
| `edit.transform {"scaleX":1e9}` | 5.5 s | Ok |
| `select.transformSelection {"scaleX":1e30}` (or `scaleY` 1e308) | 5.5 s | Ok, selection bounds `[-1048577,1,2097154,5]` |
| `edit.transform {"scaleX":1e6}` | 0.2 s | Ok |

No panic; it's an unbounded stall on the UI or command thread. `panic_hunt` misses it because it has no content layer and no large scale values.

## Suggested fix

Have `corner_bounds` return `None` / an error when a corner is outside ±2²⁰ instead of clamping (or check the unclamped size against the budget), so huge scales are refused as #3773 intended.

## Duplicate check

Searched transform scale huge / hang / slow, edit.transform scaleX, Transform Selection scale. Related only: #3773 (closed).

Found on PhotoCraft 0.9.0 (c699e3cda, Arch `photocraft-bin`, CachyOS / KDE Plasma Wayland) and confirmed against source at `main` 3cb3580a4.

title: `photocraft --help` (and any unknown flag) launches the GUI and tries to open the flag as a file
author: Dromares
body:
## Summary

The desktop binary's argument loop (`apps/photocraft/src/main.rs:203-243`) only handles `--version` and the control/GPU flags; everything else falls into `Some(s) => files.push(s.to_owned())` (`:241`). So `photocraft --help`, `-h` or a typo such as `--safegpu` opens the full GUI and logs:

```
WARN  [main] photocraft_ui_egui::file_open: Couldn't open --help: /current/dir/--help: No such file or directory (os error 2)
```

`photocraft --version` works and exits. #423 fixed the same thing for `photocraft-cli`, but not for the desktop binary.

## Repro

```sh
timeout 10 photocraft --help </dev/null; echo $?   # 124: the GUI opened instead of printing usage
```

## Suggested fix

Print usage and exit 0 for `--help` / `-h`. Treat any other argument starting with `-` (except `-psn_`, and anything after a `--` separator) as a usage error, exiting 2 as the bad `--control` port case does.

## Duplicate check

Searched help, --help, flag, argument, usage (open + closed). Only #423 (CLI only, closed).

Found on PhotoCraft 0.9.0 (c699e3cda, Arch `photocraft-bin`, CachyOS / KDE Plasma Wayland) and confirmed against source at `main` 3cb3580a4.

title: Launching a second instance rotates the running instance's log file out from under it
author: Dromares
body:
## Summary

`logging::rotate` (`apps/photocraft/src/logging.rs:121-132`) runs on every start and renames `photocraft.log` → `.1.log` → `.2.log` (`KEEP = 2`) without checking whether another instance is still writing to `photocraft.log`. The running instance keeps its open file handle, so after a second launch its live log is suddenly `photocraft.1.log`; after a third, `.2.log`; and one more launch deletes it. This is exactly the file the module docs say a bug report should attach ("so the log of a run that crashed survives the next launch"), and it's lost in the common case of a long-running session plus a quick second launch, e.g. opening a file from the file manager.

## Observed

Session started at 20:52 (PID 188042). After two short extra launches:

```
photocraft.2.log   starts 2026-10-16T00:52:36Z   <- still the live log of PID 188042
photocraft.1.log   starts 01:47:39Z               (second launch)
photocraft.log     starts 01:50:49Z               (third launch)
$ ls -l /proc/188042/fd | grep log
3 -> ~/.config/photocraft/logs/photocraft.2.log
```

One more launch and the running session's log is deleted.

## Suggested fix

Either take an advisory lock (`flock`) on `photocraft.log` and skip rotation, writing to `photocraft-<pid>.log`, when it's held; or name logs per process/start time and prune the oldest by age.

## Duplicate check

Searched log, logs, rotate, log file, second instance (open + closed): nothing.

Found on PhotoCraft 0.9.0 (c699e3cda, Arch `photocraft-bin`, CachyOS / KDE Plasma Wayland) and confirmed against source at `main` 3cb3580a4.

title: Holding Ctrl while using the Hand tool does not switch to Zoom
author: estranhosidade
body:
Description

In Photoshop, when using the Hand tool, holding `Ctrl` temporarily switches to the Zoom tool. When the modifier is released, the active tool returns to Hand.

PhotoCraft doesn't appear to support this behavior.

Steps to reproduce

1. Select the Hand tool.
2. Hold `Ctrl`.
3. Try to zoom in or out.

Expected behavior

Holding `Ctrl` while using the Hand tool should temporarily activate Zoom, allowing the user to zoom without manually switching tools. Releasing `Ctrl` should return to the Hand tool.

Actual behavior

Holding `Ctrl` while using the Hand tool does not switch to Zoom.

Why this matters

This is a familiar Photoshop workflow that makes navigating the canvas faster and more fluid. Supporting it would allow users to switch temporarily between panning and zooming without interrupting their workflow.

title: Font size cannot be adjusted by dragging the “T” label
author: estranhosidade
body: In Photoshop, you can adjust certain numeric parameters using scrubby sliders by clicking and dragging their labels, rather than having to click directly on the numeric value. This makes adjusting values much faster and easier. In PhotoCraft, the font-size control appears to require clicking precisely on the number to adjust it. Dragging from the adjacent “T” label does not work. Steps to reproduce 1. Select the Type tool or a text layer. 2. Locate the font-size control. 3. Try clicking and dragging the “T” label next to the font-size value, as you would in Photoshop. 4. Observe that the value does not adjust. Expected behavior Dragging the “T” label should adjust the font size using a scrubby-slider interaction, matching Photoshop's behavior. Actual behavior The interaction appears to work only when clicking directly on the numeric font-size value. Why this matters Requiring precise clicks on a small numeric field makes typography adjustments less convenient. Supporting scrubby sliders on parameter labels would make PhotoCraft's text-editing workflow more consistent with Photoshop and easier to use. At very least, also apply the "scrubby sliders" to T icon, as well as the slider itself

title: Confirmation dialogs do not automatically focus a button for keyboard navigation
author: estranhosidade
body: Description: In Photoshop, when a confirmation dialog appears (for example, asking whether to save changes before closing an image), one of the buttons is automatically focused. This allows you to use the arrow keys to move between options, such as switching from Yes to No or Cancel, without having to click a button first. In PhotoCraft, these dialogs don't appear to automatically focus a button, so keyboard navigation doesn't work as expected. Steps to reproduce 1. Open or edit an image. 2. Trigger a confirmation dialog, such as the prompt to save changes before closing. 3. Press the Right Arrow key to move to another option. Expected behavior A button should receive keyboard focus automatically when the dialog opens. The arrow keys should then allow you to navigate between the available options, and Enter should activate the focused button. Actual behavior No button appears to receive focus automatically, so pressing the arrow keys does not move the selection to another option. Why this matters Automatically focusing dialog buttons makes it possible to handle confirmation prompts entirely from the keyboard, without needing to reach for the mouse. This is particularly useful when repeatedly opening, editing, or closing images. Also it keep consistent with Photoshop default behavior.

title: [Feature Request] macOS: Add Format dropdown (accessoryView) to Save As dialog
author: Rehanprince
body:
### Feature Description
On macOS, when using **File › Save As…** (`Cmd+Shift+S`), the native `NSSavePanel` does not display a **Format / File Type dropdown**. Users currently have to manually type the file extension (e.g. `.png`, `.jpg`, `.psd`) into the filename field. 

Following the recent improvements in **#6151** / **#6121** (which added format-based extension handling on Linux via the XDG Desktop Portal), having a native Format selection on macOS would bring PhotoCraft closer to Photoshop parity.

### Photoshop Reference Behavior
In Adobe Photoshop (and native macOS apps like Preview / Pixelmator):
1. The `NSSavePanel` contains an accessory view at the top/bottom:
   - **Format:** `[PNG ▾]` (Dropdown with PNG, JPEG, PSD, PSB, TIFF, WebP, etc.)
2. Selecting a format from the dropdown automatically updates the extension and configures the appropriate encoder without requiring the user to type the extension manually.

### Current Behavior in PhotoCraft
- On macOS, `rfd::AsyncFileDialog` opens a standard `NSSavePanel` without a type list or format popup (`services.rs`: *"Elsewhere the whole name is kept: the macOS panel has no type list"*).
- If a user wants to save an active document as a PNG, they must explicitly write `image.png` in the name field, otherwise it defaults to `.psd`.

### Proposed Solution / Technical Implementation
- Add an `accessoryView` to `NSSavePanel` on macOS using an `NSPopUpButton` (or equivalent AppKit helper) populated with `SAVE_FILTERS`.
- When the user changes the popup selection:
  1. Update the suggested file extension in the name field (e.g., changing from `.psd` to `.png`).
  2. Return the chosen format alongside the selected path so `PhotocraftApp::save_dialog_flow` can apply the matching encoder options.

### Context / Environment
- **OS:** macOS (Apple Silicon & Intel)
- **Target App Parity:** Adobe Photoshop 2026 Save As behavior
- **Related Commits/Issues:** #6151, #6121, #4394

title: Rendering differences from Photoshop on 40 synthetic adjustment and layer-style cases
author: wojzj57
body:

The mask is a grayscale horizontal 0–255 ramp.

title: Proposal: include large-image release timings in PR descriptions
author: ha1des
body:
AI assistance: Codex · Model: not exposed · Reasoning effort: not exposed · Accountable: @ha1des

For new or changed heavy operations, make the existing large-image release measurements visible to reviewers in the PR description.

## Proposed change

Add a short reminder to the completion checklist in `AGENTS.md`: measure a release build on a 24–36 MP image, before and after where applicable; keep the results in the local dev log and include a short summary in the PR description.

Rule 8 already requires large-image benchmarks and dev-log timings. This proposal makes that requirement easier to find and explicitly asks contributors to share the results with reviewers.

## Why

`log/` is gitignored, so measurements recorded only there do not reach the PR. Maintainers have requested release timings in [#658](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/pull/658#issuecomment-6045970435), [#735](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/pull/735#issuecomment-6045975112), [#2044](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/pull/2044#issuecomment-6089199730) and [#2073](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/pull/2073#issuecomment-6089201215).

## Scope and validation

- Preserve the existing measurement requirement and checks.
- Check that the reminder names release mode, 24–36 MP, before/after where applicable, and a summary accessible in the PR.
- No new benchmark framework, CI gate, mandatory template or memory metric.
- This reporting clarification does not depend on a reading-volume experiment.

Split from #2092 following the request to track the two proposals separately. The implementation is already included in #2174; this ticket adds no implementation scope.

Related but distinct: #2094 / #2920 covers how to report check outcomes and the tested revision; #5380 / #5388 covers shared progress and remaining-work notes more generally.

title: Layers: Alt-click eye to solo and Alt-click again to restore recomposites the whole large document, the previous composite isn't reused
author: theriseandfallofitall
body:
## Summary

On a large layered PSB, Alt-clicking a layer's eye to see it alone and Alt-clicking again to restore takes about 4 s before the full image is back, even with Memory usage raised. The window no longer freezes (#4024 moved the redraw to a worker and shows visible blocks first), but the picture is still rebuilt from scratch: the restore returns to a visibility state the app composited a moment ago, and nothing keeps that result.

Why nothing is reused: when the layers exceed the GPU memory budget, the redraw runs on the CPU compositor in 1024 px blocks (`background_redraw`), which renders from the layers each time and has no cache of earlier composites. A before/after toggle is exactly the case that wants one: the "all visible" canvas texture is overwritten block by block by the solo view and has to be rebuilt on restore.

## Measured

Measured on main @ 2a952f164c0b4cf936b1c6497db10dd095341c00 (Windows 11, 64 GB RAM, RTX 3070 Laptop 8 GB, Alt-click simulated with `layer.showOnly`):

- largetest.psb (GPU budget 3006 MB, fit 2255 MB): solo 0.02 s, restore 97.2 s and 100.7 s of background CPU composite (fit needed 2711 MB), second restore no faster; the control channel is blocked 3.1 s at a time while it runs. Memory Usage 50000 MB gives the same budget and fit (4.6 / 4.1 s on a7rv-test.psb, same on largetest.psb).
- a7rv-test.psb (6336x7920, 8-bit): solo 5-20 ms, restore 4.1-4.4 s (CPU fallback, fit 2300 MB; the solo fits at 194 MB), the "about 4 s" of the original report.

## Environment

- PhotoCraft 0.9.0 dev, Windows 11, Vulkan/DX12, `main` @ 2a952f164c0b4cf936b1c6497db10dd095341c00 (release build; the code cited below is unchanged since 58f855a4)
- 64 GB RAM, RTX 3070 Laptop 8 GB (Vulkan) + Intel UHD (hybrid laptop)

body:
## Summary

With a selection active, Alt+Tab out to another app and back, then Ctrl+D: nothing happens on the first press. Lead: the menu bar's "Alt tap" detector keeps its state across a focus loss. The Alt-down seen before leaving stays armed; when the Alt release reaches PhotoCraft on return it is read as a tap, and the keyboard moves onto the menu bar.

## Environment

- PhotoCraft 0.9.0 dev, Windows 11, `main` @ 58f855a40f67a9b6a7e9168ea03c261226845705
- Retested on installed build 7053f703 (5 commits behind 58f855a4)

## Steps to reproduce

Select all (Ctrl+A), Alt+Tab to another window and back with the keyboard, press Ctrl+D.

**Expected (Photoshop 2026):** Ctrl+D (Select > Deselect) always deselects; a window focus change never leaves a pending menu-bar activation, and the shortcut works on the first press.

**Actual:** Ctrl+D does nothing on the first press after returning. That a real Alt+Tab produces the same Alt tap was not checked (needs real keys).

## Where in the code

- https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/58f855a40f67a9b6a7e9168ea03c261226845705/crates/ui-egui/src/menu_keys.rs#L38-L47 : `alt_down` / `alt_tap` state; nothing resets it on `WindowFocused(false)`.
- https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/58f855a40f67a9b6a7e9168ea03c261226845705/crates/ui-egui/src/menu_keys.rs#L166-L179 : Alt press arms the tap, Alt release fires it; only a later key press or click disarms it.

## Likely fix

- In `Keys::keys`, on `Event::WindowFocused(false)` clear `alt_down`, `alt_tap`, `focus` and `underline` (the bar never keeps the keyboard across a focus change).
- Test: `WindowFocused(false)` after an Alt press, then `WindowFocused(true)` + Alt release + Ctrl+D deselects.

## Workaround

Press Escape once after returning, then Ctrl+D.

## Related

Split out: #6573 (Shortcuts: a command shortcut pressed while the in-window menu bar has the keyboard is swallowed)

Possibly related: #4988 (in-window menu bar Alt tap)

title: Content-Aware Fill: dialog shows Seed, Margin and Channel as bare number fields, with no explanation
author: theriseandfallofitall
body:
## Summary

Edit > Content-Aware Fill... opens the generic parameter dialog. `prefs_ui.rs` removes `margin`, `seed` and `channel` from the dialog's stored values so they stay hidden, but the dialog body draws every non-JSON parameter of the command's spec on every frame, so the three rows come back (and write their defaults into the params: `margin 0`, `seed 1`, `channel 0`). The user sees "Seed" with a number and a Random button (from #5886), "Margin" and "Channel" as integers, and no text saying what they do. Photoshop's Content-Aware Fill has none of these controls.

## Environment

- PhotoCraft 0.9.0 dev, Windows 11, `main` @ 58f855a40f67a9b6a7e9168ea03c261226845705
- Retested on installed build 7053f703 (5 commits behind 58f855a4)

{"command":"file.new","params":{"width":600,"height":400}}
{"command":"select.rect","params":{"x":200,"y":150,"width":120,"height":80}}

{"id":2,"method":"ui.inspect","params":{}}
```

**Expected:** Edit > Content-Aware Fill... shows only controls Photoshop has: Sampling Area options (Auto, Rectangular, Custom), Color Adaptation, Rotation Adaptation, Scale, Mirror, Output To and Sample All Layers. title: Content-Aware Fill: Sampling = Rectangular from the dialog fills the selection with black
author: theriseandfallofitall
body:
## Summary

The Content-Aware Fill dialog always writes its hidden `margin` default (0) into the params. With Sampling = Rectangular the engine takes margin 0 literally: the sampling window is exactly the selection, so there is nothing to sample from and the selection fills black. The dialog remembers its last Sampling, so later fills keep producing black until Sampling is changed.

## Environment

- PhotoCraft 0.9.0 dev, Windows 11, `main` @ 58f855a40f67a9b6a7e9168ea03c261226845705
- Retested on installed build 7053f703 (5 commits behind 58f855a4)

## Steps to reproduce

```json
{"command":"file.new","params":{"width":600,"height":400}}
{"command":"filter.render.clouds","params":{}}
{"command":"select.rect","params":{"x":200,"y":150,"width":120,"height":80}}
{"command":"edit.contentAwareFill","params":{"sampling":"rectangular","margin":0}}
```

The same happens through Edit > Content-Aware Fill... with Sampling set to Rectangular (the dialog sends margin 0). Read pixels inside the selection afterwards.

**Expected:** the selection is filled from the surrounding pixels, as with Auto (Photoshop 2026: Edit > Content-Aware Fill, Sampling Area Options > Rectangular).

**Actual:** (retest on 7053f703) the reply reports `window [200,150,120,80]` and the pixels inside the selection read 0.0 (black); before the fill they read 0.15, 0.61 and 0.64. With margin 1 or 40 the fill is normal, and omitting `margin` gives window [64,0,392,392].

title: Layers: hiding an adjustment layer (or a group of them) redraws the whole canvas, and past the GPU layer budget it is a from-scratch CPU composite
author: theriseandfallofitall

title: GPU compositor: 16-bit layer masks are uploaded as 32-bit floats, counting 4 bytes per pixel against the GPU budget
author: theriseandfallofitall
body:
## Summary

Only 8-bit grayscale masks are uploaded as `R8Unorm`. 16-bit masks (any mask from a 16-bit PSD, and every feathered or vector "combined" mask, which is cached as U16) become `R32Float`, 4 bytes per pixel. A painted full-canvas 16-bit mask on a 9290x6194 canvas is about 230 MB; ten are 2.3 GB, close to the 3 GB cap an 8 GB card gets (3/8 of VRAM) before any pixel layer is counted. Over budget, the redraw runs on the CPU from scratch.

## Environment

- PhotoCraft 0.9.0 dev, Windows 11, Vulkan/DX12, `main` @ 2a952f164c0b4cf936b1c6497db10dd095341c00 (release build; the code cited below is unchanged since 58f855a4)
- 64 GB RAM, RTX 3070 Laptop 8 GB (Vulkan) + Intel UHD (hybrid laptop)


## Steps to reproduce

```json
{"id":1,"method":"engine.execute","params":{"command":"file.new","params":{"width":9000,"height":6000,"depth":16}}}
{"id":2,"method":"engine.execute","params":{"command":"layer.newAdjustmentLayer.hueSaturation","params":{"hue":20}}}
{"id":3,"method":"ui.inspect","params":{}}
```

Add a layer mask to the adjustment layer (`layer.layerMask.revealAll`) and paint a 6000x3000 black rectangle into it; repeat the adjustment-and-mask step four times, reading `ui.inspect` -> `perf.timings.gpuLayerFit.needed` after each. Do the same in an 8-bit document (`"depth":8`) and compare the growth per mask.

**Expected:** a mask costs its own bit depth on the GPU: a 16-bit mask twice an 8-bit one, so `needed` grows by about 40.6 MB per mask in the 16-bit document (the 8-bit figure doubled).

**Actual:** measured: `needed` grows by 81.2 MB per mask (6000x3000 region) in a 16-bit 9000x6000 document against 20.3 MB in an 8-bit one, 4.0x instead of 2x; a full-canvas mask adds about 216 MB (4 bytes x 54 Mpx) instead of 108 MB. Identical with Memory Usage 50000 MB.

## Where in the code

- Mask pricing: https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/2a952f164c0b4cf936b1c6497db10dd095341c00/crates/gpu/src/lib.rs#L151-L175 (`TexKind::for_surface`: `Role::Mask` is `R8Direct…

title: Crop: selecting the tool starts a crop at once, so tool shortcuts can't leave it
author: theriseandfallofitall
body:
## Summary

Selecting the Crop tool immediately frames the whole image with a crop box (`ensure_frame`), and the tool treats that untouched box as a crop in progress. While it exists, P toggles Use Classic Mode instead of selecting the Pen, and I, O and H are taken by the crop too, so tool keys cannot leave Crop and Esc re-creates the box. In Photoshop the crop starts only when you click or drag on the image.

## Environment

- PhotoCraft 0.9.0 dev, Windows 11, `main` @ 2a952f164c0b4cf936b1c6497db10dd095341c00 (installed dev build at the same commit)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open any document.
2. Select the Crop tool: a full-image crop box appears without any click.
3. Press P (then Esc, then P again).

Control channel:

```json
{"command":"file.new","params":{"width":800,"height":600}}
{"method":"ui.set","params":{"tool":"crop"}}
{"method":"ui.key","params":{"key":"P"}}
{"method":"ui.inspect","params":{}}
{"method":"ui.key","params":{"key":"Escape"}}
{"method":"ui.key","params":{"key":"P"}}
{"method":"ui.inspect","params":{}}
```

`ui.inspect` -> `tool` is still `crop`, `toolOptions.crop_shield.classic_mode` flipped each time, a crop box is present.

**Expected (Photoshop 2026, checked by hand):** the crop starts only when you click or drag on the image; Esc exits it. P toggles Use Classic Mode only while a crop is in progress (a section drawn or changed); with the Crop tool merely selected, P selects the Pen and the other tool keys switch tools as usual. title: Feedback: play the OS alert sound when an action is refused, as Photoshop does
author: theriseandfallofitall
body:
## Problem

When an operation isn't possible, Photoshop plays the system error sound and, for a tool on a locked layer, shows a modal ("Can't use the tool because the layer is locked."). PhotoCraft only writes a red message in the status bar (for example "Could not complete your request because the target layer is hidden."), easy to miss while looking at the canvas. The beep hook that Beep When Done uses already exists, so an error cue is small.

## How I'd use it

Hear that a brush stroke or command was refused while looking at the canvas, instead of spotting the red status-bar text.

**Photoshop:** using a tool on a locked layer plays the system error sound and shows a modal "Can't use the tool because the layer is locked." (screenshot attached). There is no setting; the sound follows the OS sound scheme.

## Environment

- PhotoCraft 0.9.0 dev, Windows 11, `main` @ 58f855a40f67a9b6a7e9168ea03c261226845705
- Retested on installed build 7053f703 (5 commits behind 58f855a4)

## Steps to reproduce

```json
{"command":"file.new","params":{"width":64,"height":64}}
{"command":"layer.new.layer","params":{}}
{"command":"layer.setProps","params":{"layer":<new layer id>,"visible":false}}
{"method":"ui.set","params":{"tool":"brush"}}
{"method":"ui.pointer","params":{"events":[{"kind":"down","x":10,"y":10},{"kind":"up","x":10,"y":10}]}}
```

**Expected (Photoshop 2026):** a refused action plays the system sound (Windows: the sound scheme's error/default beep) as well as showing the message; on a locked layer Photoshop also shows a modal.

**Actual:** silent. Retested: the status bar shows "Could not complete your request because the target layer is hidden." with `statusError` true; nothing else happens. `general.beepWhenDone` exists (off by default).

## Where in the code

- https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/58f855a40f67a9b6a7e9168ea03c261226845705/apps/photocraft/src/services.rs#L571-L586 (`platform_beep`)
- https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/58f855a40f6…

title: Histogram panel: a black/white split image shows a spike in the middle (it counts a blurred 384 px thumbnail)
author: theriseandfallofitall
body:
## Summary

A document that is half pure black and half pure white should show two bars, at 0 and 255. The Histogram panel also shows a bar in the middle (about 128), and its Mean (127.17) and Std Dev are slightly off. The panel does not count the document's pixels: it counts a 384 px area-averaged thumbnail, and the column where the edge falls inside one averaging cell comes out mid-grey.

## Environment

- PhotoCraft 0.9.0 dev, Windows 11, `main` @ 58f855a40f67a9b6a7e9168ea03c261226845705
- Retested on installed build 7053f703 (5 commits behind 58f855a4)

## Steps to reproduce

```json
{"command":"file.new","params":{"width":1000,"height":1000,"background":"white"}}
{"command":"layer.new.layer","params":{}}
{"command":"select.rect","params":{"x":0,"y":0,"width":334,"height":1000}}
{"command":"edit.fill","params":{"color":"#000000"}}
{"command":"select.deselect","params":{}}
```

Open Window â–¸ Histogram (RGB). The split is at x = 334 so it falls inside a thumbnail cell; a split at exactly 500 happens to land on a cell edge and shows no spike.

**Expected:** two bars (0 and 255) and, for a 50/50 split, Mean 127.5 (Photoshop 2026, Window â–¸ Histogram at Cache Level 1 or after Uncached Refresh).

**Actual:** a third bar in the middle of the axis; Mean (127.17 in the first report) and Std Dev computed from the blurred proxy. Retested: a pixel-column scan of the panel shows the middle bar for a split at x = 334, and only the two end bars for splits at 333 and 500 (both fall on a cell edge).

## Where in the code

- Counting runs on the proxy: https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/58f855a40f67a9b6a7e9168ea03c261226845705/crates/ui-egui/src/tone.rs#L110-L123 (`photocraft_compose::thumbnail(&d, 384)`)

title: Layers panel: mark layers PhotoCraft keeps but cannot render
author: theriseandfallofitall
body:
## Problem

When a PSD contains an adjustment PhotoCraft recognises but cannot read, the user learns of it only from a one-time open notice. After that nothing in the Layers panel says the layer does nothing, so a picture that differs from Photoshop's gives no hint why. Retested on installed build 7053f703 (5 commits behind 58f855a4): the Layers panel row code has no unsupported indicator; only the import-time warning exists.

## How I'd use it

Open a PSD, see at a glance which layers are kept as imported but not rendered (a warning icon with a tooltip such as "Not rendered: Photoshop adjustment layer, kept as imported"), and decide whether to flatten, delete or keep them. Use the theme's warning colour plus an icon, not the Red layer colour label, which already means something in Photoshop.

**Photoshop:** no equivalent; this is a usability fix, not a parity item.

## Environment

- PhotoCraft 0.9.0 dev, Windows 11, `main` @ 58f855a40f67a9b6a7e9168ea03c261226845705
- Retested on installed build 7053f703 (5 commits behind 58f855a4)

## Where in the code

- Layers panel row, where an indicator would go: https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/58f855a40f67a9b6a7e9168ea03c261226845705/crates/ui-egui/src/panels.rs#L2767
- Recognised-but-unreadable adjustments get a warning at import and then nothing persistent: https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/58f855a40f67a9b6a7e9168ea03c261226845705/crates/io/src/psd_import.rs#L354-L363
- `Adjustment::Unsupported { psd_key, raw }` and its Properties text: https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/58f855a40f67a9b6a7e9168ea03c261226845705/crates/ui-egui/src/adjust_editors.rs#L1623-L1627

## Likely fix

1. Layers panel: a small warning icon on rows whose content is `Adjustment::Unsupported`, with a tooltip stating why; use `Tokens.warning`.
2. Expose it to agents: `layer.list` / `ui.inspect` report `unsupported: true` and the key.
3. Tests: the row of an `Adjustment::Unsupported` layer reports the marker.

title: Color Lookup: PSD save always writes the LUT as .cube, so a .3dl/.look source changes format on round trip
author: theriseandfallofitall
body:
## Summary

A Color Lookup adjustment embeds its LUT in the PSD (`LUT3DFileData`, `LUTFormat`, `LUT3DFileName`). PhotoCraft re-emits the table as `.cube` text with `LUTFormatCUBE` whatever the source format was, but keeps the original display name, so the saved layer says `.3dl` while holding `.cube` data and format. Photoshop will show a different format than the one the layer was made with.

## Environment

- PhotoCraft 0.9.0 dev, Windows 11, `main` @ 58f855a40f67a9b6a7e9168ea03c261226845705

author: theriseandfallofitall

The setting is a bare drag field labelled "Memory usage mb" (the key name humanized). Nothing says what it limits: it caps each open document's pixels plus History in RAM (oldest undo states are dropped beyond it), and in Automatic mode it also feeds the GPU compositor budget. title: Object Finder: highlight every detectable object up front, not one lookup per pointer rest
author: theriseandfallofitall
body:
## Problem

Photoshop's Object Finder highlights the selectable objects as the pointer moves over them. PhotoCraft looks up one object per pointer rest: the pointer must rest 0.12 s before a lookup starts, a miss is remembered for a 5 x 5 pixel area around the point until the document changes (moving across an object edge can leave the cursor in a remembered miss), and each object is found by growing a similar-colour area from the cursor (colour step 10, distance to mean 32 in CIELAB). Textured or gradient objects stop growing early or fail the area test, so the preview is partial or absent, and you can't see what is selectable without probing the image.

## How I'd use it

Move the pointer over the photo and see every detected object highlighted immediately, then click the one I want.

**Photoshop:** Object Selection tool with Object Finder: objects under the pointer are highlighted before the click.

## Environment

- PhotoCraft 0.9.0 dev build, Windows 11, `main` @ 58f855a40f67a9b6a7e9168ea03c261226845705
- Retested on installed build 7053f703 (5 commits behind 58f855a4)

## Where in the code

- https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/58f855a40f67a9b6a7e9168ea03c261226845705/crates/ui-egui/src/object_finder.rs#L115-L124 : misses within 2 px are skipped; lookup only after `DEBOUNCE` (0.12 s); one lookup at a time.
- https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/58f855a40f67a9b6a7e9168ea03c261226845705/crates/algo/src/segment/grabcut.rs#L219-L253 : the colour region growth (`grow_similar`).

## Likely fix

Precompute all candidate objects once per document revision (segments from a superpixel pass) so every object highlights at once; the model in #2788 would replace the heuristic.

## Related

Possibly related: #4087, #5245, #2788

title: Remove tool: use the stroke's direction to continue edges and lines through the hole
author: theriseandfallofitall
body:
## Problem

Photoshop's Remove tool continues the edge or line through the repair: painting a vertical stroke over a dark line that runs along a wood edge removes the line and the edge carries on cleanly (before/after screenshots attached, a stock photo). PhotoCraft's Remove fills exactly the stroke's footprint (grown 2 px) with non-local patch completion that sees the footprint as a bare mask; the stroke's path and direction are discarded, and the edge is not kept.

Measured on a stock photo of oak slats with black gaps (1920x2560), one vertical black-to-oak edge (edge x about 243.3 px, rows 900-1100; the untouched edge wanders 0.35 px), Remove tool at its default size 20, each case on a fresh copy, strokes y 860-1140. Edge position is where luminance crosses 110 per row; "orig" is the untouched image.

| stroke | edge std px (orig 0.35) | line-fit residual px (orig 0.19) | mean offset of the edge vs orig | max offset | window luminance MAE vs orig |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| a: on the edge | 1.33 | 1.03 | 4.74 px | 7.02 px | 11.4 |
| b: offset 10 px onto the oak | 0.73 | 0.72 | 5.36 px | 6.88 px | 13.7 |
| c: centred in the black gap | 0.35 | 0.19 | 0.00 px | 0.00 px | 0.3 |

| e: Shift-click straight line | 1.41 | 1.09 | 4.80 px | 7.68 px | 11.6 |

title: Content-Aware Fill: no workspace to paint the sampling area (Sampling Brush, preview, overlay)
author: theriseandfallofitall
body:

PhotoCraft opens a generic parameter dialog instead, so the only choices are Auto, Rectangular, or a typed area. The engine already supports a custom sampling area (`sampling: "custom"` with `area` or an alpha `channel`); what is missing is the UI that paints it. Open PR #2376 implements this workspace; this ticket gives it an issue to close and tracks the scorecard row TOOL-214-15.

Today the dialog only offers Auto, Rectangular or a typed area, and a custom area needs an alpha channel made by hand (`{"command":"edit.contentAwareFill","params":{"sampling":"custom","channel":"Sampling"}}`).

**Photoshop:** Edit > Content-Aware Fill… opens the Content-Aware Fill workspace: Sampling Brush (add or subtract, Alt reverses, size with `[` `]`), Show Sampling Area overlay with Opacity, Color and Indicates (Sampling Area or Excluded Area), Sampling Area Options (Auto, Rectangular, Custom), Fill Settings (Color Adaptation, Rotation Adaptation, Scale, Mirror), a Preview panel, Output To (Current Layer, New Layer, Duplicate Layer), and OK / Apply / Cancel.

title: GPU canvas: a layer texture that fails to allocate is not caught, evicted for or retried, so one Out of Memory ends GPU drawing
author: theriseandfallofitall
body:
## Summary

Split from #5827. `Compositor::sync` creates one `pc_compose_layer` texture per layer or mask page with a bare `device.create_texture`: no OutOfMemory error scope, no check of the bytes about to be added against the budget, and eviction only runs after each cell. A document with many large 16-bit layers can overshoot the budget and the card; the driver returns `VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DEVICE_MEMORY` and every later texture in the same pass is invalid (526 `pc_compose_layer` validation errors within 4 ms in the parent). The VRAM cap from #5234 lowers the budget but adds no check: the parent's failure came at a 2.1 GB VRAM peak.

That this one error then disables the GPU for the session is #6564.

## Environment

- PhotoCraft 0.9.0 dev build, Windows 11, `main` @ 58f855a40f67a9b6a7e9168ea03c261226845705
- Seen on an 8 GB discrete NVIDIA laptop GPU (Vulkan), Memory usage 16000 MB, Rendering Mode Automatic

## Steps to reproduce

1. Raise the budget: `{"id":1,"method":"engine.execute","params":{"command":"prefs.set","params":{"path":"performance.memoryUsageMb","value":16000}}}`
2. `app.open` a 9290x6194 16-bit layered PSB with about 98 layers (smart objects with smart filters, feathered masks).
3. `{"id":2,"method":"ui.inspect","params":{}}`: read `perf.timings.gpuInfo.lost` and `canvas`.

**Actual:** the log shows one `uncaptured wgpu error: Out of Memory`, then hundreds of `Texture with 'pc_compose_layer' label is invalid`; `canvas` is `cpu`.

**Expected:** with Edit > Preferences > Performance > Graphics Processor Settings > Use Graphics Processor on (Photoshop's setting; PhotoCraft's Rendering Mode Automatic), a document that needs about 5 GB on an 8 GB card draws on the GPU. When a layer texture does not fit, PhotoCraft evicts least recently used resident pages and retries. Only if nothing is left to free does that one refresh fall back to the CPU compositor ("layers exceed the GPU memory budget"), and the next refresh uses the GPU again.

title: Select Subject: blend the Focus Area sharpness map into the saliency so shallow-depth-of-field portraits separate from a same-coloured background
author: diegochagas
body:
Follow-up to #2788, from @theriseandfallofitall's report there (a Sony A7R V portrait against trees and buildings: Select Subject and Object Selection follow colour, not the person). Classical, ships before and independently of the model work.

## What

`select_subject`'s saliency (`crates/algo/src/segment/subject.rs`, `saliency()`) is colour only: SLIC superpixels in CIELAB, boundary connectivity (Zhu et al. 2014) blended with frequency-tuned saliency (Achanta et al. 2009). On a photo with a sharp subject and a blurred background the strongest cue is never used: local sharpness. `segment/focus.rs` already computes it (`sharpness(img, noise) -> Vec<f32>`, normalised `0..=1`, the map behind Select › Focus Area), so the blend is cheap.

## Proposed

- In `saliency()`, blend a normalised sharpness map into the per-superpixel score: mean sharpness per superpixel, weighted by how bimodal the map is over the image (a flat map, as in a landscape or a scan, contributes nothing; a strongly bimodal map, as in a shallow-depth-of-field portrait, contributes up to an equal share with the colour terms). Background-connected superpixels keep their penalty.
- `select_subject` and `layer.removeBackground` get it for free; Object Selection's box prompt uses the same saliency for its seed, so it benefits too.
- No new parameters; the `backend: "classical"` path of #2788 is exactly this.
- Tests: a synthetic sharp disc on a blurred backdrop of the same colour (colour-only saliency fails, blended passes); the existing #2788 fixtures stay unchanged; a flat-sharpness image (no depth of field) keeps the current mask byte for byte; `panic_hunt`.
- Regression image to add to the acceptance set: a person against foliage with similar greens in the clothing (colour alone fails; sharpness separates it).

Not in scope: a depth map, which has no classical equivalent and belongs with the model in #2788 / #4098.

title: Shortcuts: a command shortcut pressed while the in-window menu bar has the keyboard is swallowed
author: theriseandfallofitall
body:
## Summary

Split from #6529. After a tap on Alt the in-window menu bar owns the keyboard, and `shortcuts::handle` returns before dispatching anything. A command shortcut such as Ctrl+D does nothing, and keeps doing nothing, until Escape leaves the bar. A native menu bar would leave the bar and run the shortcut.

## Environment

- PhotoCraft 0.9.0 dev, Windows 11, `main` @ 58f855a40f67a9b6a7e9168ea03c261226845705

## Steps to reproduce

Control channel (see `docs/control-protocol.md`, `ui.key`):

```json
{"command":"select.all"}
```

then the methods `ui.key {"key":"AltLeft"}` (a tap on Alt) and `ui.key {"key":"D","command":true}`; then `ui.inspect`.

**Expected (Photoshop 2026):** Ctrl+D (Select > Deselect) deselects; a command shortcut always runs.

**Actual:** the selection is still there (`hasSelection` stays true) and the menu bar has the keyboard (File lit). A second Ctrl+D does nothing either. `ui.key {"key":"Escape"}` leaves the bar, after which Ctrl+D deselects.

## Where in the code

- https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/58f855a40f67a9b6a7e9168ea03c261226845705/crates/ui-egui/src/shortcuts.rs#L344-L349 : `handle` returns early when the bar is focused.
- https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/58f855a40f67a9b6a7e9168ea03c261226845705/crates/ui-egui/src/menu_keys.rs#L56-L62 : `is_focused`, the bar owns the keys while focused.
- https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/58f855a40f67a9b6a7e9168ea03c261226845705/crates/ui-egui/src/menu_keys.rs#L237-L264 : with no menu open, a key the bar doesn't use (Ctrl+D) is neither consumed nor leaves the bar.

## Likely fix

While the bar is focused, a command shortcut (Ctrl/Cmd combos, F-keys) should leave the bar and run. Test: `AltLeft` tap, then Ctrl+D, deselects.

## Workaround

Press Escape, then the shortcut.

## Related

Split from #6529 (the Alt tap that Alt+Tab leaves armed, which puts the bar in this state after a focus change).

Possibly related: #4988 (in-window menu bar Alt tap)

title: Histogram panel: bar heights are scaled to the 251st smallest bin, so sparse histograms draw tiny counts as tall as the real peaks
author: theriseandfallofitall
body:
## Summary

Split from #6538. The Histogram panel scales its bars to the 251st smallest bin (`sorted.get(250)`), which is 0 for a histogram with few occupied levels. A bin holding a few hundred samples is then drawn as tall as bins holding hundreds of thousands, so sparse images (flat fills, posterised, black/white) mislead about how much is where.

## Environment

- PhotoCraft 0.9.0 dev, Windows 11, `main` @ 58f855a40f67a9b6a7e9168ea03c261226845705

## Steps to reproduce

```json
{"command":"file.new","params":{"width":1000,"height":1000,"background":"white"}}
{"command":"layer.new.layer","params":{}}
{"command":"select.rect","params":{"x":0,"y":0,"width":100,"height":1000}}
{"command":"edit.fill","params":{"color":"#000000"}}
{"command":"select.deselect","params":{}}
```

Open Window > Histogram (RGB). A 100 px split lands on a thumbnail cell edge, so the middle spike of #6538 does not confuse the picture: this is about bar heights only.

**Expected:** two bars, the black one a ninth of the white one's height (10 % vs 90 % of the pixels). Photoshop 2026 scales linearly to the tallest bin.

**Actual:** on the 50/50 black/white document of #6538 (screenshot there), the middle bin, which holds only the few averaged edge samples, is drawn about as tall as the two end bins that each hold half of all pixels. Bars are not proportional to counts.

## Where in the code

- https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/58f855a40f67a9b6a7e9168ea03c261226845705/crates/ui-egui/src/tone.rs#L220-L231 : display scaling to `sorted.get(250)`.

## Likely fix

Scale to the tallest bin excluding the two end bins (or a percentile of occupied bins), never to a bin index that is 0 for sparse histograms. Test: the 90/10 document draws the small bar at about a ninth of the big one.

## Related

Split from #6538 (the middle spike from counting a blurred 384 px thumbnail).

Possibly related: #49, #3050

## Summary

Split from #6541. Recognised-but-unreadable adjustments import as `Adjustment::Unsupported { psd_key, raw }` and get a warning. An adjustment-looking block with a key no mapper knows falls through to an empty pixel layer instead: the layer's data is dropped, it saves as nothing, and nothing tells the user.

## Environment

- PhotoCraft 0.9.0 dev, Windows 11, `main` @ 58f855a40f67a9b6a7e9168ea03c261226845705

## Steps to reproduce

Open a PSD whose adjustment layer uses a key outside PhotoCraft's 16 known ones (needs a Photoshop 2026 file, e.g. a newer adjustment type), then `ui.inspect`.

**Expected:** imported as `Adjustment::Unsupported` with the original block kept verbatim for export, plus the existing import warning.

**Actual (code reading, not yet confirmed with a file):** an empty pixel layer, no warning, the original block lost on save.

## Where in the code

- https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/58f855a40f67a9b6a7e9168ea03c261226845705/crates/io/src/psd_import.rs#L331 and https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/58f855a40f67a9b6a7e9168ea03c261226845705/crates/io/src/psd_import.rs#L469 : unknown keys fall through to an empty pixel layer.
- https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/58f855a40f67a9b6a7e9168ea03c261226845705/crates/io/src/psd_import.rs#L354-L363 : the warning recognised-but-unreadable adjustments get.
- https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/58f855a40f67a9b6a7e9168ea03c261226845705/crates/io/src/adjust_map.rs#L18 : the 16 known keys.

## Likely fix

When a layer record carries an adjustment-looking block no mapper knows, import it as `Adjustment::Unsupported { psd_key, raw }` so the block round-trips verbatim and gets the existing warning. Test: an adjustment record with an unknown key imports as Unsupported, warns, and exports unchanged.

## Related

Split from #6541 (the Layers panel marker for layers kept but not rendered).

Possibly related: #1763, #3777, #6542

title: Object Finder: objects a few dozen pixels wide in a large document are not found
author: theriseandfallofitall
body:
## Summary

## Environment

with `point` on the object. Repeat with a 1000x800 object.

**Expected (Photoshop 2026, Object Selection with Object Finder):** the small object under the pointer is found.

**Actual:** (retested) the 24x24 px object finds nothing; the 1000x800 object is found.

- https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/58f855a40f67a9b6a7e9168ea03c261226845705/crates/algo/src/segment/grabcut.rs#L135-L168 : the 60,000 pixel working copy.

## Likely fix

Refine in a full-resolution window around the cursor, or raise the working size for large documents, so small objects survive. Test: the 24x24 px case selects the object.

title: GPU recovery dialog: "Retry GPU" only saves a preference and needs a restart
author: theriseandfallofitall
body:
## Summary

Split from #6564. After a GPU fault the "Switched to CPU rendering" dialog offers Keep Using CPU and Retry GPU. Retry GPU writes the next-launch preference and says "Retry GPU requires a restart"; it does not rebuild the GPU canvas, so the canvas stays on the CPU for the session and the user must close PhotoCraft (and every open document) to try again.

## Environment

- PhotoCraft 0.9.0 dev, Windows 11, `main` @ 58f855a40f67a9b6a7e9168ea03c261226845705
- Seen on an 8 GB discrete NVIDIA laptop GPU (Vulkan) with an Intel UHD also present

## Steps to reproduce

Needs a GPU fault (the parent hit one opening a 9290x6194 16-bit layered PSB with about 98 layers at `performance.memoryUsageMb` 16000). When the dialog appears, press Retry GPU, then `ui.inspect`.

**Expected (Photoshop 2026, Preferences > Performance > Use Graphics Processor):** Retry GPU creates a new device and canvas without closing documents.

**Actual:** `perf.timings.gpuInfo.lost` still reads "GPU error: Out of Memory" and `canvas` stays `cpu`; the dialog says a restart is required.

## Where in the code

- https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/58f855a40f67a9b6a7e9168ea03c261226845705/crates/ui-egui/src/gpu_status.rs#L96-L150 : Retry GPU is a preference write plus "restart".
- https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/58f855a40f67a9b6a7e9168ea03c261226845705/crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs#L1655-L1690 : the canvas switches to the CPU for the session.

## Likely fix

Retry GPU drops the faulted `GpuCanvas`, creates a fresh device and re-uploads, leaving documents untouched. Test: mark a `DeviceHealth` faulted, run the retry path, assert the canvas is healthy and the documents unchanged.

## Workaround

Restart PhotoCraft.

## Related

Split from #6564 (an error on a live device being treated as a permanent fault).

Possibly related: #5827, #6563, #1015

title: Save silently overwrites changes another app made to the file
author: zuujiscom
body:
**What happens**
PhotoCraft doesn't notice when its document's file changes on disk. File › Save writes over the other app's changes with no warning.

**Repro**
1. Save a layered document as `a.psd`.
2. Change and save `a.psd` in another app. A second PhotoCraft window, Photoshop or a sync client all count.
3. Back in PhotoCraft, make any edit and press ⌘S / Ctrl+S.

**Result:** The other app's changes are gone. No notice appears, and the status bar says "Saved a.psd".

**Expected:** Before writing over the file, Save sees that it changed since it was opened or last saved. It then offers Overwrite, Save As… or Cancel.

**Where:** `DocState` (`crates/engine/src/lib.rs`) keeps only `path`. Nothing records size, mtime or a hash at open or save time, so `save_in_place` / `write_document` (`crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs`) have nothing to compare against. The size+mtime stamps that `link_watch.rs` already uses for linked smart objects would work here too.

**Why it matters:** The Craft apps hand files to each other, and synced folders (Dropbox, OneDrive, iCloud) rewrite files under the app. Both are everyday ways to hit this.

> Found during a filesystem audit; the headless repro test is available on request.

title: Save As onto a file that's open in another tab leaves that tab marked "saved"
author: zuujiscom
body:
**Repro**
1. Document A: save it as `a.psd` and keep it open.
2. Document B, in a second tab: Save As `a.psd` and confirm the overwrite.

**Result:** Both tabs now have `a.psd` as their file and both show as saved. A's content exists only in memory, and closing A asks nothing, so it is lost. A later ⌘S in tab A overwrites B's save.

**Expected:** Refuse to save over a file that is open in another document, or at least mark A as unsaved and detached from that path.

**Where:** `save_as_step` → `write_document` → `saved_inner` (`crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs`). Nothing checks the other open documents' paths.

> Found during a filesystem audit; the headless repro test is available on request.

title: Opening a file that is already open opens a second copy
author: zuujiscom
body:
**Repro:** Open `a.psd`, then open `a.psd` again (File › Open, Open Recent, drag and drop or the Home screen).

**Result:** Two tabs, both bound to `a.psd`. Saving one overwrites the other's file, which leads into #2.

**Expected:** Photoshop switches to the open document instead.

**Where:** `open_path` / `open_paths` / `open_file` (`crates/ui-egui/src/file_open.rs`) don't look for an open document with the same path. That check should compare canonical paths.

> Found during a filesystem audit; the headless repro test is available on request.

title: Quick Export as PNG with Location = Same Folder overwrites the document's source file
author: zuujiscom
body:
**Repro**
1. Set File › Export › Export Preferences… › Quick export location to Same Folder.
2. Open `photo.png` and add a layer.
3. File › Export › Quick Export as PNG.

**Result:** `photo.png`, the original, is replaced by the flattened export without a prompt. Any existing `<name>.png` beside a PSD is overwritten the same way.

**Expected:** Never overwrite silently. Either pick a free name (`photo-1.png`) or ask. Photoshop's matching option writes into a `<name>-assets` folder next to the document, so it can't collide with the source.

**Where:** `quick_export` in `crates/engine/src/web_cmds.rs` builds `join(dir, "<stem>.<fmt>")` and writes it with no existence check. Only people who changed the default (Ask) are affected.

> Found during a filesystem audit; the headless repro test is available on request.

title: Saving replaces a read-only file (Linux/macOS)
author: zuujiscom
body:
**Repro:** `chmod 444 a.psd`, open it, edit, Save.

**Result:** The save succeeds. The file is replaced (new inode) and keeps mode 0444. A rename only needs write permission on the folder, so the file's read-only mode is never consulted.

**Expected:** Refuse with "a.psd is read-only" and offer Save As. On Windows the rename already fails with an access error, so platforms currently disagree.

**Where:** `atomic_write_with_progress` (`crates/format/src/atomic.rs`). Checking `target.metadata()?.permissions().readonly()` before writing the temp file would cover it. A deliberate overwrite path can stay for callers that want one.

> Found during a filesystem audit; the headless repro test is available on request.

title: File names that aren't valid UTF-8: Open fails, and Save As writes a second file
author: zuujiscom
body:
**Repro (Linux):**
```bash
cp ok.png "$(printf 'img\xff.png')"
```
Then open that file in PhotoCraft, edit, and Save As to the suggested name.

**Result:** Open fails with `img�.png: No such file or directory`. Save As writes a new file, `img�.png` (U+FFFD), beside the untouched original `img\xFF.png`.

**Where:** Paths are carried as `String` and converted with `to_string_lossy`:
- `path_of` in `apps/photocraft/src/services.rs`
- dropped files in `crates/ui-egui/src/file_open.rs`
- `absolute()`
- `DocState.path: Option<String>`

Either carry `PathBuf`/`OsString` end to end, or refuse such paths with a clear error instead of rewriting them. #1108 only fixed the startup panic for such arguments.

**Note:** This was reproduced by passing the lossy path the way the code does. I didn't click through the real dialog on a desktop.

> Found during a filesystem audit; the headless repro test is available on request.

title: Saving breaks hard links
author: zuujiscom
body:
**Repro:** `ln a.psd b.psd`, open `a.psd`, edit, Save.

**Result:** `a.psd` has the new content and `b.psd` still has the old content (link count drops to 1).

**Why:** `atomic_write` writes a temp file and renames it over the target, which makes a new inode. Common options are to rewrite in place when `nlink > 1` (accepting the crash-safety trade-off) or at least warn. I'm filing this so it's a known, chosen behaviour rather than a surprise.

**Where:** `crates/format/src/atomic.rs`.

> Found during a filesystem audit; the headless repro test is available on request.

title: Saving drops a file's extended attributes (and probably macOS Finder tags)
author: zuujiscom
body:
**Repro (Linux):** `setfattr -n user.test -v tag a.psd`, open it, edit, Save, then `getfattr a.psd`.

**Result:** The attribute is gone.

**Why:** The rename replaces the file. Only the permission bits are copied (`copy_permissions` in `crates/format/src/atomic.rs`); ownership, xattrs and ACLs aren't. On macOS, Finder tags, comments and the per-file "Open with" choice are xattrs, so they would be dropped too. That part is untested; it would be good to confirm on a Mac.

**Possible fix:** Copy xattrs (and on macOS use `copyfile(COPYFILE_METADATA)` or `renamex_np`) onto the temp file before the rename.

> Found during a filesystem audit; the headless repro test is available on request.

title: Interrupted saves leave hidden `*.pcsave.tmp` files beside the user's file forever
author: zuujiscom
body:
**Repro:** Kill PhotoCraft (or lose power) while a big save is writing.

**Result:** `.a.psd.<pid>-<n>.pcsave.tmp` stays in the user's folder. It can be gigabytes, and it is hidden on macOS and Linux. Later saves and launches never remove it.

**Where:** `sweep_orphans` (`crates/format/src/autosave.rs`) cleans these up only inside the recovery folder (#3489). Idea: when saving `X`, remove stale `.X.*.pcsave.tmp` siblings whose PID isn't running, the same way the recovery sweep does.

> Found during a filesystem audit; the headless repro test is available on request.

title: Saving onto a dangling symlink replaces the link with a regular file
author: zuujiscom
body:
**Repro:** `ln -s missing/dir/a.psd link.psd`, then Save As `link.psd`.

**Result:** `link.psd` becomes a regular file and the link is gone.

**Expected:** Write through to the link's target, as `resolve_symlink` does for live links, or report that the target folder doesn't exist. `resolve_symlink` falls back to the link path when `canonicalize` fails (`crates/format/src/atomic.rs`). Low priority.

> Found during a filesystem audit; the headless repro test is available on request.

title: Save As or a recorded action into a missing folder silently creates the whole folder tree
author: zuujiscom
body:
**Repro:** `file.saveAs {"path": "/home/me/typo/does/not/exist/a.psd"}` from an action, a script or the CLI.

**Result:** It succeeds and creates `typo/does/not/exist/`.

**Expected:** Probably fail with "folder doesn't exist" (a dialog can't produce this path anyway). An action replayed on another machine, or a typo in a script, then scatters folders. `create_dir_all` is in `atomic_write_with_progress`. Low priority; it may be intended for batch output.

> Found during a filesystem audit; the headless repro test is available on request.

title: Saving needs about 4× the file's size in extra RAM
author: zuujiscom
body:
**Measured:** A debug build, a 4000×4000 two-layer document full of noise, and a 130 MB PSD file:
- **Save:** resident memory went from 168 MB to a 701 MB peak, so +534 MB, about 4× the file's size.
- **Open:** it peaked 387 MB above the starting point and settled at +156 MB.

**Why:** The save path encodes the whole file into one `Vec<u8>` (`ExportResult.bytes`, `photocraft_io::export_with`) and then writes it. Even `.pcraft` ZIP saves are built in memory (`store.rs` `save_path` → `save_zip`); only directory bundles stream. Opening holds the whole file in an `Arc<Vec<u8>>` while decoding (`engine/src/jobs.rs`).

**Effect:** A 2 GB PSB save would need about 8 GB on top of the document. The out-of-memory risk peaks at Save, right after the work is done.

**Related:** #4185 (scratch disk), #5106 (print-scale tracking), and #6583 / #6589 (PSD/PSB open without the whole file). No PR covers streaming saves yet.

> Found during a filesystem audit; the headless repro test is available on request.

title: Linked smart objects use absolute paths, so moving a project breaks every link
author: zuujiscom
body:
**Repro:** Place Linked `art/logo.png` into `project/design.pcraft`, then move or rename the `project` folder (or open it on another machine).

**Result:** Every link is missing.

**Expected:** Also store a path relative to the document, and look it up first, so a project folder can be moved or shared.

**Where:** The source is stored as an absolute string (`SmartSource::Linked { path }`, set in `crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs` and the place commands), and `link_watch.rs` resolves it only as given. Any fix needs to respect #2927, #5609 and #3837 (security around document-supplied paths).

> Found during a filesystem audit; the headless repro test is available on request.

title: PSD export embeds every external link, and Photoshop's own external links aren't followed
author: zuujiscom
body:
**Result:**
- **Export:** saving a document with a linked smart object as PSD embeds the file and warns "PSD export keeps no external links" (`crates/io/src/psd_export.rs`).
- **Import:** a Photoshop PSD with external (`liFE`) or alias (`liFA`) link records keeps them byte for byte, but `find_in_blocks` (`crates/io/src/linked.rs`) only reads embedded data, so those links never follow their files.

Linked workflows therefore don't survive a round trip with Photoshop in either direction.

**Related:** #2927 (any fix must keep reads capability-scoped).

title: Open Recent and the Home screen keep listing files that were moved or deleted
author: zuujiscom
body:
**Repro:** Open `a.psd`, close it, delete or move it, then click it in Open Recent or on the Home screen.

**Result:** "Couldn't open a.psd: No such file or directory", and the entry stays in both lists.

**Expected:** Show missing entries as unavailable, or drop them, possibly with a check when the menu or Home screen is built (off the UI thread for network paths). A related detail: Open Recent labels show only the file name (`menus.rs`), so `a.psd` from two folders look identical, while the Home screen shows the folder.

**Side note on #6016:** A layered document saved as a flat PNG is written as a copy, and copies aren't added to recents (`saved_inner`). That looks like the actual cause there.

title: One wrongly typed value in prefs.json resets all preferences, every launch
author: zuujiscom
body:
**Repro:** In `prefs.json`, set `"fileHandling": {"recentFileCount": "ten"}` (a hand edit, or a value a newer version wrote before a downgrade), then launch.

**Result:** The status bar shows "Preferences were reset: invalid type…", and every preference runs at its default for the whole session. The file isn't rewritten (the three-way merge in `write_prefs` keeps it), so the same reset happens on every launch until someone edits the file by hand.

**Expected:** Load everything that parses and drop or default only the bad field (serde `deserialize_with` fallbacks per field, or parse section by section). Show a proper notice that names the file, and keep a `prefs.json.bad` copy.

**Where:** `load_prefs_json` (`crates/engine/src/prefs.rs`) and `prefs_ui::load`.

title: Linux/macOS: crash-recovery autosaves live in the config folder
author: zuujiscom
body:
**What:** Recovery bundles, which can be gigabytes for big documents, go to `~/.config/photocraft/Recovery` on Linux and `~/Library/Application Support/Photocraft/Recovery` on macOS (`recovery_dir` in `apps/photocraft/src/services.rs`).

**Why it matters:** On Linux, the XDG spec puts state like this in `$XDG_STATE_HOME` (`~/.local/state`) or the cache folder. Dotfile managers and config sync often copy `~/.config` wholesale.

**Related:** #5648 / #6412 handle the Windows roaming-profile version of this. This is the same question for the other two platforms.

title: Web build: no autosave or crash recovery for open documents
author: zuujiscom
body:
**What:** On the web there is only a `beforeunload` prompt (`apps/photocraft-web/src/web.rs`). A tab crash, an out-of-memory kill or the browser discarding a background tab loses all unsaved work. The desktop recovery store is native-only (`crates/format/src/autosave.rs`), and IndexedDB is used only for presets (`indexed_presets.rs`).

**Possible direction:** Autosave snapshots into IndexedDB or OPFS through the existing incremental writer, and offer them on the next load.

**Related:** #4962, #1614, #3163.

title: Pen: Undo after finishing a path deletes the whole path
author: marmitoTH
body:
## Summary

While you draw with the Pen tool (P), Cmd/Ctrl+Z removes the last anchor you placed (#1466). After the path is finished, though, Undo deletes the **entire path** instead of taking back only the last action, and every anchor is lost.

## Steps to reproduce

1. File › New (any size).
2. Press **P** for the Pen tool and click three points.
3. Click the first point to close the path.
4. Press **Cmd/Ctrl+Z**.

**Expected:** only the closing segment is undone. The path is open again and the Pen keeps drawing from the last anchor, as in Photoshop. Each further Undo removes one anchor.

**Actual:** the whole path is deleted.

## Every way of finishing a path is affected

| Steps | What happens |
|---|---|
| Close the path on its first anchor, then Undo | The whole path is deleted |
| End the path with ↩ or Esc, then Undo | The whole path is deleted |
| Pick another tool while drawing (e.g. Move), then Undo | The whole path is deleted |
| Right-click › Make Selection, then Undo twice | The 1st Undo removes the selection; the 2nd deletes the whole path |
| Draw two or three paths, then keep pressing Undo | Each Undo deletes one whole path, last one first |

The Curvature Pen and Shape mode (Undo removes the whole shape layer) behave the same way.

## Cause

The anchors of a path being drawn are UI state, not History. Finishing the path commits it as a single History step and discards the draft, so Undo can only go back to before the path existed.

## Fix

I fixed this in an open pull request: #6413.

**Environment:** Windows 11, PhotoCraft built from `main` (2b3d0563).

title: [Feature Request] Dynamic Text  (auto-resizing and reflowing type to fit a bounding box)
author: mboeddeker
body:
### Motivation
PhotoCraft already supports point and paragraph text with Character/Paragraph panels, OpenType, variable fonts and Warp Text. What’s still missing is Photoshop’s **Dynamic Text**.

With Dynamic Text you define a bounding box (or path) and the type automatically scales and reflows so it fills that area. Short lines get larger, long lines get smaller. When you resize the box the layout updates live and the layer stays fully editable. No more manual font-size and line-break tweaking to make text fill a space.

This is especially useful for things like YouTube thumbnails, posters and titles where you want large, bold text that occupies a fixed area next to an image. Typical examples are layouts with a product or character on the left and very large impact text on the right that fills the remaining space as tightly as possible.

### Proposed behavior
Match the Photoshop implementation as closely as practical:

- Convert an existing type layer to Dynamic Text (options bar icon, menu or layer context menu).
- Supported shapes:
  - **Block** — text scales and reflows to fit a rectangular bounding box. Word Gap and Line Gap controls.
  - **Circle**, **Arch**, **Bow** — text follows the respective path and scales between start/end points. Position and direction controls.
  - **Dynamic fit** — for text placed on any path or shape; automatically resizes so the text fills it.
- Live update while resizing the bounding box or editing the text.
- Layer remains fully editable (font, weight, color, tracking, manual line breaks still work).
- Visual indicator in the Layers panel.

### References
- Adobe docs:  
  - [Dynamic Text overview](https://helpx.adobe.com/photoshop/desktop/text-typography/work-with-dynamic-text/dynamic-text-overview.html)  
  - [Adjust formatting and resize text with Dynamic Text](https://helpx.adobe.com/photoshop/desktop/text-typography/work-with-dynamic-text/adjust-formatting-and-resize-text-with-dynamic-text.html)
- Introduced in Photoshop Bet…

title: Feature request: Import Krita brushes and keyboard shortcuts
author: polvolunarck
body:
## Summary
Allow users moving from Krita to PhotoCraft to import their brush presets and keyboard shortcut configuration instead of rebuilding them manually.

## Proposed behavior
- Import Krita brush resources/presets (including brush bundles/resource packs and individual presets where supported) into the PhotoCraft Brushes panel.
- Preserve each brush tip and map compatible settings such as size, spacing, opacity/flow, and supported dynamics. Clearly report settings or resource types that cannot be represented, rather than silently importing an incomplete brush.
- Import or map a Krita keyboard shortcut configuration to PhotoCraft commands/tools, with a preview of the mappings and clear handling of unsupported commands and shortcut conflicts.
- Keep PhotoCraft's native brush and shortcut formats unchanged; imported resources should be converted into native presets/settings.

## Acceptance criteria
- Users can select a Krita brush resource or shortcut configuration through the existing import/settings workflow.
- Successful imports list what was imported and identify unsupported items or conflicts.
- Imported brushes can be used and saved as PhotoCraft presets; imported shortcuts can be reviewed and edited in PhotoCraft's shortcut settings.
- Tests cover valid imports, malformed input, unsupported settings, and shortcut conflicts.

## Context
PhotoCraft already has brush preset import and editable shortcuts, but there is no Krita-specific migration path. Krita resources can contain settings and dynamics that do not map one-to-one to PhotoCraft, so compatibility should be explicit.
