title: Content-Aware Move: no live preview for selections over 256×256 px (TOOL-213-4)
author: davidmann4
body:
> **Updated description:** this now covers both commits (87fc5f1f added the GPU-side tile copies); the numbers below are new.

Fixes #1774.

## Why
Select All + Fill on a 50 MP document is fast in the engine; the freeze comes from the GPU canvas refresh afterwards. For 16-bit layers, and any other non-RGBA8 format (CMYK, Lab, Gray, 32-bit), every changed tile was converted to Rgba16Float one after another on the UI thread. Every tile was then uploaded from the CPU on its own, even though a full-canvas fill shares one tile: 775 conversions and 387 MB of uploads per refresh, about 1.4 s per fill. In Photoshop the fill is effectively instant.

## Change
All in `crates/gpu`:
- **Convert each distinct tile once:** the layer-page sync groups changed tiles by identity and converts them in parallel batches of 64 (sequential on wasm, through the existing `fx::par_map`).
- **Upload a shared tile once:** a tile shared by several coordinates goes once into a scratch tile, then `copy_texture_to_texture` copies it to the other coordinates on the GPU. This covers solid fills, cleared areas (Delete) and non-zero defaults such as masks.
- **New layer pages** take the same path instead of assembling the whole page in a zeroed staging buffer. Filling a new layer grows its page, so this is the common case.
- **Faster 16-bit conversion:** 16-bit RGB and grayscale tiles convert to RGBA16F through a lookup table. The bytes are identical to the general path.

## Measurements
Release app over the control channel, 6336×7920, new layer, Select All + Fill, RTX 5070 Ti. The figure is `perf.timings.compositeMs`, the CPU time of the GPU refresh:

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 16-bit fill | about 1.4 s | 15–19 ms |
| 8-bit fill | 21–44 ms | 10 ms |

The 16-bit figure for main is from the first commit's live-app measurement (time to the next frame); the rest are `compositeMs`.

## Tests
- `photocraft-gpu` parity `shared_tiles_upload_once_and_copy`: GPU vs CPU at 8 and 16 bits, RGB and gray, …

title: Arabic text support: paragraph direction UI, bidi in the shell, and Middle Eastern type features
author: tareqziad1998
body:
Hi! I'm a native Arabic speaker and would like to work on **Arabic text support**: typing and
displaying Arabic correctly, with good Arabic font handling. This is separate from translating
the UI (an `ar.tsv` catalog), which can come later.

## What already works (from reading the code)

- The text engine shapes and reorders Arabic: parley + HarfRust, Unicode bidi
  (`crates/text/src/layout.rs`, test `rtl_text_is_reordered`).
- `ParagraphStyle.direction` (Auto/LTR/RTL) exists in the document model and `type_cmds`
  accepts `"rtl"`.
- Arabic fallback families (Noto Sans/Naskh/Kufi Arabic…) in `crates/text/src/scripts.rs`, and the
  font menu previews an Arabic sample for faces that cover it (`font_preview.rs`).

1. **Paragraph direction has no UI (TYPE-218-2).** No Auto/LTR/RTL control in the Paragraph
   panel or the Type options bar, and the caret doesn't move visually in RTL text.
2. **No bidi in the egui shell.** Arabic in layer names, text fields and font names joins its
   letters but lays words out left to right, so phrases read backwards
   (`crates/ui-egui/src/cjk_fonts.rs`: "it has no bidi reordering yet"). Related: #1408, #1693.

5. **No golden shaping tests for Arabic (TYPE-218-3)**: only a smoke test and a Hebrew bidi test.

1. Paragraph direction control in the Paragraph panel + options bar, wired to the existing
   command, with RTL caret movement and tests.
2. Golden shaping/bidi tests for Arabic (joining forms, lam-alef ligature, mixed Arabic/Latin
   and digits), using an OFL font from craft-fonts.
3. Bidi reordering for single-line labels in the shell (layer names, text fields), probably via
   `unicode-bidi` before han…

author: tareqziad1998
body:
Split out of #6684. The other parts of that ticket are already tracked in #218 (paragraph direction UI,
golden shaping tests) and storytold/vectorcraft#1202 (bidi in the egui shell).

## Problem

title: Paragraph text: a word wider than the box overflows instead of breaking at the box edge
author: diegochagas
body:
## What

A gap in paragraph (box) text, seen on 0.9.0 and on main while lettering a comic balloon (a manga translation: a paragraph box narrower than one word of the dialogue):

1. **A word wider than the paragraph box never breaks.** Text is laid out with parley's greedy breaker (`crates/text/src/layout.rs`, `break_all_lines(avail)`), and the style's `overflow_wrap` is left at parley's default `Normal`, which only breaks at UAX #14 opportunities (spaces, a `-`). parley only takes an *emergency* mid-word break when `overflow_wrap` is `BreakWord` or `Anywhere`, so a word longer than the box runs out past its right edge (`BLOQUEADO?!` below) and resizing the box smaller changes nothing. Photoshop wraps such a word at the box edge.
2. Paragraph › Hyphenate doing nothing is now its own ticket, #6710 (split at ticket-craft's request).

## Proposed

- Part 1 (small, a PR follows): paragraph text sets `OverflowWrap::BreakWord` on the layout, so an overlong word breaks at the box edge and resizing the box re-wraps it; point text is unchanged (it has no width to overflow). Test: a box narrower than its only word lays out on more than one line and no line exceeds the box width; a box that fits the word is byte-for-byte the same as today.
- Part 2 moved to #6710.

Related: #5565 (early wrapping with horizontal scale, same breaker), #4996 (asks that box text respects its limits), #6653 (Dynamic Text reflow).

title: Paragraph › Hyphenate does nothing: implement hyphenation (dictionary soft breaks) or hide the option
author: diegochagas
body:
Split out of #6694 at ticket-craft's request (that ticket keeps the overlong-word overflow, fixed by #6696).

## What

**Paragraph › Hyphenate is a no-op.** The checkbox is in the Paragraph panel (every catalog translates it), `type.setParagraph {"hyphenate": bool}` stores it on the paragraph style, and it round-trips to the PSD `AutoHyphenate` flag (`crates/text/src/psd.rs`), but nothing in `crates/text` reads it: the layout (`crates/text/src/layout.rs`) hands parley the text with no soft break opportunities inside words, and there is no hyphenation dictionary in the tree. The option looks implemented and silently does nothing, on 0.9.0 and main.

## Proposed

Either, in this order of preference:

1. **Make it real.** When `ps.hyphenate` is set, insert soft-hyphen break opportunities (U+00AD, which parley treats as a break opportunity that renders a hyphen only when taken) at the dictionary's hyphenation points before layout, per paragraph, in the paragraph's language (the run's `language`, else the document's). The `hyphenation` crate ships the TeX patterns for ~70 languages behind a feature per language; English, German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Dutch, Polish and Russian would cover the bundled catalogs and cost ~1–2 MB. Photoshop's Hyphenation dialog values (words longer than N letters, after/before first/last K letters, hyphen limit, hyphenation zone, capitalised words) map to the crate's `Standard` hyphenator with min-length filters; the PSD `HyphenationWordSize` / `HyphenationPreLength` / `HyphenationPostLength` / `HyphenationLimit` keys are already parsed there. Caret and selection indices must keep counting the original text (the inserted U+00AD must be stripped from every range the engine reports), and the web build (wasm) needs the same tables.
2. **Hide it until then.** Remove the checkbox from the Paragraph panel and make `type.setParagraph {"hyphenate": true}` return a clear "not implemented" error, keeping the PSD flag round-tripping so f…

title: [Bug Report] [PhotoCraft] Title bar compatibility issue
author: ticket-craft
body:
### Description

My AHK script to replace FanzyZone's **shift+left click drag and drop** to snap a window with **middle mouse click drag and drop** doesn't work on PhotoCraft because the way the title bar is coded is unproper:

**The title-bar compatibility issue:** A standard Windows caption returns `HTCAPTION (2)` from `WM_NCHITTEST`. PhotoCraft’s draggable title-bar gap returns `HTCLIENT (1)`, so external window-management tools identify it as ordinary client content. Accessibility exposes the gap as `UIA_CustomControlTypeId (50025)`, but that does not change its native hit-test result. Custom title bars are valid; this implementation simply lacks the native caption identification those tools expect. [Windows hit-test documentation](<https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/inputdev/wm-nchittest>)

**The likely cause of the stuck dragging:** `panels::title_bar` uses `drag.drag_started()` to issue `ViewportCommand::StartDrag`, without restricting the initiating mouse button. However, winit’s `drag_window()` expects the left button to have been pressed immediately beforehand. A middle-button drag therefore enters an unsupported input sequence. The same unrestricted check exists in `modal_drag_overlay`. [PhotoCraft title-bar code](<https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/v0.9.0/crates/ui-egui/src/panels.rs>), [modal overlay](<https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/v0.9.0/crates/ui-egui/src/titlebar.rs>), [winit’s documented requirement](<https://docs.rs/winit/0.30.13/winit/window/struct.Window.html#method.drag_window>)

Suggested changes:

- Restrict both `StartDrag` calls to the primary button:

  ```
  if drag.drag_started_by(egui::PointerButton::Primary) {
      ui.ctx().send_viewport_cmd(egui::ViewportCommand::StartDrag);
  }
  ```
- Consider returning `HTCAPTION` for the actual draggable gap, while preserving client hit-testing for menus/buttons and resize hit-testing at the edges.
- Add a regression test: middle-button drag, release, then ord…

title: [Bug] Save for Web exports the committed state during a pending Free Transform
author: idemax
body:
### Description
Save for Web (Legacy) can be opened with ⌘⇧⌥S while Free Transform is pending. The command remains available even though the transform has not been accepted. The export reads the last committed document and ignores the visible transform preview, so the saved image can differ from the canvas.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Open a document with a visible pixel layer, or place an image so Free Transform starts.
2. Resize or move the layer and leave Free Transform unconfirmed.
3. Press ⌘⇧⌥S.
4. Confirm the export and compare it with the visible canvas preview.

### Expected behavior
While Free Transform is active, Save for Web should be disabled in File > Export and its keyboard shortcut should not open the dialog, matching Photoshop. Commit or cancel the transform before exporting.

### Actual behavior
The shortcut opens Save for Web while the transform is pending. Confirming the export uses the committed document state and ignores the pending transform preview.

### Manual verification
Manually reproduced on a synthetic document with Free Transform active at 240%. I moved the pending layer preview from outside the canvas into its center without committing, then exported before and after moving it. The two JPEG files were identical byte for byte, both 267 × 960 px. This confirms that the export ignored the visible preview.

### Code path
- In [shortcuts.rs](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/main/crates/ui-egui/src/shortcuts.rs#L398-L408), the key handler handles Enter and Escape during Free Transform, then continues to normal shortcut dispatch.
- Shortcut dispatch checks [menus::is_enabled](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/main/crates/ui-egui/src/shortcut_dispatch.rs#L331-L355). [transform_tool::is_enabled](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/main/crates/ui-egui/src/transform_tool.rs#L1197-L1216) has no disabling rule for Save for Web, so the command falls through to the generic enabled check in [menus.rs](https://github.com/…

title: Missing Microsoft font names (Calibri, Arial, Times New Roman, Courier New…) render in bundled Inter instead of the installed metric-compatible substitutes
author: ibakard
body:
**PhotoCraft:** 0.9.0 AppImage (`photocraft-cli 0.9.0 (c699e3cda, 2026-10-14)`)
**OS:** Fedora 44, x86_64

## Summary

Text set in a Microsoft font name that is not installed (Calibri, Arial, Times New Roman, Courier New, Cambria, Georgia, Verdana, Aptos) renders in the bundled Inter. The metric-compatible substitutes are installed (Carlito, Liberation Sans/Serif/Mono, Caladea) and Fontconfig maps those names to them (`30-metric-aliases.conf`), but PhotoCraft does not use these aliases:

```
$ for f in Calibri Arial "Times New Roman" "Courier New" Cambria serif monospace; do printf '%-16s -> ' "$f"; fc-match --format='%{family[0]}\n' "$f"; done
Calibri          -> Carlito
Arial            -> Liberation Sans
Times New Roman  -> Liberation Serif
Courier New      -> Liberation Mono
Cambria          -> Caladea
serif            -> Noto Serif
monospace        -> Noto Sans Mono
```

As a result:

- Times New Roman, Cambria and Georgia come out sans-serif, and Courier New comes out proportional, not monospaced. Line widths differ from the metric-compatible substitute.
- "Bold" is Inter SemiBold, because only Inter Regular, Medium and SemiBold are bundled (`type.fonts {"family":"Inter"}` lists these three).
- "Italic" is upright Inter, slanted.
- The generic names `serif` and `monospace` also render in Inter.

Font discovery itself works: every installed family is listed by `type.fonts` and renders with its real Bold/Italic faces. The fallback is not silent: each command prints `warning: font 'Calibri' is not installed; text may render using a fallback face`, and the document keeps the requested family name. This is not specific to Fedora; any system without the Microsoft fonts is affected.

## Steps to reproduce

Requires `photocraft-cli` on `PATH` and ImageMagick (`magick`).

```sh

render() {
  photocraft-cli run --new '{"width":600,"height":60}' --cmd type.create \

title: zh-Hans: .atn step names come out as mojibake — read_ascii() assumes ASCII but localized Photoshop writes the system code page (GBK)
author: songliu0403-rgb
body:
PhotoCraft 0.9.0 (`c699e3cda`), Windows 11, UI language zh-Hans. The `.atn` was exported from Adobe Photoshop 2026 (Chinese UI).

### What happens

Every step name a zh-Hans Photoshop writes into the `.atn` shows as mojibake — in the Actions panel, in `actions.load` results, and in playback errors:

| should read | PhotoCraft shows | event |
|---|---|---|
| 可选颜色 | `��ѡ��ɫ` | `selectiveColor` |
| Camera Raw 滤镜 | `Camera Raw �˾�` | `Adobe Camera Raw Filter` |
| 色彩范围 | `��ɫ��Χ` | `colorRange` |
| 移动 | `�ƶ�` | `move` |
| 叠加 | `����` | `set` |

It also leaks into error text:

```
$ photocraft-cli run photo.jpg \
    --cmd actions.load --params '{"path":"…/相馆.ATN"}' \
    --cmd actions.play --params '{"action":"调白"}'
error: `actions.play`: action `调白` step 2 failed: Photoshop step "��ѡ��ɫ"
       (selectiveColor) has no PhotoCraft equivalent yet; …
```

### Cause

`crates/psd/src/atn.rs`, `read_ascii()`:

```rust
/// Reads a u32 length + ASCII bytes (event and dictionary names).
fn read_ascii(r: &mut Reader<'_>) -> Result<String> {
    let n = r.u32()?;
    Ok(String::from_utf8_lossy(r.bytes_u64(u64::from(n))?).into_owned())
}
```

Those strings are **not** ASCII: localized Photoshop writes the `TEXT` event name and
the dictionary name in the running system's **ANSI code page** (CP936/GBK here).
Verified against the file — `"可选颜色".encode("gbk")` = `bf c9 d1 a1 d1 d5 c9 ab`
occurs in the `.atn`, and `from_utf8_lossy` turns exactly those bytes into U+FFFD
plus stray characters. The action-set / action names are 8-byte-Pascal UTF-16 and
decode fine, which is why the action names look correct while the step names don't.

### Expected

Decode event/dictionary names the way Photoshop writes them — the system ANSI code
page — or fall back gracefully (try UTF-8, then the code page) so step names read
correctly and playback errors stop showing mojibake.

### Environment

- PhotoCraft 0.9.0 (`c699e3cda`, 2026-10-14), Windows 11 x64
- Action set exported from Photoshop 2026 zh-Hans:…

title: Actions: `select.deselect` errors with "no selection" instead of being a no-op, so imported actions that start with Deselect cannot play
author: songliu0403-rgb
body:
PhotoCraft 0.9.0 (`c699e3cda`), Windows 11. `.atn` imported from Photoshop 2026.

### What happens

An action whose **first step is Deselect** stops before doing anything:

```
$ photocraft-cli run IMG_3083.jpg \
    --cmd actions.load --params '{"path":"…/相馆.ATN"}' \
    --cmd actions.play --params '{"action":"女-蓝底"}'
error: `actions.play`: action `女-蓝底` step 1 failed:
       command `select.deselect` is not available right now: no selection
```

Exit code 1, zero steps run. 6 of the 12 actions in this set start with Deselect, so
all of them are dead on arrival.

### Why it matters

"Deselect first" is a very common opening step in recorded Photoshop actions — it's
how people make an action idempotent before it builds a selection. In Photoshop
`Deselect` with nothing selected is a **no-op**: it neither errors nor aborts the
action. So the same action plays fine there, and fails here, which reads as "the
imported actions don't work".

### Expected

State-dependent commands that Photoshop treats as no-ops should succeed silently when
the precondition is absent — at minimum `select.deselect` on a document with no
selection.

A related observation, possibly the same class: `高反差保留` fails at step 2 with
`the layer has nothing to rasterize` (`layer.rasterize.layer`), right after
`layer.new.layerViaCopy` — that may mean the copy step doesn't produce content when
there is no selection, rather than a rasterize problem. Worth checking together.

Either way, a "skip steps whose precondition doesn't apply" mode for playback would
help, since imported actions routinely contain such steps.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Import any Photoshop `.atn` whose action starts with Deselect.
2. Open an ordinary photo with no active selection.
3. Play the action.

title: Crop tool should not commit a pending crop when switching tools
author: idemax
body:
Product: PhotoCraft
Module / Feature: Crop Tool
Reference application: Adobe Photoshop
Manual Photoshop check: reporter confirmed on October 16, 2026

## Description

When the selected crop aspect ratio differs from the image dimensions, pressing C enters the Crop tool and fits the crop frame to that ratio.

In the current PhotoCraft code, pressing V before explicitly confirming the crop applies it and switches to the Move tool. This changes the document even though the user only requested a tool change. Switching tools must not implicitly confirm a crop.

The reporter manually checked this scenario in Adobe Photoshop. Pressing V while the crop preview is active does nothing. The crop remains pending, and the Crop tool stays active. The requested tool switch is ignored.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open an image whose dimensions differ from the selected crop ratio.
2. Select a crop ratio preset with a different aspect ratio.
3. Press C to enter the Crop tool and view the fitted crop preview.
4. Without confirming the crop, press V.

## Actual result in PhotoCraft

The crop is applied, and the active tool changes to Move.

## Expected result

Pressing V while a crop is pending should leave the document and crop preview unchanged, and keep the Crop tool active. A tool switch must not confirm the crop. Applying it should require an explicit crop confirmation, such as Enter or double clicking the crop.

## Photoshop comparison

The reporter verified that Photoshop does nothing in this state. It neither applies the crop nor switches tools.

## Related issue and pull request

This corrects the expected behavior recorded in #3368. PR #3451 merged the opposite behavior based on the claim that Photoshop commits the crop when switching tools. The reporter's manual check shows that claim does not match this scenario.

title: Paste: pasted image lands partly off-canvas instead of being clamped to the document bounds
author: marmitoTH
body:
## What happens

Pasting an image from the clipboard places it around the current view centre, so it can land partly outside the canvas even when the canvas has room for all of it.

- Clipboard image 2468×4096 px, pasted into a new 2468×4096 px document: the image lands slightly out of bounds.
- The same image pasted into a new 4096×4096 px document: also slightly out of bounds.
- Pasted into a document smaller than the image: depending on zoom and scroll position, the image can leave empty (uncovered) areas of the canvas.

## What Photoshop does

The paste position is clamped to the document bounds:

- **The image fits in the canvas:** it is always placed fully inside the canvas.
- **The image is larger than the canvas:** it overflows, but stays positioned so it covers the whole canvas with no blank space. Its top-left corner stays within bounds.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Copy an image of 2468×4096 px to the system clipboard.
2. File › New, 2468×4096 px (or 4096×4096 px).
3. Zoom or scroll so the view centre isn't the canvas centre, then Edit › Paste.
4. The pasted layer extends past the canvas edge.

## Notes

`paste_offset` in `crates/engine/src/edit_cmds.rs` centres the clip on the `center` param (the view centre) without clamping the result to the canvas. A fix would clamp the offset on each axis. If the clip fits on that axis, keep it within `[canvas.x0, canvas.x1 - width]`. If it doesn't fit, keep it within `[canvas.x1 - width, canvas.x0]` so the canvas stays covered.

Related: #4585 changes the same function to fix an overflow, but doesn't change placement.

title: The way the tab key toggles the toolbar, options bar, etc is not consistent with Photoshop
author: lednerg
body:
The tab key is used to hide/show the toolbar (on the left), the options bar (up top), and the floating panels (on the right). Pressing shift-tab only toggles the floating panels. If any of those three things is not currently visible, the next time tab is pressed, all three should become visible. Right now Photocraft isn't doing it this way, and you can get into situations where tab only toggles the floating panels or the other two things and it's not obvious how to make everything visible again.

When in Full Screen Mode (found in View > Screen Mode or by pressing F a few times), the tab key should be toggling the three items as well as the main menu bar (File, Edit, etc). Currently none of these items can become visible in Full Screen Mode. That said, if you press tab while in Full Screen and then switch the Screen Mode, the three items will be hidden, so it is technically toggling them, we just can't see them in Full Screen.

Whenever you switch to Full Screen Mode, the toolbars, menus, and panels should initially be hidden, no matter what. If the items were visible before going to Full Screen Mode, then when you exit Full Screen Mode, they should be visible again. However, if you press tab an even number of times in Full Screen to show and then hide the items, then they should stay hidden when switching out of Full Screen Mode.

Alright, hopefully that made sense.

title: Layered TIFF: blocks with Idnt/indx references are dropped when the byte order is converted
author: davidmann4
body:
**TL;DR:** saving or opening an Intel byte-order layered TIFF loses any layer block whose descriptor holds an `Idnt` or `indx` reference.

**What goes wrong**
`crates/psd/src/tiff.rs` (`Tx::reference_item`) converts `Idnt` and `indx` reference items as a bare u32:
```rust
b"Idnt" | b"indx" => {
    self.u32()?;
}
```
The descriptor parser reads both as class + u32 (`descriptor.rs`, `ReferenceItem::Identifier { class, id }` / `Index { class, index }`; changed in #4434 because real .atn files failed with the bare u32). The converter was never updated, so it reads the class's length field as the id and loses sync.

**Repro**
A layer or global tagged block (e.g. `lfx2`) whose descriptor contains a reference with an `Identifier` or `Index` item.
- Save as a little-endian layered TIFF: the conversion fails and the block is dropped with a "block dropped" warning.
- Open such a TIFF written little-endian: the block stays unconverted and is lost on the next PSD save.

**Expected:** the block converts and round-trips byte for byte, like the other reference items (`rele`, `name`, `Clss` …).

title: Fit Image with width or height 0 shrinks the document to 1 px
author: davidmann4
body:
**TL;DR:** `file.automate.fitImage` with an empty (0) width or height scales the whole document down to about 1 px.

**What goes wrong**
`crates/engine/src/file_cmds.rs` (`fit_image`):
```rust
let bw = f64_param(p, "width").unwrap_or(w).max(1.0);
let bh = f64_param(p, "height").unwrap_or(h).max(1.0);
```
The same file has `size_param`, documented as "zero or negative means not set (dialogs send 0 for empty fields)", and Image Processor uses it; Fit Image doesn't.

**Repro**
1000x800 document, `file.automate.fitImage {"width": 0, "height": 500}` → scale factor 1/1000, the document becomes 1x1. `{"width": -5}` does the same.

**Expected:** a missing/0 side doesn't constrain the fit (or the value is refused), as an empty field never collapses the image.

title: Preset groups can be renamed to a name another group already has
author: davidmann4
body:
**TL;DR:** renaming a gradient/style/shape/pattern preset group onto an existing group name succeeds, and a later "replace" import of that group then deletes both groups.

**What goes wrong**
`crates/engine/src/presets/mod.rs` (`edit_groups`, `renameGroup`) renames without checking that the new name is free:
```rust
let i = groups.iter().position(|x| x.name == g)...;
groups[i].name = to.clone();
```
The sibling `swatches.renameGroup` refuses with "a group named … already exists", and the append/reset paths use `unique_group`, so group names are meant to be unique.

**Repro**
`gradient.presets.edit {"action":"renameGroup","group":"Pastels","name":"Basics"}` → Ok, two groups named "Basics". `deleteGroup`/`move` then only reach the first one, and `gradient.presets.importGrd {"group":"Basics","replace":true}` removes both, including the user's renamed group.

**Expected:** an error like the swatch sibling's; renaming a group to its own name stays fine.

title: plugin.run changes a layer whose pixels are locked
author: davidmann4
body:
**TL;DR:** a filter plug-in rewrites a layer with Lock Image Pixels or Lock All, where every built-in filter refuses.

**What goes wrong**
`crates/engine/src/plugin_cmds.rs` (`run`): the raster and smart-object branches write without any lock check. Built-in filters (`filters.rs`) and Lens Correction refuse with "Could not complete your request because the layer … is locked".

**Repro**
Raster layer with `locks.pixels = true` (or Lock All), then `plugin.run {"id": "org.photocraft.example.invert"}` → Ok, the pixels are inverted.

**Expected:** the same refusal as the built-in filters; the pixels stay unchanged.

title: Renaming an action breaks Conditional steps that call it
author: davidmann4
body:
**TL;DR:** after renaming an action, a Conditional step that runs it by name fails with "no action named …".

**What goes wrong**
`crates/engine/src/actions_cmds.rs` (`rename`) only rewrites `actions.play` steps:
```rust
if id == "actions.play" && params.get("action").and_then(Value::as_str) == Some(old.as_str()) {
```
`actions.conditional` names actions in `then` / `else` (the .atn import creates these steps too), and those keep the old name.

**Repro**
1. `actions.insert {"action":"Main","id":"actions.conditional","params":{"if":"always","then":"B"}}`
2. `actions.rename {"action":"B","name":"C"}`
3. `actions.play {"action":"Main"}` → "no action named `B`".

**Expected:** the Conditional step follows the rename, as Play steps already do.

title: PSD import drops colours stored as HSB: shape fills vanish, strokes and effects turn black
author: davidmann4
body:
**TL;DR:** colours a PSD stores in HSB (`HSBC` descriptors) are not read, so fills disappear and strokes, effects and gradient stops fall back to black.

**What goes wrong**
`crates/io/src/blocks.rs` (`color_from_desc`) documents `HSBC` support but has no branch for it; it falls into the RGB fallback, finds no `Rd  ` key and returns `None`.

**Real files that hit it**
- psd-tools `descriptors/stroke-color-descriptors-hsb-with-rgb-mode.psd`: a shape whose fill and stroke colours are HSBC (white).
- ag-psd `read/gradient/src.psd`: gradient stops stored as HSBC.

**Effects**
- shape fill missing; shape stroke black (fallback) instead of white
- layer-effect colours black
- HSBC gradient stops skipped (all-HSBC gradients become black to white)
- solid colour fill layers with an HSBC colour import as pixels

**Expected:** HSBC (`H   ` angle, `Strt`, `Brgh` in percent) is converted like the other colour models.

title: Auto-Align Layers hides a layer whose mask reveals all
author: davidmann4
body:
**TL;DR:** after Auto-Align, a layer with a mostly-white (reveal-all) mask disappears completely.

**What goes wrong**
`crates/engine/src/align_cmds.rs` (`auto_align`) warps the layer mask with `warp_placed`, the colour warp. That warp adds an alpha channel to a gray surface and returns a new surface whose default pixel is 0. Stored back as the mask, everything outside the painted area reads 0 = hidden, and the mask now has 2 channels. The transform commands use `warp_gray` for masks, which keeps the format and the default.

**Repro**
Two pixel layers that register (as in the existing align tests); give the moving layer `LayerMask::reveal_all()` with a 10x10 black square painted, then `edit.autoAlignLayers {"projection":"reposition"}` → the whole layer is hidden instead of only the square.

**Expected:** the mask moves with the layer and stays a reveal-all mask outside the painted square.

title: Image Size moves the centre of a gradient fill layer
author: davidmann4
body:
**TL;DR:** resizing the image moves the centre of a Gradient Fill layer that has an offset; doubling the size doubles the offset.

**What goes wrong**
`crates/engine/src/canvas_geom.rs` (`map_fill`) multiplies the gradient's centre offset by the full canvas transform:
```rust
*offset = ((a.m[0] * ox + a.m[2] * oy) as f32, (a.m[1] * ox + a.m[3] * oy) as f32);
```
The offset is a fraction of the frame (`doc` `Fill::Gradient.offset`, PSD `Ofst`), and the frame scales with the image. The comment says this is exact for 90° turns and flips; but the same code runs for Image Size / crop-to-size (`resample_doc`) and Perspective Crop, where it scales the fraction.

**Repro**
100x100 document, gradient fill layer with offset (0.25, 0); `image.imageSize {"width": 200}` → offset (0.5, 0): the centre moves from 75% to 100% of the frame. Resizing to 50% gives (0.125, 0).

**Expected:** the offset stays (0.25, 0) after a resize; flips and 90° turns still mirror/rotate it.

title: Apply Image with the layer mask targeted changes the layer's pixels instead of the mask
author: davidmann4
body:
**TL;DR:** with a layer mask targeted, Image > Apply Image overwrites the layer's colour pixels and leaves the mask unchanged.

**What goes wrong**
`crates/engine/src/channel_cmds.rs` (`apply_image`): only alpha channels and Quick Mask count as channel targets (`is_channel_target`). For the mask target the code falls through to the layer branch, which calls `paint_surface(doc, id, &Value::Null)` and so drops the `"target":"mask"` that routing added.

**Repro**
1. Pixel layer filled red, `layer.layerMask.revealAll`.
2. `channel.target {"channel":"mask"}`.
3. `image.applyImage {"source":{"channel":"composite"},"blending":"normal"}` → the mask is unchanged and the red pixels are replaced by the composite.

**Expected:** Apply Image writes into the targeted mask (a common way to build masks from image content); the layer's pixels stay red.

title: 'Open color-less EXR as ACEScg' is ignored by File > Open and Open EXR Parts
author: davidmann4
body:
**TL;DR:** with the ACEScg File Handling option on, a colour-less EXR opened through File > Open in the desktop app (or Open EXR Parts) still opens as linear sRGB.

**What goes wrong**
#4908 tags the document in `open_bytes_as` only (`crates/engine/src/file_cmds.rs`, `tag_exr_colorspace`), i.e. `file.openAs`. The desktop app opens files as background jobs by default: File > Open, drag and drop and Open Recent go through `Session::start_open` (`crates/engine/src/jobs.rs`), which never tags. `file.openExrParts` (`exr_cmds.rs`) doesn't either.

**Repro**
Turn on `prefs.file_handling.exr_aces_cg`; open a profile-less `.exr` with `start_open` (+ `wait_job`) → the document's profile is linear sRGB, not ACEScg. `file.openExrParts` gives the same. `file.openAs` gives ACEScg.

**Expected:** every open path honours the option.

title: Actions: Shift-click layer select (addToSelectionContinuous) imports as a plain select, silently breaking Group Layers steps
author: r-neuschulz
body:
﻿PhotoCraft 0.9.0 (latest release), Windows 11, driven over MCP (headless). Code references are `main` @ `2a952f16`.

### What happens

When an `.atn` step selects a layer with **Shift-click** (`selectionModifier: addToSelectionContinuous`), `actions.load` imports it as a plain `layer.select` with no `mode`. During playback it *replaces* the layer selection instead of extending it as a range. `actions.load` reports `unsupported: []` and `warnings: []`, so you can't tell anything was lost.

Found with PiXimperfect's free "Frequency Separation" action set (not attached, it's their IP). The action shift-selects High Frequency + Low Frequency and then runs Group Layers. In PhotoCraft only Low Frequency gets grouped, and High Frequency is left outside the group.

### Cause

`select_from` in [`crates/engine/src/atn_cmds.rs`](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/2a952f164c0b4cf936b1c6497db10dd095341c00/crates/engine/src/atn_cmds.rs#L1406-L1410) maps only `addToSelection` → `add` and `removeFromSelection` → `remove`. `addToSelectionContinuous` falls into `_ => {}`, even though `layer.select` already supports `mode: "range"`.

The export side (around L1450) presumably needs the matching `range` → `addToSelectionContinuous` so the step round-trips.

### Steps to reproduce

1. In Photoshop, open a document with three layers (A, B, C), select A, and record an action: **Shift-click C**, then **Layer › Group Layers** (Ctrl+G). Save the set as `.atn`.
2. In PhotoCraft: `actions.load` the file (the result shows `unsupported: []`, `warnings: []`).

**Actual:** only C is grouped.

Replace the step: `actions.delete {step}`, then `actions.insert {"id":"layer.select","params":{"layer":"C","mode":"range"},"at":step}`.

title: Actions: Make layer + Merge Visible (Duplicate) leaves an empty layer behind; stampVisible doesn't stamp into the active empty layer like Photoshop
author: r-neuschulz
body:
﻿PhotoCraft 0.9.0 (latest release), Windows 11, driven over MCP (headless). Code references are `main` @ `2a952f16`.

### What happens

Many Photoshop actions build a "stamp visible" layer in two recorded steps:

1. **Make layer** (new empty layer, becomes active)
2. **Merge Visible** with `Duplicate: true` (Ctrl+Alt+Shift+E)

In Photoshop the stamp lands **in the active empty layer** from step 1, so the action ends up with one stamped layer. PhotoCraft imports step 2 as `layer.stampVisible`, which always creates a *new* layer above the active one ([`merge_visible_from`, atn_cmds.rs L2395-L2397](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/2a952f164c0b4cf936b1c6497db10dd095341c00/crates/engine/src/atn_cmds.rs#L2395-L2397)). The result is the stamp plus an **empty leftover "Layer 1"** under it, and `actions.load` reports no warning.

Found with PiXimperfect's free "Frequency Separation" action set (not attached, it's their IP). Every run leaves an empty `Layer 1` between Background and the frequency-separation group.

### Steps to reproduce

1. In Photoshop, record an action on any single-layer document: **Layer › New › Layer**, then **Ctrl+Alt+Shift+E**. Save the set as `.atn`.
2. In PhotoCraft, `actions.load` the file, open a single-layer document, and `actions.play`.
3. `doc_inspect` the result.

**Expected (Photoshop):** Background + 1 stamped layer.
**Actual:** Background + empty `Layer 1` (bounds `[0,0,0,0]`) + stamped layer.

### Suggested fix

Make `layer.stampVisible` match Photoshop: when the active layer is an empty pixel layer, stamp into it rather than creating a new one. Alternatively, have the importer fold a `Make layer` immediately followed by `Merge Visible (Dplc)` into a single step.

### Workaround

`actions.toggle {step: 0, enabled: false}` on the Make-layer step.

title: Layered TIFF: smart filter data of the second and later smart objects isn't byte-swapped
author: davidmann4
body:
**TL;DR:** in an Intel byte-order layered TIFF with two or more filtered smart objects, the smart filter data (`FEid`/`FXid`) of all but the first is left in the wrong byte order, so it is lost on open and misread by other apps on save.

**What goes wrong**
`crates/psd/src/tiff.rs` (`Tx::filter_effects`) converts the version and then exactly one u64-length section; `block()` copies the rest as stored. But these blocks hold one section per smart object, each padded to 4 bytes: `FilterEffects::parse` (`filter_effects.rs`) loops over them and `to_bytes` writes them that way (#396).

**Repro**
A `FEid` block with two items (`FilterEffects::to_bytes`), converted to little endian: the second section's u64 length (and its rects, depths, plane lengths) stays big-endian.
- Opening such a TIFF: `FilterEffects::parse` reads section 2's length as a huge number, fails, and the whole block's filter caches/masks are lost.
- Saving little-endian: section 2 is written big-endian.
Our own save → reopen copies section 2 unchanged both ways, so the round trip hides it; the existing test has one item.

**Expected:** every section converts, like the first.

title: Droplets leave out actions that a Conditional step calls
author: davidmann4
body:
**TL;DR:** a droplet made from an action with a Conditional step fails when run on its own, because the actions named in the step's then/else aren't bundled.

**What goes wrong**
`crates/engine/src/actions_cmds.rs` (`called_actions`, used by `create_droplet` in `automate_cmds.rs` to fill `calledActions`, #2794) only follows `actions.play` steps:
```rust
for (_, params) in steps.iter_mut().filter(|(id, _)| id == "actions.play") {
```
`actions.conditional` steps name actions in `then` / `else`.

**Repro**
An action with `actions.conditional {"if":"landscape","then":"Wide"}` → create a droplet from it → run the droplet without the Actions panel's list → "no action named `Wide`". The same action with a Play step works.

**Expected:** the then/else actions are bundled like Play targets (index references turned into names the same way).

title: Loading an .atn with clashing action names makes Play steps call the wrong action
author: davidmann4
body:
**TL;DR:** when a loaded action set has names that clash with existing actions, a Play step inside the set can end up calling a different action from the file than the one it named.

**What goes wrong**
`crates/engine/src/atn_cmds.rs` (`actions.load`) renames clashing imported actions and then applies the renames to Play steps one rename at a time:
```rust
for (from, to) in &renamed {
    for a in s.actions.list.iter_mut().filter(|a| a.set.as_deref() == Some(imp.set.as_str())) {
        ... if id == "actions.play" && params["action"] == from { params["action"] = to }
```
A step rewritten by one rename is matched again by a later one. The loop also runs over actions that were already in a set of the same name (with `replace: false`).

**Repro**
An action "A" exists. Load an .atn whose set has actions "A" and "A 2" and a step `actions.play {"action":"A"}` (calling the file's "A"). The renames are A → "A 2" and "A 2" → a new unique name; the step is rewritten twice and ends up calling the file's "A 2".

**Expected:** each Play step is rewritten once, from its original name, and only in the newly loaded actions.

title: Free Transform and Warp keep a fill layer's old cached render
author: davidmann4
body:
**TL;DR:** after Free Transform or Warp on a fill layer that carries a cached render (e.g. from a PSD), the old pixels can keep being drawn for the old frame.

**What goes wrong**
The compositor draws `layer.fill_cache` whenever the cached fill equals the layer's fill (`compose/src/lib.rs`). `apply_transform` (`crates/engine/src/transform_cmds.rs`) and `warp_layer` (`warp_cmds.rs`) move the layer's masks, and so its fill frame, but never clear the cache. Sibling paths do: `transform_layer_geometry` in `canvas_geom.rs` ("Free Transform doesn't warp fill caches: drop it") and Perspective Crop.

**Repro**
Gradient fill layer with a `fill_cache` and a mask; `edit.transform {"matrix":[1,0,0,1,200,0]}` → the mask moves, the cached gradient pixels stay laid out for the old frame.

**Expected:** the cache is dropped and the fill re-renders for the moved frame.

title: Type tool: paragraph box edge handles do not resize the box, only the corners do
author: diegochagas
body:
## What happens

With the Type tool editing paragraph text, only the four corner handles of the box resize it. Pressing one of the four edge handles (top, right, bottom, left) does not start a resize: the press lands in the text and places the caret (or starts a text selection) instead. The handles are drawn and the resize cursor appears over them, so the box looks resizable from the edges but is not.

Seen on 0.9.0 (Flatpak) and reproduced on `main` (2a952f16) with a canvas-level test.

## Steps

1. Create a paragraph text layer (drag a box with the Type tool, type a few words).
2. Hover a corner handle and drag: the box resizes.
3. Hover the middle handle of the right or top edge and drag: nothing resizes, the caret moves.

Zoomed out (25–50 %) the corners stop working too.

## Cause

`canvas::tool_event` hands the Type tool the press **after** `snap_ui::filter_event` has snapped it (View › Snap on by default, point gesture for the Type tools). The snap reach is 8 screen px (`SNAP_PX`), the handle grab reach is 6 screen px (`type_tool::box_handle_at`), and the targets include the edited layer's own bounds (`SnapTargets::from_document` with no exclusion for point tools): the glyph bounds and the layer centre lines. An edge handle sits on the box edge, a few pixels outside the glyph bounds and exactly on a centre line, so the snapped press moves off the handle and the hit test in `type_tool::pointer_down` misses. Corners sit at the box corners, usually farther than 8 px from any glyph edge, so they survive at normal zoom. Zoomed out, the reach in document pixels grows and the corners miss as well.

Free Transform already avoids this: the canvas picks its handle with the unsnapped press (`transform_ev`), as the comment in `tool_event` says.

## Fix

- The Type tools get the unsnapped press for handle and caret picking (the drag that follows still snaps).
- A handle drag of the edited box snaps to guides and other layers, not to the glyph bounds of the text being resi…

title: [Feature Request] Vector layers with editable brush strokes (Clip Studio Paint–style)
author: Falerion-git
body:
## Summary

Add a **vector layer** type on which regular brush strokes (pen, pencil, brush tools) are stored as editable paths instead of pixels. After drawing, each stroke stays an independent object whose shape, width, color and brush tip can still be changed. This is one of the most important features for line art, comics/manga and lettering, and the main reason many illustrators keep Clip Studio Paint (CSP) in their workflow next to Photoshop.

Photoshop has no equivalent: shape layers are editable but cannot be drawn freehand with pressure-sensitive brushes, and "Stroke Path" rasterizes the result.

Related: #4996 (section 5 mentions this inside a larger lettering request; the bot asked for separate tickets), #1874 (closed, but lists "tools to modify brush strokes in vector layers" as a top priority).

## Reference: how Clip Studio Paint implements it

**Storage**
- Every stroke is saved as its own path with control points. Width (from pen pressure) and opacity are stored per control point.
- Strokes stay sharp when scaled, rotated or transformed.
- Merging two vector layers keeps the paths. Merging with a raster layer produces a raster layer.

**Vector eraser** (eraser sub tool with three modes)
- *Erase touched area*: removes only the part touched.
- *Erase up to intersection*: removes the touched segment up to the nearest crossing with another stroke. This is the most-used feature for cleaning up sketchy line art.
- *Erase whole line*: removes the entire stroke on touch.

**Object tool** (select and edit finished strokes)
- Click to select a single stroke, or drag to select several.
- Move, scale, rotate or free-transform the selection, with an option to keep line thickness constant when scaling.
- Change the **color**, **brush size** and **brush shape/tip** of the selected strokes after drawing.

**Control point tool**
- Move, add or delete control points.
- Switch a point between corner and curve.
- Change **line width** at a single point (drag left/right)…

title: Duotone: inks whose curve goes above 100 % render black as green in the view and flat export
author: davidmann4
body:
TL;DR: a Duotone image whose ink curves go above 100 % shows black as pure green on screen and in exported files.

**What goes wrong**
`Duotone::render` (`crates/doc/src/mode.rs`, `let d = curve_eval(&ink.curve, density);`) uses the curve value unclamped, while `DuotoneInk::density()` clamps it to 0..1 and the Duotone → Multichannel conversion uses that clamped value. `render()` drives the screen view and flat export (`io/src/flat.rs`).

**Repro**
`image.mode.duotone` with inks red and blue and curves `[[0,0],[100,200]]` (accepted by `parse_inks`). At gray 0 each ink density is 2.0: red gives [1,-1,-1], blue [-1,-1,1], their product [-1,1,-1], so black renders green. Converting the same image to Multichannel gives black.

**Expected**
Ink density is clamped to 0..100 % everywhere, so black stays black and view, export and Multichannel conversion agree.

title: PSD import: a type warp value beyond the f32 range is dropped instead of clamped
author: davidmann4
body:
TL;DR: a PSD whose text warp has a huge bend value opens with the text unwarped instead of fully bent.

**What goes wrong**
`crates/text/src/psd.rs` reads `warpValue`, `warpPerspective` and `warpPerspectiveOther` with `dnum(..).unwrap_or(0.0) as f32`. `dnum` rejects only non-finite f64, so `1e39` becomes `f32::INFINITY`, and `StyleWarp`'s percentage helper maps non-finite values to 0: the warp is silently dropped. Same class as #4044.

**Repro**
A TySh warp descriptor with `warpValue` = Double 1e39 → `text_layer_from_tysh(..).warp.value` is inf and the text renders without the warp.

**Expected**
The values are clamped to -100..100 before the cast, as `type.warpText` already does, so the text gets the maximum bend.

title: Guides: a ruler guide drag snaps to stale targets after Grid or Snap To options change
author: davidmann4
body:
TL;DR: after showing the grid (or turning Snap To options on or off), dragged ruler guides keep snapping to the old targets until the document is edited.

**What goes wrong**
`snap_guide` in `crates/ui-egui/src/snap_ui.rs` caches its targets in `prefs_rt.guide_targets` keyed by `(doc id, revision)`. The targets also depend on the snap options (grid visible + Snap To Grid, Layers, Document Bounds, gridline spacing), none of which change the document revision.

**Repro**
Grid hidden → drag a guide from the ruler (cache built without the grid) → View › Show › Grid → drag another guide 2 px from a gridline: no snap. Same after turning Snap To Layers / Document Bounds off (still snaps) or changing Gridline Every.

**Expected**
As in Photoshop, the guide snaps to whatever the current Snap To settings allow.

title: CLI batch --actions: every file fails when the action contains a Save As or view step
author: davidmann4
body:
TL;DR: `photocraft-cli batch --actions` fails on every file when the action has a recorded Save/Save As or zoom step, although the same steps work as a plain list.

**What goes wrong**
`batch()` in `apps/photocraft-cli/src/lib.rs` skips shell-only steps (`shell_view_command(id) || shell_save_command(id)`, #3143) only at the top level. With an action set the only top-level step is `actions.play`, and the engine then runs `file.saveAs` / `view.fitOnScreen` itself → "unknown command". The .atn importer maps Save to `file.save`, and the desktop app records Save / Save As, so real actions contain these steps.

**Repro**
`actions.json` with an action Rotate: `[image.imageRotation.90cw, file.saveAs]` → `photocraft-cli batch --actions actions.json --action Rotate --in in --out out` → every file FAIL, exit 1.

**Expected**
Like Photoshop's Batch (and like the plain step list), the batch's own output handling replaces the Save steps and view steps are ignored, so every file is processed.

title: .pcraft: a number beyond the f32 range opens as infinity, and the document can then never be saved
author: davidmann4
body:
TL;DR: a .pcraft file with an out-of-range number (e.g. opacity 1e39) opens fine but then every save and autosave fails.

**What goes wrong**
`read_manifest` in `crates/format/src/store.rs` deserializes the manifest without a finite check; serde's f32 visitor casts, so `1e39` (a valid f64) loads as `inf`. The only `finite::check` runs on save, which then refuses: "`document.layers[0].opacity` is NaN or infinite". Same family as #4044 / #5752, on the load path.

**Repro**
Save a small document, edit its manifest to `"opacity": 1e39`, open it → opens with opacity inf; File › Save → error, forever.

**Expected**
The file is refused at open with an error naming the field, the way a `null` there is refused today, so no unsaveable document is created.
